title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
title_en: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
author: Tim Bradshaw and Michael Acton
article_content:
OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, in an effort to “compete unfairly by any means available”.

The ChatGPT maker filed the lawsuit in a California court on Friday, striking back after the iPhone maker accused the AI lab of stealing top-secret information this summer.

The escalating legal battle will further sour the relationship between the two Silicon Valley companies, which just two years ago struck a partnership to embed ChatGPT into the iPhone.

The new legal action comes after OpenAI acquired io, the studio led by Apple’s former design chief Sir Jony Ive, for $6.4bn in May last year.

The AI company is preparing to launch a range of new personal devices that it says could “outcompete Apple on what Apple views as its own turf”.

OpenAI claims that Apple is using its “size and wealth to forestall competition”, including threatening suppliers that might work on its new devices, alleging a “wide variety of unlawful, unfair, and tortious conduct”.

Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The iPhone maker has long used its supply chain might to its advantage, paying upfront to lock in capacity of key components or manufacturing resources to ensure its products have the latest chips.

But OpenAI accused Apple of going further by “coercing and threatening” suppliers that are also working with the ChatGPT maker.

OpenAI also said that one of its former employees who returned to Apple shared details about its product plans and suppliers.

Apple in July accused several of its former employees, including OpenAI’s chief hardware officer Tang Tan, of sharing confidential information with their new employer about Apple’s product development and supply chain.

Another former Apple engineer exploited a “vulnerability” in Apple’s network storage to steal confidential files after he left the company, the iPhone maker claimed.

OpenAI in August denied taking Apple’s trade secrets, describing the lawsuit as an attempt to stop the AI lab from hiring its staff.

On Friday, OpenAI claimed that Apple encouraged its employees to store corporate files on their personal devices and cloud storage accounts.

“Apple set quite a trap for employees,” the complaint said. “Bright young minds thought they would work in Cupertino. Instead they were joining Hotel California: you can check out any time you like, but you can never leave.”

article_content_zh:
OpenAI 对苹果发起了新的法律诉讼，指控这家科技巨头窃取其商业机密并阻止其接触硬件供应商，以“不择手段地进行不公平竞争”。

ChatGPT 制造商周五向加州法院提起诉讼，在 iPhone 制造商指责人工智能实验室今年夏天窃取绝密信息后进行反击。

不断升级的法律战将进一步恶化这两家硅谷公司之间的关系，这两家公司就在两年前达成了合作伙伴关系，将 ChatGPT 嵌入到 iPhone 中。

去年 5 月，OpenAI 以 64 亿美元收购了苹果前设计总监 Jony Ive 爵士领导的 io 工作室，之后发起了新的法律诉讼。

这家人工智能公司正准备推出一系列新的个人设备，据称这些设备可以“在苹果视为自己的地盘上击败苹果”。

OpenAI 声称，苹果正在利用其“规模和财富来阻止竞争”，包括威胁可能使用其新设备的供应商，并指控其“存在各种非法、不公平和侵权行为”。

苹果没有立即回应置评请求。

这家 iPhone 制造商长期以来一直利用其供应链优势，通过预先付款来锁定关键零部件的产能或制造资源，以确保其产品拥有最新的芯片。

但 OpenAI 指责苹果进一步“胁迫和威胁”也与 ChatGPT 制造商合作的供应商。

OpenAI还表示，一名重返苹果的前员工分享了有关其产品计划和供应商的详细信息。

苹果公司今年 7 月指控几名前员工，包括 OpenAI 首席硬件官唐坦，与新雇主分享有关苹果产品开发和供应链的机密信息。

iPhone制造商声称，另一名前苹果工程师在离开公司后利用苹果网络存储中的“漏洞”窃取机密文件。

OpenAI 在 8 月份否认窃取了苹果的商业机密，称该诉讼是为了阻止人工智能实验室雇用其员工。

周五，OpenAI 声称苹果鼓励员工将公司文件存储在个人设备和云存储帐户上。

title: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
title_en: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
author: Oliver Barnes, Sujeet Indap, and Kieran Smith
article_content:
US telecoms company Verizon is in talks over a roughly $6bn deal to buy fibre-optic broadband operator Fidium in a potential boost to its goal of making its network available to as many as 50mn homes and businesses nationwide.

The potential acquisition would come on the heels of the completion of Verizon’s $20bn takeover of Frontier Communications earlier this year, which added 2.2mn fibre-optic subscribers across 25 US states and expanded its network to reach an additional 9mn premises.

Offering bundles of high-speed home internet and mobile coverage has been a growth priority for Verizon to reduce customer churn and boost revenues per customer. Shares in the group are up more than 17 per cent this year, giving it a market capitalisation of $198bn as the company has been aggressively investing to build out its US fibre-optic network.

Discussions between Verizon and Fidium’s owners — midmarket private equity group Searchlight Capital Partners and Canadian fund manager British Columbia Investment Management Corporation — are ongoing, according to people familiar with the matter.

The potential deal, which could value Illinois-based Fidium at about $6bn including debt, may be agreed in the coming weeks, the people said. They added it is possible another bidder could emerge and there are no guarantees the talks will result in a deal. Searchlight and BCI bought Fidium, then known as Consolidated Communications, in a $3.1bn take-private deal in 2024.

Verizon and Searchlight declined to comment. BCI and Fidium did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Fidium operates in 21 states, including California and Texas, but would strengthen Verizon’s presence in northern New England by adding a subscriber base of 351,000 homes across states including Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont. Fidium is aiming to make its fibre-optic network available to up to 2mn homes nationwide by the end of 2027, rising from 1.5mn at present.

Verizon chief executive Dan Schulman at the start of the year cited “a possibility of both inorganic and partnerships” to boost its fibre-optic network reach. Schulman said the company expects such a network to be accessible to 32mn premises by year-end as part of its medium-term goal to grow the network to between 40mn and 50mn fibre connections.

Even as Verizon’s shares have rallied this year, mobile operators are girding for the chance that Elon Musk’s SpaceX may soon enter the consumer wireless industry. In a recent podcast with Fortune Magazine, Schulman said SpaceX would need to spend more than $300bn over several years to reach the scale of Verizon.

article_content_zh:
美国电信公司 Verizon 正在就以约 60 亿美元收购光纤宽带运营商 Fidium 的交易进行谈判，这可能会推动其向全国多达 5000 万家庭和企业提供网络服务的目标。

此次潜在收购是在今年早些时候 Verizon 以 200 亿美元完成对 Frontier Communications 的收购之后进行的，该收购在美国 25 个州增加了 220 万光纤用户，并将其网络扩展到另外 900 万个场所。

提供高速家庭互联网和移动覆盖捆绑服务一直是 Verizon 的增长重点，以减少客户流失并提高每位客户的收入。该集团的股价今年上涨了 17% 以上，市值达到 1,980 亿美元，因为该公司一直在积极投资建设其美国光纤网络。

Verizon 和 Fidium 的所有者——中端市场私募股权集团 Searchlight Capital Partners 和加拿大基金管理公司不列颠哥伦比亚省投资管理公司 (British Columbia Investment Management Corporation) 之间的讨论正在进行中。

知情人士称，这项潜在交易可能会在未来几周内达成一致，预计总部位于伊利诺伊州的 Fidium（包括债务）估值约为 60 亿美元。他们补充说，可能会出现另一个竞购者，并且不能保证谈判一定能达成协议。 Searchlight 和 BCI 于 2024 年以 31 亿美元的私有化交易收购了 Fidium（当时称为 Consolidated Communications）。

Verizon 和 Searchlight 拒绝置评。 BCI 和 Fidium 没有立即回应置评请求。

Fidium 在包括加利福尼亚州和德克萨斯州在内的 21 个州开展业务，但通过在缅因州、新罕布什尔州和佛蒙特州等州增加 351,000 个家庭的用户群，将加强 Verizon 在新英格兰北部的业务。 Fidium 的目标是到 2027 年底将其光纤网络覆盖全国多达 200 万个家庭，而目前的家庭数量为 150 万个。

Verizon 首席执行官丹·舒尔曼 (Dan Schulman) 在今年年初表示，“有可能通过无机合作和合作伙伴关系”来扩大其光纤网络的覆盖范围。 Schulman 表示，该公司预计到年底，这样的网络将覆盖 3200 万个场所，作为将网络增长到 4000 万至 5000 万个光纤连接的中期目标的一部分。

尽管 Verizon 的股价今年有所上涨，但移动运营商仍在为埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 可能很快进入消费无线行业的机会做好准备。舒尔曼在最近接受《财富》杂志采访时表示，SpaceX 需要在几年内花费超过 3000 亿美元才能达到 Verizon 的规模。

title: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
title_en: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
It's no surprise at this point, but for the record: Two Chinese companies installed Nvidia's powerful Blackwell chips at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The details come from documents filed with Chinese regulators and reviewed by Bloomberg.

According to the filings, Shanghai Shuoyao offered a GB300-NVL72 rack as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, while a second company, Shanghai Kezhan, listed a GB200 server at the same site in loan documents. Exporting these chips to China without a US license is banned. Bloomberg traced the rack to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte through a serial number in a public warranty database.

Shanghai Shuoyao is closely tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed, according to Bloomberg. The Trump administration added Megaspeed to a US trade blacklist this month on suspicion of chip smuggling. Alice Huang founded Megaspeed in 2023, and Nvidia approved it as a partner within four days. It went on to become Nvidia's largest customer in Southeast Asia, Bloomberg reported.

The newly tightened US export rules and anti-diffusion measures are reportedly already causing headaches for Chinese AI startups.

title_zh: 禁售英伟达芯片现身上海数据中心
summary_zh: 上海数据中心违规部署英伟达GB200/GB300服务器，该中心关联至遭美方制裁的芯片贸易链条

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 上海硕瑶与上海克展两家公司在向上海创新银行申请贷款的抵押物清单中，明确列出了英伟达GB300-NVL72机柜及GB200服务器。经查，相关硬件设备溯源指向台湾制造厂商技嘉科技，且上海硕瑶与此前被美方列入贸易黑名单的新加坡企业Megaspeed存在深度业务关联。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Shanghai Shuoyao and Shanghai Kezhan listed Nvidia GB300-NVL72 racks and GB200 servers as loan collateral in filings with Shanghai Innovation Bank. The hardware traces back to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte, and Shanghai Shuoyao maintains deep business ties with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm recently added to the US trade blacklist.

elements_zh.who: 上海硕瑶、上海克展、Megaspeed（涉事企业）、英伟达（芯片供应商）、技嘉科技（硬件制造）
elements_zh.where: 上海某数据中心
elements_zh.what: 违规安装并抵押禁售级AI加速芯片GB200/GB300系列
elements_zh.why: 绕过美方针对高端算力芯片的对华出口管制措施

elements_en.who: Shanghai Shuoyao, Shanghai Kezhan, Megaspeed, Nvidia, Gigabyte
elements_en.what: Illegal deployment and collateralization of sanctioned Blackwell-series chips
elements_en.why: Circumvention of US export control regulations on high-end AI compute

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件揭示了复杂的多层转运机制已形成针对算力封锁的“灰色通径”，即便面对严格的海关与出口管制，通过第三方保修数据库与金融抵押关联仍能暴露出黑市物流路径。这不仅挑战了英伟达自身的合规审核体系，更将倒逼美国监管机构进一步收紧对台湾代工厂及东南亚中转节点的直接制裁，未来算力供应链的审计颗粒度将从企业实体转向具体的设备序列号追溯。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the emergence of sophisticated grey-market channels for circumventing compute blockades, bypassing regulatory scrutiny through multi-layered transit. It exposes the fragility of current export compliance, likely triggering tighter US regulatory pressure on Taiwanese foundries and Southeast Asian intermediaries, shifting audit granularities from corporate entities to individual hardware serial number tracking.

article_content_zh:
在这一点上，这并不奇怪，但需要郑重声明：两家中国公司在上海数据中心安装了英伟达强大的 Blackwell 芯片，该数据中心与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有关，爱丽丝·黄与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 有染。详细信息来自向中国监管机构提交并经彭博社审阅的文件。

文件显示，上海硕耀提供了 GB300-NVL72 机架作为抵押品，从上海创新银行获得了 9600 万元人民币（1400 万美元）的贷款，而第二家公司上海科展则在贷款文件中列出了同一地点的 GB200 服务器。未经美国许可，禁止向中国出口这些芯片。彭博社通过公共保修数据库中的序列号将该机架追溯到台湾制造商技嘉。

上海硕耀与新加坡的 Megaspeed 关系密切。特朗普政府本月因涉嫌芯片走私而将 Megaspeed 列入美国贸易黑名单。 Alice Huang 于 2023 年创立了 Megaspeed，四天内 Nvidia 就批准其成为合作伙伴。据彭博社报道，它后来成为英伟达在东南亚最大的客户。

据报道，美国新收紧的出口规则和反扩散措施已经让中国人工智能初创企业感到头疼。

title: European Workers’ AI Use on Par With That of US Peers, ECB Says
title_en: European Workers’ AI Use on Par With That of US Peers, ECB Says

inline_images.caption: Credit: Jack_the_sparow via Shutterstock
inline_images.alt: Credit: Jack_the_sparow via Shutterstock

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Europe is falling behind the US on AI use at work, and the main reason is not technology, according to a new report.The report from Sifted, sponsored by London Business School, says Europe has an organisational gap rather than a tech gap. Firms struggle with skills, management, trust and the cost of fitting AI into how they work.

“Doing a fun thing with ChatGPT and running your whole business on AI are two very different things,” Celonis executive Rupal Karia told Sifted.

About 43% of US workers used AI for their jobs in early 2026, against 32% across Europe, a St Louis Fed analysis found. US workers spent more than three times as many work hours using AI as those in Germany, France and Italy.

Only 20% of EU firms use AI at all, up from 13.5% a year earlier, Eurostat data shows. Denmark leads at 42%, while Romania sits at 5.2%.

Even where firms use AI, few have gone all in. The report cites McKinsey data showing 88% of organisations use AI somewhere, but just 7% have fully scaled it.

“There is no inherent roadblock to Europe leading in AI adoption,” said Nicos Savva, a professor at London Business School.

Karia, who runs northern Europe and the Middle East for German software firm Celonis, said many companies had underestimated the human side of change. Adoption has been slower than expected, he added.

Executives cited unreliable outputs, cyber risk and running costs as reasons for caution. Some firms are now limiting AI use as they weigh cost against benefit, LBS deputy dean Gary Dushnitsky told Sifted.

Returns are also hard to find. The report cites research from marketing firm Whito showing 75% of firms using AI see productivity gains, but only 12% see more revenue.

Paul Maker, technology chief at UK firm Aiimi, put it bluntly.

“Everyone’s been given a hammer and now they’re desperately looking for nails,” he said.

Fear of job losses is also slowing take-up, said LBS professor Lynda Gratton.

“If you feel AI will destroy your work, then you won’t want to adopt it,” she said.

LBS dean Sergei Guriev warned that rushing could backfire if people stop learning to think for themselves. A quick start, he said, could undermine longer-term adoption.

Some of the delay is normal. The report cites Goldman Sachs economist Elsie Peng, who found the PC took about 15 years to show up in productivity data.

Adoption is fastest in law and banking. More than 85% of banks supervised by the European Central Bank now use AI, the report says.

Belgian startup Oper built an AI agent to check mortgage paperwork for underwriter Creafin. It is named after Herman Verdoodt, a Creafin credit technician, who said his team spends far more time fixing data than writing mortgages.

Factories are slower. Many cannot shut down for days to rewire their systems, said Dan Hobbs, chief executive of Protex AI, an intelligence platform for operations and safety leaders.

The report argues Europe should not try to copy the US on frontier models. More than 75% of advanced AI computing power sits in the US, against less than 4% in Europe, it says.

Instead, it points to startups that place engineers inside client firms, much like Palantir does. It also highlights AI roll-ups, where startups such as Dwelly buy traditional businesses and rebuild them around AI.

Some European AI firms are also choosing to stay independent. UK avatar startup Synthesia reportedly turned down a $3bn offer from Adobe last year, the report notes.

Dushnitsky said Europe’s pitch could rest on control and resilience rather than price.

“Perhaps the European value proposition should be built around resilience, confidentiality and privacy,” he said.

That echoes founders who want smarter AI rules, not fewer. The report concludes that good rules can speed adoption by giving firms the confidence to try.

title_zh: 欧洲企业AI应用滞后：组织管理短板大于技术差距
summary_zh: 欧洲央行与伦敦商学院调研显示，欧洲企业AI渗透率远低于美国，核心瓶颈在于组织变革与人才能力，而非技术基础匮乏

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 欧洲央行与伦敦商学院联合报告指出，尽管欧洲技术储备尚可，但仅20%的欧盟企业实现AI应用，远低于美国约43%的员工使用率。企业在AI部署中面临管理流程适配、人才技能匮乏及投资回报率不明确的重重阻碍，导致目前呈现出“有工具但缺场景”的被动局面。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: A report by the European Central Bank and London Business School reveals that while technical potential exists, only 20% of EU firms have adopted AI, compared to 43% of US employees. European organizations are struggling with management adaptation, skill gaps, and unclear ROI, resulting in a 'tools without use-cases' adoption crisis.

elements_zh.where: 欧盟境内企业数字化转型环境

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 欧洲市场的AI困境本质是资本配置与劳动力结构的高度刚性，导致AI从工具转化为生产力时产生的边际效应极低。这种组织级摩擦力将持续拉大欧美科技企业的营运绩效差距，迫使欧洲企业在垂直行业应用上必须寻找差异化路径，而非盲目复刻美国通用型AI应用。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The European AI dilemma is rooted in rigid capital allocation and labor structures, leading to negligible marginal productivity gains. This organizational friction will continue to widen the performance gap between US and European firms, forcing the latter to prioritize vertical-specific AI strategies over generalist implementations.

This organizational friction will continue to widen the performance gap between US and European firms, forcing the latter to prioritize vertical-specific AI strategies over generalist implementations.

article_content_zh:
一份新报告显示，欧洲在工作中使用人工智能方面落后于美国，主要原因不是技术。伦敦商学院赞助的 Sifted 报告称，欧洲存在组织差距，而不是技术差距。公司在技能、管理、信任以及将人工智能融入其工作方式的成本方面陷入困境。

“使用 ChatGPT 做一件有趣的事情和在人工智能上运行整个业务是两件截然不同的事情，”Celonis 高管 Rupal Karia 告诉 Sifted。

圣路易斯联储的一项分析发现，2026 年初，约 43% 的美国工人在工作中使用人工智能，而欧洲的这一比例为 32%。美国工人使用人工智能的工作时间是德国、法国和意大利工人的三倍多。

欧盟统计局的数据显示，只有 20% 的欧盟公司使用人工智能，高于一年前的 13.5%。丹麦以 42% 领先，罗马尼亚则为 5.2%。

即使在使用人工智能的公司中，也很少有人全力以赴。该报告引用了麦肯锡的数据，显示 88% 的组织在某些地方使用人工智能，但只有 7% 的组织完全扩展了它。

伦敦商学院教授尼科斯·萨瓦 (Nicos Savva) 表示：“欧洲在人工智能应用方面处于领先地位并没有固有的障碍。”

德国软件公司 Celonis 负责北欧和中东业务的卡里亚表示，许多公司低估了变革中人性化的一面。他补充说，采用速度比预期要慢。

高管们将不可靠的产出、网络风险和运营成本作为谨慎的理由。伦敦商学院副院长加里·杜什尼茨基 (Gary Dushnitsky) 告诉 Sifted，一些公司现在正在限制人工智能的使用，因为他们会权衡成本与收益。

回报也很难找到。该报告援引营销公司 Whito 的研究显示，75% 使用人工智能的公司看到了生产力的提高，但只有 12% 的公司看到了收入的增加。

英国公司 Aiimi 的技术主管保罗·梅克 (Paul Maker) 直言不讳地说。

“每个人都被赋予了一把锤子，现在他们正在拼命寻找钉子，”他说。

伦敦商学院教授琳达·格拉顿 (Lynda Gratton) 表示，对失业的担忧也导致了就业放缓。

“如果你觉得人工智能会毁掉你的工作，那么你就不会想采用它，”她说。

伦敦商学院院长谢尔盖·古里耶夫警告说，如果人们停止学习独立思考，匆忙可能会适得其反。他说，快速启动可能会损害长期采用。

title: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
title_en: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
AI pioneer Yann LeCun doesn't believe language models alone will lead to human-like intelligence. With his JEPA architecture, he is pursuing machines that model cause and effect and plan their actions in advance. Three new studies show how the pieces of this project fit together and where physics still sets limits.

In late 2025, Yann LeCun left Meta after shaping its AI research for 12 years. He cited the company's growing focus on large language models as one reason, then co-founded the Paris startup AMI Labs and raised more than $1 billion. While much of the tech industry trains increasingly large chatbots, LeCun is focusing on systems for robotics, industry, and wearable devices intended to operate in the physical world.

title: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform, report says
title_en: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform, report says
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud platform. Reuters reports that attackers penetrated Cloud One, the Air Force's central cloud infrastructure, potentially exposing sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data. The breach was discovered last month during routine system upgrades.

According to one source, the attackers exploited a software vulnerability to gain access to the platform's control plane. Cloud One has pooled cloud resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet since 2017, running applications that include air defense radar and munitions management. In response, the Air Force paused migration of additional applications, blocked updates, and revoked administrator privileges. US Cyber Command is assessing the damage.

The breach comes amid growing concern about AI-powered attacks, as AI models can rapidly identify vulnerabilities across large cloud networks. At least six other cyber incidents have hit US government agencies recently, and Microsoft's cybersecurity division reported widespread use of the AI tool ARTEX. Who carried out the attack and whether any data was exfiltrated remain unknown.

title: OpenAI is building "Athena"data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork
title_en: OpenAI is building "Athena"data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
OpenAI is building a data management platform codenamed "Athena"to make its AI agents more accurate when working with business data. Athena resembles a semantic layer, software that provides consistent definitions for business metrics such as revenue and customer count, The Information reports.

The report says at least one customer found that ChatGPT Work's data analysis agent, launched last fall, wasn't accurate enough. The idea is to give agents the context they need so they guess less. A person familiar with the plans says OpenAI is using Athena to build agents that collect, document, and update business rules, so other agents don't have to start from scratch every time. Data platforms such as Snowflake and Databricks already offer their own semantic layers.

Athena could be an effort to build a stronger competitive advantage, since the report says it's harder to switch semantic layer providers than to switch AI models. The platform is still in early development, and OpenAI hasn't shared a timeline or pricing.

OpenAI 正在构建一个代号为“Athena”的数据管理平台，以使其人工智能代理在处理业务数据时更加准确。据 The Information 报道，Athena 类似于一个语义层软件，为收入和客户数量等业务指标提供一致的定义。

报告称，至少一名客户发现去年秋天推出的 ChatGPT Work 数据分析代理不够准确。这个想法是为代理提供他们需要的上下文，以便他们减少猜测。一位熟悉该计划的人士表示，OpenAI 正在使用 Athena 来构建收集、记录和更新业务规则的代理，因此其他代理不必每次都从头开始。 Snowflake 和 Databricks 等数据平台已经提供了自己的语义层。

Athena 可能是为了建立更强大的竞争优势而做出的努力，因为报告称更换语义层提供商比更换人工智能模型更难。该平台仍处于早期开发阶段，OpenAI 尚未透露时间表或定价。

title: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
title_en: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
Days after GTA 6's record console launch, numerous projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build to PC. AI coding agents are dramatically speeding up reverse engineering and shaking up Rockstar's business model.

A core pillar of Rockstar's business strategy is under pressure just days after Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale. The game had a historic debut on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S with an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day revenue. But a day later, the hacking group CyberLeek distributed a stolen Xbox image of the game, and the executable itself leaked a few days ago.

Since then, a fast-moving scene of developers and modders has sprung up to get the game running on Windows through reverse engineering, compatibility layers, and recompilation. AI coding tools like Anthropic's Claude Code are driving that pace. Instead of spending months manually analyzing code and rebuilding console functions, developers are handing off much of the porting work to AI agents. One group even livestreamed the process.

### One GTA 6 PC port passes 90 percent progress as early multiplayer surfaces within days

A tracking platform lists 40 active projects less than four days after the executable leaked. Nearly half of them can boot the game on PC. On the platform's own rating scale, the furthest project is more than 90 percent of the way to a playable PC build.

Some projects are trying to add features including native ray-traced lighting. Gameplay footage of an unofficial PC multiplayer mode surfaced on November 26, and the platform's operator verified it. It shows multiple players moving through the game world with vehicles and voice chat at 25 to 30 frames per second. GTA 6 has officially launched only as a single-player title, and an online mode has no release date yet.

There is no finished PC version ready for the general public yet. The most stable builds are incomplete, circulate in closed groups, or require substantial technical know-how. Even so, this pace breaks a decades-old assumption in the gaming industry. Console emulators often took years after a hardware generation launched, and brand-new blockbusters rarely ran on them soon after release.

### Unofficial PC ports threaten Rockstar's delayed launches and online business

Rockstar and parent company Take-Two face more than a technical nuisance. The studio traditionally releases its flagship games on consoles first and follows with PC versions much later. GTA V took about 19 months to reach PC, and Red Dead Redemption 2 took about a year. So far, there is no official PC release date for GTA 6. That approach cuts optimization work at launch and encourages impatient players to buy the game twice.

The online business is an even bigger vulnerability. Nearly 80 percent of Take-Two's total revenue in fiscal year 2026 came from microtransactions and recurring digital spending. GTA Online alone has brought in more than $5 billion so far. A free, community-run PC multiplayer mode targets that financial backbone before Rockstar has even launched its own version.

Past experience with FiveM for GTA V shows how nervous Take-Two is about parallel worlds like this. In 2015, the company cracked down hard on the alternative multiplayer and roleplay mod. It banned developer accounts and, according to some developers, even sent private investigators to the creators' homes to shut down the project.

FiveM grew into the core of the roleplay scene despite that pushback and at times drew more concurrent players on Steam than the base game. Only then did Rockstar reverse course and acquire the development team Cfx.re in August 2023. Back then, the community needed years to build a parallel ecosystem like that. For GTA 6, an early PC multiplayer prototype has surfaced just a week after launch.

A trend that hit other parts of the software market earlier this year has now reached AAA gaming. In early 2026, the SaaSpocalypse (Link nicht geprüft) rattled stock markets as capable AI coding agents fueled fears that classic subscription software could be rebuilt far more cheaply. Software stocks lost about $285 billion in market value within 48 hours in February alone. At one point the losses reached as much as $1 trillion. With GTA 6, AI isn't building a rival game from scratch. Instead, it is tearing down the moat built from time and technical effort that has protected traditional business models so far.

Ports built on stolen game files are clearly illegal. Take-Two has filed a DMCA takedown on GitHub that removed an initial project and more than 3,000 forks. But that cat-and-mouse game is nearly impossible to win through legal action. Other projects stay online or move into private channels. Even if commercial AI providers tighten their safety filters and ban users, capable open-source models are available to run locally with no central oversight.

article_content_zh:
GTA 6 创纪录的主机发布几天后，众多项目正在努力将泄露的 Xbox 版本移植到 PC 上。 AI 编码代理正在极大地加速逆向工程并改变 Rockstar 的商业模式。

《侠盗猎车手 VI》发售几天后，Rockstar 业务战略的核心支柱就面临压力。该游戏在 PlayStation 5 和 Xbox Series X|S 上历史性地首次亮相，首日收入估计为 37.9 亿美元。但一天后，黑客组织 Cyber​​Leek 分发了该游戏被盗的 Xbox 映像，而可执行文件本身也在几天前泄露了。

从那时起，开发者和改装者迅速崛起，通过逆向工程、兼容层和重新编译让游戏在 Windows 上运行。 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 等人工智能编码工具正在推动这一步伐。开发人员不再花费数月时间手动分析代码和重建控制台功能，而是将大部分移植工作交给人工智能代理。一组甚至直播了整个过程。

### GTA 6 PC 移植版进度已达 90%，早期多人游戏在几天之内就已上线

可执行文件泄露后不到四天，跟踪平台就列出了 40 个活跃项目。其中近一半可以在PC上启动游戏。根据该平台自身的评级标准，最远的项目已达到可玩 PC 版本的 90% 以上。

一些项目正在尝试添加包括原生光线追踪照明在内的功能。非官方 PC 多人游戏模式的游戏片段于 11 月 26 日浮出水面，平台运营商对此进行了验证。它展示了多个玩家以每秒 25 到 30 帧的速度驾驶车辆和语音聊天在游戏世界中移动。 GTA 6 仅作为单人游戏正式推出，在线模式尚未确定发布日期。

目前还没有为公众准备好完整的 PC 版本。最稳定的构建是不完整的，在封闭的群体中流通，或者需要大量的技术知识。即便如此，这一速度还是打破了游戏行业数十年的假设。控制台模拟器通常在一代硬件推出后需要数年时间，而全新的大片很少在发布后不久就在其上运行。

### 非官方 PC 端口威胁 Rockstar 的延迟发布和在线业务

Rockstar 和母公司 Take-Two 面临的不仅仅是技术问题。该工作室传统上首先在游戏机上发布其旗舰游戏，然后再发布 PC 版本。 GTA V 花了大约 19 个月才登陆 PC，而 Red Dead Redemption 2 则花了大约一年的时间。到目前为止，GTA 6 还没有正式的 PC 发布日期。这种方法减少了发布时的优化工作，并鼓励不耐烦的玩家两次购买游戏。

在线业务是一个更大的漏洞。 Take-Two 2026 财年总收入的近 80% 来自微交易和经常性数字支出。迄今为止，仅《GTA Online》就带来了超过 50 亿美元的收入。在 Rockstar 推出自己的版本之前，一款由社区运行的免费 PC 多人游戏模式就瞄准了金融支柱。

FiveM 过去在 GTA V 中的经验表明 Take-Two 对于这样的平行世界有多么紧张。 2015年，该公司严厉打击了另类多人游戏和角色扮演模组。据一些开发商称，它禁止了开发者帐户，甚至派私人调查员到创作者家中关闭该项目。

尽管存在阻力，FiveM 仍成长为角色扮演场景的核心，有时在 Steam 上吸引的并发玩家数量比基础游戏还要多。直到那时，Rockstar 才扭转了局面，并于 2023 年 8 月收购了开发团队 Cfx.re。当时，社区需要数年时间才能建立这样的并行生态系统。 GTA 6 的早期 PC 多人游戏原型在发布一周后就已浮出水面。

今年早些时候席卷软件市场其他部分的这一趋势现已发展到 AAA 级游戏。 2026 年初，SaaSpocalypse（Link nicht geprüft）震惊了股市，因为强大的人工智能编码代理引发了人们对经典订阅软件可以以更便宜的价格重建的担忧。仅 2 月份软件股的市值就在 48 小时内蒸发了约 2850 亿美元。损失一度高达 1 万亿美元。在《GTA 6》中，人工智能并没有从头开始构建一款竞争对手的游戏。相反，它正在拆除迄今为止保护传统商业模式的时间和技术努力所建立的护城河。

基于被盗游戏文件构建的端口显然是非法的。 Take-Two 已在 GitHub 上提交了 DMCA 删除申请，删除了一个初始项目和 3,000 多个分支。但这场猫捉老鼠的游戏几乎不可能通过法律诉讼获胜。其他项目留在网上或进入私人渠道。即使商业人工智能提供商收紧安全过滤器并禁止用户，有能力的开源模型也可以在没有中央监督的情况下在本地运行。

title: The CMA says Meta made changes to Muse's ToS in the UK to reflect the country's consumer law; the terms give users far more protections than in the US (Joseph Bambridge/Politico)
title_en: The CMA says Meta made changes to Muse's ToS in the UK to reflect the country's consumer law; the terms give users far more protections than in the US (Joseph Bambridge/Politico)

inline_images.caption: This photograph shows the Meta's booth during the World Economic Forum annual meeting in Davos on January 19, 2026. | Ina Fassbender/AFP via Getty Images
inline_images.alt: This photograph shows the Meta's booth during the World Economic Forum annual meeting in Davos on Ja

author: Politico
article_content:
LONDON — Meta will be on the hook for more of Muse’s mistakes in the U.K. than in the U.S., according to a comparison of the AI agent's fine print in both countries by POLITICO.

The findings indicate the tech giant was willing to commit to meeting higher liability standards to gain access to the U.K. market, and show that tech companies and users will face different liability and consumer law rules as personal AI agents roll out globally.

Muse, an AI agent that takes actions on users’ behalf, was introduced in the U.K. this week — several months after its launch in the U.S. — following talks with British regulators.

Meta declined to comment on detailed regulatory discussions. It says Muse can lend a “helping hand” on everything from chasing a refund and renewing car insurance to doing the Christmas shopping — but publicly acknowledges the tool “can and will still make mistakes.”

The AI agent, which is the first to be launched by a Big Tech company in the U.K., can also make payments on behalf of users with their approval.

They absolve Meta of liability “to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law” for any losses or damages caused by Muse “taking any unintended, erroneous or unauthorized action.”

In the U.K. there is no financial cap and a narrower list of exceptions to Meta’s liability applies only where the company has “acted with reasonable skill and care / professional diligence.”

Under U.K. consumer law, this standard is automatically implied into contracts for services between a business and a consumer. How U.K. consumers would fare in practice when seeking redress for any problems caused by personal AI agents is yet to be tested in court.

Since its debut in the U.S., Meta staffers have reportedly raised concerns internally about “undesired actions” by the agent, from accessing encrypted messages to supplying bogus information about purchases. (A Meta spokesperson said these were “isolated incidents.”)

The CMA said it expects Muse to be the first of many personal AI agents to come to the U.K. and has invited users to report any issues they experience with personal AI agents.

Other British regulators are also watching closely. The Financial Conduct Authority said in a statement that as AI agents become capable of making transactions, payments and investment decisions, companies developing and deploying them “must understand which activities require authorisation and where regulatory requirements may apply.”

It also highlighted that a broad Consumer Duty could also apply to regulated firms’ use of AI agents, and that all companies must decide carefully whether they should accept payments initiated by an agent.

As well as contract law, consumer law, negligence and sector-specific regulation, users of AI agents may soon also be able to seek redress through product liability laws.

The Law Commission is reviewing the U.K.’s product liability laws and has proposed extending the definition to software, including AI. Doing so could make firms developing or deploying AI agents strictly liable for certain types of harm they cause.

Health minister James Frith described the extension of Palantir’s NHS contract as “a bridge, not the destination.”

Advice comes after the U.K. government vowed to take a tougher approach than Australia to enforcing its own ban.

The Mayor’s office blocked a £50 million Met Police contract with Palantir in June.

The government believes the clauses, common in tech and financial firms, undermine innovation.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Meta正式在英国市场推出AI代理Muse，相较于美国版本，英国版服务条款（ToS）大幅削减了免责空间，明确公司在发生系统错误或未经授权操作时需承担法律责任。此举是Meta为进入英国市场而进行的合规妥协，反映出全球大模型部署正面临各司法管辖区日益严峻的消费者权益保护差异。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Meta launched its AI agent Muse in the UK with revised terms of service, significantly reducing liability waivers compared to the US version to comply with local consumer protection laws. This strategic move highlights the growing regulatory friction as Big Tech companies adapt global AI deployment to heterogeneous legal frameworks.

elements_zh.who: Meta（跨国科技巨头），英国竞争与市场管理局（CMA）
elements_zh.where: 英国市场
elements_zh.what: 修改AI代理Muse服务条款，剔除部分损害赔偿免责限制，承诺在专业尽职范围内承担责任
elements_zh.why: 满足英国更严格的消费者法律准入要求，并应对监管机构对AI代理自主交易风险的担忧

elements_en.who: Meta, UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA)
elements_en.what: Revised ToS for Muse, removing broad liability shields and accepting professional diligence standards
elements_en.why: To meet stringent UK consumer law requirements and address regulatory scrutiny over autonomous agent risks

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此案例标志着全球AI代理商业化进入“属地合规时代”，头部厂商此前通过格式合同规避模型幻觉风险的策略正受到区域性法律挑战。随着金融与消费场景的渗透，AI代理的法律人格与赔偿边界将成为决定其能否规模化落地的核心技术及成本变量。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This case signals the beginning of the 'territorial compliance era' for AI agents, where standard liability-shielding contracts are increasingly challenged by regional consumer laws. As agents penetrate financial and commercial sectors, legal accountability will become a critical variable influencing the scalability and operational cost of foundation models.

article_content_zh:
伦敦——根据 POLITICO 对 Muse 在英国和美国的细则进行的比较，Meta 将在英国承担比在美国更多的 Muse 错误。

调查结果表明，这家科技巨头愿意承诺满足更高的责任标准以进入英国市场，并表明随着个人人工智能代理在全球范围内推广，科技公司和用户将面临不同的责任和消费者法规则。

Muse 是一款代表用户采取行动的人工智能代理，在与英国监管机构进行谈判后，在美国推出几个月后，本周在英国推出。

Meta 拒绝就详细的监管讨论发表评论。该公司表示，Muse 可以在从退款、续保汽车保险到圣诞购物等所有事情上伸出“帮助之手”，但公开承认该工具“可能而且仍然会犯错误”。

该人工智能代理是英国大型科技公司首次推出的人工智能代理，经用户批准后还可以代表用户进行付款。

对于 Muse“采取任何非故意、错误或未经授权的行动”造成的任何损失或损害，他们“在适用法律允许的最大范围内”免除 Meta 的责任。

在英国，Meta 的责任没有财务上限，并且只有在公司“以合理的技能和谨慎/专业勤勉行事”的情况下才适用。

根据英国消费者法，该标准自动隐含在企业与消费者之间的服务合同中。英国消费者在为个人人工智能代理造成的任何问题寻求补救时实际上会如何表现，还有待法庭检验。

据报道，自在美国首次亮相以来，Meta 工作人员在内部对代理商的“不良行为”表示担忧，从访问加密消息到提供虚假的购买信息。 （Meta 发言人表示，这些都是“孤立事件”。）

CMA 表示，预计 Muse 将成为众多个人人工智能代理中第一个来到英国的，并邀请用户报告他们在使用个人人工智能代理时遇到的任何问题。

其他英国监管机构也在密切关注。英国金融行为监管局在一份声明中表示，随着人工智能代理能够进行交易、支付和投资决策，开发和部署它们的公司“必须了解哪些活动需要授权以及哪些领域可能适用监管要求”。

它还强调，广泛的消费者责任也适用于受监管公司对人工智能代理的使用，所有公司都必须仔细决定是否应该接受代理发起的付款。

除了合同法、消费者法、玩忽职守法和特定行业法规外，人工智能代理的用户可能很快也能够通过产品责任法寻求补救。

法律委员会正在审查英国的产品责任法，并提议将该定义扩展到包括人工智能在内的软件。这样做可能会使开发或部署人工智能代理的公司对它们造成的某些类型的伤害负严格责任。

title: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs as it pivots to AI
title_en: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs as it pivots to AI
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
SAP is preparing to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as part of a sweeping AI restructuring, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. That's at least nine percent of the company's global workforce of more than 110,000. Every department has been asked to identify savings, with product development, engineering, and sales taking the biggest hit. The final number hasn't been set and could change after negotiations with employee representatives.

In Germany, where about a quarter of SAP's workforce is based, a job guarantee runs through 2028. CEO Christian Klein wants to embed AI tools across SAP's product lineup. The company already cut roughly 10,000 jobs in 2024. Its competitors are making similar moves. Oracle slashed 21,000 positions over twelve months, and Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees. SAP declined to comment on the potential cuts, saying only that it reviews its organizational structure on an ongoing basis. The company recently announced a partnership with Mistral AI and has acquired several startups.

title: Trump Tried to Cripple Huawei. Now It Is Central to China’s A.I. Push.

author: Keith Bradsher and Adam Satariano
article_content:
At Huawei Technologies’ headquarters in Shenzhen, China, a palatial corridor gleams with gold ceilings and elaborate frescoes of Russian aristocrats on galloping horses. It bears the name of the American president who tried to bring the Chinese technology giant to its knees.

Huawei executives call it the “Trump Corridor,” a pointed reference to President Trump’s campaign during his first term to drive the company out of global wireless networks and cut off its access to advanced chips.

The name is a gesture of defiance. Having survived punishing American sanctions, Huawei is determined to prove that Washington cannot dictate its future. That resolve faces a new test after the company was convicted this week in an American court of stealing trade secrets.

In 2019, Mr. Trump’s crackdown threatened Huawei’s survival, just as it had become a world leader in telecommunications and consumer devices. Seven years later, Huawei is central to Beijing’s ambitions to challenge the United States in artificial intelligence. Its chips are the closest thing China has to an answer to Nvidia's advanced semiconductors.

Last month, in a vaulted conference room beyond the corridor, Ren Zhengfei, Huawei’s 82-year-old founder and chief executive, credited the American president with forcing Huawei and China into a new era of self-reliance.

“Pass on our thanks to him, and also share the story of the Trump Corridor as well,” Mr. Ren said in an interview.

After the U.S. crackdown, he said, Huawei cemented its identity as “a company of our own country.”

Huawei’s resurgence illustrates a paradox in Washington’s efforts to contain China’s technological rise. The company was among the first targets of export restrictions that became a policy blueprint. American restrictions have slowed China’s advances, but they have also galvanized a national effort to dismantle the technological dependencies that gave Washington leverage.

On Tuesday, after an 11-week trial, a federal jury found Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets from American companies and evading sanctions against Iran. Huawei said the verdicts were “without legal or factual merit.”

As its American ties unravel, Huawei is becoming more indispensable to China. This month, the Trump administration announced plans to block Chinese companies from accessing advanced A.I. chips through overseas data centers, closing one of the last routes to Nvidia’s most powerful semiconductors.

The move comes amid turmoil at Nvidia. Jensen Huang, its chief executive, resigned two weeks ago following allegations of an affair with an executive at the Singaporean data center company Megaspeed. U.S. intelligence officials believe the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with a Chinese Ministry of State Security officer during their relationship. Beijing has denied spying.

This week, Mr. Huang returned as chief executive after a pressure campaign by President Trump, who said the reversal was necessary to ensure the “success and prosperity” of Nvidia and the American economy.

Before the upheaval at Nvidia, Mr. Ren acknowledged the challenge of building an advanced semiconductor supply chain but predicted that China would eventually surpass the United States.

“It’s just a matter of time,” he said.

Huawei’s annual spending on research and development now exceeds $27 billion. Its Ascend processors have become China’s leading alternative to Nvidia’s A.I. chips. Beyond designing chips, it is assembling the infrastructure to become one of the world’s biggest chip makers.

It has brought together suppliers, government-backed factories and equipment makers, built data centers and worked with Chinese A.I. companies, including DeepSeek, to adapt their models to its chips.

The technological gulf remains enormous. Huawei’s chips are expected to deliver less than 4 percent of Nvidia’s A.I. computing power this year, and Huawei is unlikely to match Nvidia’s current output until around 2030, according to the research firm Epoch AI.

“Huawei is pulling on every single lever available to them and they are pulling hard,” said Venkat Somala, an analyst with Epoch AI, who recently published a report on the company. “The question is, will it be enough?”

When Mr. Trump approved sweeping restrictions on Huawei in his first term, many in his administration believed they could destroy the company, which officials feared was aiding China’s military.

“We thought this could be a death blow,” said Liza Tobin, who worked on China policy on the National Security Council at the time. “It hobbled them and broke their leg and slowed them down. But now they have regrouped.”

Xi Jinping, China’s leader, responded by vowing to build a domestic technology supply chain.

“It’s a new Long March now, and we must start all over again,” he said, invoking the Communist Party’s arduous retreat in the 1930s before its rise to power.

Before the crackdown, Huawei was deeply embedded in the global technology supply chain. It bought $2.5 billion worth of chips annually from Intel and was one of the largest customers of Oracle and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s leading chip maker, according to Huawei.

“After the U.S. sanctions, our pursuits have been survival first,” Mr. Ren said.

Mr. Ren knows something about survival. Growing up in one of China’s poorest provinces, he endured the great famine of the early 1960s. During the Cultural Revolution, his father, a schoolteacher, was denounced as a “capitalist roadster” and confined in a cow barn.

Mr. Ren joined the army, rose to become deputy director of a military-run research institute and founded Huawei after China disbanded the military’s construction corps in 1983.

The showdown with Washington has also been personal. In December 2018, Mr. Ren’s daughter, Meng Wanzhou, then Huawei’s chief financial officer, was arrested in Vancouver at the request of U.S. law enforcement. It was part of a case that culminated in this week’s guilty verdict against the company. She spent nearly three years under house arrest before a deal allowed her to return to China.

Huawei executives have seen a shift in Mr. Ren as a result of the U.S. campaign. “The U.S. government hasn’t yet realized that this move is turning someone who was most pro-American into someone who is anti-American,” said Gavin Gai, Huawei’s corporate strategy director, before clarifying that Mr. Ren is not anti-American.

Around 2021, Mr. Ren accelerated efforts to build a domestic semiconductor supply chain, working with China’s Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, known as SMIC, as well as research institutes and other domestic firms.

The biggest obstacle is manufacturing, not design. China still lacks the most sophisticated chip-making equipment, including lithography machines made by the Dutch company ASML that print microscopic circuit patterns onto silicon wafers.

Huawei says it can eventually rival Nvidia’s systems by linking many less powerful processors.

Liang Wenfeng, chief executive of DeepSeek, the Chinese start-up that stunned Silicon Valley with its inexpensive, powerful A.I. model, estimated Huawei’s technology was about two years behind Nvidia’s, according to excerpts from a leaked investor call published by Chinese media outlets.

Huawei may not need to match Nvidia’s technology to dominate the Chinese market. American restrictions and Beijing’s push for self-reliance are steering Chinese companies toward domestic suppliers.

Martin Lau, the president of Tencent, the Chinese internet giant, said losing access to advanced Nvidia chips “sets everyone back in China” in A.I. development. The priority now, he told investors, must be “speeding up the domestic supply chain.”

Beijing has reinforced that imperative by blocking imports of Nvidia chips and pressing Chinese companies to buy domestic alternatives. On Nov. 17, Nvidia announced that it was halting sales to China altogether.

Inside a Huawei factory in southern China, a hall stretching the length of one and a half football fields hums with a dozen smartphone assembly lines.

What is striking is how few people are there.

Each line employs nine workers in white lab coats and baseball caps, down from nearly 90 a dozen years ago. Robots occupy the workstations, while A.I.-powered cameras inspect production of each Mate 90 Pro smartphone, from soldering circuit boards to final assembly.

If a worker’s hands make the wrong movement, a computer sounds an alarm and prevents the phone from advancing.

China’s success in A.I. may depend less on building the most powerful models than on deploying the technology across its vast industrial economy.

While Silicon Valley races to develop systems capable of surpassing human intelligence, Huawei is championing Beijing’s “A.I. Plus” strategy, using the technology to improve productivity across industries. China already manufactures more goods than the United States, Germany, Japan, South Korea and Britain combined.

Across China, Huawei’s survival has become a lesson in withstanding American pressure. Mr. Ren said he still hoped the United States and China could repair their relationship.

However, “we have now established a complete chain that allows us to survive.”

article_content_zh:
在华为位于中国深圳的总部，富丽堂皇的走廊闪闪发光，金色的天花板和精美的俄罗斯贵族骑着骏马的壁画闪闪发光。它以试图让这家中国科技巨头屈服的美国总统的名字命名。

华为高管将其称为“特朗普走廊”，指的是特朗普总统在其第一个任期内发起的竞选活动，旨在将该公司赶出全球无线网络并切断其获得先进芯片的渠道。

这个名字是一种反抗的姿态。在经历了美国的惩罚性制裁后，华为决心证明华盛顿无法主宰其未来。在该公司本周在美国法院被判窃取商业机密罪后，这一决心面临着新的考验。

2019年，特朗普的打压威胁到了华为的生存，而此时华为已成为电信和消费设备领域的全球领导者。七年后，华为成为北京在人工智能领域挑战美国的野心的核心。它的芯片是中国最接近英伟达先进半导体的产品。

上个月，在走廊另一边的一间拱形会议室里，82岁的华为创始人兼首席执行官任正非称赞美国总统迫使华为和中国进入了一个自力更生的新时代。

“转达我们对他的感谢，也分享一下特朗普走廊的故事，”任正非在接受采访时说。

他说，在美国打压之后，华为巩固了其“我们自己国家的公司”的身份。

华为的复兴说明了华盛顿遏制中国技术崛起的努力的一个悖论。该公司是首批出口限制目标之一，并成为政策蓝图。美国的限制减缓了中国的进步，但也激发了全国性的努力，以消除给华盛顿带来影响力的技术依赖。

周二，经过 11 周的审判，联邦陪审团裁定华为犯有窃取美国公司商业机密和逃避对伊朗制裁的罪名。华为表示，这些判决“没有法律或事实依据”。

随着与美国关系的破裂，华为对中国变得越来越不可或缺。本月，特朗普政府宣布计划阻止中国公司获得先进的人工智能。通过海外数据中心生产芯片，关闭了通往英伟达最强大半导体的最后路线之一。

此举正值英伟达陷入混乱之际。该公司首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 因被指控与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的一名高管发生婚外情而于两周前辞职。美国情报官员认为，这名名叫爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)的女子在与中国国家安全部的一名官员交往期间曾有过接触。北京否认从事间谍活动。

本周，在特朗普总统施压后，黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官，特朗普表示，为了确保英伟达和美国经济的“成功和繁荣”，这一转变是必要的。

在英伟达发生剧变之前，任正非承认建立先进半导体供应链面临挑战，但预测中国最终将超越美国。

“这只是时间问题，”他说。

title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
title_en: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
author: Allison Johnson
article_content:
Aside from dealing with my calendar, there’s one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I’m about to miss the bus.

What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.

Google announced the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous.

I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that shows a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one big pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did.

I also made a widget that will display the words “Tut tut, looks like rain” whenever it’s raining. This is silly, and it accomplishes nothing except making me happy. I couldn’t think of anything clever it should say when there’s no rain, so it just says “No rain right now” otherwise. But I live in Seattle, so I’ll get a lot of mileage out of this widget.

The create-a-widget interface suggests a few ideas and categories, leaning on more practical uses like habit trackers and recipe inspiration. Fine, I’ll try something normal, I thought. I’m trying to get better about my daily mental health walk, so I had it make a widget for logging a week’s worth of walks. I was hoping for something visual that would trick my little monkey brain into keeping a streak going. Instead, I got something simply labeled “Log Walk” that triggers Gemini to add a walk to my calendar when I tap it. At least Gemini suggested the extra step of creating a checklist where I could mark off the days of the week as I completed my little walk.

It took me a minute to get my head around it, but many of the widgets are basically little prompt shortcuts for Gemini. You tap one, it pulls up the Gemini interface on your home screen, thinks for a while, then comes up with whatever you were asking for. The kinds of widgets you can make also seem to fit into some well-defined templates. You can create a widget that displays a countdown to a holiday or certain event on your calendar. You can show a recent score and upcoming game time for your favorite sports team. For anything more open ended, your widget will pull from Google search results (suggest a different three-ingredient cocktail recipe every day, for example) or prompt Gemini to figure it out for you. I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature. Fair, I guess.

"I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature"

That’s why my bus schedule widget didn’t really work out. I asked for a list of real-time arrivals; it gave me a tile that reads “Bus Arrivals” and uses Gemini to search for arrival times for the stop I specified. Gemini is helpful for some things but useless for this; it gives me a wordy response about how often the bus runs and when I might expect it to arrive based on the schedule. Not what I had in mind. On the bright side, my Jurassic Park quote widget had some words of wisdom for me: “Life, uh, finds a way.” That’ll do for now.

article_content_zh:
除了处理我的日历之外，我还想让人工智能做一件事：告诉我我是否会错过公共汽车。

我需要的是一个小部件。它需要告诉我我家附近公交车站的实时到达时间。在手机屏幕上点击打开正确的应用程序并选择我的车站会让我的速度减慢，足以错过公交车。我需要一目了然的信息，我希望 Android 的 vivi-coded widget 功能可以帮助我。令我失望的是，事实并非如此，但我仍然在烹饪其他小部件时度过了愉快的时光。

谷歌在春季 I/O 大会上宣布能够使用人工智能创建自定义小部件。它被称为“创建我的小部件”，是 Android 的“Gemini Intelligence”功能套件的一部分。它处于测试阶段，本月初才开始在 Pixel 手机上推出。我很兴奋。此功能不仅引发了诸如“什么是应用程序？”之类的诱人问题。和“应用程序在哪里？” ——我们在 The Verge 网络公司赖以生存的东西——它有可能帮助我让我的主屏幕变得荒谬。

我在 Pixel 11 Pro 上启动了它，并制作了我的前几个小部件，其中一个每小时都会显示《侏罗纪公园》中的不同台词——自然是原版电影，而不是任何续集。制作花了大约 20 秒，一切顺利。点击小部件会在 r/MovieQuotes 中打开一个线程，因此显然在幕后并没有太多软件魔法。但在我的主屏幕上读到“那是一大堆狗屎”这句话给我带来真正的快乐吗？确实如此。

我还制作了一个小部件，只要下雨，它就会显示“啧啧，看起来像下雨了”。这很愚蠢，除了让我快乐之外没有任何作用。我想不出当没有下雨时它应该说什么，所以它只是说“现在没有下雨”。但我住在西雅图，所以我会从这个小部件中获得很多好处。

创建小部件界面提出了一些想法和类别，倾向于更实际的用途，例如习惯跟踪器和食谱灵感。好吧，我会尝试一些正常的事情，我想。我正在努力改善日常步行的心理健康状况，因此我让它制作了一个小部件来记录一周的步行量。我希望有一些视觉效果能够欺骗我的小猴子大脑，让我继续保持连胜。相反，我得到了一些简单标记为“Log Walk”的东西，当我点击它时，它会触发 Gemini 将散步添加到我的日历中。至少双子座建议采取额外的步骤，创建一个清单，当我完成我的小步行时，我可以在其中标记出一周中的日子。

我花了一分钟才明白它的意思，但许多小部件对于 Gemini 来说基本上都是小快捷方式。你点击其中一个，它就会在你的主屏幕上调出 Gemini 界面，思考一会儿，然后出现你想要的任何内容。您可以制作的小部件类型似乎也适合一些定义良好的模板。您可以创建一个小部件来显示日历上的假期或特定事件的倒计时。您可以显示您最喜欢的运动队的最近得分和即将到来的比赛时间。对于任何更开放的事情，您的小部件将从 Google 搜索结果中提取（例如，每天建议不同的三种成分鸡尾酒配方）或提示 Gemini 为您找出答案。我希望迷你应用程序可以根据我的喜好进行定制，但这更像是一种一刀切的功能。公平，我想。

“我希望迷你应用程序可以根据我的喜好进行定制，但这更像是一种一刀切的功能”

A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.'s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman whose extramarital affair with CEO Jensen Huang is at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall and Bloomberg Intelligence's Matt Bloxham have the details.

Bloomberg News is finding that some of Nvidia's Blackwell chips did turn up at these Chinese sites linked to Megaspeed. And Lisa, we should say we had another headline on the terminal this morning, which is that Singapore's government right now is in active discussions with the US to retain access to advanced chips, considering it was one of those countries targeted last week in the Trump administration efforts to try to crack down on this alleged chip smuggling.

Tyler Kendall, thank you so much uh as always for that reporting. Matt Bloxham of Bloomberg Intelligence joins us now with more. Matt, a lot of questions here about who knew what when, which chips were sold to who, and what this means in terms of just the demand for some of the uh highest caliber chips from Nvidia. From your perspective, do we have a sense of how much immunity the company has as a result of President Trump having an influence over Jensen Huang coming back?

I mean that's certainly going to help in the short term, but I think with the Democrats' rising uh influence yet um and ability to kind of investigate things, I think this is going to be an issue that comes under more and more scrutiny as we go into 2027. You know, there'd already been for some time quite a lot of question marks about um whether Nvidia was doing as much as it could um to do due diligence on customers it was selling its chips to uh and minimizing the risk of them you're getting illicitly shipped on to other jurisdictions, including China. Uh and, you know, the these kind of latest revelations I think going to reopen those conversations. And I imagine it's going to be uh a line of questioning uh particularly at that uh public hearing next week in Washington. So, yeah, it's a kind of a big issue. And, you know, uh I think, you know, some analysts put Nvidia's exposure um to to kind of China directly and indirectly at maybe about 20% of sales. So, you know, there's potentially quite a lot at stake here.

Matt, with the trade negotiations going on with China into January and the Trump administration and Trump specifically taking a, I guess, nicer tone coming out of the APEC summit, I mean, is there just going to be a massive divergence here between Congress and the White House?

I think so, and, you know, it it's kind of a little bit um kind of difficult to kind of really understand, you know, where that the White House policy is. Actually kind of kind of fairly conciliatory and and friendly tone, but then, you know, kind of more tariffs and the restrictions we've got uh being put in place about um where you can export to in the Southeast Asia region. So, yeah, I think it's the the kind of uncertainty is going to add to the volatility in markets, I think.

两家中国公司在与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 连接的上海数据中心安装了英伟达公司 (Nvidia Corp.) 强大的 Blackwell 半导体，爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 与首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的婚外情是围绕这家美国芯片制造商的争议的核心。彭博社的泰勒·肯德尔和彭博资讯的马特·布洛克瑟姆掌握了详细信息。

彭博社发现，一些 Nvidia 的 Blackwell 芯片确实出现在这些与 Megaspeed 相关的中国网站上。丽莎，我们应该说，今天早上我们在终端上看到了另一个头条新闻，那就是新加坡政府目前正在与美国积极讨论以保留先进芯片的使用权，考虑到新加坡是上周特朗普政府试图打击这种所谓芯片走私的目标国家之一。

泰勒·肯德尔，非常感谢您一如既往的报道。彭博资讯 (Bloomberg Intelligence) 的马特·布洛克瑟姆 (Matt Bloxham) 现在加入我们，带来更多信息。马特，这里有很多问题，比如谁知道什么时候做什么，哪些芯片卖给了谁，以及这对 Nvidia 一些最高品质芯片的需求意味着什么。从您的角度来看，我们是否知道，由于特朗普总统对黄仁勋回归的影响力，公司有多大的免疫力？

我的意思是，这肯定会在短期内有所帮助，但我认为随着民主党的影响力不断上升，嗯，以及调查事情的能力，我认为随着我们进入 2027 年，这将成为一个受到越来越多审查的问题。你知道，一段时间以来，已经有很多问号了，嗯，英伟达是否正在尽其所能地对其销售芯片的客户进行尽职调查，并将风险降至最低。其中一些被非法运往其他司法管辖区，包括中国。呃，你知道，我认为这些最新的披露将重新开始这些对话。我想这将是一系列问题，特别是下周在华盛顿举行的公开听证会上。所以，是的，这是一个大问题。而且，你知道，呃，我想，你知道，一些分析师认为 Nvidia 的直接或间接风险敞口可能占销售额的 20% 左右。所以，你知道，这里可能存在很多风险。

马特，随着与中国的贸易谈判持续到一月，特朗普政府和特朗普在亚太经合组织峰会上特别采取了更好的语气，我的意思是，国会和白宫之间是否会出现巨大分歧？

我想是的，而且，你知道，真正理解白宫的政策有点困难。实际上是一种相当和解和友好的语气，但是，你知道，我们对东南亚地区可以出口的地方实施了更多的关税和限制。所以，是的，我认为这种不确定性会增加市场的波动性。

泰勒·肯德尔，非常感谢您一如既往的报道。彭博资讯 (Bloomberg Intelligence) 的马特·布洛克瑟姆 (Matt Bloxham) 现在加入我们，带来更多信息。马特，这里有很多问题，比如谁知道什么时候做什么，哪些芯片卖给了谁，以及这对 Nvidia 一些最高品质芯片的需求意味着什么。从您的角度来看，我们是否知道，由于特朗普总统对黄仁勋回归的影响力，公司有多大的免疫力？

我的意思是，这肯定会在短期内有所帮助，但我认为随着民主党的影响力不断上升，嗯，以及调查事情的能力，我认为随着我们进入 2027 年，这将成为一个受到越来越多审查的问题。你知道，一段时间以来，已经有很多问号了，嗯，英伟达是否正在尽其所能地对其销售芯片的客户进行尽职调查，并将风险降至最低。其中一些被非法运往其他司法管辖区，包括中国。呃，你知道，我认为这些最新的披露将重新开始这些对话。我想这将是一系列问题，特别是下周在华盛顿举行的公开听证会上。所以，是的，这是一个大问题。而且，你知道，呃，我想，你知道，一些分析师认为 Nvidia 的直接或间接风险敞口可能占销售额的 20% 左右。所以，你知道，这里可能存在很多风险。

马特，随着与中国的贸易谈判持续到一月，特朗普政府和特朗普在亚太经合组织峰会上特别采取了更好的语气，我的意思是，国会和白宫之间是否会出现巨大分歧？

我想是的，而且，你知道，真正理解白宫的政策有点困难。实际上是一种相当和解和友好的语气，但是，你知道，我们对东南亚地区可以出口的地方实施了更多的关税和限制。所以，是的，我认为这种不确定性会增加市场的波动性。

title: Meituan reports Q3 revenue up 21.6% YoY to ~$17.3B, above est., and an adjusted net profit of ~$285.1M, up from a ~$2.4B adjusted net loss (Ben Jiang/South China Morning Post)
title_en: Meituan reports Q3 revenue up 21.6% YoY to ~$17.3B, above est., and an adjusted net profit of ~$285.1M, up from a ~$2.4B adjusted net loss (Ben Jiang/South China Morning Post)

inline_images.caption: Meituan food delivery riders in Chengdu, Sichuan province, on December 5, 2025. Photo: Shutterstock Images
inline_images.alt: Meituan food delivery riders in Chengdu, Sichuan province, on December 5, 2025. Photo: Shutterstock

author: South China Morning Post
article_content:
Chinese food-delivery giant Meituan reported a second consecutive profitable quarter on Friday, as the company navigates intensifying competition from Alibaba Group Holding and JD.com while seeking to sustain its earnings recovery.

The Beijing-based firm’s adjusted net profit for the three months ended September came in at 1.9 billion yuan (US$285.1 million), slightly missing analysts’ expectations of 2.2 billion yuan, marking a second straight quarterly profit after the company returned to the black in the previous quarter.

This compared with an adjusted net loss of 16 billion yuan a year earlier, showing that China’s year-long food delivery price war has shown signs of abating after government intervention, even as Meituan still faces continued competition from Alibaba’s Taobao Instant Commerce and JD.com.

Total revenue for the three months ended September reached 115.6 billion yuan, a 21.6 per cent year-on-year increase, beating the average analyst estimate of 113.37 billion yuan compiled by Bloomberg, according to an earnings statement released on Friday.

Wang Xing, founder and chief executive of Meituan, said during an earnings call that the company had improved operational efficiency in the third quarter. He pledged to continue investing in the firm’s ecosystem and technology with a single goal in mind: delivering long-term value for both consumers and merchants.

The fierce on-demand delivery battle has increasingly shifted towards improving operational efficiency, retaining customers and expanding into the broader instant retail market, where platforms are competing for a larger share of consumers’ everyday spending.

The competition has also forced Meituan to balance market share defence against the need to restore margins after an aggressive subsidy campaign pushed the company into a three-quarter losing streak.

The Beijing-based firm swung back to profitability in the second quarter on an adjusted net profit of 2.5 billion yuan, as competition eased and the company scaled back subsidies while targeting higher-value customers.

Chief financial officer Chen Shaohui highlighted the company’s focus on marketing and operational efficiency during the earnings call, saying the company was well positioned in a food delivery market where competition had returned to a more rational level.

“Irrational spending and competition are not sustainable for the industry,” Chen said. “We believe everyone needs to calm down and refocus on user experience and quality of growth.”

Third quarter operating profit from its bread-and-butter local commerce business was 5.7 billion yuan, the earnings statement showed.

Meituan’s New Initiatives segment, which includes its overseas food-delivery operations and other emerging businesses, reported an operating loss of 1.31 billion yuan, slightly wider than the year earlier’s 1.28 billion yuan loss but narrower on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

Wang said Meituan’s food delivery business Keeta had further improved its profit margin in Hong Kong and continued to gain efficiency in the Middle East, making a profit in Saudi Arabia over the full quarter.

“We continue to believe taking on-demand retailing global is a very important growth opportunity for this company,” Chen added during the call.

Meituan’s Hong Kong-listed shares closed up 8.2 per cent at HK$67.85 on Friday ahead of the earnings announcement.

Alibaba owns the South China Morning Post.

title_zh: 美团第三季度营收增长21.6%至1156亿元
summary_zh: 美团发布第三季度财报，营收同比增21.6%至1156亿元，经调整净利润达19亿元，展现了价格战缓解后的盈利修复能力
article_content_zh:
中国食品配送巨头美团点评周五公布连续第二个季度盈利，该公司在应对来自阿里巴巴集团和京东的激烈竞争的同时，力求维持盈利复苏。

这家总部位于北京的公司截至 9 月份的三个月调整后净利润为 19 亿元人民币（合 2.851 亿美元），略低于分析师预期的 22 亿元人民币，这是该公司继上一季度扭亏为盈后连续第二个季度实现盈利。

与去年同期调整后净亏损160亿元相比，显示中国长达一年的外卖价格战在政府干预后已显示出减弱的迹象，尽管美团仍面临阿里巴巴旗下淘宝即时商城和京东的持续竞争。

根据周五发布的财报，截至9月份的三个月总收入达到1156亿元人民币，同比增长21.6%，超过彭博社编制的分析师平均预期1133.7亿元人民币。

美团创始人兼首席执行官王兴在财报电话会议上表示，该公司第三季度的运营效率有所提高。他承诺继续投资该公司的生态系统和技术，并牢记一个目标：为消费者和商家提供长期价值。

激烈的按需配送之战日益转向提高运营效率、留住客户以及扩展到更广泛的即时零售市场，在该市场中，平台正在争夺消费者日常支出的更大份额。

激烈的补贴活动导致美团点评连续三个季度亏损，竞争也迫使美团点评在捍卫市场份额和恢复利润之间取得平衡。

随着竞争的缓和以及公司削减补贴并瞄准高价值客户，这家总部位于北京的公司第二季度扭亏为盈，调整后净利润为人民币 25 亿元。

首席财务官陈少辉在财报电话会议上强调了公司对营销和运营效率的关注，并表示公司在竞争已回归到更加理性水平的外卖市场中处于有利地位。

“不合理的支出和竞争对于这个行业来说是不可持续的，”陈说。 “我们相信每个人都需要冷静下来，重新关注用户体验和增长质量。”

财报显示，其主要的本地商业业务第三季度营业利润为人民币 57 亿元。

美团新业务板块（包括海外外卖业务和其他新兴业务）的营业亏损为13.1亿元人民币，略高于去年同期的12.8亿元人民币，但环比收窄。

王先生表示，美团外卖业务Keeta在香港的利润率进一步提高，在中东地区持续提高效率，在沙特阿拉伯全季度实现盈利。

“我们仍然相信，将按需零售业务推向全球对于这家公司来说是一个非常重要的增长机会，”陈在电话会议中补充道。

title: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
title_en: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform

inline_images.caption: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform

author: Mike Stone and Raphael Satter
article_content:
WASHINGTON, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.

The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen.

In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities."

Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force's IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay or logistics and maintenance.

Among them are the Air Force's Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air defense radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 US Air Force locations around the world.

SAIC was the prime contractor for Cloud One until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force.

Cloud One is among the US military's biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources.

"A breach here is a big deal," one of the sources said.

Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the US military's cyber force, to assess the damage, one of the sources said.

Cyber Command did not respond to requests for comment.

The discovery of the hack led to a range of disruption. Two of the sources, along with a fourth person familiar with the matter, said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused.

Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked.

All five sources spoke on condition of anonymity.

One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. That person likened the control plane to a universal remote, as intruders in theory could leverage their access to check the operational status of military aircraft or the movement of spare parts, though it was unclear whether the hackers did so in this case.

Reuters could not identify the specific vulnerability exploited by the hackers.

News of the breach comes amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions, a particularly serious problem for cloud-based networks because of the ability of AI models to swiftly detect weaknesses across wide surface areas.

The US government already has been dealing with the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a recent leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department.

Cloud One has long been in the crosshairs of hackers.

In a 2023 commentary carried by the online publication FedScoop, Cloud One's leadership touted what they called a "100% success rate" in beating back what they said was a "staggering" number of attempts to penetrate the platform.

"There is no room for error when it comes to security," Cloud One's leadership wrote.

key_points_en: Key Development: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform

article_content_zh:
路透华盛顿11月27日 - 三名知情人士告诉路透社，黑客已经攻破了美国空军的旗舰云计算平台，此举可能会危及大量敏感的战术、人员和后勤数据。

两名知情人士表示，Cloud One 的入侵是在过去一个月左右的系统升级工作中发现的，并补充说这一发现导致了整个平台的中断。路透社无法确定黑客的身份、入侵的全部范围或是否有任何数据被盗。

美国空军在给路透社的一份声明中表示，“不会对特定网络和系统的安全态势、漏洞或运行状态发表评论。我们不断采取审慎措施来保护（空军）部门的信息、系统和任务能力。”

Cloud One 于 2017 年启动，旨在成为满足空军 IT 需求的一站式商店，结合了微软、亚马逊、甲骨文和 Alphabet 四大运营商的资源，为数十种应用程序提供支持，包括管理人员数据和薪酬或后勤和维护的应用程序。

其中包括空军的基于云的指挥与控制系统，该系统会整理来自北美各地的防空雷达和其他数据源，以及战区综合作战弹药系统，该系统会跟踪全球 200 多个美国空军基地的炸弹和导弹。

SAIC 一直是 Cloud One 的主承包商，直到 2025 年 Leidos 接手。国家工商总局没有回应置评请求。莱多斯将问题转交给空军。

据两位消息人士称，Cloud One 是美国军方最大的云平台之一。

“这里的违规行为是一件大事，”一位消息人士说。

其中一位消息人士称，调查人员已召集美国军方网络部队网络司令部来评估损失。

网络司令部没有回应置评请求。

黑客事件的发现导致了一系列的破坏。其中两名消息人士和第四名知情人士表示，将后台应用程序迁移到云一的努力已经暂停，这是一项长期的军事优先事项。

就在科技行业披露了新一批严重软件漏洞之际，云一号上已经运行的应用程序的更新被阻止，导致空军人员无法应用修复程序。第五位消息人士称，一些用户的管理员权限被撤销。

所有五位消息人士均要求匿名。

一位消息人士称，网络入侵者利用软件漏洞到达控制平面。该人士将控制飞机比作通用遥控器，因为理论上入侵者可以利用其访问权限来检查军用飞机的运行状态或备件的移动情况，尽管目前尚不清楚黑客在这种情况下是否这样做。

title: Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open
title_en: Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open
author: Amy Nordrum
article_content:
Every year, the editors at MIT Technology Review select 35 of the world’s top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors to honor as our newest class of Innovators Under 35. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations.

We’re on the hunt for researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to some of the most formidable problems society faces, including human disease and climate change. We also recognize those who have made clever and useful inventions, important new scientific discoveries, or technological breakthroughs early in their careers.

We want to hear about people, based anywhere in the world, who are responsible for a major finding or advance and can show real-world impact from their work. To qualify for the list, a nominee must be under the age of 35 as of October 1, 2027 (that is, born on or after October 2, 1992).

Have someone in mind? Or think you’d be a great candidate and want to nominate yourself? Follow this link to suggest someone who you think should make our 2027 list. It’s free and takes only a few minutes. Just be sure to get your nomination in before the deadline—which is 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, January 19.

After the deadline, our editors will review all nominees and select a group of semifinalists, whom we’ll invite to complete a formal application. Then, dozens of expert judges will help us evaluate those applicants and settle on the finalists. You can read more about our selection process here .

Our newsroom began producing our Innovators Under 35 list in 1999. It’s an annual exercise that helps our reporters scout out the brightest young minds in the fields they cover. It also introduces our audience to dozens of rising stars worth watching in the years to come. Subscribers can explore the 2026 list and peruse the full archives.

We look forward to reviewing your nominations.

title: Developers Wanted to Build a High-Rise Data Center. Kansas City Blocked It.
title_en: Developers Wanted to Build a High-Rise Data Center. Kansas City Blocked It.

inline_images.caption: At a proposed height of 384 feet, the data center would have been taller than all but a handful of local buildings. (rendering by SOM)
inline_images.alt: At a proposed height of 384 feet, the data center would have been taller than all but a handful of local buildings.

author: Tiffany Hsu
article_content:
In the largely low-slung historic downtown of Kansas City, Mo., near a school, a cabaret theater and a fur shop turned eatery, an investment fund from out of town proposed to build a 20-story data center.

Far from the data centers of public imagination, where flat boxes sprawl horizontally across rural fields, the brick-clad tower would be the 10th-tallest property in town, designed by an architecture firm responsible for some of the loftiest structures in the world. To make room, a squat landmark that has occupied the block for 126 years would be demolished.

Locals were put off by the idea of a data center — possibly the least popular category of building globally. They were also unsettled by the idea that it would be built upward instead of out. They soured further when some suspected that the project might be a smokescreen, a private equity maneuver that uses federal incentives for heritage preservation.

The Kansas City government received more than 400 letters in opposition to the tower over the summer — one calling it “an absolutely dystopian idea” and another saying that “the data center bubble is nearing a pop.” This month, the City Council unanimously rejected the project.

Proposals for vertical data centers, however, will continue amid rising demand for computing power in the age of artificial intelligence. Other novel formats are being considered for data centers, including offshore and subsea facilities, former nuclear sites and solar-powered hubs in space (an idea backed by tech titans including Elon Musk).

Data center towers “illustrate an emerging question for city centers confronting both obsolete commercial buildings and growing demand for computing infrastructure,” according to the Council on Vertical Urbanism, a group offering expertise on tall buildings.

More than 3,000 data centers already operate nationwide, and more than 1,500 were in development as of the spring — the vast majority of them planned for the South and the Midwest, according to the Pew Research Center.

Public attention has been consumed by several enormous data center projects planned or under construction in more rural locales, many of them designed to address the immense power needs of A.I. However, more than 97 percent of data centers reside inside urban cores and their immediate surroundings (including hundreds of acres for Google and Meta in northern Kansas City), according to a report from the engineering school at New York University. The rest are, on average, 8.5 miles from the nearest urban edge.

Meta has an 11-story riverside data center in Singapore. A permit for an 11-story data center near the convention center in San Jose, Calif., is under review. In downtown Los Angeles, a proposed 13-story data center promises to serve the “entertainment and technology industries’ growing data needs.” Plans for a data center in central Chicago involve converting half of a 12-story, 99-year-old landmark. This month, activists stormed the construction site for a Microsoft data center in Amsterdam, where three high-rise towers are planned.

There are benefits to building soaring urban data centers, architects said. In cities with intensifying demand for digital services such as financial trading, telehealth and A.I., having heavy-duty computing infrastructure nearby can help users more quickly gain access to data. Building vertically is often the only option in places like Taiwan, where land is limited. In cities like New York, data centers are sharing refurbished skyscraper space with other tenants.

But keeping servers cool is a trickier proposition in a tower, where heat can rise and concentrate. Heavy equipment must be maneuvered into higher floors, requiring careful engineering to manage extreme weight. The same concerns that accompany ground-level centers also apply: How much power and water will the site extract, and how much heat and noise will it expel?

Projects around the country were thoroughly rebuked by voters in the recent midterm elections, and three communities in Kansas alone voted to ban large-scale data center construction.

In Kansas City, home to dozens of data centers but also new regulations on how they are classified and zoned, the vertical data center proposal became public in June. The developer was Revitalization Unlimited, a real estate private equity fund based in Miami, which describes itself as “enhancing investor returns through preservation of certified historic structures” by tapping “powerful tax incentives.”

The architecture firm was Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, known as SOM and based in Chicago. It designed the Willis Tower there (the tallest building in the world for decades), One World Trade Center in New York (the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere) and the Burj Khalifa in Dubai (the tallest building in the world).

For Kansas City, SOM envisioned a 384-foot downtown tower, whose height would exceed all but a handful of local buildings. The 141,000 square feet would include systems for cooling and power generation. The ground floor would feature retail space.

The proposal did not mention “artificial intelligence” or “A.I.” And no tenant was named.

The proposal called for the demolition of the Western Newspaper Union Building, which was built in 1900 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. In January, Revitalization said it had purchased the recently renovated site, adding that it planned “to continue the careful preservation of the building’s architectural features.”

The mayor publicly opposed the plan. A preservation group called the proposal “peculiar” and questioned why the data center could not be built on a parking lot or an abandoned site.

Critics also questioned the motivations for the project. A theory took hold that Revitalization was less interested in building a data center and more intent on using a complicated federal tax maneuver to increase the value of its property and maximize income for investors.

Steve Austin, Revitalization’s chief executive, explained the process in a video posted on YouTube last year. The firm can arrange for a legally binding agreement called a historical preservation easement to be placed on a historic property, which permanently protects the building from future work. The firm can donate the easement to the government or a preservation-focused nonprofit group and file for a charitable deduction, whose amount is based on the fair market value of the property if it had been redeveloped rather than preserved. (President Trump has used a similar tactic involving tax deductions through conservation easements on his golf courses.)

Revitalization’s proposal to the city imagined the Western Newspaper Union property reborn as a data center tower — an expensive undertaking. Mr. Austin told one trade publication that, at $183 million, he expected construction to exceed the average cost of building a suburban facility. But the firm had made those plans legally difficult to execute by setting up an easement for the building, critics suggested.

“They basically protected the building from the very thing they’re proposing,” said Brooke Bowlin, a community organizer with the advocacy groups Kansas City Data Center Watchdog and Sunrise Movement Kansas City. Sitting down the street among the elegant 120-year-old marble columns of the Kansas City Public Library, she called the data center pitch a form of “predatory development,” capitalizing on Kansas City history.

“There are a lot of parallels with a real data center — a wealthy company coming in and extracting from locals and their resources,” she said.

Mr. Austin said in a statement that Revitalization had ended up not taking a deduction on the property, and that the deduction was not contingent on the city’s approving the data center. The company deemed a residential, office or hospitality building too expensive to build. A data center, he said, “was the most economically viable development that would not require any incentives from the city or county.” Mr. Austin added that the tower would have created $15.7 million in local spending each year.

“The suggestion that this proposal existed to inflate an appraisal is baseless and misleading,” he said. The company, he said, was “evaluating next steps.”

In a recent YouTube video, Mr. Austin says that “right now, there’s nothing that’s more profitable in real estate, as a landlord, than building a data center.” He added that Revitalization planned to use federal historic tax credits to help convert an unoccupied former courthouse in Miami — a four-story building that is more than 100 years old — into a data center.

“You can go take these beautiful historic buildings and you can use these various tax incentives to kind of breathe new life into them,” Mr. Austin says in the video, extolling the idea of converting old structures into “something as modern and high-tech as a data center.”

“I don’t know that there’s anything more poetic in real estate,” he said.
