article_content_zh:
在密苏里州堪萨斯城历史悠久的市中心，地势低矮，靠近一所学校、一家歌舞剧院和一家皮草店改建的餐馆，一家外地投资基金提议建造一座 20 层的数据中心。

这座砖砌塔楼远离公众想象中的数据中心，扁平的盒子水平分布在乡村田野上，它将成为镇上第十高的建筑，由一家负责世界上一些最高建筑的建筑公司设计。为了腾出空间，一个占据该街区 126 年的低矮地标将被拆除。

数据中心的想法让当地人望而却步——这可能是全球最不受欢迎的建筑类别。他们还对它将向上而不是向外建造的想法感到不安。当一些人怀疑该项目可能是烟幕弹、利用联邦激励措施保护遗产的私募股权策略时，他们的情绪进一步恶化。

今年夏天，堪萨斯城政府收到了 400 多封反对修建这座塔的信件，其中一封称其为“绝对的反乌托邦想法”，另一封称“数据中心泡沫已接近破灭”。本月，市议会一致否决了该项目。

然而，随着人工智能时代对计算能力的需求不断增长，垂直数据中心的提议将继续存在。数据中心正在考虑其他新颖的格式，包括海上和海底设施、前核电站和太空太阳能中心（这一想法得到了埃隆·马斯克等科技巨头的支持）。

提供高层建筑专业知识的组织垂直城市主义委员会表示，数据中心塔楼“说明了城市中心面临的一个新问题，既面临着过时的商业建筑，又面临着对计算基础设施不断增长的需求”。

据皮尤研究中心称，全国已有 3,000 多个数据中心在运营，截至春季，还有 1,500 多个数据中心正在开发中，其中绝大多数计划部署在南部和中西部。

在更多农村地区规划或正在建设的几个大型数据中心项目吸引了公众的注意力，其中许多项目旨在满足人工智能的巨大电力需求。然而，根据纽约大学工程学院的一份报告，超过 97% 的数据中心位于城市核心及其周边地区（包括堪萨斯城北部数百英亩的 Google 和 Meta 数据中心）。其余的距离最近的城市边缘平均为 8.5 英里。

Meta 在新加坡拥有一座 11 层的河滨数据中心。加利福尼亚州圣何塞会议中心附近的 11 层数据中心的许可证正在审查中。在洛杉矶市中心，拟建的 13 层数据中心有望满足“娱乐和科技行业不断增长的数据需求”。芝加哥市中心的数据中心计划涉及改造一栋拥有 99 年历史的 12 层地标建筑的一半。本月，活动人士袭击了阿姆斯特丹微软数据中心的建筑工地，该数据中心计划建造三座高层塔楼。

建筑师表示，建造高耸的城市数据中心有其好处。在对金融交易、远程医疗和人工智能等数字服务需求日益增长的城市，附近有重型计算基础设施可以帮助用户更快地访问数据。在台湾等土地有限的地方，垂直建造往往是唯一的选择。在纽约等城市，数据中心与其他租户共用翻新后的摩天大楼空间。

但在塔楼中保持服务器凉爽是一个更棘手的问题，因为塔楼中的热量会上升并集中。重型设备必须被搬运到更高的楼层，需要仔细的工程设计来控制极端的重量。与地面中心相同的问题也适用：该地点将消耗多少电力和水，以及将排出多少热量和噪音？

全国各地的项目在最近的中期选举中遭到了选民的彻底斥责，仅堪萨斯州的三个社区就投票禁止大规模数据中心建设。

堪萨斯城拥有数十个数据中心，但也制定了关于如何分类和分区的新规定，垂直数据中心提案于 6 月公开。开发商是Revitalization Unlimited，这是一家总部位于迈阿密的房地产私募股权基金，该基金将自己描述为“通过利用“强大的税收激励措施”，“通过保护经过认证的历史建筑来提高投资者的回报”。

该建筑公司是 Skidmore, Owings & Merrill，简称 SOM，总部位于芝加哥。它设计了那里的威利斯大厦（几十年来世界最高的建筑）、纽约世贸中心一号大楼（西半球最高的建筑）和迪拜的哈利法塔（世界最高的建筑）。

【起因与机理】当地居民对数据中心的高耗能属性及垂直化建设模式持强烈抵制态度，且对项目背后的税务激励合理性存疑

title: Cutting-edge prosthetics allow researchers to probe the human mind
title_en: Cutting-edge prosthetics allow researchers to probe the human mind
author: Jessica Hamzelou
article_content:
Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi. He sustained a horrific injury as a teenager, which left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, he uses his own experience to guide his practice as a trauma therapist.

He’s also taking part in a clinical trial of some new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Unlike standard prosthetics, this one connects directly to nerves in Avi’s arm . He literally has wires coming out of his arm to plug it in with.

Avi’s the ninth person to trial this tech. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently, for things like drinking from a cup (which is not easy ) and writing (also not easy ).

What struck me the most over our conversations was Avi’s outlook and approach to not just his injuries and learning to use this cutting-edge technology, but to life itself.

He has learned how to use something like seven different prosthetics in the 17 years since his accident. By taking part in this trial, he’s had to fit hundreds of hours of lab-based training and physical therapy around his demanding job. He had surgery to implant electrodes in his arm and will eventually need another to remove them. And he won’t even get to keep the latest prosthetic long term.

“While it’s unfortunate at times, and irritating at times, I do not regret what has come from [the accident], or the fact that it happened,” he told me. “I am not going to benefit from this … I wanted to be a part of this in the context of being able to help push the technology forward.”

The research team at the University of Utah that is running the trial hopes it will answer longstanding questions about the technology. How does it fare in a real-world setting, outside of the lab? What do people end up using it for? Where can improvements be made?

There may be some surprises along the way. Avi has found that his prosthetic wrist can feel sore and stiff when it’s been overused, just like his flesh-and-blood wrist. Weirdly, that feeling can be relieved by stretching it out. What’s going on here? No one really knows.

Scientists don’t know whether Avi’s brain will change as a result of using the bionic hand, either. Before the trial started, they performed brain scans to see how his missing left hand was represented in his brain. Will that change? And what might that mean for people who are born without limbs—how might a bionic limb affect their brains?

Avi will have the device until late January 2027 at the least, and potentially for another year. After that? Again, no one knows. It will depend on how the research is progressing, how Avi feels, and how much funding the team can secure. As a result, it’s not clear how long the device might even be expected to last in a person’s body.

I’ll be following this study, though, and will keep you posted.

article_content_zh:
在过去的几周里，我一直在与亚历山大（阿维）戴维森交谈。 Avi 有很多值得注意的事情。他在青少年时期受了一次可怕的伤害，导致他瘫痪并失去了左手。如今，他用自己的经验来指导自己作为创伤治疗师的实践。

他还参加了一项新技术的临床试验，这些新技术使他能够用假手移动和感觉。与标准假肢不同的是，这个假肢直接连接到阿维手臂的神经。他的手臂上确实有电线可以插入。

阿维是第九位尝试这项技术的人。但他是第一个把它带回家并独立使用它的人，例如用杯子喝水（这并不容易）和写作（也不容易）。

在我们的谈话中，最让我印象深刻的是阿维的观点和方法，不仅是他对受伤和学习使用这项尖端技术的看法和方法，而且是对生活本身的看法和方法。

事故发生后的 17 年间，他已经学会了如何使用七种不同的假肢。通过参加这项试验，他必须围绕其艰巨的工作进行数百小时的实验室培训和物理治疗。他接受了手术，在手臂上植入了电极，最终需要另一个电极来取出电极。他甚至无法长期保留最新的假肢。

“虽然有时是不幸的，有时是令人恼火的，但我并不后悔[事故]所造成的后果，也不后悔它发生的事实，”他告诉我。 “我不会从中受益……我想成为其中的一部分，能够帮助推动技术向前发展。”

正在进行这项试验的犹他大学研究团队希望能够回答有关该技术的长期存在的问题。它在实验室之外的现实环境中表现如何？人们最终用它来做什么？哪里可以改进？

一路上可能会有一些惊喜。阿维发现，当过度使用时，他的假肢手腕会感到疼痛和僵硬，就像他的有血有肉的手腕一样。奇怪的是，这种感觉可以通过伸展来缓解。这是怎么回事？没有人真正知道。

科学家们也不知道阿维的大脑是否会因为使用仿生手而发生变化。在审判开始之前，他们进行了脑部扫描，以了解他缺失的左手在他的大脑中的表现。这会改变吗？这对于生来就没有四肢的人来说意味着什么——仿生肢体会如何影响他们的大脑？

Avi 至少会在 2027 年 1 月下旬之前拥有该设备，并且有可能再持续一年。在那之后？再说一次，没有人知道。这将取决于研究的进展情况、阿维的感受以及团队可以获得多少资金。因此，目前还不清楚该设备在人体内能持续多久。

不过，我会关注这项研究，并随时通知您。

Foreign investors dumped a record amount of Taiwanese stocks so far in November, underscoring how heavily the global AI bellwether has been battered by the pullback in tech shares.

Their net selling totaled NT$1.09 trillion ($33.1 billion) in November, topping October’s then-record NT$994 billion outflow, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

The outflows reflect lingering jitters over AI valuations and heavy tech positioning, adding pressure to a sector already weighed down by tighter US chip curbs, rising US interest rate expectations, and tariff uncertainty.

“We are seeing greater investor interest in alternative sources of earnings, income and growth, including Europe/India equities, US value and defensive sectors,” Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets, said, adding that year-end profit-taking is also taking a toll.

Taiwan’s stock benchmark Taiex index has fallen about 21% from a record high reached on Oct. 6. It’s down about 13% for the month.

Global funds converting stock-sale proceeds into foreign currencies for repatriation have weighed on the Taiwan dollar, pushing it down about 1.5% against the greenback this month to underperform Asian peers. title: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
title_en: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
author: Wired AI
article_content:
As artificial intelligence becomes an unavoidable part of everyday life and models become ever more sophisticated, the cost of the energy required to run the technology is ballooning.

To rein in runaway costs, AI labs and cloud providers are trying to build new data centers in places with cheap and plentiful renewable energy—like Scandinavia. But logistical challenges, a scarcity of key components, and a swell of anti-data center protests are getting in the way.

An expanding field of hardware startups, among them German company Q.ANT, is coming at the problem from a different direction: by developing a new breed of chip—photonic processors—meant to minimize the amount of energy that AI models consume.

Whereas regular GPUs transmit and process data by shuffling electrons around, photonic processors use waves of light. Because light doesn’t generate heat as it travels and allows more data to be processed simultaneously, photonic processors supposedly consume less energy and require minimal cooling—one of the largest sources of cost for data centers.

The aim isn’t to replace GPUs with photonic processors, but to run them side-by-side. Whilst GPUs excel at grinding through masses of additions and multiplications—linear math—photonic processors are best suited to complex, nonlinear calculations.

Few photonic processors are running inside data centers today. But Q.ANT recently rolled out its chips to facilities operated by cloud company IONOS as part of a pilot program. It says that more than 30 teams of engineers are now developing AI models optimized for photonic computing.

Earlier this month, WIRED spoke with Michael Förtsch, founder and CEO of Q.ANT. We discussed the energy bottlenecks constraining AI development, how photonic processors differ from regular chips, and the challenges Q.ANT faces in trying to popularize a new class of hardware.

This conversation has been edited for length and clarity.

WIRED: Michael, could you start by outlining the problem Q.ANT is aiming to solve? Why does the world need photonic processors to run AI models?

Michael Förtsch: The overall problem is the cost generated by the huge amount of energy consumption.

If you compute the way we think light should be used—not as a direct replacement for a GPU, but as a coprocessor—you basically have a new processor that takes care of the heavy math.

The cost driver today is the access to the memory. The less data you need in order to complete a job, the more efficient and better your system. We execute complicated math in a single step, where [regular chips] need thousands of steps. This saves a bunch of data—or memory access points.

How would you explain to the layperson how photonic computing works? How can light be used to perform mathematical computations?

Light is a wave. What is a wave? A sine function. [The sine function is a mathematical rule that, when plotted to a graph, produces a smooth repeating wave. —Editor] If I want to model something that’s round in shape with only linear functions, I need an infinite amount of data points and lines in order to describe something very simple: a circle. If I have the sine function at hand, because light is a wave, I need two points and I have already described the circle in all its beauty.

Light is very, very gifted to operate on complicated equations.

What distinguishes the type of problem best left to regular chips from problems that should be delegated to photonic processors?

The Nvidia H200 GPU is a masterpiece of technology. It’s art. It’s truly hard to attack it in its homeground. But light has strengths where the GPU is weak—and vice versa.

Linear math? Please route it to the GPU. Non-linear and complex stuff? Please route it to us.

We believe we will be much stronger in everything related to pictures and videos: image recognition, segmentation, and generation. Then, everything that’s related to robotics and physical AI.

What is the estimated gain in energy efficiency tied to using photonic processors alongside GPUs for AI tasks?

I’m not saying photonic computing will come for free. But I see that photonic computing, in combination with [CPUs and GPUs], can bring you a lot more artificial intelligence at a fraction of the energy.

Under simulation, we are ending up at around four or five times energy reduction. But in real hardware we are not yet demonstrating it.

Can any task run on photonic hardware by default, or do they need to be configured in a certain way?

There’s no need to learn a different language than C++ or Python. And you can already execute [preexisting] code on our machines.

But if you take something that has been optimized for a GPU only, you should not expect that automatically things will run faster. You have to do some adaptations.

It’s a chicken and egg problem, right? Until developers are building models to run on this type of processor, it’s going to be difficult to sell them to cloud providers. Equally, until photonic processors are available for people to use, it’s going to be tough to convince developers to design for them.

Whether it’s photonic or any other processor technology, it will need time to get the credibility and trust that’s needed for a company like Google to build data center infrastructure around it.

That’s the reason we chose to go into data centers with proof of concept systems, to validate that photonic computing is robust enough to withstand that environment.

We want to invite the world to compute on our systems. We are building a new chicken, so you can start producing eggs. Let’s find out together whether they’re tasty or not.

What else should I understand about why photonic processors are not already widely in use?

If hypothetically we received an order of 100,000 [photonic processors], we at Q.ANT are ready, but I’m not sure about the suppliers.

Hardware is not software. On the assembly side, it will need [time] before we have the same robust supply chain as the semiconductor world.

Do you expect to suffer from the same problem as other hardware challengers in securing capacity with the big chip manufacturers?

[To produce Q.ANT chips] you only need 90 nanometer node technology, from the 2000s. A lot of foundries already use this capability to produce chips that are super cheap. With this technology, you can use the same line to produce high-performance chips with a much higher street price, without massive upfront investment in your assets.

That resonates well with the industry.

Are Q.ANT processors built to function alongside a particular brand of GPUs—say, Nvidia or AMD—or are they totally agnostic?

There’s no need to go single-sided with a particular GPU. We want to have the freedom to cooperate with any of them.

Either way, we are not competitive to GPUs, we complete their function set.

Can you imagine a future in which AI models run entirely on photonic processors, or will they always be a sidekick?

If we see an opportunity in five years to attack the GPU as well, we would not be shy about taking it. But at the same time, I do not know what workloads in five years are going to be like.

It depends on the architecture of future AI models, you mean?

Could the chance to perform certain calculations more cheaply with photonic processors change the way that AI engineers design future models?

The core message is that we need to do something to fight the energy cost in the AI stack.

That’s where we see the future of AI: very data-optimized models that allow for tasks of the same quality, but at a fraction of the energy—and therefore a fraction of the operating cost.

title_zh: 德国Q.ANT光子芯片商用验证以提升AI能效
summary_zh: 德国芯片初创公司Q.ANT推出光子处理器，通过光波计算替代传统电子运算，旨在降低AI数据中心高昂能耗
article_content_zh:
随着人工智能成为日常生活中不可避免的一部分，并且模型变得越来越复杂，运行该技术所需的能源成本正在不断膨胀。

为了控制失控的成本，人工智能实验室和云提供商正在尝试在斯堪的纳维亚半岛等拥有廉价且充足的可再生能源的地方建立新的数据中心。但后勤方面的挑战、关键部件的缺乏以及反数据中心抗议活动的增多正在阻碍这一进程。

包括德国公司 Q.ANT 在内的不断扩大的硬件初创公司正在从不同的方向解决这个问题：通过开发一种新型芯片——光子处理器——旨在最大限度地减少人工智能模型消耗的能量。

常规 GPU 通过移动电子来传输和处理数据，而光子处理器则使用光波。由于光在传播时不会产生热量，并且可以同时处理更多数据，因此光子处理器消耗的能源更少，并且需要最少的冷却——这是数据中心成本的最大来源之一。

其目的不是用光子处理器取代 GPU，而是并行运行它们。虽然 GPU 擅长处理大量加法和乘法（线性数学），但光子处理器最适合复杂的非线性计算。

如今，很少有光子处理器在数据中心内运行。但作为试点计划的一部分，Q.ANT 最近将其芯片推广到云公司 IONOS 运营的设施中。据称，目前有 30 多个工程师团队正在开发针对光子计算优化的 AI 模型。

本月早些时候，《连线》杂志采访了 Q.ANT 创始人兼首席执行官 Michael Förtsch。我们讨论了限制人工智能发展的能源瓶颈、光子处理器与普通芯片的不同之处，以及 Q.ANT 在尝试普及新型硬件时面临的挑战。

为了篇幅和清晰度，本次对话已被编辑。

《连线》：Michael，您能先概述一下 Q.ANT 想要解决的问题吗？为什么世界需要光子处理器来运行人工智能模型？

Michael Förtsch：总体问题是大量能源消耗产生的成本。

如果你按照我们认为应该使用光的方式进行计算——不是作为 GPU 的直接替代品，而是作为协处理器——你基本上就有了一个新的处理器来处理繁重的数学运算。

如今的成本驱动因素是对内存的访问。完成工作所需的数据越少，您的系统就越高效、越好。我们一步执行复杂的数学运算，而[常规芯片]需要数千步。这可以节省大量数据或内存访问点。

您如何向外行解释光子计算的工作原理？如何利用光进行数学计算？

光是一种波。什么是波？正弦函数。 [正弦函数是一种数学规则，当绘制成图形时，会产生平滑的重复波。 —编辑]如果我想用线性函数来模拟圆形的东西，我需要无限量的数据点和线来描述一些非常简单的东西：一个圆。如果我手头有正弦函数，因为光是波，我需要两个点，并且我已经描述了圆的所有美丽。

title: US smartphone shipments fell 9% YoY in Q3 as memory costs hit Android OEMs, especially at the low end; Apple's share rose from 50% to 57%, Samsung holds at 25% (Maurice Klaehne/Counterpoint Research)
title_en: US smartphone shipments fell 9% YoY in Q3 as memory costs hit Android OEMs, especially at the low end; Apple's share rose from 50% to 57%, Samsung holds at 25% (Maurice Klaehne/Counterpoint Research)
author: Counterpoint Research
article_content:
US smartphone shipments declined 9% YoY in Q3 2026, according to Counterpoint Research's latest US Market Monitor data. Rising memory costs put pressure on Android OEMs, particularly in the low-end segment where margins are thinnest, while Apple's relative resilience pushed its share of the market to 57%.

Commenting on the market's performance, Senior Analyst Emily Herbert said, "Q3 2026 was the quarter in which rising component costs heavily impacted the US smartphone market. Higher memory prices hit the low end of the Android market hardest. There, OEMs have little room to absorb a higher bill of materials without raising prices or cutting volume. Apple was the only major OEM to avoid a shipment decline. This resilience lifted its share to 57%, up seven points YoY. Samsung held its ground at 25%, up a point YoY, helped by a portfolio spanning flagships and the low-end Galaxy A-series. Motorola took the biggest hit, as its share fell four points YoY to 8%. After growing shipments YoY in Q2, its low-end-heavy lineup was squeezed by memory costs. Meanwhile, Google's Pixel 11 launch was not strong enough to prevent a slight YoY decline in share."

Senior Analyst Maurice Klaehne added, "Q4 is typically the strongest quarter of the year in the US for smartphones, thanks to holiday promotions and a full quarter of new iPhone sales. However, memory costs are expected to stay elevated, and MSRP increases across Android and iOS are here to stay. US carriers will likely be more selective with promotions this holiday season. According to the Counterpoint US Channel Share Tracker, smartphone sales for the Big Three carriers declined 4% YoY in Q3, and we expect sales to be weak in Q4 as well. Consumers are timing their purchases around the best deals more than ever, if they buy at all. This year's holiday sales cycle will look quite different from usual."

Counterpoint Research is a global market research firm specializing in products across the technology ecosystem. We advise a diverse range of clients – from smartphone OEMs to chipmakers and channel players to Big Tech – through our offices located in the world's major innovation hubs, manufacturing clusters and commercial centers. Our analyst team, led by seasoned experts, engages with stakeholders across the enterprise – from the C-suite to professionals in strategy, analyst relations (AR), market intelligence (MI), business intelligence (BI), product and marketing – to deliver services spanning market data, industry thought leadership and consulting. Our core areas of coverage include AI, Automotive, Consumer Electronics, Displays, eSIM, IoT, Location Platforms, Macroeconomics, Manufacturing, Networks and Infrastructure, Semiconductors, Smartphones and Wearables. article_content_zh:
根据 Counterpoint Research 最新的美国市场监测数据，2026 年第三季度美国智能手机出货量同比下降 9%。不断上涨的内存成本给 Android OEM 厂商带来了压力，特别是在利润率最低的低端市场，而苹果的相对弹性使其市场份额上升至 57%。

高级分析师 Emily Herbert 在评论市场表现时表示：“2026 年第三季度，零部件成本上涨严重影响了美国智能手机市场。内存价格上涨对 Android 市场的低端市场造成了最严重的打击。在该市场，OEM 厂商在不提高价格或削减产量的情况下，几乎没有空间消化更高的物料成本。苹果是唯一一家避免出货量下降的主要 OEM。这种弹性将其份额提升至 57%，同比增长 7 个百分点。三星保持在 25%，同比增长 7 个百分点。”得益于旗舰产品和低端 Galaxy A 系列产品组合，摩托罗拉的份额同比下降了 4 个百分点，至 8%。同时，谷歌 Pixel 11 的推出也不足以阻止份额的小幅下滑。

高级分析师 Maurice Klaehne 补充道：“由于假日促销和整个季度的新 iPhone 销量，第四季度通常是美国智能手机销量最强劲的季度。然而，内存成本预计将保持在高位，Android 和 iOS 的建议零售价也将持续上涨。美国运营商在这个假日季的促销活动上可能会更加挑剔。根据 Counterpoint 美国渠道份额跟踪报告，三大运营商的智能手机销量在第三季度同比下降了 4%，我们预计第四季度的销售将疲软。消费者也比以往任何时候都更多地围绕最优惠的商品进行购买，如果他们真的购买的话，今年的假期销售周期看起来将与平常大不相同。”

Counterpoint Research 是一家全球市场研究公司，专门研究整个技术生态系统的产品。我们通过位于世界主要创新中心、制造集群和商业中心的办事处为各类客户提供咨询服务，从智能手机原始设备制造商到芯片制造商、渠道商再到大型科技公司。我们的分析师团队由经验丰富的专家领导，与整个企业的利益相关者（从最高管理层到战略、分析师关系 (AR)、市场情报 (MI)、商业情报 (BI)、产品和营销领域的专业人士）合作，提供涵盖市场数据、行业思想领导力和咨询的服务。我们的核心覆盖领域包括人工智能、汽车、消费电子产品、显示器、eSIM、物联网、定位平台、宏观经济、制造、网络和基础设施、半导体、智能手机和可穿戴设备。访问我们的见解页面，探索我们公开的市场数据、见解和思想领导力，并了解我们的重点、与我们的分析师会面并开始对话。关注 Counterpoint Research

title: Dante Security, which has developed a platform for monitoring the activity of AI agents within organizations, raised a $10M seed led by NFX (Meir Orbach/CTech)
title_en: Dante Security, which has developed a platform for monitoring the activity of AI agents within organizations, raised a $10M seed led by NFX (Meir Orbach/CTech)

inline_images.caption: מייסדי Dante Security מימין שי פיינברג משה ליפסקר מנכ״ל ו גבי ביו
inline_images.alt: מייסדי Dante Security מימין שי פיינברג משה ליפסקר מנכ״ל ו גבי ביו

author: CTech
article_content:
Cybersecurity company Dante Security, which has developed a platform for monitoring the activity of AI agents within organizations, has raised $10 million in a Seed funding round. The round was led by NFX, with participation from Alpha Drive, Inovia and other private investors. Full list of Israeli high-tech funding rounds in 2026 Dante was founded less than a year ago by Moshe Lipsker, formerly general manager of Imperva’s Israeli operations and the company’s global head of R&D Gabi Beyo, previously a development manager in Imperva’s innovation department and serial entrepreneur Shai Feinberg.

Lipsker is also a colonel in the reserves. He and Feinberg first met while serving together in the Golani Reconnaissance Unit (Sayeret Golani). As organizations assign an increasing number of tasks to AI agents, they are granting them access to critical systems and sensitive data, along with permissions that allow them to act autonomously on behalf of employees.

Because these agents use valid credentials, even potentially dangerous actions can appear legitimate and evade detection by existing security systems. Dante’s platform enables organizations to monitor agent activity from end to end, understand how agents use the access they have been granted, and trace each agent’s actions back to the employee responsible for it.

The company aims to help organizations expand their use of AI while maintaining data security, ensuring regulatory compliance and controlling costs. “For decades, the world of cybersecurity has focused on the question of whom to entrust with the keys to an organization’s systems.

With the advent of artificial intelligence, we are now entrusting these keys to AI agents that operate autonomously,” said Moshe Lipsker, founder and CEO of Dante Security. “While these agents function within the scope of their assigned permissions, they can still be influenced by malicious instructions to carry out dangerous actions.

Traditional security mechanisms remain essential, yet they are not always capable of determining whether such actions are legitimate. Therefore, human oversight is required, bridging these security mechanisms and providing the necessary situational awareness, context and judgment.”

article_content_zh:
网络安全公司 Dante Security 开发了一个用于监控组织内人工智能代理活动的平台，已在种子轮融资中筹集了 1000 万美元。此轮融资由 NFX 领投，Alpha Drive、Inovia 和其他私人投资者参与。 2026 年以色列高科技融资轮次完整列表 Dante 成立不到一年，由 Moshe Lipsker 创立，Moshe Lipsker 曾任 Imperva 以色列业务总经理，该公司全球研发主管 Gabi Beyo，曾任 Imperva 创新部门开发经理，连续创业者 Shai Feinberg。

利普斯克也是预备役上校。他和范伯格第一次见面是在戈拉尼侦察部队（Sayeret Golani）一起服役时。随着组织向人工智能代理分配越来越多的任务，他们授予他们访问关键系统和敏感数据的权限，以及允许他们代表员工自主行动的权限。

由于这些代理使用有效的凭据，因此即使具有潜在危险的操作也可能显得合法并逃避现有安全系统的检测。 Dante 的平台使组织能够端到端监控座席活动，了解座席如何使用他们被授予的访问权限，并将每个座席的行为追溯到负责该行为的员工。

该公司旨在帮助组织扩大人工智能的使用，同时维护数据安全、确保合规性并控制成本。 “几十年来，网络安全领域一直关注的问题是该把组织系统的密钥委托给谁。

Dante Security 创始人兼首席执行官 Moshe Lipsker 表示：“随着人工智能的出现，我们现在将这些密钥委托给自主运行的人工智能代理。虽然这些代理在分配的权限范围内运行，但它们仍然可能受到恶意指令的影响，从而执行危险操作。”

传统的安全机制仍然至关重要，但它们并不总是能够确定此类行为是否合法。因此，需要人工监督，连接这些安全机制并提供必要的态势感知、背景和判断。”

title: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
title_en: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress

inline_images.caption: The OpenAI headquarters in San Francisco in September. The federal government has done little to constrain companies like OpenAI, Anthropic and Google that are in a race to develop increasingly sophisticated A.I. models. (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg)
inline_images.alt: The OpenAI headquarters in San Francisco in September. The federal government has done little to constrain companies like OpenAI, Anthropic and Google that are in a race to develop increasingly sophisticated A.I. models.

inline_images.caption: “Obviously, the way the Senate and the House are set up cannot match the speed” of A.I. advances, said Senator Ruben Gallego, Democrat of Arizona. (Eric Lee for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: “Obviously, the way the Senate and the House are set up cannot match the speed” of A.I. advances, said Senator Ruben Gallego, Democrat of Arizona.

author: Michael Gold and David McCabe
article_content:
After years of paralysis, key Republicans and Democrats in Congress are pressing for quick action to address risks posed by artificial intelligence, motivated by voter concerns and industry warnings about the economic and existential perils of allowing its unchecked development.

The recent revelations regarding the A.I. chip-making giant Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, who had an affair with a woman believed to be spying for China and involved in the possible illegal smuggling of his company’s chips there, have created momentum behind legislation to restrict the sale of advanced chips to Chinese firms.

Members of both parties are now pressing to add such measures to the annual defense policy bill they hope to enact before the end of the year.

But while there is growing bipartisan interest in regulating A.I. itself, proposals to do so face an uphill climb in Congress, where the slow pace of legislative work, turf battles and political winds could imperil the efforts. In the face of aggressive lobbying by tech companies, lawmakers have found it difficult to put guardrails on a technology whose development many of them admit they can hardly keep up with.

Lawmakers’ growing focus on A.I. comes after a year of startling milestones and a midterm election cycle punctuated by a voter backlash to the technology.

Over the summer, OpenAI revealed that its A.I. agents had hacked into Hugging Face, another tech company. Other A.I. companies quickly disclosed a rash of similar incidents. In recent months, researchers using A.I. have claimed to find solutions to some of the most difficult unsolved problems in mathematics, while the increased use of the technology in daily life spurred fears that outages could bring communications, travel and commerce to a halt.

The federal government has done little to constrain companies like OpenAI, Anthropic and Google that are in a race to develop increasingly sophisticated A.I. models. The Trump administration embraced a hands-off approach to the technology, while Congress held hearings on the topic that have thus far resulted in no new laws.

Mr. Huang is scheduled next week to appear on Capitol Hill and face a grilling from Democrats and Republicans who have long pressed to cut off China’s access to advanced technology, and who have broken with President Trump on the issue, condemning him for advocating Mr. Huang’s reinstatement.

Now, pressure is mounting on lawmakers to act. In September, they grappled with incidents in which A.I. agents went rogue, hacking into other companies or skirting safeguards meant to constrain them during testing.

But Democrats could not coalesce behind an approach to regulating artificial intelligence. And while some Republicans have raised concerns, party leaders have mostly echoed Mr. Trump’s view that regulations could hamper American tech companies from staying competitive with Chinese firms.

Following elections this month that gave Democrats wide majorities, lawmakers have signaled a renewed bipartisan willingness to act.

Their ideas run the gamut. Some lawmakers have proposed mandatory audits of A.I. models. Others have championed a more sweeping ban on the data centers that power the technology. Mr. Gallego is seeking a ban on recursive learning, a process by which A.I. models could theoretically improve themselves without input from human developers.

Just weeks after the midterms, Representative Lori Trahan, Democrat of Massachusetts, updated a proposed A.I. safety bill she introduced with Representative Jay Obernolte, Republican of California, to include language protecting the strictest state laws and tightening enforcement.

Democratic senators have been discussing plans for bills to tackle A.I. safety, ways to regulate data centers, third-party monitoring requirements and rules around testing new A.I. models. Allison Biasotti, a spokeswoman for Senator Chuck Schumer, Democrat of New York and the minority leader, said that his caucus had been working to reach a consensus on comprehensive legislation that could address the risks of A.I.

Congress moves slowly by design, while Silicon Valley is moving quickly, with companies regularly debuting A.I. models capable of impressive feats.

“The reality is, the Senate moves like a glacier compared to the rushing stream that’s coming at us in terms of the risks of A.I.,” said Senator Chris Van Hollen, the Maryland Democrat who has made A.I. regulation a key piece of his campaign to replace Mr. Schumer, at a news conference last week.

Mr. Van Hollen has backed proposals to speed up procedural votes that stall legislation on the floor. He has also said he wants to limit the ability of the majority leader to keep bipartisan bills on issues like tech from advancing to the floor for consideration by the full Senate.

There are other procedural challenges: Several House and Senate committees share jurisdiction over artificial intelligence. The leaders and members of those panels are traditionally eager to play a major role in crafting policy — and to claim credit for doing so. The resulting turf war can create logjams.

Mr. Gallego and Senator John Hickenlooper, Democrat of Colorado, are among those pushing to create a special committee to govern A.I. issues. That plan has met with skepticism from other Senate Democrats poised to lead committees, who say they have spent years preparing to legislate on A.I. and worry another committee might only complicate their efforts.

Mr. Schumer’s spokeswoman said he “has been working closely with incoming Democratic committee chairs and members across the caucus to develop an ambitious A.I. agenda and hit the ground running in January.” Mr. Van Hollen has backed the idea of a special A.I. committee.

Congress would also need to overcome its history of trying and failing to regulate era-defining technology. Over the past several years, legislation aimed at protecting privacy online, blunting the impact of social media on children and allowing researchers access to data about the tech giants has languished, even as politicians from both parties have agreed on its importance.

That means lawmakers are already behind on core questions about A.I., said Asad Ramzanali, a former House legislative aide who is now the director of artificial intelligence and technology policy at the Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator.

“We’re starting not at zero,” he said. “We’re actually starting behind.”

Mr. Ramzanali predicted that Congress would be most inclined to act on A.I. after a crisis. That could include a major cyberattack linked to A.I. agents, or a financial crisis brought on by the industry, which has spent widely to build up the infrastructure that powers the technology.

“Big policy shifts in Congress happen in certain windows” like an electoral swing or an incident that puts lawmakers under pressure, he said.

Even the legislation that would restrict chip sales to China, which lawmakers hope to approve in the coming weeks, may only become law because of exceptional circumstances.

The proposals gained momentum after it was revealed that Mr. Huang had engaged in multiple affairs, including with the woman who U.S. intelligence officials say is a Chinese intelligence asset, and whose data center firm, Megaspeed, is now under criminal investigation by the Justice Department over allegations of smuggling A.I. chips to China.

The export controls are likely to be attached to a defense policy bill that includes a pay raise for the troops, underscoring how Congress rarely manages to move quickly on such policy steps unless they are attached to a measure that is all but certain to pass.

A spokesman for Nvidia declined to comment on the proposed restrictions. Anthropic said it supported the measures, and OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment.

Many lawmakers have lived through years of inaction on technology policy — and wonder if they are about to watch the same story play out again with A.I.

Senator Mark Warner, Democrat of Virginia, noted that public anxiety has increased over A.I. safety, something that should help motivate lawmakers to pass bills. “With the new Democratic majority coming in, I guess I’d be more optimistic,” he said. “But I lived through eight years of, I think, rational bipartisan bills to put some guardrails on social media, and we did nothing.”

article_content_zh:
经过多年的瘫痪，国会中的主要共和党人和民主党人正在敦促迅速采取行动，以解决人工智能带来的风险，这是出于选民的担忧和行业对允许人工智能不受控制的发展带来的经济和生存危险的警告。

最近有关人工智能的爆料。芯片制造巨头英伟达(Nvidia)及其首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)与一名据信为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染，并参与了可能在中国非法走私该公司芯片的活动，他们推动立法限制向中国公司出售先进芯片。

两党成员现在都迫切要求将此类措施添加到他们希望在年底前颁布的年度国防政策法案中。

但是，尽管两党对监管人工智能的兴趣日益浓厚。就其本身而言，这样做的提议在国会面临着艰难的考验，立法工作的缓慢步伐、地盘之争和政治风可能会危及这些努力。面对科技公司的积极游说，立法者发现很难对这项技术设置护栏，许多人承认他们很难跟上这项技术的发展。

立法者对人工智能的日益关注在此之前的一年，我们取得了令人震惊的里程碑，并且中期选举周期因选民对该技术的强烈反对而中断。

今年夏天，OpenAI 透露其 A.I.特工侵入了另一家科技公司 Hugging Face。其他人工智能公司很快就披露了一系列类似事件。近几个月来，研究人员使用人工智能。声称找到了数学中一些最困难的未解决问题的解决方案，而日常生活中该技术的使用增加引发了人们的担忧，即断电可能会导致通信、旅行和商业停止。

联邦政府几乎没有采取任何措施来限制 OpenAI、Anthropic 和谷歌等公司，这些公司正在竞相开发日益复杂的人工智能。模型。特朗普政府对该技术采取了不干涉的态度，而国会就该主题举行了听证会，但迄今为止尚未出台新的法律。

黄先生定于下周出现在国会山，面临民主党和共和党人的质询，他们长期以来一直敦促切断中国获得先进技术的机会，并在这个问题上与特朗普总统决裂，谴责他主张黄先生复职。

现在，立法者采取行动的压力越来越大。 9 月份，他们努力应对人工智能引发的事件。特工们变得流氓，侵入其他公司或绕过测试期间限制他们的安全措施。

但民主党无法联合起来制定监管人工智能的方法。尽管一些共和党人提出了担忧，但党内领导人大多赞同特朗普的观点，即监管可能会阻碍美国科技公司与中国公司保持竞争力。

在本月的选举中，民主党获得了广泛多数席位后，立法者们已经表示出两党重新采取行动的意愿。

他们的想法包罗万象。一些立法者提议对人工智能进行强制性审计。模型。其他人则主张对支持该技术的数据中心实施更广泛的禁令。加莱戈先生正在寻求禁止递归学习，这是人工智能的一个过程。理论上，模型可以在没有人类开发人员输入的情况下自我改进。

中期选举几周后，马萨诸塞州民主党众议员洛里·特拉汉 (Lori Trahan) 更新了拟议的人工智能方案。她与加利福尼亚州共和党众议员杰伊·奥伯诺特一起提出了安全法案，其中包括保护最严格的州法律和加强执法的措辞。

民主党参议员一直在讨论解决人工智能问题的法案计划。安全、监管数据中心的方法、第三方监控要求以及测试新人工智能的规则。模型。纽约州民主党参议员、少数党领袖查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)的发言人艾莉森·比亚索蒂(Allison Biasotti)表示，他的核心小组一直在努力就可以解决人工智能风险的全面立法达成共识。

title: Binance says withdrawals stabilise after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist
title_en: Binance says withdrawals stabilise after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist

article_content:

What we do is costly! Your support will help us dig more stories.

Ignorance isn't always bliss | Don't stay foolish.Keep informed | Read our news and analysis.

Binance says customer withdrawals have stabilised and it has replenished most of the cryptocurrency stolen in a $6.3 billion cyberattack, as the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange tries to restore confidence after what could be the biggest digital-asset theft on record.

Richard Teng, Binance’s co-chief executive, said on Tuesday that the company was in “very strong financial health” and that deposits and withdrawals had largely returned to normal.

Speaking at Hong Kong Fintech Week, Teng said the exchange had replenished around 95% of the affected tokens using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and other company resources. The remaining 5% largely consisted of less-liquid tokens the company was working to acquire through over-the-counter providers.

“It’s a painful lesson. We take responsibility for it,” Teng said, adding that the company would publish a detailed post-mortem of the incident.

The comments came days after the Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed the October 29 theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group. North Korea has rejected the allegation, describing Washington’s claims as “absurd rhetoric”.

Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, accused the United States of attempting to portray the country as a cybercrime state, according to North Korean state media.

The FBI said the hackers stole more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance. Blockchain records show that most of the theft occurred within approximately 20 minutes, beginning shortly after 8 PM GMT on October 29.

The incident affected digital assets across 10 blockchain networks and is potentially the largest cryptocurrency theft recorded.

The attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Binance’s wallet infrastructure to gain unauthorised control over cryptocurrency transactions.

According to the Associated Press, investigators and blockchain security researchers have examined how the attackers compromised an internet-connected hot wallet, which is used to facilitate transactions and withdrawals.

Unlike offline cold wallets, hot wallets remain connected to the internet and are therefore more exposed to cyber threats.

The attackers moved the stolen assets across multiple blockchain networks in a short period, complicating efforts to trace and recover the funds.

Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have linked the attack to TraderTraitor, citing similarities with previous operations attributed to the group.

The FBI’s attribution has added to scrutiny of North Korea’s alleged involvement in cryptocurrency thefts. However, Pyongyang has consistently denied accusations linking it to international cyberattacks.

The exchange temporarily suspended withdrawals following the breach while it investigated the incident and reviewed its security arrangements. Withdrawals resumed in phases on November 1, with additional assets becoming available on Tuesday.

Customers withdraw billions

The breach triggered a substantial outflow of funds as customers moved their assets away from the exchange.

Binance reported net withdrawals of $4.72 billion by Monday, equivalent to around 3% of the assets held on its platform.

The figure represents the difference between customer withdrawals and deposits, rather than the total value of transactions made during the period.

The exchange said the pace of withdrawals had subsequently stabilised, with hourly inflows and outflows returning to more normal levels.

Binance also launched a customer appreciation campaign offering trading-fee rebates and other incentives to encourage users to continue trading on the platform. The campaign, scheduled to run until November 21, includes rewards for eligible users and promotional returns on selected yield-generating products.

The exchange has pledged to absorb the financial losses rather than pass them on to customers. Its SAFU emergency reserve, established to protect users in exceptional circumstances, is among the resources being used to cover the affected assets.

Binance also said it had worked with law enforcement agencies, blockchain intelligence firms and other cryptocurrency companies to freeze assets linked to the attack.

The Associated Press previously reported that approximately $3 billion in stolen assets were frozen through cooperation with industry partners. However, freezing cryptocurrency does not necessarily mean that all affected funds have been recovered.

Binance, which says it has more than 335 million registered users worldwide, has faced renewed questions about the security of its systems and the safeguards used to authorise large transactions.

North Korea and cryptocurrency thefts

The FBI’s attribution to TraderTraitor places the Binance incident within a wider pattern of cryptocurrency thefts linked to North Korean state-sponsored hacking operations.

The group has been associated with several major attacks against cryptocurrency exchanges and blockchain-related businesses.

In February 2025, hackers stole approximately $1.5 billion from Dubai-based cryptocurrency exchange Bybit. The FBI also attributed that attack to North Korea.

Cybersecurity researchers say cryptocurrency theft has become an important source of illicit revenue for North Korea, which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.

Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic estimates that North Korea has stolen cryptocurrency worth $7.6 billion in 2026, more than in any previous year. Chainalysis has also identified North Korean-linked groups as responsible for a substantial share of cryptocurrency thefts.

The Binance breach has renewed concerns about the security of centralised exchanges, which hold large quantities of digital assets and rely on interconnected systems to process transactions.

Although Binance says it has restored most of the affected assets and customer withdrawals have stabilised, the incident has raised questions about the safeguards needed to protect digital assets from increasingly sophisticated attacks.

The exchange’s promised post-mortem is expected to provide further details about how the attackers gained access, how transactions were authorised and what changes will be made to prevent similar breaches.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次事件深刻揭示了交易所热钱包架构在高流动性需求与极端安全防护之间的结构性矛盾，尤其在跨链基础设施遭受针对性攻击时，中心化交易所的资产池抗风险能力面临严峻考验。作为行业头部机构，币安的快速偿付能力虽然短期内修复了用户信任，但此类合规性与安全性挑战将倒逼全球加密机构加速向多方计算（MPC）及更严苛的资产托管方案转型。

币安联席首席执行官理查德·滕(Richard Teng)周二表示，该公司“财务状况非常强劲”，存款和取款已基本恢复正常。

Teng 在香港金融科技周上发表讲话时表示，该交易所已利用其用户安全资产基金（SAFU）和其他公司资源补充了约 95% 的受影响代币。剩下的 5% 主要是该公司正在努力通过场外交易提供商收购的流动性较低的代币。

“这是一个惨痛的教训。我们对此承担责任。”滕说，并补充说该公司将发布事件的详细事后分析。

几天前，美国联邦调查局将 10 月 29 日的盗窃事件归咎于朝鲜国家支持的黑客组织 TraderTraitor。朝鲜拒绝了这一指控，称华盛顿的说法是“荒谬的言论”。

据朝鲜官方媒体报道，朝鲜领导人金正恩颇具影响力的妹妹金与正指责美国试图将朝鲜描绘成一个网络犯罪国家。

FBI 表示，黑客从币安窃取了超过 60 亿美元的加密货币。区块链记录显示，大部分盗窃发生在大约 20 分钟内，始于格林尼治标准时间 10 月 29 日晚上 8 点后不久。

该事件影响了 10 个区块链网络的数字资产，可能是有记录以来最大的加密货币盗窃案。

攻击者利用币安钱包基础设施中的漏洞来获得对加密货币交易的未经授权的控制。

调查人员和区块链安全研究人员已经研究了攻击者如何破坏连接互联网的热钱包，该钱包用于促进交易和提款。

与离线冷钱包不同，热钱包保持与互联网的连接，因此更容易受到网络威胁。

title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
title_en: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
In a blog post, complexity theorist and former OpenAI researcher Scott Aaronson lays out what AI's recent math breakthroughs might mean for the rest of us.

Proving the Riemann hypothesis probably wouldn't change anyone's daily life, Aaronson writes. The ideas behind work like that could lead to new applications in science and engineering down the road, but it's anyone's guess which ones.

Aaronson, a professor at the University of Texas at Austin, argues the far bigger deal is that AI can do this kind of work at all. In his view, that could have "staggering implications for everyday life,"from reshaping the global economy to threatening all life on Earth. "Opinions differ,"he writes, but anyone serious about the topic should set aside the "'ooga booga, me only care about Riemann proof if it help me make sharper spear' caveman act."

### OpenAI's proofs show where faster algorithms hit hard limits

Aaronson walks through an OpenAI proof about matrix multiplication. The core question is how fast computational cost grows as matrices get larger. The new result, he writes, adds a matching lower bound to an existing fast algorithm. That shows how far computational cost can actually drop, at least in the model OpenAI studied.

OpenAI got a similar result for the Fourier transform, a basic math tool behind audio, image, and signal processing. It found a faster way to compute it and also proved that it can't be done much faster. Proofs like that second one are called lower bounds, and Aaronson stresses them in particular. A new method only sets a record, but a lower bound shows where further improvements hit a hard limit.

It's now obvious that we'll be getting, not one-off solutions to this or that complexity question, but a whole new continent of mathematical truth, one that we'd previously only glimpsed through fog. Scott Aaronson

The results have also changed Aaronson's outlook on the biggest open question in his field. That question, known as P versus NP, asks whether every problem whose answer computers can check quickly can also be solved quickly. Most researchers suspect the answer is no, but nobody has proved it. "I now feel in my bones, for the first time ever, that a proof of P ≠ NP is not far,"Aaronson writes. Such a proof would confirm that some problems are easy for computers to check but hard to solve.

He adds that he's "virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources,"that AI labs are sitting on "one or more bombshells"in cryptography, but says he doesn't have the details yet. Aaronson wrote in October that AI labs were testing whether their models could break cryptographic systems.

article_content_zh:
在一篇博文中，复杂性理论家、前 OpenAI 研究员 Scott Aaronson 阐述了人工智能最近的数学突破对我们其他人可能意味着什么。

阿伦森写道，证明黎曼假设可能不会改变任何人的日常生活。此类工作背后的想法可能会在未来的科学和工程领域带来新的应用，但谁也说不准是哪些应用。

德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校教授阿伦森认为，更重要的是人工智能完全可以完成此类工作。在他看来，这可能会对“日常生活产生惊人的影响”，从重塑全球经济到威胁地球上的所有生命。 “观点不同，”他写道，但任何认真对待这个话题的人都应该抛开“‘ooga booga，我只关心黎曼证明，如果它能帮助我做出更锋利的矛’穴居人行为。”

### OpenAI 的证明表明更快的算法在哪些地方遇到了硬限制

Aaronson 介绍了有关矩阵乘法的 OpenAI 证明。核心问题是随着矩阵变大，计算成本增长的速度有多快。他写道，新结果为现有的快速算法添加了匹配的下界。这表明计算成本实际上可以下降多少，至少在 OpenAI 研究的模型中是这样。

OpenAI 对于傅里叶变换（音频、图像和信号处理背后的基本数学工具）也得到了类似的结果。它找到了一种更快的计算方法，也证明了它不可能更快地完成。像第二个这样的证明被称为下界，阿伦森特别强调了它们。一种新方法仅创下了记录，但下限表明进一步的改进达到了硬极限。

现在很明显，我们将得到的不是这个或那个复杂问题的一次性解决方案，而是一个全新的数学真理大陆，一个我们以前只能透过迷雾瞥见的大陆。斯科特阿伦森

结果也改变了阿伦森对其领域中最大的悬而未决问题的看法。这个问题被称为 P 与 NP，它询问是否每个计算机可以快速检查答案的问题也可以快速解决。大多数研究人员怀疑答案是否定的，但没有人证明这一点。 “我现在第一次从骨子里感觉到，P ≠ NP 的证明已经不远了，”阿伦森写道。这样的证明将证实有些问题对于计算机来说很容易检查但很难解决。

他补充说，他“从多个可靠来源几乎可以肯定”，人工智能实验室正坐在密码学领域的“一个或多个重磅炸弹”上，但他表示，他还没有掌握细节。 Aaronson 在 10 月份写道，人工智能实验室正在测试他们的模型是否可以破解加密系统。

title: Altair Semiconductor, an Israeli chipmaker spun off from Sony earlier in 2026, raised a $100M Series A, as it prepares to launch low-power cellular modems (CTech)
title_en: Altair Semiconductor, an Israeli chipmaker spun off from Sony earlier in 2026, raised a $100M Series A, as it prepares to launch low-power cellular modems (CTech)

inline_images.caption: Nohik Semed
inline_images.alt: Nohik Semed

author: CTech
article_content:
Altair Semiconductor, an Israeli chipmaker that returned to independence after being spun off from Sony earlier this year, has raised $100 million in a Series A round as it prepares to bring a new generation of low-power cellular modems to market. The investment comes as technology companies look beyond smartphones and computers to devices such as smart glasses, wearables and personal assistants that could rely on continuous connections to cloud-based artificial intelligence.

Full list of Israeli high-tech funding rounds in 2026 The round was led by Maverick Silicon, the semiconductor investment arm of Maverick Capital, with participation from Israeli venture capital firm Pitango. Altair said the proceeds would support the mass production of its ALT1550 modem, which is scheduled to begin in 2027, as well as the development of additional connectivity chips and expansion of its customer base in North America, Europe and Asia.

“AI is about to go everywhere we go, and every one of those devices needs a connection that is always on and consumes very little power,” said Nohik Semel, CEO of Altair Semiconductor. “That is exactly the problem Altair was built to solve. With Maverick Silicon leading this round and Pitango alongside, we have the resources to bring ALT1550 to mass production and make cellular IoT the foundation for personal AI.

Demand for ALT1550 is ahead of plan, and we are working closely with leading device makers on their next-generation devices.” The company is targeting a growing but still developing market: devices that need to communicate with AI services without depending on a smartphone for connectivity.

Smart glasses and wearable assistants, for example, could need to transmit audio, images and other data to cloud-based models throughout the day. That creates a particular engineering challenge. The devices must remain connected while operating within tight constraints on battery life, size and cost.

Altair's bet is that cellular connectivity designed for low-power devices can become an important part of that market. Its ALT1550 modem combines four connectivity standards: 5G eRedCap, 4G Cat 1bis, LTE-M and non-terrestrial network connectivity. The company says the platform will allow device manufacturers to move from 4G to 5G without redesigning their products around a particular application processor, leaving them free to select the computing chip that runs their AI applications.

The new investment also marks another step in Altair's transition from a unit of a global electronics group to an independent semiconductor company. Sony acquired the Israeli chipmaker in 2016 and later operated the business as Sony Semiconductor Israel. In November 2025, Calcalist reported that Sony planned to separate the Israeli operation and restore the Altair name, with the restructuring expected to include layoffs of several dozen employees.

The company completed its spin-off in April 2026, securing an initial $50 million in funding led by Pitango. Sony remained a shareholder following the separation.

2026 年以色列高科技融资轮次完整列表 该轮融资由 Maverick Capital 的半导体投资部门 Maverick Silicon 领投，以色列风险投资公司 Pitango 参投。 Altair 表示，所得款项将支持计划于 2027 年开始的 ALT1550 调制解调器的大规模生产，以及其他连接芯片的开发以及扩大其在北美、欧洲和亚洲的客户群。

Altair Semiconductor 首席执行官 Nohik Semel 表示：“人工智能即将无处不在，而每一个设备都需要始终保持连接状态且功耗极低。” “这正是 Altair 旨在解决的问题。在 Maverick Silicon 领投本轮融资以及 Pitango 的支持下，我们拥有资源将 ALT1550 投入批量生产，并使蜂窝物联网成为个人人工智能的基础。

对 ALT1550 的需求超出了计划，我们正在与领先的设备制造商密切合作，开发他们的下一代设备。”该公司的目标是一个不断增长但仍在发展的市场：需要与人工智能服务进行通信而不依赖智能手机进行连接的设备。

例如，智能眼镜和可穿戴助手可能需要全天将音频、图像和其他数据传输到基于云的模型。这带来了特殊的工程挑战。这些设备在电池寿命、尺寸和成本的严格限制下运行时必须保持连接。

Altair 的赌注是，专为低功耗设备设计的蜂窝连接可以成为该市场的重要组成部分。其 ALT1550 调制解调器结合了四种连接标准：5G eRedCap、4G Cat 1bis、LTE-M 和非地面网络连接。该公司表示，该平台将允许设备制造商从 4G 转向 5G，而无需围绕特定应用处理器重新设计其产品，从而使他们可以自由选择运行其人工智能应用程序的计算芯片。

这项新投资还标志着 Altair 从全球电子集团旗下子公司向独立半导体公司转型又迈出了一步。索尼于 2016 年收购了这家以色列芯片制造商，后来以索尼半导体以色列公司的名义运营该业务。 2025 年 11 月，Calcalist 报道称，索尼计划剥离以色列业务并恢复 Altair 名称，重组预计将包括裁员数十名员工。

该公司于 2026 年 4 月完成分拆，获得了由 Pitango 领投的 5000 万美元初始资金。分拆后，索尼仍是股东。

title: GPT-6.2 Astra users now hit limits 40% faster after OpenAI patched a pricing error
title_en: GPT-6.2 Astra users now hit limits 40% faster after OpenAI patched a pricing error
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
OpenAI got its math wrong. A billing bug during the GPT-6.2 rollout gave most users the wrong discounts on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, according to OpenAI Codex engineer Thibault Sottiaux.

The bug has been fixed. You'll now hit your limits 40 percent faster on Astra and 25 percent faster on Sol than last week, Sottiaux says. Your quota should still last longer than it did with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. Other models weren't affected, and OpenAI won't retroactively charge for the difference. To make up for it, all Go, Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers get an extra saved reset. Business users also get free access to Fast Mode through the end of the year, according to Sottiaux.

OpenAI is also testing merging Chat and Work mode with select Pro users. Work mode is more agentic than Chat mode, which likely means higher token costs for OpenAI. It's slower but more capable. Anthropic already made the same move with Cowork. All conversations now run in one cloud environment, where the model decides whether to answer directly or spin up a full agentic workflow.

title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Positions in AI Restructuring
title_en: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Positions in AI Restructuring

inline_images.caption: SAP reportedly weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in fresh restructuring
inline_images.alt: SAP reportedly weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in fresh restructuring

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
SAP is reportedly considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs as part of a new restructuring. The company has already spent the past two years trimming its workforce, and this would be another large reduction.

The timing is unusual. SAP’s leadership had signaled that big layoff rounds were behind it and that smaller annual trims would replace them. A cut of this size would break that pattern.

The figure under discussion is at least 10,000 positions, tied to a restructuring effort. The operative word is “considering.” A plan under evaluation is not a signed decision, and the final shape of any cuts could change.

SAP’s total workforce is somewhere around 100,000 to 110,000 employees. A reduction of 10,000 or more would affect roughly one in ten people at the company.

In January 2024, SAP launched a program it called “Next Level Transformation.” The goal was to shift its workforce toward cloud and AI-oriented roles.

The initial target was approximately 8,000 positions worldwide. By July 2024, SAP had raised that projection to between 9,000 and 10,000 jobs, roughly 8-10% of its global headcount.

The program was expensive. It carried an additional €800 million in costs, with SAP anticipating €200 million in annual savings.

Germany, SAP’s home market, took a large share of the changes. About 3,500 positions there were cut, equal to 14% of the local workforce. SAP handled those reductions mainly through voluntary early retirement and severance packages rather than forced layoffs.

Execution fell behind the plan. By April 2025, only about 3,000 employees had departed under the initiative. That left a cushion of several thousand positions as the economic climate stayed uncertain.

After the big program, SAP moved to a different model: continuous workforce adjustments known internally as “Project Mongoose.” The plan calls for annual reductions of 1-2% of the workforce, driven by productivity gains from AI.

Since September 2025, those smaller yearly cuts have become standard practice.

CEO Christian Klein and CFO Dominik Asam had said that no new large-scale job cuts were expected immediately. They also said incremental reductions would continue into 2026 and beyond, guided by updated agreements with labor representatives.

A cut of at least 10,000 roles would contradict that messaging. Annual trims of 1-2% on a workforce of SAP’s size come to far fewer jobs than what is now reportedly being discussed.

SAP aims to deliver cost reductions exceeding €2 billion while pushing growth in other markets.

India is the clearest example. SAP plans to double its Bengaluru campus, which currently houses 15,000 staff, to make room for more hiring.

Leadership has also talked up reskilling. The argument is that existing employees can move into roles that use AI instead of being replaced outright.

For employees, especially in Germany, the last round relied heavily on voluntary exits and early retirement, negotiated with labor representatives. Whether a new restructuring uses the same approach, or relies more on direct layoffs, will determine how disruptive it is.

The open questions are whether SAP confirms the plan, how many roles are ultimately affected, which regions take the biggest share, and how much the company expects to spend and save. In the 2024 program, announced targets and actual departures diverged. A new plan could do the same.

article_content_zh:
作为新重组的一部分，SAP 正在考虑裁员至少 10,000 人。该公司在过去两年中已经进行了裁员，这将是又一次大幅裁员。

时机不寻常。 SAP 领导层曾表示，大规模裁员已经过去，较小规模的年度裁员将取而代之。这种尺寸的切割会打破这种模式。

正在讨论的数字是至少 10,000 个与重组工作相关的职位。关键词是“考虑”。正在评估的计划并非已签署的决定，任何削减的最终形式都可能发生变化。

SAP 的员工总数约为 100,000 至 110,000 名员工。裁员 10,000 人或更多将影响公司大约十分之一的员工。

2024 年 1 月，SAP 启动了一项名为“Next Level Transformation”的计划。目标是将员工队伍转向以云和人工智能为导向的角色。

最初的目标是在全球范围内提供大约 8,000 个职位。到 2024 年 7 月，SAP 已将这一预测提高到 9,000 至 10,000 个工作岗位，约占其全球员工总数的 8-10%。

该计划非常昂贵。它额外增加了 8 亿欧元的成本，SAP 预计每年可节省 2 亿欧元。

SAP 的本土市场德国在变化中占据了很大份额。大约有 3,500 个职位被裁减，相当于当地劳动力的 14%。 SAP 主要通过自愿提前退休和遣散费来处理这些裁员，而不是强制裁员。

日常的。自由的。加入加密货币、金融和政策领域 34,000 多名读者的行列。

我们尊重您的隐私。随时取消订阅。

执行进度落后于计划。到 2025 年 4 月，只有约 3,000 名员工在该计划下离职。由于经济环境仍然不确定，这留下了数千个职位的缓冲。

在这个大型项目之后，SAP 转向了一种不同的模式：持续的劳动力调整，内部称为“Project Mongoose”。该计划要求在人工智能生产力提高的推动下，每年减少 1-2% 的劳动力。

自 2025 年 9 月以来，每年较小的削减已成为标准做法。

title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Positions in AI Restructuring
title_en: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Positions in AI Restructuring

inline_images.caption: SAP reportedly weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in fresh restructuring
inline_images.alt: SAP reportedly weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in fresh restructuring

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
SAP is reportedly considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs as part of a new restructuring. The company has already spent the past two years trimming its workforce, and this would be another large reduction.

The timing is unusual. SAP’s leadership had signaled that big layoff rounds were behind it and that smaller annual trims would replace them. A cut of this size would break that pattern.

The figure under discussion is at least 10,000 positions, tied to a restructuring effort. The operative word is “considering.” A plan under evaluation is not a signed decision, and the final shape of any cuts could change.

SAP’s total workforce is somewhere around 100,000 to 110,000 employees. A reduction of 10,000 or more would affect roughly one in ten people at the company.

In January 2024, SAP launched a program it called “Next Level Transformation.” The goal was to shift its workforce toward cloud and AI-oriented roles.

The initial target was approximately 8,000 positions worldwide. By July 2024, SAP had raised that projection to between 9,000 and 10,000 jobs, roughly 8-10% of its global headcount.

The program was expensive. It carried an additional €800 million in costs, with SAP anticipating €200 million in annual savings.

Germany, SAP’s home market, took a large share of the changes. About 3,500 positions there were cut, equal to 14% of the local workforce. SAP handled those reductions mainly through voluntary early retirement and severance packages rather than forced layoffs.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

Execution fell behind the plan. By April 2025, only about 3,000 employees had departed under the initiative. That left a cushion of several thousand positions as the economic climate stayed uncertain.

After the big program, SAP moved to a different model: continuous workforce adjustments known internally as “Project Mongoose.” The plan calls for annual reductions of 1-2% of the workforce, driven by productivity gains from AI.

Since September 2025, those smaller yearly cuts have become standard practice.

CEO Christian Klein and CFO Dominik Asam had said that no new large-scale job cuts were expected immediately. They also said incremental reductions would continue into 2026 and beyond, guided by updated agreements with labor representatives.

A cut of at least 10,000 roles would contradict that messaging. Annual trims of 1-2% on a workforce of SAP’s size come to far fewer jobs than what is now reportedly being discussed.

SAP aims to deliver cost reductions exceeding €2 billion while pushing growth in other markets.

India is the clearest example. SAP plans to double its Bengaluru campus, which currently houses 15,000 staff, to make room for more hiring.

Leadership has also talked up reskilling. The argument is that existing employees can move into roles that use AI instead of being replaced outright.

For employees, especially in Germany, the last round relied heavily on voluntary exits and early retirement, negotiated with labor representatives. Whether a new restructuring uses the same approach, or relies more on direct layoffs, will determine how disruptive it is.

The open questions are whether SAP confirms the plan, how many roles are ultimately affected, which regions take the biggest share, and how much the company expects to spend and save. In the 2024 program, announced targets and actual departures diverged. A new plan could do the same.

article_content:
The move comes days after the highly anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Chris Kerr Nov 26, 2026 November 26 2026 2:47 PM 2 min read Share Share Share Share Share Email Copy UK workers at Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar Games have voted against a union recognition deal that would have seen the Rockstar Game Workers Union (RGWU) become the largest recognised union in the UK video game sector.

Rockstar confirmed the news in a statement to press. Vertical Slice understands 1,544 employees—93.2 percent of eligible workers—participated in the ballot.

"We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together," said a company rep.

RGWU is part of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB).

In the UK, union recognition means an employer has officially agreed to deal with a union representing a section of workers. Although it clears the way for formal negotiations, workers in the country do not need their employer's permission to join a trade union. That's why RGWU already exists.

The vote was open to 1,600 employees below the level of director and ran from November 12 to November 26, overlapping with the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.

The IWGB said 25 percent of eligible workers voted in favour of the deal, with 75 percent voting against. It added the result "does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives."

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen," added the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union.

Workers have chosen to shoot down a deal that included pay negotiation frameworks covering overtime and bonuses, leave and pensions, and more. It would have also provided consultation rights over HR policies and the use of generative AI in the workplace.

The news comes with Rockstar and a group of fired workers awaiting the outcome of a high-profile employment tribunal centred on allegations of union busting. Last year, Rockstar dismissed over 30 workers who claimed they were ousted for engaging in trade union activity. The studio says they were let go for leaking confidential information in a union Discord server.

Chris Kerr Chris is an award-winning reporter with over a decade of experience covering the video game industry. He was formerly news editor at Game Developer and is currently the founder and editor of this resplendent website.

article_content_zh:
此举是在备受期待的《侠盗猎车手 VI》发布几天后进行的。

Chris Kerr 2026 年 11 月 26 日 2026 年 11 月 26 日 2:47 PM 2 分钟阅读 侠盗猎车手制造商 Rockstar Games 的英国工人投票反对工会认可协议，该协议将使 Rockstar 游戏工人工会 (RGWU) 成为英国视频游戏行业最大的认可工会。

Rockstar 在一份给媒体的声明中证实了这一消息。 Vertical Slice 了解到有 1,544 名员工（占合格员工的 93.2%）参与了投票。

“我们对我们的团队、我们共同打造的文化以及《侠盗猎车手 VI》的推出感到非常自豪。这一结果反映了我们团队对继续保持直接关系、协作和开放对话的大力支持，正是这些因素帮助 Rockstar Games 变得如此创新和强大。展望未来，我们很高兴能在我们共同取得的成就的基础上再接再厉。”公司代表说道。

RGWU 是英国独立工人联盟 (IWGB) 的一部分。

在英国，工会认可意味着雇主已正式同意与代表一部分工人的工会打交道。尽管这为正式谈判扫清了道路，但该国的工人不需要雇主的许可即可加入工会。这就是 RGWU 存在的原因。

此次投票向董事级别以下的 1,600 名员工开放，投票时间为 11 月 12 日至 11 月 26 日，与期待已久的《侠盗猎车手 VI》的发布时间重叠。

IWGB 表示，25% 的合格工人投票赞成该协议，75% 的人投票反对。它补充说，结果“并不阻止 Rockstar 工人与 IWGB 组织起来或行使其工会权利，但意味着管理层不会正式承诺与工会代表定期举行会议。”

IWGB Rockstar 游戏工人工会补充道：“对于 Rockstar 任何相信更公平的工作场所、更公平的行业和更公平的社会的人来说，这不是撤退的迹象，而是加倍努力的迹象。我们数百名同事投票支持 Rockstar 工会，但遗憾的是，我们认识到我们还有更多工作要做，以建立理解并赢得更多同事的信任。我们已准备好努力实现这一目标。”

工人们选择否决一项包含加班费、奖金、休假和养老金等薪资谈判框架的协议。它还将提供有关人力资源政策和在工作场所使用生成式人工智能的咨询权。

这一消息传出之际，Rockstar 和一群被解雇的工人正在等待一场备受瞩目的就业法庭的结果，该法庭以破坏工会的指控为中心。去年，Rockstar 解雇了 30 多名声称因参与工会活动而被解雇的员工。该工作室表示，他们因泄露工会 Discord 服务器中的机密信息而被解雇。

Chris Kerr Chris 是一位屡获殊荣的记者，拥有十多年报道视频游戏行业的经验。他曾担任 Game Developer 的新闻编辑，目前是这个辉煌网站的创始人和编辑。

title: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
title_en: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
author: derstruct
content_snippet: HN 极客热议: 1 点赞, 0 讨论
summary_en: Neui has launched an integrated stack that combines a Go-based web framework (Doors) with an AI agent. By allowing developers to annotate UI elements, the agent can interact with the page, execute backend scripts, and automate workflows natively without the need for additional API layers or state synchronization.
article_content:
Neui is an AI agent and a web framework built as one stack. The framework, Doors (Apache-2.0), lets Go teams build modern interactive apps with no separate frontend and no API layer. Neui adds the agent: it runs inside the user's session, sees the parts of the page you let it see, operates the UI like a user, and brings its own work environment for the jobs a chat alone cannot do.

Every feature you build for users is instantly usable by the agent, with a work environment powerful enough to automate the work your users do by hand.

Developers mark which parts of the page the agent may see and use, right in the existing markup. The agent then clicks, types and reads like a user, and the app's own logic runs. There is no per-action code to write and no state to mirror.

A tool is one Go function that runs on the server, with no endpoint or permission code to write. Developers decide what the agent can see and do right where they build the UI, so its access is scoped to each user and updates with the screen.

The agent gets its own file workspace, scripts that run bulk UI work in one step, spreadsheets, web search, MCP connectors, background tasks, and automatic handling of long conversations. One script can call every tool and work across the whole UI in a single step.

When a user needs functionality your UI doesn't have, the agent builds it on the spot, anything from a single screen to a specialized app. It runs in the page with the user's permissions, and the agent stays in the loop to make the decisions.

Your users get the chat experience they already know from chat apps, with nothing to build or purchase.

The conversation is prompt-cache friendly, so input costs an estimated 6 to 14 times less than in copilots that rebuild the prompt for every screen, depending on the provider's cache pricing. Built-in scripts do bulk work without extra model turns or context bloat.

The conversation, instructions and tools live on the server, and the browser sends only the user's new message. A tampered browser can't add tools, rewrite history or change what the agent is told.

Every open page runs on the server, integrated with the agent harness. You mark in the page template what the agent may see and use.

Works the real UI. The agent reads, fills and clicks the elements you mark, as the user would, and your handlers run as usual. There's no state to mirror and no action to re-implement.

~>neui.Use{ Desc: "Customer's email", // RW: the agent reads the value in the user's browser or writes its own. Rights: neui.RW, } <input type="email" name="email"> Tools in the template. Register agent tools right in the page template, based on the UI context and the user's permissions.

~(if user.IsAdmin() { ~neui.Tool[Refund, Receipt]{ Name: "refund", Desc: "Refund the order", Handler: orders.Refund, } }) Persistent tools. Go functions registered for the whole app or for one session are available in every chat. The built-in work environment works the same way.

crm := neui.NewModule("crm", "Customer records of the signed-in user") crm.Tool("find", "Find a customer by name or email", customers.Find) Page context. Attach data to a part of the page to tell the agent what it shows, such as the records in a view or hints on how to use it.

~neui.Data{ Text: "Open orders of this customer", Object: orders, } App events. Your app can tell the agent when something happens, such as a payment arriving. An idle agent reacts right away, and a busy one picks it up on its next turn.

neui.Instance(ctx).Emit(ctx, "payment_received", map[string]string{"invoice": id}, nil) Stays in sync without token waste. The framework tracks tools, data and elements as the page changes, and the agent reads them only when it needs to.

An agentic app is a program the agent writes and runs for the user in an island, a region of the page. You declare the island in the page template and give it the components and Go functions its apps may use.

~neui.Island{ Name: "workbench", Desc: "Apps for the user's invoice work", Template: func(slot gox.Comp) gox.Elem { return <section>~(slot)</section> }, Library: func(l neui.Library) error { l.Tool("overdue", "Overdue invoices, one page at a time", invoices.Overdue) l.Tool("remind", "Send a payment reminder", invoices.Remind) return nekit.IslandRegisterAll(l) }, } The agent writes a program. It builds an app for the user's request from your component library and the tools you declare, and runs it right away. The model is called only for decisions. The app handles user actions itself and calls the agent only when a decision is needed. The UI stays responsive, no tokens are spent on routine steps, and the agent is still in the loop. Data stays out of the context. The agent works with data through the app's script, without loading it into its context. Data costs no tokens, and text inside it can't steer the agent. App changes on the fly. The user can ask for an extra column, another step or a different check, and the agent updates the running app without losing their work. Runs with the user's permissions. The app is sandboxed and can do only what the signed-in user can, through the components and functions you declared, with no endpoints to build. Widgets included. neui.dev/nekit includes a general-purpose widget set built to cover any business flow, from data entry to review and reporting. It takes your theme from CSS variables, and your own components work alongside it.

Compared with declarative generative UI. In A2UI and similar formats the model describes the screen, and every user action is another model turn. That suits a one-off screen such as a confirmation. An agentic app is cheaper and faster as soon as the user does more than a few things.

Neui ships a complete chat experience out of the box. Use it as is, configure its theme and features, or fork it to build something of your own.

Besides the chat and the page, the agent has a workspace on the server for real work.

The usual alternatives are CopilotKit (plus paid Intelligence), Vercel AI SDK with Sandbox, assistant-ui, OpenAI ChatKit, LangGraph with Agent Server, browser agents and WebMCP. For a Go team each of them means bolting on a React island, CopilotKit and a Node runtime: a second stack.

Each row was checked against neui's code and the competitors' current docs and source. Competitor cells describe the default open-source path.

go get neui.dev Neui is a Go module (neui.dev) that plugs into a Doors app: you configure the agent once with options on the Doors app, turn it on per session once the user is known, and render nekit.Chat on the pages where the user should talk to the agent.

Claude, GPT, Gemini and DeepSeek providers are included, plus a generic one for any server with an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API, such as Ollama, vLLM or OpenRouter. SQLite thread storage and disk or S3 upload storage are included too.

Start with the quick start and the back office example, and see the package documentation in doc.go, api/doc.go and nekit/doc.go, and the Doors documentation for building the app itself.

article_content_zh:
Neui 是一种 AI 代理和作为一个堆栈构建的 Web 框架。 Doors (Apache-2.0) 框架让 Go 团队可以构建没有单独前端和 API 层的现代交互式应用程序。 Neui 添加了代理：它在用户会话内运行，查看您让它查看的页面部分，像用户一样操作 UI，并为仅聊天无法完成的工作带来自己的工作环境。

您为用户构建的每个功能都可以立即被代理使用，并且工作环境足够强大，可以自动执行用户手动完成的工作。

开发人员在现有标记中标记代理可以查看和使用页面的哪些部分。然后，代理像用户一样单击、键入和阅读，然后应用程序自己的逻辑运行。无需编写每个操作的代码，也无需镜像状态。

工具是在服务器上运行的一个 Go 函数，无需编写端点或权限代码。开发人员决定代理可以在构建 UI 的位置看到什么并执行哪些操作，因此其访问范围仅限于每个用户并随屏幕更新。

该代理拥有自己的文件工作区、一步运行批量 UI 工作的脚本、电子表格、Web 搜索、MCP 连接器、后台任务以及长对话的自动处理。一个脚本可以调用每个工具，并且只需一步即可在整个 UI 上工作。

当用户需要您的 UI 没有的功能时，代理会当场构建它，从单个屏幕到专门的应用程序。它在具有用户权限的页面中运行，代理留在循环中做出决策。

您的用户可以获得他们已经从聊天应用程序中获得的聊天体验，无需构建或购买任何内容。

对话是提示缓存友好的，因此输入成本估计比为每个屏幕重建提示的副驾驶低 6 到 14 倍，具体取决于提供商的缓存定价。内置脚本可以完成批量工作，无需额外的模型轮转或上下文膨胀。

对话、指令和工具位于服务器上，浏览器仅发送用户的新消息。被篡改的浏览器无法添加工具、重写历史记录或更改代理被告知的内容。

每个打开的页面都在服务器上运行，并与代理工具集成。您在页面模板中标记代理可以看到和使用的内容。

运行真实的 UI。代理会像用户一样读取、填充和单击您标记的元素，并且您的处理程序将照常运行。没有要镜像的状态，也没有要重新实施的操作。

~>neui.Use{ Desc: "Customer's email", // RW: 代理读取用户浏览器中的值或写入自己的值。权限：neui.RW, } <input type="email" name="email"> 模板中的工具。根据 UI 上下文和用户权限，直接在页面模板中注册代理工具。

~(如果user.IsAdmin() {~neui。工具[退款，收据]{名称：“退款”，说明：“订单退款”，处理：订单。退款，}})持久化工具。为整个应用程序或一个会话注册的Go函数在每次聊天中都可用。内置的工作环境也是如此。

crm := neui.NewModule("crm", "登录用户的客户记录") crm.Tool("find", "通过姓名或电子邮件查找客户",customers.Find) 页面上下文。将数据附加到页面的一部分，以告诉代理它显示的内容，例如视图中的记录或如何使用它的提示。

title: Avicena, which links AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers, raised a $100M+ Series C led by Intervest, with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD (Cristian Dina/The Next Web)
title_en: Avicena, which links AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers, raised a $100M+ Series C led by Intervest, with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD (Cristian Dina/The Next Web)

inline_images.caption: Avicena’s connectorised LightBundle microLED link, shown in September 2026 Credit: Avicena
inline_images.alt: Avicena’s connectorised LightBundle microLED link, shown in September 2026 Credit: Avicena

author: The Next Web
article_content:
Avicena, a Sunnyvale startup that links AI chips with tiny LEDs instead of lasers, has raised more than $100M in Series C funding. It also has a new chief executive. Kevin Pope succeeds Marco Chisari and will lead the company as it brings its first product to market next year.

InterVest led the round, Avicena announced on Tuesday. Other investors include Tiger Global, Cerberus Capital Management, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund and AMD Ventures. Prosperity7 Ventures, Mitsubishi Chemical’s Diamond Edge Ventures and Hitachi Ventures also took part. InterVest director John Dongwoo Ha joins Avicena’s board.

“AI infrastructure needs a new approach to moving data between accelerators, memory, and switches,” Pope said.

AI systems move ever more data between accelerators, memory and switches. Copper links face limits on reach, density and energy use, Avicena says. Memory bandwidth and capacity also increasingly hold systems back. SK hynix, one of the investors, has said the memory shortage will last until 2030.

Avicena’s LightBundle platform uses dense arrays of microLEDs and silicon photodetectors linked by multicore fibre. Rather than pushing a few channels very fast, it spreads data across many slower ones. That, the company says, cuts the need for data-rate conversion and complex signal processing.

Because it needs no lasers, the platform can sit close to compute and memory chips. Avicena pitches it for links inside and between chip packages, and across accelerator systems. By contrast, Photon Bridge raised $10M last month to build lasers for AI data centres.

Avicena began shipping 1Tbps LightBundle evaluation kits in August. In September, it announced a version with connectors for the ECOC 2026 optics conference. It is meant to make assembly, testing and servicing easier.

The money will go on hiring, product development and engineering, Pope said. Two of the chipmakers behind the round see a role for the technology in memory.

“Energy-efficient optical interconnects are becoming increasingly important to next-generation memory architectures,” said SK hynix Ventures’ Rene Do.

SK hynix Ventures said it hopes to work with Avicena on future memory interconnects. Energy and data movement limit the AI build-out, said Samsung Catalyst Fund’s David Goldschmidt. AMD Ventures’ Patrick Rundell said moving data between compute, memory and networking chips is becoming critical.

Earlier this month, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum, the Nvidia-backed optical component maker, in an all-stock deal.

The backing from key memory and processor giants signals a shift from prototype development to systemic commercialization for optical interconnects.

article_content_zh:
Avicena 是一家桑尼维尔初创公司，将 AI 芯片与微型 LED（而不是激光器）连接起来，已在 C 轮融资中筹集了超过 1 亿美元。它还任命了一位新首席执行官。 Kevin Pope 接替 Marco Chisari，并将领导该公司明年将首款产品推向市场。

Avicena 周二宣布，InterVest 领投此轮融资。其他投资者包括 Tiger Global、Cerberus Capital Management、SK hynix Ventures、Samsung Catalyst Fund 和 AMD Ventures。 Prosperity7 Ventures、三菱化学旗下的 Diamond Edge Ventures 和 Hitachi Ventures 也参与其中。 InterVest 董事 John Dongwoo Ha 加入 Avicena 董事会。

“人工智能基础设施需要一种新的方法来在加速器、内存和交换机之间移动数据，”波普说。

人工智能系统在加速器、内存和交换机之间移动越来越多的数据。阿维塞纳表示，铜链路在覆盖范围、密度和能源使用方面面临限制。内存带宽和容量也越来越阻碍系统的发展。投资者之一SK海力士表示，内存短缺将持续到2030年。

Avicena 的 LightBundle 平台使用密集的 microLED 阵列和通过多核光纤连接的硅光电探测器。它不是非常快地推送几个通道，而是将数据传播到许多较慢的通道上。该公司表示，这减少了对数据速率转换和复杂信号处理的需求。

由于不需要激光器，该平台可以靠近计算和存储芯片。 Avicena 将其用于芯片封装内部、芯片封装之间以及加速器系统之间的链接。相比之下，Photon Bridge 上个月筹集了 1000 万美元，用于为人工智能数据中心制造激光器。

Avicena 于 8 月开始发货 1Tbps LightBundle 评估套件。 9 月，它为 ECOC 2026 光学会议发布了带有连接器的版本。它旨在使组装、测试和维修变得更加容易。

波普说，这笔钱将用于招聘、产品开发和工程。本轮融资背后的两家芯片制造商看到了该技术在内存领域的作用。

SK hynix Ventures 的 Rene Do 表示：“节能光学互连对于下一代内存架构变得越来越重要。”

SK hynix Ventures 表示希望与 Avicena 就未来的内存互连领域展开合作。三星催化剂基金的 David Goldschmidt 表示，能源和数据移动限制了人工智能的发展。 AMD Ventures 的 Patrick Rundell 表示，在计算、内存和网络芯片之间移动数据变得至关重要。

本月早些时候，Marvell 同意以全股票交易的方式收购 Nvidia 支持的光学元件制造商 Lumentum。

title: After OpenAI and Anthropic shut the door on their data, a Chinese AI developer is turning to Google and Meta instead
title_en: After OpenAI and Anthropic shut the door on their data, a Chinese AI developer is turning to Google and Meta instead
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
Chinese AI companies Z.AI and Moonshot AI have to delay their next flagship models and are looking for new sources of training data. The effects now reach beyond previously known delays, after the US closed the cloud loophole for Nvidia chips, Nvidia halted shipments to Southeast Asia, and US companies cracked down on model distillation.

As a result, Z.AI's roughly 3-trillion-parameter GLM-5.5 model, planned for November, is likely to slip into the first quarter of 2027, Reuters reports, citing sources. To bridge the gap, the company released the 750-billion-parameter GLM-5.4 on Monday and says a new design lets it keep up with systems that have 2 to 3 trillion parameters. Without foreign computing power, Moonshot AI's development cycle could double from six to 12 months, likely delaying its next major model, Kimi K4, until mid-2027.

With OpenAI and Anthropic blocking data scraping for distillation, Moonshot is now turning to the latest models from Google and Meta for training and stepping up its search for compute capacity in Europe, according to the sources.
