title: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
title_en: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
author: Stephanie Findlay
article_content:
This article is an on-site version of our Energy Source newsletter. Premium subscribers can sign up here to get the newsletter delivered every Tuesday and Thursday. Standard subscribers can upgrade to Premium here, or explore all FT newsletters

Hello and welcome to Energy Source, coming to you from Houston.

Just as many suspected, Texas’s data centre freeze did not last long. Last week, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality resumed “the issuance of all permits related to data centre projects”.

TCEQ granted three air pollution permits for SpaceX’s $24bn Boca Chica gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility outside Brownsville, CloudBurst’s power plant near San Marcos and Atlas Energy Solutions’ facility north-east of Abilene.

TCEQ resumed issuing the permits after receiving a directive from outgoing Republican governor Greg Abbott’s office. The directive said the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, which manages the state’s electrical grid, had finished gathering information on how data centres affect local communities.

Data centre developers are rushing to get permits approved in the final weeks before the Texas Legislature meets in January under incoming Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa, who pledged to rein in data centre construction during her campaign.

Hinojosa said she would establish a moratorium on new development, end tax breaks for the industry and give local communities a greater say on the construction of new facilities.

Even before the midterm vote, Abbott had shifted from his pro-data centre pitch, issuing a wave of regulatory recommendations for the industry. Those included data centres paying their own way, bringing their own water and protecting the Texas grid.

The data centre boom has already slowed significantly as Ercot processes developer requests. In August, Ercot was considering more than 474 gigawatts of requests to connect to the grid.

But only 204 projects representing 66.4GW met the grid operator’s qualifications to be conditionally included as “base load”, meaning they will most likely be energised with their initial request, according to an Ercot update in September.

A further 158 projects worth 127.9GW met the qualifications to be conditionally included as “studied load”, meaning they may be given different allocations and wait longer to be connected to the grid. The Ercot interconnection study is only expected to start in April 2027 with no date set for completion, according to a lawyer familiar with the Ercot process.

Developers in Texas have already been choosing to build their own power centres to avoid delays, according to analysis by Cleanview, a market intelligence company that tracks data centre development.

Of 59 US data centres with a combined capacity of about 90GW that plan to build their own “behind-the-metre” power, almost half of that capacity is in the Lone Star State, where developers are taking advantage of the region’s ample gas supplies in the Permian Basin, extensive pipeline infrastructure and lax regulatory environment.

Hyperscalers are moving beyond gas turbines to get projects up and running, turning to companies including ERock, which manufactures generators running on natural gas. The Houston-based company’s data centre clients in Texas include Meta, Anthropic and Microsoft.

Its generators are also installed in H-E-B grocery stores across the state, helping the supermarket chain stay powered during Texas’s frequent weather disasters, including Winter Storm Uri in 2021, when there was a catastrophic grid failure.

“We have the ability to add 1.2GW in 12 months at a cost of $20mn or less,” said ERock’s chief executive John Carrington.

ERock, which went public in June, is expanding its Houston factory as it fulfils its $1.7bn contracted backlog for its generators.

Carrington said that while he expected business to remain strong in Texas, home to the bulk of the company’s operations, increased scrutiny might prompt data centre developers to explore building elsewhere.

“I think what we’re seeing now is a lot of states saying ‘come to us’, such as Arkansas, Oklahoma, West Virginia,” said Carrington, adding that “it’s not like [data centres] have a metric that says they need to stay in each state”.

Tyler Rosenlicht, portfolio manager of global listed infrastructure at Cohen & Steers, a New York investment manager, said there was significant regulatory uncertainty surrounding data centre construction after the Democrats’ election landslide.

“It does feel like there is a meaningful speed bump that is put in the road post-midterms; the question is how much of a speed bump is it and does it make the wheels fall off?”

Rosenlicht added: “We do believe all the hyperscaler capex is going to occur. It will just be reallocated a bit.”

Billionaire financier Todd Boehly said he had agreed a deal to acquire the international assets of Russian oil company Lukoil.

Opec+’s biggest oil producers are heading for a showdown over estimates of their production capacity and potential output cuts.

Britain’s energy price cap is set to rise by 26 per cent from January following a surge in the cost of gas sparked by the Iran war.

Energy Source is written by Jamie Smyth, Martha Muir, Rachel Millard, Malcolm Moore, Stephanie Findlay and Verity Ratcliffe with support from the FT’s global team of reporters. 正如许多人所怀疑的那样，德克萨斯州数据中心的冻结并没有持续很长时间。上周，德克萨斯州环境质量委员会恢复了“与数据中心项目相关的所有许可证的发放”。

TCEQ 为 SpaceX 耗资 240 亿美元的 Boca Chica 燃气发电厂和布朗斯维尔外的超级计算设施、圣马科斯附近的 CloudBurst 发电厂以及阿比林东北部的 Atlas Energy Solutions 设施颁发了三项空气污染许可证。

在收到即将卸任的共和党州长格雷格·阿博特办公室的指示后，TCEQ 恢复发放许可证。该指令称，管理该州电网的德克萨斯州电力可靠性委员会已完成数据中心如何影响当地社区的信息收集。

即将上任的民主党州长吉娜·伊诺霍萨 (Gina Hinojosa) 承诺在竞选期间控制数据中心建设，数据中心开发商正急于在 1 月份得克萨斯州立法机构会议之前的最后几周获得许可。

伊诺霍萨表示，她将暂停新开发项目，终止该行业的税收减免，并赋予当地社区在新设施建设方面更大的发言权。

甚至在中期投票之前，雅培就已经放弃了对数据中心的支持，为该行业发布了一波监管建议。其中包括数据中心自行付费、自带水以及保护德克萨斯州电网。

随着 Ercot 处理开发人员的请求，数据中心的繁荣已经显着放缓。 8 月份，Ercot 正在考虑超过 474 吉瓦的并网请求。

但根据 Ercot 9 月份的更新，只有代表 66.4GW 的 204 个项目符合电网运营商有条件纳入“基本负荷”的资格，这意味着它们很可能会根据最初的要求获得供电。

另外158个项目价值127.9GW符合有条件地纳入“研究负荷”的资格，这意味着它们可能会获得不同的分配并等待更长的时间才能并网。据一位熟悉 Ercot 流程的律师称，Ercot 互连研究预计将于 2027 年 4 月开始，尚未确定完成日期。

根据跟踪数据中心开发的市场情报公司 Cleanview 的分析，德克萨斯州的开发商已经选择建立自己的电力中心以避免延误。

美国有 59 个数据中心，总容量约为 90GW，计划建设自己的“后台”电力，其中近一半位于孤星州，开发商正在利用该地区二叠纪盆地充足的天然气供应、广泛的管道基础设施和宽松的监管环境。

超大规模企业正在超越燃气轮机来启动和运行项目，转向包括 ERock 在内的公司，该公司生产天然气发电机。这家总部位于休斯顿的公司在德克萨斯州的数据中心客户包括 Meta、Anthropic 和 Microsoft。

title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040
title_en: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
SpaceX has won approval from US communications regulators for its Starmind constellation. Up to 1 million satellites would process AI data in orbit.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites for orbital data centers, according to Reuters. The Starmind constellation of orbital compute modules is intended to meet part of the rapidly growing demand for AI computing power on Earth. The agency also approved radio links that let SpaceX monitor and control the satellites if their optical connections fail.

title: UK plans strict rules for crypto DeFi sector
title_en: UK plans strict rules for crypto DeFi sector

inline_images.caption: The FCA says a stricter approach is needed to counter the chance of fraud, scams and money laundering © Chris Batson/Alamy
inline_images.alt: The FCA says a stricter approach is needed to counter the chance of fraud, scams and money launderin

author: Martin Arnold and Nikou Asgari
article_content:
The UK financial regulator is planning to impose tight restrictions on the decentralised finance crypto sector, pointing to the recent $6.3bn heist at Binance as a reason to take a stricter approach than the US or EU to a sector that has long spurned government regulation.

The Financial Conduct Authority told the FT it planned to push ahead with requirements for so-called DeFi platforms to be authorised under its new rules. This would affect many blockchain-based services that are structured to have no controlling entity.

FCA officials said they were taking a deliberately strict approach to DeFi because of what they saw as a high risk of fraud, scams and money laundering and the limited ability of consumers to recover stolen assets or seek compensation.

DeFi platforms use automated smart contracts to execute trades or carry out borrowing and lending, rather than using traditional brokers or other intermediaries. Proponents value the sector’s independence from the financial mainstream and from government oversight.

Users of DeFi platforms typically hold their funds in their own self-custody wallets, rather than using custody services offered by centralised exchanges. Its advocates say DeFi provides a faster and better approach, but critics worry that the largely unregulated sector carries considerable risks.

The FCA pointed to last month’s record $6.3bn hack at centralised exchange Binance as a reason why DeFi platforms require regulation. As part of their efforts to launder the stolen money, the thieves moved vast amounts of tokens through DeFi exchanges, which do not freeze stolen assets, and converted them into other tokens to make them harder to trace.

“Recent hacks have underlined that operational resilience concerns are a challenge around DeFi,” said Jane Moore, head of department for payments and digital assets at the FCA.

“The speed and scale at which stolen funds move through DeFi platforms can frustrate attempts to freeze and block [their] transfer,” she said. “We are keen to see industry solutions to tackle this money laundering.”

Crypto executives say the UK’s position will put the country at a disadvantage by depriving British investors of innovative new products and services such as tokenised equities and crypto lending on decentralised platforms.

AAVE is the world’s biggest decentralised lending platform. Linda Jeng, chief legal and policy officer at AAVE Labs, a software company that builds products on the platform, has been lobbying the FCA to change its position, which Jeng called “highly problematic”.

“We’d be going down the wrong regulatory path; it’s about where along the technology stack it is appropriate to apply regulation,” she said.

Jeng has written to the FCA seeking clarification over what constitutes a “service provider” to DeFi platforms, and whether this includes companies engaged in activities such as providing fee information or sanctions screening. She argued that the FCA should not regulate activities that contribute to the security of decentralised platforms.

George Osborne, the former UK chancellor now advising US crypto exchange Coinbase, said blocking regulated companies from transferring clients to DeFi services would prevent them from acting as “gatekeepers” of the unregulated sector.

Moore said this was deliberate and reflected “a clear divide” between the regulated and unregulated sectors.

“At present, centralised regulated crypto trading platforms are not allowed to execute retail transactions on decentralised finance,” she said. “That is deliberate, considering the lack of consumer protections in place.”

EU officials are currently debating how to oversee DeFi as they look to update the bloc’s landmark crypto regulations. The European Securities and Markets Authority has proposed introducing rules allowing a crypto exchange to provide access to DeFi as a “gatekeeper” service.

DeFi is unregulated in the US, where officials say this will encourage innovation. The US Securities and Exchange Commission recently issued a five-year “innovation exemption” that allows tokenised versions of US equities and exchange-traded products to be traded on blockchain-based platforms.

A US digital assets working group last year recommended Congress “embraces DeFi technology and recognises the potential of integrating such technology into mainstream finance”. Congress has so far failed to pass landmark crypto legislation, under which decentralised platforms would not be regulated as intermediaries.

The FCA plans to require all UK retail orders for equities, whether tokenised or not, to be executed on a regulated platform, blocking access to offshore DeFi services for tokenised trades.

“Our principle is that the same risk should attract the same regulatory treatment,” said Jamie Bell, head of capital markets at the FCA. “It would be odd for tokenised equities to attract a different regulatory treatment when the underlying security is the same.”

He said the FCA’s priority was to “create a market in the UK that retail participants have confidence in, with a clear perimeter between what is in and what is out.

“If you circumvent our rules to access overseas services, you can be in no doubt that it is at your own risk.”

Katie Harries, head of policy in Europe at Coinbase, said: “The US and the EU are building rules for regulated access to DeFi, while the UK is creating a prohibition.”

summary_en: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), led by Jane Moore (Head of Payments and Digital Assets), plans to mandate authorization for DeFi platforms to close regulatory gaps in anti-money laundering and consumer protection. ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 英国此举不仅是针对特定洗钱事件的战术响应，更标志着全球加密监管正式从“中心化交易所合规”转向“协议层强制准入”的深水期。此举将极大地增加去中心化协议的合规成本，可能导致资本与技术开发者向监管更宽松的司法管辖区迁徙，从而在全球DeFi创新竞争中引发地缘监管分叉。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: This move marks a paradigm shift in global crypto regulation, transitioning from central exchange oversight to mandated protocol-level authorization. The resulting increase in compliance costs may trigger a migration of developers and capital to more permissive jurisdictions, creating a structural regulatory divergence in global DeFi innovation.

article_content_zh:
英国金融监管机构正计划对去中心化金融加密货币行业实施严格限制，并指出币安最近 63 亿美元的盗窃案是对这个长期拒绝政府监管的行业采取比美国或欧盟更严格措施的理由。

英国金融行为监管局告诉英国《金融时报》，它计划推进所谓的 DeFi 平台根据其新规则获得授权的要求。这将影响许多基于区块链的服务，这些服务的结构没有控制实体。

FCA 官员表示，他们对 DeFi 采取了刻意严格的态度，因为他们认为欺诈、诈骗和洗钱的风险很高，而且消费者追回被盗资产或寻求赔偿的能力有限。

DeFi 平台使用自动化智能合约来执行交易或进行借贷，而不是使用传统经纪人或其他中介机构。支持者重视该行业独立于金融主流和政府监管的地位。

DeFi 平台的用户通常将资金存放在自己的自助钱包中，而不是使用中心化交易所提供的托管服务。其支持者表示，DeFi 提供了一种更快、更好的方法，但批评者担心，这个基本上不受监管的行业会带来相当大的风险。

FCA 指出，上个月中心化交易所币安 (Binance) 遭受创纪录的 63 亿美元黑客攻击是 DeFi 平台需要监管的原因。作为洗钱活动的一部分，窃贼通过 DeFi 交易所转移大量代币，这些代币不会冻结被盗资产，并将其转换为其他代币，以使其更难以追踪。

FCA 支付和数字资产部门主管 Jane Moore 表示：“最近的黑客攻击凸显了运营弹性问题是 DeFi 面临的挑战。”

她说：“被盗资金通过 DeFi 平台转移的速度和规模可能会挫败冻结和阻止（其）转移的尝试。” “我们渴望看到解决洗钱问题的行业解决方案。”

加密货币高管表示，英国的立场将使该国处于不利地位，因为英国投资者将无法获得创新的新产品和服务，例如代币化股票和去中心化平台上的加密贷款。

AAVE 是全球最大的去中心化借贷平台。在该平台上构建产品的软件公司 AAVE Labs 的首席法律和政策官 Linda Jeng 一直在游说 FCA 改变其立场，Jeng 称这一立场“存在很大问题”。

“我们会走上错误的监管道路；问题在于在技术堆栈的哪个位置适合应用监管，”她说。

Jeng 已致函 FCA，寻求澄清 DeFi 平台的“服务提供商”的构成，以及这是否包括从事提供费用信息或制裁筛查等活动的公司。她认为 F​​CA 不应监管有助于去中心化平台安全的活动。

英国前财政大臣乔治·奥斯本 (George Osborne) 现为美国加密货币交易所 Coinbase 提供咨询服务，他表示，阻止受监管公司将客户转移到 DeFi 服务将阻止它们充当不受监管行业的“看门人”。

摩尔表示，这是故意的，反映了受监管部门和不受监管部门之间的“明显分歧”。

title: OpenAI says it corrected a GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch billing mistake that had incorrectly discounted usage; Astra users will now hit their limits 40% faster (Graham Barlow/TechRadar)
title_en: OpenAI says it corrected a GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch billing mistake that had incorrectly discounted usage; Astra users will now hit their limits 40% faster (Graham Barlow/TechRadar)

author: TechRadar
article_content:
If you've been enjoying using OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 models over the past week, especially since they also now work in Chat mode, I've got some bad news: OpenAI has admitted that it made a billing mistake when launching the models — and now that it's corrected the error, you'll reach your usage limits much faster.

In a post on X, OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux explained that the company had incorrectly discounted usage of its new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models for most users. As a result of this mistake being corrected, users will now hit their usage limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol, compared with last week.

OpenAI says it won't retrospectively charge users for the difference in usage and, by way of an apology, is giving Go, Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers a one-off usage reset.

When OpenAI launched its new GPT-6.2 models — Sol and Astra — it made a point of saying that “Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits.”

While Sottiaux maintains that this is still true when GPT-6.2 is compared to its predecessors, if you’ve spent the last week getting accustomed to the new models and how far your usage stretches, you’re going to have to revise those expectations.

The one-time usage reset is a welcome gesture, but it won’t change the situation in the long term.

It’s important to note that reaching your usage limits 40% faster is not mathematically equivalent to having your usage limits reduced by 40%. From my experience of using GPT-6.2, I’d say it’s very unlikely that you’ll hit your usage limit if you’re simply chatting to ChatGPT. However, if you’re a heavy user of Codex for writing code, then you’re much more likely to run into usage restrictions.

Reaction from the Reddit community to the announcement was understandably skeptical about OpenAI’s motivations. One user said “At this point I think they are actively driving users away because they don't have enough compute even for paying users”, while another said “One banked reset as an apology for burning through Astra 40% faster from now on is pretty thin lol”.

当 OpenAI 推出新的 GPT-6.2 模型（Sol 和 Astra）时，它特意表示“这两种模型都可以用更少的输出令牌在要求较高的任务上提供更好的结果，因此您可以在使用限制内完成更多工作。”

虽然 Sottiaux 坚持认为，当将 GPT-6.2 与其前身进行比较时，情况仍然如此，但如果您上周已经习惯了新模型以及您的使用范围，那么您将不得不修改这些期望。

一次性重置使用量是一种欢迎姿态，但从长远来看，它不会改变这种情况。

title: Netherlands Plans to Fight Rollout of Proposed US Curbs on ASML
title_en: Netherlands Plans to Fight Rollout of Proposed US Curbs on ASML
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
NETHERLANDS: The nationwide rollout of ERTMS in the Netherlands is proceeding too slowly, with the current pace risking a full transition only between 2060 and 2070, far beyond the original 2056 target. Now, the first steps towards a new approach to accelerate the rollout are proposed.

The Dutch ERTMS Programme Directorate describes the Dutch ERTMS rollout as ‘a major challenge for the coming decades’, and a challenge that has grown in its strategic analysis published on 9 April. It had become clear to the Directorate last year that the Netherlands is facing a “major challenge” regarding train safety, which poses a “threat to the continuity of the rail system” and was leading to rising costs for maintaining outdated systems.

To rise to this challenge, the Directorate is proposing a new approach, including an accelerated national rollout by 2040 and a shift from sequential to parallel installation across multiple regions. The ‘exploratory analysis’ examines the urgency and the possibilities for accelerating the roll-out of the ERTMS programme. The ERTMS Programme Directorate is an independent body within the rail sector that reports to the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management with input from all involved stakeholders.

The analysis points out three main reasons for the increasingly challenging ERTMS rollout. First of all, the Netherlands’ current ATB safety systems will reach the end of their lifespan between 2030 and 2040. Continuing to rely on them could force the rail sector into higher costs and reduced reliability, as knowledge of these systems declines and critical components become harder to source. Second, the GSM-R (2G) network has to be replaced by FRMCS (5G), but specifications for the new system are not expected until 2029. This situation adds further delays, as the transition requires extensive adjustments to both rolling stock and infrastructure.

Thirdly, the report highlights that the current working method, installing ERTMS in sequential tranches, is too slow and expensive. The first tranche, which began on the Northern lines, Zeeland line, and Kijfhoek-Belgian border section, has already delayed projects originally planned for the Hanzelijn, Schiphol-Amsterdam-Almere-Lelystad railway corridor (SAAL), Brabant route, and Utrecht-Meteren.

To meet the challenge, the ERTMS Programme Directorate is pushing for a more ambitious timeline: a nationwide ERTMS rollout by 2040, requiring significant acceleration from 2030 onwards. The proposed solution is to install ERTMS in parallel across multiple regions, rather than one track section at a time, whenever an opportunity arises.

Whether this approach is feasible depends on several factors. For example, there needs to be greater clarity first regarding ProRail’s capacity and the availability of resources and staff. Furthermore, an accelerated rollout would require politicians to reallocate funds that were originally earmarked for it after 2040. The ERTMS Programme Directorate estimates that around €5 billion of funding would already be needed in the period prior to that, as the work would then be carried out at an earlier stage.

The 24th ERTMS Progress Report of the Directorate concludes that while the first phase of ERTMS rollout, Tranche 1, is advancing, complex technical challenges remain. These include delays in the Central Safety System (CSS) caused by new EU specifications.

Tranche 1 consists of the Northern lines, the Zeeland line, and the Kijfhoek-Belgian border section and involves converting 419 kilometres of track to ERTMS, upgrading approximately 1,150 trains and locomotives, and training around 12,000 railway professionals.

The estimated cost for this first phase is €3.8 billion, against a €3.6 billion budget. This creates a €219 million budget tension (a €56 million increase compared to the previous progress report of October 2025), primarily attributed to insufficient price indexation. Additionally, there is a further financial risk profile of at least €105 million, attributed to cost developments of the CSS and the most recent insights on the planning.

The Dutch State Secretary for Infrastructure, Annet Bertram, will review the findings of the Programme Directorate and respond in the autumn of 2026. Meanwhile, the Directorate is refining its proposal for Tranche 2, which will focus on upgrading the outdated ERTMS systems on the HSL-Zuid, the high-speed line connecting Amsterdam and Rotterdam to Brussels and beyond. This upgrade is intended to be finalised before the current management contract, held by Infraspeed BV, expires on March 31, 2031, after which the Dutch state intends to transfer management to infrastructure manager ProRail.

The existing ERTMS sections in the Netherlands, on the HSL-Zuid, Betuweroute, Amsterdam-Utrecht, and Hanzelijn are equipped with ERTMS Baseline 2 and do not align with the newer systems being installed. These sections will also need upgrades or replacements between 2030 and 2040. Unlike Tranches 1 and 2, Tranche 3 will not be an execution phase for specific rail lines but rather a simultaneous preparatory phase to establish the groundwork and preconditions needed for the accelerated national rollout towards the 2040 ambition.

Esther Geerts focuses on data and feature stories at Railway Gazette International. She has covered European railway news for over 5 years at RailTech.com before the two titles merged.

SLOVAKIA: A Leo Express passenger train collided with a truck near the Slovak capital of Bratislava. The truck driver was killed while the resulting derailment left more than 20 passengers injured. Police are now investigating the incident as a crime of public endangerment.

FRANCE: Talgo’s planned €350 million deal to supply up to ten Avril high-speed trains to French private operator Le Train has been thrown into doubt, according to Spanish media, following the decision from Renfe to halt its planned high-speed expansion into France. The agreement had depended on the homologation of the Basque manufacturer’s Avril trains…

EUROPE: A long-delayed cross-border rail link between Finland and Sweden could launch in the coming months, according to the Finnish government. Minister of Transport and Communications Lulu Ranne told Yle News that the goal was “to get the train service started during the summer,” referring to the link between the northern Finnish and Swedish border…

PORTUGAL: Hitachi Rail has won a contract from Portuguese infrastructure manager Infraestruturas de Portugal (IP) to develop the country’s second Specific Transmission Module (STM), an onboard signalling interface that will allow ETCS-equipped trains to operate on lines still using legacy train protection systems during Portugal’s transition to ERTMS.

title: VC investors dump old funds at steep discounts to chase AI riches
title_en: VC investors dump old funds at steep discounts to chase AI riches
author: Sun Yu
article_content:
In May 2012, three members of the Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation's investment staff, Diane Mulcahy, Bill Weeks, and Harold Bradley, published "We Have Met the Enemy... and He Is Us," a detailed review of roughly twenty years of the Foundation's investing in venture capital (VC) funds. The Foundation began investing in VC funds in 1985 and had been a limited partner in more than 100 funds run by more than sixty general partners, many of which the authors describe as top-tier. As of February 29, 2012, its endowment stood at $1.83 billion, of which about $249 million was invested in or committed to venture capital and growth equity funds. The paper is now fourteen years old and its data run through 2011.

The authors' conclusion was aimed inward. They argued that the central problem was less the venture capitalists than the way institutional investors, including the Foundation itself, choose and pay them.

"Investment committees and trustees should shoulder blame for the broken LP investment model."

This article summarizes what the paper found. It then adds what later academic research says about two of the paper's central themes, the cost structure of venture funds, much of which is fixed, and whether strong performance repeats, and notes where the evidence is less one-sided than the paper's headline.

Limited partner (LP): the investor, such as a foundation, endowment, or pension plan, that supplies capital to a fund. General partner (GP): the firm that manages the fund.

Carried interest ("carry"): the share of a fund's profits, typically 20%, paid to the general partner.

Net multiple (TVPI): total value (distributions plus the remaining estimated value of holdings) divided by capital paid in, after fees and carry. A multiple of 1.0x means the investor's total value equals what it put in.

IRR: internal rate of return, an annualized measure that is sensitive to the timing of cash flows and can look high early in a fund's life.

Public market equivalent (PME): compares what an investor actually earned in a fund with what the same dollars, invested on the same dates, would have earned in a public index. Above 1.0, the fund beat the index; below 1.0, it lagged. The Kauffman authors used the Russell 2000 Index, which tracks the performance of smaller-capitalization U.S. public companies. Indexes are unmanaged. Investors cannot invest directly in any index.

J-curve: the expected pattern in which fund returns dip early, because of fees and early write-offs, and then rise as investments are sold.

Vintage year: the year in which a fund was formed and began investing; funds of the same vintage are often compared with one another.

Buyout fund: a private equity fund that acquires controlling stakes in established companies, as distinct from a venture fund, which invests in early-stage companies.

The Foundation's data covered 99 venture funds with results measured through the end of 2011. Of those, 50 had a net multiple below 1x: their total value, realized and unrealized and after fees and carry, was below the capital the Foundation invested. Another 33 landed between 1x and 2x. Only 16 funds, roughly one in six, reached 2x or better, and six of those reached 3x or more. The average across all 99 funds was 1.31x. The sample includes funds raised as recently as 2011, which had not had time to mature, and the paper does not separate them, so results for those funds may change.

Mean net multiple across all 99 funds: 1.31x. 16 of 99 funds reached 2x or more.

Results shown are the actual, net-of-fees results of the Kauffman Foundation's venture capital fund portfolio as of December 31, 2011. Net multiple is total value (distributions plus remaining estimated value) divided by capital paid in, after fees and carried interest, as reported by the Foundation. They are not the results of any IFA account, strategy, or model, and are not hypothetical. Past performance is not a guarantee of future results. Individual investor accounts (performance, allocation, etc.) may vary.

Net Multiple of Invested Capital, 99 Kauffman Venture Funds. Net of fees and carried interest, as of December 31, 2011

The authors also found that fund size mattered. None of the Foundation's funds that raised more than $500 million returned more than twice the invested capital after fees. A Silicon Valley Bank study of 850 venture funds from 1981–2003 vintages, cited in the paper, found that 51% of funds larger than $250 million failed to return investor capital after fees, while smaller funds returned more than 2x about 34% of the time.

Venture investing ties up money for a decade or more. The authors regard it as riskier and costlier than a diversified stock portfolio, and they argue that an investor is only compensated for those burdens if a fund beats what the same dollars would have earned in public markets. For that reason, the Foundation came to prefer public market equivalent (PME) analysis, measured against the Russell 2000 Index, over the "top quartile" and "vintage year" rankings common in fund marketing. Those rankings compare a fund only with other venture funds, so a top-quartile fund can still trail the stock market, or even lose money.

The authors set their bar at an excess return of about 3 percentage points a year over the index, which for a ten-year fund corresponds to a PME of roughly 1.34. Of 96 funds from 1989–2010 vintages, 25 cleared it. The ten-year hurdle is shown for reference; funds from later vintages had not completed ten years. The results differed sharply by era.

By vintage group; fund data through December 31, 2011

Outperformance measured by the public market equivalent (PME) method: each fund's actual net cash flows compared with the same dollars invested in the index on the same dates.

Investors cannot invest directly in any index. Indexes are unmanaged and do not reflect fees or expenses. Results shown are the actual, net-of-fees results of the Kauffman Foundation's venture capital fund portfolio, not IFA accounts, and are not hypothetical. Group sizes are small (13 to 48 funds), and some of the more recent funds were still active when measured, so their results could change. Past performance is not a guarantee of future results. Individual investor accounts (performance, allocation, etc.) may vary.

Share of Kauffman Venture Funds That Beat the Russell 2000 by at Least 3 Percentage Points a Year. By vintage group; fund data through December 31, 2011

Ten of 14 funds raised before 1995 cleared the bar. For the 1996–2000 group, the figure was 8 of 48, and for 2001–2005 it was 2 of 21. In the authors' experience, it has been improbable since 1995 that a venture fund would deliver better net returns than the public market. That is a statement about one portfolio, not the whole industry, but it is consistent with a broader study: Harris, Jenkinson, and Kaplan (2014), examining nearly 1,400 U.S. buyout and venture funds, found that venture funds outperformed public equities in the 1990s but underperformed them in the 2000s.

Why the comparison, and what differs. Venture fund results are compared with the Russell 2000 Index to show whether investors were compensated for the illiquidity, cost, and risk of venture funds relative to a liquid public alternative. The two are materially different: venture funds are private, illiquid, and long-term, while an index is unmanaged, liquid, and cannot be invested in directly. The PME method applies a fund's cash flows to an index and does not adjust for differences in risk or liquidity. Small-company stocks carry their own risk, including the possibility of sharp declines.

Venture funds are typically paid through a management fee, usually about 2% a year of committed capital during the five-year investment period, and carried interest of about 20% of profits, the arrangement known as "2 and 20." The Kauffman paper cites a study of venture funds raised from 1993 to 2006 in which about 90% charged fees of 2% or more and 95% charged 20% carry. During the investment period, the fee is based on capital that investors have promised rather than capital invested or earned, so it is paid whether or not the fund performs, and it grows with fund size. On a $1 billion fund, 2% is $20 million a year. After the investment period, the fee usually steps down but continues through the fund's life.

Academic work on private equity compensation points the same way. Metrick and Yasuda (2010) built a model of expected manager revenue for 238 funds raised from 1993 to 2006 and estimated that about two-thirds came from components that do not depend on performance. For venture funds, the Kauffman paper reports the study's median estimates at $14.61 in fees versus $8.20 in carry for every $100 under management.

Model-based estimate for funds raised 1993–2006; estimates as published 2010, as reported by the Kauffman Foundation, May 2012

Median estimates of expected manager revenue over a fund's life, per $100 of fund capital.

These are model-based estimates of expected revenue to managers over a fund's life, not amounts actually paid, and are not investment performance.

Estimated Median Manager Revenue per $100 Under Management, Venture Capital Funds. Model-based estimate for funds raised 1993–2006; estimates as published 2010, as reported by the Kauffman Foundation, May 2012

"...pays VCs more for raising bigger funds."

The authors illustrated how these fees stack. In a hypothetical example using their own assumptions, a firm raises a $250 million fund, then a $350 million fund in year three, then a $500 million fund in year five. Annual management fee income reaches $19.5 million in year five and $22 million from year six, under the assumption that fees stay at 2% of committed capital for all ten years. This example is hypothetical, uses assumptions chosen by the Kauffman authors, and does not reflect any actual fund. Actual fees vary and often step down after the investment period. The authors presented it to show why investors should understand a firm's economics before committing.

Rate is not the only cost. Twenty-three of the Foundation's funds were more than ten years old, and eight were fifteen years or older. Some managers charged additional fees on the remaining portfolio of older funds, for example 1.5% of the cost basis. The authors also objected to the market-standard general partner commitment of about 1% of a fund, arguing it insulates managers from poor results; the Foundation said it expects a 5% to 10% commitment.

Does success repeat? The evidence is more mixed than either side suggests

Investors often judge a new fund by the manager's last one. Whether that works is among the more contested questions in the research, and the answer depends on the type of fund, the period, and what the investor can actually see at the time of the decision.

Within a fund, early numbers can mislead. The Kauffman authors found that their funds' reported net IRRs, in aggregate, tended to peak around month 16, and that the median time to the first capital call of a manager's next fund was about 27 months. In the Foundation's portfolio, then, managers typically went back to investors while the earliest, and usually highest, marks were on the books. Only 25 of 86 funds (29%) followed the textbook J-curve. The authors suggested that early valuations, which general partners set themselves, may help explain the pattern.

Did Early Results Hold? 88 Kauffman Venture Funds vs. the Russell 2000

Paper's "VC PME" label at 27 months and at the end; fund data through December 31, 2011

"VC PME" is the paper's label for a return of 3 to 5 percentage points a year above the Russell 2000 Index, measured by the public market equivalent (PME) method.

Investors cannot invest directly in any index. Indexes are unmanaged and do not reflect fees or expenses. Results shown are the actual, net-of-fees results of the Kauffman Foundation's venture capital fund portfolio, not IFA accounts, and are not hypothetical. Past performance is not a guarantee of future results. Individual investor accounts (performance, allocation, etc.) may vary.

Did Early Results Hold? 88 Kauffman Venture Funds vs. the Russell 2000. Paper's "VC PME" label at 27 months and at the end; fund data through December 31, 2011

Early results were an imperfect guide. The paper uses the label "VC PME" for a return of 3 to 5 percentage points a year above the Russell 2000 Index, measured by PME. Only 6 of the 22 funds that had VC PME at 27 months still did at the end, while 13 funds that did not have it at 27 months eventually did. Early weakness was more informative: 53 of the 66 funds that lacked VC PME at 27 months (80%) never had it.

"...the J-curve effect is mostly notable by its absence."

Across funds, the academic record is not one-sided. Kaplan and Schoar (2005) documented strong persistence in venture and buyout fund performance. Later research by Harris, Jenkinson, Kaplan, and Stucke, using cash-flow records from institutional investors rather than the database behind the earlier study, which they say has flaws, found that venture persistence continues but weakened after 2000, while buyout persistence faded considerably. When they limited the analysis to what an investor could see when a new fund was being raised, the prior fund's interim results, they found little evidence of persistence for buyouts and continuing but reduced persistence for venture. They point to interim performance being only moderately correlated with final performance, and to managers avoiding fundraising when interim results are poor.

These findings can be read alongside the Kauffman paper. The Kauffman authors argued that great venture returns are concentrated in a small number of funds that new investors struggle to reach, and the paper cites estimates of the number of top-performing venture funds ranging from about 10 to about 50, out of several hundred. In our opinion, the practical problem for many investors is picking funds from noisy early signals, at a time when each additional fund a manager raises adds a new stream of fees.

Found strong persistence across successive funds, for venture and buyout. Later research found problems with the database used.

About two-thirds of estimated revenue came from fixed components not sensitive to performance. Venture managers earned more revenue per dollar managed than buyout managers.

Nearly 1,400 U.S. buyout and venture funds, using investor cash-flow data from Burgiss

Buyout funds beat public markets consistently. Venture funds beat public equities in the 1990s and trailed them in the 2000s.

Venture persistence continues but declines after 2000. Buyout persistence fades, and using only information available at fundraising, little persistence for buyouts.

as listed at the end of this article. Descriptions are summaries of the authors' stated findings. Past performance is not a guarantee of future results.

A fair reading of the Kauffman paper requires some context.

It is one investor's experience, and it is dated. The data run through 2011. The paper does not cover venture funds raised or measured in the years since.

The Foundation did not abandon venture capital. The authors wrote that they planned to remain venture investors, with a smaller portfolio of perhaps five to ten partnerships chosen for track record and better-aligned terms.

Top funds can deliver. Sixteen of the Foundation's 99 funds reached 2x or better, and most of its funds raised before 1995 beat the public market by more than 3 percentage points a year. The authors' point was that few investors can reliably identify and access such funds.

The academic evidence on persistence is not uniform. As described above, venture persistence is better documented than buyout persistence, even after weakening post-2000.

Public alternatives carry risk too. The authors chose the Russell 2000 because they believe it better reflects the higher price volatility and sensitivity to economic cycles of small companies. Those same characteristics mean it can fall sharply. Index funds do not remove market risk, and lower costs do not guarantee better results.

The Kauffman authors directed most of their recommendations at investment committees rather than managers. Paraphrasing their themes, the questions they pose include:

How does the fund's net performance compare with a public benchmark chosen in advance, using PME rather than rankings against other private funds?

What are the manager's total fees across all of its funds, how are partners paid, and how much of their own money is committed to the fund?

Is the allocation based on the committee's analysis of the fund, or on a target percentage that needs to be filled? (The authors call the latter "bucket filling.")

How much of the manager's reported performance is realized, and how much rests on valuations the manager sets?

What happens to costs and liquidity if the fund runs well beyond its stated ten-year life?

The authors' view was that investment committees hold more leverage than they use, because they can decline to invest. Whether the answer is a smaller allocation, better terms, or none at all is a decision each board makes under its own investment policy. These questions summarize the authors' themes; they are not IFA recommendations or advice for any investor.

Mulcahy, Diane, Bill Weeks, and Harold S. Bradley. "We Have Met the Enemy... and He Is Us": Lessons from Twenty Years of the Kauffman Foundation's Investments in Venture Capital Funds and The Triumph of Hope over Experience. Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation, May 2012 (SSRN abstract 2053258).

Kaplan, Steven N., and Antoinette Schoar. "Private Equity Performance: Returns, Persistence, and Capital Flows." Journal of Finance, 2005.

Metrick, Andrew, and Ayako Yasuda. "The Economics of Private Equity Funds." Review of Financial Studies, 2010.

Harris, Robert S., Tim Jenkinson, and Steven N. Kaplan. "Private Equity Performance: What Do We Know?" Journal of Finance, 2014 (NBER Working Paper 17874).

Harris, Robert S., Tim Jenkinson, Steven N. Kaplan, and Ruediger Stucke. "Has Persistence Persisted in Private Equity? Evidence from Buyout and Venture Capital Funds." NBER Working Paper 28109, November 2020 (SSRN 3736098).

Silicon Valley Bank. "Dialing Down: Venture Capital Returns to Smaller Fund Sizes." 2009, as cited in the Kauffman paper.

All investing involves risk, including the possible loss of principal. Past performance is not a guarantee of future results. Index funds do not eliminate market risk; when markets decline, an index portfolio declines with them. Lower costs do not guarantee better results.

Individual investor accounts (performance, allocation, etc.) may vary. Investors cannot invest directly in any index. The Russell 2000 Index, referenced in this article, tracks the performance of smaller-capitalization U.S. public companies; it is unmanaged and does not reflect fees or expenses.

All performance figures in this article are the actual, net-of-fees results of the Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation's venture capital fund portfolio, or findings of the academic studies cited, as published by their authors. None is the performance of any IFA account, strategy, or model, and none is hypothetical. Unless otherwise stated, fund data run through December 31, 2011. The fee illustration in "What the fees pay for" is a hypothetical example constructed by the Kauffman authors and does not represent any actual fund or any investment performance. Sources for all statistics are stated with each chart and in the Sources list.

article_content_zh:
2012 年 5 月，尤因·马里昂·考夫曼基金会投资人员的三名成员黛安·马尔卡希 (Diane Mulcahy)、比尔·威克斯 (Bill Weeks) 和哈罗德·布拉德利 (Harold Bradley) 发表了《我们遇到了敌人……他就是我们》，详细回顾了该基金会大约二十年的风险投资 (VC) 基金投资情况。该基金会于 1985 年开始投资风险投资基金，并一直是 100 多个基金的有限合伙人，这些基金由 60 多个普通合伙人管理，其中许多基金被作者描述为顶级合伙人。截至2012年2月29日，其捐赠额为18.3亿美元，其中约2.49亿美元投资或承诺用于风险投资和成长型股权基金。该论文已有 14 年历史，数据截至 2011 年。

作者的结论是针对内部的。他们认为，核心问题不在于风险资本家，而在于机构投资者（包括基金会本身）选择和支付风险资本家的方式。

“投资委员会和受托人应该为有限合伙人投资模式的失败承担责任。”

本文总结了论文的发现。然后，它补充了后来的学术研究对这篇论文的两个中心主题的看法：风险基金的成本结构（其中大部分是固定的），以及强劲的业绩是否会重复，并指出证据不像论文的标题那样片面。

有限合伙人 (LP)：向基金提供资金的投资者，例如基金会、捐赠基金或养老金计划。普通合伙人（GP）：管理基金的公司。

附带利息（“附带利息”）：支付给普通合伙人的基金利润份额，通常为 20%。

净倍数 (TVPI)：总价值（分配加上持有的剩余估计价值）除以扣除费用和结转后的已付资本。 1.0x 的倍数意味着投资者的总价值等于其投入的金额。

IRR：内部回报率，一种对现金流时间敏感的年化指标，在基金生命周期的早期可能看起来很高。

公开市场等价物（PME）：将投资者在基金中实际获得的收益与相同金额在同一日期投资于公开指数的收益进行比较。在1.0以上，基金跑赢指数；低于1.0，该指数就落后了。考夫曼的作者使用了罗素2000指数，该指数追踪美国市值较小的上市公司的表现。索引是非托管的。投资者不能直接投资于任何指数。

J 曲线：由于费用和提前冲销，基金回报率早期下降，然后随着投资出售而上升的预期模式。

年份：基金成立并开始投资的年份；同一年份的基金经常被相互比较。

收购基金：收购成熟公司控股权的私募股权基金，与投资于早期公司的风险基金不同。

该基金会的数据涵盖 99 只风险基金，其结果截至 2011 年底。其中 50 只的净倍数低于 1 倍：它们的总价值（已实现和未实现以及扣除费用和利差）低于基金会投资的资本。另外 33 个降落在 1x 到 2x 之间。只有 16 只基金（大约六分之一）达到 2 倍或更高，其中 6 只达到 3 倍或更高。所有 99 只基金的平均值为 1.31 倍。样本包括最近在 2011 年筹集的资金，这些资金尚未到期，并且本文没有将它们分开，因此这些基金的结果可能会发生变化。

所有 99 只基金的平均净倍数：1.31 倍。 99 只基金中有 16 只达到了 2 倍或以上。

title: X rolls out its first parental controls for users aged 13 to 17, defaulting teens to protected mode, restricting sensitive media, and disabling targeted ads (Steve Dent/Engadget)
title_en: X rolls out its first parental controls for users aged 13 to 17, defaulting teens to protected mode, restricting sensitive media, and disabling targeted ads (Steve Dent/Engadget)

inline_images.caption: New X parental controls are shown on two smartphone screens
inline_images.alt: New X parental controls are shown on two smartphone screens

author: Engadget
article_content:
Any responsible adult should probably check on their teen's X usage.

X Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Elon Musk's X has finally introduced parental controls for kids aged 13 to 17, allowing parents and guardians to manage their teen's experience on the platform. Teens' accounts will now default to protected mode, with sensitive media restricted and targeted advertising blocked. The new settings will also give families "additional tools on top of those defaults," the platform announced.

Those extra tools let adults in charge of teens see how much time their kids have spent on X and set a daily limit, require approval for new followers, and limit For You recommendations to accounts the teen already follows. They can also filter specific words, turn off sensitive media content, allow parents to control who can send direct messages, and see which accounts their teen has chatted with one-on-one (without seeing the messages themselves).

To use the new parental controls, follow the guide in X's help center. "Linking starts with the parent or guardian and finishes with the teen. Both users have to agree," the platform states.

X emphasized that the new controls let parents manage content without prying into their kids' lives. "Parents and guardians cannot read private messages, see searches or viewing history, post as their teen, or access the account," the company wrote. Parents will be able to control up to five teens' accounts.

There are reasons that parents should probably keep teens far away from X. In the last five years, it's been rife with issues including hate speech, AI-generated CSAM, misinformation, deepfake images, a lack of moderation, unauthorized AI training, propaganda, algorithms that amplify partisan content, AI bots, human trolls, and the omnipresence of awesome role model Elon Musk.

Even X admits that it's not aimed at kids or teens. "While X is not designed for or promoted to children, and users must be at least 13 or older where required by law, we take extra care with the young people who are here," the company wrote. While claiming that "child safety is a top priority at X," the platform likely introduced the new rules to comply with current or future regulations in multiple states and countries.

article_content_zh:
任何负责任的成年人都应该检查他们青少年的 X 使用情况。

X 在 Google 上添加 Engadget：首选来源 Google Discover Elon Musk 的 X 终于为 13 至 17 岁的孩子引入了家长控制功能，允许父母和监护人管理青少年在平台上的体验。青少年的帐户现在将默认为保护模式，敏感媒体受到限制并有针对性的广告被阻止。该平台宣布，新设置还将为家庭提供“除了默认设置之外的额外工具”。

这些额外的工具可以让负责青少年的成年人查看他们的孩子在 X 上花费了多少时间，并设置每日限制，要求新关注者获得批准，并将“为你推荐”限制为青少年已经关注的帐户。他们还可以过滤特定的单词，关闭敏感的媒体内容，允许父母控制谁可以发送直接消息，以及查看他们的孩子与哪些帐户进行了一对一的聊天（而无需看到消息本身）。

要使用新的家长控制，请按照 X 帮助中心的指南进行操作。该平台指出：“链接从父母或监护人开始，到青少年结束。两个用户都必须同意。”

X 强调，新的控件让父母可以管理内容，而无需窥探孩子的生活。该公司写道：“父母和监护人无法阅读私人消息、查看搜索或观看历史记录、以青少年身份发帖或访问该帐户。”家长将能够控制最多五个青少年的帐户。

父母应该让青少年远离 X 是有原因的。在过去的五年里，它充斥着各种问题，包括仇恨言论、人工智能生成的 CSAM、错误信息、深度伪造图像、缺乏节制、未经授权的人工智能培训、宣传、放大党派内容的算法、人工智能机器人、人类巨魔，以及无所不在的伟大榜样埃隆·马斯克。

就连 X 也承认它不是针对儿童或青少年的。该公司写道：“虽然 X 不是为儿童设计或推广的，而且根据法律要求，用户必须年满 13 岁或以上，但我们对这里的年轻人格外关心。”虽然声称“儿童安全是 X 的首要任务”，但该平台可能会引入新规则，以遵守多个州和国家当前或未来的法规。

title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
title_en: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
author: Reed Albergotti
article_content:
Export controls on chips and other technology shouldn’t aim to cut China off completely — a strategy that will only backfire, warns Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, the sole maker of the lithography machines needed to produce the world’s most advanced AI chips.

“You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don’t completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on development,” Fouquet said on Semafor’s Future Proof.

The debate over Chinese access to Western technology has intensified in Washington after revelations of Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy left lawmakers divided on how aggressively to tighten curbs.

As a $520 billion de facto monopoly in chipmaking equipment, ASML sits at the center of that fight. Fouquet argued that continuing to sell China older equipment — ASML’s shipments there are more than a decade behind the cutting edge — maintains a strategic “generation gap” that keeps Beijing hooked on Western hardware rather than racing to build its own.

“For almost 30 years, we have been able to keep an extremely high market share in China — very high means close to 100% — which means that they have accepted to rely on our technology with the idea that they had access to it,” Fouquet said.

芯片和其他技术的出口管制不应旨在完全切断与中国的联系，这种策略只会适得其反，ASML 首席执行官 Christophe Fouquet 警告说，ASML 是生产世界上最先进人工智能芯片所需光刻机的唯一制造商。

title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
title_en: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks

inline_images.caption: ARTEX's architecture splits tasks across specialized AI agents. | Image: Microsoft
inline_images.caption_en: ARTEX's architecture splits tasks across specialized AI agents. | Image: Microsoft

author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
The AI framework ARTEX automates cyberattacks from reconnaissance to data theft. A Microsoft analysis shows how state-backed groups and cybercriminals use its specialized agents at machine speed, and how defenders can respond.

Since its release in July 2026, the AI-powered penetration-testing framework ARTEX has become a go-to tool for cyberattacks. The software was recently suspected of being used in an intrusion into an analytics system run by the CIA, NGA, and ODNI (Link nicht geprüft). That breach surfaced shortly before US financial crimes agency FinCEN reported a security incident. The FBI and the US Department of Agriculture had reported incidents earlier.

A report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence now details how ARTEX works and how widely it has spread. GitHub user "Autumn-27"published the source code in July and deleted it in October, though other developers still distribute copies. Chinese security firm ThreatBook also sells a commercial Pro version. Microsoft says state-backed groups from China and North Korea have integrated ARTEX into their operations, including Salt Typhoon, Crystal Typhoon, Onyx Sleet, and Storm-0940. Financially motivated cybercriminals also use the system, the company says, with both state-backed and criminal groups deploying it in operations such as supply chain attacks.

### Specialized AI agents run existing security tools with minimal oversight

Microsoft points out that ARTEX doesn't invent new attack techniques. Instead, the framework operates existing security software with almost no human intervention, including tools such as Nmap, Sqlmap, Metasploit, and automated headless browsers. Attackers can connect any large language model, including modified versions without safety guardrails. A built-in pooling feature automatically switches models or API keys on errors or usage limits, making attacks hard for any single AI provider to track.

According to Microsoft, the system is built on a multi-agent architecture. A goal model breaks an attacker's instructions into verifiable subgoals. From there, a planning agent continuously reviews a knowledge graph, a dynamic map of discovered systems and vulnerabilities, to assign short attack tasks. Worker agents carry out those tasks via system commands, including deploying web shells on web servers, reading password files, or hijacking cloud accounts. Each new finding feeds back into the map and prompts the planning agent for the next step until a reporting agent documents all exploited flaws.

### Machine-speed attacks push Microsoft to recommend active deception

Automation cuts defender response times to just a few minutes, the company found. In one case, an AI agent took just five minutes to search for accidentally exposed credentials on GitHub and pull data from Azure Key Vault, a cloud key store. During a Storm-0940 campaign, the company logged more than 151,000 failed login attempts from automated password guessing, peaking at 2,900 per minute. In that same campaign, Microsoft observed some compromised apps granting themselves top administrator privileges.

Conventional rule-based filters often fail against ARTEX because they rely on fixed markers like known IP addresses or the browser identifiers "artex-enrich"and "norma."Agents and their human operators constantly change those markers and reroute blocked traffic through rotating VPNs, proxy servers, or Tor. Even when security teams spot and isolate a breach, that is often not enough. Because ARTEX usually runs two to three attack chains simultaneously, its agents adapt immediately and shift to new network paths at machine speed.

ARTEX still gives itself away with huge bursts of traffic, because the framework doesn't hide its activity by default. Microsoft recommends deception technologies tailored to how AI agents operate, alongside strict access controls, rate limits, and automated real-time isolation for compromised devices.

Honeypots present autonomous agents with attractive but worthless decoy systems to pull traffic away from real targets. Artificial delay loops, known as tarpits, slow down requests and drain an agent's built-in time and compute budget. Fake wins, Microsoft says, are especially effective because ARTEX's goal model looks for verifiable proof of a breach. When a trap returns convincing fake success messages, the AI considers its task complete and stops the attack by itself.

Decoy credentials, called honeytokens, trigger early alerts when agents try to hijack someone else's AI compute. Microsoft's own tests show these deception tactics sharply reduce successful attack traffic against real systems and deliver high-precision data for identifying the attackers behind them.

How long these defenses will hold up remains open in Microsoft's analysis. The recommended safeguards depend heavily on ARTEX remaining noisy and unmasked. Threshold filters and decoys are likely to reach their limits once attackers space out their requests. Powerful language models that independently recognize artificial test environments and deception attempts, as seen in recent safety tests, pose a similar risk.

article_content_zh:
人工智能框架 ARTEX 可自动执行从侦察到数据盗窃的网络攻击。微软的一项分析显示了国家支持的组织和网络犯罪分子如何以机器速度使用其专门代理，以及防御者如何应对。

自 2026 年 7 月发布以来，人工智能驱动的渗透测试框架 ARTEX 已成为网络攻击的首选工具。该软件最近被怀疑用于入侵 CIA、NGA 和 ODNI 运行的分析系统（Link nicht geprüft）。在美国金融犯罪机构 FinCEN 报告安全事件之前不久，该漏洞就出现了。联邦调查局和美国农业部早些时候报告了这一事件。

微软威胁情报的一份报告现在详细介绍了 ARTEX 的工作原理及其传播范围。 GitHub 用户“Autumn-27”于 7 月发布了源代码，并于 10 月将其删除，但其他开发者仍在分发副本。中国安全公司 ThreatBook 还销售商业 Pro 版本。微软表示，来自中国和朝鲜的国家支持组织已将 ARTEX 整合到其运营中，包括 Salt Typhoon、Crystal Typhoon、Onyx Sleet 和 Storm-0940。该公司表示，出于经济动机的网络犯罪分子也使用该系统，国家支持的犯罪集团和犯罪集团都在供应链攻击等行动中部署该系统。

### 专门的人工智能代理以最少的监督运行现有的安全工具

微软指出 ARTEX 并未发明新的攻击技术。相反，该框架几乎无需人工干预即可运行现有的安全软件，包括 Nmap、Sqlmap、Metasploit 和自动无头浏览器等工具。攻击者可以连接任何大型语言模型，包括没有安全护栏的修改版本。内置池功能会根据错误或使用限制自动切换模型或 API 密钥，从而使任何单个 AI 提供商都难以跟踪攻击。

据微软称，该系统建立在多代理架构之上。目标模型将攻击者的指令分解为可验证的子目标。从那里，规划代理不断审查知识图（已发现的系统和漏洞的动态图），以分配短期攻击任务。工作代理通过系统命令执行这些任务，包括在 Web 服务器上部署 Web shell、读取密码文件或劫持云帐户。每个新发现都会反馈到地图中，并提示规划代理进行下一步，直到报告代理记录所有被利用的缺陷。

### 机器速度攻击促使微软推荐主动欺骗

该公司发现，自动化将防御者的响应时间缩短至几分钟。在一个案例中，AI 代理只需五分钟即可在 GitHub 上搜索意外泄露的凭据，并从云密钥存储 Azure Key Vault 中提取数据。在 Storm-0940 活动期间，该公司记录了超过 151,000 次来自自动密码猜测的失败登录尝试，峰值为每分钟 2,900 次。在同一活动中，微软观察到一些受感染的应用程序授予自己最高管理员权限。

传统的基于规则的过滤器经常无法抵御 ARTEX，因为它们依赖于已知 IP 地址或浏览器标识符“artex-enrich”和“norma”等固定标记。代理及其人工操作员不断更改这些标记，并通过旋转 VPN、代理服务器或 Tor 重新路由被阻止的流量。即使安全团队发现并隔离了漏洞，这通常还不够。由于 ARTEX 通常同时运行两到三个攻击链，因此其代理会立即适应并以机器速度转移到新的网络路径。

ARTEX 仍然会暴露出巨大的流量，因为该框架默认情况下不会隐藏其活动。 Microsoft 建议采用针对 AI 代理操作方式量身定制的欺骗技术，以及严格的访问控制、速率限制和针对受感染设备的自动实时隔离。

蜜罐为自主代理提供了有吸引力但毫无价值的诱饵系统，以将流量从真正的目标上拉走。人工延迟循环（称为 tarpit）会减慢请求速度并耗尽代理的内置时间和计算预算。微软表示，假胜利特别有效，因为 ARTEX 的目标模型寻找可验证的违规证据。当陷阱返回令人信服的虚假成功消息时，人工智能会认为其任务已完成并自行停止攻击。

当代理试图劫持其他人的人工智能计算时，诱饵凭证（称为蜜币）会触发早期警报。微软自己的测试表明，这些欺骗策略大大减少了针对真实系统的成功攻击流量，并提供高精度数据来识别背后的攻击者。

这些防御措施能持续多久仍取决于微软的分析。建议的防护措施在很大程度上取决于 ARTEX 是否保持噪音和未被屏蔽。一旦攻击者分散其请求，阈值过滤器和诱饵可能会达到其极限。正如最近的安全测试中所见，独立识别人工测试环境和欺骗企图的强大语言模型也带来了类似的风险。

title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
title_en: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
The US is closing cloud loopholes that give Chinese companies access to AI chips. Nvidia is responding by halting shipments to four countries, while thousands of high-performance processors are looking for new buyers on the secondary market.

Nvidia has told manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The Financial Times reported the halt, citing three people familiar with the matter. It isn't clear whether the pause is only temporary, according to the report.

The move follows tighter US export controls from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security. The rules aim to stop Chinese companies from getting around existing sales bans by renting computing power from foreign cloud providers. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC the goal was to block indirect access, including smuggling through Southeast Asia and remote access via data centers in third countries.

### Thousands of B300 chips hit the market as cloud providers face chaos

The controls are already affecting the hardware market, CNBC reported. Since the announcement, dealers have listed an unusually large number of Nvidia GPUs for sale. Jack Duhamel, president of the AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two other insiders confirmed to CNBC that the surge is a direct result of the new rule. According to the report, sellers are looking for new buyers for hardware, including thousands of B300 chips, one of Nvidia's most advanced models. Those chips were originally intended for data centers with Chinese rental customers.

The rollout has created significant uncertainty in Southeast Asia, the Financial Times reported. Cloud providers have 90 days to apply for a license and prove that no restricted companies are among their end users. One cloud provider executive described the situation to the paper as chaos, saying there was no guidance on how to apply.

The fallout is also hitting major infrastructure projects. Banks have halted about $500 million in loans to Singapore-based cloud provider Aolani, which planned to rent computing power to TikTok parent ByteDance, the Financial Times reported. ByteDance could now pull out of the deal.

article_content_zh:
美国正在堵住让中国公司获得人工智能芯片的云漏洞。英伟达的回应是停止向四个国家发货，同时数以千计的高性能处理器正在二级市场上寻找新买家。

英伟达已通知戴尔和超微等制造合作伙伴停止向马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和印度尼西亚运送服务器。英国《金融时报》援引三名知情人士的话报道了此次暂停。报道称，目前尚不清楚暂停是否只是暂时的。

此举是在美国商务部工业与安全局实施更严格的出口管制之后做出的。这些规则旨在阻止中国公司通过从外国云提供商租用计算能力来绕过现有的销售禁令。美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔 (Jamieson Greer) 告诉 CNBC，目标是阻止间接访问，包括通过东南亚走私以及通过第三国数据中心进行远程访问。

### 云提供商面临混乱，数千种 B300 芯片涌入市场

据 CNBC 报道，这些控制措施已经影响了硬件市场。自该消息发布以来，经销商列出了异常大量的 Nvidia GPU 待售。人工智能基础设施市场 GPU Mart 总裁 Jack Duhamel 和另外两名内部人士向 CNBC 证实，这一激增是新规则的直接结果。报告称，卖家正在寻找硬件的新买家，其中包括数千个 B300 芯片，这是 Nvidia 最先进的型号之一。这些芯片最初是为中国租赁客户的数据中心设计的。

据英国《金融时报》报道，这一举措给东南亚带来了巨大的不确定性。云提供商有 90 天的时间来申请许可证并证明其最终用户中不存在受限制的公司。一位云提供商高管向该报描述了这种情况，称这种情况很混乱，并表示没有关于如何申请的指导。

重大基础设施项目也受到影响。据英国《金融时报》报道，银行已停止向新加坡云提供商 Aolani 提供约 5 亿美元贷款，该公司计划向 TikTok 母公司字节跳动出租计算能力。字节跳动现在可以退出交易。

Z.AI has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship AI model. Moonshot AI expects the gap between major releases could grow from six months to a year or longer if it loses access to overseas computing power, people familiar with the matter said.

Previously unreported details show that efforts by OpenAI and Anthropic to prevent distillation - training models using answers generated by more capable models - have slowed Chinese AI development. Washington’s latest chip restrictions threaten further delays. The measures put at risk a key advantage that has helped Chinese AI companies challenge their U.S. rivals despite years of export controls: developing competitive models at substantially lower cost.

title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
title_en: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
author: Isabella Ward
article_content:
Meta declined a suggestion from the UK’s financial regulator last week that they joint-test Muse using their sandbox, according to the watchdog’s head of innovation Colin Payne. It comes as regulators across the UK, including the competition and data watchdogs, warned Meta it needs to ensure its AI products comply with UK consumer protection laws.

“It’s another force of attack, agents hitting the streets, most of them coming from the US,” Payne, of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), said Tuesday in a panel hosted by AI firm Whitespace. “We’ve got a number of entrants into the market. We want to see what they’re going to be doing in the market. I think it’s just reasonable,” he later explained to WIRED. Payne told WIRED the FCA had been hoping the organizations could work together to investigate what interactions might look like between the tool, marketed as a personal assistant, and a normal customer.

His organization has been experimenting with other firms as many, including Amazon, roll out AI shopping assistants, and other agentic tools in the UK.

The FCA especially wants to understand how payments will be made by agents—as multiple British retailers, including grocers Sainsbury’s, Marks & Spencer, and Ocado, department store Debenhams Group, and electronics seller Currys said they’d been working with Meta to smooth Muse’s access to their sites. Payne is concerned about potential unintended consequences of prompts, especially when a user has a low level of understanding of how the AI product works. “If an agent is acting autonomously, we want to make sure it’s in the interest of the consumer,” he says.

Payne did note the testing would have taken time to set up. “Normally you have a long period of time speaking to a firm and then you plan it over a period of weeks or months,” he explained, but Meta only made the FCA aware of its plans last month.

“We’ve engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so,” Meta Spokesperson Matthew Pollard tells WIRED.

More than 10 million users have set up Muse in North America since it was launched in September. British watchdogs say they will be monitoring Muse’s rollout closely as they are bracing for significant uptake on their side of the pond, too, given that many Brits already use Meta’s other products, like Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp. “If it’s going to be equally popular in the UK, we need to be able to see what it’s going to do,” Payne says.

The ICO stressed the importance of users understanding and being able to control how Muse uses their personal data. The Competition and Markets Authority has already made Meta adapt its terms and conditions for UK consumers to say Meta must exercise “reasonable skill and care/professional diligence” when providing Muse, the EU and UK terms say, with the document acknowledging that outputs may still be inaccurate and actions may not be completed as intended.

“If we have concerns, we will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers,” the CMA said in a statement.

article_content_zh:
英国金融监管机构创新主管科林·佩恩 (Colin Payne) 表示，Meta 上周拒绝了英国金融监管机构使用沙箱联合测试 Muse 的建议。与此同时，英国各地的监管机构（包括竞争和数据监管机构）警告 Meta，需要确保其人工智能产品符合英国消费者保护法。

金融行为监管局 (FCA) 的佩恩周二在人工智能公司 Whitespace 主办的一次小组讨论中表示：“这是另一股攻击力量，特工们涌上街头，其中大部分来自美国。” “我们有很多进入这个市场的人。我们想看看他们将在市场上做什么。我认为这是合理的，”他后来向《连线》杂志解释道。佩恩告诉《连线》杂志，FCA 一直希望这些组织能够共同合作，调查该工具（作为个人助理销售的工具）与普通客户之间的交互可能是什么样子。

他的组织一直在与包括亚马逊在内的其他公司进行试验，在英国推出人工智能购物助手和其他代理工具。

FCA 特别想了解代理商如何付款——多家英国零售商，包括杂货商 Sainsbury’s、Marks & Spencer 和 Ocado、百货公司 Debenhams Group 和电子产品销售商 Currys 表示，他们一直在与 Meta 合作，以确保 Muse 能够顺利访问其网站。佩恩担心提示可能会带来意想不到的后果，尤其是当用户对人工智能产品的工作原理了解程度较低时。 “如果代理商自主行事，我们希望确保它符合消费者的利益，”他说。

佩恩确实指出，测试需要时间来设置。他解释说：“通常情况下，你会与一家公司进行很长一段时间的交谈，然后你会在几周或几个月内进行计划。”但 Meta 上个月才让 FCA 知道其计划。

Meta 发言人马修·波拉德 (Matthew Pollard) 告诉《连线》杂志：“我们已经与相关监管机构进行了建设性的接触，并将继续这样做。”

自9月份推出以来，Muse在北美已有超过1000万用户安装。英国监管机构表示，他们将密切关注 Muse 的推出，因为考虑到许多英国人已经在使用 Meta 的其他产品，如 Instagram、Facebook 和 WhatsApp，他们也准备在英国方面大力推广 Muse。 “如果它要在英国同样受欢迎，我们需要能够看看它会做什么，”佩恩说。

ICO 强调了用户理解并能够控制 Muse 如何使用其个人数据的重要性。欧盟和英国的条款称，竞争和市场管理局已要求 Meta 调整其针对英国消费者的条款和条件，要求 Meta 在提供 Muse 时必须运用“合理的技能和谨慎/专业勤勉”，该文件承认输出可能仍然不准确，行动可能无法按预期完成。

CMA 在一份声明中表示：“如果我们有疑虑，我们将毫不犹豫地采取行动保护英国消费者。”

title: Musk Says Every US Kid to Get Two SpaceX Shares, Doubling Pledge

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Musk says will give two SpaceX shares to 'every child in America' AFP Thu, November 26, 2026 at 12:58 AM PST 2 min read SPCX +2.50% Trading disclosure The above button links to Coinbase. Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading. Coinbase pays us for certain activity generated through this link. Prices displayed are informational.

Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month.

"Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally," Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns.

The world's richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year.

He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work.

"I recommend holding on to your shares," Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could "be worth about a million times the current global economy" if it "succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun's energy."

"These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them," he said.

In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be "the first of many."

There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau.

The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk's gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion.

SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion.

The company's Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk's ambition to colonize Mars.

title: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
title_en: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
author: Jessica Hamzelou
article_content:
Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand.

Davidson, who is taking part in a clinical trial run by the University of Utah, is the ninth person to have this experimental device implanted in his arm. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently.

The hand is part of the bionic LUKE arm, named after Luke Skywalker of Star Wars , who was fitted with a lifelike prosthetic arm after his own was light-sabered off . The arm was developed in the 2000s , initially trialed in 2014 , and approved by the FDA that same year. The trial that Davidson is enrolled in isn’t so focused on the arm itself but on a new way to connect it to a person’s nervous system. The connection allows users to control movements and receive feedback about how much pressure they’re applying.

Researchers hope that Davidson’s experiences will help them answer some long-standing questions about the technology, including how useful it really is in day-to-day life. They want to know when the device is helpful and where it might fail. They also want to learn how it might affect Davidson’s well-being as well as his brain and nervous system.

In 2009, when he was 16, Davidson climbed a telephone pole to get the best shot of a sunset. “I climbed about 35 feet up,” he recalls. But he lost his footing as he tried to descend. He grabbed for a wire, which ended up electrocuting him, before he fell to the ground.

The accident resulted in second- and third-degree burns over 37% of his body, says Davidson, “and I broke my back in approximately 50 separate locations.” He also broke eight ribs, and his spinal cord was severed. He’s pretty sure he broke his left wrist, too. But around 10 days later, his left hand—his dominant hand, and the one he’d grabbed the wire with—had started to develop gangrene. It was amputated.

Davidson was ultimately in a coma for around a month. “Once I woke up, they explained to me: You’re paralyzed, you’re never going to walk again, and also, we took your left hand,” he recalls. “A bit of an inconvenience at 16, to say the least.”

Davidson, now 33 and a trauma therapist, went on to have physical therapy and adjusted to life in his changed body. He’s tried a range of prosthetic hands. The first one, which he received a year and a half after his injury, was a basic hook that allowed him to pick things up. It wasn’t fancy, but it gave him “a psychological feeling of returning to being whole,” he says.

The hands he’s tried since have been more advanced—some have allowed him to control individual fingers with muscle movements, for example. Some have been covered by his medical insurance, which allows for replacements around every five years, he says. Others he’s had to buy himself. He bought his third prosthetic hand, for example, from eBay. “It’s funny to think I bought a secondhand second hand,” he says.

A chance encounter with a scientist at a supermarket introduced Davidson to the research team at the University of Utah, which specialized in researching devices that plug into the body. Since 2013, the team had been running a trial of a system that could connect with the nerves of a residual limb, allowing an amputee to control a bionic one. Davidson turned out to be an ideal candidate, says Jake George, director of the university’s neurorobotics lab .

Davidson, who was keen to take part, first had to undergo what George describes as “pretty extensive” physical and psychological evaluations. Not only did he have to be well enough for surgery, but the team also scanned his brain to make sure that he still had a mental representation of his left hand—suggesting he’d be able to move a bionic one. They also ran tests to check that the nerves in his arm were working.

A therapist evaluated Davidson’s motivations for taking part in the trial. “Our patients aren’t being compensated, they don’t get to keep the device, and they go through two surgeries—the surgery to get it in and the surgery to take it out,” says George. “Avi’s doing this because he wants to help others.”

In late January of this year, Davidson flew from Florida to Utah to undergo his first surgery. It was a fairly complicated procedure involving engineers as well as a full surgical team. “We [researchers] stand in the back of the room and basically answer the question when the surgeon asks, ‘Where do I put the damn thing?’” says George. The surgeon exposed three nerves in Davidson’s arm and implanted an electrode array containing 100 needles in each one.

Nerves are floppy, so pushing electrodes into them doesn’t do much, says George. Instead, the team connected the electrodes to the nerves using what he describes as a “compressed-air gun.” “You shoot the grid of needles into the nerve at a very, very high velocity,” he says.

The team also inserted 24 electrodes into the muscles around the nerves. Wires for each of the nerve arrays and for pairs of muscle electrodes were left protruding from Davidson’s skin. After the surgery, he was offered some time to recover. “By day two, I’m like ‘No, let’s get me on the machines,’” he says.

That next step involved training a computer system to essentially translate the electrical activity in Davidson’s nerves into signals for bionic hand and wrist movements.

To get it up and running, the team had to train the device in two directions. The first involved converting nerve activity into hand, wrist, and finger movements. The researchers did this by listening in on the signals collected from the hundreds of electrical connection points in Davidson’s arm while he thought about various movements. That part was easy, says George: “It takes a matter of about five minutes.”

The second direction—linking the electrodes to sensations felt by the prosthetic—is much more time-consuming. Team members would stimulate each of the electrode connection points in turn, asking Davidson if he felt anything. They’d then turn up the signal at each of those points to see the effect. “It’s like a three-day process,” says George.

Davidson’s wires have since been connected and simplified, says George, who describes the process as “more or less like plugging in an HDMI cord or a USB-C cord.” When he wants to use his prosthetic, Davidson must first put it on, connect it to the wires, and then initiate it using a small computer.

He’s also had to undergo extensive physical therapy to learn how to control the hand. After all, it’s nothing like the prostheses he’s used in the past. “It’s almost like learning a different language with this kind of technology,” says Leanne Seckinger, an occupational therapist at the University of Utah Health System, who works with Davidson.

At first, she and Davidson worked on learning to hold and stabilize objects. They focused on Davidson’s personal goals—he wanted to be able to cook at home, so the pair worked on strategies to hold and manipulate utensils, prepare and chop ingredients, and carry plates and bowls. “He was able to crack an egg,” says Seckinger. “He made an omelet.”

Davidson has been using the hand at home since July 10, and he has noticed improvements. At first it took him a few minutes to write his name; now he can manage it in seconds. “The things I’m able to do with it now are tremendous, comparatively to where I was at initially,” he says.

Today, he says, he wears the hand around six days a week. He changes the batteries once or twice during the day and takes it off overnight. It’s heavy, weighing in at around five pounds, he says.

The hand can be useful, but it has also proved surprising. Sometimes, Davidson feels pain in it. This could be what’s known as “phantom pain”—a symptom experienced by some people who have lost a limb.

Curiously, he also says he experiences wrist strain. Davidson says he’s been getting a stiffness in his prosthetic wrist similar to what he experiences when he’s been typing for a long time with his flesh-and-blood right hand. He’s also realized that he can relieve the tension by pulling the bionic fingers back to stretch out his prosthetic wrist. “It’s weird,” he says.

The phenomenon “makes no sense physiologically,” says Chris Duncan, a rehabilitation doctor and chief medical officer at BIOS, a neurotechnology company that is supporting the trial. Stretching a typical hand pulls on tendons that extend down the forearm. There aren’t any tendons in a bionic arm—Davidson’s “stretches” are just moving actuators, says Duncan. He doesn’t know why it’s helpful but suspects it might have something to do with how the hand is represented in his mind. “What Avi’s experiencing is kind of like uncharted territory, honestly,” he says.

The research team is currently planning a bigger study and hopes to get the two-way sensation device approved by the FDA so that it can be covered by health insurance. “They need to understand that this is a useful new technological paradigm that will bring value to patients,” says Duncan. Team members also hope the technology will allow users to operate other devices, such as remote controls and wheelchairs.

Davidson will have his implants and the hand for a couple more months at least. But the trial was designed to run for “at least” one year, and that year will be up by the end of January 2027. “I’m not quite sure what happens after that,” he says.

George hopes the trial could be extended, but that will depend on funding. “From our perspective, we’d like to go as long as we can,” he says. “We don’t want to leave Avi without support.”

Davidson isn’t too worried about what comes next, though. “I went into this knowing that this was not something that I get to keep,” he says. “I am not going to benefit from this … I wanted to be a part of this in the context of being able to help push the technology forward.”
