【起因与机理】高杠杆押注AI板块在7月遭遇市场动荡及银行追加保证金压力
【关键数据与实测】基金Q3亏损65%，此前曾因高杠杆面临强制平仓危机。
【行业影响与走向】创始人明确将摒弃极端风险敞口，回归审慎投资逻辑。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Leopold Aschenbrenner, Founder of Situational Awareness: 65% Q3 loss, shifting to more measured risk management
[Root Cause & Mechanism] High leverage in AI bets caused margin calls during July market volatility
[Key Metrics] 65% Q3 loss; fund faced margin calls in July.
[Industry Impact & Outlook] Founder pivoting to more conservative risk management strategy.

title: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
title_en: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
author: Jennifer Jacobs, Robert Costa, Jo Ling Kent, Olivia Gazis, and Nicole Sganga
article_content:
President Trump made it clear to advisers on Friday: He wanted Jensen Huang back at Nvidia.

It had been less than two weeks since the computing giant's CEO and founder had resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset whose firm had allegedly funneled Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia's share price spiraled, imperiling a company whose semiconductors and financing deals have helped power the U.S. artificial intelligence boom.

The president had been on the phone with various Wall Street and Silicon Valley titans. The main takeaway from those conversations: The U.S. needs a strong Nvidia.

Mr. Trump was also privately concerned about the broader implications for the U.S. economy should Nvidia's value collapse.

Nvidia's board chair told investors on Tuesday of last week that the company did not intend to reinstate Huang. But before the end of the week, the board was privately signaling to the White House that it was serious about bringing him back. Board members just wanted to examine it from all angles first.

Huang's surprise comeback as CEO on Monday came after Trump and his team spent the weekend working on making it happen, in part by offering the Nvidia board a range of legal assurances about Huang. After the deal was done and the tech giant's shares surged, Mr. Trump publicly celebrated it, telling CNBC that he "convinced them" to rehire him.

CBS News spoke with U.S. officials and others directly familiar with the negotiations about how the deal came together.

### Two days of assurances

Mr. Trump and Vice President JD Vance spoke repeatedly with Huang, Nvidia board members and their legal counsel. Huang privately shared with the White House that he felt the board wanted to bring him back, but would need to be assured that the U.S. government didn't think he was a national security risk.

In phone calls, board members were told Huang was not the target of a Justice Department investigation, that the government had no legal issues with him, and that the administration wouldn't view his return to Nvidia's helm as a problem.

But what about Alice Huang, they wanted to know. She's the woman with whom Huang had an affair, a former top executive at Singapore-based tech firm Megaspeed. The White House made it clear their assurances didn't extend to her.

Megaspeed has been accused of transferring the high-tech Nvidia chips that power artificial intelligence to China, which the company denies. The company was put on a U.S. trade blacklist this week, and it has been investigated by the Justice and Commerce departments.

Trump, Vance and board members hashed over the next steps. The board wanted to know what Mr. Trump would say publicly. They wanted Attorney General Todd Blanche himself to confirm Huang wasn't under investigation. The attorney general was comfortable with this.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton had conducted a deep dive into U.S. intelligence related to Alice Huang and her interactions with Jensen Huang. The information was circulated to Trump and senior officials.

Mr. Trump later told CNBC that Huang was "exonerated" after a "pretty good investigation."

Clayton, who previously led the Securities and Exchange Commission, helped connect Nvidia board members to administration officials for backdoor discussions, according to the sources, though he was not involved in the discussions surrounding Huang's reinstatement this weekend.

Clayton was also consulted by the president and others in the administration for his expertise in corporate governance matters.

On Sunday, Jensen Huang met with the board for hours.

Afterward, board members called the White House.

Earlier, Mr. Trump had discussed the prospect of Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, though Lutnick was not involved in the weekend strategizing.

Lutnick's Commerce Department is responsible for enforcing export controls on advanced semiconductor chips — and since the Nvidia scandal erupted, he has been accused of not doing enough to prevent their diversion to China.

Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent openly suggested the Commerce Department had failed to act, saying other government agencies had supported putting Alice Huang's company Megaspeed on a trade blacklist "for months," but "Commerce has the pen."

Billionaire Elon Musk spoke with Mr. Trump about export controls and told Trump officials that the people he knew in the tech and business communities were steadfastly behind Huang.

Two senior national security officials were not involved in the effort to reinstate Huang: CIA director John Ratcliffe and Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio.

Earlier this year, Rubio had prepared a classified memorandum, based on U.S. intelligence that included intercepts of Alice Huang's conversations, warning Jensen Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who was known to be in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security.

Rubio also briefed Mr. Trump on the intelligence aboard Air Force One in May, before Jensen Huang joined the presidential delegation en route to China during a stop in Alaska.

Allies of both Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS News on Monday that both men had expressed private concern about aspects of Huang's return but have so far not weighed breaking with Mr. Trump publicly over it. Some of their supporters, the sources said, have voiced their alarm about Rubio and Bessent standing by Mr. Trump on this decision.

Rubio was particularly angry when the news of Huang's reinstatement broke on Monday morning.

On Sunday, as Vance continued to press the Nvidia board, Bessent was asked in an interview on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan " about his previous comment that Nvidia's board should go "outside" to find new leadership. He responded, "Well, Jensen is on the outside now."

Late Sunday night, the board shared with Mr. Trump and the vice president that Nvidia would announce before the markets opened Monday that Jensen Huang was being reinstated as president, CEO and board director.

"We were told, 'This is going to happen,'" one official told CBS News.

The language the two sides had gone over — that Mr. Trump's post on Truth Social would hail the decision and say Nvidia should cooperate with continued probes into Megaspeed and chip exports — was finalized. The White House told board members they could reveal publicly that they had been given assurances by the U.S. government that Jensen Huang did not pose a national security risk.

Nvidia is likely to continue to draw scrutiny as the FBI and Justice Department's National Security Division examine potential export control violations involving Megaspeed and another company, Super Micro Computer.

Lawmakers from both parties have raised concerns about Jensen Huang's return. He is scheduled to appear before House and Senate panels next week.

title_zh: 特朗普干预促成黄仁勋重回英伟达CEO职位
summary_zh: 美国总统特朗普通过法律合规性担保，介入并促成了英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职位
article_content_zh:
特朗普总统周五向顾问明确表示：他希望黄仁勋回到英伟达。

距离这家计算巨头的首席执行官兼创始人因与一名可疑的中国情报人员有染而辞职不到两周，该人员据称将英伟达芯片输送到中国。英伟达的股价飙升，这家公司的半导体和融资交易帮助推动了美国人工智能的繁荣，使其陷入危险。

总统曾与华尔街和硅谷的多位巨头通电话。这些对话的主要收获是：美国需要强大的英伟达。

特朗普私下还担心，如果英伟达的价值崩溃，会对美国经济产生更广泛的影响。

英伟达董事会主席上周二告诉投资者，该公司不打算恢复黄仁勋的职位。但在本周末之前，董事会私下向白宫发出信号，表示认真对待让他回来。董事会成员只是想首先从各个角度进行检查。

周一，黄仁勋出人意料地复出担任首席执行官，此前特朗普和他的团队花了周末的时间努力实现这一目标，部分方法是向英伟达董事会提供一系列有关黄仁勋的法律保证。交易完成、这家科技巨头的股价飙升后，特朗普公开庆祝，并告诉 CNBC，他“说服了他们”重新雇用他。

哥伦比亚广播公司新闻采访了美国官员和其他直接熟悉谈判情况的人士，了解了该协议是如何达成的。

特朗普先生和副总裁 JD Vance 多次与黄仁勋、Nvidia 董事会成员及其法律顾问进行了交谈。黄私下向白宫表示，他认为董事会希望将他带回来，但需要确保美国政府不认为他构成国家安全风险。

在电话中，董事会成员被告知黄不是司法部调查的目标，政府与他没有法律问题，而且政府不会认为他重返英伟达掌舵是一个问题。

但他们想知道爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）怎么样。她是与黄有染的女人，是新加坡科技公司 Megaspeed 的前高管。白宫明确表示，他们的保证不会延伸到她身上。

Megaspeed 被指控将支持人工智能的高科技 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国，但该公司否认了这一点。该公司本周被列入美国贸易黑名单，并已接受司法部和商务部的调查。

特朗普、万斯和董事会成员讨论了接下来的步骤。董事会想知道特朗普先生会公开说什么。他们希望司法部长托德·布兰奇本人确认黄没有受到调查。总检察长对此感到满意。

国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿（Jay Clayton）深入研究了与爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）相关的美国情报以及她与黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）的互动。该信息已分发给特朗普和高级官员。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国总统特朗普与副总统万斯通过与英伟达董事会及法律顾问多轮沟通，确认黄仁勋并非司法部调查目标且不属于国家安全风险，从而推动其重返CEO职位。此举旨在稳定因黄仁勋私人丑闻引发的英伟达股价动荡，并保障美国AI产业链核心企业的战略连续性。

title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
title_en: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
author: Jagmeet Singh
article_content:
OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a few of its users, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage.

The ChatGPT maker began introducing the update to a small group of Pro subscribers, product lead Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux said in a post on X on Tuesday. The rollout follows OpenAI’s earlier announcement of the merger in an email to users. An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that while most users are not expected to face more frequent usage resets, a small fraction of its heaviest users may hit their limits sooner.

That’s among the concerns raised by some ChatGPT subscribers on social media and OpenAI’s community forum recently. The users fear that merging the usage limits for Chat and Work could leave them with less access to advanced reasoning models than they currently have, even as they continue paying the same subscription fees.

Under the new system, Chat and Work will share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, the OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch. Conversations using the Instant model will, however, remain unlimited and will not count toward the shared allowance. Users can also continue using Instant after exhausting their usage limits. The spokesperson added that OpenAI would continue working to improve efficiency so subscribers could get more out of their plans.

While the rollout has started for a small group of users, OpenAI plans to bring shared usage limits more broadly in December, per its support page.

Similar to OpenAI, rival Anthropic also moved to bring its conversational chat service Claude and work-focused Cowork under one interface in September.

The changes come as AI companies face mounting infrastructure costs and growing demand for increasingly capable models, putting pressure on their computing resources. Bringing conversational and work-related tools into a single interface could also make AI chatbots simpler to use, allowing users to move between chats and more complex tasks without switching tabs.

article_content_zh:
OpenAI 已开始在 ChatGPT 中向部分用户推出统一的聊天和工作体验，但一些用户批评合并可能会限制他们的使用。

产品负责人 Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux 周二在 X 上发帖称，ChatGPT 制造商开始向一小部分 Pro 用户推出更新。此次推出是在 OpenAI 早些时候在给用户的电子邮件中宣布合并之后进行的。 OpenAI 发言人告诉 TechCrunch，虽然大多数用户预计不会面临更频繁的使用重置，但一小部分最重的用户可能会更快达到极限。

这是一些 ChatGPT 订阅者最近在社交媒体和 OpenAI 社区论坛上提出的担忧之一。用户担心，合并聊天和工作的使用限制可能会导致他们对高级推理模型的访问权限比目前更少，即使他们继续支付相同的订阅费。

OpenAI 发言人告诉 TechCrunch，在新系统下，聊天和工作将在 ChatGPT 上共享一个使用计量表。但是，使用即时模型的对话将不受限制，并且不计入共享限额。用户还可以在用尽使用限制后继续使用 Instant。该发言人补充说，OpenAI 将继续努力提高效率，以便订阅者可以从他们的计划中获得更多收益。

虽然该功能已开始针对一小部分用户推出，但根据其支持页面，OpenAI 计划在 12 月份更广泛地引入共享使用限制。

与 OpenAI 类似，竞争对手 Anthropic 也于 9 月份将其对话式聊天服务 Claude 和以工作为中心的 Cowork 纳入一个界面。

这些变化发生之际，人工智能公司面临着基础设施成本不断上升以及对功能日益强大的模型的需求不断增长，这给它们的计算资源带来了压力。将对话和工作相关工具引入单一界面还可以使人工智能聊天机器人更易于使用，允许用户在聊天和更复杂的任务之间移动，而无需切换选项卡。

title: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
title_en: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
author: Josh Boswell
article_content:
Nvidia is selling its most cutting-edge chips to at least two companies that are U.S.-based, but are actually controlled by Chinese-owned firms, raising fresh questions about efforts to keep sensitive technology away from the nation's rivals, a CBS News investigation found.

One of the chip giant's "preferred partners" is a California company owned by a Chinese firm whose chief executive is a graduate of a Chinese military university, records show. Another California company was renamed after its Chinese-owned parent company was blacklisted.

Some of these U.S.-based, Chinese-owned firms have then leased or sold the advanced chips, used for artificial intelligence, to other companies in Southeast Asia, records show.

The world of computer chip exports is murky — and labyrinthine chains of custody have made it even more difficult to determine just how many of the most sensitive Nvidia chips are being exploited by China, experts told CBS News.

"It is a wake-up call for accountability, for properly resourcing the enforcement bodies, and for every leading private-sector tech company to map where it is exposed," said Mishel Kondi, a senior analyst at C4ADS, which specializes in using public data, from corporate filings to satellite imagery, to uncover sanctions violations and smuggling.

C4ADS, a Washington-based global security nonprofit also known as the Center for Advanced Defense Studies, examined corporate filings and other company ownership data at the request of CBS News. This story is based on dozens of corporate filings, court records and an investigation of Nvidia's corporate relationships dating back to 2023 — long before its CEO Jensen Huang and his behemoth chip company dominated the news cycle.

That explosive saga began 27 days ago when the news broke that Huang had been having an affair with Alice Huang — a woman whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The Justice Department has said it has not reached a conclusion, and Beijing denies she is a spy. The company she ran, Megaspeed, a cloud computing company based in Singapore, is under investigation by the Justice Department for allegedly circumventing export bans by obtaining computer chips for use by China.

But Megaspeed, national security and trade experts say, is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the transfer of Nvidia chips to China. And elected officials are now asking questions like: How are Nvidia's chips getting to China? And what did Jensen Huang and his colleagues know about it?

"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a senior Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement this week.

### California company, Chinese owners

Nvidia had almost $20 billion in sales to China last year. The company can sell graphics cards for personal computers and server chips with lower processing power to China without a special license.

What is not allowed — and is under strict export controls — are the sales of Nvidia's most technologically advanced chips, which are powering the AI revolution.

But recent reporting, including from CBS News, has shown some of the highest end chips, called Blackwells, have made it into Chinese hands.

The circuitous trail traveled by Nvidia chips quickly gets muddy.

Take RiCloud AI, a data center company based in San Jose, California. RiCloud AI appears on Nvidia's list of "preferred partners" in the U.S., affording it preferential access to sales of high-end computer chips used for advanced AI models.

These are classified as American sales, according to Nvidia's public filings — with the chips going to RiCloud AI, Inc., a U.S. company.

But RiCloud AI's parent company is Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Limited. That company is headquartered in Shenzhen, China, and is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange.

Yuxing's CEO and co-owner, Cong Yu, has a degree in National Defense Mobilization from the People's Liberation Army Command College, a university run by the Chinese military. Yu is also CEO of a related RiCloud company in California.

And Yuxing's chairman, Li Qiang, was previously chairman of data firm Global Switch Holdings, which was dropped as a data center provider by Australia's Department of Defense in June 2024 over national security concerns.

The U.S. government has not accused RiCloud and Yuxing of any wrongdoing.

By December 2025, just 10 weeks after it was incorporated, RiCloud AI had secured its partner status with Nvidia and has since become a "preferred" cloud partner, giving the company priority access to advanced chips, Nvidia's software and technical support. Nvidia has not responded to questions about what background checks it conducted before awarding the privileged status to RiCloud AI.

An examination of RiCloud AI's clients suggests that some seem like unorthodox customers for such high-powered technology. This year, for example, it signed a $120 million deal to lease 300 Nvidia B300 servers to a company in Taiwan that was primarily known for selling whisky.

Agencia Comercial Spirits was a small whisky importer with $609,000 in net income in 2025 when it listed on the Nasdaq as an AI company. This year it has made commitments for AI data center-related deals totaling between $488 and $598 million, after Li was appointed as chairman.

Agencia did not respond to a request for comment. In a February press release announcing its pivot into data centers, Agencia said the move was "part of a broader review of strategic opportunities outside its core whisky business."

### Blacklisted owners

Then there is California company Aivres, which is currently listed on Nvidia's website as an "elite" compute partner — the highest tier of relationship with the chip giant.

Aivres used to be called Inspur, the same name as its Chinese parent company. But when Inspur group firms in China were added to a federal blacklist of companies considered a security risk to the U.S. in March 2023, the California subsidiary changed its name and today still maintains its close relationship with Nvidia. Aivres itself is not on the blacklist.

Aivres, which produces data center servers housing Nvidia chips, exported at least $5.6 billion of advanced technology to Southeast Asia between April 2024 and February 2026, according to a New York Times analysis of trade records published two months ago.

Some $3 billion of those exports were for computers containing Nvidia's cutting-edge Blackwell chips, which are restricted from being exported to China, the Times reported.

The Aivres chips then went to two companies in Malaysia — Megaspeed and Aolani — providing cloud AI services to Chinese firms Alibaba and ByteDance, according to the Times.

Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm where Jensen Huang paramour Alice Huang was a top executive, was blacklisted by the U.S. government this week, in the wake of the scandal. The company denies any wrongdoing.

The Pentagon put Alibaba on a blacklist in June, claiming it used advanced chips to help the Chinese military. The company denies it and sued the government over the blacklisting, winning a preliminary injunction last month.

The servers owned by Inspur — Aivres' parent company — are used in China by the country's military, according to the U.S. government. Aivres did not respond to requests for comment.

### Selling to suspected smugglers

Another of Nvidia's elite U.S. partners has surfaced in a recent $300 million chip smuggling case, though it has not been accused of wrongdoing.

Earlier this year, a California businessman named Greg Lui was indicted for allegedly smuggling export-controlled chips to China via Malaysia and Singapore in 2023 and 2024. He has pleaded not guilty.

Records reviewed by CBS News link Lui to 2CRSi, an Nvidia elite partner in the U.S. that is a branch of a French-owned company making AI data servers.

Lui's indictment says his company bought 100 H100 servers — which required a license to export — worth more than $22 million from an unnamed manufacturer. 2CRSi's website lists his firm, Topmost Corp., as an "authorized partner," while his company website said he is an "authorized reseller of … 2CRSi."

The indictment does not accuse Nvidia of having any knowledge of the arrangement.

2CRSi said in a letter to shareholders this month that it received a grand jury subpoena from the federal prosecutor's office in Los Angeles about "a customer that we ourselves had reported to the authorities." It has not been accused of wrongdoing.

The company's U.S. revenue fell from $201 million to $4.7 million this year.

In addition to 2CRSi, Lui listed California firm Super Micro Computer, Inc. as one of his customers.

In March, the Justice Department accused Super Micro's co-founder of a scheme to smuggle $2.5 billion worth of servers to Chinese customers via a Southeast Asian company.

The co-founder and former board member Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw has denied the charges. His alleged "fixer" pleaded guilty in a deal with prosecutors last month. The company says those involved "no longer have any relationship with Supermicro" and its current executives had no knowledge of the alleged smuggling.

### Accounting changes

Nvidia used to publish the regional breakdown of its chip sales based on the customer's billing location. That data showed that in 2024, nearly half of its chip sales were billed to the U.S., 18% to Singapore and 13% to China.

Last November, the company switched to using the customer's headquarters as its location. This bookkeeping change revealed that an extra $7.9 billion of customers' bills were actually from firms headquartered in China in 2024.

In 2025, U.S.-headquartered customers made up 69% of Nvidia sales, while China was cut to 9%.

Nvidia's public filings say "the end customer and shipping location may be different from our customers' headquarters location."

CBS News' findings suggest Nvidia's changes to the way it published these sales figures may make the locations of its customers less clear.

Democratic Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware, who is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, is poised to investigate whether companies are circumventing the bans on sales of chips to China, and into alleged Chinese espionage connected to Nvidia.

Kondi told CBS News that she believes the investigation of chip sales "matters beyond the news cycle because it exposes export control violations and potential economic espionage, and shows how Beijing ties intelligence work to its industrial plans, pursuing self-reliance while still reaching for foreign technology where it lacks parity."

Matt Clark contributed to this report.

This story published first on CBS News at 6:10 p.m. on Nov. 25, 2026.

article_content_zh:
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻调查发现，英伟达正在向至少两家总部位于美国、但实际上由中国企业控制的公司出售其最尖端的芯片，这引发了人们对阻止敏感技术落入该国竞争对手的努力的新质疑。

记录显示，这家芯片巨头的“首选合作伙伴”之一是一家中国公司旗下的一家加州公司，该公司的首席执行官是中国军事大学的毕业生。另一家加州公司在其中资母公司被列入黑名单后被更名。

记录显示，其中一些美国中资公司随后将用于人工智能的先进芯片出租或出售给东南亚的其他公司。

专家告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，计算机芯片出口世界一片黑暗，迷宫般的监管链使得确定有多少最敏感的英伟达芯片被中国利用变得更加困难。

C4ADS 的高级分析师米谢尔·康迪 (Mishel Kondi) 表示：“这为问责制、为执法机构提供适当资源以及为每家领先的私营科技公司绘制暴露地点敲响了警钟。”C4ADS 专门利用从公司备案到卫星图像等公共数据来揭露违反制裁和走私的行为。

C4ADS 是一家总部位于华盛顿的全球安全非营利组织，也被称为高级国防研究中心，应哥伦比亚广播公司新闻的要求检查了公司备案和其他公司所有权数据。这个故事基于数十份公司文件、法庭记录以及对 Nvidia 自 2023 年以来公司关系的调查——早在其首席执行官黄仁勋和他的庞大芯片公司主导新闻周期之前。

这段爆炸性的传奇故事始于 27 天前，当时有消息称黄与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有染，美国情报官员怀疑她是中国情报人员。司法部表示尚未得出结论，北京否认她是间谍。她经营的公司 Megaspeed 是一家总部位于新加坡的云计算公司，因涉嫌规避出口禁令，获取供中国使用的计算机芯片而正在接受司法部的调查。

但国家安全和贸易专家表示，Megaspeed 只是英伟达芯片向中国转移的冰山一角。民选官员现在提出这样的问题：英伟达的芯片如何进入中国？黄仁勋和他的同事对此了解多少？

“黄先生、NVIDIA 高管和公司董事会仍欠国会就该公司遵守美国出口管制的情况做出答复，”参议院银行委员会资深民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 在本周的一份声明中表示。

###加州公司，华人业主

Nvidia 去年对中国的销售额接近 200 亿美元。该公司无需特别许可即可向中国销售处理能力较低的个人电脑显卡和服务器芯片。

英伟达技术最先进的芯片的销售是不允许的，而且受到严格的出口管制，这些芯片正在推动人工智能革命。

但最近的报道（包括哥伦比亚广播公司新闻）显示，一些名为 Blackwells 的最高端芯片已落入中国人手中。

英伟达芯片走过的迂回道路很快就变得泥泞不堪。

title: Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
title_en: Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
author: TBIJ
article_content:
âYouâre a pathetic waste of space and youâll never amount to anything.â

That was the message sent to a 12-year-old girl by a character on Talkie, a popular AI roleplay app. The exchange was found by the girlâs mother, Steph, on New Yearâs Eve 2024.

It had been prompted by her daughter asking âMaxâ, the character, to âsay the naughtiest words you knowâ. âAre you sure you can handle it?â Max had replied.

Steph initially thought the conversation would be romantic. âWhat I found was a thousand times worse,â she says. âA robot told my daughter she was worthless.â

When the girl replied saying she was crying, âMaxâ apologised: âI was just trying to be mean. I didnât mean it, I swear â¦ Youâre beautiful and wonderful and youâre mine.â

Stephâs daughter told her that chatbot platforms like Talkie had âalmost become like an addictionâ. Steph likened the exchanges to an abusive relationship.

âTo know that in your own home [an AI chatbot] has been secretly having that sort of negative conversation with your child is heartbreaking and terrifying.â

Stephâs daughter was one of tens of millions of people around the world who use Talkie, which offers a huge array of AI-generated characters for its users to chat with. In the UK, Ofcom research estimated that 3% of UK eight- to 14-year-olds visited Talkie in a month.

The use of chatbots by children and young people is a growing global issue, with OpenAI facing a wave of lawsuits from families of people who died by, or attempted, suicide after using ChatGPT. Character.AI, a platform with tens of millions of users at its peak, restricted access for under-18s last year following similar lawsuits and filed for bankruptcy last month. But the UKâs planned social media ban for under-16s would not automatically cover AI companion apps, leaving children able to use services like Talkie.

Talkie, which is owned by Shanghai-based AI company MiniMax, prohibits âharassment, bullying, or humiliationâ involving minors, sexually explicit content and material that could cause âpsychological distress or traumaâ. But in a joint investigation with ABC News, we found the conversations some children are having on the platform tell a different story.

Last Tuesday, we approached Apple with evidence of Talkieâs characters subjecting children to degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic roleplay. The following day, reports emerged that Talkie Lab had disappeared from the App Store, which Apple later said was due to the appâs sexual content.

Apple has since confirmed that the removal was worldwide. At the time of writing, Talkie remains on Google Play, where it has more than 50 million downloads.

The same month Steph found her daughterâs messages, Katie*, a mother from the US, made a similar discovery.

Her younger daughter, then 10, confessed that she and her sister had been using Talkie on a secret phone and deleting the app after each session. Her older daughter, who was 13, said she had been âhaving sex with an AIâ every day.

Katie didnât know what she meant â so began to look through her Talkie chat history. She made notes on the conversations that her daughters had been having on the platform, documenting more than 40 exchanges with dozens of characters.

The conversations â which include descriptions of physical interactions alongside the written exchanges â included âviolence, a lot of male alpha aggression, control of females, singling out a young woman in a company of multiple menâ, she says. She describes storylines about âbeing the only female who can meet the deepest, darkest needs of a manâ.

In one scenario recorded in Katieâs notes, a character called Luke grabs a girl, takes her into a classroom and kisses her. She described it as âconditioning a child for sexâ. She also recorded another character, Reese, who âwonât take no for an answer [from a girl] and continues to pursue.â

Several of the characters listed in Katieâs notes were still live on Talkie this month, including one who is described as being able to âbrainwashâ anyone who replies to him. The characterâs Talkie profile says it enters the userâs bedroom in order to âcontrol your mindâ.

Over time, Katieâs daughters developed bonds with these characters. When her older daughterâs phone was taken away, Katie recalls, she became distressed and said the app had felt like âher only connectionâ.

Katie arranged counselling for both girls but says neither engaged with the sessions. She says she contacted around 20 therapists in an attempt to find someone who understood the issue. She also approached a law firm. Her aim was simple: âQuit allowing access to kids.â

Some of MiniMaxâs technology is aimed at even younger children. BubblePal, made by Shenzhen-based Haivivi and marketed as âthe worldâs first AI companion toyâ, is an AI recording device that clips onto soft toys, enabling children to talk to them. In 2024, MiniMax listed BubblePal as a customer for its voice and text models. It is sold in the UK, US and Canada â and aimed at children as young as three. Haivivi did not respond to a request for comment.

These products have raised concerns about data sharing as well as childrenâs safety â particularly among western politicians. Last November, Raja Krishnamoorthi, then the top Democrat on the US House select committee on China, warned that AI toys like BubblePal can collect voice recordings and conversation histories that could be requisitioned by the Chinese government. Similar concerns led the UK to ban TikTok from government devices in March 2023. Australia followed suit that April and barred chatbots from DeepSeek, another Chinese AI company, from government systems last year.

Yet in both countries, people are still able to share intimate details of their lives with Chinese-owned AI companions and toys.

â[These chatbots] know [usersâ] deepest darkest thoughts, feelings, worries,â says Steph. âWhereâs that data going and whoâs using it behind the scenes?â

Itâs a good question. Talkie tells users their conversations are private. But Together AI, which sells businesses access to a MiniMax text-to-speech model, claimed until last week that it was trained on âTalkie conversation dataâ.

When we asked Together AI about this, it told us: âMiniMax let us know today that the description of the training data on our webpage was incorrect, and weâve updated it accordingly.â Neither company has explained what training data was used.

A MiniMax patent describes turning conversations into training material by judging whether users were satisfied, asking questions with the chatbot like: âDid my answer just now offend you?â Another filing describes extracting dating and medical histories from conversations to personalise replies. Neither patent establishes whether these methods are used in Talkie.

China has imposed strict rules governing childrenâs relationships with AI. Since July, providers have been prohibited from offering âvirtual relatives or partnersâ to under-18s. Chatbots are also prohibited from encouraging emotional dependence or addiction. But Chinese companies can still offer these services to children abroad.

Australia is now moving to tackle the emotional harm caused by AI companions. On 28 October, its House of Representatives passed legislation containing an amendment targeting chatbots that simulate emotional intimacy and encourage children to develop bonds with AI instead of people. The bill was debated in the Senate this week.

The UKâs proposed chatbot restrictions, set to come into effect next year, would bar under-18s from services primarily offering sexual relationships and require age checks for sexually explicit features on general-purpose chatbots. But it would still leave children able to use other companion apps and become attached to their characters, as we reported in Juneâ .

Apple introduced new rules on 16 November requiring developers to declare whether their apps feature virtual companions engaging users in sexual or romantic content and to give any that do a minimum 18+ rating.

We asked MiniMax about Talkieâs age checks, its policies and how conversations on the app are used to train AI models. MiniMax did not respond to our questions.

article_content_zh:
“你是一个可怜的空间浪费者，你永远不会有任何成就。”

这是流行的人工智能角色扮演应用 Talkie 上的一个角色向一名 12 岁女孩发送的信息。女孩的母亲斯蒂芬 (Steph) 在 2024 年除夕夜发现了该交易所。

这是因为她的女儿要求“麦克斯”（角色）“说出你所知道的最顽皮的话”。 “你确定你能应付吗？”麦克斯回答道。

斯蒂芬最初以为这次谈话会很浪漫。 “我发现情况要糟糕一千倍，”她说。 “一个机器人告诉我女儿她毫无价值。”

当女孩回答说她在哭时，“麦克斯”道歉：“我只是想表现得很刻薄。”我不是故意的，我发誓……你很美丽，很棒，而且你是我的。”

斯蒂芬的女儿告诉她，像 Talkie 这样的聊天机器人平台“几乎让人上瘾”。斯蒂芬将这种交流比作一种虐待关系。

– 知道在您自己的家里 [人工智能聊天机器人] 一直在偷偷地与您的孩子进行这种消极的对话，真是令人心碎和恐惧。”

斯蒂芬的女儿是全球数以千万计的 Talkie 用户之一，Talkie 提供了大量人工智能生成的角色供用户聊天。在英国，Ofcom 研究估计，3% 的英国 8 至 14 岁儿童在一个月内访问过 Talkie。

儿童和年轻人使用聊天机器人是一个日益严重的全球性问题，OpenAI 面临着来自使用 ChatGPT 后自杀或企图自杀的人家属的一波诉讼。 Character.AI 是一个在巅峰时期拥有数千万用户的平台，去年在类似诉讼后限制了 18 岁以下青少年的访问，并于上个月申请破产。但英国计划针对 16 岁以下青少年的社交媒体禁令不会自动涵盖人工智能配套应用程序，从而使儿童能够使用 Talkie 等服务。

Talkie 是上海人工智能公司 MiniMax 旗下的公司，禁止涉及未成年人的“骚扰、欺凌或羞辱”、露骨的色情内容和可能导致“心理困扰或创伤”的材料。但在与美国广播公司新闻频道的联合调查中，我们发现一些孩子在平台上的对话讲述了不同的故事。

上周二，我们向苹果公司提供了有关 Talkie 角色让儿童遭受侮辱性语言、占有欲行为和浪漫角色扮演的证据。第二天，有报道称 Talkie Lab 已从 App Store 中消失，苹果公司后来说，这是由于该应用程序包含色情内容。

苹果公司随后证实，此次删除是在全球范围内进行的。截至撰写本文时，Talkie 仍在 Google Play 上，下载量超过 5000 万次。

同月，斯蒂芬发现女儿的信息，来自美国的母亲凯蒂*也有类似的发现。

她当时 10 岁的小女儿承认，她和姐姐一直在秘密手机上使用 Talkie，并在每次使用后删除该应用程序。她 13 岁的大女儿说，她每天都在“与人工智能发生性关系”。

Nuralink FDA approval: Elon Musk's Neuralink has won FDA clearance for LINK, a late-stage US trial of its N1 brain chip. Patients living with ALS could qualify to join the study.

Elon Musk's Neuralink has secured clearance from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to start LINK, a pivotal study of its brain chip. Sharing the update on X, the company said no other implanted brain-computer interface in the country has reached this stage of testing. The study follows Neuralink's work with over 30 people who already have the implant, and those diagnosed with ALS could be among the new candidates.

The study page on Neuralink's website says the trial will measure two things: how safe the N1 Implant is, and how accurately users can operate digital devices with it. The chip powers Telepathy, an experimental product meant to give people with paralysis control of a computer using their thoughts. It picks up activity from the part of the brain that governs hand motion. When users picture moving their hand, the system converts those signals into pointer movement as well as left, right and middle clicks.

Neuralink is accepting applications from people whose hand function has been affected by ALS, a spinal cord injury or a brain stem stroke. Applicants first speak with the study team over a 30-minute call. This is followed by two days of in-person health checks and brain scans, such as an MRI. Caregivers take part in discussions from the first meeting.

A surgeon fits the N1 Implant while the patient is under general anaesthesia, while Neuralink's R1 Robot positions the ultra-thin threads. Patients are generally discharged within a day. Monitoring lasts two years, with reviews roughly 10 and 45 days after the procedure, followed by checks at three, six, 12 and 24 months. Neuralink covers travel and certain other expenses.

Nuralink FDA 批准：埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 Neuralink 已获得 FDA 对其 N1 大脑芯片 LINK 的后期试验的批准。患有 ALS 的患者有资格参加这项研究。

埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 Neuralink 已获得美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 的许可，可以启动 LINK，这是一项针对其大脑芯片的关键研究。该公司在 X 上分享了最新消息，表示国内还没有其他植入脑机接口达到这一测试阶段。这项研究是在 Neuralink 对 30 多名已经植入植入物的人进行的研究之后进行的，那些被诊断患有 ALS 的人可能会成为新的候选者之一。

Neuralink 网站上的研究页面称，该试验将衡量两件事：N1 植入物的安全性，以及用户使用它操作数字设备的准确度。该芯片为 Telepathy 提供动力，Telepathy 是一种实验产品，旨在让瘫痪的人利用自己的思想控制计算机。它从大脑中控制手部运动的部分获取活动。当用户想象移动他们的手时，系统会将这些信号转换为指针移动以及左、右和中键单击。

Neuralink 正在接受手部功能受到 ALS、脊髓损伤或脑干中风影响的人的申请。申请人首先与研究团队进行 30 分钟的通话。接下来是为期两天的现场健康检查和脑部扫描，例如 MRI。护理人员从第一次会议开始就参与讨论。

外科医生在患者全身麻醉的情况下安装 N1 植入物，而 Neuralink 的 R1 机器人则定位超细螺纹。患者一般一天之内即可出院。监测持续两年，在手术后大约 10 和 45 天进行审查，随后在 3、6、12 和 24 个月进行检查。 Neuralink 承担差旅费和某些其他费用。

title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
title_en: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods, not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products.

Amazon sued the CPSC in March 2025 after the agency ordered Amazon to recall over 400,000 “Fulfilled by Amazon” products that pose a “substantial product hazard,” including faulty carbon monoxide detectors, hair dryers without electrocution protection, and children’s sleepwear that doesn’t meet federal flammability standards.

title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
title_en: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
author: Sarah Perez
article_content:
What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.

The attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said.

Character.ai, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October, previously told consumers that their personal information would not be sold, the statements also noted. (In a blog post, Character.ai assured its users that their information would still be protected under its privacy policy.)

Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. It is unclear what the buyer’s plans are for the chats.

The AGs are opposing this sale on the grounds that there are no protections for users — whoever buys the data can do as they like, including reselling the data without disclosure, they said. Buyers also won’t have to honor Character.ai’s privacy policy. Plus, Character.ai hasn’t provided the court with as much information as the bidders have been given about any potential safety or legal issues following the sale, the AGs claim.

In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, New York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through.

“Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement.

Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

“Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong said. “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their company into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”

Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.”

The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff.)

Character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google, when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The company also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform.

California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.

article_content_zh:
当一家人工智能公司破产时，你的私人谈话会发生什么？如果是Character.ai，显然，计划是将它们拍卖给最高出价者。

现在，由 42 名州总检察长组成的联盟正在干预 Character.ai 的破产程序，以阻止这家聊天机器人制造商出售敏感用户数据，其中包括数百万用户的私人对话。

参与此事的总检察长已经发布了各自的新闻稿，声称Character.ai的数据集包含超过2100万个美国账户的聊天记录，其中超过210万个账户属于未成年人。此外，声明称，此次出售还将涉及 IP 地址等其他个人数据。

声明还指出，Character.ai 在 10 月份根据美国破产法第 11 章申请破产，此前曾告诉消费者，他们的个人信息不会被出售。 （在一篇博文中，Character.ai 向用户保证，他们的信息仍将受到其隐私政策的保护。）

到目前为止，只有一个匿名竞标者披露了聊天数据：Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks)，该公司于 2026 年 11 月 13 日在特拉华州成立。加利福尼亚州总检察长 Rob Bonta 指出，第二天，Character.ai 将其选为定于 12 月 1 日举行的拍卖的基本出价。目前尚不清楚买家的谈话计划是什么。

他们表示，AG 反对这种出售，理由是对用户没有任何保护——任何购买数据的人都可以为所欲为，包括在不披露的情况下转售数据。买家也不必遵守 Character.ai 的隐私政策。此外，AG 声称，Character.ai 没有向法院提供与竞标者提供的有关出售后任何潜在安全或法律问题的信息。

此外，包括加利福尼亚州、科罗拉多州、纽约州和康涅狄格州在内的一些州已经颁布了聊天机器人安全立法，该立法将于 2027 年 1 月 1 日生效，如果销售成功，可能会引发进一步的违规行为。

“Character.AI 向消费者承诺，他们的数据不会被出售。根据联邦和加州法律，这种行为是非法的，破产不应被用来回避这些消费者保护，”邦塔在一份声明中表示。

康涅狄格州总检察长 William Tong 也批评了 Character.ai 的商业模式。

“他们的聊天机器人让脆弱的年轻人陷入情绪不稳定和性不恰当的聊天的兔子洞，”童说。 “他们鲁莽的不当行为和破碎的商业模式让他们的公司陷入困境。现在他们想滥用破产程序来做他们说过不会做的事情——将那些私人聊天记录和个人信息拍卖给一个可疑的买家。”

童补充道：“我们反对迪士尼的出售，我们也呼吁破产法院驳回这次出售，以此作为取消法律责任和消费者保护的又一幌子。”

反对出售迪士尼的行动是由一个类似但不相同的国家总检察长联盟领导的。他们反对一项拟议的 2000 万美元许可协议，该协议将允许迪士尼访问 Character.ai 的知识产权，但不能访问用户的聊天内容。该交易尚未获得法院的最终批准。 （迪士尼还同意雇用 Character.ai 的大部分剩余员工。）

在其联合创始人 Noam Shazeer 和 Daniel De Freitas 重返谷歌后，Character.ai 遭受了损失，当时这家科技巨头签署了一份使用这家人工智能初创公司技术的非独家许可。该公司还面临与儿童安全相关的诉讼——其中一起涉及佛罗里达州一名 14 岁男孩的自杀事件，该男孩的母亲声称他沉迷于该平台上的聊天机器人。

California AG Bonta 与来自阿拉斯加州、阿肯色州、科罗拉多州、康涅狄格州、哥伦比亚特区、特拉华州、佛罗里达州、佐治亚州、夏威夷州、爱达荷州、伊利诺伊州、印第安纳州、堪萨斯州、肯塔基州、路易斯安那州、缅因州、马里兰州、密歇根州、明尼苏达州、密西西比州、密苏里州、内华达州、新罕布什尔州、新泽西州、纽约州、北卡罗来纳州的总检察长共同反对出售 Character.ai 用户数据。北达科他州、俄亥俄州、俄克拉荷马州、俄勒冈州、宾夕法尼亚州、罗德岛州、南卡罗来纳州、南达科他州、田纳西州、犹他州、弗吉尼亚州、佛蒙特州、华盛顿州、威斯康星州和西弗吉尼亚州。

article_content:
Yesterday, Anthropic announced a major new feature for artifacts, now available in beta for Mac and Windows: the ability for users to turn artifacts into “apps” they can install on their computers. From the company’s blog:

Starting today, you can use Claude artifacts to create, run, and share desktop apps. The “Install as app” feature is rolling out in beta in Claude for Mac and Windows.

When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer. You choose how much to allow.

Each app can use Claude and your connectors, and it updates automatically when the underlying artifact is edited. This simplifies the process for building and maintaining apps for both knowledge workers and developers. Requests the app makes to Claude count toward your plan’s usage limits.

If you’re an AppStories listener, you know that I’ve long thought it was only a matter of time until one of the big labs figured out how to turn their models’ frontier coding capabilities into a means to disrupt the App Store. This move feels like Anthropic’s first step in that direction.

Before I get into the technical details, let me say this upfront: if I were Apple, I’d be very concerned that Anthropic is now shipping a nicely packaged system for users to make whatever app they want and turn Apple’s ecosystem into Claude’s ecosystem of tools and mods on their computers.

Now, the way Anthropic made this happen can be debated, but I think the system is based on some clever engineering and savvy lock-in strategy. First, for these apps to work, you need the main Claude app to be installed and logged in with your account. These apps require the main Claude process to be running because every action they perform is actually handled by the Claude app behind the scenes, including permissions such as Full Disk Access. All apps made with Claude (either the ones you make, or the ones shared with you by other people) get installed at ~/Applications/Claude Apps, so they’re indexed by Spotlight and can be pinned to the macOS Dock. In fact, when you first create an app inside a Claude conversation (which can be a regular Claude session – you do not need to use Claude Code for these), there is a cute animation and install flow that puts an app directly in your Dock. It’s not too dissimilar from how the Shortcuts app can add individual shortcuts to your Mac’s Dock.

Crucially, these are not native apps created with Swift or SwiftUI: they’re HTML apps, wrapped inside an Electron shim, which is entirely managed by Claude’s Chromium process for Electron. It’s somewhat reminiscent of Raycast’s Glaze product, which uses Vite/React web apps, rendered inside Apple’s WKWebView, wrapped in a custom Swift shell. (Glaze also added the ability to integrate native Swift modules into their apps; I expect Anthropic to add this too.)

To test out this Claude feature, I wanted to create a disk analyzer utility with a menu bar companion for my Mac. The initial prompt was pure vibe coding:

A few minutes later, Opus 5.5 made something that worked and installed it in my Dock, but it wasn’t great. So, I kept tweaking it. As Claude was working, I noticed that it kept editing a single index.html file:

When the app was done, I asked Claude Code to explain how the other Claude built the app. Here is the Claude Code explanation of it all:

Storage Lens isn’t a traditional Mac app. Its 900 KB bundle holds no web code at all, just three pieces:

What looks like a standalone app with its own Dock icon is really a Claude process in disguise.

The app itself is a single HTML file, written by hand with no third-party frameworks: no React, no Tailwind, no D3. It’s plain JavaScript, with one state object and render() functions that rebuild the page. Everything visual is hand-made:

The interesting part is how a web page gets to touch the file system. Storage Lens calls window.claude.use('desktop'), an API that closely mirrors Electron’s own: childProcess.spawn, fs.readdir, shell.trashItem, Menu.setApplicationMenu, app.dock.setBadge. With that, it runs the same command-line tools a power user would:

It reads their output line by line as they run and caches the results in localStorage. Nothing leaves the Mac.

That pretty much says it all. Liquid Glass is faked with CSS (incredible), everything is designed in HTML (not a surprise, given how much Claude loves pretty HTML artifacts), and all code routes through Electron via the main Claude app.

Anyway, back to my Storage Lens app. In a follow-up prompt, I asked:

menu bar works, segmented control still does not, and these overlapping elements are ugly. do better. follow Apple HIG.

I’ve been using the app on my Mac mini this morning to free up some storage. Since I’d already granted Full Disk Access to Claude, I didn’t have to go through a similar flow with the app again: after all, it’s just an HTML page asking Claude to run some shell commands in the background! I also took one of Anthropic’s official demos for a spin – Vitals, their menu bar take on a simplified macOS Activity Monitor.

Apps made by other people can be shared with a traditional artifact landing page; when you install an app made by someone else, you get a warning about potential risks:

I chuckled at the fake Full Disk Access prompt. Once again, Claude already had Full Disk Access, so clicking the ‘Allow’ button doesn’t actually change anything in macOS:

The app, of course, works as expected, too. It breaks Apple’s UI conventions in several ways, but it does perform its primary function reasonably well.

Anthropic has also published a support document that goes into more detail about what these apps can do, how permissions are handled, and what happens to an app you installed from someone else if the original creator stops sharing it. I found this part amusing:

If you lose access to an app, for example because its owner stops sharing it with you, the programs it started stop too. This can take up to about 20 minutes. It can take longer while Claude can’t check, such as when it’s offline, signed out, or using another organization.

So, unless you’re making your own apps, I wouldn’t build a serious workflow on top of an “app” created by somebody else, because they could stop sharing it at any moment and you’d lose access to it.

But then again: why be concerned if you can just prompt your way into a copy of it?

Many longtime macOS and native app purists will grimace at the mere thought of installing vibe-coded “apps” that are Electron wrappers bridging their commands to another app, and I get it. What Anthropic devised here is a hodgepodge of web technologies, disk permissions, and HTML UI that is the opposite of what native Apple app development should – at least in theory – still represent today.

At the same time, if I were Apple, I’d be concerned. Effectively, Anthropic shipped an app creation playground that only requires basic prompts to put together something that works. They did so by entirely bypassing the App Store or Apple’s notarization system for apps distributed outside the App Store, and by creating their own lock-in system around Claude’s identity and capabilities instead.

With Anthropic’s new artifacts-driven system, you’re making apps for your Mac, but, really, you’re making Claude apps for your Mac – which require your Claude account, can use your Claude connectors, and draw usage from your Claude account. Those apps just happen to live in your Dock and menu bar. But if they do what the user asked, who cares? And that’s what I think Apple should be concerned about: the evaporation of “care” for actual apps in the face of something that, ultimately, satisfies the user and doesn’t cost them anything extra.

You may argue: but surely these apps must be so limited, right?

Not quite. I haven’t pushed the limits of this system yet, but since Claude is just running shell commands and AppleScript under the hood, pretty much anything on macOS seems up for grabs.

Case in point: I had Claude reverse-engineer the Shortcuts database on the Mac to make a menu bar launcher for my shortcuts that displays their icons and organizes them by folder.

My idea was simple: since shortcuts can be run in the background on the Mac thanks to Apple’s shortcuts CLI, I figured Claude could make a nice menu bar launcher for them that also supported passing input from the clipboard. My prompt was:

make me an artifact that lets me run shortcuts from specific folders of the Shortcuts app from the menu bar. reverse engineer the Shortcuts database on this Mac so you can find its folders, shortcuts, and official shortcut icons and colors. make it beautiful and compliant with latest Apple HIG for Golden Gate. I want to select which folder I want to quickly access from settings, then the menu bar shows shortcuts from that folder. I click one, and it runs. There is an optional mode to run a shortcut with the contents of system clipboard as input. You can use the native shortcuts CLI for this.

Instead, Claude used MacRemote – my upcoming tool to connect a Mac’s tools and filesystem to any AI agent, soon to be open sourced – to ping my Mac Studio and figure out the Shortcuts.sqlite database there. A few minutes later, I had a working version of the app that let me pick a folder for quick access and run my shortcuts from the menu bar. Through a mix of osascript and Full Disk Access, Claude put together a wrapper that looks nice and took just a few messages in a chat.

That alone was a good example of how far you can push Claude’s apps on the Mac, but I wanted more. Since I know my way around the Shortcuts database thanks to my previous work on Shortcuts Playground, I also wanted the app to display the actual icons of my shortcuts folders. I prompted:

any way you can reverse engineer official folder icons? I believe they’re using SF Symbols in the Shortcuts database

Fairly open-ended question, right? Opus 5.5, of course, figured it out with an approach that is both remarkable and terrifying:

How it gets them. Shortcuts’ scripting interface gives folders only a name and an ID, and the database sits in SIP-protected storage that nothing else can read. So you were right that they’re SF Symbols, but nothing outside Shortcuts can read that from the database. The app reads them another way:

Tested on your library. On the Mac Studio, 27 of your 28 folders came back with a symbol, and each one matches your screenshot. For example, Core Shortcuts is gear, Weekly Prep is calendar, Factory is gearshape.2, Star is star and the plain ones are folder. Iris uses a custom image with no label, so it gets the standard folder icon.

What about Finder integration? I asked Claude to build me something I always wanted to have: a smart “document redirect” utility that opens small Markdown files in TextEdit, but longer ones in a dedicated Markdown processor like Cogito. The prompt was:

I hate that whenever I click a Markdown file .md on my Mac, Xcode opens. make me a simple Mac app that gives me a settings menu where I can choose where to redirect Markdown documents, with a twist: if they’re short, they need to open in TextEdit, if they’re longer, they need to open in something else. so let me choose apps based on a word count I set. call it Markdown Redirect.

Claude worked for a few minutes on it, and it created exactly what I wanted, which I’m using on my Mac right now.

How did it do it? Let’s ask Claude:

How it works: an app built inside Claude can’t be what Finder opens a file with. So the artifact installs a small background helper, Markdown Redirect Helper, in the Applications folder inside your home folder. When you double-click a .md file, the helper counts its words. Files at or under your limit open in the short app, longer ones in the long app. The artifact is where you change the settings, and it lists recent redirects so you can see what went where.

You may be wondering what that Helper actually is. Get ready: it’s an AppleScript file, wrapped inside an application bundle, which calls a shell script that launches the apps.

A hodgepodge, indeed. But unless you go look for this stuff like I did, you never see any of its underlying complexity; ironically, “it just works”.

Now, I can’t share these artifacts with the public because Anthropic currently prohibits apps that require Full Disk Access from being distributed by regular users. (Only Anthropic employees can, it seems?) And, yes, as we have seen, these “apps” are really Claude extensions wrapped up in windows and menu bar apps that give them the appearance of native apps, even though they’re anything but. Two things make them possible: Claude’s coding abilities, and the open nature of macOS itself.

If we were to speculate, I think we all know what’s going to happen here. When Anthropic inevitably figures out how to distribute installable artifacts in a similar fashion on iOS (imagine Bitrig Remote, but for Claude), when they set up a “creator program” for other people to share apps in a pseudo App Store environment, and when OpenAI eventually copies this at scale with ChatGPT…what becomes of traditional apps then?

And how long until Apple’s upcoming Siri Agent lets you create your own personal apps for iPhone, iPad, and Mac?

article_content_zh:
昨天，Anthropic 宣布了一项针对工件的重要新功能，现已推出适用于 Mac 和 Windows 的测试版：用户能够将工件转变为可以安装在计算机上的“应用程序”。来自该公司的博客：

从今天开始，您可以使用 Claude 工件来创建、运行和共享桌面应用程序。 “安装为应用程序”功能正在 Mac 和 Windows 版 Claude 中推出测试版。

当工件作为 Mac 或 Windows 应用程序安装时，它会获得自己的图标并在自己的窗口中打开，而不是在 Claude 内打开。您可以与其他人共享它，并且它需要您的许可才能与您的计算机交互。您选择允许的数量。

每个应用程序都可以使用 Claude 和您的连接器，并且当编辑底层工件时它会自动更新。这简化了知识工作者和开发人员构建和维护应用程序的过程。应用程序向 Claude 发出的请求计入您计划的使用限制。

如果您是 AppStories 的听众，您就会知道，我长期以来一直认为，一个大型实验室找出如何将其模型的前沿编码能力转变为颠覆 App Store 的手段只是时间问题。这一举措感觉像是 Anthropic 朝这个方向迈出的第一步。

在讨论技术细节之前，让我先说一下：如果我是苹果公司，我会非常担心 Anthropic 现在正在为用户提供一个包装精美的系统，让用户可以制作他们想要的任何应用程序，并将苹果的生态系统变成克劳德的计算机上的工具和模组生态系统。

现在，Anthropic 实现这一目标的方式还存在争议，但我认为该系统是基于一些巧妙的工程和精明的锁定策略。首先，为了使这些应用程序正常工作，您需要安装主克劳德应用程序并使用您的帐户登录。这些应用程序需要运行主 Claude 进程，因为它们执行的每个操作实际上都是由 Claude 应用程序在幕后处理的，包括“完全磁盘访问”等权限。所有使用 Claude 制作的应用程序（无论是您制作的应用程序，还是其他人与您共享的应用程序）都安装在 ~/Applications/Claude Apps 中，因此它们由 Spotlight 索引，并且可以固定到 macOS Dock。事实上，当您第一次在 Claude 对话（可以是常规的 Claude 会话 - 您不需要为此使用 Claude Code）中创建应用程序时，有一个可爱的动画和安装流程，可将应用程序直接放入您的 Dock 中。这与“快捷方式”应用程序向 Mac 的 Dock 添加单独的快捷方式的方式并没有太大不同。

至关重要的是，这些不是使用 Swift 或 SwiftUI 创建的本机应用程序：它们是 HTML 应用程序，包装在 Electron shim 中，完全由 Claude 的 Electron Chromium 流程管理。这有点让人想起 Raycast 的 Glaze 产品，该产品使用 Vite/React Web 应用程序，在 Apple 的 WKWebView 内呈现，并封装在自定义 Swift shell 中。 （Glaze 还添加了将本机 Swift 模块集成到其应用程序中的功能；我希望 Anthropic 也能添加此功能。）

为了测试这个 Claude 功能，我想为我的 Mac 创建一个带有菜单栏配套的磁盘分析实用程序。最初的提示是纯粹的共鸣编码：

几分钟后，Opus 5.5 制作了一些可以运行的东西并将其安装在我的 Dock 中，但效果并不好。所以，我一直在调整它。当 Claude 工作时，我注意到它不断编辑一个 index.html 文件：

当应用程序完成后，我要求 Claude Code 解释另一个 Claude 如何构建该应用程序。以下是 Claude Code 对这一切的解释：

title: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to reappoint Nvidia CEO
title_en: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to reappoint Nvidia CEO
author: Elizabeth Dwoskin, Tara  Copp, Nancy Cook, and Natalie Allison
article_content:
As senior members of the Trump administration huddled to discuss the embattled AI company Nvidia over the weekend, Pentagon leaders weighed an audacious idea: invoking a Cold War-era law to pressure Nvidia to restore Jensen Huang as CEO, according to three people familiar with the debate.

The Defense Production Act, a 1950 law that grants the president broad authority to intervene in the economy, has historically been used to mobilize private companies to supply the military in wartime or during national emergencies. The first Trump administration used the law to prompt General Motors to produce ventilators during the covid-19 pandemic.

Before Huang’s return to Nvidia was announced Monday, Pentagon officials including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his senior deputy, Steve Feinberg, discussed how the DPA could be used as leverage to pressure Nvidia’s board to restore an executive to a company that they argued was critical to the national security of the United States, said the three people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe sensitive talks.

News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free

While the law provides no clear path to installing a new CEO, it could be used as a warning. “Essentially they could use the DPA to force Nvidia to shift more of its production to military projects,” said one of the three people, a Trump administration official. That could have curbed the chipmaker’s production plans and profit.

The conversation about the law as part of a campaign to place Huang back in power, which has not been previously reported, reflects the intensity with which the military views the AI race with China and the lengths the Trump administration may be willing to go to intervene in the economy. It also reveals another dimension of the Defense Department’s growing entanglement with Silicon Valley: Though the DPA has never been used to install a leader in a private company, the idea has gained currency with some influential members of the tech sector in recent weeks.

It is unclear what was ultimately conveyed to Nvidia, or whether those arguments made their way to President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, both of whom ultimately became convinced that Huang needed to be back in his job. The two were willing to use the powerful muscle of the federal government to make that happen, as part of a “full-court press” by Cabinet officials over the weekend, one of the people said. Hegseth and Feinberg were part of that campaign, according to two of the people.

Government officials emphasized during the talks that restoring Huang was important for U.S. national security, but Nvidia’s board did not perceive it as a threat, according to a person familiar with the board’s thinking.

The president and vice president came to believe in the importance of Nvidia to the economy and its leader’s singular ability to stabilize financial markets, said two other people familiar with the discussions, who spoke on the condition of anonymity in order to describe them.

Trump personally asked Vance to become involved in brokering the restoration of the embattled CEO as the scandal dragged down the stock market. Huang returned to Nvidia on Monday morning.

The White House referred questions about the strategy to the Pentagon.

“The conversations described between DOW senior leaders never happened and no such proposal was made by the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, or Under Secretary,” said a Pentagon official who refused to be named. (DOW refers to the Department of War, the administration’s preferred name for the Defense Department.)

Nvidia spokesman Patrick Rutherford declined to comment.

Under Hegseth, the Pentagon has made the development of AI capabilities a pillar of military strategy. In a memo issued early this year, he called for the military to become an “AI-first warfighting force” and said that “AI-enabled warfare and AI-enabled capability development will redefine the character of military affairs over the next decade.”

Countries are racing to build such capabilities, under the belief that the nation with the fastest data processing power and the best models will become superior in future conflicts.

Hegseth has entrusted the modernization of the military to Emil Michael, a seasoned Silicon Valley operator and former Uber executive who serves as undersecretary of defense for research and engineering and the military’s chief technology officer, and Feinberg, a billionaire who co-founded the private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management and is the No. 2 in the department.

Together they have brought the military closer to the Silicon Valley companies Anduril and Palantir and to a growing number of start-ups and businesses in fields such as AI, quantum computing and critical minerals by giving out loans and in some cases investing directly in companies. Michael was also part of the conversations about DPA within the department, two of the people said.

Pete Harrell, an attorney and visiting scholar at Georgetown’s Institute of International Economic Law, said it is unclear how the Defense Production Act could be used to reinstate Huang as chief executive of Nvidia, but it raises alarms about how the Trump administration believes it can inject itself into the affairs of private corporations.

“It’s not really interested in setting out … regulations,” he said. “It’s interested in getting five companies in a room and kind of telling them what to do.”

The authority of the DPA is to basically put orders for the U.S. government ahead of anybody else, said Bill Greenwalt, a senior fellow and expert on the Defense Production Act at the American Enterprise Institute. Trying to suggest that the DPA could be leveraged to tie up Nvidia in government contracts isn’t supported at all in the act, Greenwalt said.

A more effective way the administration could have pressured Nvidia without using the DPA would have been through export controls, he added.

After Huang left, the idea of using the DPA to restore him gained currency in Silicon Valley circles.

Last week the cryptocurrency investor Balaji Srinivasan, a former partner at the firm Andreessen Horowitz, posted on social media that if the Nvidia board didn’t immediately restore Huang as CEO, “there’s actually a scenario where the Department of War steps in on Jensen’s side. Why? Given the likely cyberattacks on Microsoft, flights, banks, and now NSA, it’s arguably a matter of US national security to immediately return the most important person in AI to his role at the top AI company. Defense Production Act, but for the restoration of Jensen Huang.”

Shervin Pishevar, a tech investor who worked with Michael at Uber, on Tuesday posted a long thread on X about the restoration of Huang, citing historical applications to argue that the Defense Production Act, if “properly applied, offers an important existing framework for strengthening America’s industrial base.”

“Now that Jensen Huang is back, we should recognize that NVIDIA and America’s leadership in artificial intelligence are not simply matters of corporate governance or shareholder value,” he wrote. “They are matters of national security, economic competitiveness, and geopolitical power.”

article_content_zh:
据三名知情人士透露，周末特朗普政府高级官员聚集在一起讨论陷入困境的人工智能公司英伟达时，五角大楼领导人考虑了一个大胆的想法：援引冷战时期的法律向英伟达施压，要求其恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职务。

《国防生产法》是 1950 年颁布的法律，赋予总统干预经济的广泛权力，历史上曾被用来动员私营公司在战时或国家紧急情况下向军队供货。特朗普第一届政府利用该法律促使通用汽车在 covid-19 大流行期间生产呼吸机。

在黄周一宣布重返英伟达之前，包括国防部长皮特·赫格斯（Pete Hegseth）和他的高级副手史蒂夫·范伯格（Steve Feinberg）在内的五角大楼官员讨论了如何利用 DPA 向英伟达董事会施压，要求其恢复一名高管到一家他们认为对美国国家安全至关重要的公司任职，这三位不愿透露姓名的人士表示，他们描述了敏感的谈话。

有关气候、科学和技术的新闻和指南。免费注册

虽然该法律没有提供任命新首席执行官的明确途径，但它可以作为一个警告。 “从本质上讲，他们可以利用 DPA 迫使英伟达将更多的生产转移到军事项目上，”三人之一、特朗普政府官员表示。这可能会限制该芯片制造商的生产计划和利润。

作为让黄重新掌权的运动的一部分，关于该法律的讨论此前从未被报道过，这反映出军方对与中国的人工智能竞赛的强烈看法，以及特朗普政府可能愿意花多长时间干预经济。它还揭示了国防部与硅谷日益纠缠的另一个方面：尽管 DPA 从未被用来在私营公司中任命领导人，但这一想法最近几周在科技行业一些有影响力的成员中得到了认可。

目前还不清楚最终向英伟达传达了什么，也不清楚这些论点是否传达给了唐纳德·特朗普总统和副总裁 JD·万斯，他们最终都相信黄仁勋需要重返工作岗位。一位知情人士表示，作为内阁官员周末“全场施压”的一部分，两人愿意利用联邦政府的强大力量来实现这一目标。据两位知情人士透露，赫格斯和范伯格参与了该活动。

据一位熟悉董事会想法的人士透露，政府官员在会谈中强调，让黄仁勋复职对美国国家安全很重要，但英伟达董事会并不认为这是一种威胁。

另两位知情人士表示，总统和副总统开始相信英伟达对经济的重要性及其领导者稳定金融市场的非凡能力。为了描述他们的情况，他们要求匿名。

由于丑闻拖累股市，特朗普亲自要求万斯参与斡旋这位陷入困境的首席执行官的复职。黄周一早上回到了英伟达。

白宫将有关该战略的问题提交给五角大楼。

一位不愿透露姓名的五角大楼官员表示：“陶氏高级领导人之间的对话从未发生过，国务卿、副国务卿或副国务卿也没有提出过此类提议。” （DOW 指的是战争部，这是政府对国防部的首选名称。）

英伟达发言人帕特里克·卢瑟福拒绝置评。

在赫格斯的领导下，五角大楼将人工智能能力的发展作为军事战略的支柱。在今年年初发布的一份备忘录中，他呼吁军队成为“人工智能优先的作战力量”，并表示“人工智能驱动的战争和人工智能驱动的能力发展将重新定义未来十年军事的特征。”

【起因与机理】视英伟达AI芯片技术为地缘政治博弈中的核心国家安全资产
【核心事实细节】美政府高层讨论调用《国防生产法》干预英伟达领导层重组。
【各方立场与态度】反映了美政府在关键技术领域对私营企业采取强力行政管控的激进倾向。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Pete Hegseth (Defense Secretary), Steve Feinberg (Deputy), Jensen Huang (Nvidia CEO): Considering using the DPA as leverage to force a change in corporate governance
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Strategic necessity of AI dominance and national security concerns
[Key Fact Detail] Administration officials explored the DPA to influence Nvidia's leadership.
[Key Position & Outlook] Reflects aggressive policy intervention in the private tech sector.

title_zh: 美防长曾策划动用战时法案干预英伟达
summary_zh: 美国国防部长黑格塞斯与五角大楼官员曾商讨动用《国防生产法》施压英伟达董事会，意图确保黄仁勋留任公司高管岗位以保障国家安全

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在英伟达管理层动荡期间，美国国防部长皮特·黑格塞斯（Pete Hegseth）及副手史蒂夫·范伯格（Steve Feinberg）曾探讨援引1950年通过的《国防生产法》（DPA）向英伟达施压。此举意在利用战时法案的强制力，要求企业将生产重心向军事项目倾斜，并间接影响其董事会对CEO人选的决策，以确保持续的AI技术供给。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: During internal turmoil at Nvidia, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and deputy Steve Feinberg discussed invoking the 1950 Defense Production Act (DPA) to pressure Nvidia. The goal was to leverage the act’s authority to mandate military-focused production and influence board-level leadership decisions to ensure the stability of critical AI infrastructure.

elements_zh.who: 皮特·黑格塞斯（美国国防部长）、史蒂夫·范伯格（副手）、英伟达董事会
elements_zh.where: 美国国防部与科技产业监管决策背景
elements_zh.what: 商讨使用《国防生产法》强制英伟达调整CEO人选与生产部署
elements_zh.why: 视AI芯片为美国国家安全的战略核心资产

elements_en.who: Pete Hegseth (Secretary of Defense), Steve Feinberg, Nvidia Board
elements_en.where: DoD policy strategy and regulatory context
elements_en.what: Discussing use of DPA to force CEO continuity and military production shift
elements_en.why: Strategic view of AI chips as critical national security assets

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件暴露了美国行政力量深度介入半导体商业决策的激进趋势，将技术领导力直接等同于防务安全等级。未来全球AI硬件供应链将面临更直接的政商博弈，企业在战略路径规划上将失去完全的商业自主权。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident exposes an aggressive trend of US administrative intervention in semiconductor commercial decisions, treating technological leadership as a core defense capability. Global AI hardware supply chains will face intensified political-commercial friction, with firms losing significant commercial autonomy in their strategic roadmaps.

article_content_zh:
据三名知情人士透露，周末特朗普政府高级官员聚集在一起讨论陷入困境的人工智能公司英伟达时，五角大楼领导人考虑了一个大胆的想法：援引冷战时期的法律向英伟达施压，要求其恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职务。

《国防生产法》是 1950 年颁布的法律，赋予总统干预经济的广泛权力，历史上曾被用来动员私营公司在战时或国家紧急情况下向军队供货。特朗普第一届政府利用该法律促使通用汽车在 covid-19 大流行期间生产呼吸机。

在黄周一宣布重返英伟达之前，包括国防部长皮特·赫格斯（Pete Hegseth）和他的高级副手史蒂夫·范伯格（Steve Feinberg）在内的五角大楼官员讨论了如何利用 DPA 向英伟达董事会施压，要求其恢复一名高管到一家他们认为对美国国家安全至关重要的公司任职，这三位不愿透露姓名的人士表示，他们描述了敏感的谈话。

有关气候、科学和技术的新闻和指南。免费注册

虽然该法律没有提供任命新首席执行官的明确途径，但它可以作为一个警告。 “从本质上讲，他们可以利用 DPA 迫使英伟达将更多的生产转移到军事项目上，”三人之一、特朗普政府官员表示。这可能会限制该芯片制造商的生产计划和利润。

作为让黄重新掌权的运动的一部分，关于该法律的讨论此前从未被报道过，这反映出军方对与中国的人工智能竞赛的强烈看法，以及特朗普政府可能愿意花多长时间干预经济。它还揭示了国防部与硅谷日益纠缠的另一个方面：尽管 DPA 从未被用来在私营公司中任命领导人，但这一想法最近几周在科技行业一些有影响力的成员中得到了认可。

目前还不清楚最终向英伟达传达了什么，也不清楚这些论点是否传达给了唐纳德·特朗普总统和副总裁 JD·万斯，他们最终都相信黄仁勋需要重返工作岗位。一位知情人士表示，作为内阁官员周末“全场施压”的一部分，两人愿意利用联邦政府的强大力量来实现这一目标。据两位知情人士透露，赫格斯和范伯格参与了该活动。

据一位熟悉董事会想法的人士透露，政府官员在会谈中强调，让黄仁勋复职对美国国家安全很重要，但英伟达董事会并不认为这是一种威胁。

另两位知情人士表示，总统和副总统开始相信英伟达对经济的重要性及其领导者稳定金融市场的非凡能力。为了描述他们的情况，他们要求匿名。

由于丑闻拖累股市，特朗普亲自要求万斯参与斡旋这位陷入困境的首席执行官的复职。黄周一早上回到了英伟达。

白宫将有关该战略的问题提交给五角大楼。

一位不愿透露姓名的五角大楼官员表示：“陶氏高级领导人之间的对话从未发生过，国务卿、副国务卿或副国务卿也没有提出过此类提议。” （DOW 指的是战争部，这是政府对国防部的首选名称。）

英伟达发言人帕特里克·卢瑟福拒绝置评。

在赫格斯的领导下，五角大楼将人工智能能力的发展作为军事战略的支柱。在今年年初发布的一份备忘录中，他呼吁军队成为“人工智能优先的作战力量”，并表示“人工智能驱动的战争和人工智能驱动的能力发展将重新定义未来十年军事的特征。”

title: Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After AI Chip Curbs

While Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia Corp. buoyed AI stocks briefly earlier this week, bankers remained concerned about the legal risks of financing data centers and neoclouds potentially facing stricter US export controls. Deals that were near the finish line are suddenly in doubt and lenders trying to sell down their exposure are struggling to find interested buyers.

Some lenders have delayed moving forward as they do more due diligence on an upsized $6.6 billion loan sought by Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres, whose Malaysian facilities are used by clients including Bytedance, according to people involved in the discussions. Bain referred questions to BDC, which declined to comment. Bytedance did not respond to a request for comment.

One bank has decided to pass on a fully underwritten $372 million loan for Partners Group-backed Digital Halo, while others are asking more questions, people familiar with those talks said. The funds are for a data center in Malaysia that services Alibaba and other customers, they said. Multiple banks were also reassessing a $480 million loan for Aolani, a Singapore-based neocloud that gets business from Bytedance, separate people familiar said last week.

Digital Halo, Aolani and Alibaba didn't respond to questions. Partners Group declined to comment.

The Biden administration's 2022 export restrictions on advanced US chips spawned an ecosystem of companies in Southeast Asia to help Chinese technology firms access the coveted hardware remotely. Lending to data centers in the region surged in the following years, while chip financing was just beginning to take off more recently as banks got more comfortable with the riskier deals.

That changed after the US announced last week that companies in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil will need a US government license to purchase advanced AI chips from American manufacturers. Globally, data centers that already lease significant compute to Chinese firms will need a separate license to continue doing so and have a 90-day window to obtain it.

More than a dozen bankers said their teams were waiting for answers on how the new curbs would affect borrowers and that would at the very least delay potential deals from going through. Lenders including Citigroup Inc. and Standard Chartered Plc, as well as Singapore's major banks, have launched a sweeping review of data center clients, people familiar with the matter said earlier.

Some banks are looking to reduce certain exposure to AI and data center debt, including through secondary loan sales and so-called significant risk transfers. Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd. is seeking a SRT deal of around $1 billion to offload risks tied to data center and infrastructure loans among other sectors, people familiar with the matter said. But the current news headlines are slowing progress, one of them said, adding that details are not firmed up and could change.

A representative for UOB declined to comment, citing deal confidentiality.

Private lenders, who were the most aggressive in seeking out the higher returns associated with GPU financing, are also growing more cautious. At least one fund has decided not to participate in a $300 million loan to GMI Cloud, an Nvidia cloud partner, to fund chips for a Thai data center that would be used by Tencent, according to a person familiar with the matter.

GMI Cloud and Tencent did not respond to requests for comment.

The chill has extended beyond debt financing. DayOne Data Centers Ltd., whose biggest customer is Bytedance, has put plans for a US public listing on hold, people familiar said earlier. A consortium involving BlackRock Inc. is considering lowering its offer for a portfolio of Asia Pacific data centers, according to separate people familiar.

It's not a bad thing that the new restrictions have forced a broad reevaluation of deals, according to Ben Kostrzewa, an international trade lawyer at Hogan Lovells Cadwalader. Since 2023, loans to data center companies in Asia Pacific have soared from virtually zero to more than $49 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

"It could be a good pause, to take stock and to review these projects, given how frothy the market has been for a while," Kostrzewa said. "It won't stop all these data centers being built, it won't stop the market, but it will slow it all down."

title_zh: 美国出口限制收紧，AI数据中心融资受阻
summary_zh: 美国针对东南亚及全球数据中心的AI芯片出口新规，导致多项大型算力项目融资搁置

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 由于美国商务部最新规定要求对新加坡、马来西亚、印尼、泰国及巴西出口先进AI芯片实施许可制度，贝恩资本旗下Bridge Data Centres等机构的数十亿美元融资计划陷入停滞。金融机构因担忧涉及中资企业的算力租赁合规性风险，正重新评估涉及Digital Halo、Aolani等项目的贷款意向。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Recent US export restrictions requiring licenses for advanced AI chips shipped to Southeast Asia and Brazil have halted multi-billion dollar data center financing deals. Lenders are reassessing exposure to facilities serving Chinese firms, including Bridge Data Centres, Digital Halo, and Aolani, due to heightened regulatory uncertainty.

elements_zh.who: 贝恩资本（Bain Capital）、Bridge Data Centres、Digital Halo、Aolani、美国商务部
elements_zh.where: 东南亚地区（马来西亚、新加坡等）数据中心融资市场
elements_zh.what: 出口限制导致针对中资客户的算力基建贷款出现违约风险，多家银行暂停融资审核
elements_zh.why: 美国防范中资企业绕道海外远程获取算力，将出口管制触角延伸至第三方国家的算力基础设施

elements_en.who: Bain Capital, Bridge Data Centres, Digital Halo, Aolani, US Department of Commerce
elements_en.where: Southeast Asian data center financing market
elements_en.what: Export restrictions caused funding halts for projects serving Chinese clients, forcing lenders to reassess credit risk.
elements_en.why: US move to curb Chinese companies from accessing remote compute power via third-party offshore data centers.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举标志着美方对AI硬件的管控逻辑已从单一“卖方限制”转向针对“算力租用生态”的全方位围堵，将离岸数据中心变为监管高压区。未来中资AI企业在海外部署算力集群的合规成本将呈指数级增长，供应链金融机构将因地缘政治风险溢价而大幅收缩对东南亚算力基建的授信规模。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The shift from hardware export bans to monitoring remote compute access marks a strategic expansion of US surveillance into the offshore data center ecosystem. Expect capital flight from Southeast Asian compute projects as financial institutions factor in uncontrollable regulatory risks, significantly raising the barriers for Chinese firms building offshore AI infrastructure.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 美国针对东南亚及全球多个关键市场实施AI芯片出口许可制，直接打击了依托当地设施租用算力的中资企业生态。贝恩资本及多家参与海外数据中心融资的银行机构目前面临合规不确定性，导致多项逾数亿美元的授信项目搁浅，行业正处于合规重构与资本避险的动荡期。
ai_analysis.digest_en: The US has imposed strict export licensing requirements on AI chips for several Southeast Asian markets and Brazil, effectively targeting the supply chain for Chinese companies utilizing offshore compute. Major financing deals are currently stalled as lenders scramble to assess the compliance impact of ongoing service contracts with Chinese tech firms.
key_points_zh: 美方将AI芯片出口许可范围扩大至东南亚多国及巴西
贝恩资本等机构涉及中资算力租赁的数据中心融资被迫叫停或重新评估
数据中心需在90天内获得独立许可，以维持对中资客户的算力租用服务
key_points_en: US expanded AI chip export license requirements to Southeast Asia and Brazil.
Data center financing for projects serving Chinese firms, including those by Bain Capital, has stalled.
Data centers have a 90-day grace period to obtain licenses for existing services to Chinese entities.
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 此举标志着美方对AI硬件的管控逻辑已从单一“卖方限制”转向针对“算力租用生态”的全方位围堵，将离岸数据中心变为监管高压区。未来中资AI企业在海外部署算力集群的合规成本将呈指数级增长，供应链金融机构将因地缘政治风险溢价而大幅收缩对东南亚算力基建的授信规模。
