尽管黄仁勋出人意料地重返英伟达公司，本周早些时候短暂提振了人工智能股票，但银行家们仍然担心数据中心和新云融资可能面临更严格的美国出口管制的法律风险。接近终点线的交易突然受到质疑，试图出售其风险敞口的贷款人正在努力寻找感兴趣的买家。

据参与讨论的人士透露，一些贷款机构推迟了行动，因为他们对贝恩资本 Bridge Data Centres 寻求的 66 亿美元巨额贷款进行了更多尽职调查，字节跳动等客户使用了该中心马来西亚的设施。贝恩将问题转给了 BDC，但 BDC 拒绝置评。字节跳动没有回应置评请求。

知情人士称，一家银行已决定为合众集团支持的 Digital Halo 提供全额承保的 3.72 亿美元贷款，而其他银行则提出了更多问题。他们表示，这些资金将用于马来西亚的一个数据中心，为阿里巴巴和其他客户提供服务。另一位知情人士上周表示，多家银行也在重新评估为 Aolani 提供的 4.8 亿美元贷款，Aolani 是一家总部位于新加坡的 Neocloud，从字节跳动获得业务。

Digital Halo、奥拉尼和阿里巴巴均未回应提问。合众集团拒绝置评。

拜登政府 2022 年对美国先进芯片的出口限制催生了东南亚公司的生态系统，帮助中国科技公司远程访问令人垂涎的硬件。接下来几年，对该地区数据中心的贷款激增，而随着银行对风险较高的交易更加放心，芯片融资最近才刚刚开始起飞。

在美国上周宣布新加坡、马来西亚、印度尼西亚、泰国和巴西的公司需要获得美国政府许可才能从美国制造商购买先进的人工智能芯片后，情况发生了变化。在全球范围内，已经向中国公司租赁大量计算能力的数据中心将需要单独的许可证才能继续这样做，并且有 90 天的时间窗口来获得它。

十几位银行家表示，他们的团队正在等待新限制措施将如何影响借款人的答案，这至少会推迟潜在交易的进行。知情人士早些时候表示，包括花旗集团和渣打银行在内的贷款机构以及新加坡的主要银行已经对数据中心客户进行了全面审查。

一些银行正在寻求减少人工智能和数据中心债务的某些风险敞口，包括通过二次贷款销售和所谓的重大风险转移。知情人士称，新加坡大华银行正在寻求约 10 亿美元的 SRT 交易，以缓解与数据中心和基础设施贷款等其他行业相关的风险。但其中一位人士表示，目前的新闻头条正在减缓进展，并补充说细节尚未确定，可能会发生变化。

大华银行的一名代表以交易保密为由拒绝置评。

私人贷款机构在寻求与 GPU 融资相关的更高回报方面最为积极，但也变得更加谨慎。据一位知情人士透露，至少有一只基金已决定不参与向 Nvidia 云合作伙伴 GMI Cloud 提供的 3 亿美元贷款，该贷款旨在为腾讯将使用的泰国数据中心提供芯片资金。

GMI云和腾讯没有回应置评请求。

寒意已经蔓延到债务融资之外。知情人士早些时候表示，DayOne Data Centers Ltd. 的最大客户是字节跳动，该公司已搁置在美国公开上市的计划。另据知情人士透露，贝莱德 (BlackRock Inc.) 参与的一个财团正在考虑降低对亚太数据中心投资组合的报价。

霍金路伟凯威莱德 (Hogan Lovells Cadwalader) 的国际贸易律师本·科斯特泽瓦 (Ben Kostrzewa) 表示，新的限制措施迫使人们对交易进行广泛的重新评估，这并不是一件坏事。彭博社汇编的数据显示，自 2023 年以来，亚太地区数据中心公司的贷款已从几乎为零飙升至超过 490 亿美元。

【起因与机理】美国防范中资企业绕道海外远程获取算力，将出口管制触角延伸至第三方国家的算力基础设施

title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
title_en: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
article_content:
Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that’s designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market.

First spotted by Patentlyze, the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.

According to the patent, My Channel would be able to churn out entire movies of various genres. If a user watches a lot of videos about Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, the system might serve up something like Ash Koosha’s Odysseus: The Fall. The patent details how My Channel might be able to connect to other streaming services — which would give it even more information about users and, presumably, access to useful training data for video generation. It all seems like a convoluted way to whip up AI knockoffs of professionally produced art, but what’s most unsettling about the patent are its mentions of My Channel creating digital avatars of users and turning them into “the protagonist or lead character” in the content it pumps out.

Setting aside the fact that My Channel would use photos, videos, and audio clips of people to create these avatars, the system sounds like it is designed to generate a form of “entertainment” that is deeply at odds with what makes engaging with art a worthwhile, enjoyable experience. It can be fun to metaphorically project one’s self into fictional narratives to understand how characters feel, but what Google is proposing is giving people access to an endless supply of bespoke content that doesn’t at all encourage them to use their imaginations to empathize with or relate to the characters. The patent makes it seem like Google thinks that viewers would be entertained enough just by seeing themselves onscreen. That’s bleak in and of itself because My Channel sounds very much like an unholy cross between JibJab and the panoptic elements of Google.

My Channel feels like an even more depressing idea when you consider how the service would make it that much easier for its users to avoid broadening their horizons by being exposed to new things that exist outside their comfort zones. If Google were able to strike the right licensing deals with other streaming services, My Channel users could presumably gorge themselves on artless AI regurgitations of preexisting content. That might keep some people glued to the service — a goal that every streaming platform strives for — but it would also discourage them from engaging with entertainment that isn’t expressly crafted to appeal to their assumed tastes.

When people refer to AI-generated videos as “slop,” they’re talking about the fact that generative models are incapable of generating art with the same kind of creative intention that makes human-made stories compelling. Video generation models can mimic visual elements of the data (read: movies and series) they’re trained on, but they cannot truly think or feel in the way that directors, writers, and actors can. This reality is why it has been so baffling to see AI-boosting entertainment companies, streamers, and studios insisting that the technology will fundamentally revolutionize the industry for the better. It feels much more likely that gen AI is going to keep flooding the internet with garbage no one wants to watch.

article_content_zh:
去年，谷歌为名为“我的频道”的系统申请了专利，该系统旨在根据公司了解的用户信息创建充满个性化、人工智能生成的视频和广告的提要。该专利已被拒绝，但不幸的是，谷歌可能会上诉或重新提交修改版本，我们可以看到这个怪物进入市场。

该专利于去年 5 月提交并于上周发布，最先由 Patentlyze 发现。该专利描述了 My Channel 如何使用个人的人口统计数据和观看历史记录来创建自己的提示，然后将其输入法学硕士，帮助生成适合该人特定兴趣的人工智能视频。除了考虑用户倾向于观看哪些类型的视频之外，系统还会从他们的设备捕获上下文数据，例如 IP 地址、GPS 位置以及有关用户年龄的具体详细信息。我的频道还可以根据体育比分和社交媒体上发生的事情等当前新闻进行提示，并且所有视频生成都将在谷歌的服务器上进行。

根据该专利，我的频道将能够制作各种类型的整部电影。如果用户观看了很多有关克里斯托弗·诺兰的《奥德赛》的视频，系统可能会提供类似 Ash Koosha 的《奥德修斯：堕落》之类的视频。该专利详细说明了“我的频道”如何连接到其他流媒体服务，这将为其提供更多有关用户的信息，并可能获得用于视频生成的有用训练数据。这一切似乎都是用人工智能模仿专业艺术作品的复杂方式，但该专利最令人不安的是它提到“我的频道”创建用户的数字化身，并将其变成内容中的“主角或主角”。

撇开“我的频道”会使用人们的照片、视频和音频片段来创建这些头像这一事实不谈，该系统听起来像是为了生成一种“娱乐”形式而设计的，而这种形式与让艺术成为一种有价值的、令人愉快的体验截然不同。将自己隐喻地投射到虚构的叙述中以了解角色的感受可能很有趣，但谷歌的提议是让人们获得无穷无尽的定制内容，而这根本不鼓励他们利用想象力来同情角色或与角色建立联系。这项专利让人觉得谷歌认为观众只要在屏幕上看到自己就已经足够有趣了。这本身就很黯淡，因为“我的频道”听起来很像 JibJab 和 Google 全景元素之间的邪恶交叉。

当你考虑到该服务如何让用户更容易避免接触舒适区之外的新事物来扩大视野时，“我的频道”感觉就像是一个更令人沮丧的想法。如果谷歌能够与其他流媒体服务达成正确的许可协议，那么“我的频道”的用户可能会沉迷于对现有内容进行简单的人工智能反刍。这可能会让一些人坚持使用该服务——这是每个流媒体平台都努力追求的目标——但也会阻止他们参与那些并非专门为迎合他们假定口味而设计的娱乐活动。

当人们将人工智能生成的视频称为“slop”时，他们谈论的是这样一个事实：生成模型无法生成具有与使人造故事引人入胜的创意意图相同的艺术。视频生成模型可以模仿它们所训练的数据的视觉元素（例如：电影和电视剧），但它们无法像导演、编剧和演员那样真正思考或感受。这一现实就是为什么看到人工智能推动的娱乐公司、流媒体和工作室坚持认为这项技术将从根本上彻底改变这个行业，让这个行业变得更好，这是令人困惑的。感觉更有可能的是，新一代人工智能将继续在互联网上充斥着没人愿意看到的垃圾。

author: NBC News

title: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales
title_en: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales

inline_images.caption: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales

author: Reuters
article_content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: $NVDA) has agreed to pay $290 million to settle a long-running US investor lawsuit accusing the chipmaker of misleading shareholders about the role crypto mining played in its gaming business.

The proposed settlement follows a lawsuit filed in 2018 by investors who claimed Nvidia failed to properly disclose how much of its graphics processing unit (GPU) revenue came from crypto miners rather than video game players, according to a court filing on Tuesday,

The investors, led by Stockholm-based asset manager E. Ohman J:or Fonder AB, argued that Nvidia presented strong gaming revenue as evidence of demand from gamers while a significant portion of sales was driven by crypto mining.

NYSE Parent ICE to Bring Hyperliquid-Based Perpetual Futures to US

Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Price Forecast To $1.6 Million By 2036

Survey Finds 90% Of Large Businesses Are Embracing Tokenized Money

Moody's Assigns Investment-Grade Rating To Ripple's Stablecoin

Stablecoin Firm RedotPay To Hold IPO By Year's End: Reports

Nvidia denied wrongdoing as part of the agreement. The settlement still requires preliminary approval from a US judge before it can move forward.

The case centers on Nvidia's sales during the 2017 crypto boom, when rising prices for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) and Ether (CRYPTO: $ETH) encouraged miners to buy large numbers of powerful GPUs.

Although Nvidia introduced graphics cards specifically designed for crypto mining, investors alleged that miners also purchased GeForce gaming GPUs, helping drive reported gaming revenue higher.

The issue became more apparent in 2018, when crypto prices fell and demand for mining hardware weakened. Nvidia subsequently lowered its revenue forecast, citing a sharp decline in crypto-related demand and excess inventory of gaming GPUs. The company's shares also came under pressure after the news.

A federal district court initially dismissed the case in 2021, but an appeals court revived key claims in August 2023. The US Supreme Court later dismissed Nvidia's appeal in December 2024, allowing the case to return to the lower court.

In March 2026, the court certified the lawsuit as a class action, covering investors who bought Nvidia shares between August 10, 2017, and November 15, 2018.

Nvidia shares are currently trading at $142.97, down around 8% today.

Nvidia（纳斯达克股票代码：$NVDA）已同意支付 2.9 亿美元，以和解一项长期存在的美国投资者诉讼，该诉讼指控该芯片制造商在加密货币挖矿在其游戏业务中所扮演的角色方面误导股东。

根据周二的一份法庭文件，投资者在 2018 年提起诉讼，声称英伟达未能正确披露其图形处理单元 (GPU) 收入有多少来自加密货币矿工而不是视频游戏玩家，随后提出了和解方案。

以斯德哥尔摩资产管理公司 E. Ohman J:or Fonder AB 为首的投资者认为，英伟达提供了强劲的游戏收入，证明了游戏玩家的需求，而很大一部分销售是由加密货币挖矿推动的。

作为协议的一部分，英伟达否认存在不当行为。该和解协议仍需获得美国法官的初步批准才能继续推进。

该案例以 Nvidia 在 2017 年加密货币繁荣期间的销售为中心，当时比特币（加密货币：$BTC）和以太币（加密货币：$ETH）价格上涨鼓励矿工购买大量强大的 GPU。

尽管 Nvidia 推出了专门为加密货币挖矿设计的显卡，但投资者声称矿工还购买了 GeForce 游戏 GPU，从而帮助推高了报告的游戏收入。

这个问题在 2018 年变得更加明显，当时加密货币价格下跌，采矿硬件的需求减弱。英伟达随后下调了收入预期，理由是加密货币相关需求急剧下降以及游戏 GPU 库存过剩。消息传出后，该公司股价也承压。

联邦地方法院最初于 2021 年驳回了此案，但上诉法院于 2023 年 8 月恢复了关键索赔。美国最高法院后来于 2024 年 12 月驳回了 Nvidia 的上诉，允许案件返回下级法院。

2026 年 3 月，法院将该诉讼认证为集体诉讼，涵盖在 2017 年 8 月 10 日至 2018 年 11 月 15 日期间购买 Nvidia 股票的投资者。

title: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat
title_en: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat

inline_images.caption: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat

author: Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff, Erin Banco, Jonathan Landay and Andrew Goudsward
article_content:
WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US Justice Department did not conduct a formal investigation into Jensen Huang before US President Donald Trump pushed for his return as Nvidia chief executive this week, despite active probes into the chipmaker’s customers and allegations he conducted an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence, according to three people familiar with the matter.

Instead, Attorney General Todd Blanche concluded that there was no evidence the tech titan had broken any laws based on the Justice Department’s ongoing investigations into two Nvidia clients, Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, which are suspected of smuggling advanced microchips to China, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

That determination, which is subject to change as the probes continue, was crucial to Blanche’s decision to tell Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the weekend that he possessed no evidence that Huang posed a risk to national security, said two of the people.

Jensen Huang’s reinstatement has angered members of Congress — both Republicans and Democrats — who say it’s too soon to set aside questions about whether Nvidia or its CEO endangered US national security. The lack of any additional effort to examine their roles prior to Trump’s intervention will likely fuel a push for more investigations on Capitol Hill.

Huang is due to testify next week.

The Justice Department probes of Nvidia customers found no evidence that Huang was acting as an agent of China or knowingly transferred sensitive semiconductor technology or information to China, the two people said. Nvidia was not a target of those investigations and cooperated, providing documents, interviews and other data that helped lead to that conclusion, they added.

There was also no counterintelligence probe of Huang himself. US spy agencies have gathered information on Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive and alleged paramour of Jensen Huang suspected of working with Chinese intelligence, said two other people familiar with the effort. But the US had no details that would warrant a probe into the Nvidia CEO, they said.

Counterintelligence investigations are run separately from criminal investigations and are aimed at monitoring and neutralizing national security threats, rather than building a case for indictment.

Justice Department officials concluded that Nvidia and Huang had committed no wrongdoing and did not suspect its chief executive posed a national-security risk, two of the people familiar with the matter said.

Trump and Vance conveyed that conclusion to Nvidia’s board, which decided to reinstate Huang, according to Trump’s account of events in a CNBC interview on Monday.

Speaking to reporters in Ohio on Wednesday, Vance said Justice Department and national security officials told him that Huang was not the subject of an investigation prior to his reinstatement.

“We were told that he was under no investigation,” he said, adding that he didn’t think Trump would need to pardon Huang because he had not broken the law. “I haven’t seen any evidence again that he committed a crime.”

Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12 following allegations he conducted affairs with Alice Huang and at least two employees. Jensen Huang acknowledged infidelities but has not confirmed his involvement with Alice Huang specifically. Reuters has been unable to reach her or confirm her links to Chinese spy services.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio briefed Trump in May about the affair, according to the New York Times.

The Times also reported that Alice Huang was in touch with a top Chinese spy official for more than a year during the affair.

Blanche said following Huang’s departure that the FBI was “looking into” reports that he was having an affair with a spy, but had not reached any conclusions.

At a press conference on Tuesday, Blanche repeatedly declined to answer questions about how the Trump administration determined that Huang was not a threat to US national security.

He said he had found no evidence that Nvidia engaged in wrongdoing.

“I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything other than a good corporate citizen,” he said at the press conference.

The Justice Department is also conducting antitrust reviews of Nvidia business deals unrelated to Huang’s personal behavior.

A Justice Department spokesperson referred questions to Blanche’s statement, and a DOJ official previously told Reuters that no evidence of wrongdoing has been found. The FBI and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence did not respond to requests for comment.

The Wall Street Journal first reported that Blanche’s assessment was based on evidence from the two related investigations.

Experts said the federal officials bypassed standard counterintelligence protocols.

“No formal Justice Department investigation into the national security allegations has been reported. That’s alarming, if unsurprising,” said Steve Cash, a former CIA officer who heads The Steady State, an association of former national security officials.

The FBI has provided at least two “defensive briefings” to Nvidia leadership regarding Chinese espionage tactics, according to a law enforcement official familiar with the briefings, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

It was not clear whether those briefings, which have not been previously reported, were standard security engagements routinely provided to major American technology firms, or focused specifically on the threat posed by Alice Huang. It also was not clear whether Huang himself was briefed.

Federal officials often deliver broad warnings to US companies about espionage risks, two former senior law enforcement officials told Reuters.

Defensive briefings can lead to a criminal inquiry if the warnings are ignored, said Kevin Carroll, a former undercover CIA operations officer, but their main purpose is to protect national security.

Di Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff, Erin Banco, Jonathan Landay e Andrew Goudsward

WASHINGTON, 25 novembre (Reuters) - Il Dipartimento di Giustizia degli Stati Uniti non ha condotto un’indagine formale su Jensen Huang prima che il presidente degli Stati Uniti Donald Trump spingesse per il suo ritorno come amministratore delegato di Nvidia questa settimana, nonostante le indagini in corso sui clienti del produttore di chip e le accuse secondo cui avrebbe avuto una relazione con una donna legata ai servizi segreti cinesi, secondo tre persone a conoscenza della questione.

Al contrario, il procuratore generale Todd Blanche ha concluso che non vi fossero prove che il magnate della tecnologia avesse violato alcuna legge, sulla base delle indagini in corso del Dipartimento di Giustizia su due clienti di Nvidia, Super Micro Computer e Megaspeed International, sospettati di contrabbandare microchip avanzati in Cina, hanno affermato le fonti, che hanno parlato a condizione di rimanere anonime.

Tale valutazione, soggetta a modifiche man mano che le indagini proseguono, è stata determinante nella decisione di Blanche di comunicare a Trump e al vicepresidente JD Vance nel fine settimana di non disporre di prove che Huang rappresentasse un rischio per la sicurezza nazionale, hanno affermato due delle fonti.

La reintegrazione di Jensen Huang ha suscitato l’indignazione dei membri del Congresso — sia repubblicani che democratici — i quali sostengono che sia troppo presto per accantonare i dubbi sul fatto che Nvidia o il suo amministratore delegato abbiano messo a rischio la sicurezza nazionale degli Stati Uniti. La mancanza di ulteriori sforzi per esaminare i loro ruoli prima dell’intervento di Trump alimenterà probabilmente la richiesta di ulteriori indagini a Capitol Hill.

Huang è chiamato a testimoniare la prossima settimana.

Le indagini del Dipartimento di Giustizia sui clienti di Nvidia non hanno trovato prove che Huang agisse come agente della Cina o che avesse consapevolmente trasferito in Cina tecnologia o informazioni sensibili relative ai semiconduttori, hanno affermato le due fonti. Nvidia non era oggetto di tali indagini e ha collaborato, fornendo documenti, interviste e altri dati che hanno contribuito a giungere a tale conclusione, hanno aggiunto.

Non è stata inoltre condotta alcuna indagine di controspionaggio su Huang stesso. Le agenzie di intelligence statunitensi hanno raccolto informazioni su Alice Huang, ex dirigente di Megaspeed e presunta compagna di Jensen Huang, sospettata di collaborare con i servizi segreti cinesi, hanno affermato altre due persone a conoscenza dell’operazione. Tuttavia, gli Stati Uniti non disponevano di dettagli che giustificassero un’indagine sul CEO di Nvidia, hanno affermato.

Le indagini di controspionaggio sono condotte separatamente dalle indagini penali e mirano a monitorare e neutralizzare le minacce alla sicurezza nazionale, piuttosto che a costruire un caso per un’incriminazione.

I funzionari del Dipartimento di Giustizia hanno concluso che Nvidia e Huang non avessero commesso alcun illecito e non sospettavano che il suo amministratore delegato rappresentasse un rischio per la sicurezza nazionale, hanno affermato due delle persone a conoscenza della questione.

Trump e Vance hanno comunicato tale conclusione al consiglio di amministrazione di Nvidia, che ha deciso di reintegrare Huang, secondo quanto riferito da Trump in un’intervista alla CNBC lunedì.

Parlando con i giornalisti in Ohio mercoledì, Vance ha affermato che i funzionari del Dipartimento di Giustizia e della sicurezza nazionale gli avevano comunicato che Huang non era oggetto di alcuna indagine prima della sua reintegrazione.

«Ci è stato detto che non era oggetto di alcuna indagine», ha affermato, aggiungendo che non riteneva necessario che Trump concedesse la grazia a Huang poiché questi non aveva violato la legge. «Non ho visto alcuna prova che dimostri che abbia commesso un reato».

«UN BUON CITTADINO AZIENDALE»

Huang si è dimesso dalla carica di amministratore delegato di Nvidia il 12 novembre a seguito delle accuse di aver intrattenuto relazioni extraconiugali con Alice Huang e almeno due dipendenti. Jensen Huang ha ammesso le infedeltà, ma non ha confermato in modo specifico la sua relazione con Alice Huang. Reuters non è riuscita a contattarla né a confermare i suoi legami con i servizi segreti cinesi.

Secondo il New York Times, a maggio il segretario di Stato Marco Rubio ha informato Trump della vicenda.

Il Times ha inoltre riferito che Alice Huang è rimasta in contatto con un alto funzionario dei servizi segreti cinesi per più di un anno durante la relazione.

Blanche ha dichiarato, in seguito alle dimissioni di Huang, che l’FBI stava “esaminando” le segnalazioni secondo cui egli avrebbe avuto una relazione con una spia, ma non era giunta ad alcuna conclusione.

Martedì, durante una conferenza stampa, Blanche ha ripetutamente rifiutato di rispondere alle domande su come l’amministrazione Trump abbia stabilito che Huang non rappresentasse una minaccia per la sicurezza nazionale degli Stati Uniti.

Ha affermato di non aver trovato alcuna prova che Nvidia fosse coinvolta in attività illecite.

«Non ho alcun motivo di stare qui a dire che Nvidia sia altro che un’azienda socialmente responsabile», ha dichiarato durante la conferenza stampa.

Il Dipartimento di Giustizia sta inoltre conducendo indagini antitrust su operazioni commerciali di Nvidia non correlate al comportamento personale di Huang.

Un portavoce del Dipartimento di Giustizia ha rinviato le domande alla dichiarazione di Blanche, mentre un funzionario del Dipartimento di Giustizia aveva precedentemente dichiarato a Reuters che non erano state trovate prove di comportamenti illeciti. L’FBI e l’Ufficio del Direttore dell’Intelligence Nazionale non hanno risposto alle richieste di commento.

Il Wall Street Journal ha riportato per primo che la valutazione di Blanche si basava su prove provenienti dalle due indagini correlate.

Gli esperti hanno affermato che i funzionari federali hanno aggirato i protocolli standard di controspionaggio.

«Non è stata segnalata alcuna indagine formale del Dipartimento di Giustizia sulle accuse relative alla sicurezza nazionale. È allarmante, anche se non sorprendente», ha affermato Steve Cash, ex funzionario della CIA a capo di The Steady State, un’associazione di ex funzionari della sicurezza nazionale.

L’FBI ha fornito almeno due “briefing difensivi” alla dirigenza di Nvidia riguardo alle tattiche di spionaggio cinesi, secondo un funzionario delle forze dell’ordine a conoscenza dei briefing, che ha parlato a condizione di rimanere anonimo.

Non è chiaro se tali briefing, di cui non si era mai parlato prima, fossero incontri di sicurezza standard forniti di routine alle principali aziende tecnologiche americane, oppure se fossero incentrati specificamente sulla minaccia rappresentata da Alice Huang. Non è chiaro nemmeno se lo stesso Huang sia stato informato.

I funzionari federali spesso rivolgono avvertimenti generali alle aziende statunitensi sui rischi di spionaggio, hanno riferito a Reuters due ex alti funzionari delle forze dell’ordine.

I briefing difensivi possono portare a un’indagine penale se gli avvertimenti vengono ignorati, ha affermato Kevin Carroll, ex agente operativo sotto copertura della CIA, ma il loro scopo principale è proteggere la sicurezza nazionale.

(Reporter Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff, Erin Banco, Jonathan Landay e Andrew Goudsward; editor Andy Sullivan, Don Durfee e Nick Zieminski)

article_content_zh:
华盛顿，11 月 25 日（路透社）——据三名知情人士透露，在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周推动黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官之前，美国司法部并未对黄仁勋进行正式调查，尽管对这家芯片制造商的客户进行了积极调查，并指控他与一名与中国情报部门有关的女性有染。

不愿透露姓名的人士表示，司法部长托德·布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 得出的结论是，根据司法部对 Nvidia 的两家客户 Super Micro Computer 和 Megaspeed International 的持续调查，没有证据表明这家科技巨头违反了任何法律，这两家公司涉嫌向中国走私先进的微芯片。

两名知情人士表示，随着调查的继续，这一决定可能会发生变化，这一决定对于布兰奇周末决定告诉特朗普和副总统万斯来说，他没有证据表明黄对国家安全构成风险至关重要。

黄仁勋的复职激怒了国会议员（包括共和党和民主党），他们表示现在搁置有关英伟达或其首席执行官是否危及美国国家安全的问题还为时过早。在特朗普干预之前，缺乏任何额外的努力来检查他们的角色，这可能会推动国会山进行更多调查。

黄定于下周作证。

两位知情人士表示，司法部对 Nvidia 客户的调查没有发现任何证据表明黄仁勋充当中国代理人或故意将敏感半导体技术或信息转移到中国。他们补充说，英伟达不是这些调查的目标，并且进行了合作，提供了有助于得出这一结论的文件、采访和其他数据。

黄本人也没有受到反情报调查。另两位知情人士称，美国间谍机构已收集了有关 Megaspeed 前高管、黄仁勋情人的爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的信息，她涉嫌与中国情报机构合作。但他们表示，美国没有任何细节可以证明对英伟达首席执行官进行调查。

反情报调查与刑事调查分开进行，旨在监测和消除国家安全威胁，而不是提出起诉。

两位知情人士表示，司法部官员得出的结论是，英伟达和黄仁勋没有犯下任何不当行为，也没有怀疑其首席执行官构成国家安全风险。

根据特朗普周一在 CNBC 采访中对事件的描述，特朗普和万斯向英伟达董事会传达了这一结论，董事会决定恢复黄仁勋的职位。

万斯周三在俄亥俄州接受记者采访时表示，司法部和国家安全官员告诉他，黄在复职前并未受到调查。

“我们被告知他没有受到调查，”他说，并补充说，他认为特朗普不需要赦免黄，因为他没有违法。 “我没有再看到任何证据证明他犯罪了。”

黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞去 Nvidia 首席执行官一职，此前他被指控与 Alice Huang 和至少两名员工有染。黄仁勋承认不忠，但尚未具体证实他与黄爱丽丝的关系。路透社一直无法联系到她或确认她与中国间谍机构的联系。

据《纽约时报》报道，国务卿马可·卢比奥五月份向特朗普通报了此事。

title: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
title_en: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
The US is tightening its grip in the AI race with China, and the push is already having an effect, according to The Information. Chinese AI developers including Deepseek, Moonshot AI, and Alibaba have been under pressure since September, squeezed by restrictions on Chinese firms' remote access to advanced Nvidia chips in foreign data centers and by successful anti-distillation measures from OpenAI and Anthropic.

As a result, many ongoing projects are facing delays, the report says. Last month, Deepseek researchers internally estimated that their gap to top US models could grow from three to six months to nine months if distillation disappears completely. Moonshot AI has already canceled a $150 million deal for Nvidia Blackwell chips in Indonesia.

Chinese firms are now looking for new workarounds, the publication reports. Some are trying to rent computing power through non-Chinese third parties, while companies such as MiniMax, Mihoyo, and Alibaba are leaning more heavily on domestic chips. They are also investing more in training data for their own reinforcement learning.

title_zh: 美芯片禁令与反蒸馏技术重挫中国AI实验室

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国政府针对中国AI开发者实施的算力访问限制及大型模型开发商推行的反蒸馏防御措施，已显著拉大中美顶尖模型研发效率差距。DeepSeek内部评估显示，若蒸馏路径受阻，其与美国顶尖模型的迭代差距可能从3-6个月扩大至9个月，促使部分中国AI实验室转向国内芯片替代或加大强化学习数据投入。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 美方的策略已从单纯的物理制裁（芯片禁运）升级为针对算法迭代机制（反蒸馏）的逻辑阻断。这意味着中国AI产业的‘算力+数据+模型蒸馏’三位一体追赶模式失效，倒逼企业必须从依赖外部模型蒸馏转向基于完全自主训练的‘强化学习’路径，这将显著提高大模型研发的边际成本与人才门槛。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The US strategy has evolved from physical chip embargoes to algorithmic blocking (anti-distillation), neutralizing the primary catch-up mechanism for Chinese labs. This necessitates a strategic pivot from distillation-heavy approaches to resource-intensive autonomous RL training, effectively raising the capital and talent barriers for entry.

article_content_zh:
美国正在加强在与中国的人工智能竞赛中的控制力，而且这种推动已经产生了效果。自 9 月份以来，包括 Deepseek、Moonshot AI 和阿里巴巴在内的中国人工智能开发商一直面临压力，受到中国公司远程访问外国数据中心先进 Nvidia 芯片的限制以及 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 成功的反蒸馏措施的挤压。

报告称，因此，许多正在进行的项目面临延误。上个月，Deepseek 研究人员内部估计，如果蒸馏完全消失，他们与美国顶级模型的差距可能会从三到六个月扩大到九个月。 Moonshot AI 已经取消了在印度尼西亚购买 Nvidia Blackwell 芯片的价值 1.5 亿美元的交易。

据该出版物报道，中国企业现在正在寻找新的解决办法。一些公司试图通过非中国第三方租用计算能力，而MiniMax、Mihoyo和阿里巴巴等公司则更加依赖国产芯片。他们还在自己的强化学习训练数据上投入更多资金。

title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
title_en: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
author: Ivan Mehta
article_content:
WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.

The feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.

Users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.

Notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.

The feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to update their teams.

WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says letting AI govern society would be "a bad idea"
title_en: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says letting AI govern society would be "a bad idea"
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
Dario Amodei said it was "absurd"to suggest he believed people should "surrender human free will"to AI systems.

In a lengthy post on X, he responded to an Axios report that cited people familiar with internal discussions. The outlet reported that some Anthropic employees believed humanity would safely hand authority to superintelligent systems, and often should, rather than fight for control.

AI must be governed by "legitimate democratic processes,"Amodei wrote. Political decisions should stay in human hands, he argued, and he rejected handing power to AI as firmly as he rejected autocracy.

[...] We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination on the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word to governance by AI, and I feel just as strongly that handing over governance to AI is a bad idea. Dario Amodei

Automating specific tasks such as driving, developing cancer drugs, and writing software could benefit humanity, Amodei said, but that was a different matter from giving up free will in politics.

### Amodei says that full automation isn't always worth the risk

End-to-end automation could also bring risks, Amodei wrote, including serious job disruption and AI building new models without human oversight. "It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives,"he wrote. "But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it."In many cases, he added, "humans would simply prefer to do some activities themselves, so they can stay deeply engaged in what matters to them, even if AI can do those activities better."

Amodei said AI companies didn't differ much on automating specific tasks. Some AI CEOs, he wrote, repeated slogans like "human control and agency"and "AI should be just a tool"but still shipped products built for more and more automation.

Anthropic, by contrast, refused to allow its existing models to be used for autonomous weapons during its dispute with the Pentagon. He was "willing to risk Anthropic's future as a company"over that refusal, "even in the face of legal sanctions,"Amodei wrote.

达里奥·阿莫代表示，他认为人们应该向人工智能系统“投降人类自由意志”，这是“荒谬的”。

在 X 上的一篇长文中，他对 Axios 的一份报告做出了回应，该报告援引了熟悉内部讨论的人士的说法。该媒体报道称，一些 Anthropic 员工相信人类会安全地将权力交给超级智能系统，而且通常应该这样做，而不是争夺控制权。

阿莫迪写道，人工智能必须受到“合法的民主程序”的管理。他认为，政治决策应该掌握在人类手中，他拒绝将权力交给人工智能，就像他拒绝独裁一样。

我们决不应该为了效率或安全而牺牲合法性或自决权。这种反对专制的论点逐字逐句地适用于人工智能的治理，我同样强烈地认为将治理移交给人工智能是一个坏主意。达里奥·阿莫代

阿莫代说，自动化驾驶、开发抗癌药物和编写软件等特定任务可以造福人类，但这与放弃政治自由意志是两回事。

### Amodei 表示完全自动化并不总是值得冒险

阿莫代写道，端到端自动化也可能带来风险，包括严重的工作中断和人工智能在没有人类监督的情况下构建新模型。 “这在许多情况下显然是可取的，并且可以挽救很多生命，”他写道。 “但它也有缺点，在某些领域可能不值得。”他补充道，在很多情况下，“人类只是更喜欢自己做一些活动，这样他们就可以深入参与对他们来说重要的事情，即使人工智能可以更好地完成这些活动。”

阿莫代表示，人工智能公司在自动化特定任务方面没有太大区别。他写道，一些人工智能首席执行官重复了“人类控制和代理”和“人工智能应该只是一种工具”等口号，但仍然推出了为越来越多的自动化而构建的产品。

相比之下，Anthropic 在与五角大楼的争端中拒绝允许其现有模型用于自主武器。阿莫代写道，他“愿意拿 Anthropic 公司的未来冒险”，因为他的拒绝，“即使面临法律制裁”。

title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe
title_en: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe
author: Zack Whittaker
article_content:
Password manager maker 1Password has confirmed that some customer information was taken in a recent intrusion into its internal systems, but that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed.

The Toronto-based tech company said in a blog post published Wednesday that it detected an intrusion on November 19, in which an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate account with GitHub, which the company uses to share and store its source code.

The attacker used that employee’s access to push malicious code to the company’s internal servers, which allowed the hacker to download some data about 1Password customers, including their names and the email address that they use for logging into their account. The company said that the attacker also took details about when a 1Password account was created and when a user last logged in.

1Password said that customer vaults, which store their passwords, were “at no point” available to the attacker. The company also said that it doesn’t have access to customer account passwords or their secret keys, which are used to scramble their passwords so that 1Password cannot see them.

In addition, the company said that its apps and extensions are unaffected by the incident.

It’s unclear how the attacker gained access to the employee’s corporate account, and a spokesperson for 1Password did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s questions about the incident.

1Password did not say whether it had notified customers whose information was taken in the breach, or how many customers had information taken. We’ve also asked if the company has received any communication or demands from the hackers. We’ll update if we hear back from 1Password.

The company touts millions of customers and more than 200,000 businesses who use its password manager products to store their passwords, credentials, payment card information, and more. Security experts have long recommended password managers as a better way of generating stronger credentials and keeping track of online accounts.

这家总部位于多伦多的科技公司在周三发布的一篇博客文章中表示，它在 11 月 19 日检测到一次入侵，攻击者获得了一名员工在 GitHub 上的公司帐户的访问权限，该公司使用该帐户共享和存储其源代码。

攻击者利用该员工的访问权限将恶意代码推送到公司的内部服务器，这使得黑客能够下载有关 1Password 客户的一些数据，包括他们的姓名和用于登录帐户的电子邮件地址。该公司表示，攻击者还获取了有关 1Password 帐户创建时间以及用户上次登录时间的详细信息。

1Password 表示，攻击者“在任何时候”都无法使用存储密码的客户保险库。该公司还表示，它无法访问客户帐户密码或其密钥，这些密钥用于扰乱他们的密码，以便 1Password 无法看到它们。

此外，该公司表示其应用程序和扩展程序未受到该事件的影响。

目前尚不清楚攻击者如何访问该员工的公司帐户，1Password 的发言人没有立即回应 TechCrunch 关于该事件的问题。

title: Dario Amodei rejects the idea of surrendering free will to AI and accuses rival AI execs of "vibes-based" positioning, rebutting a report on AI leaders' views (Madison Mills/Axios)
title_en: Dario Amodei rejects the idea of surrendering free will to AI and accuses rival AI execs of "vibes-based" positioning, rebutting a report on AI leaders' views (Madison Mills/Axios)

inline_images.caption: Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: Jason Henry/Bloomberg via Getty Images
inline_images.alt: Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: Jason Henry/Bloomberg via Getty Images

author: Axios
article_content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Wednesday rejected the notion that humans should surrender free will to AI, pushing back on Axios' reporting about a growing ideological divide among top AI executives.

Why it matters: This is Amodei's most significant public remarks since the company went public last week.

What he's saying: "We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security," Amodei said.

The debate about control comes amid a rocky debut for Anthropic's stock, which dipped below its IPO day price on Wednesday.

Zoom out: Amodei's essay is a response to an Axios story published Wednesday morning that detailed a commonly held view inside Anthropic: AI will one day be so capable and powerful, that humanity should surrender some decision-making power to superintelligent AI systems, according to multiple sources.

Inside Anthropic, people inside the company believe superintelligent AI will arrive soon. There is widespread concern among employees at Anthropic and OpenAI that internal models are advancing so rapidly that it may not be safe to release them or to continue training more capable systems, Axios has reported.

The intrigue: Amodei also took aim at rival AI executives, accusing them of engaging in "vibes-based commercial and political positioning" by championing human agency without meaningfully differentiating their products.

title: ElevenLabs in Early Talks for 2027 Funding at $33 Billion Value
title_en: ElevenLabs in Early Talks for 2027 Funding at $33 Billion Value
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
ElevenLabs is in early talks for a funding round at a $33B valuation, planned for the first quarter of 2027, Bloomberg reported. That would be 50% above its $22B valuation in September, and its annual recurring revenue has reached $700M, one person said.

ElevenLabs is in early talks to raise money at a $33B valuation, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The voice AI company plans to start the round in the first quarter of 2027, though some investors want it to begin sooner.

That would be a 50% jump from the $22B ElevenLabs was valued at in a $300M share sale in September. It also fits the company’s habit of setting valuations in multiples of 11, a nod to its name.

ElevenLabs’ annual recurring revenue has reached $700M, one person told Bloomberg, up from the $600M it reported in September. ElevenLabs declined to comment.

The price would be steep next to its peers. London video AI firm Synthesia was valued at $4B in January with about $140M in yearly revenue. Mistral was valued at €21B in September, having passed $400M early in the year.

Investors may be spurred on by Anthropic’s record $107.3B IPO, which brought early backers huge gains.

ElevenLabs was founded in London in 2022 by Mati Staniszewski and Piotr Dabkowski, and makes realistic AI voices for games, audiobooks and AI agents. Staniszewski has said it could start preparing for an IPO in 2028.

article_content_zh:
ElevenLabs 是一家语音人工智能公司，将配音不佳的投诉变成了欧洲增长最快的软件公司之一，目前正在与投资者就二次股票出售进行早期谈判，该公司的估值将达到约 220 亿美元，几乎是五个月前 D 轮融资中 110 亿美元的两倍。

该交易是一项要约收购——一种允许员工向外部投资者出售现有股票的机制，而公司无需筹集新资本、发行新股票或发布主要融资轮所需的财务披露。这种区别正是价值 220 亿美元的标题所掩盖的。The Next Web 于 7 月 3 日首次报道了早期会谈的细节，引用了彭博社 7 月 2 日的原始报道，ElevenLabs 拒绝发表评论。

据描述，这些讨论是初步的；条款仍可能发生变化。招标预计于九月结束。已经很清楚的模式是：ElevenLabs 现在在不到两年的时间内将自己重新定价了三次，每次都比上一次更快，而且每次的机制都在不向资产负债表上注入新资本的情况下奖励了现有股东。十八个月内估值翻了四倍这一轨迹值得精确绘制。

ElevenLabs 于 2024 年初估值达到 11 亿美元。其 2025 年 1 月的 C 轮融资将价格定为 33 亿美元。 2025 年 9 月的员工收购要约将股票定价为 66 亿美元。

2026 年 2 月的 D 轮融资由红杉资本领投，并得到贝莱德、英伟达、a16z 和 Iconiq Growth 的支持，所有这些公司都在该轮融资中大幅增持了股份，使该公司估值达到 110 亿美元。如果目前的谈判维持在 220 亿美元的水平，那么该公司将在两年内实现约 20 倍的增长。收入故事提供了一些支持。

截至 2025 年，ElevenLabs 的年度经常性收入约为 3.3 亿美元，到 2026 年 5 月将超过 5 亿美元。企业客户包括思科、德国电信、Revolut、Meta、Salesforce 和华盛顿邮报，而包括 Paradox Interactive 在内的游戏开发商和包括波士顿咨询集团在内的咨询公司的客户群有望在 2027 年占企业收入的 70%。估值为 220 亿美元，而 5 亿美元为在年度经常性收入中，投资者支付的费用约为经常性收入的 44 倍。

按照传统软件标准来看，这个倍数是非常陡峭的。他们实际上定价的问题包括两个部分：ElevenLabs 是否已经巩固了自己作为人工智能语音默认基础设施层的地位，以及该地位所承受的法律和竞争压力是否已经被定价。 什么是要约收购——以及 220 亿美元的数字没有告诉你什么私人公司要约收购是一种公司控制的流动性事件，邀请员工和早期投资者在设定的窗口内以固定价格将部分或全部既得股份出售给指定买家。

这不是主要融资轮。没有新的现金进入公司金库。没有发行新股。

公司设定价格，选择合格的卖家，并决定可以转手的库存量。与公开市场交易不同，它没有义务发布经审计的财务数据、更新上一轮主要融资的收入数据或披露买方投资者是谁。彭博社的报道没有透露任何将在本次招标中购买员工股票的买家，没有指定任何超出已披露数据的收入数据，并指出这些条款是初步的。

从狭义上讲，一张价值 220 亿美元但没有这些细节的邮票是一个或多个熟悉一组私人谈判的匿名人士告诉记者的数字。这就是私募市场估值的运作方式。这也是为什么如果交易完成，买家的身份将与价格一样重要的原因。 语音克隆实际上是如何运作的——以及为什么三秒就足够了 ElevenLabs 估值的业务案例依赖于特定的技术能力：能够以任何语音、70 多种语言、以延迟水平生成高度逼真的合成语音，从而使实时对话成为可能。

底层架构在概念上并不新鲜，但在效率方面有了显着提高。现代语音克隆通过三阶段管道进行操作。说话人编码器（一种经过数千种声音训练的神经网络）从简短的参考音频剪辑中提取紧凑的数字表示，称为说话人嵌入。

ElevenLabs 的 Eleven v3 模型于 2026 年 2 月全面发布，可以从短短几秒的音频中生成可用的说话者嵌入，因为编码器已经学会识别声学特征（音调、音调分布、共振峰结构、节奏模式），从而区分一种声音和另一种声音。

然后，该嵌入被传递到自回归转换器，该转换器生成以文本输入和说话者的声学签名为条件的语音标记。声码器将这些标记转换为波形。这条管道的实际结果是 ElevenLabs 的国会批评者最常引用的发现：根据 Axios 引用的研究，安全研究人员和网络安全公司已经证实，三秒的参考音频（语音邮件、播客剪辑、社交媒体视频）足以生成几乎任何声音的令人信服的克隆。

ElevenLabs 的 Flash v2.5 模型的端到端延迟约为 75 毫秒，低于听众可靠感知处理延迟的阈值，使得电话呼叫中的实时模拟在技术上以低成本实现可行。使该技术具有商业价值的效率与使其成为欺诈媒介的效率相同。产品案例：从配音工具到 Audible ChallengerElevenLabs 于 2022 年由首席执行官 Mati Staniszewski 和首席技术官创立彼得·达布科夫斯基（Piotr Dąbkowski）是两个在华沙长大的儿时好友，他们注意到波兰消费的外国内容依赖于一个单调的叙述者。

title: Backblaze explains why it’s sharing customer information with advertisers
title_en: Backblaze explains why it’s sharing customer information with advertisers
author: Scharon Harding
article_content:
Some customers have raised concerns about Backblaze’s privacy policy taking effect next month, which says the backup and cloud storage company may sell certain personal information to advertisers.

Backblaze’s current privacy policy says that in addition to the personal information that users may provide, such as their email address when creating an account, it may also “automatically” collect information, such as “your software, the operating system you use when accessing our service, your Internet Protocol address, and the date and time of each request you make to Backblaze.”

The current policy adds: “Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.” It also makes no mention of advertisers.

On December 1, a new privacy policy takes effect. It includes a table listing the types of “general personal information” that Backblaze says it has been collecting and sharing with third parties, including “advertising and marketing partners” since December 1, 2025, This information includes identifiers (such as “name, address, Internet Protocol address, [and] email address”); commercial information (such as “records of personal property, products or services purchased, obtained, or considered, or other purchasing or consuming histories or tendencies”; geolocation data that “can be used to determine a device’s physical location”; and “sensory or surveillance data” (which includes “call recordings or other audio, electronic, or visual monitoring or surveillance”).

This has concerned some users, but a Backblaze spokesperson told Ars Technica that “Backblaze does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data, such as call recordings, for targeted advertising, and we do not disclose it to advertising or marketing partners.” They added:

The Privacy Policy table lists one set of recipients across all data categories, which is why it can read differently. Our legal team will review the table for clarity as part of our next review cycle.

### No “sensitive personal information” shared

Notably, no “sensitive personal information,” such as social security numbers, credit card numbers, or “precise geolocation,” is shared with advertisers, the policy states. However, identifiers, commercial information, “Internet or Other Similar Network Activity,” and “geolocation data” may be “sold or shared for targeted Advertising”

Critically, the upcoming policy “only applies to the information collected in respect of your account and not to the content that you store on our system.” Backblaze’s broader terms of service also state that: “Files stored using Backblaze Computer Backup are encrypted prior to being sent to us.”

However, some customers remain concerned that the privacy policy doesn’t more clearly and distinctly explain that Backblaze won’t share or sell content from customers’ backup files. In response, Backblaze’s representative explained:

This is because the Privacy Notice’s sale and sharing disclosures relate to website and marketing data, such as information collected through cookies and similar technologies on our site. They do not apply to files customers store with us.

Renatta Siewert, Backblaze’s director of communications and brand programs, reiterated to Ars that Backblaze doesn’t share the contents of backup or storage files with advertisers:

Backblaze takes the privacy and security of our customers’ data seriously. We updated our Privacy Notice to keep pace with the changing legal landscape, which increasingly requires companies to spell out how they collect and use marketing-related information. This update gives customers a clearer, more specific view of what we collect and why. These disclosures are separate from the files customers entrust to Backblaze for backup and storage, which we do not sell or share with advertisers, data brokers, or analytics partners.

Customers can use this link to opt out of the selling or sharing of their personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising.

article_content_zh:
一些客户对下个月生效的 Backblaze 隐私政策表示担忧，该政策称备份和云存储公司可能会向广告商出售某些个人信息。

Backblaze 目前的隐私政策规定，除了用户可能提供的个人信息（例如创建帐户时的电子邮件地址）之外，它还可能“自动”收集信息，例如“您的软件、您访问我们的服务时使用的操作系统、您的互联网协议地址以及您向 Backblaze 提出的每个请求的日期和时间”。

目前的政策补充道：“在任何情况下，未经您的同意，我们都不会出于营销目的与任何其他公司出租、交易或共享您的地址或电子邮件地址。”它还没有提及广告商。

12 月 1 日，新的隐私政策生效。其中包括一个表格，列出了 Backblaze 表示自 2025 年 12 月 1 日以来一直在收集并与第三方（包括“广告和营销合作伙伴”）共享的“一般个人信息”类型，这些信息包括标识符（例如“姓名、地址、互联网协议地址、[和]电子邮件地址”）；商业信息（例如“购买、获得或考虑的个人财产、产品或服务的记录，或其他购买或消费历史或倾向”；“可用于确定设备物理位置”的地理位置数据；以及“感知或监视数据”（包括“通话录音或其他音频、电子或视觉监控或监视”）。

这引起了一些用户的担忧，但 Backblaze 发言人告诉 Ars Technica，“Backblaze 不会出售或共享用于定向广告的传感或监控数据，例如通话录音，我们也不会向广告或营销合作伙伴透露这些数据。”他们补充道：

隐私策略表列出了所有数据类别的一组收件人，这就是它可以以不同方式读取的原因。作为我们下一个审核周期的一部分，我们的法律团队将审核该表以确保其清晰度。

### 不共享“敏感个人信息”

值得注意的是，该政策规定，不会与广告商共享“敏感的个人信息”，例如社会安全号码、信用卡号码或“精确的地理位置”。但是，标识符、商业信息、“互联网或其他类似网络活动”和“地理位置数据”可能会“出于定向广告目的而出售或共享”

重要的是，即将出台的政策“仅适用于收集的有关您帐户的信息，不适用于您存储在我们系统上的内容。” Backblaze 更广泛的服务条款还规定：“使用 Backblaze Computer Backup 存储的文件在发送给我们之前已进行加密。”

然而，一些客户仍然担心隐私政策没有更清晰地解释 Backblaze 不会共享或出售客户备份文件中的内容。对此，Backblaze 的代表解释道：

这是因为隐私声明的销售和共享披露涉及网站和营销数据，例如通过我们网站上的 cookie 和类似技术收集的信息。它们不适用于客户存储在我们这里的文件。

Backblaze 的传播和品牌项目总监 Renatta Siewert 向 Ars 重申，Backblaze 不会与广告商共享备份或存储文件的内容：

Backblaze 非常重视客户数据的隐私和安全。我们更新了隐私声明，以跟上不断变化的法律环境，这越来越要求公司阐明如何收集和使用营销相关信息。此次更新让客户能够更清晰、更具体地了解我们收集的内容及其原因。这些披露与客户委托给 Backblaze 进行备份和存储的文件是分开的，我们不会向广告商、数据经纪人或分析合作伙伴出售或共享这些文件。

客户可以使用此链接选择不出售或共享其个人信息以用于跨上下文行为广告。

title: Nvidia sellers seek new buyers as U.S. curbs China AI chip access, sources tell CNBC
title_en: Nvidia sellers seek new buyers as U.S. curbs China AI chip access, sources tell CNBC
author: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
article_content:
Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems.

Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.

Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two people familiar with the matter told CNBC the surge in GPUs for sale was directly attributable to the new rule. Duhamel added that one company looking to sell Nvidia chips told GPU Mart the sale was related to the new rule.

The two people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload them because they were originally for use in data centers in which Chinese companies would rent access. They asked not to be named because they were discussing private information.

The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced an interim final rule as part of a clampdown on Chinese companies bypassing export controls, which effectively ban the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China, by accessing them remotely in overseas data centers. The rule came into effect on Nov. 19.

Deals to find buyers for thousands of B300 GPUs, one of Nvidia's most advanced offerings, have been floated since the rule was announced, said Duhamel and one of the people.

Nvidia declined to comment. BIS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

### Scrutiny over Chinese access to Nvidia chips

Nvidia has been facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips.

The chip giant warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action,"sources previously told CNBC.

In July, the U.S. accused a Chinese AI lab, Moonshot AI, of accessing Nvidia chips via a facility in Thailand. CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that the company had sought access to the chips via data centers in Europe.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box"on Wednesday that the new rule announced last week was intended to close "loopholes."

"For a long time, we have not allowed the sale of Blackwell chips, which are the highest AI chips or similar chips to China directly,"he said.

"Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries."

During Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, then-interim CEO Colette Kress said the company was still studying the controls, but expected performance to remain strong because demand for chips far exceeded supply.

Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.

Jack Duhamel

三名知情人士告诉 CNBC，在特朗普政府收紧规则以限制中国公司远程访问最先进的人工智能系统后，英伟达芯片销售商正在为这家半导体巨头的硬件寻找新买家。

知情人士称，自 11 月 16 日宣布限制中国公司租用先进 Nvidia 芯片的新措施以来，各公司已在市场上投放了异常大量的 Nvidia 图形处理单元 (GPU)。

人工智能基础设施市场 GPU Mart 总裁 Jack Duhamel 和两位知情人士告诉 CNBC，GPU 销售量的激增直接归因于新规则。 Duhamel 补充说，一家希望销售 Nvidia 芯片的公司告诉 GPU Mart，这次销售与新规则有关。

两人表示，芯片销售商似乎正在寻求出售它们，因为它们最初用于中国公司租用访问权的数据中心。他们要求不透露姓名，因为他们正在讨论私人信息。

美国商务部工业与安全局 (BIS) 宣布了一项临时最终规则，作为打击绕过出口管制的中国公司的一部分，出口管制实际上禁止通过在海外数据中心远程访问最先进的 Nvidia 芯片来向中国出售这些芯片。该规定于11月19日生效。

杜哈梅尔和其中一位知情人士表示，自该规则宣布以来，为数千块 B300 GPU（Nvidia 最先进的产品之一）寻找买家的交易一直在进行中。

英伟达拒绝置评。国际清算银行没有立即回应置评请求。

### 对中国获取 Nvidia 芯片的审查

英伟达一直面临着美国立法者对中国公司使用其先进芯片的越来越严格的审查。

消息人士此前告诉 CNBC，这家芯片巨头警告其客户，拟议的《远程访问安全法案》（已在众议院获得通过，但尚未在参议院获得通过）将赋予美国政府更广泛的权力来控制对云服务的访问，这可能会让双方面临“法律诉讼”。

7 月，美国指责中国人工智能实验室 Moonshot AI 通过泰国的一家设施访问 Nvidia 芯片。 CNBC 11 月 5 日报道称，该公司已寻求通过欧洲的数据中心获取这些芯片。

美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔周三对 CNBC 的“Squawk Box”表示，上周宣布的新规则旨在堵住“漏洞”。

“长期以来，我们不允许直接向中国出售Blackwell芯片，这是最高的AI芯片或类似芯片，”他说。

“商务部上周发布了一些规则，以关闭间接访问，无论是通过东南亚等地走私，还是从第三国数据中心进行远程访问。”

title: OpenAI wants companies to trust it with sensitive work by promising not to look at their data
title_en: OpenAI wants companies to trust it with sensitive work by promising not to look at their data
author: Jonathan Kemper
article_content:
OpenAI is testing a new feature called "Private Inference"that lets companies run queries on its most powerful models without OpenAI being able to access the data. CEO Sam Altman said the company is now piloting the previously announced offering with its first enterprise customers. Better privacy makes AI useful for a much wider range of work, Altman wrote.

Shekar, the OpenAI employee leading the effort, called it a first step toward "private intelligence for everyone."OpenAI is currently scaling up the compute capacity needed to expand the offering. For now, Private Inference targets business customers, whose data OpenAI already doesn't use for training. Consumer ChatGPT conversations, by contrast, are used for training by default unless users opt out.

With Private Inference, queries are processed on specially isolated hardware whose security can be independently verified, according to OpenAI. Altman also pointed to Private Safety Processing, a system that lets OpenAI scan for abuse without storing customer data. Flagged content is encrypted and stored in the customer's own cloud, and only a secured review system can read it. Google is pursuing a similar approach with Private AI Compute.

title: Every raises $17.5 million at $110 million valuation, betting venture-backed media can work
title_en: Every raises $17.5 million at $110 million valuation, betting venture-backed media can work
author: Allie Garfinkle
article_content:
Ask Dan Shipper how often venture-backed media startups succeed, and he’s candid.

“My feeling about the history of media companies taking venture capital is that it doesn’t go very well,” he said. In other words, it usually doesn’t work out, I suggest. “It works out never, actually,” laughs Shipper, founder of AI-focused media and software company Every.

Shipper’s right: VC-backed media startups of yesteryear have frequently tanked in spectacular fashion, from The Messenger and Vice to Ozy Media and Quibi. But Shipper is betting that Every—currently with about 130,000 unpaid subscribers and almost 10,000 paid—can play by its own rules and ultimately win its own game.

Hence, the fundraise: Every recently raised $17.5 million in Series A funding, at a $110 million post-money valuation, Fortune has exclusively learned. IA Ventures’s Jesse Beyroutey led the round, with Betaworks and The Atlantic CEO Nicholas Thompson joining, among others. Shipper, 35, will retain full control of the company, and is changing his title to “Philosopher King,” which I rib him about. He good-naturedly says the change is semiotic.

“The really important thing about taking the money for me was that we’d do it in a way that allows us to achieve our goals… and do it in a way that doesn’t require us to sacrifice our soul or the things about the company that I love deeply,” said Shipper. “I think of changing my title as a symbolic thing. If this was a normal venture capital deal, that would be completely off the table and ridiculous.”

And this isn’t a normal venture deal, in a couple of ways. First, Every is a media company. With its neoclassical pop art aesthetic, Every has a multi-pronged business model: Its writing serves a professional audience seeking to become “AI-native,” while the 35-person company also provides consulting services to large companies and produces conferences (I recently interviewed Shipper at Every’s Thesis: 2027 conference in Brooklyn). Second, Shipper didn’t raise in a standard startup process: IA’s Beyroutey and Shipper are close friends (they went to college together) and Shipper went straight to Beyroutey.

“I didn’t shop the deal,” said Shipper. “I went to someone I deeply trust, who understands the business deeply, who understands exactly what I want to do with it, and has put me in the position where I make all the decisions to build the company in the way that I want to build it,” Shipper said. “I think that’s the only way to build a business like this, because this is a very unique shape. It’s a media company and a technology company, kind of smushed together.”

Shipper started Every in 2020, about six years after exiting his first startup, co-browsing company Firefly, in 2014 (the acquisition came right as he was graduating college). He spent the intervening years finding the right next thing. Every became the answer, in part because it addressed a number of questions that Shipper had been asking throughout his life. For one, he’d long felt tension between writing and entrepreneurship (at Every he could be both). He’d also been interested in tech since he was a kid.

“I thought a lot about why Microsoft and Windows had worked, and one of the big reasons is that they came during a hardware platform shift, from mainframes to PCs,” said Shipper. “They started building operating systems for that, and that’s always a really big opportunity…. And I thought: I wonder what my platform shift is going to be?”

Shipper and Every are all-in on AI, and the company is built to help people understand how they can actually use AI, in their jobs and their lives.

“I think too few companies are trying to do that,” said Shipper. “Too many companies are trying to build the machine god or are worrying about Armageddon, and I’m not…. I would expect improvements we’re seeing [in AI] to continue, and I would expect there to be a gap between the improvements that you see on the charts and how well those improvements translate into actually better work by people (and that people at companies are proud of). Our job is to fill that gap.”

Shipper is optimistic that AI won’t replace humans at work, a common fear and feature of AI discourse.

“The narrative is ‘it’s so over for humans’, and I think that’s exactly wrong,” he said. “That relies on this sleight of hand where you forget that humans are the ones who make these things, and humans are the ones that prompt these things—and decide what’s valuable and what’s not.”

In some sense, Shipper expects AI to eventually blur into the background, much in the same way we don’t really say “I used the Internet.”

“Ultimately, I think the technology and the model advances will disappear, and we’ll actually just think about the humans that did it,” said Shipper. “Asking if Claude did it will be like asking if you used your laptop. ‘Did your laptop do it?’ No, you did it.”

Happy Thanksgiving and we’ll see you again on Monday.

article_content_zh:
如果你问丹·希珀（Dan Shipper），风险投资支持的媒体初创公司成功的几率有多少，他很坦率。

“我对媒体公司接受风险投资的历史的感觉是，进展并不顺利，”他说。换句话说，我建议，它通常不会成功。 “实际上，这永远不会成功，”专注于人工智能的媒体和软件公司 Every 的创始人 Shipper 笑着说。

Shipper 的观点是正确的：从 The Messenger 和 Vice 到 Ozy Media 和 Quibi，过去由风险投资支持的媒体初创公司经常以惊人的方式陷入困境。但 Shipper 押注，Every——目前拥有约 130,000 名未付费订阅者和近 10,000 名付费订阅者——可以按照自己的规则进行游戏，并最终赢得自己的游戏。

据《财富》杂志独家获悉，最近的 A 轮融资均筹集了 1750 万美元，投后估值为 1.1 亿美元。 IA Ventures 的 Jesse Beyroutey 领投此轮融资，Betaworks 和 The Atlantic 首席执行官 Nicholas Thompson 等也跟投。 35 岁的希珀将保留对公司的完全控制权，并将他的头衔改为“哲学家王”，我对此开玩笑。他善意地说这种变化是符号学上的。

“对我来说，拿这笔钱真正重要的是，我们会以一种能够实现我们目标的方式来做这件事……并且以一种不需要我们牺牲我们的灵魂或我深爱的公司的东西的方式来做这件事，”托普说。 “我认为改变我的头衔是一件具有象征意义的事情。如果这是一笔正常的风险投资交易，那将是完全不可能的，而且很荒谬。”

从几个方面来看，这不是一笔正常的风险交易。首先，Every 是一家媒体公司。凭借新古典主义的波普艺术美学，Every 拥有多管齐下的商业模式：其作品为寻求成为“AI 原生”的专业受众提供服务，而这家拥有 35 名员工的公司还为大公司提供咨询服务并举办会议（我最近在布鲁克林举行的 Every’s Thesis: 2027 会议上采访了 Shipper）。其次，Shipper 并没有按照标准的启动流程进行融资：IA 的 Beyroutey 和 Shipper 是亲密的朋友（他们一起上大学），Shipper 直接去了 Beyroutey。

“我没有接受这笔交易，”希珀说。 “我找到了一个我深深信任的人，他深入了解公司业务，准确理解我想用它做什么，并让我做出所有决定，以我想要的方式建立公司，”托普说。 “我认为这是建立这样一家企业的唯一方法，因为这是一个非常独特的形状。它是一家媒体公司和一家科技公司，有点混在一起。”

Shipper 于 2020 年创立 Every，距 2014 年退出他的第一家初创公司、共同浏览的公司 Firefly 大约六年（这次收购是在他大学毕业时进行的）。在接下来的几年里，他一直在寻找合适的下一个目标。每个都成为了答案，部分原因是它解决了托普一生中一直在问的许多问题。其一，他长期以来一直感受到写作和创业之间的紧张关系（在Every，他可以两者兼而有之）。他从小就对科技感兴趣。

“我思考了很多关于微软和 Windows 为何能够奏效的问题，其中一个重要原因是它们出现在硬件平台从大型机向 PC 转变的时期，”Shipper 说道。 “他们开始为此构建操作系统，这始终是一个非常大的机会……我想：我想知道我的平台转变将会是什么？”

Shipper 和 Every 都全力投入人工智能，该公司的成立是为了帮助人们了解如何在工作和生活中实际使用人工智能。

“我认为尝试这样做的公司太少了，”托普说。 “太多的公司正在试图打造机器之神，或者担心世界末日，而我不是……我希望我们在人工智能领域看到的改进能够继续下去，而且我希望你在图表上看到的改进与这些改进转化为人们实际更好的工作（公司的人们为此感到自豪）之间存在差距。我们的工作就是填补这一差距。”

托普乐观地认为人工智能不会在工作中取代人类，这是人工智能话语的常见恐惧和特征。

“这种说法是‘人类已经结束了’，我认为这是完全错误的，”他说。 “这依赖于这种技巧，你会忘记人类是制造这些东西的人，也是人类推动这些东西的人，并决定什么是有价值的，什么是无价值的。”

从某种意义上说，托普预计人工智能最终会消失在背景中，就像我们不会真正说“我使用了互联网”一样。

title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
title_en: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company’s “Starmind” initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full “constellation” of AI satellites.

The FCC’s approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX’s request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in space “graveyard” orbits, rather than having them burn up in the Earth’s atmosphere, saying the company hasn’t provided “sufficient information” about its disposal process plans.

SpaceX has described its Starmind project as a way to “capture solar energy in space to power” AI capabilities on Earth. The company says Starmind will transmit data to Earth using high-speed lasers that connect to Starlink. It plans to produce chips for its satellites at an upcoming Terafab facility.

Google has already taken its first steps toward putting compute into space, with the launch of a “Project Suncatcher” AI server satellite last month. Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin will carry out the first dedicated heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher in 2029.

title: FCC Authorizes 1M Satellites for Data Centers in Space
title_en: FCC Authorizes 1M Satellites for Data Centers in Space

author: Reuters
article_content:
The FCC on Wednesday granted the first authorization ever for a constellation of data centers in space — a win for Elon Musk and his SpaceX operation that comes less than two years after his role as the head of the Department of Government Efficiency under President Trump.

The authorization sees the Commission approve SpaceX’s deployment of 1 million orbital compute modules “to process massive amounts of data to be used back here on Earth.”

And, the Carr Commission proclaims, “it promises to bring the human race closer to a Kardashev II civilization—one that can harness the full power of the sun.”

The system also operates consistent with the FCC’s orbital debris rules.

In a statement, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said, “This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth. Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI. By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centers are meeting the moment. This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home.”

With data centers a divisive topic across the U.S. in a wide range of communities, including Nashville, where a proposed center adjacent to the city’s zoo generated a vociferous round of protests in June, the idea of putting them in space could supercharge a company already seen by Wall Street as a potential disruptor to the cellular telephone industry. Already, T-Mobile has seen its stock price fall by $50 a share from earlier this year thanks to SpaceX efforts. On November 25, Microsoft shares were down to the low $480s after recently climbing above $500 per share.

article_content_zh:
周三，美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 首次授予了太空数据中心群的授权，这是埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和他的 SpaceX 业务的胜利，距离他担任特朗普总统领导下的政府效率部负责人不到两年。

该授权表明，委员会批准 SpaceX 部署 100 万个轨道计算模块，“以处理大量数据，以便在地球上使用”。

而且，卡尔委员会宣称，“它承诺让人类更接近卡尔达肖夫二世文明——一个可以充分利用太阳力量的文明。”

该系统的运行还符合美国联邦通信委员会的轨道碎片规则。

FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔在一份声明中表示：“这一行动为推动美国领导力和增长所需的计算基础设施开辟了一个大胆的新领域。计算园区或数据中心对于维持美国在 SI 领域的领导地位至关重要。通过将计算能力转移到地球之外，SpaceX 和许多致力于自己轨道数据中心的竞争对手正在迎接这一时刻。这就是美国的独创性，可以结合我们在太空和先进技术方面的优势，加强我们的经济领导地位，并扩大国内的繁荣。”

由于数据中心在美国许多社区都存在争议，其中包括纳什维尔，该市动物园附近拟建的数据中心于 6 月份引发了一轮激烈的抗议，因此将数据中心放入太空的想法可能会增强这家已经被华尔街视为移动电话行业潜在颠覆者的公司的实力。由于 SpaceX 的努力，T-Mobile 的股价已较今年早些时候每股下跌 50 美元。 11 月 25 日，微软股价在近期攀升至每股 500 美元以上后，跌至 480 美元低点。
