article_content_zh:
华盛顿多年来一直阻止先进的人工智能芯片实际到达中国。事实证明，芯片根本不需要移动。

周一，美国商务部发布了一项针对使用位于中国境外数据中心的高端人工智能硬件的中国公司的规定。这一举措对东南亚影响最大，该地区一直在快速建设服务器集群。

该规则来自商务部工业与安全局（BIS）。这是一项临时最终规则，生效日期约为 2026 年 11 月 16 日。

其核心目标是远程访问。中国公司无需拥有 Nvidia 或 AMD 芯片即可使用该芯片。它可以简单地从国外的设施租用计算并通过互联网运行其工作负载。

该规则还直接到达数据中心。任何向中国实体提供大量计算的设施都需要获得许可证，并且一旦超过总 TPP 超过 1200 万的门槛，就必须进行强化的尽职调查。

该规则生效后，运营商将获得 90 天的合规期限。那些错过的人可能会面临未来的限制。

有一个值得注意的例外情况。总部位于美国的运营商可以免除某些许可要求，但必须每月提交合规报告。

该规定主要是针对英伟达和数据中心运营商 Megaspeed 丑闻的回应。 2023 年至 2025 年间，Megaspeed 在 Nvidia 服务器上花费了至少 46 亿美元。

争议的焦点是芯片被转移以及包括阿里巴巴在内的主要中国客户获得远程计算访问权的指控。这些只是指控，而不是调查结果，但足以促使监管机构采取行动。

市场反应迅速。消息公布后，与数据中心相关的东南亚公司股价下跌，部分跌幅高达 20%。

这个时机引发了一些尴尬的比较。 2026年初，近90万个先进人工智能芯片已获准出口给中国公司，其中包括一些与军方有联系的公司。

因此，清理了大量芯片用于直接销售的同一政府现在正在收紧对国外租赁接入的限制。

title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
title_en: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
author: Manuel Uth
article_content:
MIT researchers have developed a method that makes training AI climate models faster, cheaper, and more reliable. According to MIT News, these emulators now need only a fraction of the data typically required.

Normally, researchers rely on massive, physics-based climate simulations that take months to run a single scenario on supercomputers. Fast AI models for climate prediction can mimic these in seconds and help plan power grids, public health measures, and agriculture. But training them previously required six to eight runs of those large simulations using evenly distributed, realistic future scenarios. That took so long the finished models were usually outdated, according to co-author Noelle Selin. They also often failed on unfamiliar situations.

An algorithm built by a team from MIT, ETH Zurich, and Imperial College London uses synthetic training data with extreme swings instead, like a sudden CO2 spike in 2050 or dropping methane in 2037. These targeted spikes help the AI understand the climate system far more precisely, according to lead author Christopher Womack. A single simulation run is enough for training, according to the team, and the AI reliably calculates the effects of local environmental policies too.

article_content_zh:
麻省理工学院的研究人员开发了一种方法，可以使人工智能气候模型的训练更快、更便宜、更可靠。据麻省理工学院新闻报道，这些模拟器现在只需要通常所需数据的一小部分。

通常，研究人员依赖于基于物理的大规模气候模拟，在超级计算机上运行单个场景需要数月时间。用于气候预测的快速人工智能模型可以在几秒钟内模仿这些模型，并帮助规划电网、公共卫生措施和农业。但以前训练它们需要使用均匀分布的真实未来场景运行六到八次大型模拟。合著者诺埃尔·塞林 (Noelle Selin) 表示，由于花费了很长时间，最终的模型通常已经过时。他们也经常在不熟悉的情况下失败。

由麻省理工学院、苏黎世联邦理工学院和伦敦帝国理工学院的团队构建的算法使用具有极端波动的合成训练数据，例如 2050 年二氧化碳浓度突然飙升或 2037 年甲烷浓度下降。主要作者 Christopher Womack 表示，这些有针对性的峰值有助于人工智能更准确地了解气候系统。该团队表示，一次模拟运行就足以进行训练，并且人工智能还可以可靠地计算当地环境政策的影响。

title: Exclusive: Meta and Amazon discuss ending Muse shopping bot blockade, as ads, search emerge as key issues
title_en: Exclusive: Meta and Amazon discuss ending Muse shopping bot blockade, as ads, search emerge as key issues
author: Sebastian Herrera
article_content:
Amazon and Meta Platforms are in ongoing discussions over a potential deal to connect Meta’s popular Muse AI agent to the e-commerce giant’s online store and end a blockade of the shopping bot imposed by Amazon two months ago.

The two tech giants have held talks on multiple occasions, and two major factors being negotiated are how the companies will handle search results and advertising in any deal, according to people familiar with the matter. Discussions are fluid, and it’s unclear if or how soon an agreement will be struck. There are numerous issues, ranging from Amazon’s own AI shopping ambitions to how exactly Muse would connect to Amazon. A major threat Muse poses to Amazon is that, in theory, it would bypass advertisements on Amazon’s website, which are a large source of revenue for the retailer.

Amazon is worried about losing advertising revenue and about the quality of the product search results Muse would surface, and executives are also concerned that shopping agents like Muse will weaken the relationship Amazon has with consumers, the people said. Any deal between Amazon and Meta is expected to require sign-off from the CEOs of both companies, they said.

Meta and Amazon declined to comment. The negotiations are being closely followed because they have major implications for the future of online shopping and represent an important test case for how large corporations respond to the advent of AI agents. As agents like Muse become more widely used, companies like Amazon are scrambling to understand how the bots alter typical shopping patterns as well as the valued connections that brands and retailers have with consumers.

The talks are ongoing as Amazon prepares for another Black Friday and Cyber Monday, one of its most critical shopping periods of the year. This year, roughly half of holiday shoppers plan to use AI in some way to help make purchases, a National Retail Federation survey this month showed.

AI agents promise to bring major changes to many industries. Agentic shopping could total $190 billion to $385 billion in U.S. e-commerce spending by 2030, representing 10% to 20% of the total market, according to a 2025 report by Morgan Stanley. Analysts at JPMorgan have praised Muse as a powerful agent, recently writing that tens of millions of businesses could eventually use the tool.

Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse app from accessing its store in September, saying at the time that Muse’s access would violate its user agreements. Muse, which Meta released in the U.S. that month, is a personalized AI agent that users can name and have autonomously carry out tasks on their behalf, such as checking email, managing calendars and booking reservations. As of October, more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up the app, making it Meta’s biggest consumer AI hit to date. Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg has said shopping is Muse’s top use case.

“We think that billions of Muses in a network at scale will be able to get more done for people and businesses by working together,” Zuckerberg said last month in a call with analysts. “We’d like to create a large scale Muse network as quickly as possible.”

One of Amazon’s main concerns is how shopping agents such as Muse will affect its advertising business. Advertising has become a $68.6 billion business for Amazon, representing nearly 10% of its total yearly revenue. In October, Amazon Chief Executive Andy Jassy, while not naming Muse, tried to quell investor concern by saying few customers are buying with outside shopping agents because the experience is “still not great, nor more convenient than coming to a retailer directly.”

Still, Jassy said this month at a Semafor conference that Amazon hadn’t ruled out letting outside shopping agents into its store, but that they would have to provide a “fair exchange of value.”

Aside from Meta, OpenAI launched its Dots personal AI agents in September, and startup Instinct’s personal assistant has also become a mainstream AI agent. Amazon has its own shopping agent for its website, dubbed “Alexa for shopping,” which Jassy said has been used by more than 400 million customers in the past year.

Meta and Amazon have partnered on e-commerce before. In 2023, the companies struck a deal that allowed Facebook and Instagram users to purchase Amazon products without leaving the apps. Meta makes money from ads it serves users on its apps, including for Amazon products, and Amazon earns revenue through the actual purchases. The partnership was made as TikTok expanded into U.S. e-commerce.

Meta signed on other partners early in its Muse efforts, including Amazon rivals such as Shopify, Walmart and Best Buy. Retailers have gained another channel for selling products, while Meta tries to grow Muse and, according to Zuckerberg, eventually plans to profit by taking a “small fee from transactions.”

title_zh: Meta与Amazon就Muse购物AI接入谈判
summary_zh: Meta与Amazon正探讨解封Muse AI代理的平台访问权，核心博弈在于搜索权重、广告收益分成及消费者关系归属
article_content_zh:
亚马逊和 Meta Platforms 正在就一项潜在交易进行讨论，将 Meta 广受欢迎的 Muse AI 代理连接到这家电子商务巨头的在线商店，并结束亚马逊两个月前对购物机器人实施的封锁。

这两家科技巨头已多次举行会谈，正在谈判的两个主要因素是两家公司将如何在任何交易中处理搜索结果和广告。讨论尚不明确，目前尚不清楚是否或多久能达成协议。存在很多问题，从亚马逊自己的人工智能购物野心到 Muse 究竟如何与亚马逊连接。 Muse 对亚马逊构成的主要威胁是，从理论上讲，它将绕过亚马逊网站上的广告，而亚马逊网站上的广告是零售商的一大收入来源。

知情人士称，亚马逊担心失去广告收入以及 Muse 出现的产品搜索结果的质量，高管们还担心像 Muse 这样的购物代理会削弱亚马逊与消费者的关系。他们表示，亚马逊和 Meta 之间的任何交易预计都需要两家公司首席执行官的签署。

Meta 和亚马逊拒绝置评。此次谈判受到密切关注，因为它们对在线购物的未来具有重大影响，并且是大公司如何应对人工智能代理出现的重要测试案例。随着 Muse 等代理的使用越来越广泛，亚马逊等公司正在努力了解机器人如何改变典型的购物模式以及品牌和零售商与消费者之间的宝贵联系。

谈判正在进行之际，亚马逊正在为另一个黑色星期五和网络星期一做准备，这是亚马逊一年中最关键的购物时期之一。美国零售联合会本月的一项调查显示，今年大约一半的假日购物者计划以某种方式使用人工智能来帮助购物。

人工智能代理有望给许多行业带来重大变化。根据摩根士丹利 2025 年的一份报告，到 2030 年，代理购物在美国电子商务支出中的总额可能达到 1900 亿至 3850 亿美元，占整个市场的 10% 至 20%。摩根大通的分析师称赞 Muse 是一个强大的代理，最近写道，数千万企业最终可能会使用该工具。

亚马逊于 9 月份阻止了 Meta 的 Muse 应用程序访问其商店，当时表示 Muse 的访问将违反其用户协议。 Meta 当月在美国发布的 Muse 是一款个性化人工智能代理，用户可以命名并代表他们自主执行任务，例如检查电子邮件、管理日历和预订。截至 10 月，美国和加拿大已有超过 1000 万人安装了该应用程序，使其成为 Meta 迄今为止最热门的消费者人工智能产品。首席执行官马克·扎克伯格表示，购物是 Muse 的首要用途。

扎克伯格上个月在与分析师的电话会议上表示：“我们认为，大规模网络中的数十亿缪斯将能够通过共同努力为人们和企业做出更多贡献。” “我们希望尽快创建一个大规模的 Muse 网络。”

亚马逊主要担心的问题之一是 Muse 等购物代理将如何影响其广告业务。广告已成为亚马逊一项价值 686 亿美元的业务，占其年总收入的近 10%。十月，亚马逊首席执行官安迪·贾西（Andy Jassy）虽然没有点名缪斯，但试图平息投资者的担忧，他表示很少有顾客通过外部购物代理购买，因为这种体验“仍然不是很好，也比直接到零售商那里更方便”。

尽管如此，贾西本月在 Semafor 会议上表示，亚马逊并未排除让外部购物代理进入其商店的可能性，但他们必须提供“公平的价值交换”。

除了Meta之外，OpenAI在9月份推出了Dots个人AI代理，初创公司Instinct的个人助理也成为主流AI代理。亚马逊在其网站上拥有自己的购物代理，被称为“Alexa for Shopping”，贾西表示，去年有超过 4 亿客户使用该代理。

Meta 和亚马逊之前曾在电子商务领域进行过合作。 2023 年，两家公司达成一项协议，允许 Facebook 和 Instagram 用户无需离开应用程序即可购买亚马逊产品。 Meta 通过在其应用程序上为用户提供的广告（包括亚马逊产品）来赚钱，而亚马逊则通过实际购买赚取收入。此次合作是在 TikTok 进军美国电子商务之际达成的。

Meta 在 Muse 项目的早期就与其他合作伙伴签约，包括 Shopify、沃尔玛和百思买等亚马逊竞争对手。零售商获得了另一个销售产品的渠道，而 Meta 则试图发展 Muse，据扎克伯格称，最终计划通过“从交易中收取少量费用”来获利。

article_content:
By ROD MCGUIRK Updated [hour]:[minute] [AMPM] [timezone], [monthFull] [day], [year] --> Add AP News on Google Add AP News as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. --> Share

MELBOURNE, Australia (AP) — Australia’s Parliament on Wednesday passed online safety laws that could expose tech giants to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable online harms.

The United States and the Australian opposition party warned that the legislation would lead to censorship of lawful speech.

The Digital Duty of Care Act requires Big Tech to proactively reduce the risk of harm before it occurs, according to an Australian government statement.

The legislation is similar to the European Union’s Digital Services Act, passed in 2022, and the United Kingdom’s Online Safety Act passed a year later.

The legislation became law in the House of Representatives, where the center-left Labor Party government commands a majority, by 97 votes to 43.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told Parliament the law would stand as a “powerful instrument to protect our children and our society from online harms by placing the onus on the tech platforms to ensure a safer online environment.”

“This is a victory for our children and young people. The dangers were unforeseen when the digital world was young,” Albanese said. “But now that the digital world has matured, they can be easily recognized and they can be remedied.”

Opposition leader Angus Taylor told Parliament he would repeal the legislation if his conservative Liberal Party wins elections in 2028. Taylor described the legislation as “authoritarian.”

“This bill is a blank check for political censorship,” Taylor told Parliament. “The bill is an attack on free speech that is absolutely central to our democracy.”

Australia set to pass a digital duty of care law, with fines up to 5% of tech giants’ global revenue 3 MIN READ 15 Medicare for All was once a long shot. Now, steps toward it are part of the Democratic agenda 5 MIN READ 1605 House to debate slightly tweaked version of Protect College Sports Act 1 MIN READ 37 The government struck a deal with the minor Greens party on Tuesday to get the legislation through the Senate, where no party holds a majority.

“Today, the safety and wellbeing of Australians and their children have finally been put ahead of Big Tech’s bottom line,” Greens chief negotiator Sarah Hanson-Young said in a statement after the bill passed the Senate by 36 votes to 23.

“My message to Big Tech companies is, it’s time to make your platforms safe or we will see you in court,” she added.

The Australian legislation sets minimum safety standards for online services, including games, apps and artificial intelligence chatbots, requiring them to protect Australians from seriously harmful material and conduct, the government said.

The Greens’ amendments include increasing maximum penalties for breaches from 109 million Australian dollars ($72 million), as the government originally proposed, to 5% of a tech company’s global revenue.

U.S. Ambassador to Australia David Brat said on Tuesday the then-proposed laws would “impose disproportionate compliance burdens on American companies relative to competitors.”

“Vaguely defined ‘harms,’ backed by penalties of up to 5% of global revenue, will push platforms to censor lawful speech,” Brat posted on social media.

澳大利亚墨尔本（美联社）——澳大利亚议会周三通过了网络安全法，科技巨头可能因未能防止可预见的网络伤害而面临数十亿美元的罚款。

美国和澳大利亚反对党警告称，该立法将导致对合法言论的审查。

根据澳大利亚政府的一份声明，《数字谨慎责任法案》要求大型科技公司在伤害发生之前主动降低风险。

该立法类似于 2022 年通过的欧盟《数字服务法案》和一年后通过的英国《在线安全法案》。

该法案在众议院成为法律，中左翼工党政府以 97 票对 43 票在众议院占据多数席位。

总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞告诉议会，该法律将成为“保护我们的孩子和社会免受网络伤害的强大工具，让技术平台承担确保更安全的网络环境的责任。”

“这对我们的孩子和年轻人来说是一次胜利。当数字世界还很年轻时，危险是无法预见的，”阿尔巴尼斯说。 “但现在数字世界已经成熟，它们可以很容易地被识别，并且可以得到补救。”

反对党领袖安格斯·泰勒 (Angus Taylor) 告诉议会，如果他领导的保守党自由党在 2028 年赢得选举，他将废除该立法。泰勒称该立法是“独裁的”。

“这项法案是政治审查的空白支票，”泰勒告诉议会。 “该法案是对言论自由的攻击，而言论自由对于我们的民主来说绝对是核心。”

该法案以 36 票对 23 票在参议院获得通过后，绿党首席谈判代表莎拉·汉森-杨 (Sarah Hanson-Young) 在一份声明中表示：“今天，澳大利亚人和他们孩子的安全和福祉终于被置于大型科技公司的底线之上。”

“我向大型科技公司传达的信息是，是时候确保你们的平台安全了，否则我们将在法庭上见到你们，”她补充道。

政府表示，澳大利亚立法为包括游戏、应用程序和人工智能聊天机器人在内的在线服务设定了最低安全标准，要求它们保护澳大利亚人免受严重有害的材料和行为的侵害。

title: AI is straining America’s open records systems
title_en: AI is straining America’s open records systems
author: Rachel Courtland
article_content:
In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer. During morning office hours at the town hall—a wood-frame structure built as a church in 1858—he also fielded public records requests. Recently, he got rather busy.

Panton used to get a request every year or so from a company called SmartProcure for “all purchasing records,” covering everything from road salt to computers to toilet paper. Last year, those requests started coming quarterly. Then different companies began making more specific requests, like records of every purchase related to emergency road flares. These targeted inquiries started coming monthly or more. “I’m happy to answer public records requests from people,” says Rowe, who recently moved into a position at a nearby town. “But answering it for these purposes—it feels like I’m doing unpaid opposition research on the taxpayers’ time.”

Rowe’s experiences are being repeated across the US. While data brokers have mined public records for decades, AI has intensified investors’ interest. Over the last few years, venture-backed startups have raised upwards of $100 million to collect data from thousands of agencies and turn it into AI-powered “signals” that help businesses sell to governments.

At the same time, AI tools have made it easier for individuals to draft public records requests. Many places have seen double-digit annual increases in recent years. While more activity is good for democracy, AI-drafted requests tend to be longer, and broader in scope—and the offices answering them haven’t always grown in head count or budget.

As agencies struggle to tell whether they’re dealing with a citizen, a chatbot, or a sales pipeline, some states are passing legislation that makes it easier to deny requests, possibly making public offices less transparent.

The US Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) of 1966 established citizens’ right to know what their government is doing, and by now every state has written its own version into law. Greater transparency has led to cleaner drinking water, lower taxes, and better schools. But the system is far from perfect: Many requests linger for months, the process is often frustratingly bureaucratic, and rules and guidelines vary by state, county, and even town.

This is why businesses, with the time and resources to navigate this labyrinth, have often dominated FOIA since its early days. Margaret Kwoka, a law professor at Ohio State University and a recent member of the FOIA Advisory Committee, documented the trend in her 2016 study “ FOIA, Inc .”

Her analysis found that commercial requesters of all kinds—regulated companies, government contractors, information resellers—have accounted for 79% to 96% of public records requests at federal agencies like the Environmental Protection Agency and the Food and Drug Administration. What Kwoka once described as a cottage industry of small shops reselling public records has become a lucrative market for “much more sophisticated and integrated database products,” she says.

SmartProcure (which does business as GovSpend) pioneered the model 15 years ago, with a standardized approach for collecting government purchasing data. Its requests are “handled by real people with long-standing relationships,” says Trip Colden, GovSpend’s chief operating officer, and the company has preferential pricing for agencies.

The newer AI startups promise to make selling to government faster and fairer. Starbridge has raised $52 million, including a Series A led by Craft Ventures (the firm of David Sacks, the former White House AI and crypto czar), to build the equivalent of a “Bloomberg Terminal for public sector data,” a reference to the pricey data consoles that are a fixture on Wall Street trading desks. The company describes its mission as getting “the best technology into the hands of public leaders,” with public records as one input that helps match agencies with vendors. Pursuit, backed by investors including Bill Gurley and Jack Altman, has raised $25.5 million to help companies identify likely government buyers, drawing on board minutes, budgets, and what it calls “an industrial-scale FOIA operation.” CEO and cofounder Mike Vichich says Pursuit’s data will benefit the public, noting that many towns are seeing costs rise faster than revenues and “competition is what saves taxpayers money.”

While incumbents employ account teams to build a rapport with agencies, several clerks and county attorneys say newer startups often send many requests as they scramble to catch up on historical data. For example, PinPoint Analytics, which analyzes construction bid data, sent as many as 2,000 requests per day while building its dataset before settling closer to 500 today, says chief operating officer Mark Zurada. That mirrors the activity of SmartProcure and Pursuit, which send roughly 180,000 requests per year, according to their websites.

But the numbers can be much higher. NationGraph, which serves midsize vendors such as janitorial service providers, claims to send about 10,000 requests per day on behalf of clients; the company did not respond to requests for comment. The requests that companies send are typically written with templates, not AI. But AI helps standardize what comes back—spreadsheets, PDFs, mailed packets—and analyze it all to create branded sales “signals,” or benchmarks to help the business clients set their prices.

In small towns, this activity can be an annoyance; in cities and counties, which get many times the volume, handling it is becoming a full-time job. Chautauqua County, New York, hired a paralegal this summer after seeing requests double—an increase its county attorney blamed on people using ChatGPT to generate requests and on others seeking records to resell.

In Ann Arbor, Michigan, chief deputy clerk Sarah Alanis has seen the number of requests climb from 581 in 2021 to 937 last year—“our new normal is high,” she says. A growing share comes from requesters harvesting data at scale, sometimes asking for purchases from “vendors that don’t have much to do with one another,” or ones the city has never used. FOIA used to take a few hours of her week; now it’s often half her day , she told the Michigan Advance earlier this year.

It’s not just sales tech—AI tools have made it easy for anyone to fire off requests. Federal agencies received a record 1.7 million last year, which a New York Times report attributed partly to AI, as well as to mass filings by the Heritage Foundation and a rise in the number of immigrants seeking their own records for legal protection. David Cuillier, director of the Brechner Freedom of Information Project at the University of Florida, ran the US Department of Education’s July request log through an AI detector and concluded that at least 29% of requests had been written at least partly by AI, up from almost none before 2025. The AI-written requests were twice as long, and 83% asked for long lists of records.

In Pennsylvania, AI-driven activity is “breaking records every month,” says Liz Wagenseller, executive director of the Office of Open Records, which fields appeals for denied requests. Volumes had surged before—during the covid years, at the height of the 2020 election fight, or amid battles over school curricula. But Wagenseller says this wave isn’t driven by a hot-button issue, and appeals keep rising—from about 3,000 in 2021 and just under 4,000 in 2025 to a projected 6,000 this year.

While more activity signals stronger civic engagement, AI is straining an already fragile infrastructure with often poorly drafted requests. Wagenseller notes that when it comes to appealing a denial, chatbots “always give [people] encouragement to try,” even when it has no chance. Filings that used to take a paragraph now run pages. Some contain hallucinated legal citations, and one even included the user’s prompt to Claude.

On the other side of the records requests, resource-strapped offices are using tech to manage it all. One-fifth of federal agencies report using AI or machine learning to help search for records. The Washington Post reported that the Department of Homeland Security is using AI to speed redactions , which transparency advocates worry could lock in agencies’ long habit of withholding more than the law requires. Local governments are catching up, with many still migrating from email to centralized request portals. The software vendor CivicPlus says its NextRequest platform handles more than a million requests a year and uses captchas to screen out bots. That stops automated agents, says chief marketing officer Jane Snyder, but it “doesn’t determine whether a person used AI to help draft a request.”

As volumes rise, legislatures are responding. CivicPlus counts more than 20 state and federal measures in play this year, several of which give agencies new ways to say no. California’s, signed in September, declares that AI systems are not “members of the public,” though people may still use AI “at an ordinary human volume and frequency.” A stalled Pennsylvania bill would let agencies deny requests they “reasonably suspect” were generated by a script or AI. Wagenseller doesn’t think that’s the answer. The real choice, she says, is funding agencies to keep up or making the system less free, fast, and open—“and you’re giving up something for both.”

Arguably the most aggressive action yet has been in Indiana, where Allen County officials described a growing trend in “suspiciously non-human” requests for years of purchase orders, eating up to 20 hours a week of staff time, as reported by the Journal Gazette . A state law that passed without a single dissenting vote and took effect July 1 lets agencies charge out-of-state requesters, prioritize residents, and deny requests they suspect are aimed at data scraping or phishing.

Neighboring Adams County went further. In March, it banned commercial use of its records, including resale. The county still hands over the documents, though; a notice of the ban is attached, but there are few means to enforce it. Requests had jumped from about one a week to as many as 10, often in a single burst; since the state law took effect, they’ve settled at one to five. County attorney Clayton Lengerich says the new rules don’t affect “any individual requester’s ability to keep their local municipality accountable,” only requests that “someone’s going to throw into an AI generator for some sales analysis.”

Fielding FOIA requests is expensive, and someone has to pay. Congress tried to put the responsibility on business in 1986, amending FOIA to let agencies charge commercial requesters more, but the rules were so riddled with exceptions that this rarely happens. “It costs more for the agencies to collect the fees than it’s worth in fees, and so they just don’t,” says Kwoka, the Ohio State law professor. She estimates that agencies recoup less than 5% of their costs from commercial requesters; at the FDA in one year she studied, it was $328,000 against $33.6 million spent.

Kwoka has long argued for “affirmative disclosure,” or proactively posting the information that gets asked for most. She points to the EPA, which put property contamination records online after commercial buyers had requested them one address at a time for years. A handful of states have adopted portals, such as California’s Open FI$Cal , that regularly publish high-level spending data. But this doesn’t include the full contracts that sales-tech firms often request, which reveal expiration dates, termination clauses, and service commitments.

Startups like Pursuit and Starbridge say they’d welcome this approach, and they seem confident their business model could survive if the data became freely available. “The best request is one that no one has to file because the data is already out there,” says Vichich. But publishing isn’t free, and commercial requesters also aren’t raising their hands to fund the fix.

As states negotiate reforms, the biggest risk is that rules built to limit bulk AI requests or sales-tech crawlers will land on everyone else: out-of-state reporters, academic researchers, immigration lawyers. Meanwhile, the requests keep increasing. “It’s something we’re going to have to hold our nose and continue doing,” says Rowe, the small-town Vermont clerk. “The alternative sets a dangerous precedent for a person being able to hold government accountable.”

article_content_zh:
在人口 660 的佛蒙特州潘顿，镇书记凯尔·罗 (Kyle Rowe) 完成了这一切。他制定预算、向供应商付款、处理财产税纠纷，并担任该镇的分区主管和主持选举的官员。在市政厅（一座建于 1858 年的木框架结构教堂）的早上办公时间，他还处理了公共记录请求。最近一段时间，他比较忙。

过去，潘顿每年都会收到一家名为 SmartProcure 的公司索取“所有采购记录”的请求，涵盖从道路盐到电脑再到卫生纸的所有物品。去年，这些请求开始每季度提出一次。然后，不同的公司开始提出更具体的要求，例如与紧急道路照明弹相关的每次购买的记录。这些有针对性的询问开始每月或更长时间进行。 “我很高兴回答人们的公共记录请求，”罗说，他最近搬到了附近城镇的一个职位。 “但出于这些目的回答这个问题——感觉就像我在利用纳税人的时间进行无偿的反对派研究。”

罗的经历正在美国各地重演。尽管数据经纪人挖掘公共记录已有数十年之久，但人工智能却增强了投资者的兴趣。在过去的几年里，风险投资支持的初创公司已筹集了超过 1 亿美元，用于从数千个机构收集数据，并将其转化为人工智能驱动的“信号”，帮助企业向政府出售产品。

与此同时，人工智能工具使个人更容易起草公共记录请求。近年来，许多地方的年增长率均达到两位数。虽然更多的活动有利于民主，但人工智能起草的请求往往更长、范围更广，而且答复这些请求的办公室的人员数量或预算并不总是增加。

由于各机构很难判断他们是在与公民、聊天机器人还是销售渠道打交道，一些州正在通过立法，使拒绝请求变得更容易，这可能会降低公共办公室的透明度。

1966 年的美国信息自由法案 (FOIA) 确立了公民了解政府正在做什么的权利，到目前为止，每个州都已将自己的版本写入法律。更大的透明度带来了更清洁的饮用水、更低的税收和更好的学校。但这个系统远非完美：许多请求会持续数月，整个过程往往官僚得令人沮丧，而且规则和指导方针因州、县甚至城镇而异。

这就是为什么拥有时间和资源来探索这个迷宫的企业从早期开始就常常主导《信息自由法》。俄亥俄州立大学法学教授、最近加入 FOIA 咨询委员会的玛格丽特·科沃卡 (Margaret Kwoka) 在她 2016 年的研究“FOIA, Inc”中记录了这一趋势。

她的分析发现，各类商业请求者（受监管公司、政府承包商、信息经销商）占环境保护局和食品药品管理局等联邦机构公共记录请求的 79% 至 96%。她说，科沃卡曾将其描述为转售公共记录的小商店家庭手工业，但现在已经成为“更加复杂和集成的数据库产品”的利润丰厚的市场。

SmartProcure（以 GovSpend 名义开展业务）在 15 年前首创了该模型，采用标准化方法收集政府采购数据。 GovSpend 首席运营官 Trip Colden 表示，其请求“由具有长期关系的真人处理”，并且该公司为代理机构提供优惠价格。

较新的人工智能初创公司承诺更快、更公平地向政府出售产品。 Starbridge 已筹集了 5200 万美元，其中包括由 Craft Ventures（前白宫人工智能和加密货币沙皇 David Sacks 的公司）牵头的 A 轮融资，用于构建相当于“公共部门数据的彭博终端”，指的是华尔街交易柜台上常见的昂贵数据控制台。该公司将其使命描述为“将最好的技术交到公共领导人手中”，并将公共记录作为帮助机构与供应商进行匹配的一项输入。 Pursuit 得到了 Bill Gurley 和 Jack Altman 等投资者的支持，已筹集 2550 万美元，帮助公司确定可能的政府买家，并利用董事会会议记录、预算和所谓的“工业规模的 FOIA 操作”。首席执行官兼联合创始人迈克·维奇奇表示，Pursuit 的数据将使公众受益，并指出许多城镇的成本增长速度快于收入增长速度，“竞争可以节省纳税人的钱”。

虽然现有企业聘请客户团队与各机构建立融洽的关系，但几名办事员和县检察官表示，新成立的初创公司在争先恐后地追赶历史数据时经常会发出许多请求。例如，首席运营官马克·祖拉达 (Mark Zurada) 表示，分析建筑投标数据的 PinPoint Analytics 在构建数据集时每天发送多达 2,000 个请求，如今已接近 500 个。这反映了 SmartProcure 和 Pursuit 的活动，根据其网站，它们每年发送大约 180,000 个请求。

但数字可能要高得多。 NationGraph 为清洁服务提供商等中型供应商提供服务，声称每天代表客户发送约 10,000 个请求；该公司没有回应置评请求。公司发送的请求通常是用模板编写的，而不是人工智能。但人工智能有助于标准化返回的内容（电子表格、PDF、邮寄数据包）并对其进行分析，以创建品牌销售“信号”或基准来帮助企业客户设定价格。

在小城镇，这项活动可能会很烦人。在处理量成倍增加的城市和县，处理它正在成为一项全职工作。纽约州肖托夸县在看到请求翻倍后于今年夏天聘请了一名律师助理，县检察官将这一增加归咎于使用 ChatGPT 生成请求的人和其他寻求转售记录的人。

在密歇根州安娜堡，首席副书记员 Sarah Alanis 发现请求数量从 2021 年的 581 项攀升至去年的 937 项——“我们的新常态很高，”她说。越来越多的份额来自大规模收集数据的请求者，有时要求从“彼此没有太多关系的供应商”或该市从未使用过的供应商处购买。过去，FOIA 每周要花几个小时的时间。今年早些时候，她告诉《密歇根进展报》，现在她的工作时间通常是一半。

【起因与机理】AI降低了 opposition research 及数据信号挖掘的边际成本

title: Flipkart CEO to Exit After Transforming Walmart’s India Play
title_en: Flipkart CEO to Exit After Transforming Walmart’s India Play

inline_images.caption: g_105603_walmart_flipkart_280x210.jpg
inline_images.alt: g_105603_walmart_flipkart_280x210.jpg

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Walmart’s president and CEO Doug McMillon (left) with Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal. The deal marks the latest milestone in Walmart’s drawn-out pursuit of India’s lucrative retail market Walmart Inc has signed definitive agreements to become the largest shareholder in the Flipkart Group, in a transaction that values Flipkart at $20.8 billion (around Rs 1.4 lakh crore).

The investment “underscores Walmart’s commitment to sustained job creation and investment in India, one of the largest and fastest-growing economies in the world,” the US company said in a press release on Wednesday.Subject to regulatory approval in India, Walmart will pay approximately $16 billion (around Rs 1 lakh crore) for an initial stake of approximately 77 percent in Flipkart, formally Flipkart Private Limited.

The remainder of the business will be held by some of Flipkart’s existing shareholders, including Flipkart co- founder Binny Bansal, Tencent Holdings Limited, Tiger Global Management LLC and Microsoft Corp, Walmart said in its press release. This implies that the other co-founder Sachin Bansal (unrelated to Binny Bansal) will sell all his stake in the ecommerce company he founded in 2007.

“India is one of the most attractive retail markets in the world, given its size and growth rate, and our investment is an opportunity to partner with the company that is leading the transformation of the ecommerce in the market,” Doug McMillon, Walmart’s president and chief executive officer, said in the press release.

India was a “critical market” for Walmart, he added. “Walmart has been looking to get into the Indian retail market for more than 15 years but the regulation of not allowing FDI into multi-brand retail has made it impossible for Walmart to access the Indian market,” Satish Meena, senior forecast analyst at consultancy Forrester, told Forbes India in an emailed statement.

“Walmart tried to enter via a wholesale model with Bharti Enterprises in India but failed. Now they see online as the only method to enter the Indian market, which leaves Flipkart as the best investment option for Walmart.”According to Forrester, the Indian online retail market was around $20 billion in 2017 (2.4 percent of total retail market in India).

No other market except China and US can compete in terms of total retail opportunity. Forrester projects the online retail market in India to reach $73 billion by 2022.In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2018, Flipkart recorded gross merchandise value(GMV) of $7.5 billion and net sales of $4.6 billion representing more than 50 percent year-over-year growth in both, according to the press release.

Currently, Walmart India operates 21 Best Price cash-and-carry stores and one fulfilment centre, across 19 cities in nine Indian states, with more than 95 percent of sourcing coming from India. In a presentation to investors, Walmart said that with Flipkart, there’s an opportunity to tap the latter's strong foundations in India, become the lowest cost operator and offer differentiated customer service.

The American company sees India as its only other “key growth market” apart from China, while America remains its core market, with a clutch of other markets comprising other growth opportunities — such as in Africa and Latin America. The Flipkart transaction is an exercise in marrying “local talent with global expertise,” Walmart said.Flipkart had 54 million active users in a market where there were 443 million millennials and about two-thirds of the country’s 1.3 billion population comprises the so-called ‘Generation Z’ or those who were typically born from the mid-1990s onwards.

India is also the second largest internet market in the world, by number of users — the first being China. India is also unique in that 79 percent of its internet users access the net via the mobile phone, whereas the proportion is about 50 percent for the global average.The company cited a report by consultancy Bain and Co. to point out it was entering a market where total retail is set to grow at about 9 percent whereas ecommerce is projected to surge ahead at a rate of 36 percent, growing four-times faster.

Penetration would triple from today’s 2.1 percent to 6.2 percent in the year 2023, therefore leaving a massive opportunity for further growth by achieving deeper online commerce penetration. Walmart and Flipkart are also in discussions with additional potential investors who may join the investment round, which could result in Walmart’s investment stake moving lower after the transaction is complete.

Even so, the company would retain clear majority ownership. Tencent and Tiger Global will continue on the Flipkart board, joined by new members from Walmart, according to the release.The final make-up of the board has yet to be determined, but it will also include independent members.

The board will work to maintain Flipkart’s core values and entrepreneurial spirit, while ensuring it has strategic and competitive advantages, Walmart said in the release.The transaction includes a $2 billion infusion of fresh equity investment into Flipkart, enlarging its war chest as it gears up for a three-way fight for India’s retail market against Amazon on one side and China’s Alibaba Group on the other, which has backed Flipkart’s local rival One97 Communications that operates both India’s largest mobile wallet service and an ecommerce marketplace under the brand name Paytm.“For Flipkart, this deal is more than just money,” said Forrester’s Meena.

To remain the number one player in India (Amazon coming a close second in just four years in India), they are looking to expand beyond smartphones and fashion. This deal with Walmart can provide Flipkart the expertise of running offline stores, access to sellers and manufacturers, supply chain and the know-how to get into the grocery segment, he said.Amazon has been selling groceries in India for the past one year while Flipkart has not rolled out this category.

With Amazon closing the gap in categories other than fashion, Meena added that “Flipkart needs Walmart to remain competitive in the long term.”While the immediate focus will be on growing the business, “Walmart supports Flipkart’s ambition to transition into a publicly-listed, majority-owned subsidiary in the future,” the Bentonville, Arkansas-based company said in the release.

The current transaction is expected to close later this calendar year, subject to regulatory approvals.

article_content_zh:
沃尔玛总裁兼首席执行官 Doug McMillon（左）与 Flipkart 联合创始人 Binny Bansal。这笔交易标志着沃尔玛对印度利润丰厚的零售市场的长期追求的最新里程碑。沃尔玛公司已签署最终协议，成为 Flipkart 集团的最大股东，此次交易对 Flipkart 的估值为 208 亿美元（约合 14 亿卢比）。

这家美国公司在周三的一份新闻稿中表示，这项投资“突显了沃尔玛对在印度持续创造就业和投资的承诺，印度是世界上最大、增长最快的经济体之一。”根据印度监管部门的批准，沃尔玛将支付约 160 亿美元（约合 10 亿卢比）购买 Flipkart（原名 Flipkart Private Limited）约 77% 的初始股权。

沃尔玛在新闻稿中表示，剩余业务将由 Flipkart 的一些现有股东持有，包括 Flipkart 联合创始人 Binny Bansal、腾讯控股有限公司、Tiger Global Management LLC 和微软公司。这意味着另一位联合创始人 Sachin Bansal（与 Binny Bansal 无关）将出售他在 2007 年创立的电子商务公司的所有股份。

沃尔玛总裁兼首席执行官道格·麦克米伦 (Doug McMillon) 在新闻稿中表示：“鉴于其规模和增长率，印度是世界上最具吸引力的零售市场之一，我们的投资是与引领市场电子商务转型的公司合作的机会。”

他补充说，印度是沃尔玛的“关键市场”。咨询公司 Forrester 的高级预测分析师萨蒂什·米纳 (Satish Meena) 在一份电子邮件声明中对《福布斯》印度版表示：“沃尔玛 15 年来一直寻求进入印度零售市场，但不允许外国直接投资进入多品牌零售的规定使沃尔玛无法进入印度市场。”

“沃尔玛试图通过 Bharti Enterprises 的批发模式进入印度，但失败了。现在他们将线上视为进入印度市场的唯一方式，这使得 Flipkart 成为沃尔玛的最佳投资选择。” 据 Forrester 数据显示，2017 年印度在线零售市场规模约为 200 亿美元（占印度零售市场总额的 2.4%）。

在总零售机会方面，除了中国和美国之外，没有其他市场可以与之竞争。 Forrester 预计，到 2022 年，印度在线零售市场将达到 730 亿美元。 据新闻稿称，在截至 2018 年 3 月 31 日的财年中，Flipkart 的商品总价值 (GMV) 为 75 亿美元，净销售额为 46 亿美元，同比增长超过 50%。

目前，沃尔玛印度公司在印度九个邦的 19 个城市运营着 21 家 Best Price 现购自运店和 1 个配送中心，其中 95% 以上的采购来自印度。沃尔玛在向投资者发表的演讲中表示，通过 Flipkart，我们有机会利用后者在印度的强大基础，成为成本最低的运营商并提供差异化​​的客户服务。

这家美国公司将印度视为除中国之外唯一的另一个“关键增长市场”，而美国仍然是其核心市场，还有一些包含其他增长机会的其他市场，例如非洲和拉丁美洲。沃尔玛表示，Flipkart 的交易是将“本地人才与全球专业知识”结合起来。Flipkart 拥有 5400 万活跃用户，该市场有 4.43 亿千禧一代，而该国 13 亿人口中约三分之二是所谓的“Z 世代”或通常出生于 90 年代中期以后的人。

按用户数量计算，印度也是世界第二大互联网市场——第一是中国。印度的独特之处还在于，79%的互联网用户通过手机上网，而全球平均水平约为50%。该公司援引贝恩咨询公司的一份报告指出，印度正在进入一个零售总额预计将增长约9%的市场，而电子商务预计将以36%的速度飙升，增长速度是其四倍。

到 2023 年，渗透率将从目前的 2.1% 增加两倍至 6.2%，因此通过实现更深层次的在线商务渗透率，为进一步增长留下了巨大的机会。沃尔玛和 Flipkart 还在与可能加入此轮投资的其他潜在投资者进行讨论，这可能导致交易完成后沃尔玛的投资股份减少。

即便如此，该公司仍将保留明显的多数股权。据新闻稿称，腾讯和 Tiger Global 将继续留在 Flipkart 董事会，沃尔玛的新成员也将加入其中。董事会的最终组成尚未确定，但也将包括独立成员。

沃尔玛在新闻稿中表示，董事会将致力于维护 Flipkart 的核心价值观和创业精神，同时确保其拥有战略和竞争优势。该交易包括向 Flipkart 注入 20 亿美元的新股权投资，扩大其资金，以准备在印度零售市场与亚马逊和中国阿里巴巴集团进行三方争夺。品牌名称为 Paytm 的电子商务市场。“对于 Flipkart 来说，这笔交易不仅仅是金钱，”Forrester 的 Meena 说道。

为了保持印度第一的地位（亚马逊在短短四年内就在印度紧随其后），他们正在寻求将业务扩展到智能手机和时尚以外的领域。他表示，与沃尔玛的这项交易可以为 Flipkart 提供运营线下商店、接触卖家和制造商、供应链以及进入食品杂货领域的专业知识。过去一年，亚马逊一直在印度销售食品杂货，而 Flipkart 尚未推出这一类别。

title: Chinese EDA software provider Phlexing says it has been collaborating with Huawei since 2019 to develop a suite of EDA tools based on Huawei's Tau Scaling Law (Nikkei Asia)
title_en: Chinese EDA software provider Phlexing says it has been collaborating with Huawei since 2019 to develop a suite of EDA tools based on Huawei's Tau Scaling Law (Nikkei Asia)

inline_images.caption: 20261124 Huawei
inline_images.alt: 20261124 Huawei

inline_images.caption: China's Huawei convicted in US criminal trial over Iran business
inline_images.alt: China's Huawei convicted in US criminal trial over Iran business

inline_images.caption: Synopsys looks to work with Chinese AI labs to speed up chip design
inline_images.alt: Synopsys looks to work with Chinese AI labs to speed up chip design

author: Nikkei Asia
article_content:
TAIPEI -- China's Huawei Technologies and a local partner say they have overcome a U.S. crackdown on its use of advanced chip design tools, a market long dominated by American leaders Synopsys and Cadence, paving the way for the Chinese tech titan to design next-generation chips for phones and servers domestically.

Phlexing Technology, a little-known electronic design automation (EDA) software provider, said it has been partnering with Huawei to develop toolkits to design chips based on Huawei's chip design principle known as the Tau Scaling Law. Qing He, chairman of Phlexing, said strategic collaboration began in 2019 with work on a new suite of EDA tools, later dubbed Tau EDA.

"Huawei brings telecom-grade stringent standards to enable Phlexing's EDA development. It lifts the whole EDA sector," He said on Tuesday at Huawei's Innovation and Intellectual Property Forum in Beijing, adding that Huawei was linking Phlexing EDA with other homegrown EDA tool suppliers for real project tool training. "Fabless [chipmakers], fabs [chip plants] and packaging houses work together via this mechanism. Phlexing EDA unlocks huge productivity across the whole chain," He said.

Yu Liu, Huawei's Kirin chip architect, said the Chinese company had made major efforts to overhaul the chip design process and overcome many hurdles to drive a comeback for the company's own chips.

"We had to tackle eight major technological challenges. We ran a large program covering architecture, design, process workflows, and EDA tools," Liu said.

The disclosure came as Huawei announced record revenue from its patent licensing business. It said it generated $800 million last year, up from $630 million in 2024, and had made $6.9 billion in accumulated patent licensing revenue between 2011 and September 2026.

China has aimed to cut its reliance on foreign companies for EDA ever since Huawei lost access to U.S. technologies when Washington added it to its so-called Entity List in May 2019.

In 2025, Huawei's research and development spending was 192 billion yuan ($29 billion), or 21.8% of its annual revenue. More than half of its employees, or 114,000 people, work in R&D. It has established 86 foundational technology labs, and more than 180 joint innovation labs.

Wireless communications account for 41% of Huawei's active granted patents, terminal hardware for 16%, and artificial intelligence and compute for 13%. Huawei now holds more than 8,000 AI-related patents.

Alan Fan, Huawei's chief intellectual property officer, told reporters that the company has elevated its IP division to a top-level department reporting directly to the board, underscoring its commitment to developing proprietary technologies and patents. The move also reflected the leadership's push to strengthen Huawei's legal capabilities and give intellectual property a more prominent role in its strategy.

Asia has become the predominant player in intellectual property worldwide, according to Francis Gurry, former director-general of the World Intellectual Property Organization.

"Seventy per cent of all intellectual property applications are filed in Asia ... and that reflects Asia's preeminence as a technological power, and as a market with 58% of the world's population," Gurry told a forum in Beijing.

Huawei's licensing partners include Qualcomm and HP in the U.S., Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen in Europe, and Seiko Solutions and Mitsubishi Fuso in Japan, according to the Chinese company.

Huawei's announcement comes as the AI industry experiences severe volatility over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt departure and dramatic return as CEO following an alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. U.S. President Donald Trump touted his efforts to secure Huang's return, saying China could have poached him to work for Nvidia's rival Huawei.

Huawei has accelerated its chip-building ambitions, debuting a supercomputer chip cluster for the overseas market earlier this year and introducing a UnifiedBus and near-packaged optics (NPO) standard to compete with Nvidia's interconnect networking technology. In May, it said it had overcome U.S. restrictions by finding a new way to design chips with its Tau Scaling Law.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 华为与国产EDA软件商飞昂科技（Phlexing）合作，深度整合芯片架构、设计流程及EDA工具链。该项目依托华为“Tau缩放定律”核心技术，旨在解决先进制程下芯片设计的全链路自动化难题，以此对抗美国对其实施的实体清单封锁。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该项协作标志着华为试图将芯片设计标准从通用的美国工具范式迁移至其自研的数学规律体系，属于彻底的“软硬协同”重构。这一举措不仅是单一工具的替代，更是通过绑定晶圆厂与封装厂，试图构筑一套绕过国际商业EDA垄断的独立算力供应链闭环。

It aims to build an isolated compute supply chain by linking fabs and packaging houses, effectively bypassing international EDA monopolies.

article_content_zh:
台北——中国华为技术公司和一家当地合作伙伴表示，他们已经克服了美国对其使用先进芯片设计工具的限制，该市场长期由美国领导者 Synopsys 和 Cadence 主导，为这家中国科技巨头在国内设计下一代手机和服务器芯片铺平了道路。

鲜为人知的电子设计自动化（EDA）软件提供商Phlexing Technology表示，它一直在与华为合作开发工具包，以根据华为的芯片设计原理（即Tau缩放定律）设计芯片。 Phlexing 董事长何庆表示，战略合作始于 2019 年，致力于开发一套新的 EDA 工具，后来被称为 Tau EDA。

他周二在北京举行的华为创新与知识产权论坛上表示：“华为带来了电信级的严格标准来支持Phlexing的EDA开发。它提升了整个EDA行业。”他补充说，华为正在将Phlexing EDA与其他本土EDA工具供应商联系起来，进行真正的项目工具培训。 “无晶圆厂（芯片制造商）、晶圆厂（芯片厂）和封装厂通过这种机制协同工作。Phlexing EDA 释放了整个链条的巨大生产力，”他说。

华为麒麟芯片架构师刘宇表示，这家中国公司为彻底改革芯片设计流程付出了巨大努力，并克服了许多障碍，以推动该公司自有芯片的东山再起。

“我们必须解决八项主要技术挑战。我们运行了一个涵盖架构、设计、流程工作流程和 EDA 工具的大型项目，”刘说。

这一消息披露之际，华为宣布其专利许可业务收入创历史新高。该公司表示，去年的收入为 8 亿美元，高于 2024 年的 6.3 亿美元，2011 年至 2026 年 9 月期间累计专利许可收入为 69 亿美元。

自从华盛顿于 2019 年 5 月将华为列入所谓的实体清单以来，华为失去了获得美国技术的机会，中国一直致力于减少对外国公司 EDA 的依赖。

2025年，华为的研发支出为1920亿元人民币（290亿美元），占其年收入的21.8%。超过一半的员工（114,000 人）从事研发工作。建有基础技术实验室86个，联合创新实验室180多个。

无线通信占华为活跃授权专利的41%，终端硬件占16%，人工智能和计算占13%。华为目前拥有8000多项人工智能相关专利。

华为首席知识产权官范艾伦告诉记者，该公司已将知识产权部门提升为直接向董事会报告的顶级部门，强调了其对开发专有技术和专利的承诺。此举还反映出领导层致力于加强华为的法律能力，并使知识产权在其战略中发挥更加突出的作用。

世界知识产权组织前总干事弗朗西斯·高锐表示，亚洲已成为全球知识产权领域的主要参与者。

高锐在北京的一个论坛上表示：“所有知识产权申请的 70% 是在亚洲提出的……这反映了亚洲作为技术强国和占世界人口 58% 的市场的卓越地位。”

据华为称，华为的授权合作伙伴包括美国的高通和惠普、欧洲的梅赛德斯-奔驰和大众、以及日本的精工解决方案和三菱扶桑。

华为宣布这一消息之际，正值人工智能行业经历严重波动之际，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌与中国间谍嫌疑人有关系而突然离职，又戏剧性地重新担任首席执行官。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普吹捧了他为确保黄仁勋回归所做的努力，称中国可能挖走他为英伟达的竞争对手华为工作。

author: Financial Times
article_content:
Four large adult content websites are seeking to reach a deal with the European Commission on preventing children from accessing porn, as the sites try to minimise upcoming fines under the bloc’s push to protect minors online.

The Commission is investigating Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX and XVideos for alleged breaches of the Digital Services Act by failing to adequately protect children from accessing adult content, as minors could access the porn platforms by simply claiming via one click that they are over 18. The DSA — which fully took effect in 2024 and forms part of the bloc’s broader digital rulebook — sets out how tech companies should police the internet.

The probe forms part of a broader European push to protect minors online that also includes a proposal to ban the use of social media, certain gaming platforms and AI chatbots by children under 13.

Since the start of the porn investigation in May last year, the four platforms have submitted co-ordinated commitments to address the concerns, but the Commission found those to be insufficient, two EU officials said.

The Commission is now discussing further remedies with the companies, although they are set to face fines for failing to take adequate measures in the past, the officials said.

Companies that fail to follow the EU digital rules face fines of up to 6 per cent of their global revenue, although the fines are rarely that high. The potential fines were first reported by MLex.

Brussels is simultaneously developing an EU-wide age-verification app that will allow all digital platforms, including porn websites, to confirm the age of a user without revealing additional personal information.

But it will take time to implement that technology, so the Commission is now discussing with the porn sites measures they can take to verify users’ ages in the transition phase. Any such measures would seek to avoid ongoing fines.

“We are looking into what we can accept,” one of the officials said.

The platforms have also raised concerns with the Commission that overly strict checks would lead adults to turn to lesser-known, smaller porn platforms which would be easier to access as they may have less strict age-verification systems.

To avoid this, EU member states have — in parallel with the EU probe — launched a co-ordinated crackdown on smaller platforms under national jurisdictions.

The companies did not immediately reply to a request for comment. The Commission declined to comment.

article_content_zh:
四个大型成人内容网站正在寻求与欧盟委员会就防止儿童访问色情内容达成协议，因为在欧盟推动保护未成年人上网的推动下，这些网站试图将即将到来的罚款降到最低。

该委员会正在调查 Pornhub、Stripchat、XNXX 和 XVideos 涉嫌违反《数字服务法》，因为它们未能充分保护儿童访问成人内容，因为未成年人只需一键声称自己已年满 18 岁即可访问色情平台。DSA 于 2024 年全面生效，是欧盟更广泛的数字规则手册的一部分，规定了科技公司应如何监管互联网。

该调查是欧洲保护未成年人在线行动的一部分，其中还包括一项禁止 13 岁以下儿童使用社交媒体、某些游戏平台和人工智能聊天机器人的提案。

两名欧盟官员表示，自去年 5 月开始色情调查以来，四大平台已提交协调承诺来解决这些问题，但欧盟委员会认为这些承诺还不够。

官员们表示，欧盟委员会目前正在与这些公司讨论进一步的补救措施，尽管它们将因过去未能采取适当措施而面临罚款。

不遵守欧盟数字规则的公司将面临高达其全球收入 6% 的罚款，尽管罚款很少这么高。 MLex 最先报道了可能的罚款。

布鲁塞尔正在同时开发一款欧盟范围内的年龄验证应用程序，该应用程序将允许包括色情网站在内的所有数字平台在不透露其他个人信息的情况下确认用户的年龄。

但实施这项技术需要时间，因此委员会现在正在与色情网站讨论在过渡阶段可以采取的措施来验证用户的年龄。任何此类措施都旨在避免持续的罚款。

“我们正在研究我们可以接受什么，”一位官员说。

这些平台还向委员会提出了担忧，认为过于严格的检查会导致成年人转向鲜为人知、规模较小的色情平台，这些平台可能更容易访问，因为它们的年龄验证系统可能不太严格。

为了避免这种情况，欧盟成员国在欧盟调查的同时，对国家管辖范围内的小型平台发起了协调一致的打击行动。

两家公司没有立即回复置评请求。该委员会拒绝发表评论。

title: Huawei says HarmonyOS has surpassed 100M installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, offering 460K+ apps and services from 12M+ registered developers (Iris Deng/South China Morning Post)
title_en: Huawei says HarmonyOS has surpassed 100M installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, offering 460K+ apps and services from 12M+ registered developers (Iris Deng/South China Morning Post)

inline_images.caption: The logo of Huawei during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai on July 6, 2023. Photo: AFP
inline_images.alt: The logo of Huawei during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai on July 6, 2023.

author: South China Morning Post
article_content:
Huawei Technologies has announced that HarmonyOS, its home-grown, Android-free operating system, has surpassed 100 million installations, marking a milestone in its effort to build a software ecosystem independent of Google’s mobile services amid US-led sanctions.

The Shenzhen-based firm said the total was reached this month across smartphones, tablets and personal computers running HarmonyOS 5, 6 and 7. Its ecosystem now offered more than 460,000 apps and services from over 12 million registered developers, according to a Huawei statement on Tuesday.

In a social media post on Tuesday, Richard Yu Chengdong, chairman of Huawei’s Consumer Business Group, called the achievement a “landmark moment” and said the ecosystem had crossed a “critical scale threshold”.

“It has officially entered a new phase of maturity, usability and innovation-driven growth,” Yu wrote on China’s social media platform Weibo, which is similar to X.

The milestone comes two years after Huawei debuted HarmonyOS 5 in 2024, its fully self-developed operating system designed to replace Android on the company’s devices. Adoption quickly grew alongside the Chinese tech giant’s strong comeback in the smartphone industry, powered by in-house semiconductors, as the US-sanctioned company stepped up efforts to achieve self-reliance in software and hardware.

In China, HarmonyOS was the second-largest smartphone operating system in the second quarter, accounting for 24 per cent of the market, ahead of the 18 per cent by Apple’s iOS, according to data by Counterpoint Research. Google’s Android still led the market with a 58 per cent share.

Globally, HarmonyOS had only a 5 per cent share in the second quarter, compared with Android’s 75 per cent share and iOS’s 20 per cent, as limited app compatibility continued to limit its reach.

Huawei planned to make a stronger push to expand HarmonyOS internationally, “gradually” bringing the operating system to the global market in the next one to three years, Yu told reporters in September.

Huawei first launched HarmonyOS in China in August 2019, months after Washington added the company to a trade blacklist that blocked access to products using US-origin technologies without explicit approval.

Early similarities in HarmonyOS’s kernel – the core of an operating system that manages how software interfaces with hardware – initially made it compatible with Android apps. But that started to change with HarmonyOS 5, also marketed as HarmonyOS Next.

title_zh: 华为鸿蒙系统装机量突破一亿大关
summary_zh: 华为宣布鸿蒙系统装机量超1亿，拥有超46万应用服务与1200万注册开发者，生态规模进入成熟期
article_content_zh:
华为技术有限公司宣布，其自主研发的、不含 Android 的操作系统 HarmonyOS 的安装量已超过 1 亿，这标志着华为在美国主导的制裁下构建独立于谷歌移动服务的软件生态系统的努力取得了里程碑式的进展。

这家总部位于深圳的公司表示，运行 HarmonyOS 5、6 和 7 的智能手机、平板电脑和个人电脑本月已达到这一目标。根据华为周二的声明，其生态系统目前提供了来自超过 1200 万注册开发者的超过 46 万个应用程序和服务。

华为消费者业务集团董事长余承东在周二的社交媒体帖子中称这一成就是“里程碑式的时刻”，并表示该生态系统已经跨越了“关键规模门槛”。

“它正式进入了成熟、可用性和创新驱动增长的新阶段，”余在中国社交媒体平台微博上写道，该平台与X类似。

这一里程碑是在华为于 2024 年推出 HarmonyOS 5 两年后实现的，这是其完全自主开发的操作系统，旨在取代该公司设备上的 Android。随着这家受到美国制裁的公司加紧努力实现软件和硬件的自力更生，随着这家中国科技巨头在内部半导体的推动下在智能手机行业的强劲复苏，采用率迅速增长。

Counterpoint Research 的数据显示，在中国，鸿蒙操作系统是第二季度第二大智能手机操作系统，占据 24% 的市场份额，领先于苹果 iOS 的 18%。谷歌的Android仍然以58%的份额领先市场。

在全球范围内，HarmonyOS 第二季度的份额仅为 5%，而 Android 的份额为 75%，iOS 为 20%，因为有限的应用程序兼容性继续限制了其覆盖范围。

余承东9月份对记者表示，华为计划加大力度推动HarmonyOS的国际扩张，在未来一到三年内“逐步”将该操作系统推向全球市场。

华为于 2019 年 8 月首次在中国推出 HarmonyOS，几个月前，华盛顿将该公司列入贸易黑名单，禁止未经明确批准使用美国原产技术的产品。

HarmonyOS 内核（管理软件与硬件交互方式的操作系统的核心）的早期相似之处最初使其与 Android 应用程序兼容。但随着 HarmonyOS 5（也以 HarmonyOS Next 的名称进行销售），这种情况开始发生变化。

title: Sources: Samsung and SK Hynix agree to adopt parts of YMTC's "Xtacking" tech for 3D NAND flash via cross-licensing deals, signaling YMTC's rapid tech progress (Nikkei Asia)
title_en: Sources: Samsung and SK Hynix agree to adopt parts of YMTC's "Xtacking" tech for 3D NAND flash via cross-licensing deals, signaling YMTC's rapid tech progress (Nikkei Asia)

inline_images.caption: Memory breakthrough by China's CXMT puts chip rivals on back foot
inline_images.alt: Memory breakthrough by China's CXMT puts chip rivals on back foot

inline_images.caption: Micron won't pursue 4F-squared memory chips despite CXMT's advance: CTO
inline_images.alt: Micron won't pursue 4F-squared memory chips despite CXMT's advance: CTO

author: Nikkei Asia
article_content:
TAIPEI/PALO ALTO/SEOUL -- The world's top memory chipmakers, South Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, are adopting chip-stacking technology first developed by Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., signaling how one of China's national champions has rapidly caught up with its larger semiconductor rivals and has built a substantial intellectual property portfolio.

Samsung and SK Hynix have been exploring stacking technologies for 3D NAND flash memory and, through cross-licensing deals, agreed they could adopt parts of related tech in Xtacking— a stacking technology developed by YMTC — three people briefed on the matter told Nikkei Asia.

Their move recognizes a significant breakthrough by YMTC, founded just a decade ago and now seen as playing a key role in helping China overcome its reliance on foreign chipmakers as the U.S. restricts exports of advanced products.

In Xtacking, first unveiled in 2018, memory cells and the "CMOS" circuits that control them are manufactured separately on two wafers before being bonded and connected together to form a 3D NAND flash memory chip.

This approach means each part can be produced and optimized independently, with the CMOS circuits manufactured using methods similar to those used for processor chips. YMTC has said it began mass-producing 3D NAND flash chips using Xtacking technology in 2019.

The Chinese company has filed more than 4,000 patent applications in the U.S. since 2018, with most covering 3D memory fabrication, semiconductor manufacturing processes and advanced chip packaging technologies, according to public records from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO). YMTC says it has filed more than 12,000 patents globally and has more than 8,000 engineers.

NAND flash memory is widely used in consumer electronics, computers and storage systems. With high storage capacity in small chips, it suits electronic devices like smartphones, laptops and game consoles that require fast, durable memory.

YMTC did not respond to requests for comment, and SK Hynix declined to comment. Samsung declined to comment on cross-licensing agreements, but told Nikkei Asia that bonding technology offered many advantages over conventional NAND flash manufacturing.

It “reduces structural limitations that may arise during stacking, enabling higher memory density” and “enables performance improvements and lower power consumption through the adoption of processes optimized for each component,” it said. The company added that “if applied to a wider range of products, it could enable large storage capacities even in thinner and lighter devices.” The world's top memory chipmaker said its latest V10 BV-NAND technology, unveiled last year, uses advanced wafer bonding to improve chip performance and manufacturing efficiency.

According to multiple industry experts, YMTC's approach gives chipmakers greater manufacturing flexibility by reducing the complexity of building both memory cells and logic circuits on a single wafer, and allowing them to outsource.

"Memory chipmakers can manufacture memory arrays in-house while outsourcing the logic portion of the chips to contract chipmaking partners," said Claire Wen, a senior analyst at the Omdia research firm. "This gives them greater flexibility in organizing production and allows them to tap more advanced logic chipmaking technologies without having to invest in all the necessary manufacturing capabilities themselves."

In the past, leading chipmakers saw little need to stack and bond two wafers together. But that thinking has gradually shifted, with such technologies increasingly seen as a key part of the future of NAND flash memory manufacturing, three people familiar with the matter told Nikkei Asia.

"Xtacking technologies are actually not that hard. The main reason the top chipmakers do cross-licensing with YMTC is just to avoid any legal disputes and because China's YMTC already filed a lot of patents around its stacking technologies," a chip industry executive told Nikkei Asia. "In a way, YMTC was fortunate to have adopted this technology, which has made it less vulnerable to U.S. export controls on advanced chipmaking equipment. Now, more leading chipmakers are moving toward similar approaches, with some even choosing to license parts of the technology from YMTC."

A manager at a component supplier to YMTC and Micron told Nikkei Asia that the Chinese memory chipmaker was smart to build a patent wall around its Xtacking technologies, even though manufacturing did not require advanced chipmaking equipment.

"It's not like Xtacking technologies are a must-go technological roadmap; however, if a memory chipmaker would like to take this approach, it would be hard to bypass YMTC's patents," said the source, who has direct knowledge of the cross-licensing matter.

The main global players in NAND are Samsung, SK Hynix, Japan's Kioxia, SanDisk and Micron in the U.S., and YMTC. It held a 14% market share in the April-June quarter, up from 11% a year earlier, and trailed only Samsung (28%) and SK Hynix (19%), while nearly matching Micron (15%) and Kioxia (14%), according to Counterpoint Research.

Longtime partners Kioxia and SanDisk unveiled their "CMOS directly Bonded to Array" (CBA) technology in 2023, a concept similar to YMTC's approach.

SanDisk chief technology officer Alper Ilkbahar told Nikkei Asia that rather than building all the structures on a single wafer, fabricating the two parts separately means each wafer can be optimized for its specific functions before being bonded, improving overall performance.

"By using CBA, we are able to really drive and optimize the memory and then the circuits [performance] independently," Ilkbahar said. "We could get very reliable, high-performance memory array, and we could get a very high-performance CMOS [logic chips]." He said he believed all of its rivals were looking into hybrid bonding technologies.

YMTC has become more aggressive in asserting its intellectual property rights in recent years, filing lawsuits against Micron for allegedly violating its patents involving NAND flash memory and DRAM technologies in both the U.S. and Europe. The American memory chipmaker has challenged the validity of YMTC's claims.

The Chinese company sued Micron in California over eight 3D NAND patents in 2023, and by July this year, it had filed U.S. suits covering 27 patents, along with 295 patent claims in courts in China, the U.S., the U.K., Germany and elsewhere in Europe against its U.S. rival.On Sept.18, the Munich I Regional Court found Micron infringed two YMTC German utility models and ordered an injunction covering related product sales in Germany. It was YMTC's first substantive injunction win, although Micron is appealing. Also in September, Micron sued YMTC in its home state of Idaho, alleging the Chinese company poached Micron engineers and turned their know-how into patents later used against Micron. Micron will start using its own wafer-on-wafer bonding technology in its next-generation 3D NAND flash memory G11, scheduled to enter mass production in the second half of 2027.In an interview with Nikkei Asia in late October, Scott DeBoer, Micron's president and chief technology officer, said, "Every company will implement and has had the opportunity to choose to implement wafer bonding on NAND for the past 10 years; Micron will implement wafer bonding at the time when it actually provides a strategic advantage. With growing demand to meet AI workloads, wafer bonding would provide that advantage for G11 products"

YMTC filed for an initial public offering in August through its parent holding company, CCSH Corp. It is also building new facilities in the Chinese city of Wuhan, with plans to expand NAND flash memory production and also enter the market for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, which are used in a wide range of electronic devices.

Nikkei Asia previously reported that YMTC was embarking on its most aggressive expansion to date, alongside fellow Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT. YMTC has also been among the most aggressive Chinese chipmakers in localizing procurement of its semiconductor equipment, seeking to reduce its reliance on U.S. technology and minimize the risk of production disruptions caused by Washington's export restrictions, Nikkei first reported.

article_content_zh:
台北/帕洛阿尔托/首尔——世界顶级存储芯片制造商韩国三星电子和 SK 海力士正在采用长江存储科技有限公司首先开发的芯片堆叠技术，这标志着中国的国家冠军之一如何迅速赶上其更大的半导体竞争对手，并建立了丰富的知识产权组合。

三名知情人士告诉《日经亚洲》，三星和 SK 海力士一直在探索 3D NAND 闪存的堆叠技术，并通过交叉许可协议，同意他们可以在 Xtacking（长江存储开发的堆叠技术）中采用部分相关技术。

他们的举动认可了长江存储的重大突破。该公司成立于十年前，现在被视为在美国限制先进产品出口之际帮助中国克服对外国芯片制造商的依赖方面发挥着关键作用。

在 2018 年首次推出的 Xtacking 中，存储单元和控制它们的“CMOS”电路分别在两个晶圆上制造，然后粘合并连接在一起形成 3D NAND 闪存芯片。

这种方法意味着每个部件都可以独立生产和优化，并且使用与处理器芯片类似的方法制造 CMOS 电路。长江存储表示，已于 2019 年开始使用 Xtacking 技术批量生产 3D NAND 闪存芯片。

根据美国专利商标局 (USPTO) 的公开记录，自 2018 年以来，这家中国公司已在美国提交了 4,000 多项专利申请，其中大多数涉及 3D 内存制造、半导体制造工艺和先进芯片封装技术。长江存储表示，该公司已在全球申请了超过 12,000 项专利，拥有超过 8,000 名工程师。

NAND闪存广泛应用于消费电子、计算机和存储系统。它采用小芯片实现高存储容量，适合需要快速、耐用内存的智能手机、笔记本电脑和游戏机等电子设备。

长江存储没有回应置评请求，SK 海力士也拒绝置评。三星拒绝就交叉许可协议发表评论，但告诉《日经亚洲》，键合技术比传统 NAND 闪存制造具有许多优势。

它“减少了堆叠过程中可能出现的结构限制，从而实现更高的存储密度”，并且“通过采用针对每个组件优化的工艺来提高性能并降低功耗”。该公司补充说，“如果应用于更广泛的产品，即使在更薄、更轻的设备中，它也可以实现大存储容量。”这家全球顶级存储芯片制造商表示，其去年推出的最新 V10 BV-NAND 技术采用先进的晶圆键合技术来提高芯片性能和制造效率。

多位行业专家表示，长江存储的方法通过降低在单个晶圆上构建存储单元和逻辑电路的复杂性并允许他们外包，为芯片制造商提供了更大的制造灵活性。

Omdia 研究公司的高级分析师 Claire Wen 表示：“内存芯片制造商可以在内部制造内存阵列，同时将芯片的逻辑部分外包给芯片制造合作伙伴。” “这使他们在组织生产方面具有更大的灵活性，并使他们能够利用更先进的逻辑芯片制造技术，而无需自己投资所有必要的制造能力。”

过去，领先的芯片制造商认为很少需要将两个晶圆堆叠和键合在一起。但三位知情人士告诉《日经亚洲》，这种想法已经逐渐转变，此类技术越来越被视为 NAND 闪存制造未来的关键部分。

“Xtacking技术实际上并不难。顶级芯片制造商与长江存储进行交叉许可的主要原因只是为了避免任何法律纠纷，而且因为中国的长江存储已经围绕其堆叠技术申请了大量专利，”一位芯片行业高管告诉《日经亚洲》。 “在某种程度上，长江存储很幸运地采用了这项技术，这使其不易受到美国对先进芯片制造设备的出口管制的影响。现在，更多领先的芯片制造商正在采取类似的方法，有些甚至选择从长江存储获得部分技术的许可。”

长江存储和美光一家零部件供应商的经理告诉《日经亚洲》，这家中国存储芯片制造商很聪明，围绕其 Xtacking 技术建立了专利墙，尽管制造过程并不需要先进的芯片制造设备。

【关键技术规格】三星与SK海力士通过交叉许可协议采纳长江存储Xtacking架构。
【各方立场与态度】该事件确立了中国厂商在闪存核心知识产权领域的技术话语权。

title: Amazon Targets UK Car Buyers Being Reeled In by Chinese Brands
title_en: Amazon Targets UK Car Buyers Being Reeled In by Chinese Brands
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
The boss of Amazon Autos believes there is plenty of room for more competition in the UK car advertising market as the retail giant prepares to take on Autotrader.

Speaking exclusively to Car Dealer in a video interview you can watch above, Matt Nuffort, director of Amazon Autos International, said he was undeterred by the number of established automotive marketplaces already operating in Britain.

Amazon has today confirmed it will launch its car advertising platform in the UK in early 2027, with Hyundai and listed dealer group Vertu among its first partners.

Asked directly by Car Dealer whether Autotrader should be worried about Amazon’s arrival, Nuffort said: ‘It’s a really large market and I think there’s a lot of room for many different competitors.’

However, he played down suggestions Amazon was targeting a particular position in the UK market.

Asked whether Amazon would be happy being a dominant number two or whether it was coming to Britain to be number one, he said: ‘We really don’t think in those terms.

‘We think in terms of, are we serving customers? And if we’re doing that, then I think we’ll be successful.’

Nuffort believes one of Amazon’s biggest advantages is the familiarity consumers already have with its technology.

‘We’re really offering Amazon technology, our digital storefront, to dealers to reach a wider set of customers,’ he said.

‘Customers often are already logged in. They already have the Amazon app. They’re familiar with the experience. Amazon Autos will look and feel like Amazon to them.’

While Amazon Autos will initially focus on franchised car dealers in the UK, Nuffort opened the door to independent used car dealers eventually being able to advertise their stock on the platform.

He revealed Amazon had already held talks with a number of businesses and trade associations.

‘Initially, we’re focused on franchise dealers who offer new cars. But we have talked to a number of independent dealers and associations,’ he told Car Dealer.

‘I know that there are many independent dealers, I’m sure, like yourself, that deliver a great customer experience.

‘So that’s the number one thing that we’re looking for – a dealer who is as excited about delivering a great customer experience as we are.’

He added that dealers would need to have the technology and processes in place to ensure customers received a good experience after leaving Amazon’s platform.

Nuffort said Amazon wanted to offer customers a wide selection of cars and dealers, and said the firm wanted to ‘open it up to a much wider set of dealers over time’.

Amazon has also established a UK dealer council to help shape its offering ahead of launch and has been working with dealers both large and small.

Nuffort declined to reveal how much Amazon Autos would charge UK car dealers to advertise on the platform or precisely how its charging model would work.

However, he revealed Amazon was developing new advertising tools specifically for the automotive sector.

‘I can’t disclose precise commercials, but what I can say is that Amazon makes money when we deliver additional customers to the dealership,’ he said.

‘We are developing new advertising tools for this space to give dealers and brands the ability to reach a new set of customers on Amazon.’

Asked about the backlash from some UK car dealers following Autotrader’s introduction of its Deal Builder product, Nuffort said Amazon’s success would be dependent on that of its dealer partners.

He said dealers would ‘vote with their pounds’ and choose products that made sense for their businesses. Amazon’s aim, he added, was to give dealers the ability to reach a wider set of customers more efficiently than they do today.

One of the more contentious issues among UK used car dealers is the use of price indicators by online advertising platforms.

Asked whether Amazon Autos would use price flags, Nuffort acknowledged concerns in the motor trade about a ‘race to the bottom’.

He told Car Dealer: ‘It’s one that we’ve talked a lot about internally and with dealers and brands because, of course, the industry, it’s a low-margin industry, lots of competition and everybody’s worried about a race to the bottom.’

He said Amazon wanted to highlight good deals to consumers but pointed out that it did not do so across all its stock in America.

Interestingly, Nuffort also revealed Amazon had adapted its search algorithm for its automotive business to take into account the distance customers were from car dealerships.

He said the majority of customers who start their car purchase on Amazon in America do so with a dealer within 30 miles.

‘Our search algorithm now accounts for distance,’ he said. ‘Customers do have a preference to purchase from a dealer who’s close to them because they want to service the car there too.’

Asked how quickly Amazon Autos could reach scale in the UK, Nuffort admitted he did not know.

He said Amazon would listen to feedback from consumers, car dealers and manufacturers after launch and evolve the platform accordingly.

He added: ‘It’s a challenging space, but it’s a great product, great industry. And we’re excited to be coming to the UK.’

You can watch our full exclusive interview with Nuffort in the video at the top of this post.

亚马逊汽车公司的老板认为，随着这家零售巨头准备与 Autotrader 竞争，英国汽车广告市场还有很大的竞争空间。

亚马逊汽车国际总监马特·纳福特 (Matt Nuffort) 在上面的视频采访中接受《汽车经销商》独家采访时表示，他并没有因为已经在英国运营的成熟汽车市场的数量而被吓倒。

亚马逊今天确认将于 2027 年初在英国推出汽车广告平台，现代汽车和上市经销商集团 Vertu 是其首批合作伙伴。

当被《汽车经销商》直接问及 Autotrader 是否应该担心亚马逊的到来时，纳福特表示：“这是一个非常大的市场，我认为对于许多不同的竞争对手来说，有很大的空间。”

当被问及亚马逊是否愿意成为第二大市场，或者是否愿意在英国成为第一大市场时，他说：“我们真的不这么想。”

纳福特认为，亚马逊最大的优势之一是消费者对其技术的熟悉程度。

他说：“我们实际上是在向经销商提供亚马逊技术、我们的数字店面，以接触更广泛的客户。”

“顾客通常已经登录。他们已经安装了亚马逊应用程序。他们熟悉这种经历。对他们来说，亚马逊汽车的外观和感觉都像亚马逊。

虽然亚马逊汽车最初将专注于英国的特许汽车经销商，但纳福特为独立二手车经销商最终能够在该平台上宣传他们的库存打开了大门。

他透露，亚马逊已经与多家企业和行业协会进行了会谈。

“最初，我们专注于提供新车的特许经销商。但我们已经与一些独立经销商和协会进行了交谈，”他告诉《汽车经销商》。

“我知道有很多独立经销商，我确信，像您一样，可以提供出色的客户体验。

title: ‘Tech bros strike back’ as Donald Trump rescues Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
title_en: ‘Tech bros strike back’ as Donald Trump rescues Nvidia’s Jensen Huang

inline_images.caption: Tech investors, including Gavin Baker, made entreaties on Huang’s behalf to US officials © Eva Marie Uzcategui/Bloomberg
inline_images.alt: Tech investors, including Gavin Baker, made entreaties on Huang’s behalf to US officials © Eva Marie Uzcategui/Bloomberg

inline_images.caption: People close to vice-president JD Vance were keen to stress that his ‘stature’ in the tech world helped seal Huang’s return © Finn Gomez/Getty Images
inline_images.alt: People close to vice-president JD Vance were keen to stress that his ‘stature’ in the tech world helped seal Huang’s return © Finn Gomez/Getty Images

inline_images.caption: Attorney-general Todd Blanche assured Trump that the Department of Justice had ‘no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Jensen Huang or Nvidia’ © Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg
inline_images.alt: Attorney-general Todd Blanche assured Trump that the Department of Justice had ‘no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Jensen Huang or Nvidia’ © Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg

author: Joe Miller, Alex Rogers, Ella Lee, Claire Jones, and George Hammond
article_content:
Silicon Valley’s alliance with Donald Trump’s White House looked broken this month, after voters punished Republicans and Big Tech donors, markets soured on AI and the boss of America’s biggest chipmaker went down in a spy scandal.

But in a single weekend, Trump’s tech allies reasserted their power in Washington, lobbying the commander-in-chief to defy his own intelligence agencies and lean on Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang as chief executive.

“The return of Jensen is the tech bros striking back,” said a former Trump official.

Tech investors, including Gavin Baker, Brad Gerstner and Marc Andreessen, made entreaties on Huang’s behalf to officials including US vice-president JD Vance, who has deep ties to Silicon Valley.

Together they convinced the president that Huang was crucial to keeping the AI boom going, and Vance helped lobby Nvidia’s board to accept his return as CEO.

Silicon Valley figures proved they “still clearly have the president’s ear on these issues”, the person added.

However, Huang’s reinstatement could store up trouble for his allies in Trump’s orbit, since the Nvidia CEO still faces investigations that could unearth evidence that would tarnish his defenders.

Their victory came despite alarm among many Republicans about the national security implications of Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy. It was a setback for secretary of state Marco Rubio, who reportedly issued a memo to Trump officials warning of Huang’s close relationship with the woman.

Rubio, also Trump’s national security adviser, did not respond to a shouted request for comment during a brief appearance with the Qatari prime minister on Monday.

Trump was convinced to back Huang’s reinstatement by the plunge in tech stocks and warnings the US risked recession without Huang, which overrode security considerations, people familiar with the matter said.

Attorney-general Todd Blanche also assured the president that the Department of Justice had “no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Jensen Huang or Nvidia”, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Trump then repeated tech billionaires’ talking points about Huang’s singular importance to the economy in an hour-long TV interview with CNBC on Monday.

As tech shares temporarily surged in the wake of the Nvidia news, people close to Vance — a Peter Thiel protégé who has publicly kept his distance from AI billionaires since assuming office — were keen to stress that his “stature” in the tech world helped seal the deal.

They said the White House came to believe that Huang had been targeted by opponents in the AI industry because he championed open-source AI models, which are a threat to the business models of OpenAI and Anthropic.

Trump, who has defended Huang throughout the scandal, was increasingly receptive to such arguments, according to people familiar with the matter.

“I think Jensen . . . has played Trump like a very adept fiddler — gifts and garlands and flattery — he’s lauded him and heaped him with the praise Trump likes so much,” said one veteran Silicon Valley investor.

Huang, who donated $25mn to the president’s ballroom project last year and credited him with fuelling the AI boom, “can thank Trump entirely for being reinstated”, the investor added. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

Tech figures were quick to cheer Huang’s return, and dismiss fears about his conduct. “I hate to break it to you, but there are double standards for high performers,” venture capitalist and tech podcaster Jason Calacanis told Fox News.

Outside the Oval Office, however, anger was mounting among the Maga faithful.

“On Sunday, the Director of National Intelligence told the public there were multiple investigations into Nvidia and Jensen Huang. Monday morning, he is reinstated,” Steve Bannon, Trump’s former chief strategist, told the FT, referring to comments made by Jay Clayton over the weekend. “I think we may have just nationalised Nvidia.”

The whole Nvidia affair smacked of “absolute blazing corruption”, said Ryan Girdusky, a Maga-aligned political strategist and commentator. “Either we’re a country of laws or a country where billionaire tech people are allowed to do whatever they want.”

“We’re gonna have this bump in the market that could probably go away tomorrow,” he said of the surge in US stocks following Monday’s Nvidia news. “I don’t know why you would take ownership of [Huang’s reinstatement] . . . I would be distancing myself from it.”

His comments proved prescient as Nvidia stock closed down nearly 6 per cent on Tuesday, leading a 2 per cent drop in the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100.

Few senior Republicans besides Vance publicly backed Trump’s move to rescue Huang. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent, who previously accused Nvidia of trying to “goose their revenues and their earnings” via “seemingly illicit sales”, did not come out in support of Huang’s return, although he did appear to retract some of his criticism in a TV appearance on the Sunday before Nvidia’s announcement.

Huang’s friends in the administration also distanced themselves. A person close to Trump’s former AI tsar David Sacks — an important ally of Huang’s in Big Tech’s fight against stringent AI regulation — said he had not been involved “in any way” in the lobbying of the president over the weekend.

A person close to commerce secretary Howard Lutnick, who brokered Huang’s introduction to Trump in 2025 and has remained close to the Nvidia executive, said he too had played no part.

On Monday, the commerce department blacklisted Megaspeed, the company that formerly employed Huang’s paramour Alice Huang, citing “significant risk of [the company] being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorized . . . end users”.

Huang’s few remaining allies in Washington also fear his resurrection may prove shortlived.

Congressional Republicans who once would have fallen into line behind the president’s decision made it clear that they would continue to investigate Nvidia and its chief executive. Several vowed to back tighter chip export controls in the must-pass defence budget bill, known as the NDAA.

If that fails, Democrats, who will be in the majority in both houses of Congress in January, might get enough Republicans onside for measures targeting Nvidia to override a veto from the president, a person working on legislation with Republicans said.

“You’re likely to see China hawk fury in Congress only grow,” the former Trump official said. “And they will lash out through things like the upcoming NDAA.”
content_snippet: Silicon Valley elites flexed their muscles in Washington to back Nvidia boss after humbling midterms defeat.

article_content_zh:
在选民惩罚共和党人和大型科技捐助者、市场对人工智能的态度恶化以及​​美国最大芯片制造商的老板陷入间谍丑闻之后，硅谷与唐纳德·特朗普领导的白宫的联盟本月似乎破裂了。

但仅仅一个周末，特朗普的科技盟友就在华盛顿重申了他们的权力，游说这位总司令藐视自己的情报机构，并依靠英伟达重新任命黄仁勋为首席执行官。

“詹森的回归是科技兄弟的反击，”一位前特朗普官员表示。

加文·贝克(Gavin Baker)、布拉德·格斯特纳(Brad Gerstner)和马克·安德森(Marc Andreessen)等科技投资者代表黄仁勋向美国副总统万斯(JD Vance)等官员提出请求，万斯与硅谷有着深厚的联系。

他们一起让总统相信黄仁勋对于保持人工智能繁荣至关重要，万斯帮助游说英伟达董事会接受他再次担任首席执行官。

这位人士补充说，硅谷的数据证明他们“在这些问题上仍然清楚地听取了总统的意见”。

然而，黄仁勋的复职可能会给他在特朗普轨道上的盟友带来麻烦，因为这位英伟达首席执行官仍然面临调查，可能会发现有损其支持者形象的证据。

尽管许多共和党人对黄与一名疑似中国间谍的恋情对国家安全的影响感到震惊，但他们还是取得了胜利。这对国务卿马可·卢比奥来说是一个挫折，据报道，他向特朗普官员发出了一份备忘录，警告黄与这名女性的密切关系。

卢比奥也是特朗普的国家安全顾问，他在周一与卡塔尔首相短暂会面时没有回应置评请求。

知情人士称，特朗普因科技股暴跌而确信支持黄仁勋复职，并警告说，没有黄仁勋，美国将面临经济衰退的风险，这超越了安全考虑。

司法部长托德·布兰奇还向总统保证，司法部“没有证据表明黄仁勋或英伟达有任何不当行为”。

随后，特朗普在周一接受 CNBC 长达一小时的电视采访时，重申了科技亿万富翁关于黄仁勋对经济的非凡重要性的观点。

英伟达的消息传出后，科技股暂时飙升，与万斯关系密切的人士——彼得·蒂尔的门徒，自上任以来一直公开与人工智能亿万富翁保持距离——热衷于强调他在科技界的“地位”帮助达成了这笔交易。

他们表示，白宫开始相信黄仁勋已成为人工智能行业反对者的目标，因为他支持开源人工智能模型，这对 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的商业模式构成了威胁。

title: NJ-based AidenAI, which helps enterprises integrate AI into apps, data infrastructure, and business workflows, raised a $32M Series A led by A91 Partners (Anne Florentyna/Inc42)
