author: Inc42
article_content:
Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment firm A91 Partners, as it looks to expand its AI platform and engineering capabilities. The fresh capital will be used to invest in its platform and engineering talent as it looks to scale its global enterprise AI business.

“With A91 as our partner, we are excited to invest in our people and platforms and help shape the next wave of enterprise technology services,” AidenAI founder and CEO Srinivas Kamadi said. How AidenAI Builds Its Enterprise AI Business Kamadi founded AidenAI in 2023 after spending nearly two decades with Infosys.

Drawing on his experience of leading digital transformation at the company, Kamadi launched AidenAI to solve a recurring bottleneck faced by large enterprises: enterprise AI was stuck in the experimentation phase because outdated legacy systems made digital transformation too slow.

The New Jersey-based startup, whose majority of workforce is based out of Hyderabad, helps large enterprises integrate AI into existing applications, data infrastructure and business workflows. Its proprietary AI Builder Platform is designed to help businesses move beyond AI experimentation and deploy AI applications within their existing tech infrastructure.

This platform connects with an enterprise's existing systems and AI models, providing tools for AI agents. The startup also offers AiDAP, an AI-driven technology modernisation platform that helps enterprises modernise legacy software systems. This positions AidenAI in the enterprise AI implementation market, where businesses are increasingly looking for solutions to integrate AI into business-critical operations rather than deploy standalone tools.

“While enterprise AI adoption is still in its early stages, AidenAI has spent the last 3 years helping over 30 large enterprises turn the promise of AI into live, measurable business outcomes," said A91 Partners' partner Kaushik Anand. AidenAI's Bet On Frontier AI Engineering Alongside its platform expansion, AidenAI plans to build a team of more than 1,000 frontier AI engineers through its AidenAI Builder Academy.

The academy is designed to develop forward-deployed engineering talent that can work directly with enterprise clients to build and deploy production-ready AI applications using the company's platform and frontier AI models. The expansion comes as enterprises increasingly explore agentic AI applications to automate complex, multi-step workflows across functions such as finance, insurance, healthcare and human resources.

AidenAI aims to tap this demand by combining AI agents, enterprise software modernisation and specialised engineering services. This comes as the broader Indian enterprise AI market, which was valued at $11 Bn in 2025, is projected to reach $71 Bn by 2030, according to Inc42’s Bharat AI Startups Report 2026.

The Inc42 Take: Can AidenAI Scale Its Enterprise AI Platform? As more companies adopt GenAI in their daily operations, demand is growing for providers that can build and deploy AI solutions at an enterprise scale. AidenAI is positioning itself at this intersection via its AI Builder Platform and engineering-led deployment model.

Its presence across six countries and a client base of over 30 enterprises provide an early indication of market traction. However, the startup’s ability to scale will depend on how effectively it can standardise its platform across enterprise customers with different technology infrastructure and business requirements.

article_content_zh:
企业人工智能初创公司 AidenAI 在成长投资公司 A91 Partners 领投的 A 轮融资中筹集了 3200 万美元（297.1 卢比），该公司希望扩大其人工智能平台和工程能力。新资金将用于投资其平台和工程人才，以扩大其全球企业人工智能业务。

AidenAI 创始人兼首席执行官 Srinivas Kamadi 表示：“与 A91 作为我们的合作伙伴，我们很高兴能够投资于我们的人员和平台，并帮助塑造下一波企业技术服务浪潮。” AidenAI 如何构建企业人工智能业务 Kamadi 在 Infosys 工作了近二十年后，于 2023 年创立了 AidenAI。

凭借在公司领导数字化转型的经验，Kamadi 推出了 AidenAI，以解决大型企业经常面临的瓶颈：企业 AI 因过时的遗留系统导致数字化转型速度过慢而陷入实验阶段。

这家总部位于新泽西州的初创公司的大部分员工都在海得拉巴，帮助大型企业将人工智能集成到现有应用程序、数据基础设施和业务工作流程中。其专有的 AI Builder 平台旨在帮助企业超越人工智能实验，并在现有技术基础设施中部署人工智能应用程序。

该平台连接企业现有系统和AI模型，为AI代理提供工具。该初创公司还提供 AiDAP，这是一个人工智能驱动的技术现代化平台，可帮助企业实现遗留软件系统的现代化。这将 AidenAI 定位于企业人工智能实施市场，企业越来越多地寻求将人工智能集成到关键业务运营中的解决方案，而不是部署独立的工具。

A91 Partners 的合伙人 Kaushik Anand 表示：“虽然企业人工智能的采用仍处于早期阶段，但 AidenAI 在过去 3 年里帮助 30 多家大型企业将人工智能的承诺转化为现实的、可衡量的业务成果。” AidenAI 押注前沿人工智能工程 除了平台扩展之外，AidenAI 还计划通过其 AidenAI Builder Academy 建立一支由 1,000 多名前沿人工智能工程师组成的团队。

该学院旨在培养前沿部署的工程人才，他们可以直接与企业客户合作，使用公司的平台和前沿人工智能模型构建和部署可立即投入生产的人工智能应用程序。随着企业越来越多地探索代理人工智能应用程序，以实现金融、保险、医疗保健和人力资源等职能部门复杂的多步骤工作流程的自动化，这种扩张也随之而来。

AidenAI 旨在通过结合人工智能代理、企业软件现代化和专业工程服务来满足这一需求。据 Inc42 的《2026 年巴拉特人工智能初创公司报告》称，更广泛的印度企业人工智能市场在 2025 年估值为 110 亿美元，预计到 2030 年将达到 710 亿美元。

Inc42 观点：AidenAI 能否扩展其企业人工智能平台？随着越来越多的公司在日常运营中采用 GenAI，对能够在企业规模构建和部署 AI 解决方案的提供商的需求不断增长。 AidenAI 通过其 AI Builder 平台和工程主导的部署模型将自己定位在这个十字路口。

它在六个国家的业务和超过 30 家企业的客户群提供了市场吸引力的早期迹象。然而，初创公司的扩展能力将取决于它如何有效地在具有不同技术基础设施和业务需求的企业客户之间标准化其平台。

title: EU plans €50bn tech fund to close gap with US and China
title_en: EU plans €50bn tech fund to close gap with US and China
author: Barbara Moens
article_content:
The EU is drawing up plans to mobilise up to €50bn for a new fund that would make long-term, high-risk investments in European artificial intelligence and quantum computing companies, as Brussels seeks to reduce its dependence on US and Chinese technology.

The proposed Sovereign Tech Equity Fund (Stef) would make larger, riskier and longer-term investments than existing EU financing schemes, according to two officials involved in the discussions.

“These are long-term, stable investments in risky stuff,” one of the officials said. “It’s the opposite of what the EU usually does, which is exactly why we need it.”

The main focus of the investments will be in AI and quantum, which applies the principles of quantum mechanics to carry out calculations that are extremely difficult for conventional computers. The Commission will present a quantum strategy on Wednesday as it hopes to strengthen the bloc’s position in the emerging industry.

The new fund plans are part of a broader push to strengthen Europe’s technological independence amid growing uncertainty over US policy and an increasingly volatile geopolitical landscape.

Brussels also hopes to spur investment in emerging technologies where European companies have struggled to compete with their American and Chinese rivals. Stef investing in a company would encourage other investors to follow, the officials said.

Europe’s inability to fund and scale innovative tech companies is often cited as a key reason for the EU lagging behind the US and China, including in Mario Draghi’s recommendations on how to improve the bloc’s competitiveness.

European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen promised an “ambitious proposal” to finance initiatives aimed at bolstering the bloc’s “tech sovereignty” after a discussion among leaders on AI earlier this month.

The goal is set to present operational details of the new fund in February, the officials said, when EU leaders will discuss the bloc’s competitiveness at a retreat in the Belgian town of Alden Biesen.

The precise financing of the fund is still being discussed. The Commission aims to use EU funds as seed money that would attract additional investment from the private sector, with the aim to mobilise as much as €6 for every euro committed, one of the officials said.

EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen already discussed the fund idea with the European Investment Bank last week. The bank could provide financial expertise without carrying the investment risk itself.

Virkkunen said at a conference last week the fund should aim to attract €50bn, which is a 10th of what the Commission estimates it will cost to achieve full tech sovereignty.

As with an existing Scaleup Europe Fund, Stef would be managed by an independent fund manager to ensure investment decisions were not subject to any political considerations.

Scaleup, which is available for the wider European tech sector, is managed by the Swedish private equity firm EQT and has a much lower fundraising target of €5bn.

article_content_zh:
欧盟正在制定计划，筹集高达 500 亿欧元的资金，用于对欧洲人工智能和量子计算公司进行长期、高风险投资，以减少对美国和中国技术的依赖。

参与讨论的两名官员表示，拟议中的主权科技股权基金（Stef）将比现有的欧盟融资计划进行规模更大、风险更高、期限更长的投资。

一位官员表示：“这些都是对高风险资产的长期、稳定投资。” “这与欧盟通常的做法相反，这正是我们需要它的原因。”

投资的主要重点将是人工智能和量子，它应用量子力学原理来进行传统计算机极其困难的计算。欧盟委员会将于周三提出量子战略，希望加强欧盟在新兴行业的地位。

在美国政策的不确定性日益增加以及地缘政治格局日益动荡的情况下，新的基金计划是加强欧洲技术独立性的更广泛努力的一部分。

布鲁塞尔还希望刺激对新兴技术的投资，欧洲公司在这些技术上一直难以与美国和中国的竞争对手竞争。官员们表示，Stef 投资一家公司将鼓励其他投资者效仿。

欧洲无力资助和扩大创新科技公司的规模常常被认为是欧盟落后于美国和中国的一个关键原因，马里奥·德拉吉(Mario Draghi)关于如何提高欧盟竞争力的建议也是如此。

在本月早些时候领导人就人工智能进行讨论后，欧盟委员会主席乌苏拉·冯德莱恩承诺提出一项“雄心勃勃的提案”，为旨在加强欧盟“技术主权”的举措提供资金。

官员们表示，目标是在二月份公布新基金的运营细节，届时欧盟领导人将在比利时阿尔登比森镇举行的一次务虚会上讨论欧盟的竞争力。

该基金的具体融资事宜仍在讨论中。一位官员表示，欧盟委员会的目标是利用欧盟资金作为种子资金，吸引私营部门的额外投资，目标是每承诺一欧元就筹集最多 6 欧元。

欧盟科技主管 Henna Virkkunen 上周已与欧洲投资银行讨论了该基金的想法。银行可以提供金融专业知识，而无需承担投资风险。

Virkkunen 在上周的一次会议上表示，该基金的目标应该是吸引 500 亿欧元，这是委员会估计实现全面技术主权所需成本的十分之一。

与现有的 Scaleup Europe 基金一样，Stef 将由独立基金经理管理，以确保投资决策不受任何政治考虑。

Scaleup 面向更广泛的欧洲科技行业，由瑞典私募股权公司 EQT 管理，其融资目标要低得多，为 50 亿欧元。

title: How Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent
title_en: How Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent
author: Julia Boorstin
article_content:
Meta' s ad-free Muse personal artificial intelligence agent is already helping the social media giant boost its advertising business, and it's happening through Instagram, multiple people told CNBC.

Instagram is a major advertising revenue engine for the social media giant, and the company is leveraging existing habits on the platform by prompting users to organize their saved posts in Muse.

About 20% of daily Instagram users save at least one post to the app per day, according to a person familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because the information is not public. Many of those saved items, the person said, are either shoppable items or ads.

A senior executive told CNBC that Muse, even without ads, "is still very valuable for our ads business because it raises conversions for advertisers."It does this by reducing friction in the shopping process and allowing users to go back to items later, said the executive, who asked not to be named because the details have not been reported publicly.

"It gives advertisers a way to get more ROI for the dollars they're already spending, and that's all because Muse is helping people shop,"the executive said.

Mark Zuckerberg announced in Meta's last earnings call that 25% of Muse's users shop via the agentic tool — it's the most common use case for Muse — and the average purchase price is over $200. Zuckerberg said the company plans to take a small fee from transactions made through the agentic platform.

All that information about what people are shopping for with their agent is a valuable asset to target ads more precisely within Instagram. If consumers complete purchases with their Muse, that builds Meta's new revenue stream.

Meta's efforts to drive transactions seem to be paying off, and the buzz around Muse has made it a leader in agentic shopping.

In the week ending Nov. 22, 51% of all agentic orders were done by Meta's Muse, according to transactions measured by Forter Intelligence, an e-commerce analytics and cybertechnology company.

Meta dominates agentic AI shopping market share, according to Forter, which said that SpaceX 's Grok held a 24% market share in that same time period, followed by 22% to OpenAI's ChatGPT. The remaining 3% is divided between Google and startup Instinct.

Meta is expected to eventually launch ads in Muse, though multiple people said that it's not under any financial pressure to do so and tends to take its time building an audience before monetizing it.

The people said that putting ads in the Muse feed, which is more akin to a newsfeed instead of responses to specific queries, would be a natural way for Meta to test ads on the platform.

article_content_zh:
许多人告诉 CNBC，Meta 的无广告 Muse 个人人工智能代理已经在帮助这家社交媒体巨头推动其广告业务，而且是通过 Instagram 实现的。

Instagram 是这家社交媒体巨头的主要广告收入引擎，该公司正在利用该平台上的现有习惯，提示用户在 Muse 中整理他们保存的帖子。

一位高管告诉 CNBC，即使没有广告，Muse“对我们的广告业务仍然非常有价值，因为它可以提高广告商的转化率。”这位高管表示，它通过减少购物过程中的摩擦并允许用户稍后返回商品来做到这一点。这位高管要求匿名，因为详细信息尚未公开报道。

这位高管表示：“它为广告商提供了一种让他们已经投入的资金获得更多投资回报率的方法，而这一切都是因为 Muse 正在帮助人们购物。”

马克·扎克伯格在 Meta 的上次财报电话会议上宣布，25% 的 Muse 用户通过代理工具进行购物——这是 Muse 最常见的用例——平均购买价格超过 200 美元。扎克伯格表示，该公司计划从通过代理平台进行的交易中收取少量费用。

所有有关人们通过代理购物的信息都是宝贵的资产，可以在 Instagram 中更准确地定位广告。如果消费者用他们的 Muse 完成购买，这将建立 Meta 的新收入来源。

Meta 推动交易的努力似乎得到了回报，围绕 Muse 的热议使其成为代理购物领域的领导者。

根据电子商务分析和网络技术公司 Forter Intelligence 测量的交易数据，截至 11 月 22 日的一周，所有代理订单的 51% 是由 Meta 的 Muse 完成的。

据 Forter 称，Meta 在代理人工智能购物市场份额中占据主导地位，同时 SpaceX 的 Grok 占据了 24% 的市场份额，其次是 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 的 22%。剩下的 3% 由谷歌和初创公司 Instinct 瓜分。

Meta 预计最终将在 Muse 上推出广告，不过多位人士表示，Meta 这样做并没有任何财务压力，并且倾向于在货币化之前花些时间建立受众群体。

知情人士表示，将广告放入 Muse feed 中（这更类似于新闻源，而不是对特定查询的响应）将是 Meta 在平台上测试广告的自然方式。

title: Officials Brief Congressional Staff on Intelligence Surrounding Nvidia Affair
title_en: Officials Brief Congressional Staff on Intelligence Surrounding Nvidia Affair

inline_images.caption: President Trump publicly proclaimed that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a national security threat or facing criminal prosecution. (John Macdougall/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images)
inline_images.alt: President Trump publicly proclaimed that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a national security threat or facing criminal prosecution.

author: Julian E. Barnes, Maggie Haberman, and Jonathan Swan
article_content:
A day after President Trump publicly proclaimed that Jensen Huang was not a national security threat or facing criminal prosecution, U.S. officials provided a tempered account of the intelligence at the heart of the Nvidia scandal in a briefing for Congress on Tuesday, people told about the briefing said.

The briefing, for staff members of the House and Senate intelligence committees and aides to the leaders of both chambers, outlined in broad terms some of what intelligence agencies have collected on Alice Huang, the Chinese woman whose affair with the Nvidia chief is at the center of the episode.

The U.S. intelligence officials told the aides to the lawmakers that they still do not fully understand the role played by Ms. Huang, who helped to run a Singapore-based data center firm, Megaspeed, that is suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips to China.

The briefers, who included officials from the F.B.I., C.I.A. and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, explained the contacts between Ms. Huang and China’s Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the meeting. The intelligence officials told the group there was no evidence she was directed by that agency to initiate an affair with Mr. Huang, though they did not dispute that she passed intelligence back to the agency after the affair began.

The briefers told the congressional staffers that the man who was often introduced as Ms. Huang’s husband, Kang Wei, was a more significant figure. He had been, at least at times, an M.S.S. asset and had more significant contacts with the Chinese spy agency, the briefers said.

The briefing did not include the most sensitive intelligence that the U.S. has collected about Ms. Huang, nor did it include a highly classified March 30 memo overseen by Marco Rubio, the secretary of state and national security adviser. That memo described Mr. Huang’s relationship with Ms. Huang, and hers with Chinese intelligence services, according to people briefed on it.

The congressional intelligence committees have requested a copy of the Rubio memo.

The New York Times reported last month that the U.S. government had collected intelligence showing that Mr. Huang, an ally of Mr. Trump, was having a close relationship with Ms. Huang, who U.S. officials believed was an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The Times reported on Sunday that people briefed on the U.S. intelligence said Ms. Huang was in contact with the Chinese spy agency from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, covering at least part of the period when she was having the affair with Mr. Huang. The Times also reported that Mr. Kang was in contact with the spy agency, as well.

Soon after The Times first reported last month on Ms. Huang’s links to Chinese intelligence, Mr. Trump publicly suggested that he was unsure whether Ms. Huang was a spy, and declared Mr. Huang a good man and a genius deserving of support from the government. Over this past weekend, the president set in motion a drive by the White House to reinstate Mr. Huang as Nvidia’s chief executive, reversing the Nvidia board’s decision to force his resignation.

The company’s announcement Monday that Mr. Huang would return was quickly followed by a social media statement from Mr. Trump in which the president asserted that the Nvidia chief was not a security threat and that he was not a target of any criminal prosecution. Mr. Trump made those statements even though he was briefed at least twice about Ms. Huang’s ties to Chinese intelligence, including once by Mr. Rubio, The Times has reported, and even though the Justice Department investigation into the diversion of chips to China is still in an early stage.

The briefing on Tuesday for congressional aides continued, behind closed doors, the public pattern by the administration of seeking to minimize any damage to Mr. Huang and Nvidia from the episode.

On Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche followed up on Mr. Trump’s statements, saying there was no evidence that Nvidia was anything other than “a good corporate citizen” and repeating that there was no evidence of wrongdoing by Mr. Huang.

In an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, Mr. Trump said Mr. Huang had nothing to hide and that he should not invoke his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination during a scheduled hearing before Congress next week. Asked about issuing a pardon for Mr. Huang, Mr. Trump replied, “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”

Megaspeed, the data center company that employed Ms. Huang, is under investigation by the Justice Department for diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China to evade U.S. export controls. The Trump administration on Monday placed Megaspeed on a trading blacklist, meaning that U.S. companies cannot ship technology to Megaspeed without obtaining a license.

In restoring Mr. Huang to the chief executive role on Monday, Nvidia agreed to establish a chief compliance officer, in effect acknowledging that it needs to do more to police where its chips end up.

In recent years the M.S.S., China’s top spy agency, has prioritized trying to break what Beijing calls an American “blockade” that is restricting their access to the most advanced computer chips.

The spy agency has worked to help Chinese companies acquire and smuggle advanced chips into China. The M.S.S., according to U.S., European and Asian national security officials, also collects intelligence about the semiconductor sector and its supply chains.

article_content_zh:
在特朗普总统公开宣布黄仁勋不构成国家安全威胁或面临刑事起诉的第二天，美国官员在周二向国会举行的简报中对英伟达丑闻的核心情报进行了温和的描述。

这份面向参众两院情报委员会工作人员以及参众两院领导人助手的简报，概括性地概述了情报机构收集到的有关爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的一些信息，这位中国女性与英伟达首席执行官的恋情是这一事件的核心。

美国情报官员告诉议员助手，他们仍然不完全了解黄女士所扮演的角色。黄女士帮助运营一家总部位于新加坡的数据中心公司Megaspeed，该公司涉嫌将先进的英伟达人工智能芯片转移到中国。

通报人包括联邦调查局 (FBI)、中央情报局 (C.I.A) 的官员。据了解会议情况的人士透露，美国国家情报总监办公室解释了黄女士与中国国家安全部之间的联系。情报官员告诉该组织，没有证据表明她受该机构指示与黄先生发生婚外情，不过他们并不否认她在婚外情发生后将情报传回该机构。

通报人告诉国会工作人员，经常被介绍为黄女士丈夫的康伟是一个更重要的人物。至少有时他是一名 M.S.S.简报称，该公司拥有资产，并与中国间谍机构有更重要的接触。

该简报不包括美国收集到的有关黄女士的最敏感情报，也不包括国务卿兼国家安全顾问马可·卢比奥监督的 3 月 30 日的高度机密备忘录。据知情人士透露，这份备忘录描述了黄先生与黄女士的关系，以及她与中国情报部门的关系。

国会情报委员会已要求获得卢比奥备忘录的副本。

《纽约时报》上个月报道称，美国政府收集的情报显示，特朗普的盟友黄先生与黄女士关系密切，美国官员认为黄女士是中国情报部门的资产。

《泰晤士报》周日报道称，了解美国情报的人士称，黄女士从 2025 年春季到今年秋季一直与中国间谍机构保持联系，至少涵盖了她与黄先生有染的部分时期。 《泰晤士报》还报道称，康先生也与该间谍机构有联系。

上个月，《泰晤士报》首次报道黄女士与中国情报机构的联系后不久，特朗普就公开表示，他不确定黄女士是否是间谍，并宣称黄女士是一个好人，是一个值得政府支持的天才。上周末，总统发起白宫推动，恢复黄先生担任英伟达首席执行官，推翻了英伟达董事会迫使他辞职的决定。

该公司周一宣布黄先生将回归，随后特朗普先生在社交媒体上发表声明，总统在声明中声称，这位英伟达首席执行官并不构成安全威胁，也不是任何刑事起诉的目标。据《泰晤士报》报道，尽管特朗普至少两次向他通报了黄女士与中国情报部门的关系，其中包括卢比奥向他通报的一次，而且司法部对芯片转移到中国的调查仍处于早期阶段，但特朗普还是发表了这些声明。

周二为国会助手举行的闭门简报会延续了政府寻求尽量减少这一事件对黄先生和英伟达造成的损害的公开模式。

周二，司法部长托德·布兰奇(Todd Blanche)对特朗普的声明进行了跟进，称没有证据表明英伟达不是“优秀的企业公民”，并重申没有证据表明黄先生有不当行为。

特朗普周二在接受《纽约邮报》采访时表示，黄先生没有什么可隐瞒的，他不应该在下周国会举行的预定听证会上援引第五修正案反对自证其罪的权利。当被问及是否赦免黄先生时，特朗普回答道：“我想这总是一个选择，但我认为没有必要。”

title: Rajiv Ramaswami to step down as Nutanix begins hunt for its next CEO
title_en: Rajiv Ramaswami to step down as Nutanix begins hunt for its next CEO
author: Mike Wheatley
article_content:
Rajiv Ramaswami is stepping down from his role as chief executive of Nutanix Inc., six years after he joined the hyperconverged cloud infrastructure company from its rival VMware Inc.

In a letter to company employees, Ramaswami (pictured) said he’s going to continue in the role for the time being while he works with Nutanix’s board of directors to identify a successor and assist with the transition. “After that, I will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time,” he said in the letter.

Ramaswami, who is 60 years old, did not give any reason for his coming departure, but the letter seems to indicate that he’s not ready to retire just yet.

“Our next CEO will inherit a strong platform, a loyal customer base and, most importantly, an exceptional team,” Ramaswami wrote. “Until then, my focus remains on leading this company and nothing about our day-to-day priorities changes. I am committed to helping our next leader succeed, and my ask of you, as always, is to continue to focus on executing as we go through this leadership transition.”

Ramaswami added that Nutanix has hired an executive search firm to lead the hunt for his successor. The news came as the company delivered its first-quarter earnings report, posting modest year-over-year gains in profit and revenue.

The company reported adjusted earnings of 73 cents per share, beating Wall Street’s target of 61 cents per share by a strong margin. Revenue for the period came to $772.4 million, up 15% from a year earlier and above the Street’s forecast of $762.7 million.

Nutanix’s outlook for the current quarter is strong, with the company guiding for sales of between $820 million and $830 million, compared with the Street’s consensus estimate of $820.4 million. However, the full-year picture is a little less rosy, with Nutanix guiding for annual sales of $3.18 billion to $3.23 billion. The midpoint of that range trails the Street’s forecast of $3.22 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue.

Investors did not take the news very well. The cautious full-year guidance compared with the uncertainty over leadership prompted many to sell, and Nutanix’s stock was down 8% after-hours, having already fallen more than 5% during the regular trading session, on a down day for many tech stocks.

Virginia Gambale, of the board at Nutanix, hailed the “tremendous impact” Ramaswami had on the company during his six-year tenure. “Rajiv led the company’s transformation to subscription software, built a loyal and expanding global enterprise base and established a technology portfolio that we believe positions us well for the AI era,” she said. “We’re focused on selecting an exceptional leader who can build on that foundation.”

### A new chapter begins

In a conference call with analysts, Ramaswami said he believes the company is embarking on the third major chapter in its history. The first chapter, before his arrival, saw the company establish itself as the leader of the hyperconverged infrastructure industry. Chapter two began when he took over, and saw Nutanix expand from those roots to become a platform company, he said.

“[We have] transformed the company to be profitable while growing and expanding the product portfolio quite significantly, from HCI to a platform that works across clouds, supports external storage and has cloud-native capabilities and now moving into the future with AI capabilities,” Ramaswami said. “Chapter two is well-established at this point and there’s a lot of opportunity in terms of driving growth. I feel like we are in a very good place.”

According to Ramaswami, Nutanix now stands at an inflection point as it looks to cash in on the new era of artificial intelligence. “I’ve been talking to the board for a bit about this, as well as in terms of our strategic direction and the timing for succession, and so we came to the conclusion together that this is perhaps the right time,” he told analysts. “[We wanted] to announce it ahead of time as we look for the appropriate next leader.”

Ramaswami’s departure from the company should at least be a lot smoother than his arrival. Nutanix announced it had appointed Ramaswami as its CEO in late 2020, just two days after he quit his role as chief operating officer of its biggest rival, VMware.

VMware was indignant about the manner of his departure, and responded with a lawsuit that accused Ramaswami of breaching his legal and contractual duties to the company by “secretly meeting” with Nutanix’s board to discuss taking over, while continuing to play a leading role in shaping its product and business strategy. The lawsuit was ultimately settled out of court about a year later.

In April, Ramaswami appeared on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s mobile livestreaming studio, where he talked about how Nutanix is shifting away from HCI to focus on more of a “disaggregated infrastructure” strategy to support demand for autonomous AI agents:

article_content_zh:
拉吉夫·拉马斯瓦米 (Rajiv Ramaswami) 辞去 Nutanix Inc. 首席执行官一职，六年前，他从竞争对手 VMware Inc. 加入这家超融合云基础设施公司。

Ramaswami（如图）在致公司员工的一封信中表示，他将暂时继续担任该职位，同时与 Nutanix 董事会合作物色继任者并协助过渡。 “此后，我将继续担任公司高级顾问一段时间，”他在信中表示。

现年 60 岁的拉马斯瓦米没有给出任何离职原因，但这封信似乎表明他还没有准备好退休。

拉马斯瓦米写道：“我们的下一任首席执行官将继承一个强大的平台、忠诚的客户群，以及最重要的是一支出色的团队。” “在那之前，我的重点仍然是领导这家公司，我们的日常优先事项不会发生任何变化。我致力于帮助我们的下一任领导者取得成功，而我对你们的要求是，一如既往，在我们经历领导层过渡时继续专注于执行。”

Ramaswami 补充说，Nutanix 已经聘请了一家猎头公司来领导寻找他的继任者。这一消息发布之际，该公司发布了第一季度收益报告，利润和收入同比小幅增长。

该公司报告调整后每股收益为 73 美分，大幅超出华尔街每股 61 美分的目标。该季度收入达到 7.724 亿美元，比去年同期增长 15%，高于华尔街预期的 7.627 亿美元。

Nutanix 对本季度的前景十分乐观，该公司预计销售额在 8.2 亿至 8.3 亿美元之间，而华尔街普遍预期为 8.204 亿美元。然而，全年情况不太乐观，Nutanix 预计年销售额为 31.8 亿美元至 32.3 亿美元。该区间的中点低于华尔街对 2027 财年 32.2 亿美元收入的预测。

投资者对这个消息不太感冒。与领导层的不确定性相比，谨慎的全年指引促使许多人抛售，Nutanix 的股价在盘后下跌了 8%，在常规交易时段已经下跌了 5% 以上，而在许多科技股下跌的日子里。

Nutanix 董事会成员弗吉尼亚·甘贝尔 (Virginia Gambale) 对拉马斯瓦米 (Ramaswami) 在其六年任期内对公司产生的“巨大影响”表示赞赏。她说：“拉吉夫领导了公司向订阅软件的转型，建立了忠诚且不断扩大的全球企业基础，并建立了一个技术组合，我们相信这使我们在人工智能时代处于有利地位。” “我们专注于选择一位能够在此基础上继续发展的杰出领导者。”

拉马斯瓦米在与分析师的电话会议上表示，他相信该公司正在开启其历史上的第三个重要篇章。在他到来之前的第一章中，公司确立了自己作为超融合基础设施行业领导者的地位。他说，第二章是在他接手后开始的，并见证了 Nutanix 从这些根源扩展到一家平台公司。

Ramaswami 表示：“（我们）已经使公司实现盈利，同时大幅增长和扩展了产品组合，从 HCI 到跨云工作、支持外部存储并具有云原生功能的平台，现在又凭借 AI 功能迈向未来。” “目前第二章已经很完善，在推动增长方面有很多机会。我觉得我们处于一个非常好的位置。”

Ramaswami 表示，Nutanix 现在正处于一个拐点，它希望在人工智能新时代中获利。他对分析师表示：“我已经与董事会就此事以及我们的战略方向和继任时间进行了一些讨论，因此我们共同得出的结论是，这也许是正确的时机。” “[我们希望]在寻找合适的下一任领导者时提前宣布这一消息。”

拉马斯瓦米离开公司至少应该比他的到来顺利很多。 Nutanix 于 2020 年底宣布任命 Ramaswami 为首席执行官，就在他辞去最大竞争对手 VMware 首席运营官职务两天后。

VMware 对他的离职方式感到愤怒，并以诉讼回应，指控 Ramaswami 违反了他对公司的法律和合同义务，与 Nutanix 董事会“秘密开会”讨论接管事宜，同时继续在制定其产品和业务战略方面发挥主导作用。大约一年后，这起诉讼最终在庭外和解。

title: HP Gives Profit Forecast Signaling Better Handle on Memory Costs
title_en: HP Gives Profit Forecast Signaling Better Handle on Memory Costs
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
HP GAVE a profit forecast for the current year that will likely exceed analysts’ estimates, signalling the computer and printer maker is improving its ability to manage rising costs associated with memory chips. The shares jumped in extended trading.

Earnings, excluding items such as restructuring costs, will be US$3.15 to US$3.45 a share for the year beginning this month, the company said on Tuesday (Nov 24) in a statement. Analysts, on average, projected US$3.18, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

For the current quarter ending January, profit will be 66 cents to 76 cents a share, HP said. Analysts, on average, estimated 72 cents. The forecasts include the impact of tariff refunds, the company said.

The shares rose about 15 per cent in late trading after closing at US$27.94 in New York. The stock had gained 15 per cent this year through the close.

HP and other computing device makers are coping with an unprecedented surge in demand for memory chips fuelled by the AI build-out.

Amid skyrocketing costs for those components, HP has raised prices on its products, leading consumers to push off buying new computers. Corporate customers, however, are investing in new machines and revenue in that business rose 23 per cent.

Sustainability has reached Apac boardrooms but are board members sufficiently equipped? Find out more in our report.

Global PC shipments declined more than 22 per cent in the July-September period from a year earlier, according to industry research firm Gartner.

“We continued to grow our higher-value businesses, with AI PCs reaching nearly 60 per cent of shipments, while taking steps to address memory and storage cost pressures,” Bruce Broussard, the company’s interim chief executive officer, said in the statement.

Revenue increased 9.3 per cent to US$16 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, which ended Oct 31. Profit, excluding some items, was 83 cents a share.

Analysts, on average, estimated earnings of 74 cents on revenue of US$15.3 billion. The earnings included a larger-than-forecast tariff refund of 15 cents a share, compared with a previously forecast 8 cents.

“While our fiscal 2027 outlook reflects a prudent view of continued cost and demand pressures, we have a strong track record of addressing challenges and are confident in our ability to drive improvement in our profitability throughout the year,” said chief financial officer Karen Parkhill.

HP has named Emma Walmsley to take over as new CEO in January. BLOOMBERG

title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
title_en: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
author: Lauren Feiner
article_content:
The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed on Tuesday that it’s investigating a “cybersecurity incident.” The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it’s looking into an “incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.” It hasn’t offered any information about the full scope or source of the breach, but FinCEN has taken some systems offline as a precaution.

The news comes hours after The New York Times reported that the Central Intelligence Agency and Office of the Director of National Security discovered a breach of an open source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information. It’s unclear if the FinCEN breach is related. Americans have been on high alert about security incidents after a series of seemingly unrelated outages earlier this month.

"Americans have been on high alert about security incidents"

FinCEN’s role is to protect the financial system from illegal activity, including by combatting money laundering and terrorism financing. The bureau maintains financial transaction data and distributes it for law enforcement purposes. FinCEN also houses reports of suspicious activity that financial institutions file as part of the Bank Secrecy Act.

FinCEN says in its alert that banks can still file reports about suspicious activity online, but some services may not be immediately available. Filers that need to expedite their reports in the meantime can still call the Financial Institutions Hotline, which it says was not impacted by the disruption.

title: SoftBank drops over 11% as Wall Street AI sell-off ripples across Asian tech names
title_en: SoftBank drops over 11% as Wall Street AI sell-off ripples across Asian tech names
author: Lee Ying Shan
article_content:
Asian technology stocks tumbled Wednesday, led by a rout in Japanese semiconductor stocks, as renewed concerns over the artificial intelligence trade rattles investors following an overnight sell-off on Wall Street.

Japanese semiconductor stocks tied to the global AI supply chain were among the hardest hit. Advantest, a supplier of chip testing equipment to Nvidia, plunged 12.26%. Tokyo Electron, which supplies chipmaking equipment to Nvidia's manufacturing partner TSMC, slumped 10.9%.

Technology conglomerate SoftBank Group shed 10%, while semiconductor inspection equipment maker Lasertec lost 10.15%.

Other Japanese chip stocks also came under heavy selling pressure, with Disco Corporation falling 9.41% and Renesas Electronics losing 10%.

Tech stocks have seen heightened volatility over the past few months amid concerns over capital expenditure, skepticism over return on investments, circular AI financing, with Jensen Huang's ouster as Nvidia CEO adding fresh worries, and his return sparking a massive rally.

In South Korea, memory chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both plunged more than 7%. Both companies are key suppliers of the high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI accelerators.

Other South Korean technology stocks also traded lower. LG Innotek shed 6.15%, while LG Display declined 4.09%.

The losses followed the decline in U.S. technology stocks, with the Nasdaq Composite giving back some of the sharp gains from the previous session sparked by Huang's return as Nvidia CEO.

亚洲科技股周三暴跌，日本半导体股暴跌，原因是在华尔街隔夜抛售之后，对人工智能交易的新担忧令投资者感到不安。

其他日本芯片股也面临沉重抛售压力，Disco Corporation 下跌 9.41%，瑞萨电子下跌 10%。

过去几个月，由于对资本支出的担忧、对投资回报的怀疑、循环人工智能融资，科技股波动加剧，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的下台增添了新的担忧，而他的回归引发了大规模反弹。

在韩国，存储芯片巨头三星电子和SK海力士股价均下跌超过7%。两家公司都是人工智能加速器中使用的高带宽存储芯片的主要供应商。

其他韩国科技股也走低。 LG Innotek 下跌 6.15%，LG Display 下跌 4.09%。

这些损失是在美国科技股下跌之后出现的，纳斯达克综合指数回吐了前一交易日因黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官而引发的一些大幅涨幅。

title: Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
title_en: Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
author: Duncan Riley
article_content:
Shares of human resources and finance software company Workday Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after a softer-than-expected subscription revenue forecast for the current quarter overshadowed fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s targets.

For the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.75 per share on revenue of $2.69 billion.

Subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion. Net income on an unadjusted basis came to $237 million, down from $252 million in the same quarter a year ago. Included in the quarter were $51 million in restructuring expenses, which followed the company’s disclosure in late September that it would cut about 2.5% of its workforce, mostly in its product and technology team.

Total subscription revenue backlog grew 6.1%, to $27.548 billion, with the 12-month figure up 12.3%, to $9.216 billion. Free cash flow came to $691 million, up from $550 million. During the quarter, Workday spent $750 million buying back about 3.8 million shares.

The quarter also saw Workday hold its annual Rising customer conference in Las Vegas in October, when the company made Sana the new home experience for its platform. Built on technology from Sana Labs AB, which Workday acquired for about $1.1 billion last year, Sana is an AI interface that brings tasks, decisions, meetings and agent activity together in one place. Autopilot Agents, also launched at the event, are designed to handle routine HR, finance and IT processes in the background.

On the opening day of Rising, Workday announced that it had agreed to acquire agentic identity platform ConductorOne Inc., better known as C1.ai. That deal closed on Monday. A partnership with Anthropic PBC, also unveiled at Rising, is set to bring Claude together with Sana AI agents and Workday’s HR and finance data.

“The past few quarters have been our strongest on the innovation and invention front, and in Q3, our AI products drove nearly $150 million in new ACV, more than three times what we delivered a year ago,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Aneel Bhusri, who returned to the top job in February after Carl Eschenbach stepped down. The priority now, Bhusri added, is to get more customers running agents in production.

According to Workday, the number of core customers that have bought at least one of its AI products rose nearly 25% from the previous quarter, to more than 2,200.

Pointing to what he called “ongoing adoption across our AI portfolio,” Chief Financial Officer Zane Rowe said the company is raising its full-year targets.

For its fiscal fourth quarter, Workday expects subscription revenue of $2.6 billion, up 10%, and an adjusted operating margin of 31.7%. Full-year subscription revenue is now forecast at $9.958 billion, up 13%, compared with the $9.94 billion to $9.95 billion guided in August. The full-year adjusted operating margin forecast was also raised, to 31.5%, ahead of the 31.1% expected by analysts.

Though the full-year numbers moved higher, the fourth-quarter subscription forecast came in narrowly below the $2.61 billion analysts had been expecting. Growth of 10% in the period would also be a step down from the 12.8% Workday posted in the third quarter.

Workday Chief Technology Officer Gabe Monroy made the case for taking agents to where employees already work during an interview in August. Speaking with theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, for the Google Cloud: AI Agents in Action series, Monroy said enterprise agents need the deterministic rules of a system like Workday to go with the probabilistic reasoning of AI. “We don’t want to ask customers to have to switch their front doors or log into Workday when they’re happy to use Gemini systems,” he said.

article_content_zh:
人力资源和财务软件公司 Workday Inc. 的股价在今天尾盘下跌超过 7%，因为本季度的订阅收入预测低于预期，盖过了超过华尔街目标的第三财季盈利和收入。

截至 10 月 31 日的季度，Workday 报告调整后每股收益为 2.82 美元，较上年同期的 2.32 美元增长 22%，营收为 27.05 亿美元，同比增长 11.2%。分析师预计每股收益为 2.75 美元，营收为 26.9 亿美元。

订阅收入较上年同期增长 12.8%，达到 25.32 亿美元。未经调整的净利润为 2.37 亿美元，低于去年同期的 2.52 亿美元。该季度包括 5100 万美元的重组费用，该费用是在该公司 9 月底披露将裁员约 2.5%（主要是产品和技术团队）之后发生的。

总订阅收入增长了 6.1%，达到 275.48 亿美元，12 个月的数字增长了 12.3%，达到 92.16 亿美元。自由现金流从 5.5 亿美元增至 6.91 亿美元。本季度，Workday 花费 7.5 亿美元回购约 380 万股股票。

本季度，Workday 还于 10 月份在拉斯维加斯举行了年度 Rising 客户会议，当时该公司将 Sana 为其平台提供了新的家庭体验。 Sana 基于 Sana Labs AB 的技术（Workday 去年以约 11 亿美元的价格收购了该公司），Sana 是一种人工智能界面，可将任务、决策、会议和座席活动集中到一个地方。活动中还推出了 Autopilot Agents，旨在在后台处理日常人力资源、财务和 IT 流程。

在 Rising 开业当天，Workday 宣布已同意收购代理身份平台 ConductorOne Inc.（更广为人知的名称为 C1.ai）。该交易于周一结束。与 Anthropic PBC 的合作也在 Rising 上揭晓，旨在将 Claude 与 Sana 人工智能代理以及 Workday 的人力资源和财务数据结合起来。

联合创始人兼首席执行官阿内尔·布斯里 (Aneel Bhusri) 表示：“过去几个季度是我们在创新和发明方面表现最强劲的几个季度，在第三季度，我们的人工智能产品为新 ACV 带来了近 1.5 亿美元的收入，是我们一年前交付额的三倍多。”他在 Carl Eschenbach 下台后于 2 月份重返最高职位。 Bhusri 补充说，现在的首要任务是让更多客户在生产中运行代理。

据Workday统计，至少购买过其一款AI产品的核心客户数量较上一季度增长近25%，达到2200多家。

首席财务官 Zane Rowe 在谈到他所谓的“我们的人工智能产品组合中的持续采用”时表示，该公司正在提高其全年目标。

Workday 预计第四财季的订阅收入将达到 26 亿美元，增长 10%，调整后的营业利润率为 31.7%。目前预计全年订阅收入为 99.58 亿美元，较 8 月份指导的 99.4 亿至 99.5 亿美元增长 13%。全年调整后营业利润率预测也上调至 31.5%，高于分析师预期的 31.1%。

尽管全年数字有所上升，但第四季度订阅预测仅略低于分析师预期的 26.1 亿美元。在此期间 10% 的增长也将比第三季度 Workday 的 12.8% 有所下降。

Workday 首席技术官 Gabe Monroy 在 8 月份的一次采访中阐述了将代理带到员工已经工作的地方的理由。 Monroy 在接受 SiliconANGLE Media 直播工作室 theCUBE 的 Google Cloud：AI 代理实际行动系列采访时表示，企业代理需要 Workday 等系统的确定性规则来配合 AI 的概率推理。 “当客户乐意使用 Gemini 系统时，我们不想要求他们必须打开前门或登录 Workday，”他说。

title: Utah prosecutors drop criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders, one day after the company halted operations in the state (Marshall Cohen/CNN)
title_en: Utah prosecutors drop criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders, one day after the company halted operations in the state (Marshall Cohen/CNN)

inline_images.caption: Marshall Cohen
inline_images.alt: Marshall Cohen

author: CNN
article_content:
Utah prosecutors dropped criminal charges against the prediction company Kalshi and its co-founders on Tuesday, one day after the company halted operations in the state. This is the latest — and perhaps most dramatic — victory for the states in their longstanding push to regulate prediction markets like gambling.

The companies and the Trump administration insist they should be federally regulated as financial exchanges. Prediction platforms let users bet on real-world events, like sports, elections, the weather and more. Kalshi is the biggest prediction market in the US, but some or all of its markets are now unavailable in Utah, Nevada, Michigan, Louisiana and Washington state after the states fought back against the companies.

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown, a Republican, pursued both civil and criminal cases against Kalshi, ratcheting up the pressure. A conservative state with a sizable Mormon population, Utah has some of the strictest anti-gambling laws in the US, including a prohibition in its state constitution.

“Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown said in a statement. “Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges. Every company in this space should take note.

If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.” There wasn’t any deal or settlement between Utah and Kalshi, according to two sources familiar with the matter. Kalshi unilaterally exited Utah on Monday after a setback in federal court, and state prosecutors asked the judge to dismiss the criminal case on Tuesday.

Civil litigation is still pending. Kalshi’s newly minted general counsel, former Trump-era Justice Department official Yaakov Roth, posted on X that he was “pleased” that Utah prosecutors dropped the criminal case and said the company is “ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.” If the charges weren’t dropped, Kalshi co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara would be required to appear in a Salt Lake City courtroom next week for their arraignment.

Kalshi spokeswoman Jacki McGavick said in a statement that the company withdrew from Utah because of recent setbacks in federal court. A federal judge ruled months ago that Utah could enforce its gambling laws against Kalshi, and last week, the judge also largely rebuffed a new push by the Trump administration to shut down the state criminal case.

“This is an unfortunate outcome for the more than 177,000 Utahns who use Kalshi,” McGavick said. “We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated.” The Utah case is one of dozens of lawsuits playing out across the country involving prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket, which have exploded in popularity this year and now see billions of dollars in weekly trading volume.

Experts believe the Supreme Court will ultimately decide the legality of prediction markets and who gets to regulate them. The states have seen significant momentum in recent months, with courtroom victories and even recent action on Capitol Hill. States have argued that more regulations and consumer protections are needed because prediction markets are addictive like gambling and most users lose money.

However, it hasn’t been all bad news for the companies. A New York judge on Monday refused to immediately shut down Kalshi in the state. But the developments in Utah show how a state can successfully pressure the companies with aggressive moves in state and federal court.

“Kalshi has steadfastly argued that it is legal under federal law and state laws don’t apply,” said Dustin Gouker, an independent journalist who chronicles the prediction industry. “But the threat of criminal charges against its co-founders has changed the calculus in terms of how far it’s willing to go to defend that argument.” CNN has a partnership with Kalshi and uses its data to cover major events.

CNN employees aren’t permitted to trade on prediction platforms.

article_content_zh:
周二，在该公司停止在该州运营一天后，犹他州检察官撤销了对预测公司 Kalshi 及其联合创始人的刑事指控。这是各州长期以来推动监管赌博等预测市场的最新胜利，也许也是最引人注目的胜利。

这些公司和特朗普政府坚称它们应该作为金融交易所受到联邦监管。预测平台让用户可以对现实世界的事件进行投注，例如体育、选举、天气等。 Kalshi 是美国最大的预测市场，但在犹他州、内华达州、密歇根州、路易斯安那州和华盛顿州对这些公司进行反击后，其部分或全部市场现已无法使用。

犹他州司法部长、共和党人德里克·布朗对卡尔希提起民事和刑事诉讼，加大了压力。犹他州是一个拥有大量摩门教人口的保守州，拥有美国最严格的一些反赌博法律，其中包括州宪法中的禁令。

布朗在一份声明中表示：“犹他州不允许赌博，而预测市场就是赌博。” “Kalshi 已退出犹他州，如果它返回，指控也会如此。这个领域的每个公司都应该注意。

如果他们宣扬、支持或纵容赌博，我们将追究他们的责任。”据两位知情人士透露，犹他州和卡尔希之间没有达成任何协议或和解。在联邦法院受挫后，卡尔希于周一单方面离开犹他州，周二州检察官要求法官驳回刑事案件。

民事诉讼仍在审理中。 Kalshi 新任总法律顾问、特朗普时代的前司法部官员雅科夫·罗斯 (Yaakov Roth) 在 X 上发帖表示，他对犹他州检察官撤销刑事案件感到“高兴”，并表示该公司“准备与州总检察长合作采取合理的临时措施，直到法院解决谁监管预测市场的争端。”如果指控不被撤销，Kalshi 联合创始人塔里克·曼苏尔 (Tarek Mansour) 和卢安娜·洛佩斯·拉拉 (Luana Lopes Lara) 将被要求下周在盐湖城法庭接受提审。

Kalshi 发言人 Jacki McGavick 在一份声明中表示，由于最近在联邦法院遭遇挫折，该公司退出犹他州。几个月前，一名联邦法官裁定犹他州可以对卡尔希执行赌博法，上周，该法官还基本上拒绝了特朗普政府提出的终止该州刑事案件的新举措。

“对于超过 177,000 名使用 Kalshi 的犹他州人来说，这是一个不幸的结果，”麦加维克说。 “我们将继续在法庭上抗争，我们期待着在我们的法律立场得到证实后返回犹他州。”犹他州的案件是全国范围内涉及 Kalshi 和 Polymarket 等预测市场的数十起诉讼之一，这些市场今年人气激增，目前每周交易量已达数十亿美元。

专家认为，最高法院将最终决定预测市场的合法性以及由谁来监管它们。近几个月来，各州取得了显着的势头，在法庭上取得了胜利，甚至最近在国会山采取了行动。各州认为，需要更多的监管和消费者保护，因为预测市场像赌博一样容易上瘾，而且大多数用户都会赔钱。

然而，对于这些公司来说，这并不全是坏消息。纽约一名法官周一拒绝立即关闭该州的卡尔希。但犹他州的事态发展表明，一个州如何能够在州和联邦法院采取积极行动，成功地向这些公司施压。

“卡尔希坚定地认为，根据联邦法律，这是合法的，州法律并不适用，”记录预测行业的独立记者达斯汀·古克 (Dustin Gouker) 说。 “但对其联合创始人提出刑事指控的威胁已经改变了它愿意在多大程度上捍卫这一论点的考量。” CNN 与 Kalshi 建立了合作伙伴关系，并使用其数据来报道重大事件。

CNN 员工不得在预测平台上进行交易。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】犹他州检察长Derek Brown、预测市场平台Kalshi在犹他州法律诉讼环境：撤销刑事指控，前提是Kalshi退出该州
【起因与机理】地方州层面反赌博立法与联邦监管权归属存分歧
【调查与监管诉求】犹他州检察长Derek Brown宣布撤销对预测市场平台Kalshi及其创始人Tarek Mansour和Luana Lopes Lara的刑事起诉，前提是该公司已主动停止在该州的运营。
【各方立场与态度】通过刑事起诉迫使平台下架是州政府针对新兴金融衍生品的一种防卫性行政博弈，预计此类诉讼将持续推动预测市场在合规架构上被迫向“金融交易所”属性靠拢，以规避地方刑责。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Jurisdictional conflict between state anti-gambling laws and federal regulation

[Industry Impact & Outlook] State-level criminal pressure acts as a defensive administrative barrier; expect prediction platforms to increasingly align with 'financial exchange' definitions to mitigate local criminal liability risks.

title: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police
title_en: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police
author: Dell Cameron
article_content:
Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO signals that the chipmaker may have grown too important to the stock market for the US government to hold it accountable for national security lapses, intelligence and export-control experts warn WIRED. The move also undercuts the warnings Washington routinely issues to American companies and foreign governments about Beijing’s pursuit of US technology, they say.

Nvidia’s board brought back Huang on Monday, 11 days after he resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs—one of them with Alice Huang, a woman US intelligence suspects has ties to China’s Ministry of State Security. The board said input from “senior levels of the United States government” left it confident that his return poses no national security risk.

President Donald Trump told The Wall Street Journal he lobbied the board directly and through intermediaries, and that Nvidia’s falling share price helped his case. The board acted before its own investigation of Huang had concluded, and while the Justice Department is pursuing a criminal probe of Megaspeed—a Singapore company Alice Huang once ran—over the alleged diversion of Nvidia chips to China. Alice Huang is also under investigation, according to director of national intelligence Jay Clayton.

The experts tell WIRED they worry more about the precedent Huang’s return sets than about Huang himself. Some say the scrutiny now on him makes further compromise unlikely. But Beijing may already have gained insight into Nvidia’s chip designs and its private conversations with the White House and Congress, or, through Megaspeed, obtained the chips themselves, they say, and no one has publicly established what, if anything, it got.

Several want to know who gave the board its assurances and on what basis, and whether the government ran a counterintelligence damage assessment or simply made a political judgment. They also say the administration has repeatedly failed to enforce its own export controls, and that when intelligence concerns appear to yield to market pressure, US warnings about China start to sound negotiable, to Beijing’s benefit.

“If intelligence assessments are seen to be overridden, selectively interpreted, or publicly dismissed for political or commercial reasons, this could undermine long-term confidence in the independence of national security institutions,” says Tahlia Peterson, a cyber and technology research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, a London defense think tank. “That would be damaging to US national security, and potentially advantageous to Beijing.”

Advisers briefed Trump at least twice on Alice Huang’s links to Chinese intelligence before the affair became public, and both times he played down their concerns, The New York Times reported Sunday. When the Journal asked him on Monday about Republican lawmakers who say Huang’s return endangers national security, Trump pointed to Nvidia’s rebounding stock.

“Some tech companies have become so big—and so important to the stock market—that Washington is reluctant to hold them accountable for national security lapses,” says Edward Fishman, director of the Council on Foreign Relations’ Maurice R. Greenberg Center for Geoeconomics.

Fishman sees a parallel in Wall Street’s slow reckoning with sanctions. “It took years of aggressive enforcement to get banks to take US sanctions compliance seriously,” he says. “We haven’t seen anything comparable in the tech sector, which helps explain why US export controls remain so weak and leaky.” Reinstating Huang on the administration's assurances before Nvidia’s own investigation has concluded “does not inspire confidence that meaningful enforcement is coming,” he says.

Emily Kilcrease, a former deputy assistant US trade representative who now directs the Energy, Economics, and Security program at the Center for a New American Security, says the administration’s record gives little reason to take those assurances at face value. “We cannot rely on the administration’s judgment, as it has repeatedly failed to enforce export controls over the past year,” she says.

On Monday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist, and the administration has recently moved to tighten rules on China’s AI industry. But Kilcrease says it acted only under pressure. “Given the poor track record on export controls and their broader accommodationist stance toward China, it’s fair to ask whether they are willing to really enforce the new controls,” she says.

The board’s assurances appear to have come mostly from the Justice Department. Attorney general Todd Blanche allegedly told Trump and vice president JD Vance on Saturday that Huang was neither a target nor a subject of any department investigation, and that the department had no evidence he had broken the law or posed a national security risk, the Journal reports. Vance then reportedly sought assurances for the board that the administration did not consider Huang a threat and that he would not face criminal charges. Trump told the Times he also consulted Clayton before pushing for Huang’s return. (“I can’t do this and then all of a sudden have somebody get indicted,” he said.)

Nvidia did not immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment.

Whether Huang broke any laws is a separate question from whether Beijing gained anything through him. “Did [the assurances] reflect a counterintelligence damage assessment by the intelligence community or the FBI, or were they political in nature?” says Jessica Brandt, a senior fellow for technology and national security at the Council on Foreign Relations who previously directed the Foreign Malign Influence Center at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. “Lawmakers should press on that.”

Senior officials may have seen intelligence that isn’t public, so the assurances shouldn’t just be dismissed, says Sunny Cheung, a China studies fellow at the Jamestown Foundation. “However, we still don’t know who provided those assurances, what evidence they reviewed, or how they reached their conclusion, particularly when Nvidia’s own independent investigation remains unfinished,” he says.

Lawmakers appear to have seen little of that evidence. At a briefing this month by CIA director John Ratcliffe and Clayton that was scheduled to cover Iran, lawmakers pressed for answers about Huang, and the responses left some of them puzzled, according to the Times. A follow-up briefing for senior national security staff was postponed.

Cheung says the Ministry of State Security may not have needed Nvidia’s secrets to profit from the relationship. “From a counterintelligence perspective, I think people are too focused on whether Jensen handed over trade secrets,” he says. “China’s Ministry of State Security wouldn’t necessarily need Nvidia’s next-generation chip blueprints to benefit from access to him.” Insight into Huang’s direct conversations with the president, senior officials, and other top tech executives, along with his views on China and Taiwan and his role in Washington’s export-control debate, “could already be extremely valuable to Beijing,” he says.

Brandt sees the same mix of risks. “Information about Nvidia’s proprietary chip designs could help China advance its own chip design efforts,” she says. “Insight into Nvidia’s conversations with the White House and Congress could help Beijing anticipate where US export control policy is headed.” Investigators should also ask whether Alice Huang compromised Huang’s devices, what security clearance he held, and whether he still holds it, she says.

Huang successfully lobbied the Trump administration to roll back restrictions on Nvidia’s chip sales to China and negotiated a deal giving the US government a 25 percent cut of sales of certain chips approved for export there, the Times has reported. In April, minister of state security Chen Yixin made overcoming the “blockades” that limit China’s access to key technologies like AI a sixth core mission for his ministry, known as the MSS. Alice Huang’s network of chip-buying companies “lines up precisely” with that mission, Matt Pottinger, who served as deputy national security adviser during Trump’s first term, told the paper.

“A further question is whether Alice Huang was tasked by Chinese intelligence to influence Jensen Huang's views or approach to US export restrictions on China, and, if so, to what extent she succeeded,” Peterson says. The Journal also reported that the intelligence is inconclusive on whether she was actively tasked to collect information on Huang, and Cheung says “whether any such information was obtained or influence exercised remains unproven.”

Megaspeed’s purchases are better documented. A Malaysian subsidiary bought at least $4.8 billion worth of equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, according to trade records the Times reviewed. Its subsidiaries have also served Chinese clients, including Alibaba. US intelligence indicates Alice Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from spring 2025 until this fall, and that her business partner, Kang Wei, also worked with the agency, the paper reported Sunday. Her network has been linked to efforts to supply Nvidia chips to China’s state-owned military contractors. Enough has been reported to suggest that Huang, “wittingly or not, may have played a role in helping Megaspeed as it sought access to advanced Nvidia chips,” Kilcrease says.

Megaspeed did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Nicholas Eftimiades, a former CIA and Defense Intelligence Agency officer who teaches homeland security at Penn State Harrisburg, says Huang himself poses no security risk. Now that the relationship is public, he says, Huang has little chance of unwittingly passing along more information about US government policy or Nvidia’s board deliberations. Peterson agrees that scrutiny from Nvidia’s board, its compliance staff, federal agencies, and Congress likely limits any further exposure. But “we are still in the dark as to whether any sensitive information may already have been compromised,” she says, “or whether any resulting harm can be identified or mitigated.”

Huang’s defenders have repeatedly noted that he never received a defensive briefing, a warning the government sometimes gives Americans whom foreign intelligence services target. Nvidia’s board says its investigation will continue with Huang’s cooperation, and the company is searching for a chief compliance officer. A committee of independent directors is examining whether Huang shared corporate or national security information with Alice Huang. The board has also formed a new committee of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

Peterson says the company’s leadership matters. “Nvidia is an exceptionally important company, and there are legitimate arguments about the implications of losing its leadership at a critical moment in the global AI race,” she says. “But those considerations should not determine the conclusions of national security investigations.”

Trump told CNBC Monday that keeping the United States ahead of China made reinstating Huang imperative. “If we didn't do this, I could see China coming in and saying to Jensen, ‘Hey, how would you like to come to China?’” he said.

For Brandt, the bigger cost may come with Washington’s next warning. “This erodes the credibility of US government warnings about China’s technological ambitions and how far it will go to achieve them,” she says. “How will those warnings land going forward, both with our own companies and with foreign governments? We risk making a hard problem harder: emboldening Beijing while weakening our own defenses.”

That cost extends to the allies Washington depends on to police its controls, adds Sarah Bauerle Danzman, an associate professor of international studies at Indiana University’s Hamilton Lugar School. The Commerce Department has few enforcement agents abroad to monitor transshipment, she says, so the system relies on partner countries to run checks and share information about problematic buyers. Singapore says it repeatedly raised concerns with US authorities in this case.

“These types of incidents make such cooperation more difficult to sustain,” Bauerle Danzman says.

Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter have agreed to closed-door, transcribed interviews with three House committees on December 1 and 2. “The legal and reputational risk of hiring a CEO who may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws is now [borne] by the board of Nvidia, but the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens,” Senator Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican, said on X.

“I think Congress has gotten fed up,” says Kilcrease, who cites bipartisan concern about Megaspeed and what she calls the administration’s broader accommodation of China. “We can expect hearings and investigations from multiple committees, and Congress is highly motivated to pass legislation to tighten export controls, increase its oversight of administration decisions, and bolster enforcement.”

“Jensen may be back, and he should not be presumed guilty of wrongdoing,” Cheung says. “But his reinstatement should not be mistaken for a clean bill of health. Nvidia and the administration still have important questions to answer.”

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Nvidia已成为事实上的“国家级”算力基础设施，黄仁勋的复职折射出地缘安全诉求在资本市场核心资产面前的脆弱平衡。当行政力量被迫介入企业人事以稳定市值，这也意味着美国出口管制体系的公信力正受到利益交换逻辑的侵蚀，未来针对敏感技术的长臂管辖将面临更大阻力。

article_content_zh:
情报和出口管制专家警告《连线》杂志，英伟达决定恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官，这表明这家芯片制造商对股市来说可能已经变得太重要了，以至于美国政府无法追究其对国家安全失误的责任。他们表示，此举还削弱了华盛顿经常就北京追求美国技术向美国公司和外国政府发出的警告。

黄伟因婚外情被曝光而辞职 11 天后，英伟达董事会于周一重新召回了黄伟，其中包括与美国情报部门怀疑与中国国家安全部有联系的女性爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang)。该委员会表示，“美国政府高层”的意见使其确信他的回国不会构成国家安全风险。

唐纳德·特朗普总统告诉《华尔街日报》，他直接并通过中间人游说董事会，英伟达股价下跌对他的案子有所帮助。该委员会在对黄的调查结束之前就采取了行动，而司法部正在对黄爱丽丝曾经经营的一家新加坡公司 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查，指控其将 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国。国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿表示，爱丽丝·黄也正在接受调查。

专家们告诉《连线》杂志，他们更担心黄的回归先例，而不是黄本人。有人说，现在对他的审查使得进一步妥协的可能性不大。但他们表示，北京可能已经深入了解了英伟达的芯片设计及其与白宫和国会的私人对话，或者通过 Megaspeed 自己获得了芯片，但没有人公开证实它获得了什么（如果有的话）。

一些人想知道谁向委员会提供了保证，依据是什么，以及政府是否进行了反情报损害评估，或者只是做出了政治判断。他们还表示，政府一再未能执行自己的出口管制，当情报担忧似乎屈服于市场压力时，美国对中国的警告开始听起来可以商量，这对北京有利。

伦敦国防智囊团皇家联合三军研究所的网络和技术研究员塔利亚·彼得森表示：“如果情报评估被视为被推翻、有选择地解释或出于政治或商业原因被公开驳回，这可能会损害人们对国家安全机构独立性的长期信心。” “这将损害美国的国家安全，并可能对北京有利。”

据《纽约时报》周日报道，在事件公开之前，顾问们至少两次向特朗普通报了黄爱丽与中国情报部门的联系，而特朗普两次都淡化了他们的担忧。当《华尔街日报》周一向他询问共和党议员如何看待黄仁勋的回归危及国家安全时，特朗普指出了英伟达股价的反弹。

美国外交关系委员会莫里斯·R·格林伯格地缘经济中心主任爱德华·菲什曼表示：“一些科技公司已经变得如此庞大，对股市也如此重要，以至于华盛顿不愿意追究它们对国家安全失误的责任。”

菲什曼在华尔街对制裁的缓慢思考中看到了类似的情况。 “经过多年的积极执法，银行才认真对待美国制裁合规问题，”他表示。 “我们在科技领域还没有看到任何类似的东西，这有助于解释为什么美国的出口管制仍然如此薄弱和漏洞百出。”他表示，在英伟达自己的调查得出结论之前，让黄先生恢复政府的保证“并不能激发人们对即将采取有意义的执法行动的信心”。

美国前贸易代表副助理艾米丽·基尔克里斯 (Emily Kilcrease) 现任新美国安全中心能源、经济和安全项目负责人，她表示，政府的记录没有理由相信这些保证的表面意义。 “我们不能依赖政府的判断，因为它在过去一年里一再未能执行出口管制，”她说。

周一，美国商务部将 Megaspeed 添加到贸易黑名单中，政府最近采取行动收紧对中国人工智能行业的规则。但基尔克里斯表示，它只是在压力下才采取行动。 “鉴于出口管制的不良记录以及他们对中国更广泛的包容主义立场，公平地问他们是否愿意真正执行新的管制措施，”她说。

董事会的保证似乎主要来自司法部。据《华尔街日报》报道，司法部长托德·布兰奇周六对特朗普和副总统万斯表示，黄既不是任何部门调查的目标，也不是任何部门调查的对象，该部门没有证据表明他违法或构成国家安全风险。据报道，万斯随后向董事会保证，政府不认为黄是威胁，并且他不会面临刑事指控。特朗普告诉《泰晤士报》，在推动黄回归之前，他还咨询了克莱顿。 （“我不能这样做，然后突然有人被起诉，”他说。）

英伟达没有立即回应《连线》杂志的置评请求。

黄是否违反任何法律与北京是否通过他获得任何利益是两个不同的问题。 “[这些保证]是否反映了情报界或联邦调查局的反情报损害评估，或者它们本质上是政治性的？”美国外交关系委员会技术和国家安全高级研究员杰西卡·布兰特（Jessica Brandt）表示，她曾担任国家情报总监办公室外国恶意影响中心的负责人。 “立法者应该对此施加压力。”

title: WiseTech’s White Cleared in Human Trafficking Probe by Police
title_en: WiseTech’s White Cleared in Human Trafficking Probe by Police
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
WiseTech Global Ltd (ASX:WTC) shares gained 3% to around $34.56 after the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) cleared founder Richard White and two employees following an almost year-long investigation into alleged insider trading. The corporate regulator issued no-action letters to all three individuals, although an investigation remains ongoing into another person who is not employed by WiseTech.

ASIC has also concluded a separate corporate governance investigation launched in late 2024, removing another regulatory uncertainty for the logistics software giant. Regulatory investigations continue WiseTech chair Raelene Murphy welcomed the resolution, describing it as another step towards allowing the company to focus on creating long-term shareholder value.

However, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) is continuing a separate investigation following a search of WiseTech's offices on August 19. The competition regulator has sought documents and electronic records relating to global logistics services and software as part of an investigation into potential breaches of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010.

No findings have been made against the company or any individual. WiseTech is also defending a shareholder class action concerning disclosures made in 2019. Separately, the Australian Federal Police's human exploitation taskforce continues to investigate allegations raised by Kathy Phelan, a former executive of Richard White-controlled company Kyckr, who stepped down last year.

澳大利亚证券和投资委员会 (ASIC) 在对涉嫌内幕交易进行了近一年的调查后，批准了 WiseTech Global Ltd (ASX:WTC) 创始人 Richard White 和两名员工的清查，该公司股价上涨 3%，至 34.56 美元左右。该公司监管机构向所有三人发出了不采取行动信函，但对另一名未受雇于慧咨科技的人员的调查仍在进行中。

ASIC 还完成了 2024 年底启动的一项单独的公司治理调查，消除了这家物流软件巨头的另一个监管不确定性。监管调查仍在继续 WiseTech 董事长 Raelene Murphy 对这项决议表示欢迎，称这是让公司专注于创造长期股东价值的又一步。

然而，澳大利亚竞争与消费者委员会 (ACCC) 在 8 月 19 日搜查慧咨科技的办公室后，仍在继续进行单独调查。竞争监管机构已寻求与全球物流服务和软件相关的文件和电子记录，作为对可能违反《2010 年竞争与消费者法》的调查的一部分。

目前还没有针对该公司或任何个人的调查结果。 WiseTech 还在为涉及 2019 年披露的股东集体诉讼进行辩护。另外，澳大利亚联邦警察的人类剥削特别工作组继续调查凯西·费兰 (Kathy Phelan) 提出的指控，凯西·费兰是理查德·怀特 (Richard White) 控制的公司 Kyckr 的前高管，于去年辞职。

author: Steven Nelson, Emily Goodin, and Marisa Schultz
article_content:
WASHINGTON — President Trump told The Post in an exclusive interview that he’s willing to pardon Jensen Huang if necessary — but that he believes the reinstalled Nvidia CEO should be fine without one and should “tell the truth” to Congress when he testifies next week.

Trump, who pressured the company’s board to take Huang back, took a victory lap after Nvidia’s stock surged Monday — inspecting the latest numbers at the Resolute Desk during the interview and noting the price ticked up in the afternoon, partially reversing a slump earlier Tuesday.

“That’s not bad, went down a couple of points,” Trump commented while reviewing the numbers. “It really picked up at the end.”

Huang doesn’t need to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights to avoid self-incrimination when he sits for an interview with the House Foreign Affairs Committee next Tuesday and appears before a hearing of the Senate Banking Committee next Thursday, Trump added.

“I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people,” Trump said.

“I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person.”

Asked about a pardon for any potential crimes, Trump said, “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”

Both Democratic and Republican members of Congress blasted the reinstatement of Huang before getting answers on whether he was a national security threat or violated export controls on shipping chips to communist China.

Angry lawmakers previewed a tough grilling of Huang with Louisiana Republican Sen. John Kennedy predicting Huang will plead the Fifth to avoid self-incrimination amid potential criminal prosecution.

Trump said that he hadn’t learned granular details of additional affairs that Huang admitted to before being restored as CEO — after the firestorm over his tryst with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang (no relation) and at least two company employees.

The president said, however, that it’s his understanding that Huang wasn’t sleeping with any other women with questionable links to Beijing.

“No, not from what I understand. I didn’t really get into it very much, to be honest with you. But no, from what I understand, no,” Trump replied.

He also said he didn’t know precisely how many affairs Huang fessed up to as part of his restoration.

“I really didn’t get into that. I got into the business of chips, much more than the business of sex,” Trump joked.

The president said that Nvidia’s success was essential to the US retaining an edge in artificial intelligence — and that he’s even open to the company giving the American government an equity stake, noting Intel handed over 10% of its value last year.

“I thought about it. I said, ‘You know, maybe I should do it,’ but I didn’t bring it up at this point. It’s probably not too late,” Trump said.

The president said he intervened to restore Huang, including by giving assurances that he faced no issues from the executive branch, because if Nvidia picked “the wrong person” to replace Huang, “that would be a terrible thing for our country in many ways.”

article_content_zh:
华盛顿——特朗普总统在接受《华盛顿邮报》独家采访时表示，如有必要，他愿意赦免黄仁勋，但他认为重新上任的英伟达首席执行官应该不会有任何问题，并且应该在下周作证时向国会“说出真相”。

在英伟达股价周一飙升后，特朗普向公司董事会施压，要求其重新接回黄仁勋，他在接受采访时检查了 Resolute Desk 的最新数据，发现股价在下午有所上涨，部分扭转了周二早些时候的暴跌。

“这还不错，下降了几个百分点，”特朗普在查看这些数字时评论道。 “最后真的恢复了。”

特朗普补充说，黄在下周二接受众议院外交事务委员会的采访以及下周四出席参议院银行委员会的听证会时，不需要援引第五修正案的权利来避免自证其罪。

“我认为他不需要拿第五。我认为这对人们来说是一个有趣的故事，”特朗普说。

“我想我希望他说实话，我的意思是，他的律师将不得不为他提供建议，但我一直发现他是 100% 光明正大的，你知道他是一个非常聪明的人。”

当被问及是否会赦免任何潜在的罪行时，特朗普说：“我想这总是一个选择，但我认为没有必要。”

国会民主党和共和党议员都对黄仁勋的复职进行了猛烈抨击，然后才得到关于黄仁勋是否构成国家安全威胁或违反向共产主义中国运送芯片的出口管制的答案。

愤怒的议员们预演了对黄的严厉拷问，路易斯安那州共和党参议员约翰·肯尼迪预测，黄将向第五法院求情，以避免在潜在的刑事起诉中自证其罪。

特朗普表示，在黄与被指控的中国间谍黄爱丽丝（无亲属关系）和至少两名公司员工的幽会引发轩然大波之后，他在恢复首席执行官职务之前还没有了解到黄所承认的其他事务的具体细节。

不过，总统表示，据他了解，黄没有与任何其他与北京有可疑联系的女性发生过关系。

“不，据我了解，不是。说实话，我并没有真正深入了解它。但不，据我了解，不，”特朗普回答道。

他还表示，他不知道黄到底承认了多少事，作为他复辟的一部分。

“我真的没有涉足这一领域。我涉足的是芯片行业，而不是性行业，”特朗普开玩笑说。

title: ‘The king is back!’ Huang’s return to Nvidia is greeted with relief in Asia.
title_en: ‘The king is back!’ Huang’s return to Nvidia is greeted with relief in Asia.
author: Sammy Westfall, Lyric Li, Huiyee Chiew, and Joshua Yang
article_content:
As Asian stocks rallied over the decision by Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, nowhere were the celebrations more ebullient than in China and Taiwan, where tech leaders, investors and even street market vendors hailed the AI executive as a hometown hero on whom the success of the tech industry — and global markets — relies.

Huang’s reinstatement, under direct pressure from President Donald Trump, seemed to avert a short-term diplomatic crisis — Beijing had forcefully denied allegations that his paramour Alice Huang was a Chinese operative — but left open serious questions about the White House’s handling of serious espionage concerns and potential investigations by the Democratic Congress that is set to take office in January.

News of Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy seemed to do little to dim the adoration many across Asia had for him.

The day's top stories, curated by Washington Post editors. Sign up for free

“The king is back!” read one headline by China’s state-affiliated financial news outlet Star Market Daily.

At least three Huang-related hashtags topped trends on the Chinese social media platform Weibo on Tuesday, as Japan’s Nikkei rose nearly 4 percent, Korea’s Kospi index gained more than 6 percent and Taiwan’s main stock market index gained nearly 9 percent.

“I’m so happy that [Huang] is making a comeback,” Duan Yongping, a Chinese American billionaire entrepreneur and value investor nicknamed the “Chinese Buffett,” posted on Xueqiu, a major Chinese investment social network and wealth management platform.

In the nearly two-week period of upheaval — from Huang’s resignation Nov. 12 to the board’s announcement Monday — people in Asia sent wishes for his return.

The message was particularly clear in Taiwan, where Huang was born before moving to the United States at age 9. Taipei 101, Taiwan’s tallest building, lit up with messages of support: “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” and “Thrive Together.” Representatives of Taiwan’s technology industry associations organized and funded the display.

At a temple to the matchmaker god Yue Lao in Taiwan’s Tainan, lanterns were lit for Huang to “cut off bad romantic relationships,” according to a local news station. The reason for this: “to save Taiwan’s stock market supply chain.”

On the other side of the world, Silicon Valley tech leaders including Elon Musk had also been backing Huang as the scandal unfolded. But his biggest cheerleader, it seemed, was Trump, who said he personally orchestrated the effort to reinstate Huang over the past several days.

Nvidia said in announcing Huang’s reinstatement that its board received input from “senior levels of the United States government.”

“The Trump administration’s intervention mattered enormously. If anything, it shows just how important Nvidia, and Huang at the center of it, have become to America’s AI ambitions,” said Lizzi C. Lee, a fellow on the Chinese economy at the Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis.

Huang’s return is good news for China’s AI industry, given its dependence on Nvidia and the importance of American technology to Chinese models, Lee said. Beijing’s leadership may also see the reinstatement “as reassurance that practical and commercial interests still carry the day in Washington, particularly with Trump.”

Others on Chinese social media met Huang’s reinstatement with celebratory humor.

One Shanghai-based user of China’s Jike social networking site wrote that “I wouldn’t be surprised if Jensen Huang announced a comeback in Avengers 5.”

“He took 3 days off to play [‘Grand Theft Auto VI’] and beat the game. Time for him to go back to work,” a commentator from Sichuan wrote on Weibo.

Many compared the fall and rise of Huang to the typical melodramatic underdog storylines of male leads in China’s viral short-form drama platform Hongguo. “I don’t watch Hongguo, but I bet even Hongguo can’t write a story as wild as his,” wrote a commentator from Beijing.

For many people in China, Huang’s return is seen “as a victory against those seeking to smear China,” said Zichen Wang, deputy secretary general of the Center for China and Globalization, a Beijing think tank. Huang had fought hard in Washington to secure the company’s right to sell its powerful artificial intelligence chips there, and his dismissal was widely perceived as politically motivated and “closely tied” to that advocacy, he said.

Huang’s reinstatement appears to have “galvanized” scrutiny of Nvidia among Democrats as they prepare to take control of Congress, Wang said. “Although their motivations may have more to do with domestic partisan battles, the practical consequence could be intensified congressional scrutiny of semiconductor exports, Nvidia’s operations and Huang himself,” he said.

The scandal showed that “even someone as formidable as Jensen Huang is still not trusted in America,” said Zhao Minghao, professor and deputy director of the Center for American Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai. “Chinese tech elites in America are merely needed, but not trusted.”

Trump’s apparent willingness to look past the allegations that Huang and Nvidia violated U.S. export controls on China stands in contrast to the tough line that the first Trump administration took when the Chinese firm Huawei Technologies was accused of breaching sanctions on Iran, as well as committing bank and wire fraud.

Trump on CNBC on Monday called Huang “a national treasure” and brought up the “vast amount of knowledge in his brain.”

“Nobody’s ever come back like this. … I’ve seen some unbelievably talented CEOs get thrown out because they were kissing somebody inappropriately at a game … and I’ve seen the company go through hell for 10 years, 15. They never got somebody back who was this good,” Trump said.

China is closely watching how Trump treats “genius entrepreneurs,” Zhao said. From Beijing’s perspective, what it saw as an attack on Huang was a combination of “anti-China, anti-Trump, especially Democratic, and anti-AI/Big Tech forces.”

Huang’s reinstatement means that the “U.S.-China tech rivalry will probably enter a more precise, more targeted phase,” he said.

“China won’t harbor any illusions, and won’t feel optimistic just because Jensen Huang has returned to Nvidia,” Zhao said. “Democrats may target China as a tool for striking at Trump. This is what Beijing is most worried about right now.”

article_content_zh:
随着亚洲股市因英伟达董事会决定恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官而上涨，中国和台湾的庆祝活动最为热烈，科技领袖、投资者甚至街头小贩都将这位人工智能高管视为家乡英雄，科技行业和全球市场的成功都依赖于他。

在唐纳德·特朗普总统的直接压力下，黄的复职似乎避免了一场短期的外交危机——北京方面强力否认了有关他的情人黄爱丽是中国特工的指控——但对白宫处理严重间谍问题的方式以及定于一月上任的民主党国会可能进行的调查留下了严重的疑问。

黄与一名所谓的中国间谍有染的消息似乎并没有削弱亚洲许多人对他的崇拜。

当天的头条新闻，由《华盛顿邮报》编辑策划。免费注册

“王回来了！”中国官方财经新闻媒体《星报日报》的一则头条新闻写道。

周二，至少三个与黄相关的话题标签成为中国社交媒体平台微博上的热门话题，其中日本日经指数上涨近 4%，韩国 Kospi 指数上涨超过 6%，台湾主要股市指数上涨近 9%。

“我很高兴（黄）卷土重来，”绰号“中国巴菲特”的美籍华裔亿万富翁企业家和价值投资者段永平在中国主要投资社交网络和财富管理平台雪球上发帖称。

从黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞职到董事会周一宣布这一消息，在近两周的动荡期间，亚洲人民纷纷祝福他回归。

这一信息在台湾尤为明显，黄在台湾出生，9 岁移居美国。台湾最高的建筑台北 101 亮起了支持的信息：“台湾 ♡ 詹森”、“家庭 ♡ 友谊”和“共同繁荣”。台湾科技产业协会的代表组织并资助了这次展览。

据当地一家新闻台报道，在台湾台南的一座月老庙里，人们为黄点燃灯笼，以“断绝不良的恋爱关系”。理由是：“拯救台湾股市供应链”。

在世界的另一边，丑闻曝光后，包括埃隆·马斯克在内的硅谷科技领袖也一直支持黄。但他最大的支持者似乎是特朗普，特朗普表示过去几天他亲自策划了恢复黄的工作。

英伟达在宣布黄仁勋复职时表示，其董事会收到了“美国政府高层”的意见。

亚洲协会政策研究所中国分析中心的中国经济研究员 Lizzi C. Lee 表示：“特朗普政府的干预非常重要。如果说有什么影响的话，那就是它表明了英伟达以及其核心人物黄仁勋对美国的人工智能雄心有多么重要。”

李说，考虑到中国人工智能行业对英伟达的依赖以及美国技术对中国模式的重要性，黄仁勋的回归对中国人工智能行业来说是个好消息。北京领导层也可能将这一恢复视为“一种保证，即华盛顿的实际和商业利益仍然占上风，尤其是特朗普的利益”。

title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
title_en: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
author: Anthropic
article_content:
Starting today, you can use Claude artifacts to create, run, and share desktop apps. The "Install as app" feature is rolling out in beta in Claude for Mac and Windows.

When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer. You choose how much to allow.

Each app can use Claude and your connectors, and it updates automatically when the underlying artifact is edited. This simplifies the process for building and maintaining apps for both knowledge workers and developers. Requests the app makes to Claude count toward your plan’s usage limits.

Artifacts started out as a work output you’d share, like a chart or a webpage. People now use them as tools for everyday work, like a meeting prep page that regularly pulls from their calendar and email, or a tracker for the orders that need to ship that day.

If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention.

### What installed apps can do

Installed apps can send notifications or add items to your menu bar or system tray. You choose permissions for each app, and Team and Enterprise admins can turn app permissions and full access on or off for their organization.

People at Anthropic have used these to make:

• Linnet (opens in new tab), a full layered image editor

• Phosphor (opens in new tab), a file manager that looks made for a movie set

• Sift (opens in new tab), which sets up folder rules and uses Claude to keep your stuff organized

• Tern (opens in new tab), a terminal with Claude by your side to help and explain

• Vitals (opens in new tab), a menu bar and tray app for peeking at your computer’s performance

You can see more demo apps made by one of our engineers here (opens in new tab).

### Permissions

There are three levels of permissions:

• Default: Installed apps can only do what they’d be able to do in a browser.

• App permissions: Apps can ask to use common features that Claude can tightly control, like creating always-on-top windows, listening for global shortcuts, or sending notifications.

• Full computer access: Apps can ask to run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time.

Your permission only covers the current version of the app, so Claude asks again after every update, even your own edits. If part of an app comes from another website, that part can change without Claude asking you again.

You can only give full access to apps you made or, on Team and Enterprise, apps made by people in your organization. Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust.

### Getting started

Describe your app to Claude, try it as an artifact, and then click "Install as app." You don’t have to package or sign it, and it uses your Claude account, so there’s no API key or separate login.

Install as app is rolling out in beta on all plans. HIPAA-ready organizations and hybrid deployments can’t use it. It’s on by default for Team, with full access off. On Enterprise, it’s off until an owner turns it on. You need to be online and signed in to Claude to open an app. Some artifacts can’t be installed, including Claude Docs, Slides, and Sheets.

Update Claude for Mac or Windows, open an artifact you use every day, and choose "Install as app" from the Share menu.
