title: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand
title_en: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand

inline_images.caption: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand

author: Reuters
article_content:
Nov 24 (Reuters) – Dell Technologies on Tuesday raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts for the third time this year after record quarterly results, fueled by soaring enterprise demand for AI infrastructure.

Shares of Dell were up about 5% in extended trading after the company’s board also approved an additional $25 billion share repurchase plan.

The Texas-based company has been benefiting from the generative AI boom, as more businesses and cloud providers are buying Dell’s AI servers, which are powered by Nvidia chips, to run complex AI workloads and autonomous agents.

For fiscal 2027, Dell now expects revenue of $202 billion, above its prior target of $192 billion and Wall Street expectations of $194.48 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company also raised its annual AI-optimized server revenue forecast to $78 billion from $74 billion and its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $29.68 from $25.50.

Rival PC maker HP on Tuesday reported fourth-quarter revenue of $16 billion, beating analysts’ average estimate of $15.42 billion, driven by AI-powered device shipments and commercial PC demand.

Dell, meanwhile, reported slower growth in its PC business as customers prioritized spending on servers and storage. Its PC unit revenue rose 3% to $12.89 billion in the third quarter ended October 30, compared with 20% growth in the previous three months.

Both Dell and HP warned of continued memory cost pressures, with Dell expecting the memory chip shortage to continue into 2027.

Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group, which houses its server and storage operations, largely drove the gains in the company’s profit and growth, with revenue from the segment nearly tripling to $41.97 billion in the third quarter.

Enterprises are “buying more compute to accommodate growing workloads, refreshing their installed base and modernizing their data centers to free up power and space to be positioned for the AI era,” said Jeff Clarke, Dell’s chief operating officer.

Dell’s record third-quarter revenue of $54.94 billion exceeded analysts’ average estimate of $49.32 billion. Its adjusted EPS of $9.45 also topped estimates of $6.59.

Clarke said demand continues to accelerate and broaden globally, with more than 7,500 customers deploying Dell AI Factories, a bundle that combines servers, storage, networking and software to help businesses build and run AI models.

Dell ended the third quarter with a record $132.3 billion in AI server backlog after logging $60.2 billion in new orders during the period.

article_content_zh:
11 月 24 日（路透社）——在企业对人工智能基础设施需求飙升的推动下，戴尔科技集团在创纪录的季度业绩后，周二第三次上调了年度收入和利润预测。

在公司董事会还批准了额外的 250 亿美元股票回购计划后，戴尔股价在盘后交易中上涨了约 5%。

这家总部位于德克萨斯州的公司一直受益于生成式人工智能的繁荣，因为越来越多的企业和云提供商正在购买由 Nvidia 芯片驱动的戴尔人工智能服务器，以运行复杂的人工智能工作负载和自主代理。

根据 LSEG 汇编的数据，戴尔目前预计 2027 财年营收为 2020 亿美元，高于其先前目标 1920 亿美元和华尔街预期的 1944.8 亿美元。

该公司还将人工智能优化服务器年度收入预期从 740 亿美元上调至 780 亿美元，调整后每股收益预期从 25.50 美元上调至 29.68 美元。

其竞争对手 PC 制造商惠普周二公布第四季度营收为 160 亿美元，超过分析师平均预期的 154.2 亿美元，这主要得益于人工智能设备出货量和商用 PC 需求。

与此同时，戴尔报告称，由于客户优先考虑服务器和存储方面的支出，其个人电脑业务增长放缓。截至 10 月 30 日的第三季度，其 PC 部门收入增长 3%，达到 128.9 亿美元，而前三个月增长 20%。

戴尔和惠普都警告内存成本压力持续存在，戴尔预计内存芯片短缺将持续到 2027 年。

戴尔的基础设施解决方案集团负责其服务器和存储业务，在很大程度上推动了该公司的利润和增长，第三季度该部门的收入几乎增长了两倍，达到 419.7 亿美元。

戴尔首席运营官杰夫·克拉克(Jeff Clarke)表示，企业正在“购买更多的计算设备来适应不断增长的工作负载，更新其安装基础并对数据中心进行现代化改造，以释放电力和空间，为人工智能时代做好准备”。

戴尔第三季度营收达到创纪录的 549.4 亿美元，超过分析师平均预期的 493.2 亿美元。其调整后每股收益为 9.45 美元，也高于预期的 6.59 美元。

Clarke 表示，全球需求持续加速和扩大，超过 7,500 家客户部署了 Dell AI Factory，这是一个结合了服务器、存储、网络和软件的捆绑包，可帮助企业构建和运行 AI 模型。

戴尔在第三季度录得 602 亿美元的新订单后，AI 服务器积压金额达到创纪录的 1,323 亿美元。

title: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Planting Bug Released on Bond
title_en: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Planting Bug Released on Bond

inline_images.caption: Image: U.S. v. Abdulrahman Alfozan via DOJ
inline_images.alt: Image: U.S. v. Abdulrahman Alfozan via DOJ

inline_images.caption: Image: U.S. v. Abdulrahman Alfozan via DOJ
inline_images.alt: Image: U.S. v. Abdulrahman Alfozan via DOJ

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Federal prosecutors have charged a former OpenAI engineer with planting a concealed audio recorder in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco office, allegedly to capture sensitive communications about its artificial intelligence technology.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national who joined OpenAI in July 2025, was arrested on October 9, 2026, and made his first federal court appearance on October 13. He faces a charge of using or attempting to use a surveillance app to intercept oral communications.

What prosecutors describe is a low-tech approach to one of the most closely watched companies in the AI industry.

Prosecutors allege Alfozan installed the device around September 28, connecting it through a USB port on the back of a conference room television. According to the complaint, it was concealed in toilet paper and contained encrypted material.

OpenAI personnel discovered the device on or about September 30. The investigation did not end there.

Prosecutors allege Alfozan appeared near or returned to the conference-room area on October 5. CCTV footage reportedly showed him near the conference room, and OpenAI security personnel that same day found an unattended bag containing his wallet, identification, and a second recording device similar to the first.

Prosecutors also allege, according to the criminal complaint, that chatbot activity associated with Alfozan or an account linked to his spouse included recorded research queries. Those queries reportedly covered building, customizing, installing, disguising, remotely accessing, and encrypting a continuous audio recorder.

OpenAI turned its own technology on the problem, but the investigation ultimately belonged to law enforcement.

OpenAI fired Alfozan and referred the matter to the FBI. According to OpenAI, the company used its own AI models to help analyze the device and identify the source. Those internal findings fed into a broader investigation that law enforcement ultimately took over.

The AI-assisted analysis did not independently establish criminal guilt; it was one component of an investigation that also relied on CCTV footage and physical evidence.

Critically, OpenAI stated it found no indication that model weights, source code, or confidential files had been improperly accessed or removed. That distinction matters.

Physical access to an executive conference room and digital access to core AI systems are two separate threat surfaces. Prosecutors allege the former was compromised in this case; OpenAI says the latter was not.

If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum of five years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and three years of supervised release. Those are statutory maximums, not a forecast of any eventual sentence. No defense position was identified in the sources reviewed for this article.

The case is a pointed reminder that even technically sophisticated organizations remain vulnerable to physical-access threats. An encrypted device plugged into a USB port and placed in a room used for confidential discussions can represent a serious security exposure, regardless of how robust the surrounding digital infrastructure may be.

article_content_zh:
联邦检察官指控一名前 OpenAI 工程师在该公司旧金山办事处的行政会议室中安装了隐藏的录音机，据称是为了捕获有关其人工智能技术的敏感通信。

Abdulrahman Alfozan，35 岁，沙特公民，于 2025 年 7 月加入 OpenAI，于 2026 年 10 月 9 日被捕，并于 10 月 13 日首次出庭联邦法庭。他面临使用或试图使用监控应用程序拦截口头通信的指控。

检察官所描述的是对人工智能行业最受关注的公司之一采取的低技术手段。

检察官称 Alfozan 在 9 月 28 日左右安装了该设备，通过会议室电视背面的 USB 端口连接。根据投诉，它被隐藏在卫生纸中并包含加密材料。

OpenAI 人员于 9 月 30 日左右发现了该设备。调查并未就此结束。

检察官指控阿尔福赞于 10 月 5 日出现在会议室附近或返回会议室区域。据报道，闭路电视录像显示他在会议室附近，OpenAI 安全人员当天发现了一个无人看管的包，里面装有他的钱包、身份证件和与第一个类似的第二个录音设备。

根据刑事起诉书，检察官还声称，与阿尔福赞或与其配偶相关的账户相关的聊天机器人活动包括记录的研究查询。据报道，这些查询涵盖了构建、定制、安装、伪装、远程访问和加密连续录音机。

OpenAI 利用自己的技术来解决这个问题，但调查最终属于执法部门。

OpenAI 解雇了 Alfozan，并将此事提交给 FBI。据 OpenAI 称，该公司使用自己的人工智能模型来帮助分析设备并识别来源。这些内部调查结果被纳入执法部门最终接管的更广泛的调查中。

人工智能辅助分析并未独立确立刑事犯罪；这是一项调查的一部分，该调查也依赖于闭路电视录像和物证。

至关重要的是，OpenAI 表示，没有发现任何迹象表明模型权重、源代码或机密文件被不当访问或删除。这种区别很重要。

对行政会议室的物理访问和对核心人工智能系统的数字访问是两个独立的威胁面。检察官称前者在本案中受到损害；后者在本案中受到损害。 OpenAI 表示后者并非如此。

如果罪名成立，阿尔福赞将面临最高五年的监禁、25万美元的罚款和三年的监管释放。这些是法定最高刑罚，而不是对任何最终刑罚的预测。本文审查的来源中没有指出辩护立场。

该案例尖锐地提醒我们，即使技术先进的组织也仍然容易受到物理访问威胁。插入 USB 端口并放置在用于机密讨论的房间中的加密设备可能会带来严重的安全隐患，无论周围的数字基础设施有多强大。

article_content:
NEW YORK (AP) — A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiring to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks as it grew into one of the world’s biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.

But jurors acquitted Huawei of the most serious charge: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy, a result that the company’s lawyer said was a “profound rejection” of the government’s narrative that it was corrupt from top to bottom and had a corporate culture of cheating, stealing and lying.

Prosecutors had used the charge, commonly found in organized crime and drug cases, to accuse Huawei of operating illicitly to poach intellectual property and technological secrets from competitors and partners.

The convictions covered allegations that the company did business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions — including Iran and North Korea — and made false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

In all, Huawei was convicted on 10 of 12 counts. The case in Brooklyn federal court involved no human defendants, but the company could be made to pay billions of dollars in penalties when it is sentenced next September.

“Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering U.S. national security, violating the sanctity of U.S. commerce, and impeding the enforcement of U.S. laws,” Brooklyn U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. said in a statement.

“No person or company is above the law,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said.

Huawei’s lawyers said U.S. investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of the company’s more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that didn’t actually exist.

Taiwan warns Canada’s Carney that deeper ties with China come with risks 3 MIN READ 53 China’s Huawei Technologies faces racketeering trial in New York 2 MIN READ 27 Huawei lawyer Brian Heberlig said the company would appeal the convictions but was heartened by the acquittals on racketeering conspiracy and another charge, conspiracy to obstruct justice. He called those not guilty verdicts “a vindication of the company and its good-faith compliance culture.”

“The allegations that the government made in this case overreached and simply weren’t consistent with the successful, innovative and hardworking company that we came to know and deeply respect,” Heberlig said outside the courthouse.

It’s unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei’s global fortunes. The company hasn’t been allowed to sell equipment to U.S. carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and Britain.

That hasn’t stopped the company from doing a robust business elsewhere. Its smartphones and other telecom equipment are sold globally. More recently, it has expanded into chipmaking as the boom in artificial intelligence fuels demand for microprocessors, becoming an important alternative in China to chips made by companies such as Nvidia.

“Huawei has always adhered to integrity in business, upheld business ethics, respected intellectual property, and remained committed to complying with all applicable laws and regulations,” the company said in a statement.

“We remain focused on serving our customers and partners and ensuring continuous and stable business operations,” the statement said.

The U.S. announced its criminal charges against Huawei in early 2019 and later expanded the allegations. The lengthy trial began in September.

Chinese officials said the U.S. has engaged in “economic bullying” and improperly used national security as a pretext for oppressing Chinese companies.

The indictment against Huawei accused it of a long pattern of outright technology thefts.

Huawei, prosecutors said, once sold internet routers containing source code copied from a competitor. In another episode, a person working for Huawei slipped into a competitor’s booth at a Chicago trade show to surreptitiously photograph the circuits inside another company’s networking device, the indictment said.

Prosecutors said that on another occasion, a Huawei worker removed a robotic arm from a competitor’s lab so it could be photographed and measured.

The victim companies included Cisco Systems, Motorola Solutions, T-Mobile, Quintel USA and Fujitsu, according to court records.

“The tone was set at the top by Huawei leaders and executives who themselves engaged in criminal conduct, like lying to Congress, lying to banks, violating U.S. sanctions and trying to interfere with the very criminal investigation that led to this case,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa told the jury at the trial.

In its statement, Huawei referred to those matters as “trade secret-related disputes” that were the subject of civil litigation that was resolved over the past two decades.

“No court ever found Huawei liable for willful intellectual property misappropriation, and the company was never ordered to pay damages for trade secret misappropriation,” the company said.

In his closing argument to jurors, Huawei’s lawyer said prosecutors leaned on “innuendo and facts ripped out of context,” and testimony from ex-employees “with a bone to pick,” to pursue a company that had relied on “hard work, innovation and competition” to succeed.

“Huawei didn’t steal its way to success,” Heberlig said, noting that much of the material the U.S. alleges was stolen was already public.

“You can’t steal a secret that isn’t a secret,” he said.

He said Huawei paid billions of dollars in licensing fees over the years, with 75% of that money going to U.S. companies, and had reprimanded or fired employees found to have engaged in wrongdoing.

Heberlig noted that lines of Cisco source code turned up in Huawei software more than two decades ago. He said when the source-code copying was discovered, Huawei recalled routers sold in the U.S. and offered to replace them with Cisco routers and created a “compliance culture that permeates Huawei today.”

No individual executives or employees faced trial, although prosecutors at one point also brought criminal charges against Huawei’s chief financial officer, Meng Wanzhou. They accused her of misleading HSBC bank about the company’s business dealings in Iran.

Meng, the daughter of Huawei’s founder, was arrested in Canada in 2018, but ultimately was allowed to return to China in 2021 in a prisoner swap that freed two Canadians held by China. As part of the deal, the U.S. dropped its case against Meng.

The trial in New York overlapped with a summit between President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin in the technology-centric city of Shenzhen, China.

article_content_zh:
纽约（美联社）——美国陪审团周二判定中国科技巨头华为技术有限公司合谋窃取商业机密和欺诈银行，该公司已成长为全球最大的无线电信网络设备供应商之一。

但陪审团宣判华为无罪，罪名是参与犯罪敲诈勒索阴谋，该公司的律师表示，这一结果是对政府说法的“深刻反驳”，即该公司从上到下腐败，并具有欺骗、盗窃和撒谎的企业文化。

检察官利用这一常见于有组织犯罪和毒品案件的指控，指控华为非法经营，从竞争对手和合作伙伴那里窃取知识产权和技术机密。

这些定罪涉及指控该公司在受美国制裁的国家（包括伊朗和朝鲜）开展业务，并向美国政府官员和银行做出虚假陈述，以掩盖其不当行为。

华为总共被定罪 12 项罪名中的 10 项。布鲁克林联邦法院的案件没有涉及人类被告，但该公司在明年 9 月宣判时可能会被要求支付数十亿美元的罚款。

布鲁克林美国检察官小约瑟夫·诺塞拉 (Joseph Nocella Jr.) 在一份声明中表示，“很少有罪行比华为数十年来危害美国国家安全、侵犯美国商业的神圣性和阻碍美国法律执行的行为更严重。”

“没有任何人或公司可以凌驾于法律之上，”司法部长托德·布兰奇说。

华为律师表示，美国调查人员利用该公司20万多名员工中少数人的个别不当行为，编造了一个实际上并不存在的大阴谋的虚假叙述。

台湾警告加拿大卡尼，加深与中国的关系会带来风险 3 MIN READ 53 中国华为技术有限公司在纽约面临敲诈勒索审判 2 MIN READ 27 华为律师 Brian Heberlig 表示，该公司将对定罪提出上诉，但对敲诈勒索串谋和另一项串谋妨碍司法公正的指控无罪释放感到鼓舞。他称这些无罪判决“证明了公司及其诚信合规文化”。

赫伯利格在法院外表示：“政府在本案中提出的指控有些过分，与我们所了解并深深尊敬的这家成功、创新和勤奋的公司完全不符。”

目前尚不清楚该判决可能会对华为的全球命运产生什么影响。出于安全考虑，该公司多年来一直不允许向美国运营商出售设备。它还被包括加拿大和英国在内的其他西方盟友列入黑名单。

但这并没有阻止该公司在其他地方开展强劲的业务。其智能手机和其他电信设备销往全球。最近，随着人工智能的繁荣刺激了对微处理器的需求，它已扩展到芯片制造领域，成为中国英伟达等公司制造的芯片的重要替代品。

该公司在一份声明中表示：“华为始终坚守商业诚信，维护商业道德，尊重知识产权，并始终致力于遵守所有适用的法律法规。”

声明称：“我们仍然专注于为客户和合作伙伴提供服务，确保业务持续稳定运营。”

title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows
title_en: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
Anthropic now lets you install Claude Artifacts as Mac or Windows apps. The feature is in beta as of today and requires the latest version of Claude for macOS or Windows. You build an Artifact in chat and keep it in the dock without writing any code.

The installed apps can use OS APIs, connectors, and Claude itself. That lets an app add menu bar items, create transparent windows, and send notifications, among other things. Examples include custom terminals, file managers, and video editors. Several demos are available to try.

Anthropic's Felix Rieseberg wrote on X that you need a Claude account and the Claude app for now, though a free account is enough. If you have an Apple Developer account, you can also have Claude build a standalone app.

title: Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan
title_en: Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan
author: Kif Leswing and Seema Mody
article_content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Tuesday struck a conciliatory and remorseful tone while leading his first employee meeting since being reinstated, and said how sorry he was for what he had done.

Huang told employees that he let them down and promised to do a better job the second time around, according to people inside the room, who asked not to be named in order to share details. "I hurt all of you,"Huang said, according to one of the people.

The CEO also addressed succession planning during the event, the people said. He told staff that Nvidia has built a team that doesn't require succession planning the way a normal organization does, because the company operates a unique business model where there are multiple capable leaders at Nvidia that are leading different parts of the organization.

A succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy, Huang said, according to one of the people present.

Investors and analysts were left to speculate about the company's future leadership in the wake of Huang's resignation on Nov. 12.

On Monday, Huang was reinstated as CEO of the chipmaker by Nvidia's board of directors. Eleven days before, Huang had resigned from Nvidia after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, said last week that Huang resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms."

Huang started the meeting by thanking CFO Colette Kress for her leadership as interim CEO.

Huang told staff that Tuesday's company meeting was the second hardest meeting of his life, the first one being with his wife. He said he is in therapy, according to one of the people present.

In a press release announcing Huang's return on Monday, the company said the board "received input"from senior officials in the federal government about any potential national security risk around the CEO. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he gave the board assurances and "made the deal"to restore Huang to his post.

After the company had its worst week in the stock market since 2008, the stock surged more than 30% the day his return was announced. Shares fell on Tuesday, however.

An Nvidia representative didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

article_content_zh:
周二，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在主持复职后的首次员工会议时，语气中流露出安抚和悔恨之情，并表示他对自己的所作所为感到非常抱歉。

据房间内不愿透露姓名的人士透露，黄告诉员工，他让他们失望了，并承诺第二次会做得更好。据一位知情人士透露，黄说：“我伤害了你们所有人。”

知情人士称，首席执行官还在活动期间谈到了继任计划。他告诉员工，英伟达已经建立了一支不需要像正常组织那样进行继任计划的团队，因为该公司采用独特的商业模式，英伟达有多名有能力的领导者，他们领导着组织的不同部门。

据一位在场人士透露，黄说，继任计划会产生不必要的等级制度。

黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞职后，投资者和分析师纷纷猜测该公司未来的领导层。

周一，黄仁勋被英伟达董事会恢复担任该芯片制造商首席执行官。十一天前，黄仁勋在多起婚外情报道后辞去了英伟达的职务，其中包括与一名被指控为北京间谍的中国女商人的婚外情。

英伟达新任命的董事会主席哈维·琼斯上周表示，黄仁勋在“披露了不符合公司行为准则、标准和文化规范的个人行为”后辞职。

黄在会议开始时首先感谢首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 作为临时首席执行官的领导。

黄告诉员工，周二的公司会议是他一生中第二艰难的会议，第一次是和妻子的会议。据一位在场人士透露，他说他正在接受治疗。

该公司在周一宣布黄仁勋回归的新闻稿中表示，董事会“收到了联邦政府高级官员关于首席执行官周围任何潜在国家安全风险的意见”。唐纳德·特朗普总统告诉 CNBC，他向董事会做出了保证，并“达成协议”让黄继续担任职务。

在经历了自 2008 年以来股市最糟糕的一周后，在他宣布回归的当天，该公司股价飙升了 30% 以上。然而，周二股价下跌。

英伟达代表没有立即回应置评请求。

title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
title_en: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas.

During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.

Along with attempting to dismiss Trump’s involvement, Huang reportedly said he also didn’t return because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.” He added that, “no story has been more tortured than this one in human history,” Kabas reports. Instead, Huang said the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation,” while receiving assurance from the government that he posed no national security threat, according to the NYT.

Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12th, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees, including vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. On Monday, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and member of the board — a decision the White House said Trump was “totally involved in.” Trump also confirmed that he worked with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, were also in favor of Huang’s return.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the government “has no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a risk to national security, adding that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” that he engaged in “unlawful conduct.” Nvidia is still facing an investigation over its accounting practices, according to Reuters. The company is also carrying out its own internal investigation surrounding reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st to answer questions about national security concerns, and Democrats are already planning to press Huang about his return, as well as Trump’s involvement.

Even after all this, Huang reportedly said he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.” He also acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct, adding that he is attending therapy daily, Bloomberg reports. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang said, according to the NYT. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”

article_content_zh:
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在回到公司后的第一次全体会议上向员工道歉，同时试图与白宫和科技领导人帮助他重新获得工作的说法保持距离。

据报道，在会议期间，黄称有关唐纳德·特朗普总统直接参与他复职的说法——特朗普本人公开宣传的想法——“完全不真实”。他补充说，“不要再认为政治在公司中发挥了作用。我们是最不关心政治的公司，”卡巴斯说。

据报道，黄除了试图否认特朗普的参与之外，还表示他没有回来，因为他是一个“高于法律”或“高于行为准则”的“科技兄弟”。卡巴斯报道说，他补充说，“人类历史上没有比这更令人痛苦的故事了”。据《纽约时报》报道，黄仁勋表示，英伟达董事会“评估了整个情况”，同时得到了政府的保证，称他不会对国家安全构成威胁。

黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞去英伟达首席执行官一职，此前有报道称，黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国间谍和包括医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔 (Kimberly Powell) 在内的两名员工有染。周一，英伟达宣布恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官、总裁和董事会成员职务——白宫称特朗普“完全参与了这一决定”。特朗普还证实，他与副总统万斯和其他官员合作，将黄带回。包括特斯拉首席执行官埃隆·马斯克、Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼和前白宫人工智能沙皇大卫·萨克斯在内的一大批科技领袖也支持黄仁勋的回归。

特朗普在《Truth Social》上发表的一篇文章中表示，政府“没有理由相信”黄的回归对国家安全构成风险，并补充说美国司法部长“没有证据”证明他从事“非法行为”。据路透社报道，英伟达仍面临对其会计实践的调查。该公司还针对有关黄是中国间谍阴谋目标的报道进行内部调查。黄将于 12 月 1 日在国会作证，回答有关国家安全问题的问题，民主党人已经计划就黄的回归以及特朗普的参与向黄施加压力。

据报道，即使在这一切之后，黄说他“不相信继任计划”。据彭博社报道，他还承认自己违反了英伟达的行为准则，并补充说他每天都在接受治疗。据《纽约时报》报道，黄说：“我犯了一些可怕的错误。” “我对洛瑞不忠，我伤害了我的孩子，当然，我也伤害了你们所有人。”

title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents
title_en: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents

inline_images.caption: "Skills over MCP"(beta) lets servers provide specialized knowledge tailored to users or organizations alongside tools and resources. Skills load only when needed and update with the server. | Image: Anthropic
inline_images.caption_en: "Skills over MCP"(beta) lets servers provide specialized knowledge tailored to users or organizations alongside tools and resources. Skills load only when needed and update with the server. | Image: Anthropic

inline_images.caption: With "Tasks,"Claude hands off lengthy jobs to an MCP server, keeps working in the meantime, and picks up the result once it's ready. | Image: Anthropic
inline_images.caption_en: With "Tasks,"Claude hands off lengthy jobs to an MCP server, keeps working in the meantime, and picks up the result once it's ready. | Image: Anthropic

author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
Anthropic reports more than 700 million monthly downloads for its MCP standard two years after launch. New features such as background tasks, follow-up questions for users, and file uploads are designed to let Claude work more independently.

The company says the standard now tops 700 million monthly downloads of its developer tools (SDK) and more than 10,000 MCP connectors for Claude. Anthropic is expanding the protocol so AI agents can communicate with each other and coordinate workflows more smoothly.

"Tasks"and "Elicitation"rank among the biggest additions, reaching general availability after a public test in October. With Tasks, a server can run a longer job in the background and report back only when the result is ready. Elicitation lets a running process pause and ask the user for specific missing details. Both features are meant to let MCP servers operate more independently.

### AI agents could soon pass files directly to external services

Skills over MCP is also new and in public beta for now. The feature lets servers pair their tools with skills that guide Claude through long, multistep tasks. Anthropic says these skills cover best practices, step-by-step workflows, and instructions tailored to a specific user account or organization.

The company also announced that file upload support is coming soon. Once it ships, Claude will be able to pass files such as PDFs, spreadsheets, and images directly to MCP servers. Anthropic plans to roll the feature out shortly in Claude and Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers, and for eligible Team and Enterprise customers.

### Technical changes lay the groundwork for larger MCP deployments

These new agent features build on several technical changes Anthropic made over the past year. To cut memory demands during active conversations, Tool Search waits to load individual tool descriptions until they're needed. Anthropic says this can reduce context usage by more than 85 percent in multi-server setups.

The current MCP specification is stateless, meaning it doesn't have to store session data permanently. It works across all Claude products. The goal is to make servers easier for developers to build and more reliable to run as usage grows.

Anthropic has also rolled out Enterprise Managed Auth for business customers. Admins can approve supported servers once so employees connect automatically. MCP Apps lets developers embed full user interfaces inside Claude, either beside the active chat or in full-screen mode.

In November 2024, Anthropic introduced the Model Context Protocol as an open standard that gives AI assistants uniform access to business tools, development environments, and other data sources. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced in March 2025 that his company would adopt its rival's standard across its own products. In May 2025, OpenAI upgraded its Responses API with remote MCP servers. Researchers at the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory used MCP as a model for the Science Context Protocol (SCP), introduced in January 2026.

title_zh: Anthropic强化MCP协议推动AI代理自治
summary_zh: Anthropic宣布MCP标准月下载量超7亿，并新增后台任务与文件上传功能，大幅提升AI代理间协作能力
article_content_zh:
Anthropic 报告称，其 MCP 标准推出两年后每月下载量超过 7 亿次。后台任务、用户跟进问题、文件上传等新功能旨在让克劳德更加独立地工作。

该公司表示，该标准的开发工具 (SDK) 每月下载量已超过 7 亿次，Claude 的 MCP 连接器下载量已超过 10,000 个。 Anthropic 正在扩展该协议，以便人工智能代理可以相互通信并更顺畅地协调工作流程。

“任务”和“启发”是最大的新增功能之一，在 10 月份的公开测试后正式上线。通过任务，服务器可以在后台运行更长的作业，并仅在结果准备就绪时才报告。启发可以让正在运行的进程暂停并询问用户特定的缺失细节。这两个功能都是为了让 MCP 服务器更加独立地运行。

### 人工智能代理很快就能将文件直接传递给外部服务

MCP 技能也是新的，目前处于公开测试阶段。该功能使服务器能够将他们的工具与技能相结合，指导克劳德完成长期、多步骤的任务。 Anthropic 表示，这些技能涵盖最佳实践、分步工作流程以及针对特定用户帐户或组织量身定制的说明。

该公司还宣布即将推出文件上传支持。发货后，Claude 将能够将 PDF、电子表格和图像等文件直接传递到 MCP 服务器。 Anthropic 计划很快在 Claude 和 Claude Code 中为 Pro、Max 和 Ultra 订阅者以及符合条件的团队和企业客户推出该功能。

### 技术变革为更大规模的 MCP 部署奠定了基础

这些新的代理功能建立在 Anthropic 在过去一年中所做的多项技术变革的基础上。为了减少活动对话期间的内存需求，工具搜索会等待加载各个工具描述，直到需要它们为止。 Anthropic 表示，这可以在多服务器设置中减少 85% 以上的上下文使用。

当前的 MCP 规范是无状态的，这意味着它不必永久存储会话数据。它适用于所有 Claude 产品。目标是让开发人员更容易构建服务器，并随着使用量的增长而更可靠地运行。

Anthropic 还为企业客户推出了企业托管身份验证。管理员可以一次性批准支持的服务器，以便员工自动连接。 MCP Apps 允许开发人员在 Claude 内部嵌入完整的用户界面，无论是在活动聊天旁边还是在全屏模式下。

2024 年 11 月，Anthropic 推出了模型上下文协议作为开放标准，使 AI 助手能够统一访问业务工具、开发环境和其他数据源。 OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 于 2025 年 3 月宣布，他的公司将在自己的产品中采用竞争对手的标准。 2025 年 5 月，OpenAI 使用远程 MCP 服务器升级了其 Responses API。上海人工智能实验室的研究人员使用 MCP 作为 2026 年 1 月推出的科学上下文协议 (SCP) 的模型。

title: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film
title_en: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film
author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
article_content:
Though David Fincher’s fans had been eagerly anticipating The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, early screenings of the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel starring Brad Pitt have raised questions about whether generative AI was used in the film. People have claimed that the movie is chock-full of uncanny, inconsistent visuals that make it feel more like slop than the sort of polished film you’d expect from the director of sleek productions like Fight Club and The Social Network.

Following a number of Cliff Booth critics screenings that took place last week ahead of the film’s premiere on November 25th, moviegoers rushed to social media to lament what they saw. One of the most vocal reactions came from YouTuber / director Patrick Tomasso, who said on X that he walked out of his screening feeling “completely gutted” and that the film featured “some of the most blatant and egregious AI use” he has ever seen from a major studio. Tomasso also insisted you can see AI-generated footage in Cliff Booth’s trailers that have been posted online, and he was confident that Fincher’s latest film is filled with “slop as you know and loathe it. The shit you can pump out of Higgsfield.”

Others echoed Tomasso’s sentiments, writing that “the amount of AI in the CLIFF BOOTH movie is astounding to an absurd degree” and vowing to “never watch another Fincher, Pitt or Tarintino [sic] movie again.” Yet some critics enjoyed the film and suggested that the bad AI people thought they were seeing might have actually just been bad CGI. Netflix has neither confirmed nor denied whether AI was used in any capacity to make the film, but Netflix’s heavy involvement in the film’s production and the company’s recent investments in generative AI technology left many suspicious.

It did not help that David Fincher, in a recent interview with the Los Angeles Times, responded to questions about his thoughts on AI with “I’m not a Luddite, so I don’t fear the unknown.” Fincher also reasoned that the anti-AI crowd is advocating for artists to stop iterating on their creative processes: “Is everyone satisfied that we have figured this art form out enough that what we really need to do is go back to celluloid? How long have people painted? 40,000 years? We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.’ Well, it exists. Should we not use it?” The spiel made it sound like he might be jumping on the AI bandwagon.

Set about a decade after Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, Cliff Booth picks up in 1977 at a time when Booth (Pitt) has left his life as a stuntman behind to become a fixer who quietly deals with scandalous problems for Hollywood elites. Cliff still works a number of side gigs as a projectionist and bartender. But the movie is primarily focused on his budding romance with critic-turned-talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki) and his working relationship with Charlie Peters (Scott Caan), a TV actor who needs Booth’s services to keep his wife (Carla Gugino) from being murdered.

At least one trailer for the film features some baffling shots of what looks like people sitting backward in a horse-drawn carriage that make it seem like there might be some generative AI in the mix. It’s hard to tell from the trailers whether that’s actually the case, but in a moment when many creators have been trying to pass off AI generations as human-made art, it’s not surprising that people are suspicious.

Netflix has been incorporating AI into its movies and series for some time now, and it seemed like the company was doubling down earlier this year when it acquired Ben Affleck’s startup, InterPositive, for around $600 million. Rather than turning text into visual outputs like many commercially available AI tools, InterPositive’s AI models are designed to generate assets based on footage captured during a film’s production. According to Netflix, InterPositive’s AI was developed with the intention of making it easier to tweak details like lighting or to remove unwanted background elements. The company also made a big deal of emphasizing that InterPositive’s models were highly customizable and well suited to replicating a human director’s signature style.

Netflix buying InterPositive and absorbing the company’s development team is part of why there has been so much speculation about AI being used in Cliff Booth. If Cliff Booth actually uses AI and the visuals really are as bad as some have said, it would be a major knock against both Netflix and Fincher — a director known for his meticulous (obsessive, some might argue) attention to detail.

title_zh: Fincher新作AI视觉争议调查
summary_zh: David Fincher执导的新片因视觉效果呈现不一致引发AI使用质疑，导演此前曾对AI迭代持开放态度
article_content_zh:
尽管大卫·芬奇的粉丝们一直热切期待《克里夫·布斯的进一步不幸冒险》，但布拉德·皮特主演的《好莱坞往事》续集的早期放映引发了人们对电影中是否使用了生成人工智能的质疑。人们声称这部电影充满了怪异、不一致的视觉效果，让人感觉它更像是马虎，而不是你想象中的《搏击俱乐部》和《社交网络》等时尚作品的导演所期待的那种精致的电影。

上周，在该片于 11 月 25 日首映之前，克里夫·布斯 (Cliff Booth) 进行了多场影评人的放映，电影观众纷纷在社交媒体上对他们所看到的一切表示哀叹。最强烈的反应之一来自 YouTuber/导演帕特里克·托马索 (Patrick Tomasso)，他在 X 上表示，他在看完放映后感到“彻底崩溃”，并且这部电影的特色是他在大型制片厂见过的“一些最明目张胆、最令人震惊的人工智能使用”。托马索还坚持认为，你可以在网上发布的克利夫·布斯的预告片中看到人工智能生成的镜头，他相信芬奇的最新电影充满了“你所知道和厌恶的垃圾。你可以从希格斯菲尔德抽出的狗屎。”

其他人也赞同托马索的观点，写道“《悬崖布斯》电影中的人工智能数量令人震惊，达到了荒谬的程度”，并发誓“再也不会看芬奇、皮特或塔林蒂诺[原文如此]的另一部电影。”然而，一些评论家很喜欢这部电影，并表示人们认为他们看到的糟糕的人工智能实际上可能只是糟糕的 CGI。 Netflix 既没有证实也没有否认人工智能是否被用于制作这部电影，但 Netflix 对电影制作的大量参与以及该公司最近对生成人工智能技术的投资引起了许多人的怀疑。

大卫·芬奇最近在接受《洛杉矶时报》采访时回答有关他对人工智能的看法的问题时说：“我不是卢德分子，所以我不害怕未知。”这也无济于事。芬奇还推断，反人工智能人群主张艺术家停止迭代他们的创作过程：“每个人都满意我们已经足够了解这种艺术形式，以至于我们真正需要做的是回到赛璐珞吗？人们画画有多久了？四万年了？我们正在谈论一个有一百年历史的东西，每个人都会说，‘停止。放下铅笔。不再迭代。没有必要在你的指尖就能改变那个人眼睛的颜色。’好吧，我们不应该使用它吗？”这段长篇大论让人觉得他可能正在追随人工智能的潮流。

故事发生在《好莱坞往事》大约十年后，克里夫·布斯 (Cliff Booth) 的故事发生在 1977 年，当时布斯 (皮特饰) 已经放弃了替身演员的生活，成为了一名秘密处理者，悄悄为好莱坞精英处理丑闻问题。克里夫仍然担任一些兼职工作，担任放映员和调酒师。但这部电影主要关注的是他与评论家出身的经纪人凯伦·克罗斯比（伊丽莎白·德比茨基饰）的恋情，以及他与电视演员查理·彼得斯（斯科特·凯恩饰）的工作关系，布斯需要布斯的帮助来防止他的妻子（卡拉·古奇诺饰）被谋杀。

这部电影至少有一个预告片展示了一些令人困惑的镜头，看起来像是人们向后坐在马车里，这让人觉得其中可能有一些生成人工智能。从预告片中很难看出事实是否如此，但在许多创作者试图将人工智能世代冒充为人造艺术的时刻，人们的怀疑也就不足为奇了。

Netflix 将人工智能融入其电影和电视剧已有一段时间了，今年早些时候，该公司以约 6 亿美元收购了本·阿弗莱克 (Ben Affleck) 的初创公司 InterPositive，似乎加大了投资力度。 InterPositive 的 AI 模型不是像许多商用 AI 工具那样将文本转换为视觉输出，而是根据电影制作过程中捕获的镜头生成资产。据 Netflix 称，InterPositive 的人工智能开发的目的是让调整灯光等细节或删除不需要的背景元素变得更容易。该公司还大力强调 InterPositive 的模型具有高度可定制性，非常适合复制人类导演的标志性风格。

Netflix 收购了 InterPositive 并吸收了该公司的开发团队，这也是人们对 Cliff Booth 使用人工智能的猜测如此之多的部分原因。如果克里夫·布斯真的使用了人工智能，而且视觉效果确实像一些人所说的那么糟糕，那么这将是对 Netflix 和芬奇的重大打击——这位导演以对细节一丝不苟（有些人可能会说是痴迷）的关注而闻名。

title: Novartis CEO says AI will shave four years off drug development, not cure all disease
title_en: Novartis CEO says AI will shave four years off drug development, not cure all disease
author: Manuel Uth
article_content:
Vas Narasimhan, CEO of Swiss drugmaker Novartis and an Anthropic board member, is pushing back on expectations that AI could cure cancer in five to 10 years. That puts him at odds with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and chemistry Nobel laureate Demis Hassabis, who founded DeepMind and its drug discovery spinoff Isomorphic. Around Anthropic's IPO, Amodei suggested that cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease, and mental illness could be cured in under a decade, while Hassabis said last year that AI could defeat all diseases within 10 years.

According to the Financial Times, Narasimhan points to a limited understanding of human biology, which is why lengthy animal and human trials will still be needed. His forecast is more cautious: within a decade, he expects AI to cut average drug development only from 12 years to eight, with the early phase before human trials alone accounting for up to two years of that. He also expects success rates in clinical development to rise from 8 percent to 12 percent.

Anthropic is investing in its own drug research, acquired biotech startup Coefficient Bio, and is building a biology lab. Isomorphic raised $5 billion last week and is working with pharmaceutical companies including Novartis on new drugs. Narasimhan sees AI's real benefit as "somewhere in the middle"between ambitious AI forecasts and a skeptical pharma industry.

瑞士制药商诺华公司首席执行官兼 Anthropic 董事会成员 Vas Narasimhan 正在推翻人工智能可以在 5 到 10 年内治愈癌症的预期。这让他与 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和诺贝尔化学奖获得者德米斯·哈萨比斯 (Demis Hassabis) 产生了分歧，后者创立了 DeepMind 及其药物发现衍生公司 Isomorphic。在 Anthropic 首次公开募股期间，Amodei 表示癌症、阿尔茨海默病、心脏病和精神疾病可以在十年内治愈，而 Hassabis 去年表示人工智能可以在 10 年内战胜所有疾病。

据英国《金融时报》报道，纳拉西姆汉指出，人们对人类生物学的了解有限，这就是为什么仍需要进行漫长的动物和人体试验。他的预测更为谨慎：在十年内，他预计人工智能只会将平均药物开发时间从 12 年缩短到 8 年，其中仅人体试验前的早期阶段就长达两年。他还预计临床开发的成功率将从 8% 上升到 12%。

Anthropic 正在投资自己的药物研究，收购了生物技术初创公司 Coefficient Bio，并正在建设一个生物实验室。 Isomorphic 上周筹集了 50 亿美元，目前正在与诺华等制药公司合作开发新药。 Narasimhan 认为人工智能的真正好处介于雄心勃勃的人工智能预测和持怀疑态度的制药行业之间。

title: OpenAI o1 co-creator Noam Brown urges promising students to drop out as AI enters a "very steep rate of progress"
title_en: OpenAI o1 co-creator Noam Brown urges promising students to drop out as AI enters a "very steep rate of progress"
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
At a poker bot tournament, OpenAI o1 co-creator Noam Brown explained why game theory's core assumption fails in practice and why AI models must think before acting. He also argued that talented students should drop out.

Brown developed Libratus and Pluribus, the first poker AIs to beat human pros, and worked on Meta's Diplomacy AI, CICERO. He has been researching reasoning models at OpenAI since 2023. At the "No Limit"poker bot tournament, hosted by Sequoia Capital, Citadel Securities, and OpenAI, he outlined key lessons from more than a decade of research on games.

### Game theory fails because humans aren't rational

The biggest lesson from his work on Diplomacy, Brown said, is that game theory stops working once humans are involved. Its central premise, he explained, is that every player acts rationally and that this rationality is common knowledge. "People are not actually rational,"he said.

He illustrated the point with the ultimatum game, where one person splits $100 and the other can accept or reject the offer. Under game theory, the optimal move would be to offer just one cent. "But I mean, you can imagine what would happen if you actually tried to offer somebody a penny in this game,"Brown said.

Brown's Diplomacy bots behaved the same way when they relied purely on game theory. The team first tried programming concepts like fairness and retaliation into the bots, but that proved too complex. Instead of assuming rationality, they trained AI models to imitate human behavior as closely as possible and then trained the AI against those "imitation humans."That approach finally let the AI succeed when playing alongside real people.

### Brown pivots from game theory to general reasoning

For Brown, the failure of game theory in Diplomacy was a "crisis of faith moment."All of his expertise up to that point had been in computational game theory. Still, the evidence convinced him that AI needed training on large amounts of human data and that models lacked reasoning, the ability to think before acting.

He decided to leave his specialty behind and switch to general reasoning, but he ran into pushback when interviewing at AI labs in 2022. The large language models of that generation couldn't play Go, chess, or poker. Brown argued that reasoning was the missing ingredient, while most labs countered that pretraining bigger models would solve those problems on its own. He pushed back, saying playing Go competently through pretraining alone would require scaling training by about six orders of magnitude. "And that doesn't seem, you know, realistic,"he said.

OpenAI was the exception, Brown said. The company already had a team working to get general reasoning out of language models, though Brown didn't know that when he applied. He joined the effort and helped build what eventually became o1.

According to Brown, the breakthrough came from using reinforcement learning to get models to think before answering. He said simple chain-of-thought prompting, telling a model to "think step by step before answering,"wasn't enough. It took reinforcement learning on chain of thought to make longer thinking reliably produce better results, he explained. "And that that was I think the key unlock that was like okay now we have a way to scale up test time compute not just in these games but actually in a general purpose way with language models that can be applied to basically any domain,"Brown said. Chain of thought is "probably not the best solution,"he added, because humans think in images, not just words, though the approach is good enough.

### AI models have uneven skills and still need humans

Brown said we are in a "centaur period"where humans and AI work best together. He described current models as "jagged,"superhuman in some areas and surprisingly weak in others. They can write excellent partial poker solvers, he said, but fail at long-term planning, organization, and especially self-correction. Models can't tell when they are heading in the wrong direction, according to Brown, and struggle to pause and rethink their approach from the ground up. He watched one model spend hours trying to fix irrelevant numerical errors in an algorithm that already handles small inaccuracies well.

In this phase, Brown said, the key human skill is understanding a model's uneven strengths and weaknesses and breaking problems down accordingly. Good prompters, he said, can split tasks into ever smaller subproblems for the model to solve one by one. You delegate what the model handles well, and you break down the rest further or solve it yourself.

Even so, progress is moving fast, and OpenAI's Astra model is "able to make money playing online poker at this point,"Brown said. He cited bottlenecks in available compute and in the skills models haven't mastered yet. Brown left open which specific methods would close those gaps, adding only that he expects some abilities to take much longer than others to reach human level.

Brown described this momentum as accelerating recursive self-improvement, since LLMs are already being used to build the next generation of models. Over the next one to two years, he expects a "very steep rate of progress."

That outlook led to his most provocative advice. "Perhaps my most controversial take is that if somebody is a promising student, the best thing to do is actually to drop out and join the labs now,"he said, Things are moving so quickly, he added, that it's "not a great time to sit on the sidelines", maybe already looking for new talent in the room, as OpenAI and other AI labs are still growing, fighting over the one thing they can't scale.

article_content_zh:
在一场扑克机器人锦标赛上，OpenAI o1 联合创始人 Noam Brown 解释了为什么博弈论的核心假设在实践中失败，以及为什么 AI 模型必须在行动之前思考。他还认为有才华的学生应该退学。

Brown 开发了 Libratus 和 Pluribus，这是第一个击败人类职业选手的扑克人工智能，并致力于开发 Meta 的外交人工智能 CICERO。自 2023 年以来，他一直在 OpenAI 研究推理模型。在由红杉资本、Citadel 证券和 OpenAI 主办的“No Limit”扑克机器人锦标赛上，他概述了十多年来游戏研究的重要经验教训。

### 博弈论失败是因为人类不理性

布朗说，他从外交工作中得到的最大教训是，一旦人类参与其中，博弈论就不再起作用。他解释说，其核心前提是每个参与者都理性行事，并且这种理性是常识。 “人们实际上并不理性，”他说。

他用最后通牒游戏来说明这一点，其中一个人分出 100 美元，另一个人可以接受或拒绝这一提议。根据博弈论，最佳举措是只提供一分钱。 “但我的意思是，你可以想象如果你真的试图在这个游戏中给某人一分钱会发生什么，”布朗说。

布朗的外交机器人在纯粹依赖博弈论时也有同样的行为。该团队首先尝试了对机器人进行公平和报复等编程概念，但事实证明这太复杂了。他们没有假设理性，而是训练人工智能模型尽可能模仿人类的行为，然后训练人工智能对抗那些“模仿人类”。这种方法最终让人工智能在与真人一起比赛时取得了成功。

### 布朗从博弈论转向一般推理

对于布朗来说，博弈论在外交中的失败是一个“信仰危机时刻”。到目前为止，他的所有专业知识都是计算博弈论。尽管如此，证据还是让他相信人工智能需要对大量人类数据进行训练，而模型缺乏推理能力，缺乏先思考后行动的能力。

他决定放弃自己的专业，转向一般推理，但在 2022 年人工智能实验室面试时遇到了阻力。那一代的大型语言模型无法下围棋、国际象棋或扑克。布朗认为，推理是缺失的要素，而大多数实验室则反驳说，预训练更大的模型本身就能解决这些问题。他反驳说，仅通过预训练就可以熟练地玩围棋，就需要将训练规模扩大约六个数量级。 “你知道，这看起来并不现实，”他说。

布朗说，OpenAI 是个例外。该公司已经有一个团队致力于从语言模型中获得一般推理，尽管布朗在申请时并不知道这一点。他加入了这项工作并帮助建立了最终成为 o1 的公司。

布朗表示，这一突破来自于使用强化学习让模型在回答之前进行思考。他说，简单的思维链提示，告诉模型“在回答之前一步步思考”是不够的。他解释说，需要在思想链上进行强化学习，才能使更长的思考可靠地产生更好的结果。布朗说：“我认为这就是关键，现在我们有一种方法可以扩大测试时间计算，不仅在这些游戏中，而且实际上以一种通用的方式，使用可以应用于基本上任何领域的语言模型。”他补充说，思想链“可能不是最好的解决方案”，因为人类以图像方式思考，而不仅仅是文字，尽管这种方法已经足够好了。

### 人工智能模型的技能参差不齐，仍然需要人类

布朗说，我们正处于一个“半人马时期”，人类和人工智能可以最好地合作。他将当前的模型描述为“参差不齐”，在某些领域超人，而在另一些领域却出人意料地薄弱。他说，他们可以编写优秀的部分扑克求解器，但无法进行长期规划、组织，尤其是自我纠正。布朗表示，模型无法判断自己何时走错了方向，并且很难停下来从头开始重新思考自己的方法。他看到一个模型花费数小时试图修复算法中不相关的数值错误，而该算法已​​经可以很好地处理小误差。

布朗说，在这个阶段，关键的人类技能是理解模型不均匀的优点和缺点，并相应地分解问题。他说，好的提示器可以将任务分解为更小的子问题，供模型一一解决。您将模型可以很好处理的部分委托给他人，然后进一步分解其余部分或自己解决。

title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Employees in First All-Hands Since His Return
title_en: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Employees in First All-Hands Since His Return
author: Paresh Dave
article_content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that the company’s code of conduct allows room for a “second chance,” that succession planning is a “flawed’ process,” and that he would work to rein in his “insanely intense” management style, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED.

During his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the company’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two children and prompted him to resign. But he said Nvidia’s board of directors made the appropriate decision for the company in welcoming him back. He added that the board made that call, not “the highest levels of our government.”

Huang spoke for about an hour, offering deeply personal thoughts about his therapy sessions and drawing applause at times from employees at Nvidia’s Silicon Valley headquarters as he spoke about the company’s success and future. He didn’t take any questions. While some Nvidia employees celebrated Huang’s return, others remained concerned about his behavior and the board’s decision to reinstate him.

“This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang said as he began to speak. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.”

Nvidia’s board accepted Huang’s resignation earlier this month, citing concerns about his personal behavior and lack of candor following news reports about extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of having ties to Chinese intelligence services. The very same board reinstated him on Monday, just 11 days later, after receiving fresh assurances from Huang and learning from the Trump administration that he was not under federal criminal scrutiny and his return would not be a risk to national security.

Huang and Nvidia, though, continue to face other legal and regulatory challenges. The board is investigating whether he was the target of foreign intelligence. US lawmakers expect him to testify before Congress next week. Lawsuits and other probes are ongoing into Nvidia’s disclosures about Huang’s behavior and its compliance with US export controls on chips.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Huang told staffers that he has been going to therapy “every day for an hour and a half” and that it’s “been helping me a lot.” He added that he “made some very serious personal mistakes. I hurt my family, I hurt my wife.”

While Huang said he had never knowingly made a decision contrary to the company’s interests, he conceded that “in this one area” he had lacked “the courage” to disclose information that he knew would hurt his family, seemingly referring to the extramarital affairs.

“The board and I spent the whole weekend together, and they, of course, they've been contemplating, and they've been collecting facts,” Huang said. “They came to the judgment that they would like to invite me back as the CEO, to give me a second chance.”

The CEO emphasized that Nvidia’s code of conduct, much of which he said he wrote himself, still governs how employees are expected to treat one another and is intended to “create an environment that’s safe for people.”

Huang told employees that violations of the code would not be tolerated. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he said. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would factor in.

“It has to always be evaluated in the context of the human,” he said. “And this company has been more than gracious, more than thoughtful, more than fair in giving me a second chance.”

Huang also pushed back against the notion that he had received preferential treatment because of his status in Silicon Valley. “There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,” Huang said. He rejected the suggestion that he was above the law or Nvidia’s code of conduct.

Later in the meeting, Huang addressed criticism of his self-described “deeply intense, insanely intense” management style, acknowledging that his behavior had at times negatively affected employees. While Huang maintained that the intensity he brings to his job elevates those around him, he conceded that he sometimes takes things too far.

“It disempowers them, and that’s not right,” Huang said. The Nvidia CEO said he needed to figure out how to maintain his level of dedication to the company without hurting the people who work there.

“I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,” Huang said. He said that he would undergo a 360-degree performance review, soliciting feedback as often as monthly from people who work with him. The CEO added that he would be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo such a review and that he did not want to institute the practice companywide.

Huang acknowledged during the meeting that Trump was a vocal supporter of Nvidia but insisted that politics played no role in how the company operated. “It is absolutely true that President Trump really, really loves our company,” Huang said. “He is my president. And I’ll do everything I can to help this president.”

Huang said he would take the same approach with future US presidents. “We are the most apolitical company,” he said. “I don’t love that we talk about politics here. I love that we talk about work here.”

Huang also sought to reassure women at Nvidia, describing himself as “one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women” and touting the company’s flexible work policies, which he said allow employees to simultaneously build their families and careers.

“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,” Huang said.

After Huang’s resignation, he and the company’s board received criticism from Wall Street for not having an obvious internal successor in line. Huang addressed the issue head-on during the company meeting. “I don't believe in succession planning; I think it’s flawed,” he said, specifying that the concept may make sense but the implementation often causes issues.

Huang described each of his 60 reports as CEOs of their own units who could step up when he eventually leaves. “It creates resilience, and it creates the opportunity, which is ultimately the responsibility of the board, to give them the opportunity to decide at that time what the world needed, what the company needed, and be able to choose from a large collection of amazing people,” he said.

The CEO also argued that his brief absence had demonstrated Nvidia’s ability to operate without him. “I promise you, whether I’m here or not, this company is wired up to execute, execute, and execute,” Huang said.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that the company’s code of conduct allows room for a “second chance,” that succession planning is a “flawed’ process,” and that he would work to rein in his “insanely intense” management style, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED.

During his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the company’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two child

article_content_zh:
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋周二对员工表示，公司的行为准则为“第二次机会”留有空间，继任计划是一个“有缺陷的”流程，他将努力控制自己“疯狂的紧张”管理风格。

在重新担任首席执行官后的第一次全体会议上，黄承认自己违反了公司政策，并犯了一些“非常严重的个人错误”，损害了他与妻子和两个孩子的关系，并促使他辞职。但他表示，英伟达董事会欢迎他回来，为公司做出了适当的决定。他补充说，做出这一决定的是董事会，而不是“我们政府的最高层”。

黄仁勋演讲了大约一个小时，对他的治疗课程提出了深刻的个人想法，在谈到公司的成功和未来时，他不时赢得了英伟达硅谷总部员工的掌声。他没有回答任何问题。尽管一些英伟达员工庆祝黄仁勋的回归，但其他人仍然对他的行为以及董事会恢复他职位的决定感到担忧。

“这将是我参加过的最艰难的公司会议，也是我参加过的第二难的会议，”黄在开始讲话时说道。 “我见过的最艰难的会议是和我妻子的会议。”

本月早些时候，英伟达董事会接受了黄仁勋的辞职，理由是对黄仁勋个人行为的担忧，以及在有关婚外情的新闻报道后缺乏坦诚，其中包括一名被指控与中国情报部门有联系的女性的婚外情。仅仅 11 天后，同一委员会在收到黄的新保证并从特朗普政府处获悉他不受联邦刑事调查并且他的回归不会对国家安全构成风险后，于周一恢复了他的职位。

不过，黄仁勋和英伟达仍然面临其他法律和监管挑战。该委员会正在调查他是否是外国情报的目标。美国立法者预计他下周将在国会作证。针对英伟达披露黄的行为及其遵守美国芯片出口管制的情况，诉讼和其他调查正在进行中。

英伟达没有立即回应置评请求。

黄告诉工作人员，他“每天都会接受一个半小时的治疗”，这“对我帮助很大”。他补充说，他“犯了一些非常严重的个人错误。我伤害了我的家人，我伤害了我的妻子。”

虽然黄说他从未故意做出违背公司利益的决定，但他承认“在这一领域”他缺乏“勇气”去披露他知道会伤害家人的信息，似乎指的是婚外情。

“董事会和我一起度过了整个周末，当然，他们一直在思考，他们一直在收集事实，”黄说。 “他们做出的判断是，他们想邀请我重新担任首席执行官，给我第二次机会。”

这位首席执行官强调，英伟达的行为准则（他说其中大部分是他自己编写的）仍然规范着员工如何对待彼此，旨在“创造一个对人们安全的环境”。

黄告诉员工，违反准则的行为是不会容忍的。但这“并不意味着，一旦你违反了行为准则，我们就会把你赶出家门，”他说。 “事实、情况、大量评估”都会被考虑在内。

“必须始终在人类的背景下对其进行评估，”他说。 “这家公司给了我第二次机会，非常慷慨、非常体贴、非常公平。”

黄还反驳了他因为自己在硅谷的地位而获得优惠待遇的说法。 “网上有传言说我显然是一个科技兄弟，所以我回来了，”黄说。他否认了他凌驾于法律或英伟达行为准则之上的说法。

title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
title_en: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.

The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated. In a post on X, Andersen says Tidal needed to take a more “drastic” measure, as AI music made up 43 percent of the tracks distributed to the platform in the last 90 days. “We believe this will resonate with both artists and listeners alike, as 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays at all,” Andersen adds.

Bandcamp similarly banned AI music earlier this year, while other music streaming platforms attempt to address a flood of AI songs by applying new labels or removing them from user algorithms. Spotify recently announced that it removed 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from recommendations over the past year, and also launched new “AI persona” badges for artists that use an AI identity. YouTube has rolled out AI music labels as well, while Apple Music is planning to launch AI labels this year. Meanwhile, Deezer is giving users the option to filter out AI music.

“Wholly AI-generated music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists is another serious problem that has only increased in scale: It diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans,” Tidal says in a separate post on X.

The platform is also going to ban music distributors from submitting AI songs, using the AI detection tool Ircam Amplify and metadata checks to reject submissions generated solely with AI. Tidal notes that it won’t ban songs made with the assistance of AI tools, as long as AI doesn’t make up the “sole output.”

article_content_zh:
Tidal 将于 12 月 9 日正式禁止人工智能生成的音乐。据 Tidal 音乐主管罗伯特·安德森 (Robert Andersen) 称，由于这一变化，Tidal 将删除约 2900 万首人工智能生成的歌曲，并每天拒绝估计 80,000 至 85,000 首曲目。

就在几个月前，Tidal 开始为 100% 人工智能生成的曲目贴上标签并取消其货币化。安德森在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，Tidal 需要采取更“严厉”的措施，因为人工智能音乐占过去 90 天内分发到该平台的曲目的 43%。安德森补充道：“我们相信这会引起艺术家和听众的共鸣，因为 96% 的人工智能生成歌曲的播放次数为零。”

Bandcamp 今年早些时候也同样禁止了人工智能音乐，而其他音乐流媒体平台则试图通过应用新标签或将其从用户算法中删除来解决大量人工智能歌曲的问题。 Spotify 最近宣布，它在过去一年中从推荐中删除了 5000 万首 AI 垃圾歌曲，并为使用 AI 身份的艺术家推出了新的“AI 角色”徽章。 YouTube 也推出了人工智能音乐标签，而 Apple Music 计划今年推出人工智能标签。与此同时，Deezer 为用户提供了过滤 AI 音乐的选项。

Tidal 在 X 上的另一篇文章中表示：“完全由人工智能生成的音乐旨在误导听众和冒充艺术家，这是另一个严重问题，而且规模只会越来越大：它从艺术家那里转移了流量和版税，并让粉丝感到困惑。”

该平台还将禁止音乐发行商提交人工智能歌曲，使用人工智能检测工具 Ircam Amplify 和元数据检查来拒绝仅由人工智能生成的提交。 Tidal 指出，只要人工智能不构成“唯一输出”，它就不会禁止在人工智能工具的帮助下制作的歌曲。

title: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop
title_en: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop
author: Kat Tenbarge
article_content:
Jensen Huang is partying it up in Ibiza. In a video with nearly 6 million views on Instagram, the former CEO of Nvidia is dancing in a crowded club, champagne glass in hand, still wearing his signature black leather jacket. Suddenly, from behind him, Alice Huang — the Chinese technology executive and suspected spy he had an affair with, sparking congressional investigations and his resignation from the chipmaking company he cofounded — appears. She puts her hand on his shoulder and he wraps his arm around her waist as they begin dancing together. The video’s caption reads “Honey Trap Final Boss. #inthemoodforlove.”

Of course, it’s AI-generated. This Instagram Reel is one of hundreds of AI deepfakes featuring Huang, his wife Lori, Alice, and sometimes Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, Kimberly Powell (the second of three reported affair partners). In this case, Huang is being swapped into an existing meme called “Ibiza Final Boss.” The original video featured a British construction worker with a bowl cut dancing in exactly the same way, minus a woman sidling up to him. Other viral AI hits include Huang in a scene from The Office, Huang in the music video for George Michael’s “Careless Whisper,” and Huang as the former Astronomer CEO who got caught in an affair with one of his employees by the jumbotron at a Coldplay concert last summer. Even the rapper 50 Cent posted an AI edit of his “P.I.M.P.” music video, now featuring Huang with some flashy silver accessories.

Unlike deepfake pornography or election disinformation, these AI videos aren’t necessarily intended to harm or mislead people. They’re memes making fun of Huang’s cheating scandal and its global implications, created with AI technology that in many cases relies heavily on Nvidia’s tech stack: video diffusion models running on the Nvidia GPUs that power much of the modern generative AI industry. “It’s ironic that without Nvidia generating millions of these AI memes ... would not be possible,” reads one of the top comments on the Ibiza deepfake. “In some sense, Jensen is making Nvidia richer by his own scandal.” The comment was punctuated by multiple cry-laughing emoji.

As it turns out, Huang may benefit, too. On Monday, the Nvidia board announced he was reinstated as president, CEO, and board director following “a series of discussions and meetings” and “input from senior levels of the United States government.” Nvidia’s stock has since surged, and new AI Huang memes cast him in a victorious light. One variation swaps him into a scene from The Wolf of Wall Street, announcing “I’m not leaving” to a crowd of cheering men that has been edited to include AI versions of Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and Mark Zuckerberg.

While the saga continues, many social media users are finding the humor in these Huang deepfakes, and their creators are churning out variations to meet the sudden demand. The Instagram account behind the Ibiza one has made three Huang deepfakes so far, all remakes of the same scene. Another version features Powell dancing with him, and the third one shows a sea of young women in bikini tops and shorts surrounding Huang, who lifts his champagne up in celebration. Each has accrued millions of views.

“His story has just come at the best time for ai creators and a terrible time for him,” wrote the account behind the Ibiza videos in a direct message to The Verge. “Everyone was doing him. Most I’ve seen anyone AI-ed.”

This deepfake creator identified himself as a 40-year-old man from Melbourne, Australia, but wouldn’t share his real name. He says he has spent “thousands” on AI video generation, using models like TikTok developer ByteDance’s Seedance 2.5 and Alibaba’s Wan 3. These, along with other AI tools like Google’s Nano Banana, help power the ecosystem of deepfakes.

He said his Instagram page has been going “super viral” in the past two weeks, thanks to the Ibiza meme format. He has nearly 100 million views on various iterations of it featuring different celebrities. The Huang ones are among the most popular, alongside versions featuring Elizabeth Holmes and Amanda Seyfried playing her in the hit Nathan Fielder documentary You Can See Everything.

“I wanted to elevate the content and know that putting what is happening in the news ... would get traction,” he wrote. “Always wanted to be a filmmaker but this technology is beyond whatever I imagined was possible.”

As generative AI has taken hold of the internet in recent years, a lot of the resulting viral content has been disparaged as “AI slop.” Hollywood productions, mainstream artists, and even local businesses have been maligned for using (or appearing to use) AI in their advertisements and final cuts. Video trends like putting sexy AI fruit characters in Love Island parodies racked up millions of views online but failed to deliver any real cultural momentum. The ubiquity of the Huang deepfakes and the relative lack of blowback from AI critics may indicate that the future of AI-generated content is similar to the rest of meme culture: If the topic’s trending, people will engage with something, even if it’s following the same formula as the slop. That an AI tech titan’s own indiscretions are inspiring this latest evolution in deepfakes is just the sardonic cherry on top.

“It’s not that we’re inundated in deepfakes of Trump being like ‘Nuclear war tomorrow,’ like the way it was framed as the big problem,” says misinformation researcher Abbie Richards. “Instead, it just feels like there is so much slop to push through to have any grounding in reality.”

The AI memes of Huang and other public figures don’t feel as sinister as other forms of AI disinformation and misinformation, mainly because of how goofy they are. It’s hard to imagine anyone falling for a “Gangnam Style” parody or any serious implications if they did. But these deepfakes are still eerily realistic, as one comment on the Seyfried Ibiza variation pointed out: “All jokes aside, is anyone else finding it increasingly alarming that AI is capable of this?”

Even the creator behind the Ibiza AI videos thinks “someone will try and clamp down because it’s getting outta control.” But in the meantime, he’s looking for ways to monetize his newfound virality. Despite his significant financial outlay, he says he hasn’t made any money yet, besides getting “gifted $3 on a reel once.”

While Instagram has started to invite some creators to earn direct payouts from views on their Reels, the account behind the AI “Careless Whisper” parody featuring Huang told The Verge that “the way to earn is through creating content for clients and companies after gaining attention on social media.” This AI creator, who declined to share any identifying information, wrote in a direct message that they receive dozens of requests from new and returning clients for AI commissions every time they go viral, “which is quite often.” In addition to Huang deepfakes, some of their most viral AI edits feature Tobey Maguire’s Spider-Man as a rapper.

The Ibiza AI meme creator has worked with one celebrity brand so far, belonging to the Irish mixed martial artist Conor McGregor. Four months ago, McGregor launched an energy drink called MAC Energy, and the company requested an AI Ibiza meme showing McGregor dancing with a can of it. The creator complied, and the post exists as a collaboration between the two Instagram pages, but it isn’t labeled as an advertisement and he says he didn’t ask for any money in return.

“I just did it because it was a good opportunity for my page,” he says.

It seems like the entity that stands to reap the biggest reward from viral Huang deepfakes is Instagram itself and the other social media sites where creators are posting them. And these humorous AI edits are technically allowed on Meta platforms, as long as creators disclose that they’re AI-generated. Meta didn’t respond to a request for comment by publication time.

But there are other considerations besides profitability. Many of these AI memes hinge on sexist portrayals and racist stereotypes as the joke. Asian American women in Silicon Valley have reported an uptick in microaggressions revolving around “honeypot” and “Chinese spy” allegations. And when it comes to Powell and the other Nvidia employee who Huang reportedly had a relationship with, the workplace power dynamic at play has faded into the background of mockery.

"The more troubling dynamics of Huang’s affairs have faded into the background of mockery"

“Even though we know that he was wielding his power to have inappropriate relationships with his subordinates and his employees, it’s still like ‘LOL, let’s make an AI deepfake of him at the office,’” says Josh Lora, a writer and creator who has a popular TikTok series about the role of cheating scandals in American culture. “Why aren’t we having a real conversation about the effects of this on women, the effects of this workplace on women, especially 10 years after #MeToo?”

The apparent lack of interest from major social media companies to stem the flow of this kind of disparaging AI content isn’t surprising to misinformation expert Richards, even as some tech CEOs, like Elon Musk, called for Huang’s reinstatement and cast doubt on the reporting against him. If Huang memes are truly in vogue, that may be worth more to the AI industry than his dignity.

“I think that they are invested in the widespread adoption of AI,” she says. “So anything with AI going viral and appearing to be popular and liked by the public probably, in their mind, benefits them.”

With Huang back as CEO, the message couldn’t be clearer: For him, the consequences of his affairs were temporary, including whatever humiliation stemmed from the AI memes. Ultimately, all any of it meant was more power for Nvidia and more power for Jensen Huang.

article_content_zh:
黄仁勋正在伊维萨岛举办派对。在 Instagram 上一段观看次数近 600 万次的视频中，这位英伟达前首席执行官在拥挤的俱乐部里跳舞，手里拿着香槟酒杯，仍然穿着他标志性的黑色皮夹克。突然，他身后出现了爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）——一位与他有染的中国科技高管，涉嫌间谍，引发了国会调查，并导致他从他共同创立的芯片制造公司辞职。当他们开始一起跳舞时，她把手放在他的肩膀上，他用手臂搂住她的腰。视频的标题是“美人计最终首领。#inthemoodforlove”。

当然，它是人工智能生成的。这张 Instagram Reel 是数百个人工智能 Deepfake 之一，主角包括黄仁勋、他的妻子 Lori、Alice，有时还有 Nvidia 的医疗保健副总裁 Kimberly Powell（据报道的三位外遇伙伴中的第二位）。在这种情况下，黄被替换为一个名为“伊维萨最终老板”的现有模因。最初的视频中，一名留着碗形发型的英国建筑工人以完全相同的方式跳舞，只是没有一个女人侧身靠近他。其他病毒般的 AI 热门作品包括《办公室》中的一个场景、乔治·迈克尔 (George Michael) 的《Careless Whisper》音乐录影带中的 Huang，以及去年夏天在酷玩乐队 (Coldplay) 演唱会的大屏幕上饰演天文学家前首席执行官的黄，他与一名员工发生了婚外情。甚至说唱歌手 50 Cent 也发布了他的“P.I.M.P.”的人工智能编辑版。音乐视频，现在以黄与一些华丽的银色配饰为主角。

与深度伪造色情内容或选举虚假信息不同，这些人工智能视频不一定是为了伤害或误导人们。它们是取笑黄的作弊丑闻及其全球影响的模因，这些都是用人工智能技术创建的，在许多情况下严重依赖英伟达的技术堆栈：在英伟达 GPU 上运行的视频扩散模型为现代生成人工智能行业提供了动力。 “具有讽刺意味的是，如果没有 Nvidia 生成数以百万计的人工智能模因……这一切都是不可能的，”伊维萨岛 Deepfake 的热门评论之一写道。 “从某种意义上说，詹森正在通过自己的丑闻让英伟达变得更加富有。”这条评论被多个哭笑的表情符号打断。

事实证明，黄也可能受益。周一，英伟达董事会宣布，经过“一系列讨论和会议”以及“美国政府高层的意见”，他恢复了总裁、首席执行官和董事会董事的职务。此后，英伟达的股价飙升，新的人工智能黄模因给他带来了胜利的光芒。其中一个版本将他变成了《华尔街之狼》中的场景，向一群欢呼的人们宣布“我不会离开”，经过编辑，其中包括人工智能版本的唐纳德·特朗普、埃隆·马斯克和马克·扎克伯格。

当传奇仍在继续时，许多社交媒体用户在这些黄深赝品中找到了幽默，它们的创作者正在大量生产变体来满足突然的需求。到目前为止，伊维萨岛背后的 Instagram 账户已经制作了三张黄的 Deepfake 作品，全部都是同一场景的翻拍。另一个版本是鲍威尔与他一起跳舞，第三个版本则展示了一群穿着比基尼上衣和短裤的年轻女性围绕着黄，而黄则举起香槟庆祝。每个都积累了数百万次观看次数。

伊维萨岛视频背后的账户在给 The Verge 的直接消息中写道：“他的故事刚刚出现在人工智能创作者的最佳时机，但对他来说却是一个可怕的时刻。” “每个人都在模仿他。我见过的大多数人都是人工智能的。”

这位 Deepfake 创作者自称是一名来自澳大利亚墨尔本的 40 岁男子，但不愿透露自己的真实姓名。他说，他已经在人工智能视频生成上花费了“数千”美元，使用了 TikTok 开发商字节跳动的 Seedance 2.5 和阿里巴巴的 Wan 3 等模型。这些模型与谷歌的 Nano Banana 等其他人工智能工具一起，有助于为 Deepfakes 生态系统提供动力。

他说，得益于伊比沙岛模因格式，过去两周他的 Instagram 页面“超级病毒式传播”。他在不同名人主演的各种版本中拥有近 1 亿的观看次数。黄的版本是最受欢迎的版本之一，另外还有伊丽莎白·霍姆斯和阿曼达·塞弗里德在内森·菲尔德的热门纪录片《你可以看到一切》中扮演她的版本。

“我想提升内容，并知道将正在发生的事情放在新闻中……会受到关注，”他写道。 “一直想成为一名电影制片人，但这项技术超出了我的想象。”

近年来，随着生成式人工智能在互联网上占据一席之地，由此产生的许多病毒式内容被贬为“人工智能垃圾”。好莱坞制作、主流艺术家，甚至当地企业都因在广告和最终剪辑中使用（或看似使用）人工智能而受到诟病。像在爱情岛模仿中加入性感的人工智能水果角色这样的视频趋势在网上获得了数百万次观看，但未能带来任何真正的文化动力。黄氏深度赝品的普遍存在以及人工智能批评者相对较少的反击可能表明，人工智能生成内容的未来与模因文化的其他部分类似：如果该话题流行，人们就会参与其中，即使它遵循与slop相同的公式。人工智能技术巨头自己的轻率行为激发了深度造假的最新发展，这只是最讽刺的樱桃。

错误信息研究员艾比·理查兹（Abbie Richards）表示：“我们并不是被特朗普‘明日核战争’之类的深度赝品所淹没，就像它被描述为一个大问题一样。” “相反，感觉就像有太多的障碍需要克服才能在现实中扎根。”

黄和其他公众人物的人工智能模因并不像其他形式的人工智能虚假信息和错误信息那样险恶，主要是因为它们非常愚蠢。很难想象有人会爱上“江南Style”的模仿，或者如果他们这样做的话会产生任何严重的影响。但这些深度造假仍然异常真实，正如一篇关于 Seyfried Ibiza 变体的评论所指出的那样：“除了所有的笑话之外，还有其他人对人工智能能够做到这一点感到越来越震惊吗？”

甚至伊维萨岛人工智能视频背后的创作者也认为“有人会试图压制，因为它已经失控了。”但与此同时，他正在寻找方法将他新发现的病毒式传播货币化。尽管他的经济支出相当可观，但他表示，除了“一次收到 3 美元的礼物”外，他还没有赚到任何钱。

虽然 Instagram 已开始邀请一些创作者通过其 Reels 上的观看次数直接赚取报酬，但以黄为主角的人工智能“Careless Whisper”模仿背后的账户告诉 The Verge，“赚钱的方式是在社交媒体上获得关注后，为客户和公司创造内容。”这位拒绝透露任何身份信息的人工智能创造者在一条直接消息中写道，每次他们病毒式传播时，他们都会收到来自新客户和老客户的数十个人工智能佣金请求，“这种情况很常见”。除了 Huang 的 Deepfakes 之外，他们的一些最热门的 AI 剪辑还以托比·马奎尔 (Tobey Maguire) 的蜘蛛侠作为说唱歌手。

title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
title_en: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI “in ways that may not be apparent to users.” In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times’ photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.”

Adobe has spent the past few years filling Photoshop and other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools. The November update cited by the NYT’s email adds several new AI features, including Adobe’s new “AI Assisted Editor” view, which lets users access all of Photoshop’s AI features from a single toolbar. It also adds an AI assistant for step-by-step editing instructions, prompt-based image transformation and editing, new AI upscaling options, and an AI-powered tool that recomposes images for different canvas sizes.

It’s not always clear which tools in Adobe’s apps are AI-powered, and even some older options like automated selection tools may now be considered part of the AI suite. This can lead to photos ending up with metadata indicating they were edited with AI, which is a blunt way of describing what happened in post-production. For a newsroom like the Times, where photo editing is kept to a minimum, the metadata risks losing readers’ trust. Last year, the Times said that it does not “retouch or digitally manipulate” photos but may “make minimal adjustments to color to ensure we are accurately reproducing the image.”

In August, Adobe began rolling out support for C2PA metadata across its apps, which indicates whether an image is AI-generated or edited using AI features. The NYT is issuing its restriction to keep these tags from inadvertently appearing in its photos. “At this time, we are requiring that all contributing photographers avoid using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and subsequent updates) when working on assignment for The Times,” the email reads. NYT spokesperson Graham James confirmed the requirement in a statement to The Verge, which reiterated the policy outlined in the email.

It’s still not clear which specific Photoshop features the NYT is referring to. Adobe didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for more information.

Update, November 24th: Added confirmation from the NYT.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 纽约时报摄影部主管Meaghan Looram与Josh Haner发布内部备忘录，明确禁止旗下摄影师使用Adobe Photoshop 2027（版本28.0.0及后续）。该禁令旨在规避该软件内嵌的AI功能自动添加C2PA元数据，从而误将新闻摄影标注为“AI生成”，以维护其影像记录的公信力。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The New York Times photography leadership, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, has issued a directive prohibiting contributing photographers from using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (version 28.0.0 and later). The ban is designed to prevent the software's AI features from embedding C2PA metadata, which would falsely label authentic news photography as 'AI-generated' and threaten editorial integrity.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举揭示了传统新闻行业在AI自动化工作流下的合规困境，即软件厂商的“默认AI化”策略正挑战新闻事实的物理定义。C2PA作为防伪标准，在缺乏颗粒度识别的软件环境下，反而成为媒体行业判断影像真实性的“负资产”。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This move highlights the compliance dilemma in journalism where software vendors' 'default-AI' strategy challenges the definition of photographic truth. C2PA standards, lacking granular discernment, are inadvertently becoming a liability for newsrooms attempting to distinguish between post-production and synthetic content.

article_content_zh:
《纽约时报》要求自由摄影师不要使用最新版本的 Adob​​e Photoshop，因为 2027 年更新中的功能“以用户可能不明显的方式”使用人工智能。在 The Verge 看到并发布在 Threads 上的一封电子邮件中，《纽约时报》的两位摄影领袖 Meaghan Looram 和 Josh Haner 写道，使用这些功能“可以导致元数据将照片识别为人工智能生成的”。

Adobe 在过去的几年里一直在其创意套件中使用大量人工智能工具填充 Photoshop 和其他应用程序。 《纽约时报》电子邮件引用的 11 月更新添加了多项新的 AI 功能，包括 Adob​​e 新的“AI 辅助编辑器”视图，该视图允许用户从单个工具栏访问 Photoshop 的所有 AI 功能。它还添加了一个人工智能助手，用于分步编辑指令、基于提示的图像转换和编辑、新的人工智能升级选项，以及一个人工智能驱动的工具，可以根据不同的画布尺寸重新组合图像。

Adobe 应用程序中的哪些工具是由 AI 驱动的并不总是很清楚，甚至一些较旧的选项（例如自动选择工具）现在也可能被视为 AI 套件的一部分。这可能会导致照片最终带有元数据，表明它们是用人工智能编辑的，这是描述后期制作中发生的情况的一种直白方式。对于像《纽约时报》这样的新闻编辑室来说，照片编辑被保持在最低限度，元数据可能会失去读者的信任。去年，《纽约时报》表示，它不会“修饰或数字化处理”照片，但可能“对颜色进行最小程度的调整，以确保我们准确地再现图像。”

8 月，Adobe 开始在其应用程序中推出对 C2PA 元数据的支持，该元数据表明图像是 AI 生成的还是使用 AI 功能编辑的。 《纽约时报》正在发布限制，以防止这些标签无意中出现在其照片中。 “目前，我们要求所有投稿摄影师在为《纽约时报》拍摄作业时避免使用 Adob​​e Photoshop 2027（版本 28.0.0 及后续更新），”电子邮件中写道。 《纽约时报》发言人 Graham James 在给 The Verge 的一份声明中证实了这一要求，并重申了电子邮件中概述的政策。

目前尚不清楚《纽约时报》所指的是 Photoshop 的哪些具体功能。 Adobe 没有立即回应 The Verge 提供更多信息的请求。

11 月 24 日更新：添加了《纽约时报》的确认。
