author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Xiaomi’s Sales Slip After Memory Shortages Weigh on Smartphones Bloomberg News Tue, 24 November 2026 at 2:35 am GMT-7 2 min read 1810.HK -3.71% AAPL +0.50% (Bloomberg) -- Xiaomi Corp. reported a revenue contraction for the third quarter in a row while it grapples with a global memory crunch that's hobbled the world's biggest smartphone makers.

The Beijing-based maker of smartphones and cars saw revenue drop 5.2% in the three months ended September to 107.2 billion yuan ($16.1 billion). Analysts on average expected a 6% decline. Net income tumbled 68% to 3.9 billion yuan during the same period.

AI's voracious demand for memory chips has created a dire shortage of conventional chips that's hitting consumer electronics makers around the globe. That's compelled smartphone makers from Apple Inc. to Xiaomi to raise prices on their devices.

Xiaomi's budget smartphones have been especially vulnerable to skyrocketing memory costs, forcing the company to sharply curtail production of low-end devices to stem losses. Its smartphone shipments have been shrinking since the first quarter this year, sliding nearly 30% in the third quarter versus the overall market's 20% decline, according to market tracker Counterpoint Research.

Still, Counterpoint says a double-digit increase in Xiaomi's average selling prices has stabilized its smartphone revenue, as it shifts away from entry-level devices toward premium phones.

Xiaomi's latest Xiaomi 18 Fold, released at the end of the third quarter, is priced at more than 10,000 yuan and is contending with Apple's iPhone Duo and similar gadgets from Huawei Technologies Co. in the premium segment.

The company also launched a new line of hybrid sports utility vehicles in the third quarter. Robust initial demand for the SkyNomad series are expected to help offset the company's flagging electric-vehicle deliveries.

article_content_zh:
内存短缺影响智能手机，小米销量下滑 彭博新闻社，2026 年 11 月 24 日，星期二，凌晨 2:35 GMT-7 2 分钟阅读 1810.HK -3.71% AAPL +0.50%（彭博社）——小米公司公布连续第三季度收入萎缩，同时该公司正在努力应对全球最大智能手机制造商陷入困境的内存紧缺问题。

这家总部位于北京的智能手机和汽车制造商在截至 9 月份的三个月内收入下降了 5.2%，至 1072 亿元人民币（161 亿美元）。分析师平均预期下降 6%。同期净利润下降68%至39亿元人民币。

人工智能对存储芯片的巨大需求造成了传统芯片的严重短缺，这对全球消费电子产品制造商造成了打击。这迫使苹果公司和小米等智能手机制造商提高其设备的价格。

小米的廉价智能手机特别容易受到内存成本飙升的影响，迫使该公司大幅削减低端设备的产量以遏制损失。市场跟踪机构 Counterpoint Research 的数据显示，自今年第一季度以来，其智能手机出货量一直在萎缩，第三季度下滑近 30%，而整体市场下降了 20%。

不过，Counterpoint 表示，随着小米从入门级设备转向高端手机，小米平均售价的两位数增长稳定了其智能手机收入。

小米最新的小米18 Fold于第三季度末发布，售价超过1万元，在高端市场与苹果iPhone Duo和华为技术有限公司的类似产品展开竞争。

该公司还在第三季度推出了新的混合动力运动型多用途车系列。 SkyNomad 系列的强劲初始需求预计将有助于抵消该公司电动汽车交付量的疲软。

title: AI Solved Math’s Most Famous Problem. Now Humans Are Struggling to Understand It
title_en: AI Solved Math’s Most Famous Problem. Now Humans Are Struggling to Understand It
author: Isabella Ward
article_content:
Mathematicians are struggling to decode a 17-million-line solution to their field’s most famous problem, published by an Anthropic researcher on Friday.

Levent Alpöge released a proof in the programming language Lean of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, which he had created with Claude. While the conjecture, which describes how prime numbers are distributed, is widely assumed to be true, many mathematicians have tried and failed to definitively show this, and the problem has become something of a holy grail of number theory.

Since Alpöge published his proof, more than 200 people have been collaborating to verify it. On Saturday, the nonprofit the Lean Focused Research Organization and volunteer-led organization Mathlib said on Saturday they have “full confidence” that the proof is sound. The problem is formulated correctly and the code compiles, they confirmed. Now, “we look forward to all the activity in the mathematical community that will help explain the new ideas in this proof,” they wrote.

Lean proofs are written to be checked by machine, while mathematical papers are written to explain the results to the community so that they can be reviewed and advanced. But Alpöge hasn’t released the paper version, which clocks in at 250,000 pages and is, in his own estimation, a “travesty of slop.” (On Monday, he added in an X post that the Lean proof “is full of garbage obviously” but that it still “compiles.” He also said that the 250,000 pages was a “joke … I find big number [sic] extremely hilarious.”) That’s left mathematicians to their own devices as they try to decipher what new findings they can obtain and build from the result.

“Knowing there is a proof is one thing,” Abhishek Saha, a professor of mathematics at Queen Mary University of London, tells WIRED, “but when we understand the proof, that would allow us to actually go beyond what has happened, to build new branches of mathematics perhaps or formulate the next conjecture to push the horizon further.”

Saha reckons the community effort should be able to simplify the result into a human-readable form of under 10,000, if not 1,000, pages. But complicating this feat is the fact that the proof appears to draw on many advanced branches of number theory in a long and “incredibly counterintuitive” argument. “I don't think this kind of proof would ever come from a human,” says Saha, “but AIs can do something completely different and almost alien, and that breaks our intuition about how very difficult mathematical results might come about.”

He was shocked to see even his own corner of number theory utilized by the proof, and has since been trying to understand how. Saha has been using OpenAI’s Astra model to convert sections of the Lean proof into more digestible formats, such as single-page posters like those presented at conferences and shorter documents. But there’s a limit to that approach.

“It may well be that no single person has the expertise to understand in detail every part of the proof,” he says.

More than 60 other individuals are using AI agents to try to translate the Lean lines into understandable ideas on Principia Math, a collaborative platform designed to facilitate the understanding of AI breakthroughs. So far, they have done this for more than 3,000 pieces of the Lean proof, though platform chief executive officer Anton Shakov expects it will take mathematicians months before they have a good conceptual understanding of the proof Alpöge produced with Claude in roughly six weeks. “I personally believe the picture we will get in the end, once the ideas of this proof have been properly understood, will be astoundingly beautiful," he tells WIRED.

Independent mathematicians have already understood and written up one smaller result to have come out of Alpöge’s proof.

AI labs have previously been criticized for rushing to publish breakthrough mathematical results, claiming glory while leaving the academic community to digest the results—and clean up mistakes.

“No human being can reasonably claim to be responsible for, or even to understand, such a document,” the Association for Human Mathematics, a group of more than 1,000 mathematicians founded in September, wrote in a statement on Friday of the 17-million-line opus. It complained that Alpöge’s announcement “builds upon over a century of human work, but fails to advance mathematical understanding in the same way.”

Alpöge, who before joining Anthropic was a researcher at Harvard University, acknowledged on Friday what an “extraordinary” situation it was to present “the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighborhood around its mathematics,” and wrote that he would try his best to help digest the proof, including by writing it up properly. But having had to hold off from making the announcement ahead of Anthropic’s initial public offering on Thursday, “I just could not live if I waited even longer,” he wrote.

Anthropic rival OpenAI in October proved a weaker version of the problem, called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. Alpöge had been scooped by OpenAI in September on another Millennium Prize Problem concerning the Navier-Stokes equations, which describe fluid motion. When the company said it had solved part of the problem, Alpöge’s collaborator, New York University professor Tristan Buckmaster, claimed OpenAI had rushed ahead to beat the pair to it after becoming aware of his work. The pair also announced on Friday that they had completed the remaining unsolved parts of the Navier-Stokes problem.

article_content_zh:
数学家们正在努力解码该领域最著名问题的 1700 万行解决方案，该解决方案由一位人类研究人员于周五发布。

Levent Alpöge 用编程语言 Lean 发布了他与 Claude 共同创建的 167 年黎曼假设的证明。虽然描述素数如何分布的猜想被广泛认为是正确的，但许多数学家试图明确地证明这一点但未能明确，这个问题已成为数论的圣杯。

自从 Alpöge 发表他的证明以来，已有 200 多人合作验证。周六，非营利组织精益聚焦研究组织和志愿者领导的组织 Mathlib 周六表示，他们“完全有信心”证明证据是可靠的。他们确认，问题的表述正确并且代码可以编译。现在，“我们期待数学界的所有活动都将有助于解释这个证明中的新想法，”他们写道。

编写精益证明是为了让机器检查，而编写数学论文是为了向社区解释结果，以便对其进行审查和改进。但 Alpöge 尚未发布纸质版本，该版本有 250,000 页，据他自己估计，这是“对废话的嘲讽”。 （周一，他在一篇 X 帖子中补充道，精益证明“显然充满了垃圾”，但它仍然“可以编译”。他还说 250,000 页是一个“笑话……我发现大数字[原文如此]非常搞笑。”）这让数学家们只能依靠自己的设备，试图破译他们可以从结果中获得和构建哪些新发现。

伦敦玛丽女王大学数学教授阿布舍克·萨哈 (Abhishek Saha) 告诉《连线》杂志：“知道有证据是一回事，但当我们理解了证据时，这将使我们能够真正超越已经发生的事情，或许能够建立新的数学分支，或者制定下一个猜想，进一步推动我们的发展。”

Saha 认为社区的努力应该能够将结果简化为人类可读的形式，即使不是 1,000 页，也不会超过 10,000 页。但让这一壮举变得复杂的是，这个证明似乎在一个漫长且“极其违反直觉”的论证中借鉴了数论的许多高级分支。 “我认为这种证明永远不会来自人类，”萨哈说，“但人工智能可以做一些完全不同、几乎是外星人的事情，这打破了我们对数学结果可能如何产生的直觉。”

他惊讶地发现证明甚至使用了他自己的数论角落，并且从那时起就一直试图理解其中的原理。 Saha 一直在使用 OpenAI 的 Astra 模型将精益证明的各个部分转换为更易于理解的格式，例如会议上展示的单页海报和较短的文档。但这种方法有其局限性。

“很可能没有一个人拥有专业知识来详细理解证明的每个部分，”他说。

超过 60 名其他人正在 Principia Math 上使用 AI 代理，尝试将精益路线转化为可理解的想法，Principia Math 是一个协作平台，旨在促进对 AI 突破的理解。到目前为止，他们已经对 3,000 多条精益证明进行了此操作，尽管平台首席执行官 Anton Shakov 预计数学家们还需要几个月的时间才能对 Alpöge 与 Claude 在大约六周内制作的证明有一个良好的概念理解。他告诉《连线》杂志：“我个人相信，一旦这个证明的思想被正确理解，我们最终得到的画面将会非常美丽。”

独立数学家已经理解并写下了阿尔波格证明中的一个较小的结果。

人工智能实验室此前曾因急于发表突破性的数学结果而受到批评，声称自己的荣耀，却让学术界消化结果并纠正错误。

“没有人可以合理地声称对这样一份文件负责，甚至无法理解，”9 月成立的由 1000 多名数学家组成的人类数学协会在周五的一份关于这份 1700 万行作品的声明中写道。它抱怨说，Alpöge 的声明“建立在人类一个多世纪的工作基础上，但未能以同样的方式促进数学理解。”

Alpöge 在加入 Anthropic 之前是哈佛大学的一名研究员，他周五承认，“在掌握了围绕数学的大量邻域之前，向世界呈现一个完整的论证”是一种多么“非同寻常”的情况，并写道，他将尽力帮助消化证明，包括正确地把它写下来。但由于不得不在周四 Anthropic 首次公开募股之前推迟宣布这一消息，“如果我再等更长时间，我就活不下去了，”他写道。

人类竞争对手 OpenAI 在 10 月份证明了该问题的一个较弱版本，称为拟黎曼假设。 Alpöge 在 9 月份被 OpenAI 凭借另一个涉及纳维-斯托克斯方程的千年奖问题获得，该方程描述了流体运动。当该公司表示已经解决了部分问题时，Alpöge 的合作者、纽约大学教授特里斯坦·巴克马斯特 (Tristan Buckmaster) 声称，OpenAI 在了解他的工作后，冲在了前面，击败了两人。两人还在周五宣布，他们已经完成了纳维-斯托克斯问题剩余的未解决部分。

title: Sony says GTA VI is the biggest game launch in PlayStation history across five generations, drawing 39M+ unique PS5 players, who logged 683M total hours (Tim Turi/PlayStation.Blog)
title_en: Sony says GTA VI is the biggest game launch in PlayStation history across five generations, drawing 39M+ unique PS5 players, who logged 683M total hours (Tim Turi/PlayStation.Blog)
author: PlayStation.Blog
article_content:
Celebrating the PlayStation community and Rockstar Games for creating an incredible moment in gaming and entertainment.

After a long wait, players finally have had the chance to jump into Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s been amazing to see the PlayStation community around the world begin their adventures in the state of Leonida.

Whether you’ve been counting down the days to return to the streets of Vice City or you’re experiencing the Grand Theft Auto series for the very first time, we want to take a moment to say: thank you. The excitement and passion of the community have made this a truly special moment for all of us.

The launch of GTAVI marks an extraordinary moment for gaming and entertainment, becoming the biggest game launch in PlayStation history, across three decades and five console generations. More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia’s story in Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5.

The PlayStation community came together in a big way to experience Grand Theft Auto VI during its launch and opening weekend. Here are a few highlights from the launch window ending November 22, 2026*:

These are just a few ways we’ve seen our PlayStation community come together around this incredible moment in gaming, and we’re excited to see how you continue to build and share new memories and experiences in the months ahead.

Finally, we want to congratulate our partners at Rockstar Games for bringing this extraordinary game to players around the world and continuing a partnership with PlayStation that stretches back to Grand Theft Auto III on PlayStation 2. With GTAVI, we worked to bring the best experience on PS5 and gave players a memorable way to commemorate the game with two special limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Vice City. We also celebrated the launch with live events including Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival in Miami this past weekend.And to our PlayStation community, thank you for your continued passion and support, and for choosing to experience GTAVI on PS5. It’s your enthusiasm that make moments like these so meaningful for all of us.

We can’t wait to see where your adventures in Leonida take you next!

Please be kind, considerate, and constructive. Report inappropriate comments to PlayStationBlogModeration@sony.com

庆祝 PlayStation 社区和 Rockstar Games 在游戏和娱乐领域创造了令人难以置信的时刻。

经过漫长的等待，玩家们终于有机会进入侠盗猎车手VI了。看到世界各地的 PlayStation 社区在列奥尼达州开始他们的冒险真是太棒了。

无论您是在倒数重返罪恶都市街道的日子，还是第一次体验侠盗猎车手系列，我们都想花点时间说声：谢谢。社区的兴奋和热情使这对我们所有人来说都是一个真正特别的时刻。

GTAVI 的发布标志着游戏和娱乐领域的一个非凡时刻，成为 PlayStation 历史上跨越三十年和五代主机的最大规模的游戏发布。超过 3900 万独立玩家在 PlayStation 5 上体验过杰森和露西亚在侠盗猎车手 VI 中的故事。

title: Meta rolls out its personal AI agent Muse to UK adults to help with everyday tasks, the first AI agent product launched by a Big Tech company in the UK (Mizy Clifton/Politico)
title_en: Meta rolls out its personal AI agent Muse to UK adults to help with everyday tasks, the first AI agent product launched by a Big Tech company in the UK (Mizy Clifton/Politico)

inline_images.caption: The Meta logo is seen on a phone in Frankfurt, Germany on Jan. 8, 2025. | Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP via Getty Images
inline_images.alt: The Meta logo is seen on a phone in Frankfurt, Germany on Jan. 8, 2025. | Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP via

author: Politico
article_content:
Regulators will be watching the U.K. rollout of Muse carefully.

LONDON — Meta rolled out its personal AI agent Muse to the U.K. adults on Tuesday, promising users a tool they can trust to lend a “helping hand” on everything from chasing a refund and renewing car insurance to doing the Christmas shopping.

It is the first AI agent product to be launched by a Big Tech company in the U.K., and regulators will be watching closely.

The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (DRCF), comprising the Competition and Markets Authority, Financial Conduct Authority, Ofcom, and the Information Commission, published a statement last month warning that AI agent products “may amplify and accelerate risks” to consumers.

Reuters reported last week that Meta staffers had raised concerns internally about “undesired actions” carried out by the agent since its debut in the U.S., from accessing encrypted messages to supplying bogus information about purchases (a Meta spokesperson said these were “isolated incidents.”)

In a blog post published Tuesday morning, Meta sought to reassure would-be users that although the agent is built to carry out tasks on their behalf, Muse is “private, safe and secure by design.” For example, users can choose whether their interactions with the agent are used to develop and improve Meta’s AI — though will need to actively switch this setting off.

“We’ve engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so,” Meta said in its blog post.

Legal challenges brought by Meta threaten the building blocks of how the U.K.’s Online Safety Act is enforced.

Ofcom is worried Pornhub over-relied on Apple’s age checks to keep kids off its platform.

The U.K. can learn from Australia and France’s attempts to kick kids off social media.

Reform UK said GDPR has “strangled small businesses and tech firms.”

title: Novartis rejects AI industry hopes to cure cancer in five to 10 years
title_en: Novartis rejects AI industry hopes to cure cancer in five to 10 years
author: Financial Times
article_content:
Micah Abiodun 3 mins read Published 54 seconds ago Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan says AI could cut average drug-development time from 12 years to eight over the next decade. AI is already helping with early drug discovery, but predicting whether a medicine will actually work safely in humans remains much harder. Only a small number of AI-enabled medicines have reached late-stage trials, leaving claims of dramatically higher clinical success largely unproven. Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, who also sits on Anthropic’s board, has pushed back against predictions that artificial intelligence (AI) will cure cancer within a decade. In a November 23 Financial Times interview, he said AI would need ten years just to shorten drug development by four years.

AI can identify compounds with the potential to become medicines. Predicting how those compounds will behave inside the human body is much harder.

Narasimhan expects AI to shorten average drug development time from 12 to eight years within a decade. He also sees the success rate of medicines entering human trials rising from 8% to 12%.

Novartis has already used AI to cut up to two years from early drug discovery, a process that typically takes four years.

However, Narasimhan’s estimates are far more modest than the predictions of AI industry leaders.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei believes AI could help overcome cancer and Alzheimer’s within a decade. Demis Hassabis, Google DeepMind CEO and founder of its drug-discovery spinoff Isomorphic Labs, has suggested AI could solve all diseases within a similar timeframe.

The disagreement has been ascribed by Narasimhan to the “engineering mindset” of the technology industry.

He estimates that only 5% of everything that takes place in the human body is understood by scientists. Unlike programming and languages, a great deal of what is known as human biology is poorly understood. This makes it harder for AI to make reliable predictions.

In September, a McKinsey report emphasized similar problems. Much of the investment in AI by the industry gets directed toward the design of molecules rather than focusing on understanding the biological mechanisms behind diseases.

The gap between knowing the molecular structure and predicting the molecular behavior is seen in the latest research of OpenAI. On November 20, the company presented MedChemBench, which tests the AI models on 99 problems that are taken from existing published scientific papers in the area of medicinal chemistry.

GPT-6.2 Astra achieved an overall score of 84.5% at the highest shared reasoning setting. However, its performance differed significantly by task. GPT-6 Astra scored 95.4% in reconstructing molecular structures. However, it earned only 50% in terms of choosing candidates among substances and predicting their properties.

The findings suggest that identifying molecular structures is easier for AI than determining which compounds could make effective medicines. OpenAI acknowledged that the results have yet to establish whether AI can discover new drugs or improve laboratory decisions.

Faster drug discovery offers little benefit if medicines cannot make it through clinical trials. A June review published in Pharmaceuticals found that roughly 90% of drug candidates entering clinical development fail to gain approval. The high failure rate remains a concern despite global AI investment in life sciences exceeding $100 billion.

Even drug candidates that advance through clinical trials face setbacks. A September Bain & Company survey found that 53% of Phase II and III trials run behind schedule.

Faster discovery could put even more pressure on clinical development. In August, Jean-Philippe Vert, CEO of Bioptimus, a developer of AI foundation models for biology, warned that AI could generate more promising drug candidates than the clinical trial process can accommodate.

An October study published in Cancer Treatment Reviews identified 129 AI-enabled drug candidates that had entered human trials by March 1, 2026.

Of these, 74 targeted cancer. However, only five candidates across all disease areas had reached or completed Phase III.

Jeff Leiden, executive chairman of biotechnology company Vertex Pharmaceuticals, said that roughly 50 AI companies examined Vertex’s dataset of 10,000 compounds. Not one independently produced a working drug.

Even without delivering cures within a decade, AI could improve pharmaceutical research returns. Raising clinical success rates from 8% to 12% would represent a 50% relative improvement.

Novartis’ November 19 investor presentation showed that the company spent $104 billion on core research and development (R&D) and capital projects between 2016 and September 2026.

Even Anthropic recognizes the limits of AI. As Cryptopolitan previously reported following the launch of Claude for Life Sciences, Anthropic’s biology head Eric Kauderer-Abrams cautioned:

Clinical trials that take three years are not suddenly going to take one month.

No. He rejected that forecast, telling the Financial Times that AI will take about a decade just to shorten average drug development from 12 years to eight, and placed the likely outcome "somewhere in the middle" of AI leaders' claims and the pharma industry's skepticism.

In early discovery. Narasimhan said AI has cut up to two years off a discovery phase that usually ran four, and Bioptimus CEO Jean-Philippe Vert said some work that once took five to seven years can now be done in under two. However, both warned clinical trials remain the slow step.

Its top model, GPT-6.2 Astra, scored 84.5 percent overall and 95.4 percent on reconstructing molecular structures, but earned only about half the credit for selecting compounds and predicting their real-world properties. OpenAI said the results do not show that models can discover new drugs.

We strongly recommend independent research and/or consultation with a qualified professional before making any investment decisions.

Now on his 7th year in the crypto media space, he covers major cryptos, altcoins, DeFi, stablecoins, macro trends, and emerging tech.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

article_content_zh:
Micah Abiodun 阅读 3 分钟 54 秒前发布 诺华公司首席执行官 Vas Narasimhan 表示，人工智能可以在未来十年将平均药物开发时间从 12 年缩短到 8 年。人工智能已经在帮助早期药物发现，但预测药物是否能真正在人体中安全发挥作用仍然困难得多。只有少数人工智能药物已进入后期试验，因此临床成功率大幅提高的说法在很大程度上尚未得到证实。诺华公司首席执行官兼 Anthropic 董事会成员 Vas Narasimhan 反驳了人工智能 (AI) 将在十年内治愈癌症的预测。在 11 月 23 日接受英国《金融时报》采访时，他表示人工智能需要十年时间才能将药物开发时间缩短四年。

人工智能可以识别有潜力成为药物的化合物。预测这些化合物在人体内的表现要困难得多。

Narasimhan 预计人工智能将在十年内将平均药物开发时间从 12 年缩短至 8 年。他还认为药物进入人体试验的成功率从 8% 上升到 12%。

诺华公司已经利用人工智能将早期药物发现的时间缩短了两年，而这一过程通常需要四年的时间。

然而，Narasimhan 的估计比人工智能行业领导者的预测要温和得多。

Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 相信人工智能可以在十年内帮助克服癌症和阿尔茨海默氏症。谷歌 DeepMind 首席执行官兼药物发现衍生公司 Isomorphic Labs 的创始人 Demis Hassabis 表示，人工智能可以在相似的时间内解决所有疾病。

Narasimhan 将这种分歧归咎于科技行业的“工程思维”。

他估计，人体中发生的一切事情只有 5% 能够被科学家了解。与编程和语言不同，人们对人类生物学的很多知识知之甚少。这使得人工智能更难做出可靠的预测。

九月，麦肯锡的一份报告强调了类似的问题。业界对人工智能的大部分投资都直接用于分子设计，而不是专注于理解疾病背后的生物机制。

OpenAI 的最新研究显示了了解分子结构和预测分子行为之间的差距。 11 月 20 日，该公司推出了 MedChemBench，该软件针对 99 个问题测试了 AI 模型，这些问题取自药物化学领域现有已发表的科学论文。

GPT-6.2 Astra 在最高共享推理设置下取得了 84.5% 的总分。然而，其性能因任务而异。 GPT-6 Astra 在重建分子结构方面得分为 95.4%。然而，在选择候选物质并预测其特性方面，它只获得了 50% 的成绩。

研究结果表明，对于人工智能来说，识别分子结构比确定哪些化合物可以制造有效的药物更容易。 OpenAI 承认，结果尚未确定人工智能是否可以发现新药或改善实验室决策。

如果药物无法通过临床试验，那么更快的药物发现几乎没有什么好处。 《Pharmaceuticals》 6 月份发表的一篇评论发现，大约 90% 进入临床开发的候选药物未能获得批准。尽管全球人工智能在生命科学领域的投资超过 1000 亿美元，但高失败率仍然令人担忧。

即使是通过临床试验取得进展的候选药物也面临着挫折。贝恩公司 9 月份的一项调查发现，53% 的 II 期和 III 期试验进度落后于计划。

title: Singapore Won’t Be Conduit to Skirt US Chip Curbs, Wong Says
title_en: Singapore Won’t Be Conduit to Skirt US Chip Curbs, Wong Says

inline_images.caption: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming, in a portrait released by the company in 2021. Credit: ByteDance
inline_images.alt: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming, in a portrait released by the company in 2021. Credit: ByteDance

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
SINGAPORE – Singapore will not allow itself to be used as a conduit for illegal trade practices, but neither can it possibly trace and verify the entire supply chain behind every product that passes through its shores, said Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

He was referring to the higher 12.5 per cent tariffs imposed by America on Singapore’s exports, due to the alleged use of forced labour, as well as to recent concerns raised by the US over goods being routed through other countries to circumvent tariffs.

However, tariffs are but one symptom of deeper global tensions and a more unstable world that Singapore has to survive and endure for years to come, he added.

PM Wong said during his National Day Rally speech on Aug 23: “Across the globe, the rules and norms that underpinned stability and prosperity for decades are being overturned.”

One reason for this change is that China has risen rapidly and is a peer competitor of the US with deep capabilities in many areas. Both countries have to live with a new reality where they compete fiercely but avoid outright conflict, PM Wong said.

The world is also shaped by other forces like Europe and India, and middle powers are also asserting their interests more actively, he added.

“Power is becoming dispersed,” he said. “Different centres are jostling for influence, competing for markets, technology, resources, and increasingly, over who sets the rules of the game.”

This is reflected in the changing global trading system, which used to be about countries lowering their barriers and tariffs, and having open economies.

“Companies assumed that if one supplier failed, another would easily step in,” PM Wong said.

“That was the world we knew. Now all that is changing.”

He noted that the Covid-19 pandemic was a wake-up call when suppliers that could usually be counted on stopped delivering goods.

This was followed by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the current Middle East crisis which expose vulnerabilities in energy, food and other critical supplies, PM Wong said.

Europe was affected when Russia cut off gas supplies during the invasion.

Meanwhile, the Middle East crisis impacted many countries due to the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global shipping channel for oil and gas supplies.

Oil prices have skyrocketed to above US$100 a barrel in the past few months, creating inflationary pressures and adding fuel to the global energy crisis.

“Countries have learnt from these crises,” PM Wong said. “Security now weighs much more heavily in their economic decisions.”

Hence, governments are increasingly using trade, technology and investment to advance their strategic and security objectives, he added.

An example was the US imposing “liberation day” tariffs in April 2025 on countries globally.

At that point, the baseline tariff of 10 per cent was imposed on Singapore.

The US courts later ruled the tariffs unlawful, but the US administration found another way to reimpose tariffs, which increased to 12.5 per cent on Singapore due to the alleged use of forced labour.

PM Wong said: “We all agree there should be no place for forced labour. This is a global problem.”

But he said the better way to tackle this issue is through international cooperation and common standards, not tariffs.

The US now expects countries to have domestic measures to stop imported goods made with forced labour, he noted.

Another concern the US has raised is regarding Chinese goods being routed through other countries, especially in South-east Asia, to circumvent its tariff.

PM Wong said Singapore takes both issues seriously.

“We have clear rules and laws in place. We enforce them and we expect companies operating here to comply,” he said, noting that Singapore will investigate and take action if there is credible evidence of wrongdoing.

However, as a major centre for re-exports and transshipment, Singapore also cannot possibly verify the entire supply chain behind every product, he said. Goods pass through Singapore from all over the world.

“We must also be realistic about what Singapore can do on our own,” PM Wong said.

“So we will continue engaging the US and explaining our position.”

But this issue is just part of a larger reality, where trade is no longer just about economics, but increasingly shaped by security considerations, he said.

“They reflect deeper tensions around the world,” PM Wong said.

He noted that there are major conflicts in Europe and the Middle East that seem far away from Singapore.

“But the conflicts do not always stay neatly contained. Other powers can get drawn in – because of their alliances, their interests, or simply because events force their hand,” he said, adding that new technologies like cheap drones that can inflict serious damage add to the risks.

Hence, the risks of miscalculation and escalation are much higher and a regional conflict can quickly become something bigger.

“Each thinks it is acting defensively. But step by step, the conflict can widen far beyond what anyone originally intended,” PM Wong said.

He added that no one wants another world war, but cautioned that major wars historically have begun because events spiralled out of control, not because they were planned.

“We all hope never to see a global conflict in our lifetimes. But we cannot ignore the growing risks,” he said.

PM Wong noted that there has been more pressure “below the threshold of open war”, with tactics such as economic coercion, foreign interference, disinformation campaigns, and cyberattacks on critical infrastructure.

These grey-zone tactics can cause real damage, even if troops do not physically cross over borders, he said.

“So this is our world today – more contested, more unstable and more dangerous than before,” PM Wong said.

“These are not temporary disruptions. This is the new normal that Singapore will have to endure and survive for many years to come.”

Sue-Ann Tan is a business correspondent at The Straits Times, covering capital markets and sustainable finance.

article_content_zh:
字节跳动联合创始人张一鸣现在是亚洲首富，估计财富超过 1050 亿美元，领先于印度实业家高塔姆·阿达尼 (Gautam Adani)。该排名来自彭博亿万富翁指数，43岁的张此前从未占据过榜首。

该数字是估计值，其他追踪者不同意。周三，《福布斯》实时榜单显示张的净资产为 840 亿美元。这种差距主要来自于每个榜单对字节跳动的估值，字节跳动是一家私人公司，其股票不公开交易。彭博对其估值进行了 10% 的风险折扣。

投资者估值推动了最新的上涨。在彭博社分析了贝莱德、富达投资和 T. Rowe Price 持有的字节跳动股票的最新标记后，张的财富本月增加了超过 120 亿美元。今年 6 月，在字节跳动美国重组完成后，彭博社将字节跳动折扣从 25% 下调后，该指数已将他超越穆克什·安巴尼 (Mukesh Ambani) 升至第二位。

这次重组几乎走向了相反的方向。去年的大部分时间里，字节跳动都面临着 TikTok 在美国可能被关闭的问题，随后 1 月份将该应用程序的美国业务控制权交给了甲骨文和 Silver Lake 牵头的一家企业。从那时起，该公司更加注重人工智能，推出了豆宝聊天机器人和 Seedance 视频生成器，以及目前正在训练的 10 万亿参数模型。

研究公司 Omdia 首席分析师苏连杰 (Lian Jye Su) 告诉彭博社：“他的牌打得很好。他坚持走自己的路线，然后继续加大对人工智能的投资。”

苏表示，即使美国立法者在 2023 年质疑 TikTok 首席执行官 Shou Chew，张仍继续支持人工智能开发，字节跳动的社交媒体数据存储理论上可以帮助其训练模型。

他称人工智能字节跳动是自视频平台以来最大的机遇，而中国激烈的竞争则是最大的风险。

阿达尼的幻灯片解释了互换的另一半。据彭博社报道，他的财富在 6 月份达到了约 1200 亿美元的峰值，随后 MSCI 指数的重新平衡在 8 月底使他的集团市值蒸发了约 150 亿美元。在油价和债券收益率上涨的推动下，更广泛的抛售导致股价进一步走低。

自 2019 年 3 月彭博社首次对其估值为 130 亿美元以来，张的估计财富增长了约八倍。他已经是中国首富，现在排名高于阿达尼、安巴尼和优衣库创始人柳井正，财富建立在港口、能源和零售业。据彭博社上周报道，同样的繁荣也让中国芯片制造商的创始人成为亿万富翁，尽管这些公司尚未实现盈利。

该排名发布一周后，北京方面一直公开捍卫其人工智能雄心。中国商务部驳回了美国人工智能高管为争夺技术霸权而减缓前沿发展的呼吁，而财富越来越依赖于人工智能的中国首富现在也是亚洲首富。

title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
title_en: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
author: Mike Wheatley
article_content:
Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence. Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution.

They’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks. The first project within that initiative is Shirudo, which is designed to protect infrastructure systems automatically from critical exploits before they can be patched.

In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact. It has gotten away with this because much of the world’s computing infrastructure was built for workflows that proceed at human speeds. But with the emergence of AI models that can discover and work out how to exploit vulnerabilities in a matter of seconds, this kind of reactive security is no longer enough.

According to Graf, even now, when a major vulnerability is discovered in widely used software, it can take weeks or even months to come up with a fix and ensure that every major system is patched against it. “That timeframe is no longer acceptable given that the mean time to exploitation has become negative, meaning that a growing number of vulnerabilities are now being exploited before they are publicly disclosed,” he said. “This will only accelerate with the further evolution of AI models and cybersecurity capabilities, becoming the norm in open-weight models.”

To counter these kinds of automated attacks, Cisco and OpenAI believe that infrastructure has to be rebuilt from scratch with security in mind. They argue that it’s time to abandon static defenses and embrace systems that are hardened by default, immutable and rebuildable from a previous “good” state, so users can quickly revert back in the event of an attack. To do this, infrastructure systems must be based on Trusted Platform Modules and utilize reinforcement learning techniques to safely test their own defenses so they can adapt when faced with novel cyberattacks from previously unknown vectors.

Graf said the key to doing this is to secure workloads at runtime, which is why the initial focus of Cisco’s and OpenAI’s initiative is Shirudo, an evolution of the open-source Tetragon runtime security project that aims to provide autonomous defense for AI agents.

Shirudo, named after the Japanese word for “shield,” is based on extended Berkeley Packet Filter or eBPF, which is a Linux kernel technology that acts like a kind of sandbox within the operating system. Similar to how JavaScript makes web browsers programmable without a restart, eBPF enables small, verified programs to run inside the Linux kernel to observe an application’s activity and modify its behavior without altering its source code or rebooting it.

Graf explained that Cisco and OpenAI chose to use eBPF because there are no other real alternatives. Human-focused security consoles and policy languages are simply too slow for AI agents, and will limit their productivity.

By exposing programmable kernel interfaces, eBPF enables AI agents to capture granular telemetry, evaluate mitigations in monitoring mode and deploy cryptographically-signed shields in milliseconds. So cyberattacks that exploit unknown vulnerabilities can be blocked in real time without causing disruption to their live workloads.

“There is nothing more important than giving security teams the tools they need to match the speed of the AI-driven threats they are facing,” said Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel. “We need self-defending infrastructure that acts at the speed of code, learns in real time and shields itself until patches are safely rolled out.”

OpenAI’s role in this is to prove that eBPF is up to the job, and it has already deployed Shirudo as part of an agentic control plane that’s powered by its Codex coding agent. When given details of a new vulnerability, Codex can use Shirudo to autonomously build an exploit reproducer and then design a mitigation strategy. It then validates the mitigation code and deploys the cryptographically-signed shields across all affected nodes.

The two partners recently tested Shirudo against a critical new vulnerability in OpenJDK called Java4Shell, and it was able to rapidly generate Java bytecode that it injected directly into a running Elasticsearch agent to block malicious Base64 overwrites that would have compromised the system.

OpenAI co-founder and President Greg Brockman said the goal of Shirudo is to help companies protect their systems from new threats until they can build and deploy a more durable patch. “When one team finds a better way to protect a system, others shouldn’t have to start from scratch,” he explained.

To that end, Cisco and OpenAI say they’re welcoming developers, kernel engineers, platform builders and security experts to collaborate on Shirudo and other initiatives within their broader Secure Infrastructure Project.

article_content_zh:
网络犯罪分子已经能够在几秒钟内发现软件中的漏洞并利用它们，而这一切都归功于人工智能。企业需要更好的方式来保护自己，因此世界顶级人工智能公司之一 OpenAI Group PBC 与思科系统公司合作，正在加紧推出解决方案，这是理所应当的。

他们刚刚宣布了一项新的开源且雄心勃勃的计划，称为“安全基础设施项目”，该计划旨在确保所有人工智能计算基础设施的设计都是安全的，并且能够防御闪电般快速的人工智能驱动的攻击。该计划中的第一个项目是 Shirudo，旨在在修补基础设施系统之前自动保护其免受关键漏洞的攻击。

思科安全首席技术官兼工程副总裁 Thomas Graf 在一篇博文中解释说，业界一直将安全视为事后的想法，本质上是事后才将安全性附加到系统上的东西。它已经摆脱了这一点，因为世界上大部分计算基础设施都是为以人类速度进行的工作流程而构建的。但随着人工智能模型的出现，可以在几秒钟内发现并找出如何利用漏洞，这种反应式安全已经不够了。

Graf 表示，即使是现在，当在广泛使用的软件中发现重大漏洞时，也可能需要数周甚至数月的时间才能找到修复方案并确保每个主要系统都针对该漏洞进行修补。他说：“鉴于平均利用时间已变为负数，这个时间范围已不再可接受，这意味着越来越多的漏洞在公开披露之前就已被利用。” “随着人工智能模型和网络安全能力的进一步发展，这只会加速，成为开放权重模型的规范。”

为了应对此类自动攻击，思科和 OpenAI 认为必须从头开始重建基础设施，并牢记安全性。他们认为，是时候放弃静态防御并采用默认强化的、不可变的、可从之前的“良好”状态重建的系统，这样用户就可以在受到攻击时快速恢复。为此，基础设施系统必须基于可信平台模块，并利用强化学习技术来安全地测试自身的防御能力，以便在面临来自先前未知向量的新型网络攻击时能够适应。

Graf 表示，做到这一点的关键是确保运行时工作负载的安全，这就是为什么思科和 OpenAI 计划的最初重点是 Shirudo，这是开源 Tetragon 运行时安全项目的演变，旨在为 AI 代理提供自主防御。

Shirudo 得名于日语中的“盾牌”一词，它基于扩展的伯克利数据包过滤器或 eBPF，这是一种 Linux 内核技术，其作用类似于操作系统中的一种沙箱。与 JavaScript 如何使 Web 浏览器无需重新启动即可进行编程类似，eBPF 允许小型、经过验证的程序在 Linux 内核内运行，以观察应用程序的活动并修改其行为，而无需更改其源代码或重新启动它。

Graf 解释说，Cisco 和 OpenAI 选择使用 eBPF 是因为没有其他真正的替代方案。以人为本的安全控制台和策略语言对于人工智能代理来说太慢了，并且会限制他们的生产力。

通过公开可编程内核接口，eBPF 使 AI 代理能够捕获粒度遥测、评估监控模式下的缓解措施并在几毫秒内部署加密签名的防护罩。因此，可以实时阻止利用未知漏洞的网络攻击，而不会对其实时工作负载造成干扰。

思科总裁兼首席产品官 Jeetu Patel 表示：“没有什么比为安​​全团队提供所需的工具来应对他们面临的人工智能威胁的速度更重要的了。” “我们需要自卫基础设施，以代码的速度运行，实时学习并自我保护，直到补丁安全推出。”

OpenAI 在这方面的作用是证明 eBPF 能够胜任这项工作，并且它已经将 Shirudo 部署为由 Codex 编码代理提供支持的代理控制平面的一部分。当给出新漏洞的详细信息时，Codex 可以使用 Shirudo 自主构建漏洞重现器，然后设计缓解策略。然后，它会验证缓解代码并在所有受影响的节点上部署加密签名的防护罩。

这两个合作伙伴最近针对 OpenJDK 中名为 Java4Shell 的严重新漏洞测试了 Shirudo，它能够快速生成 Java 字节码，并将其直接注入正在运行的 Elasticsearch 代理中，以阻止可能危害系统的恶意 Base64 覆盖。

OpenAI 联合创始人兼总裁 Greg Brockman 表示，Shirudo 的目标是帮助公司保护其系统免受新威胁，直到他们能够构建和部署更持久的补丁。 “当一个团队找到更好的方法来保护系统时，其他团队就不必从头开始，”他解释道。

为此，思科和 OpenAI 表示，他们欢迎开发人员、内核工程师、平台构建者和安全专家在其更广泛的安全基础设施项目中就 Shirudo 和其他计划进行合作。

title: Inside Google’s Failure to Make Google Maps Work for Palestinians
title_en: Inside Google’s Failure to Make Google Maps Work for Palestinians

inline_images.caption: Comparing the route to Rawabi vs. to Ateret on Google Maps
inline_images.alt: Comparing the route to Rawabi vs. to Ateret on Google Maps

inline_images.caption: Google Maps showing a road closure in the West Bank
inline_images.alt: Google Maps showing a road closure in the West Bank

author: Elena DeBre, Paresh Dave, and Lama Rabah
article_content:
On the road that connects the villages to the north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, there is always a watchtower and a gate, often flanked by Israeli soldiers with machine guns around their necks. None of these things are visible on Google Maps. Where drivers see a checkpoint, a barrier, and soldiers searching cars, the world’s most popular navigation app renders a clear blue line indicating the coast is clear.

This story was produced in partnership with the Palestine Reporting Lab, Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism (ARIJ), Lighthouse Reports, and Evident.

Routes and maps are not just a matter of journey times or congestion for the nearly 3.5 million Palestinians in the West Bank. Drivers there are forced to navigate a growing and arbitrary system of more than 900 movement obstacles, like checkpoints, which can be policed with lethal force. For Palestinians, these roads can be a matter of life or death. Google Maps could help them make safer choices. It has failed for years to do so.

Google has the ability to alert checkpoints, a feature that it added to Maps in some locations around the world during the Covid crisis. It is aware of the problems experienced by Palestinian drivers in the West Bank. In fact, a former Google product manager spent six years trying to get Maps to serve Palestinians in the same way it serves the rest of the world.

Interviews with more than a dozen former and current Google employees reveal for the first time the inner tensions at the heart of the Google Maps project. Multiple former employees described how the company abandoned the effort and settled on a map that fails, and even harms, Palestinians. As we revealed last month, Palestinians in the West Bank have bootstrapped makeshift navigation solutions such as the popular Road Conditions Telegram channel to help them go about their lives more safely—achieving what Google will not.

Rubén Lozano joined Google Maps as a product manager in 2019. He devoted his days to keeping track of hyperlocal driving restrictions, making sure that what appeared on the map matched what appeared on the ground. He fielded emails from Barcelona city officials about small shifts in their emission zones and flew to Australia to document one city’s toll prices. Whatever he missed, drivers were sure to alert in feedback forums.

One day in 2019, Lozano was sifting through user complaints when he came across “Mapping Segregation,” a report published by 7amleh, a Palestinian digital rights organization. It alleged a failure of Google Maps unlike any he had ever seen: its exclusion of the web of road restrictions choking Palestinian life in the West Bank. The report notes the way in which Maps privileges illegal Israeli settlements and makes Palestinian communities invisible. The report described that the app’s functions amounted to discrimination and that this was “not a technological issue, but rather a systematic omission.” Lozano saw it as a challenge—one he was uniquely suited to take on.

“How can we help this?” Lozano remembers thinking after reading the report. Google was the best-equipped company in the world at dealing with mapping infrastructure, he thought; surely he could use these resources to make Google Maps relevant and safe for Palestinian drivers. Lozano worked for over six years to create a more equitable map of the West Bank. His effort cratered in close to six weeks.

“Google has more than enough computing capacity and engineering capacity,” one former Google Maps engineer told us. “They have solved much larger problems.”

A driver who maps a route from a point inside Israel to a Palestinian town, such as Rawabi, is alerted to a border crossing. If a driver takes that same route to Ateret, the settlement next door, the map shows one seamless drive, with no mention of a border. Israel and an illegal West Bank settlement are shown as part of one contiguous territory on Google Maps.

Google spokesperson Caroline Bourdeau tells WIRED that the company has experienced “challenges acquiring comprehensive and reliable data in this highly complex area.” Since the launch of Maps in 2005, Google has specialized in innovating methods to secure the best data from the hardest-to-access places. Over the past two decades it has carried out crowdsourcing efforts in almost every country in the world. Jennifer Mazzon, who helped lead the company's first community mapping tool, says the company had “armies of people” manually adding and updating map information for everywhere from Costa Rica to the Democratic Republic of Congo. In addition to relying on user inputs, Google built out its maps using satellite, aerial, and street view imagery, as well as government data, and licensed third-party sources when necessary. This commitment to completeness has not extended to Palestinians.

When Lozano first decided he wanted to map the West Bank, his direct managers agreed to back and fund the project. But his colleagues warned him against any optimism. He discovered he was not the first person at Google to try this. “It's a very difficult problem,” he recalls being told. People at the company remembered the backlash when, six years earlier, the company began referring to “Palestine” rather than the “Palestinian Territories” on a regional site: The Knesset questioned a company executive about this, and Google reportedly promised to keep the Israeli government updated about any related policy decisions in the future.

Lozano remained undeterred. Mapping the world as it is was his job, he thought. He picked up the pieces of previous efforts and set to work.

Lozano learned that since the 1995 Oslo Accords, the West Bank has been divided into three zones. Two of them, known as A and B, should be administered to a greater or lesser extent by the Palestinian Authority and are where most of the Palestinian population lives. But Areas A and B are small islands inside Area C, which constitutes the vast majority of the landmass, mostly comprising farmland and smaller Palestinian communities. Although Area C forms part of what's internationally recognized as the Palestinian West Bank, the land is under complete Israeli control, crowded with outposts and settlements, military firing zones, and segregated corridors from which West Bank Palestinians are banned.

Lozano wasn't willing to route users differently based on their nationality, as he felt that would risk violating drivers' privacy. He decided to focus instead on making the map as information-rich as possible, so that road users could make informed choices. There seemed an obvious way to do this: display alerts for permanent checkpoints, highlight the respective Israeli and Palestinian-controlled parts of the West Bank, and warn drivers what they would encounter on their route.

Google has increasingly preferred to rely on outside authorities to provide and maintain various types of data used in Maps, according to a current employee. In search of reliable information on West Bank roads, Lozano discovered that a former colleague had identified what seemed like the best source for data on Palestinian geography: an Egyptian company that he says held detailed information on coordinates of Palestinian- and Israeli-controlled areas in the territory, as well as descriptions and locations of permanent checkpoints, which the Israeli government has never published. Using Google's internal app for map building and testing, a process known as “fish fooding,” Lozano created a prototype. It was getting close, he thought, but was missing crucial input. He wanted to talk to Palestinian drivers, the actual people the map was supposed to help. “We don't want to launch this just based on the team here in Seattle,” he recalls thinking.

Lozano had previously conducted user research around the world for other projects at Google. He thought this process would be no different. As usual, he reached out to Google’s user research (UX) team with his request for interview subjects to discuss how to improve his product, asking them to connect him with Palestinians who had driven in the West Bank. Typically, the UX team would then coordinate with their external contractors to plan the research. He had sometimes experienced delays as the researchers connected him with people. But he had never been denied, until now.

The UX team told him that Google’s research vendors did not have access to users with experience driving in the West Bank and were not going to look for them. “We couldn't get Palestinians as part of the users to take our study because most of the companies that Google was contracting with would not be able to source Palestinians,” Lozano says. Another Google source familiar with UX projects and the region says that these vendors would not interview people in Palestine because of concerns for the safety of their workers. Google tells WIRED that it has solicited input on its West Bank map before, from employees who know the region. But Lozano wanted to talk to Palestinian drivers on the ground. Cut off from Google's sprawling network, Lozano drew on distant personal connections to conduct user research. “We were asking, for the Palestinians, ‘What do you want to know?’”he said, “‘What is the information that you want?’”

The Palestinians he spoke with told him that even if the map could not route around Israeli-controlled areas or checkpoints, they still saw value in having a map that gave them a bit more visibility before getting on the road, mitigating the unpredictability they faced in their journeys.

Just as Lozano was ready to have Palestinian drivers test the product on actual West Bank roads, Covid-19 hit. His scheduled trip there in April 2020 was canceled, and he was pulled away from his West Bank work to prioritize mapping pandemic restrictions around the world. This had an upside for his waylaid project. “The concept of a checkpoint,” Lozano says, was introduced into Google's infrastructure. This included a new checkpoint icon and a navigation algorithm to help drivers route through it.

A road closure update on the map sourced from the “Binyamin Council,” which is responsible for governing nearly 50 Israeli settlements and outposts occupying the West Bank in violation of international law.

As the pandemic subsided, Lozano's attention returned slowly to Palestine, continuing to work on the problem when other duties permitted. By the time he chose to leave Google, in March 2025, he felt that his West Bank map was ready to go live. “As long as we ingest it in the system,” he says he told the team, “it will work.”

Multiple former Google colleagues agreed that the work Lozano did was robust. After a user plugged in directions for a West Bank drive on Google Maps, the display would shade the Israeli- and Palestinian-controlled areas that the person would pass through on their route. A note in the step-by-step directions would notify drivers about which areas the route crossed too. He had developed a way to mark and route through checkpoints, a list of permanent checkpoints with their locations for the West Bank, and a plan to display them on drivers' routes using the system built for Covid checkpoints. He was satisfied with the handover: “I’m leaving happy that the person that is taking over also cares about this,” he says he thought at the time.

A few months after he left, Lozano's confidence was rewarded. Google updated its West Bank map. The administrative zones were highlighted and route alerts activated.

Drivers traveling between Israeli cities, on Israeli roads that cut through the West Bank, would be alerted that the route “may cross country/region borders” and would be told in the directions that they were going through “Area C.” It was clear, in other words, that the drivers were exiting Israeli territory.

A former Google manager, who was familiar with the project but asked for anonymity for fear of reprisal, described the new map as a qualified success: The checkpoints were not shown, but nonetheless it was “the maximum that could be done based on the resources that we knew would be available.” Google retired its checkpoint icon for Covid in March 2025, the same month Lozano left, and did not repurpose the system for West Bank checkpoints, as Lozano had set his colleagues up to be able to do.

The success was short-lived, however. Days after Google updated the West Bank mobile map with Lozano's work, Israeli newspaper Haaretz published an article criticizing a “glitch” impacting Israeli drivers. It reported that Google Maps was now avoiding routes on Israeli-built roads that cross into the West Bank, designed to let Israelis travel through the territory quickly. Google responded to the article saying that it was aware of these problems and was “working to fix them.”

Weeks later, by December 2025, the company had retracted important parts of the West Bank map update. Google confirmed this to WIRED. A current employee close to the company's work in the region said that he was not aware of any communication, even internally, about Google's decision to do this.

Now, drivers routing from Tel Aviv to a major settlement in the West Bank could travel without once being informed that they were leaving Israel and entering the West Bank. Although Google's map includes a static dashed line marking a 1949 “armistice agreement line,” drivers using the mobile app are given no notification that they are crossing it. From a user experience perspective, Google Maps made much of the West Bank seem to Israeli drivers like it was Israel.

What did remain of Lozano's efforts were notifications when users were entering the parts of the West Bank that contain the towns and cities where most Palestinians live. The updates effectively amount to warnings for Israeli drivers before entering Palestinian population centers.

The former Google manager with knowledge of the project was unsurprised that Google backtracked part of Lozano's work: A complaint from Israel is all it would take for Google to alter the West Bank map, he believes. Google did not deny this. The company has become increasingly entangled with Israel in recent years through its acquisition of two Israeli companies, Wiz and Waze, and the signing of a joint $1.2 billion cloud infrastructure contract with Amazon Web Services and the Israeli government, known as Project Nimbus, that rights groups claim has enabled war crimes in Gaza. Today, as Israeli military and settler violence reaches unprecedented levels in the West Bank, the stakes of a wrong turn have never been higher for Palestinians there. Yet, Google's West Bank map continues to cater exclusively to Israelis. “Any claims of Google Maps showing bias in this region are false,” Google’s Bourdeau tells WIRED. “We are constantly working to improve the map for all users.” In response to WIRED’s questions about military and settler actions, the Israeli military says that “the security forces operate” in the West Bank “to provide security to all residents.”

Amazon did not respond to a request for comment.

Not only are there indications that the world's leading tech company has in effect ceded the West Bank to Israel; in at least one instance, Google populated its map with information drawn from an illegal settlement authority. Google tells WIRED that it does not have a policy against using or purchasing data from settlers. As recently as this November, a road closure update appeared on the map that had been sourced from the “Binyamin Council,” which is responsible for governing nearly 50 Israeli settlements and outposts occupying the West Bank in violation of international law.

“Israel's changing the facts on the ground, and the map is then adapting to represent that,” says Zena Agha, a scholar of colonial cartography. “They’ll put that on their maps because that's what the Israelis are saying, and then it de facto creates a reality in itself.”
content_snippet:
On the road that connects the villages to the north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, there is always a watchtower and a gate, often flanked by Israeli soldiers with machine guns around their necks. None of these things are visible on Google Maps. Where drivers see a checkpoint, a barrier, and soldiers searching cars, the world’s most popular navigation app renders a clear blue line indicating the coast is clear.

This story was produced in partnership with the Palestine Reporting Lab, Ara
summary_en: Google Maps has failed to annotate over 900 checkpoints and movement restrictions in the West Bank, creating significant safety risks for Palestinian drivers. Despite internal awareness and technical capability to implement such features, Google has neglected to integrate real-time hazard data, forcing users to rely on makeshift third-party reporting channels for navigation safety.

title_zh: 谷歌地图被指长期无视约旦河西岸地理实况
summary_zh: 谷歌地图未能标记约旦河西岸的检查站与行动障碍，被指置巴勒斯坦驾驶者于生命危险之中
article_content_zh:
在被占领的约旦河西岸，连接村庄和拉马拉北部的道路上，总有一座瞭望塔和一扇大门，两侧经常有脖子上挂着机枪的以色列士兵。这些东西在谷歌地图上都看不到。当司机看到检查站、障碍物和士兵搜查汽车时，世界上最受欢迎的导航应用程序会呈现一条清晰的蓝线，表明海岸畅通无阻。

本报道是与巴勒斯坦报道实验室、阿拉伯调查新闻记者 (ARIJ)、灯塔报道和 Evident 合作制作的。

对于约旦河西岸近 350 万巴勒斯坦人来说，路线和地图不仅仅是出行时间或交通拥堵的问题。那里的司机被迫通过一个由 900 多个移动障碍组成的不断增长的任意系统，例如检查站，这些障碍可以用致命武力进行监管。对于巴勒斯坦人来说，这些道路可能事关生死。谷歌地图可以帮助他们做出更安全的选择。多年来它一直未能做到这一点。

谷歌有能力向检查站发出警报，这一功能在新冠危机期间被添加到世界各地某些地点的地图中。它了解约旦河西岸的巴勒斯坦司机所经历的问题。事实上，一位前谷歌产品经理花了六年时间试图让地图为巴勒斯坦人提供服务，就像为世界其他地区服务一样。

对十多名谷歌前任和现任员工的采访首次揭示了谷歌地图项目核心的内部紧张局势。多位前员工描述了该公司如何放弃这一努力并最终选择了一张失败的地图，甚至伤害了巴勒斯坦人。正如我们上个月透露的那样，约旦河西岸的巴勒斯坦人已经启动了临时导航解决方案，例如流行的 Road Conditions Telegram 频道，以帮助他们更安全地生活，从而实现了 Google 无法实现的目标。

Rubén Lozano 于 2019 年加入 Google 地图，担任产品经理。他整天致力于跟踪超本地化驾驶限制，确保地图上显示的内容与地面上显示的内容相符。他回复了巴塞罗那市官员关于排放区小幅变化的电子邮件，并飞往澳大利亚记录了一个城市的通行费价格。无论他错过了什么，司机们一定会在反馈论坛中发出警报。

2019 年的一天，洛萨诺在筛选用户投诉时，偶然发现了巴勒斯坦数字权利组织 7amleh 发布的一份报告《映射隔离》。它声称谷歌地图的失败是他从未见过的：它排除了阻碍约旦河西岸巴勒斯坦人生活的道路限制网络。报告指出了地图如何赋予以色列非法定居点特权，并使巴勒斯坦社区隐形。报告称，该应用程序的功能构成歧视，这“不是技术问题，而是系统性疏忽”。洛萨诺认为这是一个挑战——他非常适合接受这个挑战。

“我们能帮什么忙吗？”洛萨诺记得读完报告后的思考。他认为，谷歌是世界上在处理地图基础设施方面装备最齐全的公司；他当然可以利用这些资源使谷歌地图对巴勒斯坦司机来说更有意义且安全。洛萨诺花了六年多的时间来绘制更加公平的西岸地图。他的努力在近六周内就化为泡影。

“谷歌拥有足够的计算能力和工程能力，”一位前谷歌地图工程师告诉我们。 “他们解决了更大的问题。”

司机在绘制从以色列境内某个地点到拉瓦比等巴勒斯坦城镇的路线时，会收到过境提醒。如果司机沿着同一条路线前往隔壁的定居点阿特雷特，地图上会显示一条无缝的车程，没有提及边界。以色列和约旦河西岸非法定居点在谷歌地图上显示为连续领土的一部分。

谷歌发言人卡罗琳·布尔多 (Caroline Bourdeau) 告诉《连线》杂志，该公司“在这个高度复杂的领域获取全面可靠的数据时遇到了挑战”。自 2005 年推出地图以来，Google 一直专注于创新方法，以确保从最难访问的地方获取最佳数据。过去二十年来，它几乎在世界每个国家都开展了众包工作。帮助领导该公司第一个社区地图工具的 Jennifer Mazzon 表示，该公司有“大量人员”手动添加和更新从哥斯达黎加到刚果民主共和国等各地的地图信息。除了依赖用户输入之外，谷歌还使用卫星、航空和街景图像以及政府数据以及必要时获得许可的第三方来源来构建地图。这种对完整性的承诺并未延伸到巴勒斯坦人。

当洛萨诺第一次决定绘制约旦河西岸地图时，他的直接经理同意支持并资助该项目。但他的同事警告他不要乐观。他发现自己并不是谷歌第一个尝试这一做法的人。 “这是一个非常困难的问题，”他回忆起被告知的情况。该公司的员工还记得六年前，该公司开始在一个地区网站上提及“巴勒斯坦”而不是“巴勒斯坦领土”时所引起的强烈反对：以色列议会就此向一名公司高管提出质询，据报道，谷歌承诺向以色列政府通报未来任何相关政策决定的最新情况。

洛萨诺仍然没有被吓倒。他想，绘制世界地图就是他的工作。他收拾起之前的努力并开始工作。

洛萨诺了解到，自1995年《奥斯陆协议》以来，西岸已分为三个区域。其中两个被称为 A 和 B 的地方应或多或少地由巴勒斯坦权力机构管理，并且是大多数巴勒斯坦人口居住的地方。但 A 区和 B 区是 C 区内的小岛屿，C 区构成了绝大多数陆地，主要由农田和较小的巴勒斯坦社区组成。尽管C区是国际公认的巴勒斯坦西岸的一部分，但这片土地完全处于以色列控制之下，布满了前哨基地和定居点、军事射击区以及禁止西岸巴勒斯坦人进入的隔离走廊。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌公司在约旦河西岸的地图服务中，长期未能标注约900个检查站及通行限制点，导致当地驾驶者面临致命的安全隐患。内部员工访谈证实，谷歌虽具备相关技术能力，但因产品研发路线及内部争议，拒绝将该地区地理数据完整纳入导航系统，迫使当地用户不得不转向第三方即时通讯软件进行手动路径避险。

title: ChatGPT expands GPT-6.2 Sol as OpenAI sets retirement date for two models
title_en: ChatGPT expands GPT-6.2 Sol as OpenAI sets retirement date for two models
author: Zac Hall
article_content:
OpenAI is bringing GPT-6.2 Sol to the Chat tab in ChatGPT today, less than a week after the model debuted in Work and Codex. The company also set a retirement date for two older models.

OpenAI says it tuned this version of Sol for everyday conversation. It’s better at picking out details in photos, like the symbols on a parking sign, and following your instructions when searching the web.

If you’re comparing hotels for a weekend trip, for example, ChatGPT can weigh a shorter walk against a lower nightly rate. It can also offer to alert you when something you’re shopping for drops in price.

The global rollout starts today for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.

As for the outgoing models, OpenAI says it will retire GPT-5.6 Sol from Chat, Work, and Codex on December 23.

GPT-5.6 Terra will also leave ChatGPT Work and Codex on the same day next month.

Related ChatGPT stories:

ChatGPT Health feature now works with Mac app, Dots, more

OpenAI expanding ChatGPT Dots access to iMessage and RCS

iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins now work with ChatGPT

author: Amrith Ramkumar and Josh Dawsey and C. Ryan Barber and Robbie Whelan
article_content:
WASHINGTON—The artificial-intelligence boom that had powered the U.S. stock market and economy for months was coming undone.

Jensen Huang, the longtime CEO of chipmaking giant Nvidia, had been ousted following revelations of two affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Investors were hitting sell on the entire AI trade.

President Trump told associates there was only one solution: getting Huang, a friend and ally, his job back.

Over the weekend, Attorney General Todd Blanche presented an opening. The nation’s top law enforcement officer informed Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Saturday that Huang wasn’t the target or the subject of any Justice Department investigation, adding that the department had no evidence to suggest that he had broken laws or was a national security risk, according to U.S. officials.

President Donald Trump has had plenty of reason to cheer the rise of Nvidia.

The chipmaker helped propel the stock market that Trump is fond of touting. Its billionaire co-founder, Jensen Huang, became one of the president's favorite businessmen. And by the end of last year, Nvidia had become one of Trump's three largest individual stock holdings, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, up from between $615,000 and $1.3 million a year earlier.

Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times — transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, according to a new CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures, which were most recently updated through August.

By midday Monday, Trump's Nvidia stake, based on the value he reported holding in August, would be worth $4.5 million to $57.7 million with stock priced around $157. But the filings give broad dollar ranges for holdings rather than the number of shares, leaving his current stake unclear.

Now, Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, following revelations about his relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China and reports of affairs with company employees, has put those trades back in the spotlight.

Among them was a sale of $500,001 to $1 million on May 18, the first Monday after Trump returned from a state visit to China with Huang. Five days earlier, before Huang boarded Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska, Secretary of State Marco Rubio had briefed Trump on intelligence concerning Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, The New York Times reported.

Trump on Monday denied being briefed. Asked about the reported briefing from Rubio, Trump said, "I haven't heard that," adding that he did not know whether the woman, Alice Huang, was a Chinese spy.

The president's financial accounts also bought smaller amounts of Nvidia shares in the days immediately before and after the May 18 sale, part of a broader trading blitz. Such flurries have defined his second term: Trump disclosed more than 21,000 trades in 2025 alone, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.

A White House spokesperson told CNBC independent advisors manage Trump's portfolio without his input. Trump Organization spokesperson Kimberly Benza said the arrangement is designed to "avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest." The disclosures offer no evidence Trump directed the trades or that his advisors had access to classified intelligence.

Trump has long used the stock market as a scorecard for the economy, touting its record highs — sometimes when highs have not actually been reached — despite the turbulence caused by his tariffs and the Iran war.

"Look, we have the highest stock market we've ever had," Trump told ESPN commentator and political talk show host Stephen A. Smith on Thursday when pressed about Republicans' midterm losses.

Nvidia alone accounted for about 13.5% of the S&P 500's 2026 gains through September, according to an analysis by Choate Wealth that looked at how chip stocks have driven the year's performance.

Huang's rise in Trump's Washington has been nearly as striking as Nvidia's on Wall Street. The two have met or appeared together at least 15 times since Trump returned to office, according to a CNBC review of public records and news reports. Huang in June told The Associated Press that Trump even "calls me in the middle of the night."

At Trump's Jan. 20, 2025, inauguration, several Silicon Valley titans occupied prime seats, but Huang wasn't there. The two men had never met.

That changed on Jan. 31, 2025, when Huang visited the White House, capping a bruising week for Nvidia: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek had wiped $593 billion off the company's market value in a single day, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.

Two days before the meeting, Trump's money managers bought between $1 million and $5 million in Nvidia stock.

For Huang, much of the relationship hinged on access to China. In April 2025, the administration effectively halted sales of Nvidia's H20 chips to China, prompting a $4.5 billion charge, according to an SEC filing. Huang argued that withholding U.S. chips would only accelerate China's development of its own.

The administration eventually relented. After another meeting with Trump in July 2025, Huang announced from Beijing that Nvidia expected to resume H20 sales. A week after Trump confirmed an August 2025 deal calling for 15% of the revenue from the company's chip sales to China to go to the U.S. government, his accounts also bought between $5 million and $25 million in Nvidia stock, one of several large tech investments that day.

Huang was also becoming a fixture of Trump's international diplomacy, joining him in Saudi Arabia and the U.K. Nvidia, already a $1 million donor to Trump's inaugural fund, would pledge another $25 million to his planned White House ballroom on condition of anonymity, The Washington Post first reported.

But behind the scenes, intelligence officials first briefed Trump last fall on Huang's relationship with the woman suspected of spying for China, The New York Times reported.

Trump nevertheless continued to ease restrictions on Nvidia's business in China, announcing Dec. 8 that the company could sell its more powerful H200 chips. His accounts had sold as much as $1 million in Nvidia stock four days earlier and bought more the day after.

In the first eight months of 2026, Trump's accounts made another 38 Nvidia trades worth a combined $9.4 million to $28.3 million, according to CNBC's analysis. A disclosure released Oct. 8 — the day Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science — showed purchases of up to $1.6 million and sales of up to $1 million in August alone.

Trump stood by Huang as Nvidia's board weighed his future last week, urging him to fight to keep his job, the Times reported.

With Huang out and Nvidia's shares tumbling, Trump described him Thursday as a "tremendous talent" who was "going through hell" — in the same interview in which he boasted of the market's record highs.

Trump is already floating a comeback for Huang, telling reporters Monday that reinstating him "certainly isn't a bad idea." But Nvidia's board is not considering his return, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The person asked not to be named because they were discussing internal matters."

article_content_zh:
华盛顿——几个月来为美国股市和经济提供动力的人工智能繁荣即将结束。

芯片制造巨头英伟达 (Nvidia) 的长期首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 在两起事件被曝光后被罢免，其中一起事件与涉嫌中国情报资产有关。投资者正在抛售整个人工智能交易。

特朗普总统告诉同事们，只有一个解决方案：让朋友和盟友黄先生恢复工作。

周末，司法部长托德·布兰奇提出了一个开场白。据美国官员称，美国最高执法官员周六告知特朗普和副总统万斯，黄不是司法部任何调查的目标或对象，并补充说，司法部没有证据表明他违反了法律或构成国家安全风险。

唐纳德·特朗普总统有充分的理由为英伟达的崛起欢呼。

这家芯片制造商帮助推动了特朗普喜欢吹捧的股市。其亿万富翁联合创始人黄仁勋成为总统最喜欢的商人之一。截至去年年底，英伟达已成为特朗普持有的三大个股之一，其价值在 1250 万美元至 5800 万美元之间，高于一年前的 61.5 万美元至 130 万美元。

自从回到白宫以来，特朗普的投资账户至少买卖了 103 次 Nvidia 股票，根据 CNBC 对他的年度和定期财务披露的最新分析，交易总价值为 2,700 万至 9,750 万美元，最新数据截至 8 月份。

到周一中午，根据特朗普 8 月份公布的持股价值，特朗普持有的 Nvidia 股份价值将达到 450 万至 5770 万美元，股价约为 157 美元。但文件给出了所持股份的大致美元范围，而不是股票数量，这使得他目前的持股情况不清楚。

现在，在他与一名涉嫌为中国从事间谍活动的女性的关系被曝光以及与公司员工的风流报道之后，黄周四辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务，使这些交易重新成为人们关注的焦点。

其中包括 5 月 18 日，也就是特朗普与黄一起对中国进行国事访问回国后的第一个周一，成交金额为 50 万至 100 万美元。据《纽约时报》报道，五天前，黄在阿拉斯加加油期间登上空军一号之前，国务卿马可·卢比奥向特朗普通报了有关黄与嫌疑间谍关系的情报。

特朗普周一否认听取了通报。当被问及卢比奥的简报报道时，特朗普说，“我没有听说过”，并补充说，他不知道这名女子艾丽丝·黄是否是中国间谍。

总统的财务账户还在 5 月 18 日出售之前和之后的几天内购买了少量的 Nvidia 股票，这是更广泛的交易闪电战的一部分。这样的混乱定义了他的第二个任期：根据 CNBC 的分析，特朗普仅在 2025 年就披露了超过 21,000 笔交易，而在他的整个第一个任期内披露了大约 500 笔交易。

白宫发言人告诉 CNBC，独立顾问在没有特朗普参与的情况下管理他的投资组合。特朗普集团发言人金伯利·本扎表示，这一安排旨在“避免出现利益冲突”。这些披露没有提供特朗普指导这些交易或他的顾问有权获取机密情报的证据。

特朗普长期以来一直将股市作为经济的记分卡，吹捧其历史新高——有时实际上并未达到高点——尽管他的关税和伊朗战争造成了动荡。

【行业影响与走向】特朗普政府担忧英伟达资产变动对AI产业链的系统性影响。

title: OpenAI Engineer Secretly Recorded Dozens of Meetings, Prosecutors Say
title_en: OpenAI Engineer Secretly Recorded Dozens of Meetings, Prosecutors Say

inline_images.caption: An image from the Justice Department shows what prosecutors said was an audio recording device hidden in an OpenAI executive conference room by Mr. Alfozan. (U.S. Department of Justice, via Reuters)
inline_images.alt: An image from the Justice Department shows what prosecutors said was an audio recording device hidden in an OpenAI executive conference room by Mr. Alfozan.

author: Emmy Martin
article_content:
A former OpenAI engineer accused of planting a hidden recording device at the company captured dozens of internal meetings, including at least one between OpenAI and representatives of a foreign government, federal prosecutors said in a court filing on Monday.

The engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, stored hundreds of audio files on his personal computer, sorted into folders by date and renamed according to their contents, prosecutors said. Many of the recordings involved what appeared to be confidential trade secrets, including meetings with OpenAI customers, they said, and OpenAI identified others as containing material protected by attorney-client privilege.

The filing, which opposes Mr. Alfozan’s request to be released from jail before trial, offers the most detailed account yet of what investigators say he recorded. It also comes days after prosecutors told a federal judge that they were “not aware of any” evidence that Mr. Alfozan had committed espionage, stolen trade secrets or acted as an agent of a foreign government.

Prosecutors did not say in Monday’s filing that he had shared the recordings with anyone. “What the defendant did or intended to do with those audio files remains under investigation,” they wrote.

Mr. Alfozan, a Saudi citizen and U.S. permanent resident, has been charged with one count of illegally intercepting conversations and has pleaded not guilty. A hearing on his release is scheduled for Tuesday morning.

His lawyer, David Rizk, argued in a filing last week that the case had turned out to be far less serious than prosecutors initially suggested, describing his client as “an overly curious tinkerer.” Mr. Rizk wrote that the vast majority of recordings on Mr. Alfozan’s computer “apparently contain just random noise and silence.”

Mr. Rizk could not be immediately reached for comment on Monday.

According to prosecutors, the recordings span 15 folders dated Sept. 8 to Sept. 28 and include meetings held on 12 days in an executive conference room. One file was titled “1200-sovereign-bilateral-briefing-sep22.” The filing did not identify the foreign government.

Mr. Alfozan used Codex, an OpenAI A.I. tool, through his wife’s account to help configure the recording device, add voice detection so it would “only record speech,” and move recordings through a Dropbox account, prosecutors said. His wife has not been accused of wrongdoing.

Prosecutors also said he photographed each printed page of a confidential term sheet for a “strategic partnership” between OpenAI and another company in the early hours of Oct. 5. That was the same day a hidden camera recorded him checking behind the television where OpenAI’s security team had found the listening device days earlier.

The filing also described Mr. Alfozan’s contact with Saudi officials. On Oct. 6, a member of the Saudi royal family sent him a link to Echelon, a Riyadh-based A.I. company, and asked: “Time to move back to KSA and join us?”

Mr. Alfozan suggested he might do so “after the IPO,” prosecutors said. The night before his Oct. 9 arrest, he spoke with the Saudi official by WhatsApp for 16 minutes. Prosecutors said he had also exchanged WhatsApp messages with officials at Saudi Arabia’s communications ministry, including the minister in August and September.

Before planning a trip to Saudi Arabia scheduled for Oct. 12, he asked Codex to find “Saudi shipping deals for boxes” and how much it would cost to fly five suitcases to Riyadh, the filing said.

Prosecutors argued that the timing of his Saudi contacts and travel plans “appears to match the timing of his efforts to record OpenAI meetings.” His lawyers have said the trip was planned for paternity leave.

Mr. Alfozan has offered a $1 million bond, secured in part by $500,000 of his own money and backed by friends from college. He is not proposing to use an earlier offer from the Saudi Consulate to pay his bail. Prosecutors said that if he is released, he should be barred from accessing any OpenAI materials, citing concern that he may still have access to the recordings through cloud storage.

A trial is scheduled for January.

(The New York Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to A.I. systems. The two companies have denied those claims.)

article_content_zh:
联邦检察官在周一提交的一份法庭文件中称，一名前 OpenAI 工程师被指控在该公司安装隐藏录音设备，拍摄了数十场内部会议，其中至少有一场 OpenAI 与外国政府代表之间的会议。

检察官称，这名 35 岁的工程师阿卜杜拉赫曼·阿尔福赞 (Abdulrahman Alfozan) 在他的个人电脑上存储了数百个音频文件，这些文件按日期分类到文件夹中，并根据内容重新命名。他们说，许多录音涉及似乎是机密的商业秘密，包括与 OpenAI 客户的会议，而 OpenAI 认为其他录音包含受律师-委托人特权保护的材料。

该文件反对阿尔福赞先生在审判前出狱的请求，提供了调查人员所说的他所记录内容的最详细描述。几天前，检察官告诉一名联邦法官，他们“不知道”任何证据表明阿尔福赞曾从事间谍活动、窃取商业机密或充当外国政府代理人。

检察官在周一的文件中没有说他曾与任何人分享过这些录音。他们写道：“被告对这些音频文件做了什么或打算做什么仍在调查中。”

阿尔福赞是沙特公民和美国永久居民，他被指控犯有一项非法窃听通话罪，但他不认罪。关于他获释的听证会定于周二上午举行。

他的律师大卫·里兹克(David Rizk)在上周提交的一份文件中辩称，事实证明，案件远没有检察官最初暗示的那么严重，并将他的当事人描述为“一个过于好奇的修补匠”。里兹克写道，阿尔福赞电脑上的绝大多数录音“显然只包含随机的噪音和沉默”。

周一未能立即联系到里兹克置评。

据检察官称，这些录音涵盖了 9 月 8 日至 9 月 28 日期间的 15 个文件夹，其中包括 12 天在行政会议室举行的会议。一份文件的标题是“1200-sovereign-bilingual-briefing-sep22”。该文件没有透露外国政府的身份。

Alfozan 先生使用了 OpenAI A.I. Codex。检察官称，他使用了一个工具，通过他妻子的帐户来帮助配置录音设备，添加语音检测，以便“只录制语音”，并通过 Dropbox 帐户移动录音。他的妻子没有被指控有不当行为。

检察官还表示，他在 10 月 5 日凌晨拍摄了 OpenAI 与另一家公司之间“战略合作伙伴关系”的机密条款清单的每一页。就在同一天，一个隐藏的摄像机记录了他在电视后面检查的情况，OpenAI 的安全团队几天前在电视上发现了窃听设备。

文件还描述了阿尔福赞与沙特官员的接触情况。 10 月 6 日，沙特王室的一名成员向他发送了一个位于利雅得的人工智能公司 Echelon 的链接。公司，并问道：“是时候搬回沙特阿拉伯加入我们了吗？”

检察官表示，阿尔福赞表示他可能会在“首次公开募股之后”这样做。 10 月 9 日被捕的前一天晚上，他通过 WhatsApp 与沙特官员进行了 16 分钟的通话。检察官表示，他还在 8 月和 9 月与沙特阿拉伯通讯部官员（包括部长）交换了 WhatsApp 信息。

文件称，在计划 10 月 12 日前往沙特阿拉伯之前，他要求 Codex 查找“沙特箱子运输优惠”以及将 5 个行李箱空运到利雅得的费用。

检察官辩称，他与沙特的接触和旅行计划的时间“似乎与他记录 OpenAI 会议的时间相符”。他的律师表示，这次旅行是为了休陪产假而计划的。
