【起因与机理】违反企业内部安全合规，涉嫌非法拦截通讯及窃取商业秘密
【关键技术规格】被告利用OpenAI内部Codex模型优化非法录音设备配置。
【行业影响与走向】检方正就数据的外泄风险进行深度调查并拒绝保释请求。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Defendant Abdulrahman Alfozan (Former OpenAI Engineer): Illegally deployed recording devices to capture confidential meetings including foreign government briefings
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Violation of internal security compliance, suspected illegal interception of communications and potential trade secret theft
[Key Metrics] Alfozan has offered a $1 million bond, secured in part by $500,000 of his own money and backed by friends from college.
[Scope & Next Steps] Prosecutors are investigating potential data dissemination while opposing pre-trial release.

title: OpenAI Staffer Likely Captured Secrets on Hidden Bug, US Says
title_en: OpenAI Staffer Likely Captured Secrets on Hidden Bug, US Says

inline_images.caption: An image from the Justice Department shows what prosecutors said was an audio recording device hidden in an OpenAI executive conference room by Mr. Alfozan. (U.S. Department of Justice, via Reuters)
inline_images.alt: An image from the Justice Department shows what prosecutors said was an audio recording device hidden in an OpenAI executive conference room by Mr. Alfozan.

author: Emmy Martin
article_content:
A former OpenAI engineer accused of planting a hidden recording device at the company captured dozens of internal meetings, including at least one between OpenAI and representatives of a foreign government, federal prosecutors said in a court filing on Monday.

The engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, stored hundreds of audio files on his personal computer, sorted into folders by date and renamed according to their contents, prosecutors said. Many of the recordings involved what appeared to be confidential trade secrets, including meetings with OpenAI customers, they said, and OpenAI identified others as containing material protected by attorney-client privilege.

The filing, which opposes Mr. Alfozan’s request to be released from jail before trial, offers the most detailed account yet of what investigators say he recorded. It also comes days after prosecutors told a federal judge that they were “not aware of any” evidence that Mr. Alfozan had committed espionage, stolen trade secrets or acted as an agent of a foreign government.

Prosecutors did not say in Monday’s filing that he had shared the recordings with anyone. “What the defendant did or intended to do with those audio files remains under investigation,” they wrote.

Mr. Alfozan, a Saudi citizen and U.S. permanent resident, has been charged with one count of illegally intercepting conversations and has pleaded not guilty. A hearing on his release is scheduled for Tuesday morning.

His lawyer, David Rizk, argued in a filing last week that the case had turned out to be far less serious than prosecutors initially suggested, describing his client as “an overly curious tinkerer.” Mr. Rizk wrote that the vast majority of recordings on Mr. Alfozan’s computer “apparently contain just random noise and silence.”

Mr. Rizk could not be immediately reached for comment on Monday.

According to prosecutors, the recordings span 15 folders dated Sept. 8 to Sept. 28 and include meetings held on 12 days in an executive conference room. One file was titled “1200-sovereign-bilateral-briefing-sep22.” The filing did not identify the foreign government.

Mr. Alfozan used Codex, an OpenAI A.I. tool, through his wife’s account to help configure the recording device, add voice detection so it would “only record speech,” and move recordings through a Dropbox account, prosecutors said. His wife has not been accused of wrongdoing.

Prosecutors also said he photographed each printed page of a confidential term sheet for a “strategic partnership” between OpenAI and another company in the early hours of Oct. 5. That was the same day a hidden camera recorded him checking behind the television where OpenAI’s security team had found the listening device days earlier.

The filing also described Mr. Alfozan’s contact with Saudi officials. On Oct. 6, a member of the Saudi royal family sent him a link to Echelon, a Riyadh-based A.I. company, and asked: “Time to move back to KSA and join us?”

Mr. Alfozan suggested he might do so “after the IPO,” prosecutors said. The night before his Oct. 9 arrest, he spoke with the Saudi official by WhatsApp for 16 minutes. Prosecutors said he had also exchanged WhatsApp messages with officials at Saudi Arabia’s communications ministry, including the minister in August and September.

Before planning a trip to Saudi Arabia scheduled for Oct. 12, he asked Codex to find “Saudi shipping deals for boxes” and how much it would cost to fly five suitcases to Riyadh, the filing said.

Prosecutors argued that the timing of his Saudi contacts and travel plans “appears to match the timing of his efforts to record OpenAI meetings.” His lawyers have said the trip was planned for paternity leave.

Mr. Alfozan has offered a $1 million bond, secured in part by $500,000 of his own money and backed by friends from college. He is not proposing to use an earlier offer from the Saudi Consulate to pay his bail. Prosecutors said that if he is released, he should be barred from accessing any OpenAI materials, citing concern that he may still have access to the recordings through cloud storage.

A trial is scheduled for January.

(The New York Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to A.I. systems. The two companies have denied those claims.)

title: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges
title_en: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges

inline_images.caption: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges

author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
French and U.S. authorities suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Europe, an incident that reportedly spoiled food and caused equipment failures, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in damage. The attack affected about 700 supermarkets, raising concerns about the exposure of connected refrigeration systems and the potential for cyber operations to disrupt essential commercial infrastructure.

France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot accused Tehran of orchestrating the attack, warning that Iran would face retribution. Speaking Monday at a Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Paris, Barrot described the incident as the first large-scale cyberattack conducted for sabotage on French national territory, calling it a major threat to the country’s interests and the security of its population.

“Following its investigation, France is able to attribute these destructive actions to Iran, carried out by the SHAHID KAVEH cyber offensive unit, affiliated with the electronic and cyber center of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” France’s Foreign Ministry wrote in a Monday statement attributing cyberattacks targeting France to Iran. “This actor poses a persistent threat to our critical infrastructure.”

It added that these destructive cyberattacks are unjustifiable, inexcusable, and violate international law. “They also contravene the principles of the United Nations’ normative framework for responsible state behavior in cyberspace, to which the Islamic Republic of Iran has subscribed.”

The agency highlighted that the Iranian cyber threat against French interests is not new. “Iran has already carried out several destabilizing acts against us, notably targeting the weekly magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and the organization of the Paris Olympic Games in 2024. In March 2026, the European Union adopted sanctions against the Iranian entity Emmenet Pasargad, which had contributed to conducting these cyberattacks.”

During the night of October 11-12, a cyberattack campaign targeted supermarket refrigeration controllers deployed in over 700 major retail locations across France. These cyberattacks caused considerable material damage, fires, and food losses estimated at tens of millions of euros.

The agency recognized that “this is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory.”

The incident highlights the potential consequences of cyberattacks against connected systems outside traditional IT networks, particularly refrigeration infrastructure used to preserve food supplies and maintain supermarket operations. Reported damage ranged from spoiled inventory and equipment failures, underscoring how attacks on OT (operational technology) infrastructure can translate into direct economic losses and disruption to services relied on by the public.

“In accordance with the 2026 national cybersecurity strategy, France is determined to use all available means of response, including within the European Union and alongside its European and international partners, to anticipate, prevent, deter and respond to destabilizing and destructive actions targeting it in cyberspace,” the agency added. “Consequently, France will summon the Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to France to express its strongest condemnation of these cyberattacks.”

Furthermore, France will propose to its European partners the adoption of new sanctions against Iranian entities and individuals involved in this cyberattack against it, as well as in other malicious cyber activities.

Finally, France reserves the right to take any additional measures, public and non-public, deemed necessary and proportionate to respond to these cyberattacks.

In response, Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as ‘baseless and hostile.’

On Tuesday, France summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would be seeking European-level sanctions in response.

The EU said it would seek to provide a “swift and united response” pending discussion with member states.

“As the EU, we have consistently called on all states to refrain from malicious behavior in the cyberspace, and we will continue to address such malicious behavior, making use of all the tools that we have, also under the EU cyber diplomacy toolbox, including sanctions,” spokesman Anouar El Anouni said.

title_zh: 法美指控伊朗网攻欧洲超市冷链系统
summary_zh: 法国外交部长指控伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队旗下SHAHID KAVEH组织针对欧洲700家超市冷链设施实施蓄意破坏攻击
article_content_zh:
法国和美国当局怀疑伊朗是针对欧洲各地超市冰箱和冰柜的网络攻击的幕后黑手，据报道，该事件导致食品变质并导致设备故障，造成数千万美元的损失。此次攻击影响了约 700 家超市，引发了人们对互联制冷系统暴露以及网络操作可能破坏重要商业基础设施的担忧。

法国外交部长让-诺埃尔·巴罗指责德黑兰策划了这次袭击，并警告伊朗将面临报复。巴罗周一在巴黎举行的七国集团 (G7) 会议上发表讲话，称该事件是法国领土上首次大规模破坏性网络攻击，称其对法国利益和人民安全构成重大威胁。

法国外交部在周一的一份声明中写道，“经过调查，法国能够将这些破坏性行为归咎于伊朗，这些行为是由隶属于伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队电子和网络中心的 SHAHID KAVEH 网络攻击部队实施的”，并将针对法国的网络攻击归咎于伊朗。 “该行为者对我们的关键基础设施构成持续威胁。”

它补充说，这些破坏性网络攻击是不合理、不可原谅的，并且违反了国际法。 “它们还违反了伊朗伊斯兰共和国签署的联合国网络空间负责任国家行为规范框架的原则。”

该机构强调，伊朗针对法国利益的网络威胁并不新鲜。 “伊朗已经对我们实施了几起破坏稳定的行为，特别是针对 2023 年《查理周刊》周刊和 2024 年巴黎奥运会的组织。2026 年 3 月，欧盟对伊朗实体 Emmenet Pasargad 实施了制裁，该实体参与了这些网络攻击。”

10 月 11 日至 12 日夜间，一场网络攻击活动针对部署在法国 700 多个主要零售点的超市制冷控制器。这些网络攻击造成了相当大的物质损失、火灾和粮食损失，估计价值数千万欧元。

该机构承认，“就其规模和攻击性而言，这是一场前所未有的活动，因此构成了首次纯粹以在国家领土上进行破坏为目的的网络攻击活动。”

该事件突显了针对传统 IT 网络之外的互联系统的网络攻击的潜在后果，特别是用于保存食品供应和维持超市运营的制冷基础设施。报告的损害包括库存损坏和设备故障，这凸显了对 OT（运营技术）基础设施的攻击如何转化为直接经济损失和公众所依赖的服务中断。

该机构补充说：“根据2026年国家网络安全战略，法国决心使用一切可用的应对手段，包括在欧盟内部以及与欧洲和国际合作伙伴一起，预测、预防、威慑和应对网络空间中针对法国的破坏稳定和破坏性行动。” “因此，法国将召见伊朗伊斯兰共和国驻法国大使，对这些网络攻击表示最强烈的谴责。”

此外，法国将向其欧洲伙伴提议对参与此次网络攻击以及其他恶意网络活动的伊朗实体和个人实施新的制裁。

最后，法国保留采取任何认为必要且适当的额外措施（公开和非公开）的权利，以应对这些网络攻击。

作为回应，伊朗称法国指控伊朗是导致超市冰箱和冰柜温度升高的网络攻击的幕后黑手，“毫无根据且充满敌意”。

周二，法国召见伊朗大使，并表示将寻求欧洲层面的制裁作为回应。

欧盟表示，在与成员国讨论之前，它将寻求提供“迅速和统一的反应”。

title: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges
title_en: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges

inline_images.caption: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges (Source: Wall Street Journal)

author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
French and U.S. authorities suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Europe, an incident that reportedly spoiled food and caused equipment failures, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in damage. The attack affected about 700 supermarkets, raising concerns about the exposure of connected refrigeration systems and the potential for cyber operations to disrupt essential commercial infrastructure.

France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot accused Tehran of orchestrating the attack, warning that Iran would face retribution. Speaking Monday at a Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Paris, Barrot described the incident as the first large-scale cyberattack conducted for sabotage on French national territory, calling it a major threat to the country’s interests and the security of its population.

“Following its investigation, France is able to attribute these destructive actions to Iran, carried out by the SHAHID KAVEH cyber offensive unit, affiliated with the electronic and cyber center of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” France’s Foreign Ministry wrote in a Monday statement attributing cyberattacks targeting France to Iran. “This actor poses a persistent threat to our critical infrastructure.”

It added that these destructive cyberattacks are unjustifiable, inexcusable, and violate international law. “They also contravene the principles of the United Nations’ normative framework for responsible state behavior in cyberspace, to which the Islamic Republic of Iran has subscribed.”

The agency highlighted that the Iranian cyber threat against French interests is not new. “Iran has already carried out several destabilizing acts against us, notably targeting the weekly magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and the organization of the Paris Olympic Games in 2024. In March 2026, the European Union adopted sanctions against the Iranian entity Emmenet Pasargad, which had contributed to conducting these cyberattacks.”

During the night of October 11-12, a cyberattack campaign targeted supermarket refrigeration controllers deployed in over 700 major retail locations across France. These cyberattacks caused considerable material damage, fires, and food losses estimated at tens of millions of euros.

The agency recognized that “this is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory.”

The incident highlights the potential consequences of cyberattacks against connected systems outside traditional IT networks, particularly refrigeration infrastructure used to preserve food supplies and maintain supermarket operations. Reported damage ranged from spoiled inventory and equipment failures, underscoring how attacks on OT (operational technology) infrastructure can translate into direct economic losses and disruption to services relied on by the public.

“In accordance with the 2026 national cybersecurity strategy, France is determined to use all available means of response, including within the European Union and alongside its European and international partners, to anticipate, prevent, deter and respond to destabilizing and destructive actions targeting it in cyberspace,” the agency added. “Consequently, France will summon the Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to France to express its strongest condemnation of these cyberattacks.”

Furthermore, France will propose to its European partners the adoption of new sanctions against Iranian entities and individuals involved in this cyberattack against it, as well as in other malicious cyber activities.

Finally, France reserves the right to take any additional measures, public and non-public, deemed necessary and proportionate to respond to these cyberattacks.

In response, Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as ‘baseless and hostile.’

On Tuesday, France summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would be seeking European-level sanctions in response.

The EU said it would seek to provide a “swift and united response” pending discussion with member states.

“As the EU, we have consistently called on all states to refrain from malicious behavior in the cyberspace, and we will continue to address such malicious behavior, making use of all the tools that we have, also under the EU cyber diplomacy toolbox, including sanctions,” spokesman Anouar El Anouni said.

title: How Intentful uses dots to make more time for growth
title_en: How Intentful uses dots to make more time for growth
author: OpenAI
article_content:
How a small business founder’s dot helps her with research and proposals, while alerting her to critical messages and resolving issues.

Marina Petrova is CEO and cofounder of Intentful, a lean team that helps brands make their marketing interactive, with products such as ads that answer customers’ questions in real time and tools that make website information readable by AI. The company also advises and trains marketers on using AI.

In travel and tourism, Intentful works with destination organizations and local businesses such as hotels, restaurants, and attractions. A custom proposal is part of how Marina wins their business, showing prospects what’s possible and what it would take to deliver.

To keep Intentful growing, she needed more room for that strategic work, but she was spending too much time on research, hunting for files, and formatting decks. Her dot changed all that, taking on tasks and meeting Marina’s needs before she even had to ask.

“My dot makes me feel like I gained a new superpower.”

### From 300 websites to a proposal in hours instead of days

For one of Intentful’s tourism clients, Marina wanted to propose a package of Intentful’s AI services for hundreds of local businesses in the destination. Before she could price the package, she needed to work out which businesses’ websites the package could cover and what Intentful had charged other clients for similar work.

She brought in her dot, which she named Aria, to help her get from research to a proposal she could put her name on in a few hours instead of several days. First, Marina gave Aria a spreadsheet of URLs and criteria for deciding which sites to include. For example, a site needed a readable sitemap listing no more than 3,000 pages.

“My dot looked through about 300 website sitemaps, helped me figure out which sites to include in a new offer for local businesses, and pulled pricing from past agreements.”

Next, Aria helped Marina research pricing. Through ChatGPT plugins, Aria reviewed Intentful’s sales data, including past engagements and discussions in HubSpot. It surfaced pricing from earlier agreements and context from Intentful’s plans for the following year.

Using that data, Marina and Aria then built a pricing model: page counts determined the pricing tier, and previous customer agreements also informed the price. “We worked through a custom pricing model together, and then Aria turned it into a one-page proposal I reviewed and edited,” said Marina.

When drafting proposals, Aria knows to use Intentful’s templates from Google Drive. Marina can also point Aria to an earlier proposal as a reference, so the draft follows Intentful’s style from the start. “I need to say what needs to be in a proposal, but I don’t need to spend an hour figuring out its layout. My dot handles that,” Marina says.

Aria can also spot things Marina hadn’t thought to check. When Marina asked Aria to reuse pricing from an earlier proposal, it noticed that the original renewal date didn’t match the timing she remembered. Aria flagged the discrepancy and left the date out of the new draft.

### Staying ahead of messages, tasks, and team updates

Marina uses the Gmail and Slack plugins in ChatGPT to catch up on conversations, find open tasks, and see where the team needs her. Aria checks for messages that need Marina’s attention. While Marina was offline, Aria spotted a reply she had been waiting for and let her know it included an invitation for a call that morning.

Marina also uses Aria to talk through ideas, find conversations, check an account’s history in the CRM, or open and assign tasks in Asana. She often briefs Aria by phone while she travels.

“On a long drive, I call my dot and talk through what needs to get done. We chat through updates for client proposals, and my dot already knows the structure, the formatting, and what needs to be done.”

Marina loves that her dot works in the tools she already uses. When Aria writes a draft, Marina can leave comments in Google Docs exactly where she wants changes. On longer documents, she asks Aria to use suggesting mode so she can see what changed.

Aria also keeps up with changes in shared work without being asked. For a conference presentation, Marina created the deck and a colleague added two slides. “Aria noticed the new slides, updated the speaker notes without being asked, and let me know,” Marina says.

Marina chooses which information Aria can access and always reviews outgoing email. She can keep work moving without handing over the final call.

### Using dots to teach others about AI

When Marina prepared an AI 101 session on agents, she used Aria to help build the lesson. The process was itself an example of what she wanted attendees to learn: delegate a real task, give the agent enough context, challenge the result, and stay in control of what goes out.

Aria’s support continued even after the class. After a flight, Marina saw a participant’s request for access to a training file. When she checked with Aria, it had already shared the file. And after a session for 50 marketers, Aria noticed that a software glitch was preventing participants from opening the recording. It flagged the access issue and offered to fix it before the link was shared.

“With my dot, I can focus on strategic things. I can focus on ideas and growth.”

Marina Petrova 是 Intentful 的首席执行官兼联合创始人，Intentful 是一个精益团队，帮助品牌实现互动营销，提供实时回答客户问题的广告等产品，以及让人工智能可读网站信息的工具。该公司还为营销人员提供有关人工智能使用的建议和培训。

为了保持 Intentful 的发展，她需要更多的空间来进行战略工作，但她在研究、寻找文件和格式化卡片组上花费了太多时间。她的点改变了这一切，在玛丽娜提出要求之前就承担起任务并满足她的需求。

“我的点让我感觉自己获得了新的超能力。”

### 从 300 个网站到提案只需几小时而不是几天

对于 Intentful 的一位旅游客户，Marina 希望为该目的地的数百家当地企业提供一套 Intentful 的人工智能服务。在为套餐定价之前，她需要弄清楚该套餐可以覆盖哪些企业网站，以及 Intentful 向其他客户收取的类似工作费用是多少。

她带来了自己的点，她将其命名为 Aria，以帮助她从研究到提出提案，她可以在几个小时而不是几天内将自己的名字命名。首先，Marina 向 Aria 提供了一份包含 URL 的电子表格以及用于决定包含哪些网站的标准。例如，一个站点需要一个可读的站点地图，列出不超过 3,000 个页面。

接下来，Aria 帮助 Marina 研究定价。通过 ChatGPT 插件，Aria 审查了 Intentful 的销售数据，包括 HubSpot 中过去的参与和讨论。它显示了早期协议的定价和 Intentful 下一年计划的背景。

然后，Marina 和 Aria 使用这些数据构建了一个定价模型：页数决定了定价等级，之前的客户协议也决定了价格。 “我们一起制定了定制定价模型，然后 Aria 将其变成了我审阅和编辑的一页提案，”Marina 说。

title: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
title_en: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
author: OpenAI
article_content:

The Remote Agents Platform turned engineering tasks into API calls: teams delegate the work, execution takes place in a remote sandbox, and the result comes back as a merge request. In the internal security platform, the number of vulnerabilities fixed more than doubled.

### The challenge isn’t the task—it’s the scale

iFood maintains more than 15,000 code repositories. Each periodically needs specific tasks performed: validating code to ensure it meets internal standards, fixing vulnerable dependencies, or running an analysis.

None of these tasks is difficult on its own. The challenge comes when those tasks multiply.

“Solving this for one repository is easy. The challenge is solving it at scale,” says Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer at iFood. “The Remote Agents Platform is designed to make it possible to solve this at scale across all 15,000 repositories.”

Before the platform, each team tackled the problem in its own way—and they all ran into the same obstacle.

“Before, we had fragmented solutions. Imagine several teams at iFood trying to solve different problems, but without this layer, this agentic runtime, available to them. In the end, those solutions always ran into the same problem.”

What was missing wasn’t intelligence or a use case. It was execution infrastructure. A dedicated runtime.

“Teams can focus on solving their business problems and delegate execution to our platform.”

### A coding agent in the cloud, accessible through an API

The team describes the Remote Agents Platform as an API that launches a remote agentic coding task. The cycle has three steps: the user submits a prompt and environment requirements through a REST call; the platform processes the task on a dedicated remote runner inside an isolated sandbox; and the result is retrieved later.

“The platform’s entry point, its interface, is a simple REST API. Users can use this API to create the runs they need. Internally, we handle and manage the entire lifecycle and delegate execution to isolated sandboxes,” he explains. Task progress can be monitored in real time.

The runner’s internal design alternates between two different types of steps—and that combination makes the overall workflow predictable.

Deterministic steps bookend the workflow: cloning the repository, importing the skills the agent can use, and setting up the working branch at the start; publishing the merge request and making the generated artifacts available at the end. In between is the agentic execution itself, running GPT‑5.6 Luna inside the sandbox.

“It’s a combination of those two things: deterministic steps and agentic execution within the workflow.”

The sandbox runs Ubuntu and includes the toolchains iFood’s ecosystem requires—Python, Java, Kotlin, C#, TypeScript, Rust, JavaScript, and Go—along with general-purpose tools. Beyond the sandbox, the agent can access Nexus, GitLab, Docker, Snyk, Kubernetes, and AWS.

### Why GPT‑5.6 Luna

The model choice came down to three factors considered together, rather than just one.

“We chose GPT‑5.6 Luna because, among models at the same checkpoint, the benchmarks showed it offered a great balance of intelligence, efficiency, and execution speed—how quickly it could complete tasks. Those three qualities together led us to choose GPT‑5.6 Luna.”

That balance matters more for a platform built to scale than it would for a one-off use case. With tens of thousands of tokens being consumed, the average cost of four U.S. cents per run stops being a minor detail and becomes an architectural consideration.

“Given our plans to scale the platform across many use cases at iFood, the balance of efficiency and intelligence that OpenAI’s model provides ensures we can scale sustainably.”

### How to tell whether the agent completed the task

Delegating execution at scale creates a new challenge: automatically determining whether the agent did what it was supposed to do.

iFood’s answer comes in the step after the session. Once execution is complete, the result is processed using OpenAI’s Structured Outputs, which requires the output to conform to a predefined contract.

“We process the result using Structured Outputs, which ensures the response follows a predefined contract. From the agent’s session, we can identify the outputs within the response structure we expect. This helps reduce uncertainty and ensures we can always get a response from the agent’s session, whether positive or negative.”

### The first major user: security

The platform already powers an internal iFood security product that scans the 15,000 repositories for vulnerable dependencies and attempts to fix them.

The migration had a direct impact: “With our platform, the accuracy of those changes, those fixes, more than doubled,” says Coelho.

This use case illustrates the idea behind the platform: the security team didn’t need to build its own agentic runtime or become experts in agent orchestration. It needed to call an API.

### Asynchronous execution gives developers their time back

The team emphasizes what asynchronous execution frees developers to do, rather than replacement.

Because the task is delegated and runs without supervision, the developer doesn’t have to stay focused on monitoring it.

“While they’re in a meeting, they can launch a code fix, a performance analysis, or another task that’s a little more routine—something they can delegate without having to monitor it at that moment.”

Routine work no longer competes for the team’s attention. That leaves time for problems that require judgment.

“You can unlock those productivity gains without necessarily having to monitor the work as it happens.”

### Modeled on the APIs that inspired it

The Remote Agents Platform was designed as an internal layer with similarities to the way OpenAI makes this type of task available to external customers.

“The Remote Agents Platform drew a lot of inspiration from OpenAI’s APIs, both the Batch API and the Agents API, which is an even more recent OpenAI product. We built a platform that resembles those products, but is internal to iFood.”

The inspiration went beyond the concept. It extends to the design of the interfaces, the organization of resources, and the approach to asynchronous execution with results retrieved later.

“These products directly inspired how we built our solution.”

### Results at a glance

The platform has completed more than 25,000 tasks, consuming more than 27 billion tokens, at an average cost of US$0.04 per run.

After migrating to the Remote Agents Platform, the internal security platform more than doubled both the accuracy of its fixes and the number of vulnerabilities resolved.

Coverage extends across iFood’s more than 15,000 code repositories.

All runs use GPT‑5.6 Luna, chosen for its balance of intelligence, efficiency, and speed.

Structured Outputs ensures that each session returns a result that follows a predefined contract, whether positive or negative.

Product teams have moved from building fragmented solutions to delegating agentic execution through a REST API.

### Lessons for leaders

The bottleneck is often the runtime, not the use case. Several teams already knew what they wanted to automate; they lacked an environment in which to run it.

Combine deterministic steps with agentic execution. Cloning, publishing, and making artifacts available don’t require a model; the complex task in between does.

Treat cost per run as an architectural decision. At scale, the cost per task determines what is feasible to automate.

Require outputs to follow a contract. Without a structured response, there’s no way to know at scale whether the agent achieved its objective.

Asynchronous execution is the real productivity gain. The value lies in not having to monitor the work, rather than completing it faster while watching over it.

### Tips

Expose agentic capabilities through an internal API so other teams can use them without rebuilding the infrastructure.

Isolate each run in its own sandbox, with your ecosystem’s toolchains already installed.

Choose a model by considering intelligence, cost, and speed together, rather than a single benchmark.

Use structured outputs to classify success and failure automatically.

Start with an internal user with a clear pain point and high volume—at iFood, that was the security platform.

### Next steps

The team plans to bring the platform to many more use cases across iFood, expanding the range of internal products that delegate agentic execution to it—with cost per task determining whether that expansion can be sustained.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该案例验证了AI软件工程的核心趋势：从个人编码辅助向系统级运行时（Runtime）架构演进。对于拥有海量代码库的企业而言，能够通过API进行标准化治理的闭环编排系统，比单纯的LLM模型能力更能直接转化为生产环境的合规性与安全性提升。

iFood 的代码存储库

平台完成的运行

每次运行的平均推理成本

通过安全平台修复了尽可能多的漏洞

远程代理平台将工程任务转化为 API 调用：团队委派工作，在远程沙箱中执行，结果作为合并请求返回。在内部安全平台中，修复的漏洞数量增加了一倍多。

### 挑战不是任务，而是规模

iFood 维护着超过 15,000 个代码存储库。每个任务都需要定期执行特定任务：验证代码以确保其符合内部标准、修复易受攻击的依赖项或运行分析。

这些任务本身并不困难。当这些任务成倍增加时，挑战就来了。

“解决一个存储库的这个问题很容易。挑战在于大规模解决它，”iFood 高级软件工程师 Victor Coelho 说。 “远程代理平台旨在使跨所有 15,000 个存储库大规模解决此问题成为可能。”

在平台出现之前，每个团队都以自己的方式解决问题，但他们都遇到了同样的障碍。

“以前，我们有支离破碎的解决方案。想象一下 iFood 的多个团队试图解决不同的问题，但没有可用的这一层、代理运行时。最终，这些解决方案总是遇到相同的问题。”

缺少的不是情报或用例。这是执行基础设施。专用运行时。

“团队可以专注于解决他们的业务问题并将执行委托给我们的平台。”

title: Clay helps sales teams win with Codex and ChatGPT
title_en: Clay helps sales teams win with Codex and ChatGPT
author: OpenAI
article_content:
ChatGPT and Codex integrations help Clay users research deals and turn data into go-to-market plays, and GPT‑6 models handle the reasoning.

Even when sales teams have plenty of data about a prospect, they can still struggle to understand what matters most and develop a winning pitch. Clay is a self-learning revenue engine designed to help. Using GPT‑6 Astra, GPT‑6 Sol, and other models, Clay enables users to build lists of companies and people, enrich those records using agents, and use that information in go-to-market plays.

Clay also brings these capabilities to where customers are already working with plugins for Codex and ChatGPT, making it easier to create and run go-to-market workflows and research accounts and deals.

“Clay in ChatGPT gives sales reps a way to understand more about the customers they’re trying to sell to. It brings all of that rich context to the places they’re already working.”

### Giving sales reps more context to act on

Clay’s Codex integration lets builders create and run go-to-market plays in Codex, while giving sales reps access to data they can use to research an account or understand a deal they’re trying to close.

Jeff has seen reps combine information from their own systems and public datasets to determine how to best communicate their product’s value to a customer. “Customers love using Codex for a lot of different tasks in sales,” he says. “We’ve seen the best sales reps be the most empowered by this.”

Clay’s ChatGPT plugin brings the same customer data into another tool reps already use, helping them learn more about prospects without leaving ChatGPT. Jeff says, “It’s been a big success.”

### Matching intelligence and cost to the task

OpenAI models power Claygent’s research, qualification, enrichment, and signal detection, as well as the agent that helps users build workflows and coordinate other Clay agents.

Clay uses GPT‑6 Sol as its primary model, with GPT‑6 Astra for harder tasks and GPT‑6 Luna for cost-sensitive work. That range supports background research and copywriting as well as agents that users work with directly.

“GPT-6 Sol is a really great model for go-to-market plays. It has really good intuition and can build long-horizon, outcome-based go-to-market tasks.”

The Responses API lets Clay use different levels of intelligence and cost through the same interface. “Having the same Responses API across the different price points is something that’s super appealing to us with OpenAI models,” said Jeff.

### Building end-to-end plays that self-improve over time

GPT‑6 Astra also helps Jeff build and test software. He used to spend much of his time manually checking features he had built; now he can ask GPT‑6 Astra to handle more of that work.

He explains, “GPT‑6 Astra really changed how I build software because it fully closed the loop on the engineering process. Now I can have Astra write code, add tests, and then actually run the tests and test the feature and record that and upload that in the PR. It simplifies my life a lot.”

For Clay’s customers, Jeff sees GPT‑Live‑1 as a way to use Clay and Codex by voice and help prospects learn about a product. Clay is working on inbound sales development features that would let an agent show a product or service to a prospect. He also sees the Decisions API as another way to integrate models into Clay and open up new use cases.

Clay’s ambition is to carry go-to-market workflows from start to finish, with agents that improve as they learn from the results. For Jeff, the goal is to empower builders “to bring the same shift that happened in software engineering to go-to-market.”

article_content_zh:
ChatGPT 和 Codex 集成可帮助 Clay 用户研究交易并将数据转化为进入市场的策略，而 GPT-6 模型则负责推理。

即使销售团队拥有大量有关潜在客户的数据，他们仍然很难理解什么是最重要的，也很难制定出获胜的方案。 Clay 是一个自学收入引擎，旨在提供帮助。使用 GPT-6 Astra、GPT-6 Sol 和其他模型，Clay 使用户能够构建公司和人员列表，使用代理丰富这些记录，并在市场推广中使用该信息。

Clay 还将这些功能引入客户已经使用 Codex 和 ChatGPT 插件的地方，从而更轻松地创建和运行上市工作流程以及研究帐户和交易。

“ChatGPT 中的 Clay 为销售代表提供了一种方式来更多地了解他们想要销售的客户。它将所有丰富的背景带到他们已经工作的地方。”

### 为销售代表提供更多行动背景

Clay 的 Codex 集成允许构建者在 Codex 中创建和运行进入市场的策略，同时让销售代表能够访问数据，他们可以使用这些数据来研究客户或了解他们试图完成的交易。

杰夫看到销售代表将来自自己的系统和公共数据集的信息结合起来，以确定如何最好地向客户传达其产品的价值。 “客户喜欢使用 Codex 来完成许多不同的销售任务，”他说。 “我们已经看到最好的销售代表最能从中获得权力。”

Clay 的 ChatGPT 插件将相同的客户数据带入销售代表已经使用的另一个工具中，帮助他们在不离开 ChatGPT 的情况下了解更多关于潜在客户的信息。杰夫说：“这是一次巨大的成功。”

### 将情报和成本与任务相匹配

OpenAI 模型为 Claygent 的研究、鉴定、丰富和信号检测以及帮助用户构建工作流程和协调其他 Clay 代理的代理提供支持。

Clay 使用 GPT-6 Sol 作为其主要模型，GPT-6 Astra 适合较困难的任务，GPT-6 Luna 适合成本敏感的工作。该范围支持背景研究和文案写作以及用户直接合作的代理。

“GPT-6 Sol 是一个非常适合上市的模型。它具有非常好的直觉，可以构建长期的、基于结果的上市任务。”

Responses API 让 Clay 通过同一接口使用不同级别的智能和成本。 “对于 OpenAI 模型来说，在不同价位上拥有相同的 Responses API 对我们来说非常有吸引力，”Jeff 说。

### 构建随着时间的推移不断自我完善的端到端游戏

title: HPE Gives Outlook That Falls Short of Optimistic Estimates
title_en: HPE Gives Outlook That Falls Short of Optimistic Estimates
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue climbed 50% year-over-year to $14.5 billion, topping Wall Street estimates of $14.3 billion.HPE projected Q1 revenue outlook between $14 billion to $14.6 billion, marginally lower than the highest Wall Street estimates of $14.7 billion.The cloud infrastructure firm lifted its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to as high as $63.1 billion.Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (HPE) reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and profit that surpassed Wall Street expectations on Monday, however, its share price slipped after-hours as its Q1 FY27 outlook fell short of the rosiest of Wall Street expectations.For the quarter ended October 31, the Houston-based technology company posted revenue of $14.5 billion, up 50% from the same period a year earlier and ahead of the $14.3 billion average forecast from analysts polled by Fiscal.ai.

The cloud infrastructure firm reported earnings of $1.43 per share, beating the consensus projection of $1.28 a share. “We are now a fundamentally different company, with greater earnings power, a stronger competitive position, and a portfolio built to capitalize on the next phase of AI,” said Antonio Neri, president and CEO of HPE.

AI Servers And Juniper Integration Drive GrowthHPE’s rapid expansion was anchored by its Cloud & AI division, where quarterly revenue jumped 68.6% year-over-year to $11.3 billion and operating margins nearly doubled to 18.4% from 9.3%. Within that unit, server revenue soared 94.7% to $8.8 billion on the back of demand for systems powered by Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD) processors, while storage revenue rose 33.8% to $1.5 billion.

The company’s networking segment, bolstered by its integration of Juniper Networks, generated $3.1 billion in revenue, representing a 12.3% increase over the prior year with an operating profit margin of 22.1%. HPE Fiscal 2027 Earnings GuidanceHPE now projects fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 27% to 35% with revenues reaching as high as $63.1 billion, beating analyst expectations of $55.05 billion.

Full-year adjusted earnings are projected to reach up to $5.35 per share.For the current fiscal first quarter ending in January, HPE forecast revenue between $14 billion and $14.6 billion. While the bottom-line guidance comfortably exceeded Wall Street’s average estimate of $1.08 per share, the top-line range fell just shy of the most bullish analyst projections of $14.7 billion, tempering investor enthusiasm.HPE Stock: Retail View Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘extremely bullish’ with ‘extremely high’ message volumes.

第四财季收入同比增长 50%，达到 145 亿美元，超过华尔街预期的 143 亿美元。HPE 预计第一季度收入前景在 140 亿美元至 146 亿美元之间，略低于华尔街最高预期 147 亿美元。这家云基础设施公司将 2027 财年收入预期上调至高达 631 亿美元。惠普企业公司 (HPE) 公布了财报周一第四季度营收和利润超出华尔街预期，但由于其 2027 财年第一季度前景未达到华尔街最乐观的预期，该公司股价在盘后下跌。截至 10 月 31 日的季度，这家总部位于休斯顿的科技公司公布的营收为 145 亿美元，较去年同期增长 50%，高于 Fiscal.ai 调查的分析师平均预测的 143 亿美元。

这家云基础设施公司公布的每股收益为 1.43 美元，超出了每股 1.28 美元的普遍预测。 HPE 总裁兼首席执行官 Antonio Neri 表示：“我们现在是一家截然不同的公司，拥有更强的盈利能力、更强的竞争地位，以及为利用人工智能下一阶段而构建的投资组合。”

AI 服务器和瞻博网络集成推动增长HPE 的快速扩张得益于其云和 AI 部门，该部门的季度收入同比增长 68.6% 至 113 亿美元，营业利润率几乎翻倍，从 9.3% 升至 18.4%。在该部门中，由于对 Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) 和 Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) 处理器支持的系统的需求增长，服务器收入飙升 94.7% 至 88 亿美元，而存储收入增长 33.8% 至 15 亿美元。

该公司的网络部门在与瞻博网络整合的推动下，创造了 31 亿美元的收入，比上年增长 12.3%，营业利润率为 22.1%。 HPE 2027 财年盈利指引HPE 目前预计 2027 财年收入增长 27% 至 35%，收入高达 631 亿美元，超出分析师预期的 550.5 亿美元。

全年调整后收益预计将达到每股 5.35 美元。对于截至 1 月份的当前第一财季，HPE 预计收入在 140 亿美元至 146 亿美元之间。虽然盈利指引轻松超过了华尔街每股 1.08 美元的平均预期，但盈利区间仅略低于分析师最乐观的 147 亿美元预测，从而削弱了投资者的热情。 HPE 股票：零售观点 Stocktwits 上的零售情绪“极其乐观”，消息量“极高”。

Revenue will be $1.29 billion to $1.3 billion in the period ending in January, Zoom said Monday in a statement. Analysts, on average, estimated $1.3 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Zoom's forecast projects sales growth of about 4% after the company reported sales gained 4.9% in the period that ended Oct. 31.

Known for its videoconferencing tool, Zoom has added more office collaboration products, such as corporate phone systems and software for contact centers. Many of these offerings include artificial intelligence features, which can be expensive to provide because they rely on models from firms like Anthropic PBC.

The shares were little changed in extended trading after closing at $86.03 in New York. While Zoom's stock has dipped less than 1% this year, it has been volatile — falling as low as $72.72 in March while rising as high as $111.88 in early June.

For the fiscal third quarter, sales climbed to $1.29 billion. That topped analysts' average estimate of $1.28 billion. Profit, excluding some items, was $1.59 a share, compared with analysts' average estimate of $1.49.

Enterprise revenue increased 8.6% to $805.4 million. Zoom said it had 4,732 customers contributing more than $100,000 each in trailing-12-month revenue.

Investing.com——据彭博社报道，欧盟和加拿大正准备制定一个广泛的战略联盟，旨在深化经济、国防和贸易关系。这一努力反映出中等强国有意推动对抗以美国和中国为首的大国政治日益增长的主导地位。

欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩定于 9 月 16 日在斯特拉斯堡举行的年度国情咨文演讲中宣布这一倡议。加拿大总理马克·卡尼将出席演讲，预计第二天将向欧洲立法者发表讲话，强调渥太华致力于在正式加入欧盟的情况下实现更紧密的一体化。

即将出台的框架旨在扩大关键供应链、原材料、太空探索和科学研究方面的合作。谈判的重点还在于加强联合防御能力，渥太华去年成为第一个参与欧盟1500亿欧元（1740亿美元）国防采购基金的非欧盟国家。

这一外交推动是在卡尼总理早些时候发出警告之后做出的，他在世界经济论坛上宣称，基于规则的传统国际秩序实际上已经破裂。在此背景下，两个司法管辖区都在寻求结构性平衡措施，以应对单边经济压力策略和日益加剧的全球贸易摩擦。

该联盟建立在现有的双边贸易协定和安全伙伴关系的基础上，官员们探讨加拿大如何在法律上与欧盟单一市场保持一致。虽然有关必要的监管或法律机制的讨论仍在进行中，但双方计划在今年 10 月于加拿大举行的联合峰会上正式确定下一步措施。

title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
title_en: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
author: Lauren Feiner and Hayden Field
article_content:
After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”

“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.

It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.

“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.

Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.

Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.

News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.

Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”

But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.

The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.

The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.

The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.

Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts.

If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump said that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy.

Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the new Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible, and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.

“The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement. “Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk.” Rep. Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said, “A real Congress will find out” whether Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had any alternative incentives for their role in Nvidia’s dealings. Sen. Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Intelligence Committee, called Trump’s intervention to bring back Huang “outrageous.” Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX), a member of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs Committees, which are interviewing Huang next week, said he wants to know how Trump stands to benefit from “personally champion[ing] Huang’s return.”

At closed-door hearings next week, Democrats say they intend to press Huang and the administration further, and several accused the administration of corruption. “We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO and why his administration failed to restrict the PRC’s access to our most sensitive technology,” Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement to The Verge. The board’s decision is “outrageous,” said Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a member of the House Select Committee on China. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Krishnamoorthi said in a statement, calling for Huang to testify publicly. “Reinstatement is no substitute for accountability,” Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL), another China Committee member, said in a statement.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta also intends to continue an investigation into the company. “The reinstatement of Jensen Huang does not change the fact that the American people deserve to know what happened here — whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” California Department of Justice spokesperson Elissa Perez said in a statement.

Last week, before Huang was reinstated, at least two Republican China hawks opposed the idea. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), a rumored potential presidential candidate, told reporters that he would not like to see Huang return to the top post, but would “defer to the board how they want to run their company. If it were me and a guy who just was caught up in a Chinese honeytrap — I think is the technical term for it — I don’t think that I would impose massive security concerns, not just for the company, but for American national security.”

While it was up to the board to decide whether to bring Huang back, Hawley said, “We in Congress ought to be concerned about the American national security implications and I think we should be looking into that.”

House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) said on stage last week at the Aspen Cyber Summit in Washington, D.C., that Huang “has a serious credibility problem, and I don’t believe he would be as effective now as he was before.” His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment after Huang’s reinstatement.

Sitting beside Moolenaar on stage last week, Rep. Greg Stanton (D-AZ) gave his advice to the board: “Don’t do it. Don’t bring it back. And at the very least, slow your roll, because there are so many questions that have to be answered. What else is out there that Jensen Huang has done to put US national security at risk?” Stanton warned that Congress is just beginning to probe what happened here. “There are going to be very serious investigations with very serious ramifications if in fact it is as it seems,” he said. “The company needs to know this ain’t going away for a while. This is a very serious issue.” After news of Huang’s return, Stanton doubled down on calls for investigations.

Other Republicans — some of whom are leaving Congress — notably disagreed with Trump’s jubilance for Huang’s return. “It’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO,” retiring Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) told CNBC. “To me it’s a failure of character.” Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE) wrote on X that Huang’s “behavior does not support reinstatement,” and said he must still testify before Congress. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips,” he wrote. Senate Intelligence Committee Chair Tom Cotton (R-AR) wrote on X that he’s not done investigating. “The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back,” he said. “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other.”

Market analysts have been watching and waiting for a Huang comeback since reports that he had assembled a “war room” of allies to help with his possible reinstatement. Not only did Huang cofound one of the world’s most valuable companies and arguably the most important one in the AI boom, but he has personally helped secure hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure funding from US financial institutions. Demand for Nvidia chips constantly outpaces supply, and Huang has had the president’s ear for months. Despite all that, though, Huang’s clout seemed like it wouldn’t help him up until the past 24 hours.

Lindsey Stewart, director of institutional insights at Morningstar, wrote in a note that although investors may consider this a “good move given his history of value creation at the company,” questions remain about the best way to provide corporate governance and oversight at such an important company.

Jacob Bourne, an eMarketer analyst specializing in ad tech and consumer technologies, said in a statement to The Verge that it was difficult to gauge “how much protection Trump’s assurances will ultimately provide Nvidia.” And Heather West, head of Eurasia Group’s geo-technology practice, highlighted the fact that Trump recently met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. The timing offers Democrats and China hawks “a great deal to work with in 2027 as they begin scrutiny into the administration, potential corruption, and large tech companies[‘] actions here,” said West.

Analysts at Yorkville Ives wrote in a note Monday that they consider Nvidia a $300 stock with Huang and a $225 stock without him, due to his hard-to-replace influence in the sector. They said an interim structure “could not replicate” his supply relationships with TSMC and others, as well as his place in AI industry dealmaking.

“This is a board that reversed itself because the alternative, a founder-less Nvidia at the start of the Rubin cycle with a CEO search running into next year, was the bigger risk to shareholders, and it chose to pair the reversal with the governance architecture investors will want to see around him,” the Yorkville Ives analysts wrote.

Even Trump admits, though, that a true comeback story can’t be called in a single day. “I’ve seen some pretty good comebacks but I’ll tell you, what you have to have for a comeback, really, is longevity,” he told CNBC. He described the pep talk he gave Huang the night before. “I said, ‘You’ve got to promise me one thing. You’ve got the brain, you’ve got everything going, you’ve got to work hard. And if you work hard nobody can beat you.’”

According to Trump, Huang told him, “I’m going to work harder than I’ve ever worked.”

article_content_zh:
有报道称黄仁勋与一名所谓的中国间谍有染，英伟达董事会接受黄仁勋辞去首席执行官职务后，唐纳德·特朗普总统似乎也接受了新的现实。消息传出后不久，特朗普在斯蒂芬·A·史密斯的广播节目中表示，黄仁勋“最终会站起来”。

特朗普表示：“你知道这句话，任何人都可以被取代。”他将苹果前首席执行官蒂姆·库克列为潜在的首席执行官候选人。

没过多久，特朗普就开始软化他的态度，明确表示他欢迎黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官，即使英伟达自己的董事会还没有准备好这样做。在幕后，特朗普政府正在努力为黄的回归做好准备。很快，英伟达董事会就改变了态度：在坚持同意关闭黄仁勋回归的大门不到一周后，他们一致投票决定恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官、总裁和董事会董事职务。

“卷土重来并没有什么问题，”特朗普在接受 CNBC 的电话庆祝时说道。

随后，特朗普在Truth Social上发布了一张黄的照片，这张照片被移植到特朗普自己的身上，这张臭名昭著的照片显示他在竞选集会上被枪击后举起拳头。黄对特朗普举起的拳头中，紧紧抓着一件猩红色的胸罩，将其高举在空中。

即使在民主党在中期选举中大获全胜而对总统权力造成决定性打击之后，特朗普似乎仍保持着企业王者的地位。特朗普表示，他在黄仁勋复职前一天晚上与他进行了交谈，并与董事会进行了“直接和间接”的沟通。白宫通讯主管史蒂文·张 (Steven Cheung) 在一份声明中表示，“特朗普总统完全参与”了董事会的决定——据《纽约时报》报道，特朗普在上周末决定，他希望带头让黄连连任，因此他要求副总裁 JD Vance 担任黄连和英伟达董事会之间的联络人，并保证此举不会构成安全风险。据报道，特朗普还拨通了英伟达周日晚上的董事会会议，为他的回归提供理由。 “我达成了这笔交易，”他周一告诉 CNBC。

黄仁勋再次被任命的消息，几乎与山姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 在 2023 年被 OpenAI 董事会投票否决后重新担任首席执行官一职一样戏剧性，对专家、分析师和投资者来说是一个广泛的震惊，特别是在英伟达董事会上周二的季度财报电话会议上向利益相关者保证董事会“不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官”之后。周一上午，纳斯达克 100 指数期货飙升触及熔断限制，并因波动性而导致交易暂停。

特朗普还插手了其他混乱事件，包括一再（或许是非法地）延长 TikTok 完成向美国实体出售的最后期限，而且他周一承认，这是为了保护特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk)。尽管特朗普在 CNBC 上表示，马斯克“80% 是超级天才，20% 有其他问题”，但他表示，保护像他和黄这样的人很重要。 “我们必须保护我们优秀的人才，因为我们的资源还不够。”

但即将召开的民主党占多数的国会可能会考验黄和特朗普的影响力。在共和党人准备 2028 年公开总统初选之际，至少一位潜在候选人似乎与总统对黄仁勋和英伟达的怀疑态度决裂。民主党人似乎渴望调查英伟达和特朗普政府。

对于英伟达（Nvidia）来说，过去几周可谓动荡不安。黄承认他与英伟达客户Megaspeed的前高管Alice Huang有婚外情（没有关系），据报道，一些美国情报官员认为Alice Huang是一名潜在的中国间谍。几乎立即就有报道称，他与一名直接下属又发生了婚外情，并据称与另一名员工发生了第三次婚外情。据报道，Megaspeed还因试图将英伟达先进芯片非法输送到中国而受到调查。黄本人一直在推动向中国开放更多的芯片销售，据报道，他向英伟达董事会撒了谎。他将于12月1日在国会作证。

英伟达董事会在周一的声明中试图解决对黄先生的担忧，并写道，成员“收到了美国政府高层的意见，根据这些意见，董事会相信黄先生的复职不会构成国家安全风险。”它保证，针对黄和外国情报机构启动的独立调查将在黄的合作下“得出结论”。

该委员会还表示，最近成立了一个全新的国家安全和出口管制委员会，“仅由独立董事组成，负责监督贸易合规和国家安全风险”，该委员会正在与具有国家安全经验的法律顾问和顾问合作。董事会表示，英伟达将招聘一个新的高管职位：首席合规官。高管将“监督整个公司的合规性”，并向提名委员会和公司治理委员会报告。 “NVIDIA 将继续配合正在进行的政府调查和质询，”董事会补充道。

尽管如此，人们对黄回归的反应反映出，在特朗普的努力之前，黄回归的可能性是多么小。尽管特朗普此前对多起有关黄爱丽是间谍的报道表示怀疑，但《纽约时报》周日报道称，她“与中国最高间谍机构的一名官员保持了一年多的联系”。据《泰晤士报》援引多位了解美国情报报告的人士的话报道，康伟——爱丽丝·黄的商业伙伴，据一些报道称，她的丈夫，据报道将她介绍给了英伟达首席执行官——与同一家中国情报机构合作。但周日晚上，特朗普仍然主张黄仁勋回归，并在经过一个周末的努力后，设法继续扭转英伟达的董事会，对他有利。

如果董事会在让黄重新担任首席执行官方面仍存在任何疑虑，特朗普对行政部门的权力——以及他可以施加的压力——可能会提供令人信服的反驳。据《华尔街日报》报道，美国证券交易委员会此前已对英伟达是否“误导投资者”展开调查。但特朗普周一在《Truth Social》上发表的一篇文章中表示，司法部长“已确认美国政府没有证据表明他参与了任何非法行为”。我们联系司法部征求意见，但并未根据 The Verge 的编辑政策提供公开回应。

title: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
title_en: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
author: Elizabeth Lopatto
article_content:
I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.

Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.

"The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy"

I have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity. Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy. You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated. I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy, Vance.

Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed, the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments.

In September 2025, the US government began investigating Megaspeed for possible violations of chip export controls; that October, the State Department told Trump of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who was described as a Chinese intelligence asset. Also in October, The New York Times first reported on Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia. In December, Trump — who has a close relationship with Jensen Huang — allowed Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China. In March 2026, Marco Rubio warned the government about Alice, and Trump nonetheless invited Huang to a visit in China. In October, The New York Times reported on the affair. Shortly after Huang sent a note to Nvidia admitting to it, several other reports of infidelity — this time with Nvidia employees — surfaced. On November 12th, Huang resigned. On November 17th, during the Nvidia earnings call, the board’s chair said that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On November 23rd, Huang was back.

"This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive"

What changed between last week and this week? A week was not enough time to truly review all the information on Huang and his paramour, Alice “No Relation” Huang, the international woman of mystery. The explanation seems to be that Nvidia’s board succumbed to a pressure campaign from Huang’s fellow billionaires, and a direct intervention from the president and vice president of the United States of America.

Sure, all these CEOs ostensibly wanted Huang back at Nvidia to keep the AI trade going. Still, watching the likes of Epic CEO Tim Sweeney, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, investing loudmouth Bill Ackman, and Elon Musk — who actually did appear in the Epstein files, and who seemed to be pretty friendly with Epstein! — pitch a fit last week was instructive. These men worried that they might be punished for wrongdoing, that they did not get big enough to be above the law. They have now been reassured, and I suppose that is what really matters. After all, Trump said on CNBC that he gave Nvidia’s board assurances that Jensen is “absolutely fine.”

This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive, and not just because Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Almost in passing, Trump noted that he had “protected” Musk in his first term from “a certain incident [that] took place, a very tough incident.” In his own inimitable style, Trump told Jim Cramer, “You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally.

"Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally"

One thing that has perhaps emboldened this crew is the stance from professional politics-knowers — and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — that holding members of the Trump administration accountable might be a hindrance to governing. That accountability was part of the reason for the blue wave in November seems to have bypassed these pundits (and the presumptive House majority leader). But then, why should we believe that Democrats will thoroughly investigate this? Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is claiming to want an investigation, but I am skeptical of how deep that investigation will go as long as Schumer leads it, and only partially because he’s been allied with Silicon Valley for more than a decade. He also has a daughter who works at OpenAI, a company that Nvidia invests in and that is dependent on Nvidia chips. How hard is he really willing to go?

Of course, there may be more to this than just pure economic self-interest. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump posted a remarkable image. It is an altered picture of Trump himself, taken after a failed assassination attempt in 2024. Trump’s head has been replaced with Jensen Huang’s head. The American flag has been replaced with the Nvidia logo. Huang is waving a bright red bra. It seems I owe Sigmund Freud an apology. In the end, these men fear nothing more than losing power for sexual shenanigans — and especially losing power to a woman.

Leave aside the national security issues for a minute and focus on the two Nvidia employees. Dating subordinates is a serious conflict of interest; the CEO of Nestle lost his job for just that last year. This is a major violation for CEOs of normal companies, but it is common practice among the sleazeballs of Silicon Valley: Bill Gates is famous for it and it was plainly rampant at Google, a tone set by Sergey Brin himself. I am sure that you will be shocked, shocked to discover that in the wake of MeToo, Brin was among the men who suddenly swung right. I mean, Musk himself announced he was a Republican the day before Business Insider reported that he exposed himself to a flight attendant and paid hush money to cover it up.

"If you’re rich enough, and connected enough, everything is permitted"

The Republican Party has made the abuse of women without consequences one of its main issues; that the lesser violation of sleeping with subordinates would also be something the revanchists would defend seems obvious. That was clear from the botched investigation of the Epstein affair itself, the botched release of the Epstein files, and the assorted confirmation hearings of Pete Hegseth, Brett Kavanaugh, and Todd Blanche. (To say nothing of the Andrew Tate business.) But in all this, let’s not forget that Trump has been accused of sexual misconduct by no fewer than 28 women. So I’m sure it was an affront to all these guys that not only did Huang’s misconduct include a series of affairs, but he was also replaced by Colette Kress, who is known to be a woman.

I suppose we might as well pass by the various reports that Huang allegedly terrorized his employees. In light of everything else, this seems minor by comparison.

Anyway I had that all in mind when I saw Epic’s Sweeney celebrating the state intrusion into theoretically private companies by posting “Back in Black,” an oblique reference to Huang’s leather jackets that is also from the later, lesser period of AC/DC, after Bon Scott died and AC/DC became an AC/DC tribute band. He also called The New York Times’ reporting into Huang “lies.” Musk continued his streak of Sephiroth posting: “The mistake has been corrected.” Jason Calacanis, the All-In podcast’s village idiot, posted, “GPU Jesus has risen!” along with an openly blasphemous, AI-generated image of Huang as Christ.

Best of luck to Joon Kim, the Wachtell Lipton partner and former federal prosecutor who is conducting “a thorough and independent investigation” into Huang’s alleged misconduct on behalf of Nvidia’s board. I assume Kim has, like the rest of us, gotten the message loud and clear: If you’re rich enough, and connected enough, everything is permitted. Or perhaps, more succinctly: lol nothing matters.

article_content_zh:
我想我必须向黄仁勋表示衷心的祝贺。黄仁勋再次担任英伟达首席执行官，这让几乎所有人都感到惊讶，除了总统唐纳德·特朗普和副总统 JD·万斯，他们确保了这一切的发生。

现在，我们这些对什么是“自由市场”有过一些基础教育的人可能会发现，美国总统对一家美国大公司施加压力是令人反感的。但我们的亿万富翁科技巨头们对“自由市场”的关心程度和他们对“言论自由”的关心程度一样高，也就是说，他们根本不在乎。看到硅谷为这实际上是计划经济的一个迹象而欢呼，当然令人振奋。但是，他们为什么要在乎呢？他们唯一真正的信念是他们应该保持富有，凌驾于法律之上。詹森可能没有和杰弗里·爱泼斯坦交换过电子邮件，但他现在已经坐在了爱泼斯坦的桌子上。

“据报道，这笔交易是由彼得泰尔自己的儿子促成的”

我过去曾在这里指出，爱泼斯坦案暴露了美国右翼复​​仇主义的真正政治：精英完全有罪不罚。好吧，又来了！如果你与特朗普关系足够密切，即使你与一名被指控的中国间谍发生关系，从而危及国家安全，也没关系。在美国总统召开董事会要求恢复你的职位之前，你甚至不会受到调查。我的意思是，这是黑帮科技监管的时代——我们期待什么？据报道，这笔交易是由彼得泰尔自己的儿子万斯促成的。

为了让我们能够绝对清楚 Nvidia 发生的事情，让我们快速回顾一下我们所知道的事实。 2023 年，一位名叫 Alice Huang 的中国公民收购了她更名为 Megaspeed 的公司，这家新加坡数据公司是本次调查的中心。在某个时候，黄爱丽丝遇见了黄爱丽丝，人们看到两人在当年 12 月的一次晚宴上在一起。从2024年到2025年，Megaspeed收到了超过200台Nvidia的出货量。

2025年9月，美国政府开始调查Megaspeed是否违反芯片出口管制；同年 10 月，国务院向特朗普通报了黄仁勋与被称为中国情报人员的爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的恋情。同样在 10 月，《纽约时报》首次报道了 Megaspeed 与 Nvidia 的关系。去年 12 月，与黄仁勋关系密切的特朗普允许 Nvidia 向中国出售更强大的芯片。 2026 年 3 月，马可·卢比奥就爱丽丝向政府发出警告，但特朗普仍然邀请黄来访中国。十月，《纽约时报》报道了这件事。在黄仁勋向英伟达发出承认此事的说明后不久，其他几起不忠的报道也浮出水面——这次是针对英伟达员工的。 11月12日，黄某辞职。 11 月 17 日，在英伟达财报电话会议上，董事会主席表示，该公司“不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官”。 11月23日，黄某回来了。

“这种公开腐败的程度确实令人印象深刻”

上周和本周之间发生了什么变化？一周的时间还不够真正回顾黄和他的情人、国际神秘女性爱丽丝“无关系”黄的所有信息。解释似乎是，英伟达董事会屈服于黄仁勋其他亿万富翁的压力，以及美国总统和副总统的直接干预。

当然，所有这些首席执行官表面上都希望黄回到英伟达，以保持人工智能行业的发展。不过，看看 Epic 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney)、Uber 前首席执行官特拉维斯·卡兰尼克 (Travis Kalanick)、投资大嘴比尔·阿克曼 (Bill Ackman) 和埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 等人——他们确实出现在爱泼斯坦的档案中，而且似乎与爱泼斯坦非常友好！ ——上周的发脾气很有启发性。这些人担心他们可能会因不当行为而受到惩罚，担心他们的规模还不够大，无法凌驾于法律之上。他们现在已经放心了，我想这才是真正重要的。毕竟，特朗普在 CNBC 上表示，他向英伟达董事会保证詹森“绝对没问题”。

这种程度的公开腐败确实令人印象深刻，这不仅仅是因为黄再次担任英伟达首席执行官。特朗普几乎是顺便指出，他在第一个任期内“保护”了马斯克，使其免受“发生的某一事件的影响，这是一次非常艰难的事件”。特朗普以他自己独特的风格告诉吉姆·克莱默，“如果没有我，你就不会有埃隆。”当地球上最大的两家公司的首席执行官将他们的工作归功于特朗普个人时，当然不会有任何负面影响。

“当地球上最大的两家公司的首席执行官将他们的工作归功于特朗普个人时，当然不会有任何负面影响”

也许让这个团队更加大胆的一件事是专业政治人士和众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯的立场，即让特朗普政府成员承担责任可能会阻碍执政。这种问责制是 11 月蓝色浪潮的部分原因，但似乎已经绕过了这些专家（以及假定的众议院多数党领袖）。但是，我们为什么要相信民主党会彻底调查此事呢？参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 声称希望进行调查，但我对舒默领导的调查能进行多深持怀疑态度，部分原因是他十多年来一直与硅谷结盟。他还有一个女儿，在 OpenAI 工作，这是一家 Nvidia 投资的公司，该公司依赖 Nvidia 芯片。他到底愿意走多远？

当然，这可能不仅仅是纯粹的经济利益。在庆祝黄的回归时，特朗普发布了一张引人注目的照片。这是特朗普本人的修改后的照片，拍摄于 2024 年刺杀行动失败后。特朗普的头像已被黄仁勋的头像取代。美国国旗已替换为 Nvidia 徽标。黄挥舞着鲜红色的胸罩。看来我欠西格蒙德·弗洛伊德一个道歉。最终，这些男人最害怕的就是因为性恶作剧而失去权力，尤其是失去对女人的权力。

先把国家安全问题放在一边，重点关注两名英伟达员工。与下属约会是一种严重的利益冲突；雀巢首席执行官去年就因此丢掉了工作。这对普通公司的首席执行官来说是一种严重的违规行为，但在硅谷的无赖中却是常见做法：比尔·盖茨因此而闻名，而且这种行为在谷歌显然很猖獗，这是谢尔盖·布林本人定下的基调。我相信你会感到震惊，震惊地发现，在 MeToo 事件之后，布林是突然向右转的人之一。我的意思是，在《商业内幕》报道他向空乘人员暴露自己并支付封口费以掩盖此事的前一天，马斯克本人宣布自己是共和党人。

A gauge of expected volatility in the Nasdaq 100 Index is sitting at the highest level since April 2020 after back-to-back punches from the ouster of Jensen Huang from Nvidia Corp. and the Democrats' victory in the midterm elections pushed the tech-heavy index teetering near a bear market. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both entered a correction territory on Friday, defined as a decline of at least 10% from an all-time high.

Futures on the S&P 500 traded up 1.1% at 6:02 pm in New York, while contracts on the Nasdaq 100 added 1.8%. The Cboe Volatility Index, or, VIX, closed above 35 on Friday, its highest level since 2025.

Thinner than normal liquidity into a holiday-shortened week in the US may further amplify volatility in the market already dealing with fundamental risks around the future of the artificial intelligence trade and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory. Markets are closed on Thursday in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday and will close early on Friday.

"Seasonally, VIX tends to drop in November, particularly with the Thanksgiving holiday," said Amy Wu Silverman, head of derivatives strategy at RBC Capital Markets. "So it's almost comical that VIX is up over 85% so far this month. Unfortunately, it is unlikely that the volatility shock is over given ongoing probes into Nvidia's accounting."

In recent weeks, worries about the sustainability of Wall Street's biggest investment boom in decades had begun to emerge, eroding confidence in the record-setting, AI-fueled rally and the impact of artificial intelligence on growth in the broader economy. At the same time, the scandal engulfing Nvidia, which led to the ouster of Huang following revelations of multiple affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy, has been the single-largest drag on the S&P 500 as it neared a so-called technical correction.

Anthropic PBC shares began trading last week and closed its first session up 17% from its IPO price of $83 per share. However, the Claude chatbot maker's shares ended Friday down 8.5%. The worse-than-expected performance of the highly anticipated initial public offering helped to weigh down the entire equities market.

"While we think it's unlikely that the VIX moves much higher from here, especially into the holidays, we continue to get questions about protecting into yearend as opposed to bottom fishing," said Daniel Kirsch, head of options at Piper Sandler & Co.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc.'s trading desk said last week's selloff has created an attractive opportunity to snap up US stocks. Still, the bank cautions that overall investor positioning remains elevated, signaling the broader capitulation needed for a meaningful rally could be missing.

Hedge funds' equity unwind has become "quite extended" and markets are nearing a "tactical entry" point, the bank's trading desk wrote in a note to clients on Sunday. But a few major headwinds are still in place: the broader stock-market positioning remains elevated, the Federal Reserve is expected to keep raising interest rates and future profits from massive AI investments remain uncertain.

在整个人工智能行业充满魅力但也有缺陷的推动者黄仁勋出人意料地回归担任芯片公司首席执行官后，英伟达在华尔街引领了雷鸣般的涨势。美国股市收复上周惨重跌幅的一半多一点，这是自 2008 年金融危机以来最严重的跌幅之一。

标准普尔 500 指数飙升 4.7%，这表明美国股市对单一行业的依赖程度。遭受重创的人工智能股的反弹推动纳斯达克综合指数领先市场上涨 6.5%，而道琼斯工业平均指数则上涨近 1450 点，即 3%。

澳大利亚股市预计将上涨，开盘时期货预计上涨 128 点，即 1.5%。周一澳大利亚证券交易所下跌 0.3%。澳元兑美元汇率为 US66.28 美分。

甚至在华尔街开盘前，期货市场的交易就表明美国股市将结束连续 7 天的跌势，这场跌势拖累标准普尔 500 指数较上月创下的历史高点下跌逾 10%。随后，关于黄回到英伟达的爆炸性消息传来，尽管该公司董事会仍在调查他是否是外国间谍的目标并造成任何国家安全担忧。这使得涨势加速。

Nvidia 的股价飙升 31.5%，收盘价略低于 2000 年以来的最佳单日涨幅，接近互联网泡沫的顶峰。上周该股暴跌近 23%，但仍低于黄丑闻爆发前的水平。

与英伟达密切相关的股票飙升。 CoreWeave 是一家购买 Nvidia 芯片，然后通过云出租这些芯片的公司，股价飙升 22.3%。

其他受益于人工智能热潮的广泛行业的股票也收复了部分失地。 GE Vernova 帮助人工智能数据中心提供动力，继上周下跌近 13% 后，该公司股价上涨 8.2%。卡特彼勒 (Caterpillar) 的设备销售因人工智能建设热潮而受益，继上周下跌 15% 后，该公司股价上涨 7.2%。

人工智能相关股票的表现对于员工的 401(k) 账户至关重要，因为英伟达和其他芯片股已经成长为华尔街最大、最有影响力的股票之一。今天，英伟达股价波动 1% 对标准普尔 500 指数的影响大于该指数 500 强公司中除两家公司以外的所有公司股价波动 1% 的影响。

周一标准普尔 500 指数的反弹是自 2025 年 4 月以来最好的一天，当时唐纳德·特朗普总统暂停了在“解放日”宣布的大部分关税，这些关税导致股市动荡。特朗普也可能对最近的这次激增产生了直接影响。

他在周一接受 CNBC 采访时表示，“我相信我的干预对于说服英伟达董事会恢复其联合创始人的职位非常重要”。不到一周前，英伟达拒绝了黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官的提议。

特朗普表示，他的政府向英伟达保证，黄仁勋的回归不会带来国家安全方面的担忧。
