Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

With Claude Ship, announced in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said. The feature is geared toward developers who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”

The new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic said, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic said.

“It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic said it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must)

“But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he said. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”

Ultimately, Gewirtz said he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the company and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he said.

Developer platforms overall are adapting to the new state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Claude Team and Enterprise plan users can try the new feature using the /ship command now available in Claude Code. The feature uses tokens, so your overall bill may change, but it depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the new PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

Anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

article_content_zh:
您会让一些克劳德代理为您审查并发送您的代码吗？

开发人员已经在大量使用 Claude Code 和其他人工智能驱动的编码工具，例如 OpenAI 的 Codex，但有些人仍然希望在推送代码之前自行检查代码。 Anthropic 的一项新功能依赖于更具冒险精神、代理优先的编码人员能够轻松地将最后一步交给人工智能。

Anthropic 表示，通过周一宣布的测试版 Claude Ship，“Claude 现在可以审查拉取请求、修复它们，并批准团队政策允许的请求”。该功能面向那些想要更快地行动或已经将大量编码任务委托给代理的开发人员。

“团队可以控制它的运行位置以及哪些变化需要人，”Anthropic 说。 “目标：交付代码的速度与团队编写代码的速度一样快。”

新功能使用了两个新代理以及 Code Review，Anthropic 在 3 月份针对 Teams 和 Enterprise 计划发布了 Code Review。代码审查首先收集、组织调查结果并将其发布到 PR。然后，Anthropic 表示，PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals 等代理人“通过审查、修复和批准决定来指导 PR，这样团队就不必手动管理每个步骤”。

PR Steward 无法批准或合并拉取请求，而是旨在参与“失败的 CI 检查、合并冲突以及审查来自代码审查、其他审查工具或团队成员的反馈”。它还通过注释记录了每次推送中发生的更改，并提供了如何撤消它的说明（如果开发人员愿意的话）。在整个过程中，开发人员可以向 Claude 发出指示，或者通过评论 @claude 来告诉它停止。

作为最后一步，Claude Approvals 会参考团队遵守的任何政策（开发人员以存储库文件的形式提供）以及开发人员设置的其他信号（例如代码审查结果），然后在允许的情况下自主批准更改。 Anthropic 表示，如果没有，它将寻求“更深入的人类签字”。

“它的工作原理就像一个更智能的 CODEOWNERS 文件，”该新闻稿补充道。 Anthropic 表示，它建议大多数客户“首先在仅观察模式下启用这些额外检查，以在配置分支保护以要求 Claude Approvals 开绿灯之前建立信心”。

管理员可以选择该功能在哪个存储库中运行，并根据需要调整设置。

但克劳德·希普并不适合所有人。

Anthropic 在新闻稿中表示：“大多数团队都希望有人批准每一项更改，而且当人们编写每一行代码时，这很容易跟上。但现在很多开发人员都使用代理进行构建。”他指出，其自己的 Claude Code 团队使用 Claude 来编写其所需的大部分代码。

ZDNET 高级特约编辑 David Gewirtz 表示，以编写代码的速度交付代码的想法“让我感到毛骨悚然”。但他补充说，鉴于 Claude Code 迄今为止令人印象深刻，如果 Anthropic 的部署工具同样有效，他不会感到惊讶。

另外：Claude Code 与 Codex：为什么我同时使用两者以及如何选择一个（如果必须的话）

“但是，这确实取决于团队的工作流程以及他们正在进行的开发类型，”他说。 “这并不适合每个团队，当然也不适合每个独立开发人员，但对于某些部署流程来说，它可以节省大量周转时间，节省资金，并可能更快地向客户发送修复程序。这很酷。”

article_content:
An open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems without needing to wait for the patch or restarts

OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. In a controlled test, a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart.

We’re inviting developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators across the industry to help develop the project further. The project brings together OpenAI’s frontier AI, security and infrastructure research and Cisco’s infrastructure and security expertise to help protect the systems people rely on every day.

Testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks. Protecting a service in the meantime can be challenging because an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same Linux operation. Blocking that operation entirely could take the service offline.

Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”) is designed to help security teams navigate this tradeoff. Teams can test whether a temporary safeguard, called a shield, blocks the behavior that exposes a vulnerability while allowing legitimate requests through. Once an operator approves the shield, it can be deployed while the service continues running.

### How Shirudo works

Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system. This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems.

OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo around four core capabilities:

Live protection: eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system. Security teams can monitor how a proposed shield would affect applications before enforcing it.

Defense at machine speed: OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo to give agents programmable controls to investigate vulnerabilities, develop targeted shields, and validate their effectiveness against exploits and real workloads. Security teams control what gets deployed.

Trusted deployment: Shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading. Linux's eBPF verifier checks eBPF programs against its safety rules, while kernel security controls restrict unauthorized changes.

Hardware-backed verification: Shirudo uses a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) to support a verifiable record of protections being loaded or removed. Operators can use this evidence to check whether systems meet their security requirements.

The Shirudo technical walkthrough from the Linux Plumbers Conference shows how to apply a shield and verify it on the target host. The Java4Shell vulnerability is another example illustrating how a targeted shield can protect a running application while a permanent patch is being prepared. Using OpenAI's Codex, the team generated a shield that added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and attached it directly to a running Elasticsearch process. When attempting to exploit the vulnerability, the shield rejected the malicious input, blocking the attack while Elasticsearch continued running. You can read more here.

### Rethinking infrastructure

Shirudo is a first step toward infrastructure that can adapt to emerging threats while remaining reliable. We want to strengthen the operating system foundations needed to deploy these protections at scale, including hardening the kernel and core services, limiting workload permissions, and making updates and recovery safer.

Our long-term goal is to enable defenders and AI agents to quickly identify affected systems, validate protections, and deploy eBPF shields that block exploits without disrupting workloads. Applications should run with only the permissions they need, governed by policies that are automatically generated and maintained.

We will combine frontier AI with security and infrastructure research to discover vulnerabilities and test defenses against realistic attacks. We aim to make it easier for operators to detect and contain compromises, prevent attackers from moving across systems, and restore services to a verified, known-good state. Hardware-backed attestation and independent network controls provide additional assurance even if individual systems are compromised.

### Building in the open

OpenAI and Cisco are open-sourcing Shirudo so developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators can inspect the code, test protections, and contribute to its development. Shirudo is licensed under BSD 2-Clause, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.

Our goal is to make tested shields available alongside vulnerability disclosures, giving operators a way to evaluate and deploy temporary protections while preparing permanent patches.

Try Shirudo: Follow the VM quickstart to sign, load, and verify a test protection.

Get hands-on: Explore Shirudo through Isovalent's self-guided lab.

Join the technical deep dive: Register for the December 15 webinar.

We’re building Shirudo in the open with the people who build, run, and secure Linux systems. We welcome contributions to the runtime, new shields, and improvements to Linux and eBPF. If you'd like to get involved, take a look at the code on GitHub, read the docs, and let us know what you find.

article_content_zh:
开源运行时，可帮助操作员保护正在运行的 Linux 系统，无需等待补丁或重新启动

OpenAI 和 Cisco 正在推出 Shirudo，这是一个开源运行时，可帮助团队在推出补丁时保护 Linux 系统。在受控测试中，Codex 生成的防护罩阻止了针对正在运行的 Elasticsearch 服务的 Java4Shell 攻击尝试，而无需重新启动。

我们邀请整个行业的开发人员、安全研究人员和基础设施运营商来帮助进一步开发该项目。该项目汇集了 OpenAI 的前沿人工智能、安全和基础设施研究以及思科的基础设施和安全专业知识，以帮助保护人们每天依赖的系统。

测试和部署补丁仍可能需要数天或数周的时间。同时保护服务可能具有挑战性，因为漏洞利用和合法请求可能依赖于相同的 Linux 操作。完全阻止该操作可能会使服务脱机。

Shirudo（日语中的“盾牌”）旨在帮助安全团队进行这种权衡。团队可以测试称为防护罩的临时保护措施是否可以阻止暴露漏洞的行为，同时允许合法请求通过。一旦操作员批准了防护罩，就可以在服务继续运行的同时进行部署。

Shirudo 使用 eBPF，这是一种 Linux 技术，允许小程序在操作系统内的特定点运行。这使得观察可疑活动并对正在运行的系统应用有针对性的安全保护成为可能。

OpenAI 和 Cisco 正在围绕四个核心功能设计 Shirudo：

实时保护：eBPF 防护罩可以阻止易受攻击的代码路径，而无需重新启动系统。安全团队可以在实施之前监控提议的防护措施将如何影响应用程序。

以机器速度进行防御：OpenAI 和思科正在设计 Shirudo，为代理提供可编程控制来调查漏洞、开发有针对性的防护罩，并验证其针对漏洞和实际工作负载的有效性。安全团队控制部署的内容。

可信部署：Shield 在加载前经过加密签名和验证。 Linux 的 eBPF 验证程序根据其安全规则检查 eBPF 程序，而内核安全控制则限制未经授权的更改。

硬件支持的验证：Shirudo 使用可信平台模块 (TPM) 来支持加载或删除的保护的可验证记录。运营商可以使用此证据来检查系统是否满足其安全要求。

Linux Plumbers Conference 的 Shirudo 技术演练展示了如何应用防护罩并在目标主机上验证它。 Java4Shell 漏洞是另一个示例，说明了有针对性的防护如何在准备永久补丁的同时保护正在运行的应用程序。使用 OpenAI 的 Codex，该团队生成了一个盾牌，为 Java 的 Base64 解码器添加了输入检查，并将其直接附加到正在运行的 Elasticsearch 进程。当尝试利用该漏洞时，防护罩会拒绝恶意输入，从而在 Elasticsearch 继续运行的同时阻止攻击。您可以在这里阅读更多内容。

### 重新思考基础设施

Shirudo 是迈向能够适应新威胁并同时保持可靠性的基础设施的第一步。我们希望加强大规模部署这些保护所需的操作系统基础，包括强化内核和核心服务、限制工作负载权限以及使更新和恢复更安全。

title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
title_en: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
author: Justine Calma
article_content:
The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.

Each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric.

“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this”

To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of new AI data centers a climate issue alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy.

“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this, and it will inevitably come up in the discussions. It’s part of the broader energy transformation,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s minister for climate change and energy and the president of COP31 climate negotiations, told Politico in an interview at the start of the COP31 summit.

Despite becoming the longest COP yet, with debates lasting two days longer than scheduled, official negotiations fell apart spectacularly. Delegates ultimately failed to garner enough support to pass the “pact” they’d been bargaining on for two weeks. The EU, UK, and several smaller nations most vulnerable to climate change rejected the deal that they saw as too weak. The pact omitted the term “fossil fuels” despite many nations calling for stronger commitments to phase out oil, coal, and gas. And the US, the epicenter of the data center buildout and the biggest climate polluter historically, was a no-show after the pro-fossil-fuel Trump administration pulled the country out of the Paris accord (twice).

With official negotiations falling apart, and countries only making voluntary commitments on AI and electrification, some environmental and humanitarian groups called this year “the worst COP” ever.

To meet the Paris goals, nations will need to cut their greenhouse gas emissions roughly in half by 2030 before reaching net zero by the middle of the century. Many tech companies made similar commitments in recent years, including Google, Microsoft, and Meta. But thanks to the AI boom, those goals have fallen by the wayside.

Meta is “re-evaluating” its timeline to reach net zero emissions as it focuses on AI, the company said in its annual sustainability report on Thursday. Meta reported a 45 percent year-over-year increase in climate pollution. Google’s and Microsoft’s carbon footprints are also growing despite climate commitments the companies have made. Data centers’ electricity consumption is forecast to double by 2030, according to a forecast by the International Energy Agency.

“That is a huge climate risk: rising power demand from data centres is not yet sustainable, and an AI boom cannot be allowed to become a fossil fuel boom,” Bruce Douglas, CEO of the Global Renewables Alliance, tells The Verge in an email. Data centers were “a key topic” at COP31, according to Douglas, whose organization cohosted a panel on the challenges during the event.

In the US, the country with the most data centers, power sector emissions could increase 42 percent by 2030 as energy companies build more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a recent analysis by the Sierra Club. Already, hyperscale data centers in the US create more climate pollution than the country of Denmark, a separate study by Harvard researchers recently found.

To stop data centers from creating more pollution, they would need to be powered by additional new sources of renewable energy, Douglas says. He adds that data centers are currently competing with everyone else for grid connections, finance, and electricity generation capacity — and against arguably more essential tasks like heating and air conditioning, as well as electrifying transportation.

Many tech companies match their electricity use with renewable energy purchases. But unless they’re helping to build new sources of green energy to meet their added electricity demand, they might just end up hogging limited renewable energy capacity. And if more fossil fuels make up the difference, then greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise overall.

“Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”

“In many cases, datacentres are outbidding other consumers to get speed to power,” Douglas says. “Should new green electrons be used for air-conditioning, electrification or data centres?”

There was some progress. Around 80 nations signed onto a voluntary pledge to increase electricity’s share of energy consumption to 35 percent over the next decade, according to COP31 president Murat Kurum. The list of countries that includes, however, hasn’t been published yet, Carbon Brief reports.

Another voluntary pledge to keep AI from derailing climate action by calling on data centers to run on less polluting energy also failed to garner much support. Douglas notes that by using the term “low-emission energy,” the pledge still leaves the door open for natural gas (which produces less carbon pollution than coal when burned but is a significant source of methane pollution) to keep powering data centers.

“The Antalya A.I. pledge is a step in the right direction to address an important piece of the impacts, but needs teeth in order to translate into stronger protections for people and the planet,” the nonprofit Natural Resources Defense Council said in a statement when the pledge was first announced. “The speed, scale and scope of this challenge is bigger than perhaps anything before it, and the guardrails must be commensurate.”

key_points_en: Key Development: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks

article_content_zh:
清洁能源革命取决于整个全球经济的电气化，正如耗电的数据中心正在激增一样。这是来自世界各地的代表在联合国气候变化大会（COP31）期间必须应对的挑战，该会议于周日在土耳其安塔利亚结束，气氛混乱且令人不满意。

每年，与会者都会努力兑现 2015 年巴黎气候协议中阻止气候变化的承诺。为了防止极端天气变得更加可怕，防止沿海社区遭受洪水，以及防止干旱破坏粮食和水系统，需要大幅削减温室气体排放。但为了用太阳能和风能而不是石油和天然气为家庭或汽车提供动力，它们需要采用电力。

“世界上每一位气候部长都在考虑这个问题”

为此，今年谈判最令人期待的成果之一是达成协议，到 2035 年将电力在全球能源消耗中的份额提高到 35%，而目前这一比例约为 20%。然而，当数据中心导致电力需求猛增时，这就变得更加困难。这使得新的人工智能数据中心的涌现成为气候问题，同时也引发了关于如何从化石燃料过渡到可再生能源的讨论。

“世界上每个气候部长都在考虑这个问题，并且在讨论中不可避免地会提到这个问题。这是更广泛的能源转型的一部分，”澳大利亚气候变化和能源部长、COP31气候谈判主席克里斯·鲍文(Chris Bowen)在COP31峰会开始时接受Politico采访时表示。

尽管成为迄今为止时间最长的缔约方会议，辩论持续时间比原定时间长了两天，但官方谈判却严重破裂。代表们最终未能获得足够的支持来通过他们已经讨价还价了两周的“协议”。欧盟、英国和几个最容易受到气候变化影响的小国拒绝了这项协议，他们认为这项协议太软弱。尽管许多国家呼吁做出更强有力的承诺，逐步淘汰石油、煤炭和天然气，但该协议省略了“化石燃料”一词。而作为数据中心建设的中心和历史上最大的气候污染源的美国，在支持化石燃料的特朗普政府（两次）让美国退出《巴黎协定》后却没有出现。

由于官方谈判破裂，各国仅就人工智能和电气化做出自愿承诺，一些环境和人道主义组织称今年是“有史以来最糟糕的缔约方会议”。

为了实现巴黎目标，各国需要到 2030 年将温室气体排放量减少大约一半，然后在本世纪中叶实现净零排放。近年来，许多科技公司都做出了类似的承诺，包括谷歌、微软和 Meta。但由于人工智能的蓬勃发展，这些目标已经半途而废。

Meta 在周四的年度可持续发展报告中表示，由于专注于人工智能，Meta 正在“重新评估”其实现净零排放的时间表。 Meta 报告称，气候污染同比增加了 45%。尽管谷歌和微软做出了气候承诺，但它们的碳足迹也在增加。根据国际能源署的预测，到 2030 年，数据中心的电力消耗预计将增加一倍。

全球可再生能源联盟首席执行官布鲁斯·道格拉斯（Bruce Douglas）在一封电子邮件中告诉 The Verge：“这是一个巨大的气候风险：数据中心不断增长的电力需求尚不可持续，而且不能让人工智能热潮变成化石燃料热潮。”道格拉斯表示，数据中心是 COP31 上的“一个关键主题”，他的组织在活动期间共同主持了一个关于挑战的小组讨论。

根据塞拉俱乐部 (Sierra Club) 最近的一项分析，在拥有最多数据中心的美国，随着能源公司建造更多化石燃料基础设施以满足数据中心电力需求，到 2030 年，电力部门的排放量可能会增加 42%。哈佛大学研究人员最近的另一项研究发现，美国的超大规模数据中心造成的气候污染已经超过了丹麦。

道格拉斯说，为了阻止数据中心造成更多污染，它们需要由额外的新可再生能源提供动力。他补充说，数据中心目前正在与其他所有人竞争电网连接、金融和发电能力，以及可以说更重要的任务，如供暖和空调以及电气化交通。

许多科技公司将其用电量与可再生能源的采购相匹配。但除非他们帮助建立新的绿色能源来满足额外的电力需求，否则他们最终可能会占用有限的可再生能源产能。如果更多的化石燃料弥补了这一差额，那么温室气体排放量总体上将继续上升。

“新的绿色电子是否应该用于空调、电气化或数据中心？”

title: OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably
title_en: OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably

inline_images.caption: GPT-6.2 outperforms GPT-6 on expert-level tasks across all reasoning settings in ChatGPT's regular chat mode. | Image: OpenAI
inline_images.caption_en: GPT-6.2 outperforms GPT-6 on expert-level tasks across all reasoning settings in ChatGPT's regular chat mode. | Image: OpenAI

author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
OpenAI is rolling out a chat-tuned version of GPT-6.2 Sol worldwide, available now for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. The company says the model handles complex requests and web searches better than GPT-6 and asks more relevant follow-up questions. In internal tests, GPT-6.2 understands images better (71.7 vs. 47.4 percent) and follows difficult instructions more often (78.1 vs. 62.5 percent).

On an internal benchmark for expert-level tasks, GPT-6.2 beats GPT-6 across all four reasoning levels, according to OpenAI. It scores roughly 65 to just over 71 percent, compared with about 52 to 66 percent for GPT-6. OpenAI also uses an internal version of BrowseComp to test how well models find answers to tough questions on the web. GPT-6.2 leads at every level, finishing about 10 percentage points ahead at the highest one.

According to the system card, GPT-6.2 follows safety policies in 91 to 94 percent of difficult conversations, up from 77 to 80 percent for GPT-6. The model makes its biggest gains in youth safety, specifically around emotional dependency, eating disorders, and dangerous activities.

These numbers only apply to ChatGPT's chat mode. The Work and Codex models stay the same. Enterprise admins can decide whether their users get access to GPT-6.2.

title: Exclusive: Commerce to add Megaspeed to trade blacklist
title_en: Exclusive: Commerce to add Megaspeed to trade blacklist
author: Ashley Gold
article_content:
The Trump administration plans to add the company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, Megaspeed, to a trade blacklist designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The Singapore-based company will be added to the Commerce Department’s entity list on Monday, the sources said.

The addition means that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. The news comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO, after President Donald Trump implored them to do so. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been under pressure to place Megaspeed on the department’s entity list from others inside the administration, tensions that became public after news broke of Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy who was an executive at Megaspeed. The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.

Earlier this month, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his agency along with the Pentagon, the State Department, and the US Trade Representative had backed putting Megaspeed on the entity list “for months” but that “Commerce holds the pen.” Bipartisan lawmakers have pressed Lutnick to put Megaspeed on the entity list and explain his decisions around Nvidia, Megaspeed, and chip export controls.

title: Sources: Trump pushed Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang after allies argued he was "too big to fail" for the US economy and a victim of "deep state" maneuvering (Axios)
title_en: Sources: Trump pushed Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang after allies argued he was "too big to fail" for the US economy and a victim of "deep state" maneuvering (Axios)

inline_images.caption: President Trump (left) greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a White House event on U.S. investments on April 30, 2025. Photo: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images
inline_images.alt: President Trump (left) greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a White House event on U.S. investments on

author: Axios
article_content:
President Trump pushed Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO after allies argued he was "too big to fail" for the U.S. economy and a victim of "deep state" maneuvering, sources familiar with the discussions told Axios.

Why it matters: Trump put the weight of the presidency behind a private company's decision about who should run it, an intervention that strengthened Huang's allies inside the administration and put officials critical of the company in an increasingly uncomfortable position.

Driving the news: "Jensen is too big to fail," one source familiar with the discussions told Axios.

Behind the scenes: Huang's allies appealed to Trump's longstanding distrust of the intelligence community, portraying the Nvidia founder as a victim of persecution by unnamed government insiders.

Zoom in: The memo came as Nvidia lobbied the Trump administration to open up China's access to its chips.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance viewed Huang as an important champion of open models offering Americans more control and lower costs than closed models like OpenAI's and Anthropic's.

Yes, but: These conclusions come as more and more connections between Alice Huang — the alleged Chinese spy Huang had an affair with — and the Chinese government and military come to light.

"He let the U.S. stock market and economy demand his return — along with the pressure from the president — and the outcry was deafening," the source said.

Huang's reinstatement is a "big win" for Vance, a source close to Rubio said.

What we're watching: Huang's opponents in the administration now risk backlash from the president.

What's next: Trump's intervention settled the immediate fight over Nvidia's leadership but raised questions about the U.S. government's role in the board's decision.

放大：这份备忘录发布之际，英伟达正在游说特朗普政府开放中国获取其芯片的渠道。

我们正在关注的内容：黄在政府中的反对者现在面临着遭到总统强烈反对的风险。

接下来：特朗普的干预解决了围绕英伟达领导权的直接斗争，但引发了人们对美国政府在董事会决策中所扮演角色的质疑。

title: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
title_en: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
author: Jay Peters
article_content:
Anthropic is launching some new Claude AI features to help software engineers ship code. As part of a new Claude Ship product being announced today, Claude now can review, fix, and approve pull requests.

Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude’s code review capabilities thanks to the Code Review feature, which was announced in March and became generally available in October. What’s new alongside Claude Ship are the PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents, which are launching in beta today.

PR Steward “jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members” and leaves comments on what it changed, according to Anthropic. Claude Approvals can approve routine changes if an organization’s policy allows it. “Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language,” Anthropic says.

Claude Ship is now available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and works with repositories on GitHub.

title: How Jensen Huang ended up as Nvidia CEO again
title_en: How Jensen Huang ended up as Nvidia CEO again
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
The Jensen Huang era of Nvidia nearly came to an end this month. Huang, who three decades ago co-founded what’s come to be considered one of the most important companies in AI, resigned from his role on November 12th over mounting scrutiny around his alleged affairs. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and that he “created problems for the board.”

Huang’s resignation came after weeks of escalating problems, both personal and professional. First, reporting from The New York Times said he had a “close relationship” with a woman passing intelligence to China. Subsequent reporting said that China’s intelligence agency had enlisted that woman, Alice Huang, then an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, to spy on Nvidia’s leader, and that the Singapore-based company was under investigation for potentially smuggling AI chips to China. Stories followed that indicated Huang was having an affair with Alice as well as an Nvidia executive, vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell.

So when Huang resigned less than two weeks ago, the decision seemed final. Even Nvidia’s board appeared unwilling to budge. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” board chair Harvey Jones said during an earnings call last week.

But in the days following Huang’s resignation, the founder’s allies — including President Donald Trump — mounted a pressure campaign that brought him back to the company he created and sent Nvidia’s share price rocketing upward, almost as though he had never left.

The campaign in support of Huang began almost immediately after his resignation. A coterie of tech leaders began posting in support of Nvidia’s founder: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney questioned the motives of journalists who broke the stories about his affairs. Tesla CEO Elon Musk likened Huang’s departure to “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman later said on stage, “it’s hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen.”

“If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come,” Trump said.

Meanwhile, some of those tech leaders began questioning aspects of the reporting that led to Huang’s exit. Venture capitalist and former White House AI czar David Sacks cast doubt that Alice Huang was a spy, citing a lack of confirmation from US officials. Trump exacerbated the uncertainty, telling reporters, “I don’t know that she is a spy,” despite reports saying the assessment had relied on US intelligence sources.

Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, found itself in a tough position. The company’s shares crashed following Huang’s departure, and they didn’t pick up even after a rosy earnings report. The board was also scrambling to find a new CEO, something industry analysts speculated would prove exceptionally difficult. Reports indicated that Nvidia was considering hiring Arm CEO Rene Haas and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, both of whom already have powerful roles in the chip industry.

Trump quickly warmed up to Huang’s return, too. The president — whose investment accounts traded up to $97 million worth of Nvidia stock since returning to office — initially floated the idea of having former Apple CEO Tim Cook take Huang’s place, before saying that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” to bring Huang back.

This past weekend, Trump appears to have inserted himself into the situation directly. A report from The New York Times says that Trump asked Vice President JD Vance to work with Huang and Nvidia’s board to “resolve the situation,” while the Trump administration reassured the board that it “did not believe that Mr. Huang himself posed a national security risk.” Semafor reports that Trump even called into Nvidia’s board meeting to advocate for Huang’s reinstatement. Sunday evening, Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he hopes Nvidia’s board “rehires Jensen Huang.”

Hours later, Nvidia’s board did just that. The board announced on Monday that it reinstated Huang as its CEO, president, and board member. In its statement, the board said that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

Trump immediately took credit for Huang’s reinstatement, with White House spokesperson Steven Cheung saying the president “was totally involved” in the decision. “If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come,” Trump said during an interview with CNBC. He added in a post on Truth Social that the US Attorney General confirmed that it doesn’t have evidence that Huang “engaged in any unlawful conduct.”

Nvidia’s shares rose on the news of Huang’s reinstatement, while tech leaders celebrated his return on social media. But the saga is likely far from over. The board said it will finish its investigation into Huang, the Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Nvidia’s “accounting practices,” and Megaspeed is being investigated by the Justice Department. Even Trump has said that Nvidia should continue its internal investigation about export controls compliance.

Trump’s apparent involvement also leaves plenty of room for scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who will control the House and Senate next year. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) called Nvidia’s decision “reckless” and urged the Trump administration to explain the “input” government officials provided to the company’s board

Huang’s stunning reinstatement still leaves many questions unanswered. Though the backing of Wall Street, the White House, and Silicon Valley may have brought Huang back as CEO, a new wave of scrutiny from federal regulators and lawmakers is just getting started.

article_content_zh:
本月，英伟达的黄仁勋时代即将结束。三十年前，黄仁勋与他人共同创立了被认为是人工智能领域最重要的公司之一，由于对其涉嫌的事务受到越来越严格的审查，黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞去职务。黄承认他对妻子“不忠”，并且“给董事会带来了问题”。

黄的辞职是在几个星期的个人和工作问题升级之后发生的。首先，《纽约时报》的报道称，他与一名向中国传递情报的女子关系“密切”。随后的报道称，中国情报机构招募了这名女子，当时是英伟达客户Megaspeed的高管爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang），以监视英伟达的领导人，这家总部位于新加坡的公司正因可能向中国走私人工智能芯片而接受调查。随后的报道表明，黄与爱丽丝以及英伟达的一位高管、医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔（Kimberly Powell）有染。

因此，当黄在不到两周前辞职时，这个决定似乎是最终的。就连英伟达董事会似乎也不愿让步。董事会主席哈维·琼斯在上周的财报电话会议上表示：“英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞职，并且不打算恢复詹森的首席执行官职务。”

但在黄仁勋辞职后的几天里，这位创始人的盟友——包括唐纳德·特朗普总统——发起了一场压力运动，将他带回了他创建的公司，并使英伟达的股价飙升，就好像他从未离开过一样。

支持黄的运动几乎是在他辞职后立即开始的。一群科技领袖开始发帖支持 Nvidia 创始人：Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 质疑爆料他的事件的记者的动机。特斯拉首席执行官埃隆·马斯克将黄仁勋的离职比作“当你连胜时将迈克尔·乔丹踢出你的团队”。 OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 后来在台上表示，“很难想象没有 Jensen 的人工智能革命。”

特朗普表示：“如果我不参与其中，英伟达可能会在未来很长一段时间内感到非常悲伤。”

与此同时，一些科技领导人开始质疑导致黄退出的报道的各个方面。风险投资家、前白宫人工智能沙皇戴维·萨克斯 (David Sacks) 对爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是间谍表示怀疑，理由是缺乏美国官员的证实。特朗普加剧了不确定性，他告诉记者，“我不知道她是间谍”，尽管有报道称评估依赖于美国情报来源。

与此同时，英伟达董事会发现自己处境艰难。黄仁勋离职后，该公司股价暴跌，即使发布了乐观的盈利报告，股价也没有回升。董事会还在争先恐后地寻找新的首席执行官，行业分析师推测这将是异常困难的。有报道称，英伟达正在考虑聘请 Arm 首席执行官雷内·哈斯 (Rene Haas) 和苹果硬件主管约翰尼·斯鲁吉 (Johny Srouji)，两人都已经在芯片行业发挥了重要作用。

特朗普也很快对黄的回归产生了兴趣。自重返办公室以来，这位总统的投资账户交易了价值高达 9700 万美元的英伟达股票。他最初提出了让前苹果首席执行官蒂姆·库克接替黄的想法，然后表示让黄回来“当然不是一个坏主意”。

上周末，特朗普似乎直接介入了局势。 《纽约时报》的一篇报道称，特朗普要求副总统万斯与黄仁勋和英伟达董事会合作“解决问题”，而特朗普政府则向董事会保证“不认为黄仁勋本人构成国家安全风险”。 Semafor 报道称，特朗普甚至召集了英伟达董事会会议，主张黄仁勋复职。周日晚上，特朗普在 Truth Social 上发帖表示，他希望英伟达董事会“重新聘用黄仁勋”。

几个小时后，英伟达董事会就这样做了。董事会周一宣布恢复黄先生担任首席执行官、总裁和董事会成员。该委员会在声明中表示，它收到了“美国政府高层”的意见，并确定“黄的复职不会构成国家安全风险”。

特朗普立即将黄的复职归功于他，白宫发言人张史蒂文表示，总统“完全参与”了这一决定。特朗普在接受 CNBC 采访时表示：“如果我不参与其中，英伟达可能会在未来很长一段时间内感到非常悲伤。”他在 Truth Social 上的一篇帖子中补充说，美国司法部长证实，没有证据表明黄“从事任何非法行为”。

黄仁勋复职的消息传出后，英伟达股价上涨，而科技巨头们则在社交媒体上庆祝他的回归。但这个传奇很可能还远未结束。董事会表示将完成对黄的调查，美国证券交易委员会正在调查英伟达的“会计行为”，Megaspeed 正在接受司法部的调查。就连特朗普也表示，英伟达应该继续进行有关出口管制合规性的内部调查。

特朗普的明显参与也为明年将控制众议院和参议院的民主党议员留下了足够的审查空间。马萨诸塞州民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 称英伟达的决定“鲁莽”，并敦促特朗普政府解释政府官员向该公司董事会提供的“意见”

author: Steve Holland and Courtney Rozen
article_content:
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened in Nvidia's decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend, convinced he alone protected American-made open-weight AI models, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Open-weight AI models are systems whose core components are publicly available for users to download, modify and adapt for specific tasks. Their growth has become a major business opportunity for Nvidia because they broaden demand for the company's chips and computing infrastructure beyond a handful of large AI developers.

China leads in the development of open-weight AI systems, which are gaining ground with US companies because they can be cheaper than proprietary AI tools from top US labs OpenAI and Anthropic . They can also perform nearly as well.

Nvidia has been one of the most prominent backers of the US open-weight ecosystem. Nvidia in August agreed to buy the company Hugging Face, a platform that developers use to host open-weight AI models, among other AI-related resources. Nvidia is also an investor in Reflection AI, an American company that launched its first open-weight model in October.

Huang and Nvidia's lobbyists have also pressed US lawmakers to support the development of open-weight AI technology, with Huang writing in a letter earlier this year that they should avoid "premature restrictions" on such tools.

Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports that he engaged in several extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Reuters reported on November 18 that the Trump administration was considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, including open-weight models, as part of an effort to reduce reliance on Chinese technology.

Republican lawmakers have increasingly echoed the argument that open-weight AI is critical to competing with China. Two leading House Republican lawmakers on Friday called on the Trump administration to help American companies developing open-weight AI models, adding that it would position the US to better counter China.

article_content_zh:
路透华盛顿11月23日 - 知情人士周一表示，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和副总裁 JD·万斯周末亲自干预了英伟达恢复首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 职务的决定，相信他独自保护了美国制造的开放权重人工智能模型。

开放权重人工智能模型是其核心组件公开可供用户下载、修改和适应特定任务的系统。它们的增长已成为英伟达的主要商机，因为它们扩大了对该公司芯片和计算基础设施的需求，超出了少数大型人工智能开发商的范围。

中国在开放式人工智能系统的开发方面处于领先地位，这些系统正在赢得美国公司的青睐，因为它们比美国顶级实验室 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的专有人工智能工具更便宜。他们的表现也几乎一样。

英伟达一直是美国开放权重生态系统最著名的支持者之一。 Nvidia 在 8 月份同意收购 Hugging Face 公司，这是一个开发人员用来托管开放权重 AI 模型以及其他 AI 相关资源的平台。 Nvidia 也是 Reflection AI 的投资者，这家美国公司于 10 月份推出了首款开放权重模型。

黄和英伟达的游说者还向美国立法者施压，要求支持开放式人工智能技术的发展，黄在今年早些时候的一封信中写道，他们应该避免对此类工具进行“过早限制”。

本月早些时候，黄先生辞去首席执行官一职，此前有报道称，黄先生曾发生多起婚外情，其中包括与一名涉嫌中国间谍的婚外情。

路透社11月18日报道称，特朗普政府正在考虑要求美国公司公开披露其对中国人工智能模型（包括开放权重模型）的使用情况，以减少对中国技术的依赖。

共和党议员越来越赞同开放式人工智能对于与中国竞争至关重要的论点。两位主要的众议院共和党议员周五呼吁特朗普政府帮助美国公司开发开放式人工智能模型，并补充说这将使美国能够更好地对抗中国。

title: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's headquarters to cheers from employees and said "I'm gonna be a better CEO the second time around" (Geoff Weiss/Business Insider)
title_en: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's headquarters to cheers from employees and said "I'm gonna be a better CEO the second time around" (Geoff Weiss/Business Insider)

inline_images.caption: Bloomberg/Getty Images Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
inline_images.alt: Bloomberg/Getty Images Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

author: Business Insider
article_content:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters Monday to cheers from employees, less than two weeks after his stunning ouster. Nvidia employees gathered at headquarters to mark the moment, chanting "Jensen! Jensen!" as he arrived back at the office, according to a person familiar with the scene.

The crowd was so packed that employees jostled for a glimpse. Rather than his signature black leather jacket, the source said he appeared to be wearing a navy cotton coat. Huang put his hand on his heart several times and said, "This is my first day at work," according to a video of the scene.

"I'm terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this." "I'm gonna be a better CEO the second time around," he said, according to another person in attendance. "I don't have a computer, so the IT department is gonna give me a new PC," Huang added. In public posts, Nvidia employees flocked to social media to celebrate Huang's return to the company.

A "Stand with Jensen" petition calling for his reinstatement had previously garnered more than 200,000 signatures, including thousands who identified as current employees. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider. Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as CEO on Monday, reversing course just 11 days after his resignation amid revelations about his personal relationships and an ongoing investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

Prominent names in business also applauded Huang's reinstatement, while President Trump said he "convinced" Nvidia's board to make the decision as the company's stock had plummeted in his absence.

周一，黄仁勋在员工的欢呼声中回到英伟达圣克拉拉总部，距离他令人震惊的下台还不到两周。 Nvidia 员工聚集在总部纪念这一时刻，高呼“Jensen！Jensen！”据一位知情人士透露，当他回到办公室时。

人群挤满了人，员工们争先恐后地想一睹风采。消息人士称，他似乎穿着一件海军蓝棉外套，而不是他标志性的黑色皮夹克。现场视频显示，黄多次把手放在心口上，说道：“这是我第一天上班。”

“我对让你们所有人经历这一切感到非常抱歉。”据另一位与会人士透露，“第二次我会成为一名更好的首席执行官”。 “我没有电脑，所以 IT 部门会给我一台新电脑，”黄补充道。在公开帖子中，英伟达员工纷纷涌向社交媒体庆祝黄回到公司。

一份要求詹森复职的“与詹森站在一起”请愿书此前已获得超过20万签名，其中包括数千名现任员工。英伟达没有立即回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。英伟达董事会于周一恢复了黄仁勋的首席执行官职务，在黄仁勋因个人关系被曝光以及对他是否成为外国情报机构攻击目标的调查而辞职仅 11 天后，英伟达董事会就改变了做法。

商界知名人士也对黄仁勋的复职表示赞赏，而特朗普总统表示，他“说服”英伟达董事会做出了这一决定，因为在他缺席期间该公司股价暴跌。

title: Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
title_en: Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
author: Stevie Bonifield
article_content:
Nothing’s new AI device is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple’s new Watch feature and devices like Amazon’s Bee wearable. Nothing CEO Carl Pei demonstrated the new device to Bloomberg, but said the company hasn’t yet settled on a price ahead of a planned launch on December 8th.

The report also says Nothing’s rumored plans for an AI smartwatch and smart glasses are delayed, while it will be “pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next year than it did in 2026.” In a post on X, Pei said this is “the first of many products building a hardware context layer for AI. Rather than ask you to carry a new product, we took something you already wear and trust and made it intelligent.”

According to Bloomberg, the earbuds will “support interactions with various AI agents, including a more basic voice-control system developed by Nothing, letting users engage in back-and-forth conversations.” Users will also be able to record themselves with a “Talk” button on the case, like Nothing previously included on the Ear 3, which also has recording capabilities. Earlier this year, Nothing introduced an Audio Snapshot recording feature in the Ear 3A. Anker’s Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max can also record directly to the earbuds’ case and generate AI transcripts and summaries in an app.

title: Adyen Co CEO Pieter Van Der Does To Retire From Payments Firm
title_en: Adyen Co CEO Pieter Van Der Does To Retire From Payments Firm
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Adyen has turned its payment processing business into one of Europe's biggest entrepreneurial success stories. Now it's quietly deploying artificial intelligence to keep its remarkable growth streak going.

The Amsterdam-based company's philosophy of building tools from within rather than through acquisitions has been crucial to its rise, from its founding in 2006 to its 2018 IPO. Its approach to AI reflects that same philosophy. The company hasn't been talking much about its work in this area but has been cautiously deploying its algorithms internally.

Adyen CEO Pieter van der Does told VentureBeat that the company has studiously avoided hype-driven trends and so initially took a conservative approach to AI. But after developing in-house fraud-detection algorithms, van der Does was quickly convinced of AI's potential.

"When we did our first trials with it, I was surprised how effective it was," he said.

He spoke to VentureBeat as part of a podcasting partnership with Samsung Next at the Slush technology conference in Helsinki, Finland. The full conversation can be heard here.

As hype around AI began to build, van der Does' natural reaction was to be dubious. Rather than panicking and rushing to acquire a startup for its technology, the company began building its own algorithms internally. The results almost immediately exceeded expectations. "The benefits of AI are real," van der Does said.

Adyen is using AI for fraud detection. That has allowed the company to better leverage the large number of data points its system absorbs to make faster and more accurate decisions about people's creditworthiness. Its risk management service -- called RevenueProtect -- includes a ShoperDNA feature, which allows for real-time identification of shoppers.

With AI, Adyen has been able to expand the data points and methodology, which in turn enables much more granular examination of a person or pattern when a purchase is being made. Its Risk Engine automates transaction reviews, which reduces review times by 30%, according to the company.

Typically, such fraud detection is measured by how it limits losses. But van der Does said it's just as important to measure additional transactions that are approved.

He used the example of an Israeli software developer who works in New York and sends a purchase to Europe with a credit card issued in Israel. There's a good chance that such a transaction might be flagged or blocked. But with AI able to process more detail, it might realize that the developer is just sending flowers and the transaction is probably fine.

This way of incorporating AI fits with Adyen's solid, problem-solving approach. The company isn't trying to spin itself as some machine learning-driven wonder. Instead, it treats AI as a practical advance.

"Risk in payments is a way to raise authorization dollars," he said. "If you allow the transaction, your merchant has more revenue than [they] would have had with the old system. That is good for everyone."

Adyen was founded 13 years ago by van der Does, who joined with former colleagues from a payment startup called Bibit Global Payment Services. Bibit was acquired by Royal Bank of Scotland in 2004, and van der Does left the financial giant as soon as his lockup agreement expired.

"[Like] many entrepreneurs, I found it frustrating because the speed of execution suddenly is [at the speed of a] large company," he said. "But I'm actually really grateful for the things I learned there."

Part of van der Does' motivation for starting the company was his perception that innovation in payments had slowed following the Bitbit acquisition, as well as eBay's purchase of PayPal. Rather than just building another interface over payments services for banks and credit cards, Adyen set out to build the entire payment infrastructure.

Initially, this attracted interest from smaller players, like mobile gaming startups that could suddenly offer seamless in-game purchases, as well as ecommerce upstarts like Groupon, whose initial burst of growth helped Adyen go global.

Over time, as the speed and flexibility of the service proved itself, the company began to attract bigger clients, eventually even landing eBay. As Ayden evolved, it also expanded into point-of-sale services for physical retail customers.

But Adyen maintained a conservative approach to growth, which meant the company waited five years before accepting its first outside investment in 2011, though it eventually raised $266 million in venture capital. The first round came mainly from Index Ventures.

Controlling the end-to-end payment infrastructure has allowed Adyen to launch things like its most recent initiative: a platform that allows clients to issue their own virtual and real payment cards. Using Adyen's API, clients can offer a range of cards targeted at everything from narrow uses to general ongoing employee expense payments, each built on specific limits and rules established by the creators. Adyen further refined the product by observing customers' challenges, and it was able to implement changes because it manages the whole system.

"I have been called very slow," said van der Does. "I've been told that I run a pension fund for my children, stuff like that. So yes, we got criticized for our pace of execution. I must say, the shareholder who [said this] was very kind, and he said, 'Pieter, I eat my words -- that was wrong.'"

article_content_zh:
Adyen 已将其支付处理业务打造成欧洲最大的创业成功案例之一。现在，它正在悄然部署人工智能，以保持其惊人的增长势头。

从 2006 年成立到 2018 年 IPO，这家总部位于阿姆斯特丹的公司从内部而不是通过收购构建工具的理念对其崛起至关重要。它的人工智能方法也反映了同样的理念。该公司并未过多谈论其在这一领域的工作，但一直在内部谨慎部署其算法。

Adyen 首席执行官 Pieter van derDos 告诉 VentureBeat，该公司刻意避免炒作驱动的趋势，因此最初对人工智能采取了保守的态度。但在开发了内部欺诈检测算法后，范德多斯很快就相信了人工智能的潜力。

“当我们用它进行第一次试验时，我很惊讶它的效果，”他说。

作为与 Samsung Next 在芬兰赫尔辛基举行的 Slush 技术会议上播客合作的一部分，他接受了 VentureBeat 的采访。完整的对话可以在这里听到。

随着围绕人工智能的炒作开始升温，范德多斯的自然反应是持怀疑态度。该公司并没有恐慌并急于收购一家初创公司的技术，而是开始在内部构建自己的算法。结果几乎立即超出了预期。 “人工智能的好处是真实的，”范德多斯说。

Adyen 正在使用人工智能进行欺诈检测。这使得该公司能够更好地利用其系统吸收的大量数据点，对人们的信用度做出更快、更准确的决策。其风险管理服务——称为 RevenueProtect——包括 ShoperDNA 功能，可以实时识别购物者。

借助人工智能，Adyen 能够扩展数据点和方法，从而能够在购买时对人员或模式进行更精细的检查。据该公司称，其风险引擎可自动进行交易审查，从而将审查时间减少了 30%。

通常，此类欺诈检测是通过其限制损失的方式来衡量的。但范德多斯表示，衡量已批准的额外交易也同样重要。

他以一位在纽约工作的以色列软件开发人员为例，他使用以色列发行的信用卡将购买的商品发送到欧洲。此类交易很有可能被标记或阻止。但随着人工智能能够处理更多细节，它可能会意识到开发者只是在送花，交易可能没问题。

这种融入人工智能的方式符合 Adyen 可靠的解决问题的方法。该公司并没有试图将自己打造成机器学习驱动的奇迹。相反，它将人工智能视为一项实际进步。

“支付风险是筹集授权资金的一种方式，”他说。 “如果你允许交易，你的商家将获得比旧系统更多的收入。这对每个人都有好处。”

Adyen 由 van derDoes 于 13 年前创立，他与一家名为 Bibit Global Payment Services 的支付初创公司的前同事一起加入。 Bibit于2004年被苏格兰皇家银行收购，范德多斯的禁售协议一到期就离开了这家金融巨头。

“[像]许多企业家一样，我发现这令人沮丧，因为执行速度突然变得[以]大公司的速度，”他说。 “但我实际上非常感谢我在那里学到的东西。”

title: Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy
title_en: Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
Anthropic's massive compute needs align with growing profit pressure at xAI, Elon Musk's AI unit. xAI has rented compute to rivals since May, and its June IPO made the push for revenue even more urgent, the New York Times reports. Anthropic is now xAI's biggest customer with a contract worth roughly $3.1 billion a month. Google spends $800 million. Either deal can be canceled with 90 days' notice.

xAI now accounts for over half of xAI's total revenue. Insiders say the company had to finish new data centers by October to fill Anthropic's orders, and Musk says the Claude maker wants to rent even more.

In August, Musk pushed engineers in a group chat for "revenue per GPU,"frustrated in part that xAI's own models can barely compete. He reportedly renamed an internal chat "Sell compute because we can't compete."

xAI is cutting or restructuring its own AI projects to match that shift. Unit chief Mike Nicolls told staff in November that the 60-person team behind the Grok Imagine image and video generator would be disbanded. An internal memo pointed to critical business priorities. xAI shut down its AI avatars in September, and OpenAI also killed its Sora video model over capacity limits.

title: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits
title_en: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits

inline_images.caption: The lower a base model's log-perplexity, the more capabilities it shows, according to OpenAI. Starting in 2026, the scores drop much more steeply than in earlier years. | Image: OpenAI
inline_images.caption_en: The lower a base model's log-perplexity, the more capabilities it shows, according to OpenAI. Starting in 2026, the scores drop much more steeply than in earlier years. | Image: OpenAI

author: Jonathan Kemper
article_content:
OpenAI ties capabilities like fluent conversation and math breakthroughs to specific scores. For the first time, chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is showing where the GPT series sits on that scale, up to an unreleased model beyond GPT-6.

Pachocki wants to make perplexity a common measure of progress for the AI industry and published internal scores for the GPT series in a bl o g post. The metric has long been standard in AI research and Transformer development because it reliably measures how well a pretrained base model predicts the next token in a text.

Lower scores mean more accurate predictions. A perplexity of 2 roughly means the model is as uncertain about the next token as if it were choosing between two equally likely options.

Before it stopped publishing openly, OpenAI often released perplexity scores to show how its models were improving. Releasing them again is a trade-off, Pachocki writes. While rivals get a clearer picture of where OpenAI stands, he says, the need for shared safety standards outweighs that downside. He hopes for a common scientific foundation that lets labs coordinate their pace of development at critical points.

### Capabilities emerge at distinct perplexity thresholds

Pachocki says many capabilities of modern models map surprisingly closely to specific perplexity scores, even though it wasn't clear beforehand that they would appear at those thresholds. He reports the figures on a logarithmic scale called log-perplexity, where lower scores are still better. In his account, GPT-3.5 first enabled fluent conversation at around 0.99, laying the groundwork for the original ChatGPT. At about 0.91, GPT-4 unlocked productive chain-of-thought reasoning, or working through problems step by step. Below 0.8, he writes, transformative capabilities emerged in cybersecurity and math.

The published chart plots OpenAI's base-model log-perplexity by release or evaluation date through November 2026. It covers GPT-5, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.2 Astra, plus an internal model at around 0.73.

### OpenAI's models deliver math breakthroughs in a Slack thread

OpenAI has been feeding its models open math problems for more than a year. Starting with a model at about 0.76 log-perplexity, the models began producing breakthrough results, Pachocki writes. For researchers with a math background, he says, it was "deeply surreal"to watch solutions to longstanding questions pop up one after another in a single Slack thread.

Those results include a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, one of the Millennium Prize problems, though it hasn't been fully verified yet. The same goes for the proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis found by Claude and an Anthropic researcher. Pachocki thinks deep learning research itself could see something similar as soon as 2027, bringing a sudden avalanche of core advances in AI training.

A footnote says the sharp acceleration in the chart starting in 2026 comes mostly from long-term research and compute investments and less from automation. Even so, AI itself has contributed major design work on OpenAI's latest models, according to the post.

### Pachocki warns that AI oversight could erode

Between 0.68 and 0.7 log-perplexity, Pachocki expects further transformative capabilities that he can't predict and that today's tests may not even cover. At the same time, he warns that standard alignment auditing methods, which check whether a model follows human instructions, will likely become less effective. Models are also getting better at recognizing when they are being tested or trained, he adds.

Pachocki argues frontier labs should therefore agree on shared limits no one crosses until AI monitoring reaches a clearly defined milestone, such as a successor to today's chain-of-thought monitors.

### Where perplexity falls short as an industry metric

Different labs use different test datasets, so direct comparisons are harder. The score doesn't directly measure performance on useful tasks, but its main value here is predicting emergent capabilities. Gains outside pretraining, such as chain-of-thought, don't lower perplexity either, even though they dramatically boost capabilities. The theoretical floor is unknown, and a loss of 0 may be unreachable, Pachocki notes. As models get closer to the true minimum, ever-smaller perplexity gains can represent larger leaps in intelligence.

Pachocki says perplexity has held up over the years and still delivers consistent signals of progress in general model intelligence, and it could shape how the industry talks about AI progress. Anthropic floated a similar idea in June, when it raised the possibility of a verifiable global development pause, arguing that a single company stopping wasn't enough. OpenAI has already been through a unilateral pause of its own. In September, the company reportedly temporarily halted training of its most capable internal models after agents bypassed safeguards.

ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki revealed the log-perplexity scores for models from GPT-3.5 to GPT-6 and beyond, illustrating how capabilities emerge as metrics improve. article_content_zh:
OpenAI 将流畅的对话和数学突破等能力与特定分数联系起来。首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki 首次展示了 GPT 系列在该规模上的地位，直至 GPT-6 之外的未发布模型。

Pachocki 希望使困惑度成为人工智能行业进步的通用衡量标准，并在一篇博客文章中发布了 GPT 系列的内部分数。该指标长期以来一直是人工智能研究和 Transformer 开发中的标准，因为它可靠地衡量预训练基础模型预测文本中下一个标记的效果。

分数越低意味着预测越准确。困惑度为 2 大致意味着模型对下一个标记的不确定性就像在两个同等可能性的选项之间进行选择一样。

在停止公开发布之前，OpenAI 经常发布困惑度分数来显示其模型的改进情况。帕乔基写道，再次释放它们是一种权衡。他表示，虽然竞争对手对 OpenAI 的立场有了更清晰的了解，但共享安全标准的必要性超过了这一缺点。他希望建立一个共同的科学基础，让实验室能够在关键时刻协调发展步伐。

### 能力在不同的困惑阈值下出现

帕乔基说，现代模型的许多功能与特定的困惑度分数惊人地密切相关，尽管事先并不清楚它们是否会出现在这些阈值上。他以一种称为“对数困惑度”的对数尺度来报告这些数字，其中分数越低越好。在他的描述中，GPT-3.5首次在0.99左右实现了流畅的对话，为最初的ChatGPT奠定了基础。在 0.91 左右，GPT-4 解锁了富有成效的思维链推理，或者逐步解决问题。他写道，低于 0.8，网络安全和数学领域出现了变革性能力。

已发布的图表按发布或评估日期绘制了截至 2026 年 11 月的 OpenAI 基本模型对数困惑度。它涵盖了 GPT-5、GPT-5.1、GPT-5.2、GPT-5.3-Codex、GPT-5.4、GPT-5.5、GPT-5.6 Sol、GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Astra，以及大约 0.73 的内部模型。

### OpenAI 的模型在 Slack 线程中实现了数学突破

一年多来，OpenAI 一直在为其模型提供开放数学问题。 Pachocki 写道，从对数困惑度约为 0.76 的模型开始，这些模型开始产生突破性的结果。他说，对于具有数学背景的研究人员来说，看到长期存在的问题的解决方案在一个 Slack 线程中一个接一个地出现，“非常超现实”。

这些结果包括纳维-斯托克斯问题的解决方案，这是千年奖问题之一，尽管尚未得到完全验证。克劳德和一位人类研究人员发现的广义黎曼假设的证明也是如此。 Pachocki 认为深度学习研究本身最早可能会在 2027 年看到类似的情况，从而为人工智能训练带来突然的核心进步。

脚注称，从 2026 年开始，图表中的急剧加速主要来自长期研究和计算投资，较少来自自动化。即便如此，据该帖子称，AI 本身还是为 OpenAI 的最新模型做出了主要设计工作。

### Pachocki 警告人工智能监督可能会受到削弱

对数困惑度在 0.68 到 0.7 之间，Pachocki 预计会有更多他无法预测的变革能力，而今天的测试甚至可能无法涵盖。与此同时，他警告说，检查模型是否遵循人类指令的标准对齐审核方法可能会变得不那么有效。他补充道，模型在测试或训练时的识别能力也越来越强。

帕乔基认为，前沿实验室因此应该就共同的限制达成一致，直到人工智能监控达到一个明确定义的里程碑，例如当今思想链监控器的后继者。

title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
title_en: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
author: Jess Weatherbed
article_content:
In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and “instead saw a market opportunity for more profits,” describing the weak safeguards around Grok as “not a failure but a feature.”

“Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” Jones said in a press statement. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation.”

The complaints largely center around Grok Imagine, a tool that allows Grok and X users to generate images and videos. In August 2025, Grok maker xAI (which Musk has since merged with SpaceX) launched a “spicy” mode for Grok Imagine that spat out sexualized content including nude deepfakes of celebrities like Taylor Swift. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature that allowed X users to instantly edit any image without requiring consent from the original poster — resulting in X becoming flooded with nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes of adults and minors.

xAI made several changes to restrict access to Grok image editing, moving some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear, or explicit scenarios. Our testing at the Verge following these restriction updates found they did little to prevent the bot from creating sexualized deepfakes, however.

Both of the Oregon and Virginia lawsuits are seeking financial damages.

The X Safety team said in a statement released after the lawsuits were announced that it takes appropriate measures to address users who generate sexual content involving minors:

article_content_zh:
在周一提起的单独但类似的诉讼中，俄勒冈州总检察长 Dan Rayfield 和弗吉尼亚总检察长 Jay Jones 指控 SpaceX 违反了州消费者保护法，无视行业标准保障措施，并错误地宣传其 X 社交媒体平台和 Grok AI 功能的安全性。在弗吉尼亚州提交的起诉书指责马斯克故意无视人们对人工智能生成的色情深度假货日益增长的担忧，“反而看到了获取更多利润的市场机会”，并将围绕 Grok 的薄弱保障措施描述为“不是失败，而是一个特点”。

“一次又一次，xAI和X告诉消费者，他们受到了保护，不受滥用。这是错误的。相反，该工具允许用户定期创建和传播未经同意的亲密图像和性感图像，以及儿童性虐待材料（CSAM），对个人和儿童造成伤害，”琼斯在一份新闻声明中说。“部署强大工具的公司不能忽视消费者安全，称其为创新。”

这些抱怨主要集中在 Grok Imagine 上，该工具允许 Grok 和 X 用户生成图像和视频。 2025 年 8 月，Grok 制造商 xAI（马斯克后来与 SpaceX 合并）为 Grok Imagine 推出了“辣味”模式，该模式会吐出色情内容，包括泰勒·斯威夫特 (Taylor Swift) 等名人的裸体深度假货。 2026 年 1 月，Grok 获得了一项功能，允许 X 用户立即编辑任何图像，无需获得原始发布者的同意，导致 X 充斥着未经同意的、成人和未成年人的色情深度赝品。

xAI 进行了几项更改来限制对 Grok 图像编辑的访问，将某些功能移至付费墙后面，并阻止对性姿势、泳装或露骨场景的某些请求。然而，我们在这些限制更新后在 Verge 进行的测试发现，它们几乎没有阻止机器人创建色情化的深度赝品。

俄勒冈州和弗吉尼亚州的诉讼均寻求经济损失。

X Safety 团队在诉讼宣布后发布的一份声明中表示，他们将采取适当措施来解决生成涉及未成年人的色情内容的用户问题：

content_snippet:
The CyberLeek hacking gang claims to have released a key executable program that promises to help the modding community port Grand Theft Auto 6 to the PC. An early Christmas gift from CL,” CyberLeek wrote in a post titled “Xmas came early.”

The archive supposedly completes the stolen Xbox build for GTA 6 that CyberLeek initially began circulating last

article_content_zh:
Cyber​​Leek 黑客团伙声称已经发布了一个关键的可执行程序，承诺帮助改装社区将《侠盗猎车手 6》移植到 PC 上。周一，该组织更新了其网站，发布了包含可执行程序的 57MB 存档的链接。 “exe 已经出来了。永远免费。这是 CL 提前送来的圣诞礼物，”Cyber​​Leek 在一篇题为“圣诞节来得早”的帖子中写道。

该档案据称是被盗的《GTA 6》Xbox 版本的完整版本，Cyber​​Leek 最初于上周通过包含 Rockstar RAGE 游戏引擎和 Xbox 主机文件的 209GB 种子开始传播。 Cyber​​Leek 现在表示，由于 Xbox 平台在基于 Microsoft Windows 的操作系统上运行，因此文件转储足以让模组社区重新编译游戏以在 PC 上运行。

“火炬传递给开源重新编译和仿真项目，”该团伙说。在之前提高该货币市值的努力失败后，Cyber​​Leek 似乎也满足于仅仅要求对该组织的 meme 货币进行捐款。 GTA 6 社区重新编译项目 Leonida 一直在检查泄露的可执行文件。流量如此之高，以至于该群组在 Discord 上的聊天服务器出现故障，似乎崩溃了。然而，一位管理员后来发帖称：“我们至少需要一周时间才能找到可以在电脑上玩的地方。”为了避免该项目被删除，管理员补充道：“我们不会提供任何资产；您需要自己下载游戏。”“这个 .exe 文件不能运行游戏，”一位管理员在泄漏事件发生前也发帖称。 “开发人员将使用它来进行实际的重新编译，从而使用游戏文件和 exe 来构建移植。”与此同时，该项目的用户一直在使用人工智能编码工具和代理，包括 Anthropic 的 Claude，进行逆向工程并尝试让泄露的游戏文件在 Windows 上运行。 “游戏快要启动了。黑屏，音频中断，”一位用户在 Discord 聊天中声称。

你不需要 PS5 Pro。 Xbox Series S 上的《GTA 6》依然惊艳

GTA 6 终于来了...那么什么时候可以和朋友一起在线玩呢？

到目前为止，Rockstar Games 及其母公司 Take-Two Interactive 尚未回应置评请求。但据传开发商正准备最快在明年第一季度推出 GTA 6 的正式 PC 版本。尽管如此，盗版 PC 移植可能会像病毒一样传播并削弱该游戏的销量，该游戏目前仅在 PlayStation 5 和 Xbox Series X/S 上独占。转储的文件还表明，Cyber​​Leek 能够在游戏正式发布之前渗透并窃取 GTA 6 的 Xbox 副本。尽管 Take-Two 传唤了包括微软在内的主要平台提供记录，试图揭露泄密者，但 Cyber​​Leek 仍然逍遥法外。
